## #3492 — ha: buildZoneRGMap panics on nil zone value in per-RG session-sync apply path [CLOSED] (closed 2026-06-29)

**Provenance:** Codex review audit 120 (`/tmp/codex-review-120.md`, H2 + test-gap L4). Verified on `origin/master` @ 93ef2e74f. Daemon-apply sibling of the display-side #3476 and counter-resolver #3474 — same established nil-slot invariant, new uncovered (and higher-severity: daemon crash) surface.

## Defect
`buildZoneRGMap` dereferences `zone.Interfaces` without a `zone == nil` guard. The dataplane builders treat nil zone values as a real, defended invariant (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:364` `if zone == nil { continue }`; policies.go:246/252 guards), so a nil `Security.Zones["x"]` is reachable on the tolerant/programmatic/HA-peer-sync config path (the reachability premise #3474/#3476 already established). On that path the daemon apply path panics instead of degrading.

## origin/master proof
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go`: per-RG sync calls `d.sessionSync.SetZoneRGMap(buildZoneRGMap(cfg, applyResult.ZoneIDs))` during `ApplyConfig`.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace.go:428` `func buildZoneRGMap`: loops `for zoneName, zone := range cfg.Security.Zones` then `for _, ifName := range zone.Interfaces` with NO `zone == nil` check.
- Contrast (nil-safe SSOT): `pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:363-364`.

## Impact
In HA, a malformed/tolerant peer snapshot turns a config refresh into a daemon panic / failed apply BEFORE session-sync ownership can be updated — availability regression, not mere display fragility.

## Fix direction
Add `if zone == nil { continue }` in `buildZoneRGMap`. Add `TestBuildZoneRGMapSkipsNilZones` beside `TestBuildZoneRGMap` / `TestBuildZoneRGMapEmptyConfig` in `pkg/daemon/per_rg_test.go` (nil entry + healthy entry; assert only the healthy entry is mapped) — closes the L4 test-gap.

## #3499 — interface compiler: compiler_iface.go derefs nil zone map-values in the apply-path bring-down reconcile [CLOSED] (closed 2026-06-29)

Sibling of #3492 (HA buildZoneRGMap nil-zone) / #3496 (apply-path nil-safety sweep), surfaced by the #3498 SMR review. Verified on origin/master.

This is the apply path (interface management / bring-down reconcile, #1956), not retired-eBPF, so it is live. The runtime SSOT walkers (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go`, `screens.go`) already treat nil zones as skip — confirming the design intent is nil-tolerance.

**Fix:** add `if zone == nil { continue }` at the top of the zone loop, mirroring the SSOT idiom and the #3496 apply-path guards (#3496 swept pkg/daemon + pkg/flowexport but not pkg/dataplane/compiler_iface.go).

**Test:** a nil zone slot in the bring-down reconcile must not panic; reverting the guard panics (RED-on-revert).

- Apply it in the session GC / OPENING-session reaper so a bare-SYN session for a zone with `syn-flood timeout N` is aged out on `N` seconds instead of the global default.
- Define HA-sync composition: does the override travel with the synced session, or is it re-derived from config on the standby? (open question §11.1 of the #3315 plan)

## #3562 — config: 6 strict-reject AST-walk validators bypassed by duplicate top-level 'security {}' blocks (first-security-node-only) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-06-29)

Found while folding #3561 (Codex MAJOR). `parseStatements` (pkg/config/parser.go) APPENDS a repeated top-level block rather than merging, and `compileExpanded` processes EVERY top-level `security` root. But several strict-reject AST-walk validators inspect only the FIRST `security` node (`Name()=="security"` → assign → `break`), so a hierarchical config with two `security {}` blocks (first harmless, second carrying the offending stanza) BYPASSES the strict reject — the second block is still compiled. Reachable via `LoadOverride` (NewParser hierarchical path, configstore/store_command.go).

#3561 fixed `validateDNATRuleSetToScopeAST` (iterate all security roots). The SAME pattern remains in:
- `compiler_ipsec_bindiface.go:62` — validateSecureTunnelBindInterfaceAST (#2933)
- `compiler_policy_match.go:130` — validatePolicyMatchLeavesStrict (#3113)
- `compiler_policy_missing_match.go:91` — validatePolicyRequiredMatchStrict (#3044)
- `compiler_policy_then.go:82` — then-permit strict (#3114)
- `compiler_policy_then.go:233` — then-reject strict (#3115)
- `compiler_policy_then.go:406` — then-deny strict (#3141)

(`compiler_security.go:1863` is NOT affected — it iterates all roots without breaking.)

Each of these strict rejects (including the #3114/#3115/#3141 then-action fail-open gates just reworked in #3558/#3377) can be bypassed by splitting config across duplicate `security` blocks → the specific fail-open diagnostic is lost at strict commit (and suppressed on the lenient path). Note the typed-config consumers are generally fine (the compiler merges all roots into the typed config); the gap is specifically these AST-walk pre-checks.

Fix: convert all 6 to iterate EVERY top-level `security` node (mirror compiler_security.go:1863 / the #3561 fix), keeping each validator's inner narrow walk unchanged. Add a duplicate-`security`-block RED-on-revert test per validator (hierarchical NewParser, two security blocks, offending stanza in the second → strict reject). Consider a shared `forEachSecurityNode` helper to prevent recurrence.

## #3579 — daemon applySyslogConfig uses non-closing SetSyslogClients → conn leak on re-apply (CLI uses closing ReplaceSyslogClients) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-06-30)

Surfaced during the #3351 review (PR #3576).

The daemon's `applySyslogConfig` (pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go) installs syslog clients via `er.SetSyslogClients(...)`, which does a wholesale slice replace but does NOT Close the previously-installed clients. The remote-CLI apply path (pkg/cli/apply.go) uses the closing `ReplaceSyslogClients` (pkg/logging/ringbuf.go) instead.

Consequence: on every config re-apply that changes/removes a CONNECTED TCP/TLS syslog stream, the old client's connection (fd) leaks — it is dropped from the set but never closed. Over many commits this accumulates open sockets.

Fix direction: make the daemon path close superseded clients (use/мirror ReplaceSyslogClients semantics, or Close the diff). Add a test asserting an old connected client is Closed when superseded on re-apply.

Provenance: pre-existing (independent of #3351); flagged by the PR#3576 daemon-integration reviewer. (#3351/PR#3576 folded only the zero-streams teardown gap.)

Unlike `/sessions` and `/sessions/summary`, there is **no gRPC zone-pair-summary RPC** for the REST handler to forward to. ```
rust-lld: error: duplicate symbol: crc32
  >>> defined at crc32.o:(crc32) in archive .../libelf.a
  >>> defined at crc32.o:(.text+0xb60) in archive .../libz.a
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
error: could not compile `xpf-userspace-dp` (bin "xpf-userspace-dp") due to 1 previous error

The helper links `-lelf` and `-lz` (transitively via the static

hard error on modern toolchains.

Compile/test is unaffected (`cargo test --release` builds the lib test

**release binary link** for the deployable `xpf-userspace-dp` fails. So

on a gcc-15 host.

`RUSTFLAGS="-C link-arg=-Wl,--allow-multiple-definition"` for the
`make cluster-deploy` build (the linker then takes the first `crc32`,
which is benign — they are independent CRC implementations and each
library calls its own copy internally only where it was already
self-contained).

## #3604 — conntrack GC: data race on aging/session-limit config fields (sweep reads/writes without gc.mu) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

`pkg/conntrack/gc.go` has a data race on the aggressive-aging / session-limit
configuration fields. The config setters take `gc.mu`, but the GC sweep
goroutine reads (and in one place writes) the same fields with no lock.

## Provenance (origin/master 9419bbc2c)

Writers hold `gc.mu`:
- `SetAgingConfig` (`pkg/conntrack/gc.go:168-186`) — `gc.mu.Lock()`, writes
  `earlyAgeout`, `highWatermark`, `lowWatermark`, `agingActive`.
- `SetSessionLimitEnabled` (`gc.go:192-196`) — `gc.mu.Lock()`, writes
  `sessionLimitEnabled`.

Sweep goroutine (`gc.Run` -> `gc.sweep`, started `go gc.Run(ctx)`) reads/writes
the SAME fields with NO `gc.mu`:
- reads `sessionLimitEnabled` (`gc.go:266`)
- reads `agingActive` / `earlyAgeout` (`gc.go:289-290`, `363-364`, `456`, `458`, `496`)
- **writes** `agingActive` (`gc.go:459`, `463`) in the watermark hysteresis block
- the only `gc.mu.Lock()` in `sweep()` is at `gc.go:471`, scoped to `gc.stats`.

So a config commit (main daemon thread -> `SetAgingConfig` /
`SetSessionLimitEnabled`) races the GC sweep goroutine. `agingActive` is even
written under a lock by the setter and WITHOUT a lock by the sweep watermark
path — inconsistent locking on the same field.

## Impact

Per the Go memory model this is a data race (`go test -race` will flag it when
the two goroutines overlap). Practically: an aging/session-limit config update
can be missed or clobbered by the concurrent watermark write, and the compiler
is free to hoist the register-cached reads across the sweep's map-iteration
closures. Low practical damage on amd64 (word-sized fields) but a genuine race
that also masks config-vs-watermark ordering bugs.

## Suggested fix

Either snapshot the config fields under `gc.mu.RLock()` once at the top of
`sweep()` into locals, or convert `agingActive`/`earlyAgeout`/`highWatermark`/
`lowWatermark`/`sessionLimitEnabled` to `atomic.Bool`/`atomic.Uint64`/

reachable via a normal commit (and also via lenient-load / peer-sync).

public address translated differently per ingress context). On xpf the second

## #3606 — config: validatePortSpec accepts signed ports (+80) via strconv.Atoi that the dataplane/Rust parser reject — commit-vs-dataplane split [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

`validatePortSpec` (commit-time application port validation) uses
`strconv.Atoi`, which accepts a leading `+` sign. The dataplane
representability gate (`ParseUint`) and the Rust parser (`parse::<u16>`) both
REJECT a signed port. So a port spec like `+80` commits cleanly but is silently
unrepresentable at the dataplane — a commit-vs-dataplane / commit-vs-simulator
divergence on a security leaf.

## Provenance (origin/master 9419bbc2c)

- `validatePortSpec` — `port, err := strconv.Atoi(spec)`
  (`pkg/config/compiler_applications.go:568`; ranges use `Atoi` at `552-553`).
  `Atoi("+80")` = 80, nil -> passes the 1..65535 range check -> commit succeeds.
  (Note `-80` is caught: `Atoi("-80")` = -80 -> fails `< 1`. Only leading-`+`
  slips through.)
- `userspacePortSpecRepresentable` — `strconv.ParseUint(spec, 10, 16)`
  (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/capabilities.go`), which returns an error on `+80`.
  When it returns false the whole application is downgraded / not emitted:
  `if !userspacePortSpecRepresentable(...) { return nil, false }`
  (`capabilities.go:337-340`).
- Rust `parse_port_spec` — `normalized.parse::<u16>().ok()?`
  (`userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:~1510`), also rejects the sign.

## Impact

Fail-closed (the app becomes unsupported rather than fail-open to match-any),
so not a security hole, but a silent divergence: the operator's `+80` app
commits, the CLI/simulator (`portMatches` via `Atoi`) says it matches, and the
dataplane silently treats the app as unsupported so the intended policy never
takes effect — with no error surfaced. Same class as the `#2124` fail-closed
port-parse hardening.

## Suggested fix

Make `validatePortSpec` reject what the dataplane cannot represent: parse with
`strconv.ParseUint(spec, 10, 16)` (and for ranges) instead of `Atoi`, so a
signed / out-of-`u16` port fails loudly at commit, matching
`userspacePortSpecRepresentable` and the Rust parser.

## #3607 — screen: RateCounter over-throttles sustained at-threshold traffic (rejected events keep the window saturated; no recovery without an idle second) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

## Summary

The screen flood `RateCounter` (`userspace-dp/src/screen/rate.rs`, the two-bucket
sliding window that fixed `#2937`) over-throttles a sustained sender at exactly
the configured threshold. Because rejected events are still counted, a
sustained at-threshold sender is admitted only in the first second and then
dropped in every subsequent second until a FULLY IDLE second elapses. The module
doc's claim that "a sustained sender is still admitted at ~threshold events per
second" does not hold.

## Provenance (origin/master 9419bbc2c)

`increment` (`rate.rs:79-83`):
```
self.advance(now_secs);
self.count = self.count.saturating_add(1);
self.prev_count.saturating_add(self.count) > threshold
```
`advance` demotes `count` -> `prev_count` on a 1-second roll (`rate.rs:60-71`).

Trace at threshold=100, sustained 100 events/sec:
- Second N: 100 events pass (prev=0). End: count=100.
- Second N+1: first event -> advance sets prev=100, count=1 -> 100+1=101 > 100
  -> DROP (but still counted). Every later event in N+1: count grows, prev stays
  100 -> all DROP. End: count=100 (all counted).
- Second N+2: advance -> prev=100 again -> same, all DROP. No recovery without a
  fully idle second.

The over-throttle is confirmed; the existing test
(`icmp_flood_sliding_window_blocks_boundary_burst_then_recovers`,
`screen/tests.rs`) only pins the anti-burst property, not the sustained-threshold
contract, so H02 survives green (M09).

## Impact

Legitimate traffic (and standby SYN-cookie ACK validation) at the operator's
configured threshold is suppressed far below that threshold. Deviates from Junos
threshold semantics and from the module's own documented contract.

## Suggested fix (design decision)

## #3609 — userspace-dp host-inbound: per-interface override missed on VLAN logical interfaces (gate probes raw physical ifindex, not resolved logical) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

The per-interface host-inbound OVERRIDE (`#3362`) is keyed by the LOGICAL
interface ifindex in the snapshot, but the LocalDelivery host-inbound gate probes
it with the RAW physical (XSK parent) ifindex. On a VLAN subinterface (e.g.

so a per-interface host-inbound override on a logical unit is ignored.

## Provenance (origin/master 9419bbc2c)

- Snapshot keys the override by the interface's own (logical) ifindex:
  `state.ifindex_host_inbound.insert(iface.ifindex, ...)`
  (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:93-107`).
- The host-inbound gate uses the RAW meta ifindex:
  `host_inbound_admits_iface(forwarding, meta.ingress_ifindex as i32, ...)`
  (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/filter.rs:452-454`).
- The SIBLING input-filter path DOES resolve the logical ifindex first:
  `let ingress_ifindex = resolve_ingress_logical_ifindex(forwarding,
  meta.ingress_ifindex as i32, meta.ingress_vlan_id).unwrap_or(...)`
  (`filter.rs:100-105`) — the host-inbound gate omits this resolution, so
  physical vs logical diverge only on the host-inbound path.

## Impact

Per-interface host-inbound is a vSRX parity feature for exposing management /
control protocols on ONE interface within a zone. On VLAN-heavy / RETH.unit
deployments the override is silently ignored (falls back to the zone set),
which can under-permit (break intended management access) or over-permit
(expose services the operator scoped to a different unit) the control plane.

## Suggested fix

Resolve the logical ingress ifindex ONCE (as the input-filter path does) and
pass it explicitly into `host_inbound_gated_lo0_action` /
`host_inbound_admits_iface` instead of re-reading `meta.ingress_ifindex`.
Ideally introduce a resolved `HostInboundContext { raw_ifindex, logical_ifindex,
zone_id, vlan_id }` and thread it through all LocalDelivery gates (L01). Add a
VLAN-subinterface LocalDelivery regression test that sets a per-interface
override on the logical ifindex and asserts the override governs (M10) — current
direct helper tests use default `UserspaceDpMeta` with no VLAN mapping.

## Summary

Host-inbound (control-plane) denies are accounted only as aggregate counters and
have no tuple-rich dataplane event, so operators can see that host-inbound denies
happened but not who hit which control-plane service. Separately, the deny
branches increment the debug counter `dbg.policy_deny`, conflating host-inbound
drops with real security-policy denies.

## Provenance (origin/master 9419bbc2c)

In `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs`, the host-inbound-deny
branches:

  `telemetry.dbg.policy_deny` (`mod.rs:869`, `917`, `962`, `1740`), tear down the
  session, and recycle the descriptor — with NO tuple event emitted.
- `emit_policy_deny_event` (`mod.rs:122`) exists for real policy denies but is
  not called for host-inbound denies. `FlowlessLocalVerdict::HostInboundDeny`
  (`mod.rs:217-218`, `265`) is a verdict, not an event.

## Impact

1. Observability: no `HostInboundDeny` event with src/dst IP, protocol,
   service/port, ingress zone/interface, and reason -> weak incident response for
   control-plane protection (below the quality of transit RT_FLOW policy-deny
   logging). (Codex H06)

   denies, sending dataplane investigations down the wrong path. (Codex M07)

## Suggested fix

- Add a first-class `DataplaneEventKind::HostInboundDeny` (tuple +
  service/protocol + ingress zone/interface + reason), rate-limited by
  zone/source like other cold-path dataplane events, and consume it in the Go
  logging / REST surfaces (L04).
- Add `dbg.host_inbound_deny` and stop incrementing `dbg.policy_deny` on the
  host-inbound branches (M07).

## #3612 — AppID: enabled catalog (lowest app_id) vs disabled fallback (specificity) precedence divergence relabels the same session [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

AppID application-label precedence diverges between the two code paths. With
AppID ENABLED, the Rust catalog resolves overlapping entries to the LOWEST
`app_id` (sorted-name order). With AppID DISABLED, the Go display fallback
resolves overlaps by SPECIFICITY (a port-constrained app beats a protocol-only
app). The same 5-tuple can therefore be labeled with a different application name
depending on the AppID knob.

## Provenance (origin/master 9419bbc2c)

- Enabled path (Rust): `AppCatalog::lookup_directional` returns the lowest id on
  overlap — `match (exact, scan_hit) { (Some(a), Some(b)) => a.min(b), ... }`
  (`userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:~1646`), documented as "First writer wins (lowest
  app_id)" (`policy.rs:1568`, `1527`). Tests pin this
  (`policy_tests.rs` `app_catalog_overlap_lowest_id_wins`).
- Disabled fallback (Go): `resolveTupleFallback` deliberately prefers the more
  specific app — "the more-specific port-based app must win, deterministically"
  (`pkg/appid/runtime.go:136-141`, `#2578`).

## Impact

Application labels are operator-facing security/forensic evidence (session
display, RT_FLOW, logs). A TCP/443 session can be stamped as a broad
protocol-only `aaa-tcp` with AppID enabled but shown as the specific
`zzz-https-special` with AppID disabled. Inconsistent labeling erodes operator
trust and complicates incident analysis.

## Suggested fix (design decision)

Define ONE precedence rule for application labeling — preferably specificity
first (exact-port > range > protocol-only), then a deterministic name/id
tie-break — and share it across the Go fallback and the Rust enabled catalog,
with a parity test asserting both agree (L03). If lowest-id is the intended
contract for the enabled path, document that as an explicit product decision and
align the disabled fallback + docs to match.

filter-log event is emitted with action REJECT *before* the generated RST/ICMP
reply is actually enqueued. The reply can then fail closed (TX-frame budget
exhausted, reject token bucket empty, unparseable/built-frame parse error, or an

forensic ground truth for a firewall, so this makes an operator believe active

that silently drops the reject itself) and is adjacent to #3610 (host-inbound
deny event richness). #3608 is about the wire drop; this issue is about the event

firewall's XFRM stack. On vSRX, host-inbound-traffic system-services ike/ipsec is
an operator-controlled policy surface, so "no ike/ipsec in host-inbound" does not
mean "block IKE/IPsec to the box" here.

This is a deliberate pragmatic tradeoff for strongSwan/XFRM (the code documents
it as intentional), but strict vSRX host-inbound parity is a real question that
needs an explicit decision and a pinning test rather than being re-flagged on

## #3617 — userspace-dp: locally-generated reject/error replies are never mirror-cloned (mirror_clone hard-false) — analyzer misses device-sent RST/ICMP [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

Locally-generated reject/error replies (policy/filter then reject -> TCP RST or
ICMP/ICMPv6 unreachable) are enqueued with mirror_clone hard-coded to false. A
configured analyzer/port-mirror session therefore sees the trigger packet but
NOT the RST/ICMP reject the device actually sent. For firewall forensics (policy
rejects, PMTUD, scanner behavior) a mirror that misses device-generated replies
misrepresents what the box put on the wire.

Severity: Medium-low (depends on whether mirroring is intended for locally
generated control replies). Review: /tmp/codex-review-002.md M04 (folds L10, L18).

## Provenance (origin/master 0be2bd792)

- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs ~233-244: the
  TxRequest for the generated reply sets mirror_clone: false unconditionally,
  even though the same helper threads egress output-filter, cos_queue_id, and
  dscp_rewrite through classify_generated_reply (#2238/#3035). Mirror is the one
  egress attribute left un-threaded.
- The generated-reply path reflects out the ingress interface (egress_ifindex =
  ingress_ifindex) rather than going through a first-class local-output pipeline
  (L18), so mirror/analyzer selection has no natural home today.

## Fix direction

- Decide whether locally-generated replies should honor egress mirror/analyzer
  policy. If yes, thread mirror selection through classify_generated_reply (or a
  sibling helper) alongside the existing CoS/DSCP/output-filter classification.
- Add a generated-reply classification test that asserts ALL TxRequest egress
  metadata fields including mirror_clone (L10) so the value is a deliberate,
  pinned invariant either way.
- Longer term (L18): consider a shared local-output pipeline abstraction for
  reject / PTB / time-exceeded / cookie replies so mirror/CoS/DSCP/telemetry stay
  consistent as local-generated traffic grows.

Classify: design-fork (the "should local replies be mirrored" question is a
policy decision) -> becomes driveable once decided.

## #3618 — userspace-dp: one global reject token bucket lets a flood in one zone starve active rejects for all other zones [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

## Summary

Locally-generated active rejects (policy and firewall-filter then reject) are
rate-limited by a SINGLE global-per-reason token bucket (REJECT_BUCKET). There is
no per-zone / per-RG / per-worker scoping. A rejected-flow flood arriving in one
(untrusted) zone drains the shared Reject bucket, so legitimate policy rejects in
a DIFFERENT zone fail closed to silent drops even though that zone is not under
attack. The model was chosen to mirror Linux icmp_msgs_per_sec (bounded state, no
attacker-driven map growth), but a multi-zone firewall is not a single Linux host:
one zone can suppress active-reject semantics and troubleshooting signal for all
other zones.

This is a DIFFERENT limiter from #3607 (screen RateCounter over-throttle). This is
the generated-error / reject reply token bucket.

Severity: Medium. Review: /tmp/codex-review-002.md M05 (folds L12).

## Provenance (origin/master 0be2bd792)

- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_ratelimit.rs ~163-165: static REJECT_BUCKET
  (alongside TIME_EXCEEDED_BUCKET / PACKET_TOO_BIG_BUCKET) is a single global
  TokenBucket; bucket_for(Reject) returns it for every zone.
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_ratelimit.rs ~183 allow_generated_error(Reject)
  uses the compile-time DEFAULT_RATE_PER_SEC / DEFAULT_BURST with no zone key.
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs ~179 both policy and
  filter reject share this single Reject bucket.

## Fix direction

- Either move to per-zone / per-RG / per-worker Reject buckets with bounded
  cardinality (decision needed: what cardinality is safe against attacker-driven
  growth), OR keep the global bucket but expose ZONE-ATTRIBUTED suppression
  counters so an operator can see which zone drained the bucket and that another
  zone's rejects were collateral-suppressed.
- Add a test (L12) distinguishing: explicit then deny; then reject with a
  successful reply; then reject with the bucket empty -> each observable and
  distinct in telemetry.

Classify: design-fork -> /research the scoping/cardinality decision (per-zone
bucket count vs global-plus-attribution) before coding.

## #3622 — appid: CatalogNames/addPolicyApps panic on nil zone-policy/policy entries (missing nil-guard vs strict walker) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary (Codex review-122 H05 + H06 — verified against origin/master bd2443c5e)

`appid.CatalogNames` (`pkg/appid/runtime.go:42`) builds the AppID catalog by ranging `cfg.Security.Policies` and their inner policies **without nil-guards**, so a nil `*config.ZonePolicy` or nil policy entry causes a **panic (nil deref)** in a runtime helper instead of a fail-closed config error.

- `runtime.go:80-81` — `for _, zpp := range cfg.Security.Policies { if err := addPolicyApps(zpp.Policies); ... }` dereferences `zpp.Policies` with no `if zpp == nil` guard.
- `runtime.go:59-60` — `for _, pol := range policies { for _, appName := range pol.Match.Applications { ... }` dereferences `pol.Match` with no `if pol == nil` guard.

The **strict validation walker already nil-guards these exact structures** — `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict.go:155,2022` (`if zpp == nil`), `:70,210,2006,2113` (`if pol == nil`), `pkg/config/compiler_security.go:402`, `pkg/config/compiler_services.go:925`. So the codebase has the resilience pattern; `CatalogNames`/`addPolicyApps` omit it. A lenient-load / generated / test config that produces a nil entry (the tolerant-load path #1960 intentionally admits partially-broken configs) crashes the userspace app-catalog build instead of surfacing an actionable error.

## Fix
Match the strict walker: `continue` on nil zone-policy and nil policy entries in `CatalogNames` / `addPolicyApps`. Add a regression test that a malformed/nil-entry fixture returns cleanly (no panic).

## Severity
High (crash / DoS on a malformed-but-tolerated config). Driveable.

Provenance: Codex review-122 H05/H06, verified against current origin/master.

## #3623 — api/grpc: policy inventory + match-policies drop policy_id for the first runtime policy (id 0) — omitempty/proto3-zero hides the RT_FLOW join key [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary (Codex review-122 H01/H02/M08; test-gaps H03/H04 folded — verified against origin/master bd2443c5e)

The REST security-policy inventory, REST match-policies diagnostic, and gRPC PolicyRule inventory all serialize the runtime policy_id with a zero-value-omitting encoding, so the FIRST runtime policy — which legitimately has policy_id 0 — is dropped from the wire. A consumer joining an RT_FLOW / session event (policy_id=0) back to the inventory finds no matching row.

## Root cause

The first zone-pair set's first rule gets runtime id 0: RuntimePolicyIndex = policySetID*MaxRulesPerPolicy + ruleIndex = 0*256 + 0. Since #3057 the implicit default policy uses DefaultPolicySentinelID = 0xFFFFFFFF, so id 0 is UNAMBIGUOUSLY the first real policy — yet the surfaces drop it:

- pkg/api/types.go PolicyInfo.PolicyID: tag json:"policy_id,omitempty" (the comment even documents "omitted when 0 (the first rule of the first zone-pair set)").
- pkg/api/types.go MatchPoliciesResult.PolicyID: tag json:"policy_id,omitempty" — a matched first-rule response drops policy_id, looking like no runtime id was available.
- proto/xpf/v1/xpf.proto PolicyRule.policy_id = 17 (proto3 scalar uint32) — a generic JSON/proto client cannot distinguish absent from first-rule id 0.

Populated at pkg/api/security.go:176 (zone) and :260 (global) via dpuserspace.RuntimePolicyIndex(runtimeIDs, policySetID, i); match-policies at :570.

## Impact

The purpose of #3336 (surface runtime policy_id so RT_FLOW/session telemetry joins to a configured rule) is defeated exactly for the first, highest-priority policy. The first policy is a common high-priority rule.

## Note vs the (stale) review quote

## #3624 — api/grpc: structured policy inventory (PolicyInfo/PolicyRule) omits scheduler binding + runtime inactive state (structured sibling of #3062) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary (Codex review-122 H07/H08; test-gap L10 folded — verified against origin/master bd2443c5e)

The Policy config struct carries SchedulerName + Inactive (pkg/config/types_security.go), and the userspace snapshot publishes both (pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies.go). #3062 exposed scheduler name + live active/inactive state on the TEXT policy-detail surfaces (CLI + gRPC text, via policyDetailState / policySchedulerActiveState). - gRPC PolicyRule (proto/xpf/v1/xpf.proto message PolicyRule, fields 1-18) has no scheduler_name / inactive field; pkg/grpcapi/server_show_zones.go never populates one.

## Impact

A structured API client (audit / automation) cannot tell that a permit/deny rule is time-gated, nor that it is currently runtime-inactive. The live-state provider already exists: Server.policySchedulerActiveState() and PolicyInactiveFn (#3414). The inventory builders can populate an inactive flag from the same source #3062 uses for the text surface; only new proto/JSON fields + population + tests are required.

- Add REST/gRPC tests for a scheduled-inactive rule (L10: current tests cover addr-exclusion/log/count/rule-id but not scheduler state).

## Dedup

Structured-inventory sibling of the closed #3062 (which fixed only the human-readable TEXT detail: State: inactive + Scheduler: lines). The structured GetPolicies (gRPC PolicyRule) / REST PolicyInfo JSON were not touched by #3062 and the proto has no field.

## #3626 — appid: runtime catalog (CatalogNames appid-disabled) omits source/destination-NAT match-application refs that strict validation collects [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary (Codex review-122 M01; test-note M02; refactor L04 — verified against origin/master bd2443c5e)

When application-identification is DISABLED, appid.CatalogNames(cfg, false) (pkg/appid/runtime.go) builds the compiled app catalog by walking ONLY cfg.Security.Policies and cfg.Security.GlobalPolicies (addPolicyApps). It never walks NAT rule match-application references. The strict validator DOES walk them: pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict.go:3976-3992 (walkNATRules over NAT.Source + NAT.Destination.RuleSets, addRef(rule.Match.Application)).

So a config whose only reference to (e.g.) junos-ssh is a source/destination-NAT match application — with no security policy referencing it — validates fine, but the runtime catalog omits that app when appid is disabled; session introspection/naming for that flow falls back to tuple/numeric.

pkg/appid/runtime_test.go carries an explicit #2187 scope note that the NAT-reference path is intentionally excluded from the CatalogNames-vs-strict equality fixture (adding a NAT ref would break equality). The drift is documented but unpinned.

Limited: with appid disabled, session naming uses tuple fallback anyway; with appid enabled (includeAll=true) the catalog pulls all predefined + user apps, so NAT refs are covered. This is a consistency/parity gap, not a data-path bug.

## Fix direction

Have CatalogNames(false) also collect NAT rule match-application refs, or (L04) share ONE reference walker with strict validation — a single config.WalkApplicationReferences used by strict validation, the runtime catalog, and tests. Add a NAT-only catalog regression test.

## #3639 — vSRX parity: enforce to-zone junos-host GLOBAL (from-zone any) host-inbound policy (split from #3611 Piece B) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary (buildable split from #3611 Piece B — Codex-verified in the #3611 /research)

The #3611 /research (PLAN-DEFER, 3-of-3) split into:
- **Piece A** — `from-zone junos-host` (host-ORIGINATED): NOT enforceable in the AF_XDP userspace dataplane (XDP is RX-only; the firewall's own sockets egress via the kernel TX path, never the XSK). Document-only architectural limitation. Tracked on #3611.
- **Piece B (THIS ISSUE) — `to-zone junos-host` GLOBAL (`from-zone any`) host-inbound**: this IS cleanly userspace-enforceable (to-zone junos-host traverses the LocalDelivery gate). Today a global (`from-zone any`) junos-host-context policy is REJECTED at commit (the #3611 M03 half), and `evaluate_junos_host_policy` only consults the exact-zone-pair + specific host-inbound indices, not the global (from-any) junos-host tier.

## Fix (Codex-verified coupling in the #3611 plan)
In ONE coupled change:
1. Lift the commit-reject of a global (`from-zone any` / `to-zone junos-host`) policy (pkg/config strict validation).
2. Index globals into the host-inbound gate so `evaluate_junos_host_policy` (userspace-dp/src/policy.rs) also consults the from-any junos-host tier for host-bound traffic.

Both must land together (indexing without lifting the reject is dead; lifting without indexing is a silent fail-open). RED-on-revert: a global `from-zone any to-zone junos-host` deny governs host-bound traffic that no exact zone-pair matches.

## Provenance
#3611 /research Piece B, converged 3-of-3 (Codex+AGY+Claude-SMR), plan doc on branch research/3611-junos-host-self-zone. Driveable-bug.

## #3642 — output firewall filter matches pre-NAT tuple after SNAT/DNAT (wrong Junos semantics) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

The egress (interface `filter output`) firewall-filter is evaluated on the
PRE-NAT (original ingress) tuple on the userspace-dp TX/CoS selection path. Junos
applies an interface output firewall filter on the egress interface AFTER NAT
(both destination-NAT and source-NAT), so it must match the translated (POST-NAT)
on-wire headers. An operator whose output filter matches src/dst/port therefore
matches the wrong (untranslated) tuple after SNAT/DNAT.

## Provenance (origin/master c5064f4fd)

Eval site (pre-NAT key passed to the output-filter TX-selection):
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forward_request.rs:157 -- the CoS/output-filter call
  passes tx_selection_flow.map(|flow| &flow.forward_key), i.e. the flow's
  forward_key, to resolve_cos_tx_selection_at().
- forward_key is the ORIGINAL/pre-NAT tuple: SessionFlow.forward_key
  (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/mod.rs:231). The POST-NAT wire tuple is produced
  by forward_wire_key(forward_key, nat) (userspace-dp/src/session/key.rs:28),
  which every other production consumer applies to derive the on-wire key
  (session/mod.rs:1234, afxdp/flow_cache.rs:611, afxdp/shared_ops.rs:880,
  afxdp/bpf_map/mod.rs:84). forward_request.rs is the outlier that does NOT
  apply the NAT transform.

Filter evaluation reads the pre-NAT fields verbatim:
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/cos_classify.rs:382-393
  (evaluate_filter_ref_tx_selection_runtime_counted) matches on
  flow_key.src_ip / dst_ip / protocol / src_port / dst_port -- the pre-NAT key.

NAT64 makes it worse (wrong-family filter):
- cos_classify.rs:305 selects the v4-vs-v6 output filter by meta.addr_family
  (the INGRESS family). For a NAT64 flow the egress family differs, so the v4
  output filter is evaluated against the v6 key (and vice versa) -- both the
  filter table and the key are the wrong family.

## Junos basis

An interface `filter output` is applied by the PFE as the packet egresses --
after flow-module NAT (DNAT pre-route, SNAT post-policy). The source/destination
addresses/ports an output filter sees are the translated (NAT-pool / static /
DNAT) values, i.e. the packet as it leaves the box. Matching on the pre-NAT tuple

finding), verified against origin/master ae1d0631c.

The operator-facing verdict rendered for an unmatched `to-zone junos-host`
match-policies query says local delivery "proceeds" / is delivered, which is
MISLEADING after #3405. Post-#3405 a security zone with interfaces but NO
`host-inbound-traffic` stanza DEFAULT-DENIES host-bound traffic
(vSRX parity; pinned by
`pkg/dataplane/userspace.TestNoStanzaZoneDefaultDeniesBothSurfaces`). So for a
no-stanza zone the packet is DROPPED by the host-inbound default-deny, yet the
diagnostic tells the operator delivery proceeds.

The policymatch simulator only models the transit/global/default policy
precedence and the #3285 host-gate (no transit fallback for junos-host). It does
NOT model host-inbound-traffic service admission, so it cannot assert that
delivery proceeds — the honest verdict is that delivery is SUBJECT TO
host-inbound-traffic service admission (default-deny for a no-stanza zone).

Enforcement is CORRECT (nft + Rust deny); only the diagnostic message is wrong.

- `pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go` `HostInboundActionString` (REST + gRPC

  `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_firewall.go`, `pkg/cli/cli_show_security.go`,
  `pkg/cli/cli_request.go`:
  `"host-inbound: local delivery proceeds (transit global/default-policy NOT applied)"`

## Dedup

- #3285 introduced the current wording (no-transit-fallback host gate) and
  addressed the "read as final permit" concern (#3627 M05). It predates the
  #3405 default-deny understanding, so its "local delivery proceeds" wording is

  overflow sets `overflow_active` (documented, same as cold-path).
- Two direct-index `u64` writes per forwarded packet on the existing per-worker

- **Flood is NEW drop-path accounting**, not a snapshot of existing state — the

## #3653 — api,grpc,docs: host_inbound_configured + comments + README + tests still encode pre-#3405 no-stanza admit-all (posture bit disagrees with dataplane default-deny) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

#3405 flipped host-inbound enforcement so that EVERY configured security
zone is host-inbound-ENFORCING (Junos default-deny parity): a zone with no
host-inbound-traffic stanza now default-DENIES host-bound traffic. The
dataplane posture bit was updated accordingly:

    pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:495
        zs.HostInboundConfigured = true   // unconditional for every configured zone

interface override):

dataplane enforces default-DENY (HostInboundConfigured=true), while the
REST/gRPC API reports host_inbound_configured=FALSE. Per the API's own
comments that FALSE means "admit-all" — the exact OPPOSITE of runtime.

when it is actually fail-closed.

## #3655 — remote-cli: match-policies still prints 'local delivery proceeds' for unmatched host-inbound (residual of #3647) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: High. review: codex-review-123 H10

## Problem

#3647 (issue #3646) corrected the host-inbound match-policies verdict string
for the local CLI / REST / gRPC paths via the SSOT const
policymatch.HostInboundActionString — "host-inbound (local delivery subject
to host-inbound-traffic service admission — a zone with no host-inbound-traffic
stanza denies by default; transit/global/default policy not applied)".

The REMOTE cmd/cli client was NOT updated and still hard-codes the old,
false-positive wording:

    cmd/cli/show.go:1144-1148
        } else if resp.HostInboundUnmatched {
            fmt.Printf("No matching to-zone junos-host policy for %s -> junos-host\n", req.FromZone)
            fmt.Printf("  host-inbound: local delivery proceeds (transit global/default-policy NOT applied)\n")

For a no-stanza zone (now default-DENY per #3405), and for any zone where
host-inbound service admission denies, "local delivery proceeds" is an
allow/deny diagnostic false positive on a core firewall troubleshooting
workflow. The corrected wording is already referenced in
pkg/grpcapi/README.md:94-100.

## Concrete fix

Reuse policymatch.HostInboundActionString in cmd/cli (or have the server
provide the action text and render it verbatim) instead of hard-coding.
This is distinct from #3627 (server-side queried-zone context) — this is a
pure client-render residual. Add a golden test for the remote match-policies
host-inbound-unmatched case.

## #3656 — userspace-dp: reject reply TX-budget + rate-limit token consumed BEFORE reply feasibility is known (unreplyable frames drain the shared REJECT_BUCKET / mis-attribute budget drops) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: High. review: codex-review-123 H11/H12

## Problem (NOT fixed by #3615)

#3615 reordered the reject EVENT emit (enqueue-first-then-emit) and split the
suppression counters by source, but it did NOT reorder the token-bucket /
TX-budget accounting relative to reply BUILD feasibility. On current master
enqueue_reject_reply runs in this order:

    userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs
      225  if !syn_cookie_reply_budget_available(...) {        // TX-frame budget gate
      231-234  counters.{policy,filter}_reject_reply_budget_drops += 1   // counted here
             return false;
      250  if !allow_generated_error(GeneratedErrorReason::Reject) {     // token CONSUMED here
             return false;
      255  let bytes = build_reject_rst_frame / build_reject_icmp_unreachable(...)
      260  let Some(bytes) = bytes else { return false; };     // FEASIBILITY known only here

So for a frame that can never produce a reply (inbound TCP RST, inbound
ICMP error, non-first fragment, unparseable frame, ingress without a primary
of the inbound family):

- H11: a token is consumed from the shared REJECT_BUCKET at line 250 before
  the code discovers at line 260 that no reply can be built. A flood of
  unreplyable frames drains the bucket and silently downgrades LEGITIMATE
  subsequent rejects to drops — a cheap DoS against active reject behavior.
- H12: if the TX budget is exhausted, the drop is attributed to
  policy/filter reply_budget_drops at line 231-234 for a reply that could
  never have existed anyway — mis-attributing malformed/unreplyable traffic
  as queue pressure and hiding the true attack shape.

## Concrete fix

Move reply-build feasibility (build_reject_* -> Some(bytes)) BEFORE both the
TX-budget accounting and the token consumption. Only consume the token /
count a budget drop once Some(bytes) confirms an actual reply exists (and
before enqueue). If preserving queue-protection ordering is required, split
the counters into reply_budget_drops (real budget pressure on a buildable
reply) and reply_not_possible_drops (unreplyable). Add Rust tests for
inbound RST, inbound ICMP error, non-first fragment, and malformed frames

*(truncated — 48 lines total)*

## #3657 — observability: reject sent/reply-budget counters absent from 'show status' (docs contract violation) + Prometheus only aggregate (no source split) + no tests [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: High. review: codex-review-123 H13/H14/H15/M02/M08 (+ L04 note)

## Problem

The helper tracks per-source reject counters that the operator surfaces do
not fully expose:

    pkg/dataplane/userspace/protocol.go:2299-2313
        PolicyRejectSent, FilterRejectSent
        PolicyRejectReplyBudgetDrops, FilterRejectReplyBudgetDrops
    reject_reply.rs:225-330 increments all of the above

### H13 - show status omits the SENT counters
pkg/dataplane/userspace/format/status.go declares/aggregates only the
*OutputFilterDrops legs (lines 149-157, 252-253) and the
"Generated-reply drops" line (476-479) prints time_exceeded / policy_reject /
filter_reject / syn_cookie / ptb / classify_parse_errors OUTPUT-FILTER drops.
policy_reject_sent / filter_reject_sent are never aggregated or printed
(grep for "sent" in status.go shows only SYN-cookie + event-stream). An
operator cannot see active reject SUCCESS volume — as important as knowing it
was suppressed for validating vSRX-style reject under load.

### H14 - show status omits the reply-budget drops, contradicting the docs
PolicyRejectReplyBudgetDrops / FilterRejectReplyBudgetDrops are never
aggregated/printed either (only the SYN-cookie budget_drops are shown, at
status.go:459-461). But docs/junos-cli-reference.md:291-304 explicitly
promises "Suppression is counted per source in show ... status:
policy_reject/filter_reject under the Generated-reply drops line". This is a
direct observability contract violation — budget pressure during a flood is
exactly when the counter is needed.

### H15 / M02 - Prometheus exposes only the aggregate rate-limit drop
pkg/api/metrics_userspace.go:604 emits only
xpf_userspace_reject_rate_limited_total (status.RejectRateLimitedTotal,
descriptor metrics_descriptors.go:1031). No source-specific sent / budget /
output-filter series. The rate-limit drop counter itself is source-neutral
(icmp_ratelimit.rs: single global-per-reason bucket, no per-source state),
so alerting cannot tell policy-reject starvation from filter-reject
starvation, nor success from suppression.

## #3658 — cli: 'show security zones detail' policy summary omits applicable global policies + effective default-policy catch-all (says '(no policies)') [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: Medium. review: codex-review-123 M04/M05

## Problem

The zone-detail policy summary scans ONLY the zone-pair policy set and
prints "(no policies)" when a zone has no zone-pair rules:

    pkg/cli/cli_show_security_zones.go:148-180
        for _, zpp := range cfg.Security.Policies { ... if zpp.FromZone == name || zpp.ToZone == name ... }
        if totalPolicies == 0 { fmt.Println("    (no policies)") }

The runtime evaluator considers zone-pair, then GLOBAL policies, then the
default-policy catch-all. Two tiers are hidden from the zone-centric audit:

- M04: applicable global policies (cfg.Security.GlobalPolicies, possibly
  scoped by match from-zone/to-zone) can permit/deny traffic for the zone but
  are never scanned here. REST inventory already handles globals
  (pkg/api/security.go:256-261).
- M05: when no zone-pair policies exist, "(no policies)" hides the effective
  default-policy that actually decides unmatched transit. REST already
  surfaces a synthetic default-policy row (security.go:323-337,
  DefaultPolicySentinelID / DefaultPolicyName). For a firewall, "(no
  policies)" is materially different from "default-policy deny-all/permit-all".

## Concrete fix

In zone detail, after the zone-pair summary: (1) list applicable global
policies honoring scoped from/to-zone, marked as the global tier; (2) append
an explicit default-policy line (reuse dataplane.DefaultPolicyName +
policyActionStr(cfg.Security.DefaultPolicy), as REST does).

Note: distinct from #3630 (KILLed — default-policy STRUCTURED representation
was already unambiguous). This is the local CLI zone-detail text surface
showing the effective catch-all + global tier, not the structured repr.

Drive-class: driveable-bug (small feature-completeness gap; CLI-only).

## #3661 — observability: reject RATE-LIMIT drop leg still source-neutral (M02 Rust follow-up to #3657) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: Medium. Follow-up to #3657 (review: codex-review-123 M02, deferred Rust-side leg).

## Problem

#3657 surfaced the EXISTING per-source reject counters (`policy_reject_sent`
/ `filter_reject_sent`, `*_reply_budget_drops`, `*_output_filter_drops`) in
`show ... status` and Prometheus. But the reject RATE-LIMIT drop leg itself is
still source-NEUTRAL:

    userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs:250
        if !allow_generated_error(GeneratedErrorReason::Reject) { ... silent drop ... }

`allow_generated_error(GeneratedErrorReason::Reject)` is a single
global-per-reason token bucket (`icmp_ratelimit.rs`) with no per-source state.
When the bucket is empty the reply is silently downgraded to `deny` WITHOUT
attributing the drop to a security-policy `then reject` vs a firewall-filter
`then reject`. The `RejectReplySource` (Policy/Filter) IS in scope at that
call site — it is already used a few lines below to attribute
`policy_reject_sent` / `filter_reject_sent`.

The aggregate `xpf_userspace_reject_rate_limited_total` /
`status.RejectRateLimitedTotal` stays for back-compat, so alerting can see
that reject replies are being rate-limited, but cannot tell policy-reject
starvation from filter-reject starvation under a rejected-flow flood.

## Why deferred from #3657

#3657 was scoped GO-READ-SIDE (surface counters already on the wire). This
leg needs a NEW helper counter (Rust) + new wire fields + a Go read-side
surface, so it was split out to avoid colliding with the concurrent
`reject_reply.rs` work (#3656).

## Concrete fix

- Rust (`reject_reply.rs` + counters struct): at the `allow_generated_error`
  false branch, `match source { Policy => policy_reject_rate_limited += 1,
  Filter => filter_reject_rate_limited += 1 }`. Keep the aggregate
  increment (or derive the aggregate as policy+filter) for back-compat.
- Wire: add `policy_reject_rate_limited` / `filter_reject_rate_limited` to the
  helper `PerBindingCounters` (control.rs) and the Go `BindingStatus`

## #3669 — Remote 'show security zones' silently swallows GetPolicies RPC failure — zones print as policy-free on a control-plane error [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-125 (H03)

Severity: Medium (error-hygiene / observability)

## Summary
The remote CLI zone view discards the GetPolicies error and still prints a
success exit, so a transient/authorization RPC failure renders as "these zones
have no policies" instead of a loud partial-output warning.

pkg/cmd/cli/show.go (func (c *ctl) showZones), current source:
  cmd/cli/show.go:498
      polResp, _ := c.client.GetPolicies(c.ctx(), &pb.GetPoliciesRequest{})
  cmd/cli/show.go:536
      if polResp != nil { ... build "Policies:" refs ... }

The error is dropped with _. When GetPolicies fails, polResp is nil, the
"Policies:" reference section is silently empty, and showZones returns nil
(success). GetZones itself IS checked (cmd/cli/show.go:494) — only the policy
inventory call is swallowed.

## Impact
On a firewall a partial policy view should fail loud. Silent omission biases an
operator toward UNDERESTIMATING installed policy during incident response, and
hides a control-plane degradation. Automation scraping the command sees exit 0
with no policy refs and treats the zones as unprotected.

## Fix
Either return the GetPolicies error, or print an explicit
"warning: policy inventory unavailable: <err>" line and mark the policy
references as unavailable (not empty). For automation-facing use, failing the
command is the safer default; at minimum the degraded state must be visible.

Drive-class: driveable bug (small, localized to showZones).

## #3670 — Synthetic default-policy inventory row (REST + gRPC GetPolicies) omits default-policy-log state [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-125 (H06)

Severity: Medium

## Summary
default-policy-log (session-init / session-close) is a real, enforced feature:
  - config: cfg.Security.DefaultPolicyLogSessionInit /
    DefaultPolicyLogSessionClose (pkg/config/types_security.go:76-77;
    compiled at pkg/config/compiler_security.go:537-542)
  - dataplane snapshot: pkg/dataplane/userspace/builder.go:89-90 sets
    DefaultLogSessionInit / DefaultLogSessionClose, so the dataplane emits
    RT_FLOW logs for default-policy verdicts.

Both inventory surfaces synthesize a default-policy catch-all row but do NOT
populate its log fields, so the row reads as UNLOGGED while the dataplane logs:

  - REST: pkg/api/security.go:340-348 builds defRule with
    Name/Action/PolicyID/RuleID only — no Log / LogSessionInit / LogSessionClose.
  - gRPC GetPolicies: pkg/grpcapi/server_show_zones.go:307-314 builds the
    synthetic default PolicyRule with Name/PolicyId/RuleId only — no Log fields.
    (Configured rules DO set LogSessionInit at server_show_zones.go:188/264 and
    api/security.go:210-211 — only the default row is missing them.)

## Impact
Default-policy logging covers all fallback traffic not matched by an explicit
rule — the most security-relevant boundary. Inventory/audit tooling sees an
apparently unlogged default policy while the appliance is emitting default-deny
/ default-permit session logs.

## Fix
On the synthetic default row, set Log = (DefaultPolicyLogSessionInit ||
DefaultPolicyLogSessionClose), LogSessionInit = cfg.Security.
DefaultPolicyLogSessionInit, LogSessionClose = ...SessionClose, in BOTH
pkg/api/security.go and pkg/grpcapi/server_show_zones.go. Note the commit-time
"inert under default-policy" warning (compiler_validate_warn.go:869-908) — the
inventory should reflect the CONFIGURED log intent regardless.

Drive-class: driveable bug (additive; distinct from #3630 which was the
default-policy ACTION structured repr, not the LOG state).

## #3671 — Host-inbound zone view hides zone default-deny posture when ANY interface override exists (#3654 residual) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-125 (H08 / L03)

Severity: Medium (security-posture observability)

## Summary
The shared host-inbound presenter added in #3654 suppresses the zone-level
"default deny" posture line whenever the zone has any per-interface override,
even though non-overridden interfaces in that zone still inherit zone-level
default-deny.

pkg/config/host_inbound_view.go func (v HostInboundView) Render, current source:
  host_inbound_view.go:215
      if len(v.ZoneSystemServices) == 0 && len(v.ZoneProtocols) == 0 &&
         len(v.Interfaces) == 0 {
          lines = append(lines, ... "Host-inbound: default deny ("+
              HostInboundDenyReason(false, v.ZoneConfigured)+")")
      }

The len(v.Interfaces) == 0 clause means: if any interface override is present,
the zone-level default-deny line is NOT emitted. The render then prints only
"Host-inbound interface overrides:" (host_inbound_view.go:219-230).

## Repro
Zone with no zone-level host-inbound services/protocols; interface ge-0/0/0 has
an explicit override admitting ssh; ge-0/0/1 has NO override. Render output
shows the ge-0/0/0 override block but NOTHING about ge-0/0/1, and no zone-level
default-deny statement. The deny posture governing every non-overridden
interface is invisible.

## Impact
Host-inbound is a security boundary. A partial interface override should not
erase the visible default posture for the rest of the zone. This affects every
surface routed through the shared presenter (local + gRPC text + remote CLI).

## Fix
Emit the zone-level "Host-inbound: default deny (...)" line whenever the
zone-level service AND protocol lists are both empty, regardless of whether
interface overrides exist; then render the override blocks below it. (Drop the
len(v.Interfaces) == 0 clause from the guard and place the default-deny line
before the interface-overrides block.)

The gRPC PolicyRule already carries rich per-rule metadata (added by
#3336/#3623/#3624), but the remote CLI brief renderer prints only name /
description / raw addresses / action / hits. Security-relevant fields are
silently dropped in the default remote policy view.

source cmd/cli/show.go:564-575:

and count state when rule.Count is true even with zero hits. This mirrors the
local CLI brief/detail which already surfaces these.

## #3673 — Policy compiler unsupported-tail guard misses from-zone/to-zone collapsed onto a multi:true match leaf (reserved keyword swallowed as application ref) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-125 (M06)

Severity: Medium, Confidence: Medium-Low (adversarial parser edge)

## Summary
The #3142 tail-scan extension to validatePolicyMatchLeavesStrict rejects known
unsupported match keywords (dynamic-application / url-category /
source-identity) that collapse onto a multi:true match leaf's tail, but it does
NOT reject from-zone / to-zone appearing in that same tail. Those reserved
match keywords can then be swallowed as application operands.

pkg/config/compiler_policy_match.go:117-121:
    var unsupportedPolicyMatchLeaves = map[string]bool{
        "dynamic-application": true,
        "url-category":        true,
        "source-identity":     true,
    }
The tail scan (compiler_policy_match.go:170-176) only rejects tokens in that
map. The application compiler (compiler_security.go:672-679) then treats every
tail token as an application name:
    case "application":
        if len(m.Keys) >= 2 { pol.Match.Applications = append(..., m.Keys[1:]...) }

## Reachability (honest caveat)
- from-zone / to-zone ARE registered match siblings under GLOBAL policy match
  (schema_security.go:208-209), so a flat-set line under a global policy stops
  multi-absorption at from-zone and it becomes its own leaf — the global

## #3696 — policy-simulator query parser silently widens on missing selector value + ignores unknown/malformed tokens across all 4 CLI surfaces + gRPC ShowText (fail-closed strict parse) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

The policy-simulator query parsers on all four operator surfaces plus the
gRPC ShowText text bridge fail OPEN on malformed selector grammar: a
selector present without a value silently degrades to the wildcard, and an
unknown / misspelled selector token is silently ignored. Because the shared
matcher treats a zero port / empty protocol / nil icmp-type as "no
constraint", the operator gets a permit/deny verdict for a BROADER set of
traffic than they typed -- from a firewall diagnostic tool whose entire job
is to answer precisely which traffic a policy matches. This is a
security-diagnostic correctness gap: a typo silently widens the query.

The value-parsing layer was already hardened (ParsePort / ParseICMPValue /
ValidateProtocol, #3116 / #3108 / #3284 / #3679), but that inner validator
is never reached when the outer grammar drops the token. The session-filter
parser hit the EXACT same class of bug and was already fixed strictly in
#3439 (H5) via a takeValue helper + a default error arm
(cmd/cli/show.go:766-783, parseFlowSessionArgs). The policy simulators were
not given the same treatment.

## Missing-value silently widens (selector present, no value)

Every value-taking selector is guarded by `if i+1 < len(args)` with no
else, so a trailing selector leaves the field at its zero/empty wildcard:

- Local `show security match-policies`: pkg/cli/cli_show_security.go:358-423
- Local `test policy`: pkg/cli/cli_request.go:184-255
- Remote `show security match-policies`: cmd/cli/show.go:1174-1255
- Remote `test policy`: cmd/cli/main.go:447-523

Example: `show security match-policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust
destination-port` -> dstPort stays 0 -> the simulator evaluates ALL
destination ports and prints a verdict for a port the operator never
specified.

## #3697 — userspace-dp: Rust host-inbound hot-path comments still say no-stanza zone admits-all (stale post-#3405/#3653 default-deny) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

Three Rust host-inbound comments in userspace-dp still describe the
pre-#3405 semantics where a configured zone with no `host-inbound-traffic`
stanza is left absent from the snapshot and admits all host-bound traffic.
That is no longer true: after #3405 / #3653 the Go control plane sends
`HostInboundConfigured=true` for EVERY configured zone (a no-stanza zone
ships an empty token set = default-DENY), so the "absent -> admit-all"
branch now applies only to zones that are not in the snapshot at all
(legacy / truly-unconfigured), not to a configured no-stanza zone. The API/
proto comments were corrected (pkg/api/types.go:126-140, #3328/#3405), but
the Rust hot-path comments were not -- a fail-open/fail-closed documentation
drift on a security boundary.

## Ground truth (Go control plane now marks every configured zone enforcing)

- pkg/api/security.go:70 sets `zi.HostInboundConfigured = true`
  unconditionally for every non-nil zone.
- pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:430-448 ships `HostInboundConfigured=true`
  with EMPTY token sets for a no-stanza configured zone.
- Pinned by pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_host_inbound_test.go:66-75
  ("#3405: trust declared NO stanza but is still HostInboundConfigured=true")
  and pkg/api/security_zone_hostinbound_3328_test.go:165-166.

## Stale comments to fix (userspace-dp)

- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/zones.rs:46-47 -- "Zones without a
  stanza are left absent -> admit-all (pre-#3070 behaviour)." Misleading: a
  configured no-stanza zone is NOT left absent post-#3405.
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/forwarding.rs:200-205 -- "an absent entry
  means admit-all (the pre-#3070 behaviour) for that zone." The wire-field
  semantics (absent = admit-all) is fine, but the surrounding premise that a
  no-stanza configured zone produces an absent entry is now false.
- userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1819-1820 -- "A zone with no
  host-inbound stanza admits everything (admit-all default), so existing
  configs are unaffected." This is now flatly wrong: a configured no-stanza
  zone default-DENIES host-bound traffic (empty token set), it does not

## #3698 — host-inbound: addressless configured/enforcing zone has a silent transient admit window (no deny until an address appears) — add observability [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

A configured, enforcing host-inbound zone whose interfaces have no static
config address and no live kernel address yet (a DHCP WAN before its first
lease, or a backup node before VIP install) yields an empty address set, so
the daemon emits NO scoped nft deny for it until an address appears. During
that window host-bound packets to a freshly-usable address can reach the
kernel input path without the intended zone default-deny. The window
self-heals once the address is installed (the lease-change / commit paths
re-render), but it is a transient fail-open on a security boundary that is
currently silent -- no warning, no counter.

## Evidence

- pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:84-92 documents the behavior explicitly:
  a configured zone with neither a static nor a live kernel address "yields
  an empty address set, the daemon emits no deny for it, and it self-heals
  once an address appears."
- The group is created lazily on its first address
  (pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:106-112), so a configured-but-addressless
  interface stays omitted (nothing emitted) until then.

## Why it matters

vSRX-style host-inbound default-deny is an enforcement invariant, not only a
steady-state property. DHCP acquisition, VIP install, and failover windows
are exactly when a security appliance gets probed. Even if the window is
accepted as unavoidable (an address-scoped nft deny cannot be installed
without an address), it should be observable.

## Fix direction

- At minimum (this issue): emit a warning event / counter for every
  configured, enforcing zone omitted from host-inbound scoping because its
  address set is empty, so the fail-open window is visible in logs/metrics
  even though it self-heals. Add a test that a configured no-stanza /
  enforcing zone with no address surfaces the warning.
- Optional (larger): consider an interface-scoped (not address-scoped)
  fail-closed nft drop during addressless windows where the interface is
  known but its address is not.

## #3699 — userspace-dp: AF_XDP ident-reset secondary local-delivery path DROPS instead of RESETS (vSRX-parity divergence, untracked after #3310 closed) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

Junos `system-services ident-reset` actively RESETS inbound ident (TCP/113)
probes. The primary host-inbound path (kernel nft chain, for direct
host-bound traffic) does this correctly via `reject with tcp reset`
(pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:495-527, hostInboundReject / #3310, now CLOSED).
The AF_XDP secondary local-delivery path -- reached only when a
DNAT/static-NAT-to-113 rule delivers an ident packet to userspace-dp instead
of the kernel -- contributes NO admit rule for ident-reset, so `admits()`
returns false and the packet is silently DROPPED rather than reset
(userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:167-183). The code
documents this as an accepted divergence ("strictly better than the prior
plain admit") with a known home for a future secondary-path RST upgrade
(plan Option A), but there is no OPEN issue tracking it -- #3310 was closed
against the primary path, and codex reviews keep rediscovering the AF_XDP
drop.

## Evidence

- Kernel primary path (correct RST): pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:495-527.
- AF_XDP secondary path (silent drop, documented divergence):
  userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:167-183 ("this arm
  contributes NOTHING to the admit set ... dropping the rare AF_XDP-reached
  ident packet (a documented divergence from the kernel reset) ... a future
  secondary-path RST upgrade (plan Option A) has an obvious home").
- #3310 (CLOSED) fixed the primary path only.

## Why it matters

Behavior depends on which local-delivery path an ident packet takes: kernel
-> RST, AF_XDP edge -> silent drop. Even if the divergence is acceptable
(the AF_XDP path is an edge of an edge), it should be a TRACKED parity
decision with a regression test so reviews stop rediscovering it.

## Fix direction

Either implement a secondary-path RST action for ident-reset on the AF_XDP

the simulator returns an allow/deny verdict for a DIFFERENT packet than the
operator typed. For a tool whose entire job is to prove policy behavior, a
silent wrong-packet verdict is a correctness bug (fail-closed-on-ambiguity is

duplicate guard, so a repeated selector overwrites the prior value. FromZone
becomes the LAST value.

showTestPolicy — the "for kv := range strings.Split(params, \",\")" loop with

repeated key. fromZone becomes the LAST value.

REST match-policies (first-win): pkg/api/security.go matchPoliciesHandler —

config is active, but 400 once a config exists — inconsistent grammar
validation during the exact boot window monitors poll. Validate request grammar
before the cfg == nil verdict.

its views carries a single address in EITHER family. Host-inbound ENFORCEMENT,
however, is per-DESTINATION-ADDRESS and per-family (pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go
emitHostInboundZone emits "<fam> daddr <set> ... drop" separately for ip and
ip6). So a zone can be partially enforced while the observability says "all
good", and a per-family gap is invisible.

## #3711 — userspace-dp policy: malformed v3 literals + address-book prefixes silently dropped -> deny rules no-op under default-permit (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: HIGH (security fail-open). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-152 (H01, H02, H03, M02, M09, L05, L06, L13)

## Summary
The Rust policy snapshot parser silently drops malformed IP literals on the v3
literal path AND on the address-book prefix path. A dropped literal collapses the
side to MatchNone, so a deny rule stops matching and evaluation falls through to a
later permit / default-permit. This is the v3 sibling of the legacy-literal
fail-open already fixed for the source_addresses/destination_addresses field in
PR #3367 -- that fix was NOT extended to the v3 literal or address-book paths.

## Root cause (current origin/master 5d77dbde7)
The legacy path reports malformed tokens and fails the snapshot closed:

- userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:2111-2124 -- parse_legacy_address_set returns a
  malformed token, checked at :2147-2155 -> SnapshotIntegrityError::UnrepresentableLegacyAddress (#3367).

But the two sibling paths use the NON-reporting helper parse_literal_cidr_into,
which drops an unparseable token with no error:

- v3 literal path: userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:2108-2118 (source_is_v3_shaped ->
  parse_v3_literal_set) -> parse_v3_literal_set at :2480-2513 -> calls
  parse_literal_cidr_into at :2499.
- address-book path: userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:2079-2086 loops prefixes_v4 /
  prefixes_v6 through parse_literal_cidr_into at :2082/:2085.
- parse_literal_cidr_into at :2515-2552: the Err(_) arm pushes nothing and
  returns nothing when a token parses as neither IpNet, Ipv4Addr, nor Ipv6Addr.

Empty per-family vectors then collapse via from_v3_literals to MatchNone (not
MatchAny -- comment at :2076-2078). MatchNone matches no packet, so a
deny-with-that-source rule never applies.

The sentinel preflight at :2143 only catches the exact __unsupported_address__
token, NOT arbitrary malformed literals -- so a corrupt / mixed-version / direct
snapshot bypasses it. The comment at policy.rs:52-55 claims the v3 literal path
"already fails closed via the __unsupported_address__ sentinel", which is only
true for that exact token; arbitrary malformed v3 tokens are silently dropped
(H03 -- the implementation contradicts the documented invariant).

## #3712 — userspace-dp policy: invalid ICMP application field combinations accepted at Rust snapshot boundary -> icmp_code-without-type matches ALL ICMP; icmp_type on non-ICMP never matches (deny fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: HIGH (security fail-open / over-broad match). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-152 (H04, H05, M08)

## Summary
The Rust policy application parser accepts two semantically-invalid ICMP field
combinations and compiles them into wrong-behaving terms. Go strict validation
does not gate these at the app level (grep of pkg/config finds no
icmp-type-requires-icmp / icmp-code-requires-icmp-type check), so the Rust
snapshot boundary is the only backstop -- and it currently mishandles both.

## Bug A (H04): icmp_code without icmp_type -> matches ALL ICMP
- userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:1380-1408 (CompiledApplications::from_matches):
  a term is steered into icmp_constraints ONLY when app.icmp_type.is_some().
  With icmp_type=None and icmp_code=Some(3), the if is false, the exact-dst-port
  else-if is false (ICMP terms carry no ports), so it lands in the else -> a
  range_terms entry with EMPTY src/dst ranges = protocol-only match-ALL for ICMP.
- The icmp_code constraint is silently ignored; an intended narrow rule
  (type any, code 3) becomes match-all-ICMP. For a permit under default-deny this
  is a fail-open (permits more than authored).

## Bug B (H05): icmp_type on a non-ICMP protocol -> never-match -> deny fail-open
- parse_applications at policy.rs:3323-3358 carries icmp_type/icmp_code through
  for ANY protocol (:3345-3346).
- from_matches at policy.rs:1380 pushes the term into icmp_constraints under the
  NON-ICMP protocol (e.g. TCP) because icmp_type.is_some().
- matches at policy.rs:1500-1510: for a real TCP packet packet_icmp is None, so
  the icmp_constraints arm is skipped; the TCP protocol bucket has no other term,
  best stays None -> the term NEVER matches.
- A deny rule with protocol=tcp, dst-port 80, icmp_type=8 therefore never applies
  -> default permit admits TCP/80 (security fail-open).

## Runtime trace (reviewer reproduced with temp Rust tests that passed)
- icmp_code_without_type_matches_all_icmp: proto icmp, icmp_type=null,
  icmp_code=3, permit, default deny -> type 8/code 0 AND type 3/code 1 both match.
- non_icmp_term_with_icmp_type_never_denies_tcp: proto tcp, dst 80, icmp_type=8,
  deny, default permit -> TCP/80 admitted.

## Fix direction
In parse_applications (policy.rs:3323-3358), before pushing the ApplicationMatch:
- reject icmp_code.is_some() && icmp_type.is_none();
- reject (icmp_type.is_some() || icmp_code.is_some()) on a non-ICMP/non-ICMPv6

## #3713 — userspace-dp policy: duplicate rule_id / policy_id accepted -> shared hit counters + policy_id re-resolution aliasing (RT_FLOW/session identity corruption) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: HIGH (observability / identity integrity). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-152 (H06, M01, L14)

## Summary
The Rust policy snapshot parser has NO uniqueness guard for rule_id or policy_id,
even though it already hard-fails duplicate address-book IDs
(policy.rs:2073-2075). Duplicates corrupt hit counters, alias the RT_FLOW /
session / display join key, and let an existing session re-resolve to the wrong
policy.

Dedup note: this is NOT #3623 (convey policy_id 0 in the API), #3668 (convey
rule_id in match-policies output), #3395 (reorder-stable re-resolution map), or
#3709 (duplicate diagnostic SELECTORS). Those are display/conveyance/selector
work; none adds a duplicate-identity reject at snapshot parse.

## Root cause (current origin/master 5d77dbde7)
- rule_id source: stable_policy_rule_id at policy.rs:3235-3240 returns the wire
  snap.rule_id verbatim when non-empty, else from_zone->to_zone/name. Two rules
  can carry an identical explicit rule_id (corrupt / mixed-version) or an
  identical synthesized key (duplicate policy name in a zone pair).
- policy_id source: rule.policy_id = snap.policy_id verbatim (policy.rs:2241);
  no range/uniqueness check.
- shared counter: rule_hit_counter (policy.rs:1146-1156) is get-or-insert keyed
  by rule_id string -> two rules with the same rule_id share ONE
  Arc<PolicyRuleCounter>, so counter_snapshots() emits two rows with the same id
  and the same shared totals.
- last-writer-wins map: policy.rs:2393-2398 builds rule_id_to_policy_id by
  inserting each rule -> a duplicate rule_id overwrites the first rule's
  policy_id. A session admitted by the first rule then re-resolves (#3395 live-row
  refresh / RT_FLOW SESSION_CLOSE) to the SECOND rule's policy_id -> wrong policy
  attribution during incident response.

## Fix direction
In parse_policy_state_with_counters, preflight rule identities BEFORE allocating
counters or building PolicyRule entries (L14 -- otherwise the store observes
transient counters for a snapshot that is then rejected):
- reject a duplicate non-empty rule_id with a new SnapshotIntegrityError
  (mirror DuplicateAddressBookId);
- reject a duplicate non-sentinel policy_id (M01).
Add direct Rust tests for both duplicate cases.

## #3714 — userspace-dp policy: Rust per-application inactivity_timeout not capped to the Go/vSRX bound (86400s) -> effectively never-expiring sessions on corrupt/mixed-version snapshot [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: LOW (session-gc / state-retention boundary). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-152 (M03)

## Summary
The Rust policy app parser accepts any u32 inactivity_timeout; the Go compiler
caps application timeouts at 86400s. A corrupt / mixed-version snapshot can stamp
an effectively never-expiring idle timeout on a session, diverging session GC
from the commit-time contract and increasing state retention under attack or
config corruption.

## Root cause (current origin/master 5d77dbde7)
- Rust: parse_applications at policy.rs:3347-3352 does
  term.inactivity_timeout.filter(|&t| t > 0) -- collapses 0 to use-global but
  applies NO upper bound. Wire field is Option<u32>
  (protocol/security.rs:492-497).
- Go: pkg/config/compiler_applications.go:23 appTimeoutMax = 86400, enforced to
  [0, 86400] at :37 (parseAppTimeout returns false out of range).

## Runtime trace
Direct snapshot inactivity_timeout=4294967295 -> Rust accepts Some(4294967295)
-> a matching session gets an effectively never-expiring idle timeout.

## Fix direction
Enforce the same 86400 upper bound in the Rust parser (clamp or reject), ideally
via a shared generated protocol constant so the two sides cannot drift. Add a
Rust test asserting a >86400 wire value is capped/rejected.

  accepted silently.

## #3718 — host-inbound: nft rules are destination-address-only (no ingress-interface/VRF predicate) — duplicate firewall-local addresses / VRRP VIPs across zones or routing-instances collide order-dependently; no strict duplicate-local-address gate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Severity: HIGH (host-inbound is a security boundary)
review: codex-review-153 (H01, M02, M03, M04, M09, L07, L12, L15)

## Problem

The kernel host-inbound nft chain enforces admission with
destination-address-only rules and no ingress-interface / VRF / zone
predicate. Two security zones that resolve the SAME firewall-local address
(a duplicated interface address, a duplicated VRRP VIP, or the same address
reused in two routing-instances) produce two rule blocks keyed on the same
daddr, emitted in zone-sort order, and the earlier-sorting zone decides the
packet regardless of which zone/interface the traffic actually ingresses.
A config accepted by the strict compiler can therefore enforce the WRONG
zone's management-plane host-inbound policy (or the inverse: deny what the
owning zone opened).

## Evidence (origin/master 5d77dbde7)

- daddr-only renderer, no iifname/VRF match:
  pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:469-517 emitHostInboundZone —
  `daddr := family + " daddr " + nftAddrSet(addrs)`; every accept/drop is
  `<fam> daddr <addrs> ...`; the catch-all is
  `<fam> daddr <addrs> counter name "<n>" drop` (line 516-517).
- views emitted in zone-sort (signature) order:
  pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:283-303 (sort by signature, sig begins
  with zone name) → aaa before zzz for the same 192.0.2.1.
- IPv6 has the identical class — same renderer, addresses split by ':'
  (zones.go:144 addAddr, daemon_nft.go emits `ip6 daddr` the same way). [M02]
- VRRP VIPs are folded into the SAME per-zone address groups
  (zones.go:274-275 `for _, vip := range vg.VirtualAddresses { hostIPFromCIDR }`),
  and validateVRRPVirtualAddressSubnet only checks on-link containment per
  unit — nothing rejects the same VIP in two zone scopes. [M03/L07]
- No strict duplicate-local-address validator exists: the only relevant gate
  is validateZoneInterfaceMembershipStrict (compiler_validate_strict.go:3439+)
  which enforces zone OWNERSHIP uniqueness, not ADDRESS uniqueness, so two
  unique interfaces in two unique zones carrying the same IP compile clean. [M09]
- Single global `inet xpf_hostinbound` input chain (daemon_nft.go:403-419),
  so routing-instance address reuse also collapses to a global daddr
  singleton — the first rule for that address wins across VRFs. [M04]

## #3719 — zone-id: lenient StableZoneID collisions still publish BOTH colliding zones to the userspace wire; Rust helper accepts duplicate zone IDs and overwrites id-keyed state; reverse maps + warning wording contradict runtime [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: HIGH (zone-identity isolation; upgrade/HA-sync fail-open)
review: codex-review-153 (H02, H03, M08, L04, L09, L13)

## Problem

#3075/#3704 moved the whole zone-id namespace to the STABLE name-hash
config.StableZoneID (FNV-1a fold into [1,65533]) and the strict commit path

(CompileConfigLenient / peer-sync / tolerant load of a config an older,
pre-#3075 binary persisted) only WARNS — and every downstream builder still
publishes both colliding zones with the same numeric id. The runtime
contradicts the warning and merges two security zones.

  populate_zones does `zone_id_to_name.insert(zone.id, ...)` and
  `zone_host_inbound.insert(zone.id, ...)` — the later zone overwrites the
  earlier's reverse name, host-inbound set, TCP-RST bit, and counters. Both
  names' interfaces/policies resolve to one numeric zone. [H03]
- Reverse maps are lossy/nondeterministic under collision:
  pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:1157-1169 zoneNameByID returns the
  FIRST map-iteration match; pkg/cli/apply.go:31-37 syslogZoneNameMap
  overwrites `znMap[StableZoneID(name)] = name` — RT_FLOW/syslog/session-sync

- No runtime status/metric advertises an active colliding-id config. [L09]
