## #3720 — host-inbound: physical-vs-unit override precedence is first-writer-wins — a less-specific physical ref shadows a more-specific unit override (and leaks cross-zone on lenient load); presentation/API use exact-ref lookup and miss the inherited physical->unit expansion [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: HIGH (enforcement) + MEDIUM (observability drift)
review: codex-review-153 (H04, H05, M01, M07, L05, L08, L11, L14)

## Problem — enforcement (H04)

buildInterfaceHostInboundMap expands a physical host-inbound override
(e.g. `interfaces reth0 host-inbound-traffic ...`) onto every configured
unit, using FIRST-WRITER-WINS. Refs are visited in sorted order, so the
bare physical `reth0` sorts before `reth0.10`, expands to fill
out["reth0.10"], and the later, MORE-SPECIFIC exact unit override
`reth0.10` is then skipped because the key already exists. The less
specific physical ref silently wins over the more specific unit ref.

## Evidence (origin/master 5d77dbde7)

- pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:451-474 buildInterfaceHostInboundMap:
  sorted refs; for a physical ref `if _, ok := out[ref]; !ok { out[ref]=hib }`
  then expands units `if _, ok := out[un]; !ok { out[un]=hib }`. The later
  exact `reth0.10` hits `if _, ok := out[un]; !ok` == false → dropped. [H04]
- Lenient cross-zone leak: on the lenient multi-zone-ownership warn path
  (compiler_validate_strict.go:3430-3438 downgrades ownership conflicts to a
  warning), a physical `reth0` override owned by zone trust expands onto
  `reth0.20` owned by zone guest, so guest inherits trust's tokens via
  overrideByIface["reth0.20"]. [M01]
- Presentation uses EXACT-ref lookup only:
  pkg/config/host_inbound_view.go:71-88 InterfaceHostInboundEffective(ref)
  reads `z.InterfaceHostInbound[ref]` with no physical->unit inheritance;
  pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces.go:303-310 calls it per logical unit. So
  `show interfaces reth0.10` reports "no override / default-deny" while the
  dataplane admits the inherited physical override — the exact diagnostic used
  to prove why management traffic is admitted gives the OPPOSITE answer. [H05]
- REST/gRPC expose only raw authored refs, not the expanded/effective runtime
  overrides: pkg/api/security.go:71-78 and pkg/grpcapi/server_show_zones.go:69-76
  iterate SortedInterfaceHostInboundRefs() (raw), so clients cannot see which
  units inherit a physical override or whether a unit override was shadowed. [M07/L05]

## #3721 — perf(host-inbound): view grouping signature preserves token ORDER — semantically identical effective sets ([ssh ping] vs [ping ssh]) emit duplicate nft rule blocks + counters, inflating payload/apply time on large trunks [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: LOW (performance / nft payload bloat)
review: codex-review-153 (M06, L10)

## Problem

BuildZoneHostInboundViews groups interfaces by a signature that joins the
token slices in their SOURCE order, and unionHostInboundTokens preserves that
order, so two interfaces whose effective admission sets are semantically
identical but authored in a different order fall into DIFFERENT groups and
emit separate nft views / rule blocks / deny counters.

## Evidence (origin/master 5d77dbde7)

- pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:128
  `sig := zone + "\x00" + strings.Join(svc, ",") + "\x00" + strings.Join(proto, ",")`
  — order-sensitive signature.
- unionHostInboundTokens keeps zone tokens first in original order then
  appends override-only tokens (zones.go union helper) — no canonical sort.

## Runtime trace

1. Interface A effective set = [ssh ping], interface B = [ping ssh].
2. Sets are identical, signatures differ → two groups.
3. Builder emits two nft rule blocks + two deny counters instead of one.
4. A 500-unit trunk with mostly-identical services in varying authored order
   inflates nft payload size, `nft -f` replace time, and commit latency. [L10]

## Fix (driveable)

Use a CANONICAL sorted token set for grouping (dedup + sort before building
the signature) while preserving the operator's authored order only on display
surfaces. Add a benchmark for BuildZoneHostInboundViews +
buildHostInboundFilterPayload to guard against regressions on large configs.

Not a correctness bug on its own. Drive-class: driveable-perf.

## #3723 — firewall stateless filters lack the application-style cross-field semantic gate: port/tcp-flags/icmp on incompatible protocol compiles a never-match term -> deny fails OPEN [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: HIGH (security fail-open / vSRX-parity). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-154 (H01, H02, H03, M01, M02, M03)

## Summary
The stateless firewall-filter compile path accepts several cross-field
combinations that the Rust dataplane matcher can never satisfy, so a
"then discard" / "then reject" term silently becomes a never-match. Because an
xpf filter falls through to an implicit ACCEPT on no-match
(userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/eval.rs; see the #3427 no-catchall warning),
an unmatchable deny term FAILS OPEN — the traffic the operator tried to drop is
admitted by a later permit / the implicit accept.

The application validator already learned these invariants
(protocolIsPortBearing / protocolIsICMPFamily, #3373 / #3348 / #3506) and the
Rust application boundary is being hardened for the same class (open #3712).
The stateless firewall-filter path never received the equivalent gate.

## Root cause (origin/master fc6049c05)
No firewall-filter strict validator does a protocol-vs-match cross-field check.
The filter strict validators are protocol resolvability
(validateFilterProtocolsStrict, compiler_validate_strict.go:4037), match-value
parseability (validateFilterMatchValuesStrict:4157), unknown-from
(validateFilterFromMatchStrict:4565), flex-match, port-except, address-except,
address-literal, routing-instance conflict. NONE checks that a port requires a
port-bearing protocol, that tcp-flags requires TCP, or that icmp-type/code
requires ICMP.

compiler_firewall.go accumulates every field independently of protocol:
- protocol / next-header -> term.Protocols (compiler_firewall.go:275)
- destination-port -> term.DestinationPorts (:286), source-port (:305)
- icmp-type -> term.ICMPTypes (:323), icmp-code -> term.ICMPCodes (:331)
- tcp-flags -> term.TCPFlags (:338)

The Rust matcher then makes each field never-match on the wrong protocol:
- ports: port_match (matching.rs:310) tests the constrained set against the
  extracted L4 port; GRE/ESP/AH/OSPF/VRRP/SCTP present dst/src port = 0
  (only TCP/UDP carry extracted ports), so "from protocol gre; destination-port
  80" never matches.
- tcp-flags: per_packet_l4_matches returns false when protocol != PROTO_TCP
  (matching.rs:37).
- icmp-type / icmp-code: return false when the packet is not ICMP/ICMPv6

## #3724 — lo0 kernel nftables mirror: unknown terminating action maps to accept while the Rust filter compiler fails closed to Discard (mixed-version fail-open on the kernel-PRIMARY host-inbound chain), + routing-instance/log/counter/log-prefix gaps [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: MEDIUM (lead item is a mixed-version fail-open on the primary
host-bound enforcement path). Class: driveable. review: codex-review-154 (M08 lead; M04, M06, M07, M09; M05 doc-note)

The kernel lo0 nftables mirror (inet xpf_lo0, pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go) is the
PRIMARY enforcement of the lo0 input filter for ordinary host-bound traffic
(the XDP shim shunts that traffic to the kernel before userspace-dp sees it, per
the doc comment at compiler_validate_warn.go:985). A wrong verdict here is real
control-plane mis-enforcement. Several rendering/observability gaps:

## Lead (M08): unknown action -> accept, while Rust fails closed
- daemon_nft.go:1175-1177 maps any terminating action to nft accept, only
  overriding to drop for "discard" (and rendering reject specially above):
    action := "accept"
    if term.Action == "discard" { action = "drop" }
- The Rust filter compiler maps an unknown non-empty action string to
  FilterAction::Discard (userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs).
- Strict commit rejects unknown actions (validateFilterActionsStrict), so this
  is a tolerant-load / peer-sync / mixed-version hazard: a future/peer snapshot
  with a new action string would DROP host-bound traffic in userspace but be
  ADMITTED by the kernel-primary lo0 chain -- a fail-open on the control plane.
- Fix: make the lo0 renderer fail closed (drop) for an unknown non-empty
  action, or refuse to install the mirror with a loud warning, matching Rust.

## M04: routing-instance PBR term terminates-as-accept with NO operator warning
- daemon_nft.go:1103-1113 documents that a "then routing-instance <x>" lo0 term
  emits a terminating accept (the kernel input hook cannot route-select;
  userspace stays authoritative).
- validateLo0FilterKernelMirrorWarnings (compiler_validate_warn.go:1010+) warns
  for policer / dscp-rewrite / forwarding-class only -- routing-instance is not
  in the warning set. The operator is never told the PBR route-selection side
  effect is silently not honored on the primary host-bound path.
- Fix: add routing-instance to the lo0 mirror warning surface (verdict accepted,
  route selection not performed by the kernel hook).

## M06: mirrored log has no rate limiter
- daemon_nft.go:1130 emits a bare "log prefix ..." with no "limit rate". A
  permitted high-rate host-bound flow matching a logged lo0 term pushes every
  packet into kernel logging / journald -- control-plane log amplification /
  availability risk on a firewall.

## #3725 — pkg/appid tolerant-load port parsers mislabel sessions: tuple-fallback narrows out-of-range single port via uint16 cast (70000->4464) + accepts signed +80; catalog drops bad source-port -> unconstrained (over-broad stamp); reversed range silently never stamps [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: MEDIUM (correctness / security observability -- session labeling, not
policy enforcement). Class: driveable-bug (note legacy-eBPF parity tension).
review: codex-review-155 (H02, H03, M04, M05, M06, M07, L01, L02, L06, L07, L08)

All these live on the tolerant-load / stale-persisted / peer-sync path: strict
commit rejects the malformed specs (validatePortSpec, canonical unsigned
parsing), but a leniently-loaded typed config.Application still flows into the
AppID display/filter fallback and the AppID catalog. The four duplicated
port parsers each mishandle it differently.

## H02 (+ M05): tuple fallback portInSpec narrows via uint16 cast, accepts signed
- pkg/appid/runtime.go:266-278 portInSpec, single-port arm:
    v, err := strconv.Atoi(spec)
    return err == nil && uint16(v) == port
  strconv.Atoi("70000")==70000; uint16(70000)==4464, so portInSpec(4464,"70000")
  is true -- a real session to dst/src port 4464 is labeled as the malformed app
  (H02). And strconv.Atoi("+80")==80, so "+80" matches port 80 even though the
  canonical config parser rejects the signed form (M05).
- Note this path is post-#3428 (source-port is now threaded), so both source and
  destination fallback comparisons are affected.
- Fix: reuse the shared canonical port parser (ParseCanonicalUint) and require
  1 <= v <= 65535 before comparing; drop strconv.Atoi from the fallback.

## H03 (+ M06): AppID catalog discards a source-port parse error -> unconstrained
- pkg/appid/catalog.go:110-114 parses SourcePort and DISCARDS the error:
    srcLow, srcHigh, _ = parsePortRange(app.SourcePort)
  parsePortRange returns (0,0,err) on a bad spec (catalog.go:296-317), so the
  emitted CatalogEntry gets SrcPortLow=0, SrcPortHigh=0, which the Rust
  AppCatalog treats as an unconstrained source port. A custom app
  "protocol tcp destination-port 80 source-port 70000" then stamps ANY TCP/80
  flow as that app (over-broad -- fail-open labeling).
- This diverges from the tuple fallback (H03/M06): runtime.go:251-260 requires
  the source-port spec to match through portInSpec, so a bad source spec
  generally never matches there -- AppID-disabled says UNKNOWN while AppID-enabled
  stamps the app. Mode-dependent observability split.
- Fix: treat a bad source-port like a bad destination-port (skip the entry or
  error). The code comment says it mirrors legacy compileApplications, so this is
  a legacy-eBPF-parity choice (L07) -- if id parity must be preserved, separate
  id assignment from entry validity.

## #3726 — userspace-dp NAT: appPortsFromSpec turns a reversed application port range (200-100) into an exact low-port match [200] instead of a never-match sentinel -> SNAT/DNAT applies on a tolerant-loaded malformed app [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: MEDIUM (NAT match widening on the tolerant-load / peer-sync path).
Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-155 (H04, L03)

## Summary
pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat.go appPortsFromSpec (nat.go:561) expands an
application destination/source-port spec into concrete ports for NAT match
terms. For a range "lo-hi" it only expands when hi > lo; otherwise it returns a
single exact low port:

    if hi > lo { ...expand... }
    return []int{int(lo)}         // nat.go:582

So a REVERSED range "200-100" returns [200] -- an exact match on the low port --
instead of a never-match. (The equal case hi==lo legitimately returns [lo].)

## Consumers
- source-NAT application match terms: nat.go:443-460 area (buildSourceNATAppTerms
  feeds appPortsFromSpec, ~:455).
- destination-NAT application match terms: nat.go:794-833 area.

Both feed the returned ports directly into the NAT match term, so a malformed
reversed range makes the NAT rule translate traffic to the low port even though
the configured range is invalid and should fail closed.

## Threat model
Strict commit rejects lo>hi (pkg/config/compiler_applications.go range
validation), so this is the lenient-load / peer-sync backstop -- the same
accepted threat model as #3437 / #3446 / #3491. This is DISTINCT from:
- #3446 / #3450 (closed): DNAT DIRECT match destination-port wrapping / pool
  port validation -- those are the direct match/pool grammar, not the
  application-referenced port helper.
- #3437 / #3491 (closed): DNAT/source-NAT dropped the application source-port /
  ICMP constraints -- a different axis.

## Fix direction
Make appPortsFromSpec reject hi < lo (return nil so the caller emits the
existing never-match sentinel: source-NAT natNeverMatchPortRange / DNAT #3437
impossible-range sentinel), keeping hi == lo as an exact single port. Add SNAT
and DNAT regression tests for "200-100" (L03). Ideally fold into the shared
application-port parser (codex-review-155 L06 / the pkg/appid port-parser issue).

## #3730 — routing/PBR: kernel FBF ip-rule mirror silently ignores ALL L4/per-packet filter predicates (protocol, ports, port-except, tcp-flags, icmp, is-fragment, flex) -> over-steers or no-ops with no degraded signal [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-156 (H01, H02, M01-M07, M08, M10; H03 noted). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
The kernel policy-based-routing / filter-based-forwarding mirror (BuildPBRRules,
which programs ip rules so the kernel/XDP_PASS path also honours FBF
routing-instance terms -- see pkg/routing/rules.go:36-40) derives rules from
ONLY the DSCP + source/destination address/prefix-list of a filter term. It
never reads any L4 or per-packet predicate. The userspace filter engine
enforces all of them, so the two paths diverge silently.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
- buildPBRFromFilter reads term.DSCPs + term.SourceAddresses/SourcePrefixLists +
  term.DestAddresses/DestPrefixLists only: pkg/routing/rules.go:575-692. It never
  reads term.Protocols, term.SourcePorts, term.DestinationPorts,
  SourcePortsExcept/DestPortsExcept, term.TCPFlags, term.ICMPTypes,
  term.IsFragment, or FlexMatch.
- The userspace snapshot DOES carry every one of these:
  pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go:108-247 (Protocols, SourcePorts, DestPorts,
  SourcePortsExcept, DestPortsExcept, TCPFlags, IsFragment, ICMPTypes).
- The build-degraded error is emitted ONLY for a non-empty address except set
  (rules.go:785-789), a DSCP-0 match (rules.go:617-621), or the maxPBRRules
  overflow (rules.go:522-529). There is NO degraded path for an ignored L4
  predicate.

## Two concrete failures
1. OVER-STEER (fail-open widening). A term "from destination-port 443
   destination-address 203.0.113.10/32 then routing-instance blue" emits, via
   the src/dst cross-product at rules.go:675-689, an address-only rule
   "to 203.0.113.10/32 lookup blue". Port 443 is dropped -> SSH, DNS, ICMP and
   every other protocol to that host are steered into blue on the kernel path.
   No degraded error is returned to the caller.
2. UNDER-STEER (silent no-op). A term with ONLY an L4 predicate (e.g.
   destination-port 443, no DSCP/address) hits the "no ip-rule-compatible
   criteria" branch at rules.go:669-673: it warns and continues, emitting no
   rule AND no degraded error. The operator believes FBF is active.

## Daemon boundary (M08)
pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:1104-1110 only slog.Warn's the build-degraded error
and the apply error. There is no structured status/metric, so even the

## #3731 — routing: next-table and rib-group Apply swallow per-rule RuleAdd failures (return only clearErr) -> transient netlink error silently drops inter-VRF route-leak [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-156 (H04, H05). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
The next-table and rib-group ip-rule reconcilers clear the old rules first, then
best-effort add the desired rules -- but a per-rule RuleAdd FAILURE is only
logged and the function returns nil (the clear error only). After the up-front
clear has already removed the previously-working leak rules, a transient netlink
RuleAdd failure leaves inter-VRF route-leaking DOWN while Apply reports success
to the daemon. The #3430-hardened PBR path already does the right thing, so the
three sibling reconcilers are now inconsistent.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
- next-table: pkg/routing/rules.go:113-118 logs the RuleAdd error and continues;
  Apply returns clearErr only at rules.go:125.
- rib-group: pkg/routing/rules.go:272-274 (IPv4) and :288-290 (IPv6) log-only;
  Apply returns clearErr only at rules.go:299.
- Contrast, the correct pattern: PBR Apply aggregates clear/parse/add/overflow
  into errors.Join and returns it -- rules.go:379-433 (add-failure append at
  :423-425, return at :433). The clear() RuleDel failures are already joined too
  (rules.go:451-457) as part of #3430 H3.

## Impact
A single transient RuleAdd error (EEXIST from stale udev/kernel state, ENOBUFS,
a racing reconcile) after clear() -> the inter-VRF leak the operator configured
is silently gone, and neither ApplyNextTableRules/ApplyRibGroupRules nor the
daemon apply loop gets a non-nil error to log or retry on. Only an ephemeral
per-rule warn records it.

## Fix direction (driveable)
Mirror the PBR pattern in nextTableManager.Apply and ribGroupManager.Apply:
collect each RuleAdd failure with errors.Join and return non-nil while still
attempting every desired rule (forward progress preserved). Add
TestNextTableApplyAggregatesAddErrors / TestRibGroupApplyAggregatesAddErrors
(v4-only, v6-only, both-family) mirroring the existing PBR aggregation test.

## Severity
MEDIUM (silent loss of configured inter-VRF forwarding after a transient error).
Drive-class: driveable-bug.

## #3732 — ddns/surface-a: DHCP address source bypasses the IsPublicAddr public-address gate -> publishes RFC1918/CGNAT/ULA to public DNS [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-157 (H07). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
Surface A router/interface DDNS applies the ddns.IsPublicAddr safety gate to the
interface, static, and checkip address sources, but NOT to the DHCP source. A
WAN that learns a non-public DHCP address (CGNAT 100.64/10, RFC1918, ULA,
documentation, etc.) will publish that unroutable/reserved address to public DNS
via address-source dhcp -- the exact class the public-address invariant
(#2776 static, #2774 checkip ranges, #2975 temporary, #2840 transient) was built
to prevent.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
- DHCP branch returns the lease address with NO IsPublicAddr check:
  pkg/daemon/daemon_ddns_surface_a.go:289-307 (a := lease.Address.Addr().Unmap();
  returns AddressObservation{Addr: a} if a.IsValid()).
- Interface source IS gated: selectInterfaceAddr rejects !ddns.IsPublicAddr at
  pkg/daemon/daemon_ddns_surface_a.go:458.
- Static fallback IS gated: staticUnitAddr rejects !ddns.IsPublicAddr at
  pkg/daemon/daemon_ddns_surface_a.go:501.
- checkip IS gated internally: pkg/ddns/checkip.go:85 isPublicAddr in
  parseCheckIPBody.

## Impact
Per-interface router DDNS with address-source dhcp publishes reserved/private
addresses to authoritative public DNS -- a correctness/safety fail-open and a
minor information leak, inconsistent with every other Surface A source.

## Fix direction (driveable)
Run the DHCP lease observation through ddns.IsPublicAddr before returning a valid
observation (daemon_ddns_surface_a.go:303-307). A non-public lease should be a
definitive no-publish (or a warned skip) matching the static/interface behavior,
not a valid address.

## Severity
MEDIUM-HIGH (security fail-open: non-public address published to public DNS).
Drive-class: driveable-bug.

## #3733 — ddns/surface-a: checkip source-bind failure falls open to the default route -> publishes the wrong WAN's public IP (residual of #2846) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-157 (M04). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
#2846 added source-address/interface/VRF binding to the checkip probe so a
multi-WAN scope's checkip egresses from its own uplink. But if that bind fails,
the observer logs a warning and STILL runs the checkip probe with the UNBOUND
default client -- so the probe egresses via the kernel default route and returns
the DEFAULT WAN's public IP, which is then published as this scope's address.
This reintroduces the wrong-WAN publication class #2846 was meant to close, and
is a fail-open: checkip is an address oracle and must be fail-closed.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
pkg/daemon/daemon_ddns_surface_a.go:278-283
    client, berr := d.surfaceA.CheckIPClient(scope.Provider)
    if berr != nil {
        slog.Warn("...checkip source bind unusable; probing from default route",
            "provider", ..., "err", berr)
    }
    a, ok := ddns.CheckIP(ctx, client, scope.Provider.CheckIPURL, af4, allow)
CheckIPClient (pkg/ddns/surface_a.go:392) returns the unbound default client
alongside the bind error; the daemon proceeds to probe with it. The returned
public IP passes isPublicAddr and is published for the wrong scope.

## Impact
On a multi-WAN box, a transient bind failure (interface not up yet, address not
yet assigned, VRF churn) makes checkip report WAN1's public IP for a WAN2 scope,
publishing an inbound-reachability record that points at the wrong uplink.

## Fix direction (driveable)
For AddressSourceCheckIP, treat a bind-resolution failure as ok=false (transient,
no publish, never withdraw) or a visible per-scope no-publish error -- do NOT
fall back to the default route. The fail-open default may remain acceptable for
generic HTTP update backends, but the checkip oracle must be fail-closed.

## Severity
MEDIUM (security fail-open: wrong-WAN address published).
Drive-class: driveable-bug.

## #3734 — ddns/surface-a: seedFromStore and the renumber log read owned.Address (always empty for Surface A) instead of AddrText -> restart republish storm + missing replacement logs [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-157 (H04 + M02, same root). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
Surface A owned records store the DNS rdata in AddrText and leave the Address
field empty (Address is the DHCP-lease key that Surface A does not use). Two
places read the empty Address field instead of AddrText, so both silently no-op:
(H04) the restart cache seed, and (M02) the WAN-renumber replacement log.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
- ownedRecord for Surface A: pkg/ddns/surface_a.go:946 Address: "" (comment:
  "rdata lives in AddrText below"), :951 AddrText: addr.String().
- seedFromStore parses r.Address: pkg/ddns/surface_a.go:521-528
    a, err := netip.ParseAddr(r.Address)   // "" -> err -> continue
    if err != nil { continue }
    m.runtime[...] = &surfaceAState{lastAddr: a.Unmap()}
  So for every Surface A record ParseAddr("") errors and NOTHING is seeded ->
  rt.lastAddr stays zero after a restart.
- reconcileScopeLocked change-detection then sees changed = (addr != zero) =
  true on the first post-restart pass -> a redundant wire UPDATE for an unchanged
  address. This defeats the documented restart-suppression intent in the
  seedFromStore comment (surface_a.go:513-519). Codex probe
  TestCodexAuditSurfaceARestartDoesNotSuppressRedundantUpdate reproduced it.
- M02: prevAddr = prevOwned.Address at surface_a.go:936-938 (always "") so the
  "replaced record address" log at surface_a.go:1024-1026 never fires -- no
  operational evidence of a WAN renumber.

## Impact
Every daemon restart / failover generates a provider-write storm proportional to
the Surface A scope count (ban/rate-limit risk for the exact providers the cache
was documented to protect), and renumber events are invisible in the log.

## Fix direction (driveable)
Seed lastAddr from AddrText in seedFromStore, and read prevOwned.AddrText for the
replacement log. Consider also recording a restart baseline for lastPublished so
an unchanged record skips until the forced-refresh floor elapses from restart.

## Severity
MEDIUM (restart republish storm; provider ban/rate-limit risk).
Drive-class: driveable-bug.

## #3735 — ddns/surface-a: provider rename / in-place provider mutation orphans the old provider's DNS record (ownership stores only provider name; #2903 adoption guard drops old ownership without a wire delete) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

review: codex-review-157 (H01, H02, H03 -- same root). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
Surface A durable ownership carries only the provider NAME (ScopeKey.PolicyID),
not a backend delete-descriptor (server/zone/credentials). Any provider change
therefore loses cleanup authority over the record the OLD provider published:

- H01 (provider rename, same FQDN+addr): the #2903 FQDN-migration adoption guard
  drops the old-provider ownership WITHOUT a wire delete.
- H02 (in-place provider mutation, same provider name): publish overwrites the
  same ownership key with the NEW backend; nothing holds the old server/creds to
  delete the old record.
- H03 (removed-binding withdraw): backendForOwned rebuilds the backend from the
  CURRENT catalog, so a withdraw after a provider edit goes to the wrong
  endpoint/zone.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
- ScopeKey.PolicyID is the provider name only: pkg/ddns/state.go:119-125.
- Adoption guard keys liveRR on FQDN|AddrText with NO provider identity:
  pkg/ddns/surface_a.go:650-655; on a match it drops old ownership with only a
  debug log and no DeleteLease: surface_a.go:673-683 (m.state.delete at :680).
  Provider A (PolicyID=prov-A) and provider B (PolicyID=prov-B) are distinct
  scope prefixes, so after Pass 1 publishes prov-B for the same FQDN+addr, Pass 2
  sees prov-A ownership as not-configured but FQDN|AddrText-live -> drops it
  without deleting at provider A.
- Withdraw resolves the current catalog: backendForOwned at surface_a.go:1131-1147
  (prov := catalog[policyID] at :1139).

## Impact
Migrating the DDNS provider (or editing a provider's server/zone/creds in place)
can leave a stale live record at the old provider that xpf has forgotten -- the
same stale-record class the Surface A closeout was meant to prevent, hidden by
the FQDN-only migration guard.

## Fix direction (driveable-with-design)
Constrain the FQDN|AddrText adoption skip to the explicit legacy FQDN-less
migration case (or include provider/backend identity in the live key), AND store
enough delete metadata in ownedRecord (backend/server/zone) so a provider change
withdraws through the OLD backend before dropping old ownership -- or make
provider mutation a two-phase withdraw-then-mutate transition.

*(truncated — 45 lines total)*

## #3736 — ddns/surface-a: checkip observation runs blocking HTTP under SurfaceAManager.mu (residual of #2778) and ignores the reconcile/shutdown context [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-157 (H05, H06). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
#2778 moved provider Upsert/Delete off the manager mutex via providerIO, but the
per-scope ADDRESS OBSERVATION still runs under m.mu -- and for address-source
checkip that observation is a blocking external HTTP GET (up to 10s). It also
uses context.Background() instead of the reconcile/pass context, so it ignores
shutdown and the pass deadline.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
- Reconcile takes m.mu for the whole pass: pkg/ddns/surface_a.go:555-556.
- providerIO releases m.mu ONLY around one Upsert/Delete wire call:
  surface_a.go:538-542 (comment: "so a slow or hung provider must not block
  StatusViews/Stats").
- observe(sc) is called from reconcileScopeLocked WHILE m.mu is held:
  surface_a.go:747 (reconcileScopeLocked at :730, invoked under Reconcile's lock).
- For checkip, observe performs the HTTP GET: pkg/daemon/daemon_ddns_surface_a.go:
  278-283 (CheckIPClient + ddns.CheckIP), bounded by a 10s timeout at :254 which
  derives from context.Background(), NOT the reconcile rctx.
- StatusViews/Stats also lock m.mu (surface_a.go around :1241/:1355), so they
  block behind the checkip probe.

## Impact
With N checkip scopes and a black-holed checkip endpoint, the manager mutex is
held for up to N*10s, wedging StatusViews/Stats and any concurrent reconcile.
Shutdown/failover waits behind stale checkip probes because they do not observe
ctx cancellation. This violates the same lock-discipline #2778 established for
provider I/O.

## Fix direction (driveable)
Split observation from state mutation: collect checkip observations (with the
reconcile context) BEFORE taking m.mu, then reconcile decisions under the lock;
or wrap the observe call the way providerIO wraps Upsert/Delete. Thread
context.Context into AddressObserver so checkip inherits the pass/shutdown
deadline.

## Severity
MEDIUM (observability/latency: manager lock held across external HTTP).
Drive-class: driveable-bug.

## #3737 — ddns/dyndns2: explicit server URL parser is case-sensitive on scheme and skips host/scheme validation (unlike #2842 checkip / #2841 generic) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

review: codex-review-157 (H09, M05 -- same function). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
resolveDyndns2Endpoint decides whether the configured server is a full URL vs a
bare host using a case-SENSITIVE strings.HasPrefix on http:// / https://, and
does no host/scheme parse. #2842 fixed this exact class for checkip and #2841 for
the generic backend, but the dyndns2 endpoint parser was missed.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
pkg/ddns/backend_dyndns2.go:81-88
    if s := strings.TrimSpace(p.Server); s != "" {
        if strings.HasPrefix(s, "http://") || strings.HasPrefix(s, "https://") {
            return s, nil
        }
        return "https://" + s + "/nic/update", nil   // bare-host branch
    }
- H09: server = "HTTPS://updates.example/nic/update" fails the lowercase prefix
  check (URL schemes are case-insensitive, RFC 3986) -> treated as a bare host ->
  returns "https://HTTPS://updates.example/nic/update/nic/update" (malformed) ->
  first publish fails at runtime.
- M05: server = "http://" or "https:///nic/update" passes the prefix check and is
  returned verbatim (no host validation) -> UpsertLease url.Parse succeeds with an
  empty host and fails only at request time, unlike validateCheckIPURL /
  validateGenericURLTemplate which fail at commit.

## Fix direction (driveable)
Parse the server with url.Parse and compare Scheme with strings.EqualFold,
requiring a non-empty host for the full-URL case (mirror validateCheckIPURL).
Add a commit-time validation for dyndns2 server the way #2841/#2842 did for the
sibling backends.

## Severity
LOW (config error surfaced at runtime instead of commit; not a fail-open, but
inconsistent with the hardened checkip/generic validators).
Drive-class: driveable-bug.

## #3738 — ddns/surface-a: dual-stack same-name withdraw clears the sibling family (DuckDNS clear=true, dyndns2 offline=YES) -> blackhole; DuckDNS is commit-warned, dyndns2 is not [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

review: codex-review-157 (H10, M06 -- same root). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
Two backends have only a HOST-LEVEL (non-per-family) withdraw verb. When a
dual-stack same-name scope loses ONE family's address, Surface A withdraws that
family, and the host-level verb takes down BOTH families -> the still-configured
sibling family is blackholed. DuckDNS at least gets a commit-time dual-stack
warning (#2960); dyndns2 gets none.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
- DuckDNS: DeleteLease sets clear=true which removes BOTH A and AAAA:
  pkg/ddns/backend_duckdns.go:151-154 (comment at :143 "DuckDNS has no per-family
  clear: clear=true removes BOTH the A and the AAAA").
- dyndns2: DeleteLease sends offline=YES for the whole hostname (no per-family
  delete): pkg/ddns/backend_dyndns2.go:137-144 (offline=YES at :143). The
  compiler has a dual-stack warning for DuckDNS but NOT for dyndns2.
- Surface A withdraws per family on address loss: pkg/ddns/surface_a.go
  reconcileScopeLocked withdraw path (obs.Addr invalid -> withdrawOwnedLocked).

## Impact
Concrete sibling-family blackhole (not just the documented "two scopes fight on
update"): configure DuckDNS/dyndns2 on both inet and inet6 for one name; lose the
v6 PD; the v6 withdraw clears/offlines the whole hostname; v4 is blackholed until
the next v4 publish (and longer if that scope is skipped/backed off).

## Fix direction (driveable-with-design)
Promote dual-stack same-name on a host-level-withdraw backend to a HARD commit
error (or coalesce both family states into one update/clear decision per domain),
and add per-backend capability metadata (per-family update, per-family delete) so
the validator and engine can reason about it uniformly instead of ad-hoc warnings.
Add the missing dyndns2 dual-stack commit warning.

## Severity
MEDIUM (sibling-family DNS blackhole on dual-stack same-name).
Drive-class: driveable-bug with a design element (backend capability metadata).

## #3739 — ddns/surface-a: self-owned publish clobbers co-resident/foreign same-name records (Cloudflare upsert patches recs[0], Route53 UPSERT replaces RRSet, RFC2136 RemoveRRset deletes whole A/AAAA set) - no ownership marker/conflict detection [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

review: codex-review-157 (H11, M07, M08 -- same "self-owned clobber" root). Verified on origin/master fc6049c05.

## Summary
Surface A treats a configured name as exclusively self-owned by CONVENTION, but
three backends will silently overwrite/replace a co-resident or foreign
same-name record with no ownership marker or conflict detection.

## Evidence (current origin/master)
- Cloudflare (H11): findRecord returns recs[0] when NO content matches
  (pkg/ddns/backend_cloudflare.go:216), and UpsertLease then PATCHes that row's
  content to xpf's address (backend_cloudflare.go:248). So a manual/foreign
  "name A 198.51.100.10" is silently rewritten to xpf's address. (The DELETE path
  is already content-scoped; upsert is the residual.)
- Route53 (M07): buildChangeBatch appends ONE ResourceRecord with action UPSERT
  (backend_route53.go:133-149; UpsertLease at :191-192). Route53 UPSERT replaces
  the ENTIRE RRSet at name+type -> co-resident same-type values from another
  appliance/manual config are dropped.
- RFC2136 self-owned (M08): the self-owned A/AAAA path does RemoveRRset (deletes
  the ENTIRE RRset of that type at the name, CLASS=ANY) then Insert one value:
  backend_rfc2136.go:625, :800-804. The existing safety comment only guarantees a
  DIFFERENT record TYPE is untouched; co-resident SAME-type values are clobbered.

## Impact
A firewall appliance silently rewrites/removes a pre-existing foreign or
co-resident DNS record whenever the operator points Surface A at a name that
already has records -- surprising and potentially service-affecting.

## Fix direction (design-leaning)
For Cloudflare, POST when no owned/matching record exists and refuse/flag a
conflict when a different row already exists (do not blind-PATCH recs[0]). Across
backends, add an optional ownership marker (Cloudflare comment/tag, RFC2136
DHCID/TXT) or a first-publish "no existing name unless replace-existing is
configured" guard, and document/guard the Route53 whole-RRSet replacement.

## Severity
MEDIUM (silent clobber of foreign/co-resident public DNS records).
Drive-class: driveable-bug (Cloudflare upsert) plus design hardening (Route53/RFC2136 ownership).

After #2461 (per-flow-server template grouping) and #2462 (multi-instance

- Each exporter keeps its own private sequence counter starting at 0

The daemon spins up one exporter per group/instance:
pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:208-234 (v9) and :292-311 (IPFIX).

   explicitly supported config shapes after #2461/#2462 and pass the strict
   validator (pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict.go allows family/version-
   disambiguated instances).
2. The resolver correctly emits two template groups / two ExportConfigs.
3. The daemon starts two exporters. Both advertise template IDs 256 and 257

## #3741 — flowexport: Prometheus xpf_flow_export_collector_* uses only {protocol,collector} labels -> duplicate labelset (breaks scrape / hides failing group) when multiple template groups/instances/source-binds share a collector [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

The Prometheus flow-export collector-health family uses only {protocol,
collector} labels, but the daemon can return MULTIPLE health rows for the same
(protocol, collector) pair -- one per template group, per family-disjoint
instance, or per distinct source-address bind. Emitting two ConstMetrics with
an identical descriptor + identical labelset either fails the scrape
(duplicate-series error) or silently collapses the failing group, so a partial
flow-export failure becomes unattributable or breaks the whole scrape.

## Evidence (current origin/master)

- pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:461-488 -- FlowCollectorHealth() annotates
  each row with Protocol, Instance, Template (plus CollectorHealth.Address).
- pkg/api/metrics_descriptors.go:1701-1726 -- all five
  xpf_flow_export_collector_* descriptors declare labels {"protocol","collector"}.
- pkg/api/metrics_system.go:134-156 -- collectFlowExportMetrics emits each
  metric with only (h.Protocol, h.Address); Instance/Template are dropped.
- pkg/flowexport/transport.go:137 -- CollectorHealth.Address is set to
  c.Address only (no source-address).

## Runtime trace

1. Two v9 template groups (or two family-disjoint instances) use the same
   collector address.
2. FlowCollectorHealth() returns two rows: same Protocol+Address, different
   Instance/Template.
3. collectFlowExportMetrics calls prometheus.MustNewConstMetric twice on the
   same descriptor with the identical {protocol,collector} labelset.
4. The registry rejects the duplicate -> the scrape errors out (or, depending
   on the gather path, one row silently wins). A failing template group is
   invisible.

## Fix

Add instance, template, and source_address to the descriptor label set and the
emit call (bounded cardinality -- one series per configured flow-server group),
OR aggregate the rows intentionally with documented semantics. Extend the
descriptor-coverage canary (#1726) to assert the label set.

## #3742 — flowexport: reconcile stops old exporters BEFORE building new ones -> transient NewExporter failure disables export + SESSION_CLOSE in the cancel->swap window is silently lost [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

reconcileV9Exporter / reconcileIPFIXExporter STOP and close the old exporters
BEFORE constructing the new ones. This creates two problems on every
flow-export config change:

1. A transient NewExporter failure (e.g. a pinned source-address bind before
   the source interface is up, or transient collector DNS) tears down the
   healthy running exporters and leaves flow export DISABLED until the next
   commit -- an observability outage where the old config could have kept
   running.
2. A SESSION_CLOSE callback that fires in the window between "old Run goroutine
   stopped" and "new bundle stored" reads the OLD bundle, queues the record
   into the OLD exporter's batch, and that batch is never flushed (its Run
   goroutine already returned) -- the record is silently lost.

## Evidence (current origin/master)

- pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:183-191 -- flowCancel() then flowWg.Wait()
  then exp.Close() then d.flowExporters=nil. The old bundle in d.flowBundle is
  NOT cleared here; it stays published.
- daemon_flowexport.go:208-230 -- new exporters are built AFTER the stop; on
  NewExporter error it rolls back the new set, stores an empty bundle, sets
  flowHashSet=false and returns (old exporters already gone).
- daemon_flowexport.go:232-234 -- the new bundle is stored only after all new
  exporters succeed.
- daemon_flowexport.go:352-403 -- flowExportCallback reads d.flowBundle
  lock-free and calls ExportSessionClose.
- pkg/flowexport/netflow.go:565-611 -- ExportSessionClose only appends to the
  batch; only Run drains it (netflow.go:659-668), and Run has already returned.
- IPFIX path is structurally identical (daemon_flowexport.go:269-311).

## Fix

Build and validate the FULL replacement exporter set first. Only after every
new exporter constructs successfully: atomically swap d.flowBundle to the new
set, THEN cancel + wait + close the old exporters. This closes the loss window
(the bundle always points at a live, flushing exporter) AND preserves the
running exporters when a replacement build fails. Add a race test with a
callback firing during reconcile.

*(truncated — 48 lines total)*

## #3743 — flowexport: route-mask RTM_GETROUTE runs synchronously inside the EventReader session-close callback -> netlink latency stalls the event reader + all callbacks under dest churn [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

Route-mask resolution (#2866) issues an RTM_GETROUTE netlink syscall
SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the EventReader session-close callback path. On a cache
miss, kernel/netlink latency directly stalls the event reader and every other
callback behind it (including the trace writer). High-cardinality destination
churn turns close-event handling into a netlink-bound path.

## Evidence (current origin/master)

- pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:397-399 -- flowExportCallback calls
  ExportSessionClose directly from the EventReader callback (runs on the event
  reader's processing goroutine).
- pkg/flowexport/netflow.go:581 / ipfix.go:596 -- resolveMasks is called while
  building the record, i.e. inside ExportSessionClose, i.e. inside the callback.
- pkg/flowexport/routemask.go:96 -- resolve() calls c.lookup(ip) on cache miss.
- pkg/flowexport/routemask.go:151-153 -- lookup is netlink.RouteGetWithOptions
  (RTM_GETROUTE, synchronous).

The 10s TTL cache (routeMaskCacheMax=8192) bounds the syscall RATE, but a
cache miss is still a synchronous netlink round-trip on the hot close path, and
under high dest cardinality the cache thrashes (see the clear-all eviction
concern, filed separately). This is exactly the per-event heavy work the
project logging/hot-path rules warn against.

## Fix

Move route-mask resolution off the EventReader callback: resolve it in the
exporter's own Run goroutine (records already carry SrcIP/DstIP into the
batch), or pre-resolve asynchronously with bounded work, or carry the matched
route prefix from xpf's own forwarding resolution instead of a kernel query.

## Severity

Medium. Adds unbounded netlink latency to the shared event-reader path under
churn -> can back up SESSION_CLOSE processing and drop events. Driveable.

review: codex-review-158 (H10)

## #3744 — flowexport: route-mask FIB lookup is VRF/routing-instance/table/source blind (queries the main table) and discards the ok bit -> wrong srcMask/dstMask in VRF/PBR deployments, unresolved indistinguishable from /0 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

## Summary

Route-mask attribution (#2866) queries the kernel FIB in the DEFAULT lookup
context: no routing table, VRF link, fwmark, or source address. For any flow
forwarded in a VRF / routing-instance / PBR-selected table, the exporter
resolves the mask against the MAIN table and exports a srcMask/dstMask that
looks authoritative but is wrong. It also throws away the resolver ok bit, so
an unresolved lookup is indistinguishable from a real default-route (/0) match.

## Evidence (current origin/master)

- pkg/flowexport/routemask.go:151-153 -- netlink.RouteGetWithOptions(ip,
  {FIBMatch:true}) with no Table, Iif/Oif, Mark, or Src.
- pkg/logging/eventbuf.go EventRecord and pkg/flowexport/manager.go
  SessionCloseData (:739-779) carry zones/ifindexes/NAT but NO
  routing-table/VRF/routing-instance field, so the resolver has nothing to
  scope the lookup with; InIf/OutIf (manager.go:756-772) are not passed to the
  resolver either.
- pkg/flowexport/routemask.go:137-144 -- resolveMasks discards the (mask, ok)
  bool; a miss returns srcMask/dstMask 0, identical to a legitimate /0 match.
  routemask.go:22-25 documents that ok is meant to distinguish these.

## Runtime trace

1. A flow is forwarded in a routing-instance/VRF or via a PBR table.
2. SESSION_CLOSE carries only IPs/zones/ifindexes.
3. resolveMasks asks the kernel for the route to src/dst in the default context.
4. The kernel returns the MAIN-table match, not the table that forwarded the
   flow. NetFlow srcMask/dstMask (IE 9/13, IPv6 29/30) are wrong but look real.

## Fix

Carry the forwarding table / routing-instance (or the matched route prefix)
onto the SESSION_CLOSE event and scope the netlink lookup (Table/Iif/Src), or
derive masks from xpf's own routing resolution. Separately, preserve the ok bit
and expose a route-mask-miss counter so unresolved is distinguishable from /0.

## Severity

Medium (silent wrong data in VRF/PBR deployments). Design-fork: needs

## #3745 — flowexport/config: flow-server-nested source-address collapsed to one family-wide value (last-writer-wins) -> per-collector source bind is wrong; add FlowServer.SourceAddress + expose source in health surfaces [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

## Summary

A flow-server-nested source-address (per-collector override) is collapsed into
ONE family-wide value and applied to EVERY collector in that family. With two
flow-servers each carrying their own nested source-address, the last one in AST
order wins and is bound to all collectors, so a collector can dial with the
wrong source bind (failed dial or wrong routing/ACL path). Health/CLI/REST/
metrics surfaces also cannot show which source-bound connection failed.

## Evidence (current origin/master)

- pkg/config/types_system.go -- SamplingFamily has ONE SourceAddress for the
  whole family; FlowServer has no SourceAddress field.
- pkg/config/compiler_services.go:1404 -- a single flowServerSrc string.
- compiler_services.go:1459-1462 -- each nested flow-server source-address
  OVERWRITES flowServerSrc (last-writer-wins by AST/set-command order).
- compiler_services.go:1484-1488 -- the single flowServerSrc is stored as
  sf.SourceAddress (family-wide).
- pkg/flowexport/manager.go:208-218 -- srcAddr := fam.SourceAddress is applied
  to every collector in the family when building CollectorConfig.
- pkg/flowexport/manager.go:869-870 -- collectorKey dedupes by
  address+source-address+template, so the model CAN express per-collector
  source binds; the compiler just never populates them per-collector.
- pkg/flowexport/transport.go:63-72,137 -- CollectorHealth has no
  SourceAddress; CLI prints only "Collector %s (%s)"
  (pkg/cli/cli_show_flow.go:~1208).

## Fix

Add FlowServer.SourceAddress; keep the output-level source-address as the
per-output default; compute the EFFECTIVE source per collector in the resolver.
Add SourceAddress to CollectorHealth and the CLI/REST/Prometheus surfaces so a
source-bound connection is identifiable.

## Severity

Medium. Per-collector source binds are silently wrong; affects the (edge)
config with distinct nested source-addresses per flow-server. Driveable
(needs a new config field + plumbing).

## #3746 — flowexport: exported NetFlow/IPFIX volume ignores reverse (server->client) counters -> systematic underreport of asymmetric flows (reverse counters are decoded but never encoded) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

## Summary

Exported flow volume uses only the client-to-server (initiator) counters and
drops the server-to-client (reverse) counters, so collectors underreport
traffic for normal asymmetric flows (e.g. a large download reports only the
small request bytes). The reverse counters ARE decoded from the SESSION_CLOSE
frame -- they just never reach the wire.

## Evidence (current origin/master)

- pkg/logging/eventbuf.go:26-37 -- EventRecord has SessionPkts/SessionBytes AND
  RevSessionPkts/RevSessionBytes.
- pkg/logging/ringbuf.go:584-585 -- reverse counters are decoded from the frame.
- pkg/flowexport/netflow.go:588-589 -- FlowRecord.Packets/Bytes =
  rec.SessionPkts/rec.SessionBytes only.
- pkg/flowexport/ipfix.go:603-604 -- same for IPFIX.

xpf exports ONE record per bidirectional session anchored at the initiator
tuple, so the reverse half is simply discarded.

## Fix (needs a vSRX-parity decision)

Decide and document the intended semantics, then implement + test:
- initiator-to-responder only (standard unidirectional NetFlow -- but then the
  reverse direction is simply not reported at all, which is the current gap), OR
- emit a second reverse flow record (reversed tuple + reverse counters), OR
- export total bidirectional volume (Session + RevSession) with overflow-safe
  addition.

## Severity

Medium. Systematic volume underreporting for asymmetric flows. Design-fork
(parity decision on record semantics).

review: codex-review-158 (H12)

## #3747 — flowexport: batch queue (flowBatch) is unbounded with no backpressure/drop-counter/depth visibility -> memory growth under close-storm when Run goroutine is stopped/stalled [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

## Summary

The flow-export batch queue (flowBatch.v4/v6) is unbounded with no backpressure,
drop counter, or depth visibility. Under a SESSION_CLOSE storm (scan / failover)
combined with a stopped or blocked Run goroutine (see the reconcile-window and
route-mask-latency issues), ExportSessionClose keeps appending records and
memory grows with the event rate.

## Evidence (current origin/master)

- pkg/flowexport/transport.go:230-245 -- flowBatch.add appends to v4/v6 with no
  cap.
- pkg/flowexport/netflow.go:565-611 / ipfix.go:580-... -- ExportSessionClose
  queues every eligible close.
- pkg/flowexport/netflow.go:659-668 -- the batch is drained ONLY from the Run
  goroutine (100ms ticker); if Run is stopped/stalled nothing drains it.
- pkg/flowexport/transport.go:60-72 -- CollectorHealth exposes write counters
  but no queue depth / max depth / dropped-record counter; REST/Prometheus
  mirror only write health.

## Fix

Bound flowBatch by records and/or bytes; drop with a counter when full; expose
current depth, max depth, dropped records, and flush latency through
health/CLI/REST/Prometheus. Use a ring or channel with explicit backpressure.

## Severity

Medium (memory-growth hardening + missing operator visibility). Driveable.

review: codex-review-158 (H08+M15)

## #3748 — flowexport: active-flow-monitoring parity gaps -- no interim active-timeout records for long-lived flows + no IPFIX sampler/Options Template for the sampling interval [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

## Summary

Two vSRX active-flow-monitoring parity gaps for sampled export:

1. No interim active-timeout records. xpf emits a flow record ONLY on session
   close (from the SESSION_CLOSE callback). Long-lived flows produce no periodic
   accounting until they close, diverging from Junos active flow monitoring
   which emits interim records at the active-timeout.
2. No IPFIX sampler/Options Template for the sampling interval. With 1-in-N
   sampling the collector receives only sampled records and no
   samplingInterval/algorithm metadata, so it cannot correctly scale sampled
   counts without out-of-band configuration.

## Evidence (current origin/master)

- pkg/flowexport/manager.go:73-75 -- ExportConfig stores active/inactive/
  template-refresh timeouts, but no active-timeout emission path exists in
  netflow.go / ipfix.go (exporters only emit on close callbacks).
- pkg/flowexport/ipfix.go:54-58 -- ipfixSetIDOptionsTemplate (set ID 3) is
  defined but no options template is ever built (ipfix.go template path emits
  data templates only).
- pkg/flowexport/manager.go SamplingRate is carried but never encoded into an
  IPFIX options record.

## Fix

Validate the vSRX parity requirement. If required: (a) add periodic active-
timeout export fed by session snapshots (not only close events); (b) add IPFIX
Options Templates advertising samplingInterval/algorithm (RFC 5476/7011). If
collector-side manual scaling is deemed acceptable, document that explicitly.

## Severity

Low-Medium (feature/parity). Design-fork.

review: codex-review-158 (M08+L03)

## #3750 — event-options: revalidate queued remediation (policy existence + revision + cooldown) before commit — stale-action fail-open [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: MAJOR (security fail-open + documented-invariant violation)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-159 (H1+H2+H3 folded — same root)

A pre-classified event-options remediation (plannedAction, pkg/eventengine/engine.go:108-111) carries only policyName + ops. The worker (runAction / applyOnce, engine.go:525-644) never revalidates it against live engine state before committing, so three fail-opens exist. All require a config lock held by an operator while an RPM event fires (the worker is retrying on configstore.ErrConfigLocked), a normal contention window.

H1 — commits after policy removal:
1. Policy p triggers; worker retries on held lock.
2. Operator commits a config removing event-options policy p; Apply(nil) drops runtime/semRev for p (engine.go:272-294).
3. Lock releases; worker commits the OLD pre-classified commands even though no active policy authorizes them.
An operator can remove an unsafe automation policy and its remediation still mutates config after removal.

H2 — same-name redefinition commits the stale command set:
plannedAction has no semantic revision. Apply resets runtime on a semantic change (engine.go:284-291) but does not invalidate the queued/in-flight action. The old action commits ThenCommands=old, contradicting the now-active policy.

H3 — cooldown bypass (violates the documented 30s invariant, pkg/eventengine/README.md):
Cooldown is CHECKED in evaluateEvent (engine.go:745) and ARMED only after commit (engine.go:533). enqueue dedups by policy ONLY when the queue is full (engine.go:431-448); in the common case two events for policy p both queue while the worker is blocked. Worker commits action1, arms cooldown, then commits action2 without re-checking → back-to-back double-commit. The README claim "same policy will not trigger more than once in any 30s window" is false under lock contention.

Fix direction:
Add a semantic-revision token to plannedAction and revalidate under e.mu immediately before applyOnce: drop the action (with an explicit dropped_stale counter) if the policy is absent, the semRev mismatches, or the cooldown is now active. This makes H1/H2/H3 one gate.

## #3751 — event-options: strict-validate within/trigger numerics at commit — typo silently becomes always-fire (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: MAJOR (security fail-open)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-159 (H11+H12+H13 folded — same root: no commit-time numeric validation)

compileEventOptions (pkg/config/compiler_services.go:1628-1665) parses within/trigger numerics with strconv.Atoi and SILENTLY IGNORES the error, leaving the field at zero; the schema (pkg/config/schema_system.go:873-879) declares only args:1 placeholder "<seconds>" with no integer/range validator, and no SchemaValidate/commit check exists for these fields.

H11 — typo becomes always-fire (fail-open):
"within bogus { trigger on typo; }" compiles to Seconds=0, TriggerOn=0, TriggerUntil=0. withinMatches (engine.go:854-888) then skips both trigger tests (both guarded by > 0) and returns true — the policy fires on EVERY matching event. A typo in a temporal gate silently converts a threshold-gated remediation into an unconditional one.

H12 — negative / huge values accepted:
No range check. within -1 yields a nonsensical window; a huge integer risks time.Duration overflow when multiplied by time.Second (engine.go:862, 901).

H13 — both trigger on and trigger until accepted on one clause:
compiler fills both fields (compiler_services.go:1637-1663); runtime ANDs them (engine.go:872-884), producing a narrow one-count band that is almost certainly unintended and is never surfaced as ambiguous.

Fix direction:
Strict commit-time validation of event-options within/trigger: reject non-numeric, require a positive bounded range (e.g. 1..86400), and reject a single within clause carrying both trigger on and trigger until. Keep the lenient LOAD path a downgrade-to-warning for older persisted configs, mirroring the attributes-match strict/lenient split.

## #3752 — event-options: engine lifecycle — day-2 enable of first policy never starts engine; removal/shutdown leaks worker + drops queued actions [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: HIGH (feature silently inert)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-159 (H5 headline; H9/H7/H8 folded — event-options engine lifecycle)

H5 — day-2 enable never starts the engine:
Boot creates d.eventEngine ONLY when the boot config already has policies (pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:967-981, gated on len(cfg.EventOptions) > 0). Day-2 apply is a no-op when the pointer is nil (pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:1358-1359: "if d.eventEngine != nil"). So committing the FIRST event-options policy on a running daemon never constructs the engine and never registers the RPM callback — the policy is inert until a daemon restart. This directly contradicts the always-create pattern the SAME file documents and uses for LLDP and dhcpRelay (daemon_run.go:952-961) specifically to support day-2 enablement.

H9 — removal leaves an idle callback/worker:
Apply(nil) clears runtime but does not close the worker or unregister the RPM callback (engine.go:272-321; rpm.SetEventCallback has no clear path). After all policies are removed the engine stays wired to RPM forever, keeping an idle worker and ambiguous lifecycle/metrics state.

H7 — shutdown can silently discard queued remediations:
actionWorker selects stopCh and returns before draining buffered actions (engine.go:508-518); enqueue drops silently on stop (engine.go:435-436). The README says queue loss is always counted, but shutdown drops are unobservable.

H8 — HandleEvent can enqueue into a stopped worker:
After Close, startOnce is consumed (engine.go:399-409) and HandleEvent still evaluates+enqueues (engine.go:373-388); enqueue's select races stopCh vs a buffered send, so a late event can bump QueueDepth into a dead queue.

Fix direction:
Introduce reconcileEventOptions(cfg) that ALWAYS constructs the engine at boot (like LLDP/dhcpRelay), applies policy changes, registers/clears the RPM callback, and closes the worker + unregisters the callback when policies reach zero. Make Close drain-and-count buffered actions (shutdown drop reason) and HandleEvent fast-return after Close.

## #3753 — event-options: attributes-match ignores the event-name prefix (multi-event policy scoping wrong) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: MEDIUM (correctness / Junos parity)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-159 (H4)

attributes-match ignores the event-name prefix. ParseEventAttributesMatch (pkg/config/event_options_match.go:51-67) keeps only the last dot-separated component (the field) and discards the "<event>." prefix. The runtime matcher (engine.go:786-834) therefore applies the constraint to EVERY event in a multi-event policy, and the strict validator (event_options_match.go:124-148) never checks that the left-hand event name is one of the policy's events.

Trace:
- policy events [ event_a event_b ]
- attributes-match "event_a.test-owner matches ^owner$"
- runtime receives event_b with TestOwner=owner
- eventMatches accepts event_b; attributesMatch ignores "event_a" and only tests test-owner → the constraint intended to scope event_a incorrectly gates event_b (and vice-versa).

Fix direction:
Parse attributes-match into (eventName, field, pattern); at commit validate eventName is one of the policy's events; at runtime require eventName == ev.Name before applying the field/pattern test.


---

## #3754 — event-options: autonomous remediation commits carry no audit description [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: MEDIUM (forensics / audit)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-159 (H10)

Autonomous event-options remediation commits carry no audit description. applyOnce commits via e.commitFn(ctx, "") with an empty comment (pkg/eventengine/engine.go:638); commitAndApply only uses CommitWithDescription when the comment is non-empty (pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go). So an event-triggered config mutation lands in commit/rollback history as an ordinary unattributed commit. For a security appliance that mutates its own config autonomously, the operator cannot tell from history which event policy made the change or why.

Fix direction:
Thread a deterministic description into the remediation commit, e.g. "event-options policy <name>: <event>/<owner>/<test>", optionally with a count/hash of the command batch.

## #3755 — event-options: RPM first probe cycle runs before the event callback is registered — boot-time failover edge dropped [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: MEDIUM (boot-time failover edge dropped)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-159 (H6)

Boot starts RPM probes before the event-options callback is registered, so the first probe cycle's events are dropped. reconcileRPM runs at pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:949 (and inside the startup applyConfig), starting probe goroutines; runProbeLoop runs the first probe IMMEDIATELY (pkg/rpm/rpm.go:397-398 "Run first probe immediately"). The event callback is only installed later at daemon_run.go:977-978 (SetEventCallback). fireEvent is a no-op when the callback is nil (rpm.go:272-279). Any ping_probe_failed / ping_test_failed / ping_test_completed emitted by the first cycle before registration is silently lost, so boot-time failover automation can miss the exact first edge it exists to handle — for long test-interval values this materially delays remediation.

Fix direction:
Construct + register the event-options callback BEFORE starting RPM probes, or have RPM retain and replay the latest initial transition once a callback is installed.

## #3756 — event-options: Junos parity — attribute set + trigger on/until edge-vs-level semantics (design-fork) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: LOW/MEDIUM (Junos parity)
Class: design-fork
review: codex-review-159 (H14 + M1 + M2 — event-options runtime/attribute parity)

Grouped parity gaps in the event-options runtime that warrant a design decision, not a mechanical fix. Related to the vSRX parity mega-issue #2008.

H14 — attribute set is minimal: attributes-match can only resolve test-owner and test-name (pkg/config/event_options_match.go:33-36; rpm.Event carries only those, pkg/rpm/rpm.go:113-117). vSRX/Junos event-options match many more attributes (probe target, routing-instance, destination-interface, result status, loss threshold, RTT/jitter, failure reason). Operators must encode many distinct probe names instead of matching attributes. Expanding requires widening rpm.Event and the attributes-match SSOT.

M1 — trigger on N is level-triggered, not edge-triggered: withinMatches (engine.go:872-876) checks count >= N each event, so after cooldown expires while the window still holds N events, it fires again. Junos "trigger on" often reads as a threshold CROSSING. Semantics need to be pinned and regression-tested.

M2 — trigger until N boundary: current event is appended before withinMatches (engine.go:733-736) and until returns false at count >= N (engine.go:879-883), so "trigger until 1" never fires. Pin Junos parity for the N-th event and add N=1/N=2 boundary tests.

Fix direction:
Decide the intended Junos semantics for trigger on/until (edge vs level, inclusive/exclusive boundary) and the attribute model, then document + test. Defer to /research for the parity decision.


---

## #3757 — ip-monitoring: route-overlay actuator has no per-consumer convergence/retry — FRR/snapshot/FIB failures split the FIB with no autonomous recovery [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: MAJOR (availability — silent partial failover / split FIB)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-160 (H1+H2+H3+M1 folded — the route-overlay actuator has no per-consumer convergence/retry)

The ip-monitoring route-overlay actuator drives three stateful consumers (FRR reload, userspace snapshot publish, FIB-generation bump) with no success/failure feedback to the engine, so any consumer failure leaves kernel routing, dynamic routing, and userspace forwarding disagreeing with no autonomous recovery.

M1 (root) — the engine clears the dirty bit BEFORE the actuator runs and the actuator has no return value. run() sets e.dirtySince = time.Time{} at pkg/ipmon/ipmon.go:535 then calls e.actuate() at :545; actuate() returns nothing. Every failure path below is therefore invisible to the scheduler.

H1 — a HARD FRR error is swallowed, snapshot still publishes: applyFRRConfig logs and returns void on a non-degraded ApplyFull error (pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go:170-176); actuateRouteOverlayLocked ignores it and proceeds to publish the userspace snapshot (daemon_ipmon.go:228-240). Kernel/FRR holds old routes while userspace forwards to the failover next-hop — the "FRR and dataplane agree by construction" invariant (daemon_ipmon.go:3-19) breaks. (Note: the DEGRADED branch is deliberate warn-and-continue; the gap is the hard-error branch with no retry.)

H2 — snapshot publish failure has no autonomous retry: on a transient PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot error the actuator returns without re-marking dirty or scheduling a retry (daemon_ipmon.go:240-248); the dirty bit was already cleared (M1). If the policy stays failed, no further RPM transition occurs, so the dataplane stays on the old route until an unrelated commit/lease/transition.

H3 — FIB-bump failure retried only on a future unrelated actuation: BumpFIBGeneration failure sets d.pendingFIBBump=true and returns (daemon_ipmon.go:262-267) with no timer/kick. The unit test only exercises retry by manually calling actuateRouteOverlayLocked twice (pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon_test.go). A stably-failed policy leaves established flows pinned to the dead path indefinitely.

Fix direction:
Make the actuator report per-consumer results to the engine; a failed consumer keeps the state dirty and schedules a bounded-backoff retry loop (bound to the daemon context). Expose per-consumer convergence metrics (xpf_ipmon_overlay_frr_applied / _snapshot_applied / _fib_bump_pending) and a last-successful-actuation-age gauge.

## #3758 — ip-monitoring: actuateRouteOverlay can block daemon shutdown forever on applySem.Acquire(context.Background()) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: HIGH (shutdown hang / lifecycle)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-160 (H4)

actuateRouteOverlay can block daemon shutdown forever. It acquires the apply semaphore with context.Background() (pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go:207-209): _ = d.applySem.Acquire(context.Background(), 1). The ipmon run loop calls e.actuate() synchronously (pkg/ipmon/ipmon.go:541-546) and can only observe e.stop AFTER actuate returns (select at ipmon.go:555-559). If another apply holds applySem while the run loop is blocked inside actuate, daemon shutdown calls d.ipmon.Stop() (daemon_run.go), which closes e.stop and waits on e.done — but the run loop cannot reach the stop case, so shutdown hangs until the unrelated apply releases the semaphore, possibly forever if that apply is wedged. Control-plane restart is part of failover recovery, so an optional route-overlay actuator must not be able to wedge it.

Fix direction:
Acquire applySem with the daemon context (not context.Background()), make the actuator cancellable, and bound Stop()/shutdown wait. Drop or reschedule route-only actuation if shutdown has begun.


---

## #3759 — ip-monitoring: literal IPv6 link-local preferred-route next-hop commits but renders an FRR-rejected route [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: HIGH (IPv6 failover route silently fails to install)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-160 (H5; L8/L11 representation folded)

A literal IPv6 link-local ip-monitoring preferred-route next-hop passes commit but renders an FRR-rejected route. validateIPMonitoringStrict only checks address-family match for a literal next-hop (pkg/config/compiler_services.go:947-952) — it has NO link-local scope check, unlike the RPM target validator which DOES reject a bare link-local target (validateRPMLinkLocalZoneStrict, compiler_services.go:134-183). So "preferred-route route ::/0 next-hop fe80::1" (no interface) commits cleanly.

At render, renderPreferredRoutes builds a StaticRoute with NextHops:[{Address: fe80::1}] and no interface (pkg/frr/config_render.go:301-306) and calls generateStaticRouteInTable with fc.IPv6NextHopInterfaces. That map is built by inferIPv6StaticNextHopInterfaces (pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1922, populated only from cfg static routes at daemon_run.go:2145-2153) — the ip-monitoring overlay PreferredRoutes are never fed in. So IPv6NextHopInterfaces[vrf][fe80::1] is absent (unless an unrelated static route happens to name the same gateway), and FRR receives "ipv6 route ::/0 fe80::1 1" without a trailing interface, which FRR rejects. The failover route fails exactly when needed. IPv6 WAN gateways are commonly link-local. RouteOverlayEntry also has no field to carry a literal next-hop interface (types_system.go), and the userspace snapshot encodes only the bare address (pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:173-178).

Fix direction:
Either reject a literal link-local preferred-route next-hop at commit unless it carries an interface/%zone qualifier (mirroring the RPM target validator), OR extend PreferredRoute/RouteOverlayEntry with an explicit next-hop interface and feed overlay entries into the IPv6 inference map before rendering (and add an addr@iface convention to the userspace snapshot).

## #3760 — ip-monitoring: PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot mutates cached desired overlay before publication succeeds [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: MEDIUM (state consistency)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-160 (H6)

PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot mutates the cached desired overlay before publication succeeds. m.routeOverlay = cloneRouteOverlay(overlay) is assigned at pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager.go:933, before the apply_snapshot control request at manager.go:984. On a helper failure the function returns an error at manager.go:985 with m.routeOverlay already advanced to the new desired overlay while m.lastSnapshot is unchanged. A later full apply calls buildRouteSnapshots(cfg, ..., m.routeOverlay) and reads the cached overlay as if it were the last successfully-applied dynamic overlay, so internal state says "new overlay" before the dataplane ever accepted it — increasing the blast radius of a transient helper failure and defeating any desired-vs-applied observability.

Fix direction:
Split desired overlay from applied overlay: update the applied/cached overlay only after a successful apply_snapshot, and keep the pending desired overlay with explicit retry + metrics.

## #3761 — ip-monitoring: status/metrics report PASS/applied for unknown or non-converged state [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: MEDIUM (observability — masks failover failures)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-160 (H7+H8+M9+M10 folded — ip-monitoring status/metrics truth model)

ip-monitoring status and metrics report health/success for states that are not converged, which hides exactly the failover failure modes that need alerts.

H7 — PASS for unknown/absent RPM data: Status derives Failed from st.failed only (pkg/ipmon/ipmon.go:407-424) and display renders PASS when not failed (pkg/ipmon/display.go:16-27, and a "*/-/PASS" row when FailingTests is empty). Before any probe result exists (failedTests nil), a configured policy prints Status: PASS — an operator reading "show services ip-monitoring status" assumes failover protection is active and healthy when no probe has run. Unknown health is not PASS.

H8 — xpf_ipmon_routes_applied counts DESIRED, not applied: the metric sums len(ps.Routes) (pkg/api/metrics_system.go:192) where ps.Routes comes from Status() = computeOverlayLocked() = the desired winner-resolved overlay. The descriptor states "currently applied" (pkg/api/metrics_descriptors.go). If FRR/snapshot/FIB failed (see the actuator-convergence issue), the gauge still reports the routes as applied.

M9 — unresolved route status lacks detail: only the destination prefix is recorded per policy (ipmon.go:339-343; display.go:50-52) — no routing-instance, lease key/next-hop-interface, metric, or candidate. Operators cannot tell which DHCP unit is missing or which RI lost failover.

M10 — a losing failed policy shows "(none applied)": when two failed policies target the same prefix the winner takes ps.Routes and the loser shows failed with no routes (ipmon.go:392-416), indistinguishable from an unresolved/buggy route rather than a deterministic winner decision.

Fix direction:
Carry per-test known state and expose UNKNOWN/HELD distinctly from PASS; rename or split xpf_ipmon_routes_applied into desired vs applied/converged gauges; replace the []string unresolved list with a typed struct (RI, dest, next-hop-interface, metric, reason); and expose candidate result state APPLIED/SUPPRESSED_BY_POLICY/UNRESOLVED/GATED. Also add xpf_ipmon_unresolved_next_hops to the docs/multi-wan.md observability quick list (L12).

## #3762 — ip-monitoring: engine lifecycle not idempotent — double Start panics, Stop-before-Start deadlocks [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: MEDIUM (lifecycle hardening — exported engine API)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-160 (H9+H10)

The ipmon Engine lifecycle is not idempotent.

H9 — double Start panics: Start just does go e.run() (pkg/ipmon/ipmon.go:184-187) with no guard; run() defers close(e.done) (ipmon.go:519-520). A second Start spawns a second goroutine; after Stop both return and both close(e.done) → the second close panics.

H10 — Stop before Start deadlocks: Stop closes e.stop then blocks on <-e.done (ipmon.go:189-198). If the engine was constructed but never Started (a common constructor/startup error-unwind path around netlink/DHCP/dataplane/cluster wiring), no run loop exists to close e.done and the caller blocks forever.

The daemon currently starts exactly once, but this is an exported engine API and this lifecycle style has caused repeated regressions in this repo.

Fix direction:
Track lifecycle state under a mutex or sync.Once: make Start a no-op / error on double start, and make Stop safe both before Start (return without waiting, or close both channels) and after Stop.

## #3763 — ip-monitoring: hold-down pending-recovery not recomputed when hold-down value changes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: MEDIUM (config-change correctness)
Class: driveable-bug
review: codex-review-160 (M7 + L6)

Hold-down / pending-recovery is not recomputed when the operator changes the hold-down value. Apply preserves prev.pendingRecoveryAt whenever (policy name, MatchRPMProbe) survives the commit (pkg/ipmon/ipmon.go:217-223), regardless of whether HoldDownSecs changed. evaluateLocked then honors the preserved deadline (ipmon.go:479-491). So if a policy is recovering under a 300s hold-down and the operator lowers hold-down to 10s (same name, same probe) during incident response, recovery still waits for the old 300s deadline — operator intent is ignored. Lowering hold-down should shorten a pending recovery; raising it should extend it. More generally (L6), state preservation keys only on (name, probe), not on a route-action semantic revision, so pending timers/counters can stay attached to a now-different route-action set.

Fix direction:
Preserve pendingRecoveryAt only when HoldDownSecs is unchanged; otherwise recompute the deadline from now (or from a stored recovery-start timestamp + new hold-down). Consider a semantic-revision hash for the fields that should reset timers/counters independently of probe identity.

## #3764 — ip-monitoring: per-RG HA publication/probe gating keyed to lowest data RG only (design-fork) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: LOW/MEDIUM (HA / Junos parity)
Class: design-fork
review: codex-review-160 (M2 + M3)

Per-RG ip-monitoring HA gating is keyed to the lowest data RG only. ipmonPublishAllowed gates overlay publication on d.cluster.IsLocalPrimary(lowestDataRG(cfg)) (pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go:294-299), and RPM probe HA gating defaults referenced probes to lowestDataRG when no RETH/source binding exists (pkg/daemon/daemon_rpm.go:133-165). In a multi-data-RG cluster with split primaryship (RG1 primary on node A, RG2 primary on node B), a policy controlling an RG2 uplink route is suppressed on node B (the actual owner) because the node-wide gate checks RG1. This is documented as known v1 coarseness in docs/multi-wan.md:486-490 but has no first-class tracking issue.

Fix direction (design decision — defer to /research):
Compute publish eligibility and probe gating per policy/route from the matched probe's gating RG or the route egress/RETH ownership, not a node-wide boolean; or require explicit RG binding for HA-gated ip-monitoring probes.
