## #3766 — userspace-dp: same-plan runtime snapshot refresh is non-fallible and non-atomic — reports ok=true on a rejected snapshot and mutates validation/neighbor state before the fallible forwarding build [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Found by codex-review-161 (base 579768f06, re-verified on origin/master 4cc1b90850). Cluster of H1+H2+H3+M1 (same root: the same-plan refresh path is not a fail-closed atomic swap).

Severity: Critical (breaks the fail-closed snapshot contract). Drive-class: driveable-bug.

SECURITY / correctness: the control response returns ok=true while live forwarding is still the previous state, and the rejected snapshot gets persisted as the boot baseline.

Path: apply_snapshot -> refresh_runtime_snapshot -> refresh_runtime_snapshot_inner.

1) Handler treats the refresh as infallible and persists unconditionally.
   userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/snapshot.rs:110-118
     if should_run_afxdp(&guard.status) { guard.afxdp.refresh_runtime_snapshot(&snapshot); }
     else { guard.afxdp.refresh_runtime_snapshot_disarmed(&snapshot); }
     guard.snapshot = Some(snapshot);
     refresh_status(guard);
     *persist_state = true;
   refresh_runtime_snapshot returns () (no Result), so the handler cannot observe a build rejection. It still stores the snapshot, refreshes status, and sets persist_state=true. response.ok stays true. (M1)

2) The preflight only validates POLICY state. A non-policy integrity failure (invalid interface address, CoS queue, NAT64/NPTv6 rule, or any other build_forwarding_state failure) is caught only later, AFTER side effects.
   userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/snapshot_refresh.rs:71-83 (policy preflight only)
   userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/snapshot_refresh.rs:134-148 (fallible forwarding build; on Err logs to stderr and returns ())

3) self.validation is overwritten to the NEW generation BEFORE the fallible build. (H2)
   userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/snapshot_refresh.rs:122-126
     self.validation = ValidationState { snapshot_installed: true, config_generation: snapshot.generation, fib_generation: snapshot.fib_generation };
   On the build-error return at :146 self.validation is left at G2 while self.forwarding is still G1. A later bump_fib_generation (coordinator/mod.rs:805-808) then does shared_validation.store(self.validation), publishing config_generation=G2 against the old G1 forwarding table -> split-brain vs the flow cache/XDP metadata generation contract.

4) Old dynamic neighbor manager keys are removed BEFORE the fallible build. (H3)
   userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/snapshot_refresh.rs:103-115 rotate manager_keys and bulk.remove every old key.
   If the build then fails and returns, the OLD forwarding state stays live but its dynamic neighbor entries have been deleted -> transient/persistent blackhole (missing-neighbor / re-probe) on a snapshot that was supposed to be rejected with all live state intact.

Contrast: the full reconcile path (afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/snapshot.rs) builds forwarding FIRST and only then publishes — that is the intended invariant this same-plan path violates. Distinct from #2484 (full apply teardown fail-open) and #2916 (queue replan predicate).

Fix:
- Make refresh_runtime_snapshot{,_disarmed}/_inner return Result<(), SnapshotIntegrityError>.
- Build new_forwarding FIRST. Keep next_validation and next_manager_keys LOCAL; only assign self.validation, swap manager_keys/remove old dynamic keys, and store shared_validation/ha.forwarding AFTER the build succeeds and immediately before the stores.
- On Err: leave guard.snapshot, status generation, persisted state, validation, and neighbor keys untouched; set response.ok=false with the integrity error.
- Regression test: a same-plan snapshot that PASSES the policy preflight but FAILS build_forwarding_state, asserting live forwarding + neighbor keys + validation are unchanged and response.ok=false.

## #3767 — userspace-dp: bump_fib_generation has no protocol-version gate, accepts generation rollback (revives stale flow-cache entries), and never persists the bumped generation [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Found by codex-review-161 (base 579768f06, re-verified on origin/master). Cluster H4+H5+M2 (same handler / same coordinator method).

Severity: High. Drive-class: driveable-bug + hardening.

bump_fib_generation is a control message that mutates dataplane validation state, but unlike apply_snapshot it has none of apply's guards.

H4 — no version gate.
  userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/snapshot.rs:157-177 (bump_fib) checks only snapshot presence; it never checks snapshot.version != CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_PROTOCOL_VERSION the way apply does at snapshot.rs:25-32. A mixed-version / corrupt client with version=0 is accepted and mutates status + stored snapshot + worker validation FIB generation.
  Fix: reject snapshot.version != CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_PROTOCOL_VERSION with a unit test mirroring the apply version test.

H5 — accepts generation rollback -> can revive stale flow-cache decisions.
  userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/mod.rs:805-808
    pub fn bump_fib_generation(&mut self, fib_generation: u32) {
        self.validation.fib_generation = fib_generation;
        self.shared_validation.store(Arc::new(self.validation));
    }
  There is no monotonicity check. Flow-cache validation is EQUALITY based, not monotone:
  userspace-dp/src/afxdp/flow_cache.rs:827-828
    if entry.stamp.config_generation != lookup.config_generation || entry.stamp.fib_generation != lookup.fib_generation { ... invalidate }
  So publishing an OLD fib_generation (stale/duplicate/buggy control message, or a config transition that reuses a value) makes previously-invalidated cache entries match validation again -> cached forwarding reused after a route withdrawal / failover route change.
  Fix: reject a FIB bump strictly lower than the current in-memory generation (unless part of a full snapshot generation transition). Consider widening fib_generation to u64 and/or carrying a boot/session nonce in cache stamps so a value can never be re-used.

M2 — bump is not persisted.
  userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/snapshot.rs:171-176 mutates guard.status.last_fib_generation and guard.snapshot.fib_generation in RAM only; the handler has no persist_state parameter (apply has one). After a route-only overlay bump to gen N, a helper/host restart boots from persisted gen N-1 -> restart observes a stale FIB generation the control plane already considered applied.
  Fix: either do not mutate the stored snapshot on bump, or make bump persist state; add a restart test for route-only overlay bumps.

## #3768 — userspace-dp: IPv6 ip-rule route-leak NextTable emitted as '.inet.0' (should be '.inet6.0') and Rust next-table recursion is not family-canonicalized -> leaked IPv6 traffic blackholes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Found by codex-review-161 (base 579768f06, re-verified on origin/master). Cluster H6+M5 (mutually-masking: fixing EITHER end restores IPv6 leaks; both are wrong today) + M6 (weak cycle detection in the same recursion).

Severity: High (vSRX-parity, IPv6 rib-group / next-table route leaking). Drive-class: driveable-bug.

H6 — Go emitter builds every next-table name as .inet.0 even in the AF_INET6 loop.
  pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:108-113
    tableIDToName[inst.TableID] = inst.Name + ".inet.0"   // always .inet.0
  pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:114-139: the family loop iterates {AF_INET, AF_INET6} and correctly sets Table/Family to inet6.0/inet6 for the v6 pass, but NextTable = tableName is still inst.Name + ".inet.0".
  So an IPv6 ip rule leaking 2001:db8:1::/48 into instance blue emits RouteSnapshot{Table:"inet6.0", Family:"inet6", NextTable:"blue.inet.0"}. The correct v6 next-table is blue.inet6.0.
  Note: normalizeRouteSnapshotFamily (routes.go:299-319) canonicalizes static-route table names but is NOT applied to these ip-rule leak snapshots.

M5 — Rust next-table recursion uses the raw string, no per-family canonicalization.
  userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/mod.rs:1591-1616 (v4) and :1765-1789 (v6): recursion clones route.next_table and recurses WITHOUT calling canonical_route_table for the current family.
  routes_v6 is keyed by canonical_route_table(route.table, true) = "blue.inet6.0" (forwarding_build/fib.rs:64-83). The v6 lookup recurses with "blue.inet.0" -> miss -> NoRoute even though the route exists in the VRF v6 table. canonical_route_table("blue.inet.0", true) would rewrite it to "blue.inet6.0" (forwarding/mod.rs:35-52) but that helper is only used at the ENTRY table (forwarding/mod.rs:1140,1183), never on recursion.

M6 (fold) — next-table loop detection only catches direct self-loops.
  forwarding/mod.rs:1593 / :1767 reject only next_table_name == table; an A->B->A cross-table cycle burns to MAX_NEXT_TABLE_DEPTH (=8, forwarding/mod.rs:14) on every miss and hides the config defect.

Fix:
- Go: compute the next-table name per family inside the loop (inst.Name + ".inet6.0" for AF_INET6), or track table ID -> both family table names.
- Rust: canonicalize the recursive next_table name with the current address family before loop detection + recursion (or reject a cross-family next_table string at build).
- Optionally carry a small visited-table set for A->B->A cycle detection with a distinct disposition/counter.
- Add Go + Rust integration tests for an IPv6 ip-rule leak.

## #3769 — userspace-dp: NAT/DNAT non-interface local addresses are inserted into the GLOBAL local_v4/local_v6 set with no table attribution -> cross-VRF local-delivery + ifindex-0 LocalDelivery (residual of #3151) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Found by codex-review-161 (base 579768f06, re-verified on origin/master). Cluster H7+L5. Residual of #3151 (which table-scoped the connected-scan ATTRIBUTION but left the local-membership set global for NAT/DNAT-only addresses).

Severity: High (VRF isolation / zone + HA-RG mis-attribution). Drive-class: driveable-bug (or design-fork if per-table NAT ownership is deferred).

Static-NAT external IPs and DNAT destination IPs are inserted into the GLOBAL local sets:
  userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/mod.rs:407-427
    for ext_ip in state.static_nat.external_ips() { ... state.local_v4.insert(*v4) / local_v6.insert(*v6) }
    for dst_ip in state.dnat_table.destination_ips() { ... local_v4.insert(v4) / local_v6.insert(v6) }
These have no table/VRF attribution.

The local-delivery shortcut keys the DECISION on the global set membership; only the ifindex attribution is table-scoped (the #3151 fix):
  userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/mod.rs:1142-1169 (v4) and :1185-1204 (v6)
    if state.local_v4.contains(&ip) {                       // GLOBAL membership
        let local_ifindex = state.connected_v4.iter()
            .find(|e| e.table == table && e.prefix.addr() == ip)  // table-scoped attribution
            .map(|e| e.ifindex).unwrap_or(0);                     // NAT-only IP -> ifindex 0
        return ForwardingResolution { disposition: LocalDelivery, local_ifindex, egress_ifindex: local_ifindex, tx_ifindex: local_ifindex, ... };
    }

Consequences:
- A packet in VRF A destined to a NAT/DNAT address owned in VRF B (or global) hits the global membership shortcut and returns LocalDelivery, bypassing the VRF-A route lookup that may have a real route or should not own that address at all -> cross-VRF local-delivery leak.
- The connected scan cannot find a table-scoped interface for a NAT-only IP, so it returns LocalDelivery with local/egress/tx ifindex = 0 (L5). Downstream zone selection (by ifindex), security policy, HA RG ownership (owner_rg_for_flow(egress_ifindex)), and DNAT/static-NAT admission all receive ifindex 0 with no owning zone/RG.

Fix:
- Carry table/VRF attribution for NAT/DNAT local targets (per-table local sets or a table-scoped NAT-ownership record), and gate the local-delivery shortcut on a table-scoped local/NAT match.
- Never return LocalDelivery with ifindex 0 unless a specific local subsystem owns that address in the current table; otherwise fall through to the route lookup. Add a debug counter/assertion for LocalDelivery with ifindex 0.

## #3776 — userspace-dp flow-cache: session expiry/removal does not invalidate the cache — stale-descriptor forward + released-SNAT reuse after the owning session is gone (incomplete #2220 closure) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: MEDIUM-HIGH (stateful-firewall bypass window + NAT-port corruption). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-162 (H1, H2; folds L1/L6/M10).

## Summary

The per-session flow-cache keepalive shipped for #2220 (PR #2233,
`sessions.touch_if_stale` in `flow_cache_hit.rs`) fixed the case where an
*actively-forwarding* flow's session was reaped mid-flight. But #2220's own
suggested fix also called for invalidating the flow-cache slot in the session
GC path — that half was never implemented. The worker session-expiry loop
deletes session/BPF/conntrack state and **releases the SNAT allocation**, yet
never touches the flow cache. A surviving cache entry then keeps forwarding via
its stale `RewriteDescriptor` when traffic resumes on the same tuple.

## Provenance (origin/master 4cc1b9085)

- Expiry loop reaps sessions, calls `release_source_nat_allocation(...)` and
  `delete_session_map_entry_for_removed_session_with_origin(...)` for each
  expired entry — but there is NO `flow_cache.invalidate_slot` call:
  `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/loop_body/mod.rs:713-744`.
- The ONLY invalidation call sites are RST teardown
  (`worker/lifecycle.rs:231-235`) and the neighbor/fabric-mismatch fall-through
  (`poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs:125`). Expiry, operator clear, and
  FIN teardown are not covered.
- Cache lookup validates only key + config/fib generation + RG epoch + RG
  lease — never session liveness: `flow_cache.rs:820-857`.
- On a cache hit both `touch_if_stale` (`session/mod.rs:865-877`) and
  `account_packet` (`session/mod.rs:924-943`) silently no-op on a missing
  session ("the same fail-open posture as touch"), so a gone session is
  invisible to the hit path.
- Keepalive only defends *active* flows: `touch_if_stale` refreshes when idle
  for `expires_after_ns / SESSION_KEEPALIVE_DIVISOR` (=4, `session/mod.rs:80`),
  i.e. a UDP flow (60s timeout) idle >45s lets its session expire while the
  cache entry survives.

   inserted (holding a specific SNAT port).
2. The flow idles past its timeout; `expire_stale_entries_ha` reaps the

## #3778 — userspace-dp flow-cache: CoS BA classifier (DSCP + IEEE 802.1p PCP) queue is frozen by the first cached packet — admission never declines for per-packet classifiers [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: MEDIUM (CoS/QoS correctness, vSRX parity). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-162 (H4, H5; folds M8/L2/L5/L8/L9).

## Summary

Behavior-aggregate (BA) CoS classifiers are per-packet in vSRX: each packet's
DSCP (or 802.1p PCP) selects its egress queue. The flow-cache admission gate
declines a cache entry when an input/output firewall FILTER carries a DSCP or
per-packet-L4 match (#2362), but it does NOT decline when a CoS BA CLASSIFIER
is configured on the egress interface. The cached TX-selection descriptor
resolves the queue from the FIRST packet's `meta.dscp`/`meta.ingress_pcp`, and
the cache key excludes DSCP and PCP — so a mixed-marking flow is pinned to the
first packet's queue for the life of the cache entry.

## Provenance (origin/master 4cc1b9085)

- Cache key hashes only session key + ingress ifindex; DSCP/PCP are NOT in the
  key (`flow_cache.rs` set_index / lookup, admission comment at
  `flow_cache.rs:367-371`).
- Admission declines only for DSCP/per-packet-L4 FILTER terms
  (`interface_input_filter_has_dscp_match` /
  `interface_output_filter_has_per_packet_l4_match`, `flow_cache.rs:367-412`) —
  no check for a configured BA classifier.
- The cached descriptor resolves the queue at build time from the seed packet:
  `resolve_cos_dscp_classifier_queue_id(iface, meta.dscp)` then
  `resolve_cos_ieee8021_classifier_queue_id(iface, meta.ingress_pcp,
  meta.ingress_vlan_present != 0)` — `tx/cos_classify.rs:216-227`.
- Cache hit consumes the cached `queue_id` (`flow_cache_hit.rs:185`); the debug
  active-flow-by-queue telemetry (`flow_cache.rs:653-657`) is likewise stale.

## Runtime trace

1. Egress CoS maps DSCP EF -> voice queue, DSCP 0 -> default (or PCP 5 ->
   priority queue).
2. First packet of a UDP flow is DSCP 0 / untagged -> cache records default
   queue.
3. Later same-5-tuple packet is DSCP 46 / PCP 5.
4. Cache hit (key excludes DSCP/PCP) reuses the default queue; live CoS would
   have chosen voice/priority.

## #3779 — userspace-dp flow-cache: TTL/Time-Exceeded check runs AFTER egress counters/policers/logs/drop on the cache-hit path — TTL=1 packet can be policer-dropped with no ICMP Time Exceeded [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: MEDIUM (router-core correctness + observability). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-162 (H6, H7, H8; folds L4/L10/L11).

## Summary

On the flow-cache hit path, egress side effects (output/TX filter counters,
policy hit counter, three-color policers, input/output filter logs, and the
terminal drop) all run BEFORE the TTL/hop-limit check that builds ICMP Time
Exceeded. The slow paths check TTL before those side effects. For a TTL=1
packet this both (a) drops the packet on a red policer or terminal output-drop
instead of emitting Time Exceeded, and (b) charges counters/logs/telemetry for
a packet that never egresses.

## Provenance (origin/master 4cc1b9085)

Order in `stage_flow_cache_hit` (`poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs`):
1. output/TX `then count` replay (:133-140)
2. #3073 policy hit counter (:154-160)
3. `apply_cached_three_color_policers` (:161-165)
4. `emit_cached_input_filter_log` / `emit_cached_output_filter_log` (:166-182)
5. drop on `tx_selection.drop || policer_action.drop` -> recycle (:183-186)
6. `touch_if_stale` / `account_packet` (:195-215)
7. THEN `build_local_time_exceeded_request` (TTL check) (:217-240)

Slow paths check TTL first:
- session-hit: `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1076-1105`
- session-miss (rolls back NAT before enqueue): `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:2411-2435`

Also `lookup_counted` adds `packet_len` to `observed_bytes` and stamps the
active epoch on hit (`flow_cache.rs:858-874`) before the TTL outcome, so
active-flow byte/queue telemetry counts packets that became ICMP responses.

1. A cached flow has a three-color output policer that is currently red (or a
   terminal output-filter drop).
2. A TTL=1 packet hits the entry.
3. Step 5 drops it before step 7 builds Time Exceeded -> traceroute through the
   firewall breaks on the cached flow; the slow path would have emitted TE.

## #3780 — userspace-dp: scheduled-policy republish is fire-and-forget — a failed UpdatePolicyScheduleState leaves stale enforcement live (stale-permit-after-window fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-01)

Severity: MEDIUM-HIGH (security fail-open: stale permit after a scheduler window closes). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-163 (H4; folds L4/L10).

## Summary

Time-of-day `scheduler`-bound security policies are enforcement, not display.
When a scheduler window transitions, the daemon republishes the userspace
snapshot with new `inactive` bits — but the republish is fire-and-forget. Every
failure inside `UpdatePolicyScheduleState` logs a warning and returns; the
daemon caller has no error return, no retry, and no alarm. The previously
published snapshot stays live, so a scheduled PERMIT can remain active after
its window has CLOSED (or a scheduled block never engages).

## Provenance (origin/master 4cc1b9085)

- Daemon caller ignores the result entirely:
  `updatePolicyScheduleStateLocked` calls
  `updater.UpdatePolicyScheduleState(cfg, activeState)` with no error handling
  (`pkg/daemon/daemon_scheduler.go:151-163`); `publishPolicyScheduleState`
  likewise returns void (`:120-139`).
- `UpdatePolicyScheduleState` returns nothing and bails with `slog.Warn(...);
  return` on each failure — policy build, address-book build, disarm, and the
  helper `apply_snapshot` request (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager.go:794-826`).
- The mitigating comment ("the next full apply will surface the same error at
  commit time") does not apply to a time-driven transition: there is no commit
  and the next scheduler tick can be hours away.

## Runtime trace

1. A `workhours` window closes; `activeState["workhours"]` flips false.
2. The callback runs `UpdatePolicyScheduleState`.
3. The helper `apply_snapshot` (or a policy/address-book rebuild) fails
   transiently.
4. The method logs and returns; the daemon records no retry-needed state.
5. The old snapshot with the old `inactive` bits stays live -> the scheduled
   permit keeps forwarding after its window closed.

## #3781 — userspace-dp: ICMP AppID attribution ignores type/code — non-echo ICMP denies/sessions mislabel as junos-ping in RT_FLOW (AppCatalog wire row is L3/L4-only) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: MEDIUM (security-observability / log integrity — NOT a match fail-open). Class: driveable (interim) + design-fork (wire vNext). review: codex-review-163 (H1; folds M1/L1). Distinct from #3712 (that is the ICMP MATCH fail-open; this is the ICMP LOG/AppID label).

## Summary

Policy MATCHING for `junos-ping`/`junos-pingv6` is now echo-only (icmp_type in
`PolicyApplicationSnapshot`, #3020/#3194). But the AppID catalog used to STAMP
the app label on deny events and sessions has no ICMP type/code fields — it
resolves an ICMP packet by protocol alone. A non-echo ICMP packet (timestamp,
destination-unreachable, ICMPv6 NS/NA/RA) that correctly falls to default-deny
is then logged in RT_FLOW with the `junos-ping` app_id, even though it did not
match `junos-ping`. The verdict is correct; the audit label is wrong.

## Provenance (origin/master 4cc1b9085)

- `AppCatalogEntry` (Rust wire) has only app_id, protocol, dst_port_low/high,
  src_port_low/high — no icmp_type/icmp_code:

- The catalog comment itself documents "(0,0) dst-port means match on protocol
  alone, e.g. ICMP" (`protocol/security.rs:500-508`), so ANY ICMP resolves to
  the protocol-1 app in the catalog.

`show security flow session` and RT_FLOW policy-deny records name `junos-ping`
for ICMP that explicitly did not match it. For a security-sensitive allow/deny

## #3782 — userspace-dp: 'clear security policies hit-count' can wipe a post-clear hit — reset() bumps generation before zeroing, racing a worker batch flushed in the window (residual of #3448) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: LOW (counter-accuracy / audit; extremely narrow race window). Class: driveable-bug (design fix). review: codex-review-163 (H3; folds L2).

## Summary

The #3448 generation-discard fix makes a PRE-clear batch flushed after a clear
be discarded (correct). But `PolicyRuleCounter::reset()` bumps the generation
BEFORE it zeroes the counters, opening the inverse race: a POST-clear hit
captured under the new generation can be `add_batch`'d and then wiped by the
`packets.store(0)` that runs after the generation bump.

## Provenance (origin/master 4cc1b9085)

- `reset()` order: `generation.fetch_add(1, Relaxed)` then
  `packets.store(0)`/`bytes.store(0)` (Relaxed) — `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs`
  (PolicyRuleCounter::reset, ~1137-1144 per review; generation field doc at
  policy.rs:1130-1137).
- The coalescer captures `counter.generation()` and flushes a pending batch
  only if the generation still matches (`flush_pending_policy_hit_record`,
  `policy.rs:~1308-1316`).

## Runtime trace

1. clear: generation G -> G+1 (fetch_add).
2. Before `packets.store(0)` runs, a worker records a legitimate post-clear
   packet, captures generation G+1, hits its flush threshold and `add_batch`s
   (generation matches).
3. reset resumes: `packets.store(0)` wipes the post-clear hit.

Note: the window is two adjacent Relaxed stores (a few ns) AND requires the
worker to reach a flush boundary inside it, so this is a linearizability gap
rather than a field-observable loss. A plain store-before-bump reorder does NOT
fix it (it merely moves the losing window). The #3448 tests bypass the
thread-local coalescer under cfg(test) (`policy_tests.rs:5750-5865`), so
neither race direction is covered.

## Suggested fix

Make clear a two-phase / seqlocked epoch that establishes an ordering boundary
visible to workers (e.g. mark reset-in-progress, drain, then swap), and add a
loom-style or production-coalescer interleaving test for reset/record/flush.

*(truncated — 41 lines total)*

## #3783 — userspace-dp: wildcard/global-only policy deployments have no cold-path latency histogram slot — configured_zone_pairs() omits from-any/to-any/global tiers, samples silently dropped [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Severity: LOW-MEDIUM (observability gap for a common vSRX catch-all design). Class: driveable-bug. review: codex-review-163 (H5; folds L3).

## Summary

The cold-path first-packet latency histogram is built per concrete zone-pair
slot, but the slot set is derived only from the EXACT zone-pair index. A
deployment that uses only `from-zone any to-zone <z>` (or `to-zone any`, or
`security policies global`) rules produces no exact zone-pair entries, so the
concrete `(from, to)` a packet actually traverses has no histogram slot and the
latency sample is silently skipped — the instrumentation that is supposed to
prove first-packet policy health is dark for exactly the catch-all designs
operators commonly deploy.

## Provenance (origin/master 4cc1b9085)

- `configured_zone_pairs()` maps ONLY `self.zone_pair_index.keys()` (exact
  pairs), filtering reserved ids — `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:2079-2091`. It
  does not enumerate `from_any_index` / `to_any_index` / `both_any_indices` or
  global-policy scopes.
- `ColdPathSlotMap` is built from `state.policy.configured_zone_pairs()` —
  `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/mod.rs:333-338`.
- Recording is skipped on a `lookup_slot` miss —
  `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:2267-2282`.

## Runtime trace

1. Config has only `from-zone any to-zone untrust` and/or global rules; no
   exact zone-pair policy.
2. trust->untrust traffic is correctly evaluated by the wildcard/global tier.
3. The slot map has no `(trust, untrust)` slot -> `lookup_slot` returns None ->
   the latency sample is dropped.

## Suggested fix

Build histogram candidate pairs from the concrete zone-table cross-product
constrained by the wildcard/global policy scopes (or add a separate
wildcard/global bucket family). Add a fixture with only from-any / both-any /
scoped+unscoped global policies and assert the samples land.

## #3789 — snapshot: full-reconcile + same-plan-needs-reconcile legs swallow non-policy build failure (M1 sibling of #3766) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Follow-up from the #3766 (#3786) hostile review. #3766 made the same-plan snapshot-*refresh* leg fail-closed (build-fails → nack, no-persist, no split-brain). But two adjacent legs still swallow a NON-policy build failure:

- non-same-plan full-apply branch (`userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/snapshot.rs:~156-191`)
- same-plan `needs_reconcile==true` branch (`snapshot.rs:~106-109`)

Both call `reconcile_status_bindings` → `afxdp.reconcile`, which returns `()` and swallows a non-policy build failure. Prior forwarding is correctly kept fail-closed (per #2484/#2440), BUT the handler still stores `guard.snapshot`=rejected, sets `persist_state`, and reports `ok=true` — so a rejected snapshot is persisted as the boot baseline + acked positive (the same M1 class #3766 fixed for the refresh leg).

This is explicitly #2484's domain (full reconcile) and was out of #3766's scope; mitigated today by the Go commit-time gates + snapshot re-push on restart. Fix: make `afxdp.reconcile` (or the handler) observe the reconcile build result on these two legs — on failure return `ok=false` + do NOT store/persist the rejected snapshot (mirror #3766's handler pattern).

Severity: MEDIUM (persisted-reject + false-positive-ack; prior forwarding stays correct). review: #3786 hostile-review LOW/follow-up note.

## #3827 — routing: qualified-next-hop preference leaf is untyped — bypasses the Go primary preference gate (#3771 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Follow-up from the #3826 (#3771) hostile review. The route-level `preference` leaf is now typed `ValidateInteger(0, maxWireI32)` at the Go commit boundary (schema_routing.go, shared across top-level/rib/routing-instances), giving a commit-time rejection for a negative/overflow preference.

But the **`qualified-next-hop <addr> preference <n>`** schema leaf (schema_routing.go:88) remains **untyped**, and the compiler's flat-set walk folds it into `route.Preference` (compiler_routing.go:183-189). So a negative/overflow preference expressed via the qualified-next-hop syntax **bypasses the Go primary gate** and is caught only by the Rust `RoutePreferenceOutOfRange` backstop (#3826) — a fail-closed *snapshot rejection* (stale forwarding retained) rather than a clean commit-time error the operator sees immediately.

**Severity:** Low. No security invariant broken (no negative preference reaches the live FIB — the Rust backstop fail-closes). The value is unrealistic. This is a primary-gate *completeness* gap: the operator gets an opaque snapshot-rejection + retained-prior-state instead of a commit error naming the bad leaf.

**Fix:** apply the same `ValidateInteger(0, maxWireI32)` typing to the qualified-next-hop `preference` leaf at schema_routing.go:88 (mirror the route-level `preference` leaf) so it rejects at commit. Add a RED-on-revert schema-gate test (qualified-next-hop preference -1/overflow rejected, 0..2147483647 accepted). Go-only, no wire change.

Provenance: #3826 review (route/neighbor wire-integrity), finding 3 MINOR.

## #3830 — userspace-dp NAT: NatRuleCounter::reset uses store(0) — same clobber class as #3782 (narrower, cold-path) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-02)

Follow-up flagged by the #3829 (#3782) engineer. `NatRuleCounter::reset` (userspace-dp/src/nat/mod.rs:137) zeroes its counter with `store(0)`, the same primitive that #3782 replaced in `PolicyRuleCounter::reset` because a `store(0)` running after the clear-epoch bump unconditionally clobbers a concurrent post-clear `fetch_add`.

**Why narrower than #3782:** the NAT rule counter increments once per-flow on the COLD path with NO coalescer and NO generation/epoch guard, so the specific reset→record→flush interleaving that made #3782 reproducible does not exist here. The residual race is a much narrower per-flow increment landing in the same instant as a `clear`. Still the same `store(0)`-clobbers-concurrent-increment class.

**Fix:** mirror #3782 — replace `store(0)` with observe-then-`fetch_sub(observed)` (a `subtract_observed`-style helper) so a concurrent post-clear increment survives. Keep the per-flow increment a cheap relaxed `fetch_add` (cold path, unchanged). RED-on-revert: a concurrent post-clear NAT-rule increment is not lost by a clear.

**Severity:** Low (per-rule NAT hit-counter accuracy, observability; not enforcement/HA). Rust-only, no wire change.

Provenance: #3829 (clear security policies hit-count race) out-of-scope note.

## #3842 — policy: duplicate inner match/then blocks silently dropped + bypass all 6 strict gates → policy widens (fable-161 F-006) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master, empirical-probe-confirmed).

**Defect (HIGH, security fail-open, reachable via `load override`/`load merge`):** a security policy with DUPLICATE inner `match {}` or `then {}` blocks — `compiler_security.go:652,706` reads only the FIRST via `FindChild("match")`/`FindChild("then")` — silently drops the second block's constraints. Worse, the 6 policy strict-validation gates (compiler_policy_*.go checkPolicy closures) ALSO use FindChild-first-block, so a second block's content is never validated either. Net: an L7 application constraint or a deny in a duplicated block is discarded and the policy WIDENS with a clean commit.

#3562/#3377 fixed top-level and within-`then` duplicate blocks but NOT duplicate inner match/then blocks under one policy term.

**Fix:** the policy compiler + all 6 strict gates must ACCUMULATE across ALL `match`/`then` children (not FindChild-first-only), OR reject a duplicate inner block at commit (Junos merges them; xpf should merge-or-reject, never silently-drop-and-widen). The FindChild-first-block pattern is duplicated across compilePolicy + 4 gate closures (the review flags this as the root of the bug + a refactor opportunity — a shared accumulate helper).

**RED-on-revert:** a policy with two `match {}` blocks (second adds an application/from-address constraint, or a `then reject`) is enforced with BOTH constraints (or rejected at commit) — goes RED (widened / second block dropped) on revert.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-006, go-config-policy module.

## #3843 — firewall filter: hierarchical single-name source/destination-prefix-list leaf silently drops the scoping constraint → fail-wide (fable-161 F-001) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master, empirical-probe-confirmed).

**Defect (HIGH, fail-open):** a firewall-filter term with a hierarchical single-name `source-prefix-list <name>;` leaf (as produced by `load merge`/a config file, NOT flat-set) has its scoping constraint SILENTLY DROPPED — `compiler_firewall.go:287-303` iterates only `child.Children` and never reads `child.Keys[1]` (the prefix-list name in the single-leaf shape). The term then compiles UNSCOPED (matches everything) and passes strict commit cleanly. Same for `destination-prefix-list`.

This is the #2419 dual-AST-shape class but on the prefix-list-ref leaf specifically (distinct from #2506 which fixed prefix-list refs dropped in the dataplane snapshot — this is a compile-side AST-shape mechanism).

**Fix:** the source/destination-prefix-list case must read BOTH `child.Keys[1:]` (single-leaf/flat shape) AND `child.Children` (hierarchical multi-child shape) and accumulate — mirror `firewallMatchValues`/the #2419 fix. A dropped scope must be impossible; if unresolvable, fail-closed.

**RED-on-revert:** a term with a hierarchical `source-prefix-list plX;` scopes to plX's prefixes (goes RED — matches all / scope dropped — on revert); flat-set + multi-child shapes still work.

## #3844 — NAT: 'then destination-nat off' compiles to empty exemption → traffic still DNAT'd by later rules (fail-open) (fable-161 F-003) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master, empirical-probe-confirmed).

**Defect (HIGH, fail-open):** a DNAT rule `then destination-nat off` (Junos exemption — traffic matching this rule should NOT be DNAT'd) is ACCEPTED at commit but the then-parser at `compiler_nat.go:1587` recognizes only `pool` → the exemption compiles to an EMPTY Then (Type=0, pool="") and is SKIPPED at the snapshot builder (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat.go:692`). So the "exempted" traffic is NOT exempted — it falls through and is DNAT'd by later matching rules (fail-open — traffic goes somewhere the operator explicitly exempted). SNAT handles `source-nat off` correctly, so this is DNAT-specific.

Empirical: probe confirmed `then destination-nat off` passes SchemaValidate+CompileConfig yielding Then.Type=0/pool="".

**Fix (minimal):** reject `then destination-nat off` at commit until it's modeled (fail-closed — the operator gets an error, not silent non-exemption). **Full fix:** model an `Off`/exempt flag through the Go Then + the Rust DNAT snapshot so the rule is a real no-translate exemption that SHORT-CIRCUITS later DNAT rules (the Junos semantic). Prefer the full fix if the Rust DNAT path can express a no-op exemption; else commit-reject now + file the Rust follow-up.

**RED-on-revert:** `then destination-nat off` either exempts the traffic (no DNAT applied, later rules short-circuited) OR is rejected at commit — goes RED (silently compiles empty + traffic still DNAT'd) on revert.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-003, go-config-nat module.

## #3846 — config: 'delete ... <multi-leaf> <member>' deletes the WHOLE bracket-list, not just the member (fail-wide) (fable-161 F-004) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master, empirical-probe-confirmed).

**Defect (HIGH, config-integrity fail-wide):** on a `multi: true` leaf that holds a bracket-list (e.g. `from protocol [ tcp udp icmp ]`, firewall/policy match values, host-inbound services), a `delete ... from protocol tcp` command PREFIX-MATCHES the leaf node and deletes the ENTIRE list — udp + icmp are silently gone too. And a NON-FIRST member is undeletable (the delete matches the whole node, not the member). `ast_edit.go:492` (`removeMatchingNode`/`keysMatch` in `deletePath`) has no multi-leaf branch: it matches the leaf by its first key and removes the whole node.

This is the delete-side counterpart of the #2419 multi-value-leaf class (which fixed the compile/read side). An operator intending to narrow a firewall/policy match by removing ONE protocol instead widens it (removes the whole constraint), or intending to remove one host-inbound service removes them all — a config-integrity + potential fail-open (a removed match constraint widens the term).

**Fix:** `deletePath` must handle a multi-leaf specially — when the delete path's final token names a MEMBER of a multi-value leaf (the node's `Keys[1:]`/children hold the members), remove ONLY that member from the leaf (and if it was the last member, remove the leaf). Deleting the leaf itself (no trailing member) still removes the whole list. Mirror how the multi-leaf is READ (Keys[1:]+Children per #2419) on the delete side. Make a non-first member deletable.

**RED-on-revert:** `delete ... from protocol tcp` on `[ tcp udp icmp ]` leaves `[ udp icmp ]` (goes RED — whole list deleted — on revert); `delete ... from protocol udp` (non-first member) removes only udp; deleting the whole `from protocol` leaf still clears it. Test via ParseSetCommand+SetPath to build the list, then ParseDeleteCommand/the delete path.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-004, go-config-parse module.

## #3849 — scheduler: compileSchedulers never descends into 'daily { start-time/stop-time }' → time-restricted permit runs 24/7 (fail-open) (fable-161 F-014) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master, empirical-probe-confirmed).

**Defect (HIGH, fail-open):** `compileSchedulers` (`compiler_system.go:1071`) never descends into the Junos `daily { start-time ...; stop-time ...; }` container (nor the `monday`..`sunday` day arms) → the scheduler's `StartTime`/`StopTime` are left EMPTY → at runtime `isWithinWindow` returns TRUE for an empty window → a policy with `scheduler-name <s>` (time-restricted permit) is ACTIVE 24/7 instead of only within the configured window. A rule the operator scoped to business hours permits traffic around the clock (security fail-open).

**Fix:** `compileSchedulers` must descend into the `daily {}` container and the per-day (`monday`..`sunday`) containers, reading `start-time`/`stop-time` (and the day-of-week schedule) into the scheduler's StartTime/StopTime/day fields. Handle both the hierarchical (`daily { start-time X; stop-time Y; }`) and flat-set shapes. Fail-closed alternative if a window can't be parsed: reject at commit (an unparseable time window must not silently become always-on). Verify `isWithinWindow` treats an ABSENT window correctly (the current always-true-on-empty behavior is the fail-open half — an empty window on a referenced scheduler should be a commit error or a closed window, not always-open).

**RED-on-revert:** a scheduler with `daily { start-time 09:00:00; stop-time 17:00:00; }` yields a window that `isWithinWindow` honors (permit inactive outside 9-5) — goes RED (window empty → active 24/7) on revert; a scheduler without a window is rejected at commit or treated as closed.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-014, go-conntrack-appid module (compileSchedulers). Related: F-013 (schedulers stanza missing from setSchema).

## #3850 — config: NAT-rule + filter-term duplicate match/then blocks still read first-block-only (fail-open sibling of #3842) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Follow-up flagged by the #3847 (#3842/F-006) hostile review. #3842 fixed duplicate inner match/then blocks for SECURITY POLICIES (accumulate across all blocks + all 6 gates). But the SAME first-block-only fail-open class remains in sibling constructs the review identified:

- **NAT rules** (`compiler_nat.go`): a NAT rule's duplicate `match {}`/`then {}` blocks are read first-block-only → a second match block's constraint (or a second then's action) silently dropped → NAT rule widens/mis-translates.
- **Firewall filter terms** (`compiler_firewall.go`): a filter term's duplicate `from {}`/`then {}` blocks likewise first-block-only.
- **pre-id-default-policy** (`compiler_security.go:220`): singleton `then` read first-block-only (narrow surface, lower priority).

Same mechanism as #3842: `FindChild("match"/"then"/"from")` first-block-only where `load merge`/`load override` can produce two sibling blocks. Reachable via config-file/merge, silent-drop-and-widen on clean commit.

**Fix:** apply the #3842 accumulate pattern (read across ALL sibling match/then/from blocks, or reject a duplicate at commit) to the NAT-rule + filter-term compilers and their strict gates. Reuse/generalize the policyMatchChildren/policyThenChildren/policyThenActionNodes helpers where the AST shape matches.

**Also (minor, from the same review):** #3842 now over-rejects two IDENTICAL terminal-action blocks as 'conflicting permit,permit' (fail-closed/safe but imprecise) — dedup identical terminal actions before the #3043 count so an identical-duplicate merges silently (Junos-faithful) instead of erroring.

Provenance: #3847 hostile review, non-blocking notes.

## #3851 — ipsec: normalizeAuthAlg strips all dashes → canonical Junos 'hmac-sha-256-128' becomes strongSwan-invalid → whole ESP proposal rejected, tunnel never loads (fable-161 F-017) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, whole-feature dead / silent VPN outage):** `normalizeAuthAlg` (`pkg/ipsec/ike.go:256`) strips the `hmac-` prefix AND all dashes, so a canonical Junos ESP auth-algorithm name maps to a strongSwan-INVALID token:
- `hmac-sha-256-128` → `sha256128` (invalid)
- `hmac-sha1-96` → `sha196` (invalid)

strongSwan rejects the whole ESP proposal containing the invalid token → the IPsec tunnel never loads, with no useful diagnostic. The tests currently PIN the invalid spelling (so they pass while production is broken). Only the dangling-proposal fallback was hardcoded to `sha256`; the normal path is still broken.

**Fix:** `normalizeAuthAlg` must map Junos auth-algorithm names to the strongSwan-VALID integrity-algorithm tokens: `hmac-sha-256-128`/`hmac-sha256-128` → `sha256`, `hmac-sha-384-192` → `sha384`, `hmac-sha-512-256` → `sha512`, `hmac-sha1-96`/`hmac-sha1` → `sha1`, `hmac-md5-96` → `md5` (map the Junos truncated-length suffixes to the base strongSwan algorithm). Do NOT naively strip dashes. Update the tests to pin the VALID strongSwan output (the current tests pin the broken form — that's why the bug shipped). Verify against a strongSwan proposal string that swanctl/charon accepts.

**RED-on-revert:** `hmac-sha-256-128` compiles to a proposal containing `sha256` (a strongSwan-valid integ token) — goes RED (`sha256128` invalid) on revert; the full ESP proposal string is accepted by strongSwan syntax.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-017, go-ipsec-wg module.

## #3854 — config: quoteKey escapes quotes but not backslashes → Format→Parse round-trip corrupts values (incl IKE PSK) → HA config-sync diverges standby (fable-161 F-005) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, HA config-integrity divergence):** `quoteKey` (`ast.go:78-87`) escapes embedded quotes but NEVER escapes backslashes, while the LEXER interprets `\n`/`\\` on parse. So any config value containing a backslash (e.g. an IKE pre-shared-key `ascii-text` with a `\`, or any string leaf) CORRUPTS on every Format→Parse round-trip: Format emits the raw backslash, the lexer then re-interprets it → the parsed value differs from the original. Consequences: (a) HA config sync (which Format→wire→Parse) silently DIVERGES the standby's PSK from the active → IPsec fails to re-establish on failover; (b) rollback slots serialized via Format become uncommittable/corrupted (a config with a backslash round-trips to a different, possibly invalid, config).

**Fix:** `quoteKey` must escape backslashes (`\` → `\\`) BEFORE (or together with) escaping quotes, symmetric with what the lexer un-escapes on parse. Verify the full escape set is round-trip-symmetric: whatever the lexer interprets (`\\`, `\"`, `\n`, ...) must be escaped by quoteKey so Format(Parse(x)) == x and Parse(Format(x)) == x for all values. Add a round-trip property test over values containing backslashes, quotes, and newlines.

**RED-on-revert:** a config value (e.g. an IKE PSK) containing a backslash round-trips identically through Format→Parse (goes RED — corrupted/diverged — on revert); the same for quotes + newlines; the round-trip is idempotent.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-005, go-config-parse module. HA-adjacent (config sync + rollback serialization).

## #3855 — routing: routing-instance kernel TableIDs are positional → deleting/reordering one renumbers survivors → vrf.go recreates untouched live VRF devices (forwarding outage on unrelated VRFs) (fable-161 F-007) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, HA/routing outage on UNRELATED VRFs):** `compileRoutingInstances` (`compiler_routing.go:276-287`) assigns each routing-instance a kernel routing TableID POSITIONALLY (100, 101, 102, … by config order). Deleting or reordering ONE routing-instance RENUMBERS all survivors that follow it. `pkg/routing/vrf.go:231-249` then detects the table-id mismatch on the survivors and RECREATES those live VRF devices (link down/up + route reprogram) — a forwarding OUTAGE on VRFs the operator never touched. On an HA pair this happens on BOTH nodes. This is the same positional-identity class the project already solved for zone ids with #3075 (StableZoneID) and #3395 (stable policy_id).

**Fix:** derive each routing-instance's TableID from a STABLE, config-derived identity (a name-hash into a reserved table-id range, HA-symmetric, mirroring `config.StableZoneID`/#1873 StableTunnelEndpointID) instead of positional assignment. A routing-instance's TableID must be a pure function of its NAME (+ family), so adding/removing/reordering a sibling never renumbers an untouched instance → vrf.go never recreates a live VRF it shouldn't. Handle collisions the way #3719 handled StableZoneID collisions (detect + quarantine/fail-closed). Preserve the existing table-id range conventions.

**RED-on-revert:** given instances [A,B,C] compiled to stable TableIDs, DELETING B leaves A and C with their ORIGINAL TableIDs (goes RED — C renumbers → vrf.go recreates C — on revert); reordering doesn't renumber; a new instance gets a fresh stable id without disturbing existing ones. Test the compiler TableID assignment + assert vrf.go's recreate-on-mismatch is not triggered for untouched instances.

**test-failover WARRANTED:** VRF TableID stability is HA-adjacent (both nodes, forwarding). Validate on the loss cluster that a routing-instance add/delete does not disturb unrelated VRF forwarding.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-007, go-config-routing-services module. Pattern: mirror #3075 StableZoneID. Related open follow-up class.

## #3857 — userspace-dp NAT: DNAT rule with match application + destination-port widens invalid port to wildcard [0,0] on lenient/peer-sync path → fail-open bypassing #3446 (fable-161 F-018) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, fail-open bypassing #3446):** the DNAT snapshot builder (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat.go:824,900,935-949,1021`) for a DNAT rule that has BOTH `match application` AND `match destination-port` mishandles the port on the lenient/peer-sync path:
- (a) an INVALID port token widens to wildcard `[0,0]` (match-any-port) — a fail-open that bypasses the #3446 dport-wildcard/amplification guard;
- (b) a VALID port is ignored (dropped) when application is also present;
- (c) a multi-port list collapses to the first port only.

The SNAT builder does it correctly, so this is DNAT-specific. On the lenient (no-brick #1960) / HA peer-sync decode path, a corrupt/mixed-version snapshot with an unparseable DNAT destination-port silently becomes match-ANY-port → the DNAT rule translates traffic on ports the operator never intended (fail-open).

**Fix:** the DNAT builder must, when both application and destination-port are present, (a) FAIL-CLOSED on an invalid/unrepresentable destination-port (reject the rule / omit it, retain prior state — do NOT widen to [0,0]); (b) HONOR the valid destination-port alongside the application (not ignore it); (c) preserve the FULL multi-port list (not collapse to first) — mirror the SNAT builder + the #3446/#3491 dport handling. Likely a Rust userspace-dp change (the decode/build path) — if so, run FULL cargo test --release; and possibly a Go builder change.

**RED-on-revert:** a DNAT rule with match application + an invalid destination-port is rejected/omitted (NOT wildcard [0,0]) — goes RED (widens to match-any, bypasses #3446) on revert; a valid destination-port is honored alongside application; a multi-port list keeps all ports. Use the lenient/peer-sync decode path (a crafted/corrupt snapshot) since that's where the widening happens.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-018, go-usdp-programs module.

## #3860 — scheduler: warn at commit when a scheduler defines no window (silent always-on→fail-closed migration surface) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Follow-up from the #3858 (#3849/F-014) hostile review — MINOR, non-blocking.

#3858 correctly flipped an empty scheduler window from always-on (the fail-open bug) to fail-closed-inactive. But a DEGENERATE defined-but-windowless scheduler — `scheduler x {}` or `scheduler x { daily; }` (no start/stop, no all-day, no per-day, no date-range) — silently flips from always-on to fail-closed INACTIVE with NO dedicated commit warning or runtime log (only half-windows and unparseable times log today). Direction is safe (the config is nonsensical), but an operator migrating a config that relied on the old always-on bug loses enforcement silently.

**Fix:** emit a commit-time validation WARNING (the existing config-validation-warnings mechanism) when a scheduler compiles with no effective window: "scheduler <X> defines no time window; policies bound to it will be INACTIVE (use `daily all-day` for always-on)." Optionally a one-time runtime log when such a scheduler is loaded. This surfaces the always-on→fail-closed migration flip.

Also (from the same review, DOC-only): an overnight window (22:00-06:00) combined with per-day overrides resolves the post-midnight tail against the NEXT day's window rather than carrying the prior day's overnight window — matches/exceeds prior single-daily behavior; worth a doc note in pkg/scheduler/README.md.

Provenance: #3858 hostile review, minor observations 1+2.

## #3861 — configstore: plain Store.Commit / SyncApply during a commit-confirmed window does not stop the timer → newer commit silently reverted to T0 (fable-161 F-012) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, silent config loss):** while a `commit confirmed` window is pending (a rollback timer armed), a PLAIN `Store.Commit` — the path the eventengine remediation uses, which bypasses the frontend confirm-dance — does NOT stop the pending-commit timer nor bump the generation. `store_commit.go:63` (`CommitWithDescription`) + `store.go:356`. So when the timer later fires, it reverts the store + disk + dataplane back to T0, silently DISCARDING the newer commit the eventengine (or any non-frontend caller) just made. Same for `SyncApply` (HA config-sync apply arms no timer / doesn't clear a pending one).

Sequence: (1) operator `commit confirmed 5`; (2) eventengine remediation fires `Store.Commit` at T+2 (new config C2 applied); (3) at T+5 the unconfirmed-commit timer reverts to T0 (the config before `commit confirmed`), discarding C2. The operator sees C2 committed, then it silently vanishes.

**Fix:** `Store.Commit`/`CommitWithDescription` (and `SyncApply`) must, when a commit-confirmed timer is pending, STOP/clear that timer (a new explicit commit CONFIRMS the pending one — Junos semantics: any subsequent `commit` confirms a `commit confirmed`) and bump the generation. So a plain commit during the window is treated as the confirmation, not ignored. Verify the eventengine remediation path + the HA SyncApply path both clear the pending timer. Do NOT let a background commit be silently undone.

**RED-on-revert:** arm a commit-confirmed timer, then call `Store.Commit` (plain) with a new config; after the confirm window elapses the NEW config is still active (goes RED — reverted to T0, new commit discarded — on revert). Same for SyncApply.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-012, go-configstore module.

## #3863 — config: WireGuard tunnel local identity (listen-port/private-key) never validated at commit → malformed value commits clean then Rust drops the whole tunnel row → tunnel permanently dead, no signal (fable-161 F-011) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, silent VPN outage):** a WireGuard tunnel's LOCAL identity — `listen-port` and `private-key` — is never validated at commit (`compiler_validate_wireguard.go:112` validates peers but not the local identity). So `listen-port 0`, a `listen-port` out of the 1-65535 range, or a malformed/wrong-length `private-key` COMMITS CLEAN. Then at runtime the Rust `hydrate_wg_identity` fails to parse the identity and DROPS THE WHOLE TUNNEL ROW → the tunnel is permanently dead with no diagnostic (the operator sees a committed config but no tunnel).

**Fix:** extend the WireGuard commit validation (`compiler_validate_wireguard.go`) to validate the LOCAL identity: `listen-port` in [1,65535] (reject 0/out-of-range); `private-key` is a valid WireGuard key (correct base64 length/decode — 32 bytes / 44-char base64, mirror how the peer public-key is validated). A malformed local identity must be a COMMIT ERROR (fail-closed — the operator gets an error), never a clean commit that silently produces a dead tunnel. Match the Rust `hydrate_wg_identity` parse requirements exactly so anything that would drop the row at runtime is rejected at commit.

**RED-on-revert:** `listen-port 0` / `listen-port 99999` / a malformed `private-key` is REJECTED at commit (goes RED — commits clean then dead tunnel — on revert); a valid identity commits + hydrates. Verify against the Rust hydrate_wg_identity parse rules.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-011, go-config-validate module.

## #3867 — config archive: transfer-on-commit scps the boot-time /etc/xpf/xpf.conf (never rewritten since configstore became DB-canonical) → every archive uploads the day-0 config (fable-161 F-015) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, silent DR/compliance corruption):** `archiveConfig` (transfer-on-commit, `daemon_flow.go:228`) scps `d.opts.ConfigFile` — the BOOT-TIME `/etc/xpf/xpf.conf` — which nothing rewrites post-boot since the configstore became DB-canonical (the active config lives in the configstore DB, not the boot file). So every `system archival configuration` transfer-on-commit uploads the DAY-0 config, not the config that was just committed. scp logs success → the DR / compliance archive is systematically wrong (it never reflects any post-boot commit). An operator relying on transfer-on-commit for config backup has archives that silently diverge from the running config from the first commit onward.

**Fix:** `archiveConfig` must serialize + upload the CURRENT ACTIVE config from the configstore (the committed config text — e.g. via the store's active-config serializer / the same path `show configuration` uses), NOT the stale boot file `d.opts.ConfigFile`. Write the active config to a temp file (or stream it) and scp THAT. Verify the archived bytes == the just-committed config (a round-trip check). Consider including the commit metadata (who/when/comment) the operator expects.

**RED-on-revert:** commit a config change C1, trigger transfer-on-commit, fetch the archived file — it equals C1 (the just-committed config), NOT the boot config (goes RED — archives the day-0 boot file — on revert). Test the archive-source selection (active-config serializer vs d.opts.ConfigFile).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-015, go-daemon-svc module.

## #3868 — HA: commit-confirmed timeout rollback reverts only the active node — standby keeps the unconfirmed config as permanent active (SyncApply arms no timer) → failover serves the abandoned config (fable-161 F-150) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master). Sibling of #3861/F-012 (commit-confirmed timer) — DIFFERENT layer (daemon HA), fixed separately.

**Defect (HIGH, HA config divergence):** on a `commit confirmed` that TIMES OUT, `executeConfirmedRollback` (`daemon_apply.go:335`) reverts only the ACTIVE (local) node. But the standby ALREADY received the unconfirmed config via config-sync (`SyncApply`, which arms NO confirm timer), so the standby holds the unconfirmed config as its PERMANENT active. `executeConfirmedRollback` never calls `syncConfigToPeer` to push the rollback. Result: after a confirm-timeout rollback, the two nodes DIVERGE — and on failover the standby serves the ABANDONED (unconfirmed, auto-rolled-back) config.

Sequence: (1) `commit confirmed 5` on primary → config C2 syncs to standby (standby applies C2 permanently, no timer); (2) operator does NOT confirm; (3) at T+5 the primary rolls back to C1 (executeConfirmedRollback); (4) primary=C1, standby=C2 — DIVERGED; (5) failover → standby serves C2, the config the operator explicitly let expire.

**Fix:** `executeConfirmedRollback` (the confirm-timeout rollback path) must RE-SYNC the rolled-back config to the peer (call `syncConfigToPeer` / the config-sync push with the C1 rollback target) so the standby converges to the confirmed (rolled-back) config. Both nodes must end on C1. Guard for the peer being absent/disconnected (best-effort re-sync, retried on reconnect via the existing reverse-sync). Coordinate with #3861 (the store-side timer clear) — this is the daemon-side HA half.

**RED-on-revert / test-failover:** arm a `commit confirmed` (C2 syncs to standby), let it time out; after rollback BOTH nodes are on C1 (goes RED — standby stuck on C2, diverged — on revert); a failover after the rollback serves C1. Unit-test the executeConfirmedRollback→syncConfigToPeer call; test-failover WARRANTED (HA config convergence).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-150, go-daemon-lifecycle module.

## #3870 — routing: 'routing-options autonomous-system' parsed but never feeds BGP → canonical vSRX BGP config renders no BGP at all, no diagnostic (fable-161 F-009) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, whole-feature silently dead):** `routing-options autonomous-system <N>` is parsed into `ro.AutonomousSystem` (`compiler_routing.go:11`) but has NO consumer in pkg/frr — `router bgp` is gated on `bgp.LocalAS > 0` (`pkg/frr/policy_render.go:622`), and ONLY `protocols bgp local-as` sets LocalAS. So a canonical vSRX config that sets the AS at `routing-options autonomous-system` (the standard Junos placement) renders NO BGP at all, with no diagnostic — BGP silently does not come up.

**Fix:** feed `ro.AutonomousSystem` into the BGP AS resolution — `router bgp` should use `protocols bgp local-as` if set, ELSE `routing-options autonomous-system` (the Junos precedence: local-as overrides the global AS). Wire `ro.AutonomousSystem` → the frr BGP render's LocalAS resolution. A config with only `routing-options autonomous-system` + `protocols bgp` must render `router bgp <N>`.

**RED-on-revert:** a config with `routing-options autonomous-system 65001` + `protocols bgp group X neighbor Y` renders `router bgp 65001` (goes RED — no `router bgp` line — on revert); `protocols bgp local-as` still overrides.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-009, go-config-routing-services module. FILE-COUPLED with F-008/F-010 (same compiler_routing.go) — will be fixed together in one routing PR.

## #3871 — routing: qualified-next-hop preference/metric declared but folded into a single route-level Preference → floating static becomes equal-cost ECMP over the backup (fable-161 F-008) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, floating-static broken → traffic over backup path):** a static route's `qualified-next-hop <gw> { preference N; metric M; }` — the Junos idiom for a FLOATING static (a primary next-hop + a less-preferred backup) — has its per-next-hop preference/metric SCHEMA-DECLARED (`schema_routing.go` qualified-next-hop children) but the compiler folds them into a SINGLE route-level `Preference` (`compiler_routing.go:222` + `types_routing.go:164`) rather than carrying them per-next-hop. `pkg/frr/config_render.go:120,164` then renders all next-hops at equal cost → the floating static becomes EQUAL-COST ECMP, so traffic load-balances over the BACKUP path instead of preferring the primary and only failing over when it drops.

**Fix:** carry `preference` (and `metric`) PER-QUALIFIED-NEXT-HOP through the typed config (types_routing.go — a per-next-hop preference/metric field) and render each next-hop with its own admin distance in FRR (`config_render.go`) so the higher-preference (lower-distance) next-hop is primary and the qualified-next-hop is a true floating backup (installed only when the primary is down). Match Junos floating-static semantics.

**RED-on-revert:** a static route with a primary next-hop + a `qualified-next-hop <gw> { preference 250; }` renders the primary at the default distance and the qualified-NH at distance ~250 (floating — not installed while primary is up) — goes RED (both equal-cost ECMP over the backup) on revert. Note #3827 only added value-range TYPING for qualified-NH preference, not the floating behavior.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-008, go-config-routing-services module. FILE-COUPLED with F-009/F-010.

## #3872 — routing: static route 'next-hop [ gw1 gw2 ]' bracket list collapses to one next-hop → canonical Junos ECMP silently loses multipath (fable-161 F-010) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, ECMP silently lost):** a static route `next-hop [ gw1 gw2 ]` (the canonical Junos ECMP spelling — multiple next-hops = equal-cost multipath) COLLAPSES to a single next-hop: the schema leaf is not `multi: true` (`schema_routing.go:80`) and the compiler reads one address (`compiler_routing.go:199,224`). So the operator's ECMP config silently loses multipath and installs only the first gateway.

**Fix:** make the static-route `next-hop` leaf `multi: true` in setSchema (schema_routing.go) so a bracket list groups onto one leaf (the #2419 pattern), and read ALL next-hops (`child.Keys[1:]` + children, accumulate) in the compiler (compiler_routing.go) → install every gateway as an equal-cost next-hop in FRR. NOTE: this must compose with F-008 (qualified-next-hop per-NH preference) — a plain `next-hop [ a b ]` list is equal-cost ECMP; a `qualified-next-hop` is a floating backup. Keep the two distinct.

**RED-on-revert:** `next-hop [ 10.0.0.1 10.0.0.2 ]` installs BOTH as equal-cost (goes RED — only 10.0.0.1 installed — on revert); a single `next-hop 10.0.0.1` still works. Test via ParseSetCommand+SetPath.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-010, go-config-schema module. FILE-COUPLED with F-008/F-009 (combine into one routing PR).

## #3874 — syslog: octet-counted (RFC 6587) stream write-timeout can leave a partial frame on the wire → permanent framing desync at the collector (fable-161 F-151) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, audit/forensics channel corruption under load):** the syslog TCP/TLS stream client uses RFC 6587 octet-counted framing (`<len> <msg>`). A write-timeout can leave a PARTIAL frame `0<n<len` bytes on the wire, and the timeout branch (`pkg/logging/syslog.go:470`) returns WITHOUT closing the connection (deliberate, per #2287 which avoided a re-entrant-deadlock close). So the NEXT frame's bytes concatenate onto the truncated frame → the collector's octet-count parser is permanently DESYNCED (it reads the wrong length, mis-frames every subsequent message) until an unrelated connection reset. This corrupts the audit/forensics channel exactly under incident load (when writes are slow / the collector is backpressured — precisely when the logs matter most).

**Fix:** on a PARTIAL write (0<n<len) — as distinct from a clean 0-byte timeout — the connection MUST be torn down (or the stream re-synced) so the collector never sees a truncated frame followed by a fresh frame. A partial octet-counted frame is unrecoverable in-stream — the only correct recovery is to close+reconnect (the next frame starts a fresh, correctly-counted stream). Distinguish the partial-write case from the clean-timeout case at syslog.go:470; close on partial (carefully, preserving the #2287 no-re-entrant-deadlock property — close OUTSIDE the slog/mutex re-entry path, or set a flag to close on the next send). Do NOT leave a half-frame + continue.

**RED-on-revert:** a write that returns 0<n<len (partial) triggers a connection close/resync so the next frame is not concatenated onto the truncated one (goes RED — partial frame + next frame concatenated, collector desynced — on revert); a clean 0-byte timeout behaves as before (#2287); no re-entrant deadlock (the #2285/#2287 property preserved). Test with a mock conn returning a short write.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-151, go-obs module. Interacts with #2287 (the deliberate no-close-on-timeout) — preserve its deadlock fix while handling the partial-write case.

## #3876 — routing: rib-group import ip-rule at pref 33000 sits AFTER main (32766) → default route shadows it → imported interface routes never consulted; feature is a no-op in real deployments (fable-161 F-016) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master). DESIGN DECISION → /research.

**Defect (HIGH, advertised feature is a no-op):** rib-group import installs an ip-rule at preference 33000 (`pkg/routing/rules.go:231,297`) which sits AFTER the main table's rule (32766). Any main-table default route therefore SHADOWS the import rule → the imported interface routes are never consulted. The userspace leak snapshot ALSO skips `rule.Dst==nil` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:160`) → the leak is absent from BOTH FIBs. So rib-group inter-VRF route import (an advertised feature) is a no-op in any deployment that has a default route (i.e. essentially all of them). #3731 fixed only the RuleAdd error-aggregation, a different mechanism.

**Why /research (design decision — multiple viable mechanisms):**
1. **route-copy** — actually COPY the imported routes into the target table (like FRR's `import` / Junos rib-group route installation) rather than a priority rule. Most Junos-faithful; needs route lifecycle management (add/withdraw on the source route's churn).
2. **per-prefix dst-rules** — install a `to <prefix>` ip-rule per imported prefix at a preference BEFORE main (< 32766), so the specific imported prefixes win over the default. Bounded by prefix count; needs churn handling.
3. **warn/reject** — if neither is feasible now, detect + WARN at commit that rib-group import won't take effect with a default route present (fail-loud rather than silent no-op).

Also fix the userspace leak snapshot to not skip `rule.Dst==nil` (or handle the chosen mechanism's snapshot form) so the leak is present in the userspace FIB too.

Deliverable: converged PLAN (route-copy vs per-prefix-rules vs warn) recorded on this issue, then /engineer. Provenance: fable-review-161 F-016, go-frr-routing module.

## #3878 — event-stream: cross-worker seq allocate/enqueue not atomic + Go reader zero reorder tolerance → out-of-order frame → spurious owner-RG resync + disconnect, self-amplifying during recovery (fable-161 F-152) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master). Includes the F-153 residual (try_send Full burns a seq).

**Defect (HIGH, HA session-sync self-amplifying instability):** the event-stream cross-worker sequence allocation + enqueue is NOT atomic (`userspace-dp/src/event_stream/mod.rs:558,586,1463`). Two workers can allocate seq N and N+1 but enqueue/flush them out of order → an out-of-order frame reaches the wire. The Go reader (`pkg/cluster/eventstream.go:404`) has ZERO reorder tolerance → treats a seq inversion as a session-sync GAP → triggers a spurious FULL owner-RG resync + disconnect. During recovery (when reordering is most likely) this is SELF-AMPLIFYING: the resync churn causes more reordering causes more resync.

**F-153 residual (fold in):** the `try_send` Full (channel-saturation) path at `producer.rs:336-343` still BURNS a seq without rollback; since `prevSeq` is shared, a burned seq trips the NEXT session frame's gap check → resync. (#3395 was a different positional-id fix; the seq-atomicity gap is distinct.)

**Fix (design — the review flagged 3 angles; pick the soundest):**
1. **Producer-lock seq atomicity** — allocate the seq UNDER the producer lock, atomically with the commit-to-queue decision, so seq order == wire order AND a dropped/Full frame does NOT burn a seq (allocate only after the frame is committed). This is the most contained fix and covers the F-153 residual (a Full drop rolls back / never allocates).
2. **IO-thread re-sequence** — a single IO thread assigns seq at dequeue (serializes wire order regardless of producer race).
3. **Reader reorder-window** — the Go reader tolerates a small reorder window before declaring a gap (defense-in-depth; doesn't fix the producer race but stops the spurious resync).

Recommend (1) [+ possibly (3) as belt-and-suspenders]. The seq that lands on the wire MUST be monotonic per the reader's contract; a saturation-drop must not burn a seq.

**Validation:** FULL cargo test --release; test-failover WARRANTED (HA session-sync — this is the recovery-churn path). RED-on-revert: an out-of-order producer race + a Full-drop do NOT produce a wire seq gap / spurious resync (goes RED — gap → resync — on revert); the reader sees monotonic seq; a saturation drop doesn't trip the next frame's gap check.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-152 (+ F-153 residual), go-usdp-ha-events module. RUST (cargo) + Go reader.

## #3881 — routing: hierarchical inline-keys static route drops 'interface' modifier → IPv6 link-local next-hop unresolvable (Copilot on #3879) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Follow-up from Copilot inline review on PR #3879 (routing next-hop cluster). Pre-existing (the #3879 hostile review confirmed this form was already broken pre-PR + is not produced by SetPath or the brace parser — the brace/flat-set form `next-hop fe80::1 interface reth0.50` works correctly). Filed rather than folded to keep #3879 scoped.

**Defect (MEDIUM):** in the HIERARCHICAL INLINE-keys route form (a route node with NO Children, e.g. `route 2001:db8::/32 next-hop fe80::1 interface reth0.50;` on one line without braces), the multi-value next-hop absorber (compiler_routing.go:180) correctly stops before the `interface` keyword (it's a route keyword), but the inline-keys switch has NO logic to consume `interface <if>` as a modifier of the preceding gateway → the egress interface is DROPPED. For an IPv6 LINK-LOCAL next-hop (fe80::/10), the egress interface is REQUIRED (a link-local nexthop is ambiguous/unresolvable without it) → the route is unresolvable/misinstalled.

Also (compiler_routing.go:254, Copilot comment 1, negligible edge): a next-hop value literally named `interface` is treated as the modifier keyword even as the FIRST value → dropped/misparsed. Restrict the `interface` keyword handling to act as a modifier ONLY when ≥1 gateway has already been parsed.

**Fix:** in the inline-keys route parse (the no-Children route form), after the next-hop gateway run, consume a trailing `interface <if>` as the modifier of the preceding gateway (mirror the brace-form handling that already works). AND restrict the `interface`-keyword detection to fire only after ≥1 gateway is parsed (so a bare-first `interface` token is a gateway value, not the modifier).

**RED-on-revert:** `route 2001:db8::/32 next-hop fe80::1 interface reth0.50;` (hierarchical inline, no braces) compiles with the next-hop carrying interface=reth0.50 (goes RED — interface dropped, link-local unresolvable — on revert); the brace form + flat-set form still work; a gateway literally "interface" as first value parses as a gateway.

Provenance: Copilot inline review on #3879 (compiler_routing.go:180 + :254); #3879 hostile-review finding 2 (pre-existing, out-of-scope).

## #3882 — WireGuard: responder rekey promotes an UNCONFIRMED session straight to current (no 'next' keypair slot) → peer-initiated rekey blackholes xpf→peer egress, replayable → persistent egress DoS (fable-161 F-019) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (HIGH, security — replayable egress DoS):** the userspace WireGuard implementation uses a 2-slot keypair model (current/previous) with NO `next` slot. When xpf is the RESPONDER to a rekey, `peer.rs:99-140` promotes the UNCONFIRMED new session straight into `current` (before the initiator's first data packet confirms it — kernel WireGuard keeps it in `next` until the first valid inbound data packet on it). So egress (`engine.rs:957-979`) reads `current` = the unconfirmed keypair → the peer hasn't finished the handshake on that keypair → `NoSession` / the peer drops it → every PEER-INITIATED rekey BLACKHOLES the xpf→peer egress direction until the next rekey. Worse: with no handshake anti-replay, a replayed handshake-init can force this repeatedly → a PERSISTENT egress DoS.

**Fix (design — mirror kernel WireGuard's 3-slot keypair):** add a `next` keypair slot. On a responder rekey, the new keypair goes into `next` (NOT `current`); it is promoted to `current` only when the FIRST valid inbound DATA packet arrives on it (confirming the initiator completed the handshake). Egress continues to use the CURRENT (confirmed) keypair until then, so a peer-initiated rekey never blackholes egress. This is the standard current/previous/next lifecycle (RFC-ish, per the kernel WG "Sending & Receiving" keypair rules). Pairs with the MEDIUM F-190 TAI64N handshake anti-replay (a replayed init should be rejected before it can even start a rekey) — consider co-fixing to close the replay-DoS fully.

**Validation:** FULL cargo test --release; test-failover / a WG rekey soak (force repeated peer-initiated rekeys during sustained xpf→peer traffic, assert zero egress blackhole) WARRANTED. RED-on-revert: a peer-initiated rekey during xpf→peer egress does NOT drop egress (unconfirmed keypair stays in `next`, current serves egress until the first inbound data packet confirms) — goes RED (egress NoSession/blackhole on rekey) on revert.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-019, rs-wg-coord module. RUST (cargo). Design-heavy (3-slot keypair lifecycle). Pairs with F-190 (TAI64N anti-replay, MEDIUM).

## #3884 — firewall: non-inet6 filter family folds into FiltersInet → a same-name cross-family filter overwrites the IPv4 filter (discard→accept-all, fail-open) (fable-161 F-030) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master b7bf2c2c2).

**Defect (MEDIUM, security fail-open):** `compileFirewall` maps every NON-inet6 filter family into `FiltersInet` (`pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:183`: `dest := FiltersInet` for all families except inet6), then `dest[name] = filter` — an unconditional overwrite with no family-collision reject. So two filters with the SAME name in different non-inet6 families (e.g. a `family inet filter blockX { term ... then discard; }` and a `family any`/`family mpls`/etc. `filter blockX { ... then accept; }`) collapse: the second silently OVERWRITES the first in the FiltersInet map. If the IPv4 filter was a `discard`/deny and the colliding-family filter is accept-all, the effective IPv4 filter becomes accept-all → fail-open (a deny filter silently replaced by an accept).

**Fix:** either (a) key filters by (family, name) so same-name cross-family filters don't collide, OR (b) REJECT at commit a filter name reused across families that fold into the same dest map (fail-closed — the operator gets an error, not a silent overwrite). Match Junos, which namespaces filters per family. Do NOT let a discard filter be silently overwritten by a same-name accept filter.

**RED-on-revert:** two same-name filters in different non-inet6 families both survive (keyed by family) OR the reuse is rejected at commit — goes RED (second overwrites first → discard becomes accept-all) on revert; a normal single-family filter compiles unchanged; the inet6 path (already separate) is unaffected. Test via ParseSetCommand+SetPath.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-030, go-config-ifaces-cos-fw module.
