## #3886 — NAT64: no commit gate on 'prefix' — a non-/96 or malformed prefix commits green then the Rust helper aborts the ENTIRE forwarding rebuild → every later commit stops reaching the dataplane (fable-161 F-032) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master b7bf2c2c2).

**Defect (MEDIUM, availability — dataplane freeze):** NAT64 `prefix <p>` is read via raw `nodeVal` (`pkg/config/compiler_nat.go:789`) with NO commit-time validation that it is a well-known /96 (64:ff9b::/96) or a valid /96 NSP. A non-/96 or malformed NAT64 prefix COMMITS GREEN. Then the Rust userspace helper's `try_from_snapshots` /96-integrity check REJECTS it and ABORTS the entire `build_reconcile_forwarding` (abort-without-publish) → the forwarding snapshot is never published → EVERY LATER COMMIT stops reaching the dataplane (the dataplane is frozen at the last-good snapshot; new sessions/policy/NAT changes silently don't take effect). A single bad NAT64 prefix in a committed config wedges the whole control→dataplane pipeline.

**Fix:** add a commit-time strict validator for NAT64 `prefix`: require a valid IPv6 prefix with length /96 (the RFC 6052 NAT64 constraint — well-known 64:ff9b::/96 OR a /96 network-specific prefix; reject other lengths + malformed). Fail-closed at commit (the operator gets an error, not a silent dataplane freeze). Type the leaf so a typo is caught. Match what the Rust try_from_snapshots /96-integrity check requires EXACTLY, so anything that would abort the rebuild at runtime is rejected at commit (no commit-accept→runtime-abort gap). Consider: even with the gate, a malformed prefix arriving via HA peer-sync/lenient should NOT abort the WHOLE rebuild — the Rust side should skip the bad NAT64 rule and publish the rest (defense-in-depth; file/note separately if that's a larger Rust change).

**RED-on-revert:** a NAT64 `prefix 2001:db8::/64` (non-/96) or malformed prefix is REJECTED at commit (goes RED — commits green then freezes the dataplane rebuild — on revert); a valid `prefix 64:ff9b::/96` + a valid /96 NSP commit. Test via ParseSetCommand+SetPath + CompileConfig.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-032, go-config-nat module.

## #3888 — userspace-dp NAT64: try_from_snapshots aborts the ENTIRE forwarding rebuild on one bad rule — skip the bad rule + publish the rest (defense-in-depth for #3886) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Follow-up from #3886 (fable-161 F-032). #3886 added a commit-time /96 gate so a bad NAT64 prefix can't be committed. But the ROOT robustness gap remains: `Nat64State::try_from_snapshots` (userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs ~247-269) propagates `Nat64UnparseableRule` via `?` out of `build_reconcile_forwarding` (forwarding_build/mod.rs:319) → aborts the WHOLE rebuild without publishing. So a single malformed NAT64 rule arriving via a MIXED-VERSION HA peer-sync or a lenient/corrupt snapshot (paths the commit gate doesn't cover) still freezes the entire control→dataplane pipeline (every later commit stops reaching the dataplane).

**Fix (Rust, defense-in-depth):** scope the NAT64 rule rejection to the OFFENDING rule — skip the bad NAT64 rule (log a warning) and publish the rest of the forwarding snapshot, rather than aborting the whole rebuild. Match the fail-open-vs-fail-closed posture used elsewhere for a bad single rule (skip-and-continue with a loud log, not abort-all). This makes a bad NAT64 rule a NAT64-only degradation, not a total dataplane freeze.

**Validation:** FULL cargo test --release; RED-on-revert: a snapshot with one malformed NAT64 rule + valid other rules still PUBLISHES the valid rules (goes RED — whole rebuild aborted, nothing published — on revert); the bad rule is skipped + logged. Consider whether other rule types in build_reconcile_forwarding have the same abort-all-on-one-bad-rule pattern (audit the `?`-propagations).

Provenance: #3886 follow-up (Rust half). RUST (cargo).

## #3889 — daemon: super-user sudoers NOPASSWD grant (/etc/sudoers.d/xpf-<user>) never revoked on class downgrade or user removal (fable-161 F-055) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, security — stale privilege):** when a login user has the super-user class, the daemon writes a NOPASSWD sudoers grant `/etc/sudoers.d/xpf-<user>` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:778`). But there is NO removal branch: when the user is DOWNGRADED to a lower class (operator/read-only) OR REMOVED from the config entirely, the sudoers grant is NEVER revoked. The stale `/etc/sudoers.d/xpf-<user>` file persists → the (downgraded or deleted) user retains passwordless root sudo. A privilege that should follow the config is left dangling — a real access-control gap (a demoted admin keeps root).

**Fix:** reconcile the sudoers.d grants against the CURRENT config on every apply: (a) write `xpf-<user>` for each CURRENT super-user; (b) REMOVE any `xpf-<user>` file whose user is no longer a super-user in the config (downgraded) OR no longer in the config (removed). A sweep of `/etc/sudoers.d/xpf-*` diffed against the desired super-user set (mirror how other reconcilers remove stale files, e.g. the networkd .link/.network stale-file removal). Do it atomically + validate (a broken sudoers file locks out sudo — use visudo-check or the atomic-write helper).

**RED-on-revert:** a user downgraded from super-user → operator has its `/etc/sudoers.d/xpf-<user>` REMOVED on the next apply (goes RED — stale grant persists, user keeps root — on revert); a removed user's grant is removed; a current super-user's grant is written/kept. Test the reconcile with a before/after config (super-user → downgraded).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-055, go-daemon-lifecycle module.

## #3890 — applications: typo'd application-set member keyword silently dropped, no commit gate → deny application-set under-populated (fail-open) (fable-161 F-160) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, security fail-open):** the application-set member compiler (`pkg/config/compiler_applications.go:183`) has a switch over member keywords with NO default arm, so a TYPO'd member keyword (e.g. `applicaton foo` instead of `application foo`, or a mistyped `application-set`) is SILENTLY DROPPED — it never reaches the strict validator, so it commits clean. The application-set is then UNDER-POPULATED. If that application-set is used in a DENY policy, the deny matches FEWER applications than the operator intended → traffic the operator meant to block is permitted (fail-open). (For a permit policy it's fail-closed, but the deny case is the security hole.)

**Fix:** add a `default:` arm to the member-keyword switch that RECORDS the unknown member (so a strict validator can reject it) OR reject the unknown member keyword directly at commit (fail-closed — the operator gets an error, not a silent drop). Mirror the pattern used for other typo-catching gates (e.g. the #3113 policy-match-leaf strict gate, or the #3339 application-collision gate). An unknown/typo'd application-set member must be a COMMIT ERROR, never silently dropped.

**RED-on-revert:** an application-set with a typo'd member keyword is REJECTED at commit (goes RED — silently dropped, set under-populated — on revert); a valid application/application-set member compiles; the set is fully populated. Test via ParseSetCommand+SetPath + CompileConfig.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-160, go-config-policy module.

## #3893 — configstore: clusterReadOnly enforced only at EnterConfigure* — an already-open session can Set/Commit on the read-only HA secondary → active-config divergence (fable-161 F-048) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, HA config integrity):** the `clusterReadOnly` guard (which blocks config changes on the HA secondary — config authority is the RG0 primary) is checked ONLY at `EnterConfigure*` (`pkg/configstore/store_command.go:11` area). But once a config session is already OPEN (entered before the node became read-only, or via a path that doesn't re-check), `Set`/`Commit` only verify `candidate == nil` — there are ZERO `clusterReadOnly` refs on the Set/Commit path. So an open session can Set + Commit on the read-only secondary → the secondary's active config DIVERGES from the primary (the secondary applies a local edit that the primary never sees / that will be overwritten by the next config-sync, causing churn/divergence).

**Fix:** enforce `clusterReadOnly` on the mutating operations themselves (`Set`, `Delete`, `Commit`, `Load`, `Rollback` — every candidate-mutating + commit path), not just at `EnterConfigure`. A mutating op on a read-only (non-RG0-primary) node must be REJECTED with a clear "configuration is read-only on the cluster secondary" error. This closes the already-open-session and the didn't-re-check windows. Keep the existing EnterConfigure gate. (Config authority on reconnect is already handled by #78's RG0-primary reject in the daemon; this is the store-level enforcement for the local session path.)

## #3895 — RA: an over-large PREF64/router lifetime makes ndp.PREF64 marshal fail → the ENTIRE Router Advertisement is aborted → the segment silently stops getting IPv6 RAs (fable-161 F-075) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, availability — IPv6 segment blackhole):** the RA sender (`pkg/ra/sender.go:774`) appends a PREF64 option (and sets router/prefix lifetimes) with UNCAPPED values from the config. A PREF64 scaled-lifetime > 8191 (the RFC 8781 13-bit scaled-lifetime field, i.e. > ~65528s after the /8 scale) — or an over-large router/prefix lifetime — makes `ndp.PREF64`/the option marshal FAIL. Since the whole RA is built + sent in a SINGLE WriteTo, a marshal failure of ONE option aborts the ENTIRE RA → the segment silently STOPS getting IPv6 Router Advertisements → hosts lose their default route / SLAAC config when the current RAs expire (IPv6 blackhole on that segment). The schema has NO upper bound on the lifetime (a distinct residual from #2497, which added ValidatePREF64CIDR + only ValidateIntegerMin(0), no upper bound).

**Fix:** (a) add a commit-time upper-bound validator for the PREF64 lifetime (RFC 8781: the scaled lifetime must fit the 13-bit field → cap at the max representable, reject or clamp an over-large value) and the router/prefix lifetimes (RFC 4861 uint16 seconds); AND (b) make the RA sender ROBUST — if one option fails to marshal, LOG + SKIP that option and still send the rest of the RA (don't abort the whole RA over one bad option). Fail-loud at commit (the operator gets an error) + defense-in-depth at send (a bad option degrades to missing-that-option, not a total RA blackout).

**RED-on-revert:** a PREF64 lifetime > the 13-bit-scaled max is rejected at commit (goes RED — commits then the whole RA aborts, segment loses IPv6 RAs — on revert); a valid lifetime marshals + the RA sends; if a bad option somehow reaches the sender, the rest of the RA still goes out. Test the schema bound + the sender's per-option robustness.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-075, go-vrrp-ra module. Distinct from #2497 (CIDR validation, no lifetime upper bound).

## #3896 — IKE: gateway 'version' / policy 'mode' / 'nat-traversal' are untyped free-form leaves → a typo silently un-pins IKEv2-only or downgrades aggressive→main mode (fable-161 F-039) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, security — silent crypto/negotiation weakening):** the IKE gateway `version`, IKE policy `mode`, and `nat-traversal` leaves are UNTYPED free-form in setSchema (`pkg/config/schema_security.go:713` area — children:nil, no ValidateEnum, unlike sibling typed leaves). So a TYPO in these values COMMITS CLEAN and is then mis-interpreted downstream:
- `version v2-onyl` (typo of `v2-only`) → the v2-only pin is NOT recognized → the gateway silently accepts IKEv1 (downgrade — a v2-only policy meant to reject legacy IKEv1 no longer does);
- `mode agressive` (typo of `aggressive`) or an unrecognized mode → falls back to `main` (or vice-versa) → the operator's intended mode isn't enforced;
- a typo'd `nat-traversal` value → NAT-T not enabled/disabled as intended.

The typo isn't caught at commit (no enum validation) → the config compiles + generates a strongSwan config that doesn't match operator intent (a security-negotiation weakening, silently).

**Fix:** type these leaves in setSchema with `ValidateEnum` (the valid value sets): `version` ∈ {v1-only, v2-only, ...} (whatever xpf supports); IKE policy `mode` ∈ {main, aggressive}; `nat-traversal` ∈ {enable, disable, ...}. A typo'd value is then REJECTED at commit (fail-closed — the operator gets an error naming the bad value), never silently mis-mapped. Mirror how the sibling typed IKE/IPsec enum leaves are validated. Verify the accepted-value sets match what the strongSwan config generator + the compiler actually handle.

**RED-on-revert:** `set security ike gateway G version v2-onyl` (typo) is REJECTED at commit (goes RED — commits clean then silently accepts IKEv1 — on revert); a valid `version v2-only` / `mode aggressive` / `nat-traversal enable` commits; the strongSwan output matches. Test via ParseSetCommand+SetPath+SchemaValidate/CompileConfig.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-039, go-config-schema module.

## #3898 — interfaces: per-unit tunnel inheritance shallow-copies Addresses/WgPeers slice headers → a unit inherits sibling units' IPs (duplicate IP on two tunnel netdevs) (fable-161 F-031) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, config-compile correctness — duplicate IP):** per-unit tunnel inheritance does `*tc = *ifc.Tunnel` (`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:236`), a SHALLOW struct copy that copies the Addresses / WgPeers SLICE HEADERS (ptr+len+cap) rather than the elements. So every unit that inherits from the parent tunnel shares the SAME backing array — if one unit then appends/sets its own address, it mutates the aliased slice, and sibling units end up with each other's IPs. Result: two tunnel netdevs (different units) get the SAME / cross-contaminated IP addresses → a DUPLICATE IP on the wire (address conflict, one tunnel unusable) or a unit silently carrying a sibling's WgPeers.

**Fix:** DEEP-copy the per-unit tunnel config — after `*tc = *ifc.Tunnel`, clone the slice fields (`tc.Addresses = append([]T(nil), ifc.Tunnel.Addresses...)`, same for WgPeers and any other slice/map field) so each unit owns an independent backing array. Then a per-unit override mutates only that unit. Audit the Tunnel struct for ALL reference-typed fields (slices, maps, pointers) and clone each. Mirror any existing deep-copy helper if one exists.

**RED-on-revert:** a tunnel with two units, each setting its own address, compiles with each unit carrying ONLY its own address (no cross-contamination / no duplicate IP) — goes RED (units share/alias the parent's slice → duplicate/sibling IPs) on revert; a single-unit tunnel + a no-override unit still inherit correctly. Test two units with distinct addresses + assert independence.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-031, go-config-ifaces-cos-fw module.

## #3900 — config: annotations emitted verbatim into /* */ comments — an annotation containing '*/' injects tokens into the re-parsed config on HA sync / rollback reload (fable-161 F-035) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-03)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, config-integrity / injection):** config annotations (the Junos `annotate` comments) are emitted VERBATIM into `/* ... */` comment delimiters when the config is formatted (`pkg/config/ast_format.go:135`). There is NO sanitization of the annotation text. An annotation containing the sequence `*/` (or `/*`) CLOSES the comment early → the remaining annotation text is then re-parsed as CONFIG TOKENS when the formatted config is re-parsed. This happens on every Format→Parse round-trip: HA CONFIG SYNC (the primary formats + the secondary re-parses) and ROLLBACK/archive RELOAD. So a crafted (or accidental) annotation with `*/` can inject arbitrary config statements into the standby's / the reloaded config — a config-integrity break (the injected tokens become real config the operator never wrote) or a parse failure that bricks the reload.

**Fix:** sanitize annotation text before emitting it into a `/* */` comment — escape or reject the `*/` (and `/*`) sequence. Options: (a) reject an annotation containing `*/` at commit (`Store.Annotate` — fail-closed, clear error); (b) escape `*/` on emit (e.g. `*\/` or a space-split `* /`) and un-escape on parse — but this needs a matching lexer change; (a) is simpler + safe. Prefer commit-time rejection of `*/`/`/*` in annotation text (Junos annotations are single-line human notes; disallowing the comment-delimiter sequence is reasonable). Verify the round-trip: an annotation with `*/` is rejected at commit (or safely escaped) so Format→Parse can't inject.

**RED-on-revert:** an `annotate` with text containing `*/` is REJECTED at commit (or safely escaped) so a Format→Parse round-trip does NOT inject tokens / does NOT change the config (goes RED — the `*/` closes the comment and injects/corrupts on re-parse — on revert); a normal annotation round-trips identically. Test the Annotate path + a Format→Parse round-trip with a malicious `*/` annotation.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-035, go-config-parse module. Related class to #3854 (quoteKey escape round-trip).

## #3902 — screen: flowless packet path bypasses source-independent screens (LAND, icmp/udp-flood, ip-source-route) for non-query ICMP + non-first fragments (fail-open) (fable-161 F-085) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, screen/IDS fail-open):** in the packet screen stage (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_stages.rs:438` area), the flow lookup returns `Some(flow)` for a session packet and falls to the `else`/None branch for a FLOWLESS packet (non-query ICMP, non-first fragments). The flowless branch runs ONLY the fragment/ICMP-specific screens (ping-of-death, teardrop, icmp-fragment) — it does NOT run the SOURCE-INDEPENDENT screens (LAND anti-spoof, ICMP flood, UDP flood, ip-source-route). But those src-independent screens do NOT need a flow/session — they should run on EVERY packet regardless of flow state. So a crafted non-query ICMP or a non-first fragment BYPASSES LAND anti-spoof / flood / source-route screens → screen fail-open (an attack the operator enabled the screen to block gets through on the flowless path).

**Fix:** run the SOURCE-INDEPENDENT screens (LAND, icmp-flood, udp-flood, ip-source-route — the ones that don't require a flow) on BOTH the flow (Some) AND flowless (None) branches — or hoist them before the flow-conditional so they run unconditionally on every packet. Keep the flow-dependent screens (syn-flood per-session, etc.) on the flow branch. Verify each screen's actual flow-dependency + place it accordingly. Do NOT skip a src-independent screen just because the packet has no session.

**Validation:** FULL cargo test --release; a cluster smoke sending a non-query ICMP / non-first fragment that should trip LAND/flood/source-route + asserting it's dropped would validate. RED-on-revert: a LAND-spoofed non-query-ICMP / non-first-fragment packet is DROPPED by the LAND (or source-route) screen (goes RED — bypasses the screen on the flowless path — on revert); a normal packet + the flow-dependent screens are unaffected.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-085, rs-screen module. RUST (cargo).

## #3904 — config: multiple bracket-list leaves truncate to the first value — IKE/IPsec proposals, RIP export/redistribute, routing-instance interface (fable-161 F-040/F-161/F-162/F-163) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master). FOUR sibling findings of the SAME #2419/#3872 bracket-list-truncation class (the #2587/F-010 sweeps did not reach these leaves) — bundling into one "route the remaining leaves through firewallMatchValues / read Keys[1:]+children" PR.

**F-040 + F-161 (crypto negotiation narrowing):** IKE/IPsec policy `proposals [ prop-a prop-b ]` TRUNCATES to the FIRST proposal — the schema leaf is not `multi` (`schema_security.go:704`) and the compiler reads `Keys[1]` (`compiler_ipsec.go:76` + `:266`); `Proposals` is a scalar `string`. So a multi-proposal IKE/IPsec policy silently offers only the first proposal → crypto negotiation narrows (a peer requiring the second proposal fails to establish).

**F-162 (routing):** RIP `export [ a b ]` / redistribute bracket-list TRUNCATES to the first (`compiler_protocols.go` RIP path reads Keys[1]).

**F-163 (VRF isolation break):** routing-instance `interface [ a b ]` keeps only the FIRST interface (`compiler_routing.go:295` `nodeVal`=Keys[1]) → the remaining ports stay OUTSIDE the VRF → an isolation break (ports meant to be in the routing-instance are in the default table).

**Fix (all four, same mechanism):** make each leaf `multi: true` in setSchema (schema_security.go proposals, schema_routing.go RIP export + routing-instance interface) and read ALL values (`Keys[1:]` + children, accumulate — use `firewallMatchValues` or the established multi-read helper) in the compiler; change the scalar `Proposals string` → `[]string` (and its consumers in pkg/ipsec) + RIP export → []string + routing-instance Interfaces already []string but the reader drops all-but-first. Mirror the #2419/#3872 fix exactly.

**RED-on-revert (each):** `proposals [ p1 p2 ]` → BOTH proposals in the strongSwan output (RED: only p1 on revert); RIP `export [ a b ]` → both (RED: only a); routing-instance `interface [ ge-0/0/1 ge-0/0/2 ]` → BOTH in the VRF (RED: only the first, second stranded in default table). Test each via ParseSetCommand+SetPath. Single-value forms + hierarchical block forms still work.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-040/F-161 (go-config-schema), F-162/F-163 (go-config-routing-services). Bundle per the multi-value sweep pattern.

## #3906 — NAT: SNAT pool 'port range <low> to <high>' and 'port no-translation' silently ignored → default 1024-65535 PAT; reversed/out-of-range commits green then drops the rule at runtime (fable-161 F-033) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, config-compile correctness — wrong NAT ports):** SNAT source-pool `port range <low> to <high>` and `port no-translation` are SILENTLY IGNORED (`pkg/config/compiler_nat.go:1058` area — the port parser requires a specific `range`/`low`/`high` keyword shape and there is no SNAT strict validator). So:
- `port range 5000 to 6000` (or the Junos `port { range low high; }` form) is not applied → the pool falls back to the DEFAULT 1024-65535 PAT range → SNAT uses ports the operator explicitly narrowed away from (breaks a port-constrained upstream / firewall expectation);
- `port no-translation` (1:1 source-port preservation) is ignored → source ports ARE translated when the operator asked them not to be;
- a REVERSED (`low > high`) or out-of-range port range COMMITS GREEN then drops the rule / mis-behaves at runtime.

**Fix:** (a) parse `port range <low> to <high>` (both the flat `range low high` and the Junos `port { range ...; }` / `port no-translation` shapes) into the pool's port config so the configured range/no-translation is APPLIED; (b) add a SNAT-pool strict validator: reject a reversed (`low > high`) or out-of-range (not 1-65535) port range at commit (fail-closed). Mirror the DNAT port handling (#3446/#3449) + the SNAT pool structure. Match what the Rust source-NAT pool (source.rs) actually consumes.

**RED-on-revert:** `port range 5000 to 6000` yields a pool using 5000-6000 (not the 1024-65535 default); `port no-translation` preserves source ports; a reversed `port range 6000 to 5000` is REJECTED at commit — goes RED (range silently ignored → default PAT / reversed accepted) on revert; a pool with no port config still uses the default. Test via ParseSetCommand+SetPath + CompileConfig + the SNAT snapshot.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-033, go-config-nat module.

## #3909 — security: syn_cookie_master_key serialized into world-readable state.json (no skip_serializing, unlike WG keys) → local unpriv user defeats SYN-flood source validation (fable-161 F-087) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, secret exposure):** the `syn_cookie_master_key` is serialized into the userspace-dp state file (`userspace-dp/src/protocol/snapshot.rs:306` area) which is written world-readable (0644), UNLIKE the WireGuard private keys which carry `#[serde(skip_serializing)]` (or an equivalent skip) precisely to keep them out of the on-disk state. The SYN-cookie master key is the secret that makes XDP-generated SYN-ACK cookies unforgeable — it's what the source-validation check hashes against. A local UNPRIVILEGED user who reads `state.json` learns the master key → can FORGE valid SYN cookies → defeats the SYN-flood source validation (the attacker's spoofed SYN-ACKs pass validation, re-opening the SYN-flood amplification the cookie was meant to block).

**Fix:** add `#[serde(skip_serializing)]` (or the project's key-redaction attribute) to the `syn_cookie_master_key` field so it is NOT written to the world-readable state.json — mirror exactly how the WG private keys are handled. On deserialize/restore, regenerate the key (a fresh random master key per boot is acceptable — SYN cookies are short-lived [~60s], so a key rotation on restart just invalidates in-flight cookies, which is benign) OR, if a stable key across restarts is genuinely required, persist it in a SEPARATE root-only (0600) file like the WG key material. Prefer skip_serializing + regenerate-on-boot unless there's a hard cross-restart-stability requirement. Verify no other secret (auth keys, PSKs) leaks into state.json the same way.

**RED-on-revert:** the serialized state.json does NOT contain the syn_cookie_master_key (goes RED — the key is present in world-readable 0644 state — on revert); the SYN-cookie source-validation still works after a restart (fresh key or persisted-securely). Rust test asserting the serialized snapshot omits the key.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-087, rs-server module. RUST (cargo).

## #3912 — cluster-sync: pendingBulkAckEpoch stored AFTER writing BulkEnd → ack-before-store TOCTOU latches a phantom pending epoch → permanently blocks manual failover (fable-161 F-025) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, HA — permanently blocks manual failover):** in the bulk-sync barrier (`pkg/cluster/sync_bulk.go:206` area), the `pendingBulkAckEpoch` is stored AFTER the BulkEnd marker is written to the wire. If the peer's ACK arrives BEFORE the local store of the pending epoch (a TOCTOU race — the peer can ack faster than the local goroutine records the pending state), the ack is processed against a not-yet-set pending epoch, then the pending epoch is stored → a PHANTOM pending-bulk-ack epoch is latched that will NEVER be cleared (the ack that would clear it already came and went). A latched phantom pending epoch then BLOCKS manual failover (the failover gate waits for the pending bulk ack that already arrived) → `request chassis cluster failover` hangs / is refused indefinitely.

**Fix:** store `pendingBulkAckEpoch` BEFORE writing the BulkEnd marker to the wire (establish the pending state, THEN send the marker that solicits the ack), so an ack can never arrive before the pending epoch is recorded. Alternatively, make the ack-handler + pending-store atomic under the sync lock so the ordering can't interleave. Mirror the #2170/#2198 gen-guard ordering discipline (record-then-send). Verify the ack correctly clears the pending epoch regardless of arrival timing.

**RED-on-revert / test-failover:** a bulk-sync whose ack arrives immediately does NOT latch a phantom pending epoch → manual failover proceeds (goes RED — phantom epoch latched, failover blocked — on revert). Unit-test the ack-before-store ordering (inject an ack before the store); test-failover WARRANTED (HA manual-failover path — batch with the other HA-Medium fixes, force-node0-primary gate).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-025, go-cluster-sync module.

## #3915 — NAT: compileNAT reads only the FIRST source/destination/static/nat64/proxy-arp block per nat node → a duplicate hierarchical block (load override) silently drops its rule-set (fable-161 F-158) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master). Sibling of OPEN #3850 (which is the NAT-RULE match/then dup-block class) — this is a DIFFERENT hierarchy level (the `nat {}` node's top-level source/destination/static/nat64/proxy-arp sub-blocks).

**Defect (MEDIUM, config-compile silent-drop / fail-open):** `compileNAT` (`pkg/config/compiler_nat.go:695` area) reads each of the `source {}` / `destination {}` / `static {}` / `nat64 {}` / `proxy-arp {}` sub-blocks under a `nat {}` node via `FindChild` (FIRST-match only). If a config has a DUPLICATE hierarchical block (e.g. two `source {}` blocks under one `nat {}`, as `load override`/`load merge` can produce), only the FIRST is compiled — the second's rule-sets are SILENTLY DROPPED. So an operator whose merged config has a second `source {}` block (with additional SNAT rule-sets) loses those rule-sets → traffic that should be SNAT'd egresses UNtranslated (a NAT bypass / connectivity break). `forEachChild` exists in this file but is UNUSED here.

**Fix:** `compileNAT` must ACCUMULATE across ALL `source`/`destination`/`static`/`nat64`/`proxy-arp` blocks under the `nat {}` node (use the existing `forEachChild` helper, or FindChildren + merge), NOT FindChild-first-only. A duplicate block's rule-sets must be merged (Junos merges duplicate blocks), OR the duplicate must be rejected at commit (fail-closed) — never silently dropped. Mirror the #3842 policy dup-block accumulate pattern.

**RED-on-revert:** a `nat {}` with two `source {}` blocks (the second adding a rule-set) compiles BOTH rule-sets (or rejects at commit) — goes RED (second source block's rule-set dropped, SNAT missing) on revert; a single source/dest/static block compiles unchanged. Test via the hierarchical AST (dup-block shape from load override) — NewParser or a constructed AST, since flat-set won't produce two same-name blocks.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-158, go-config-nat module. Related: #3850 (NAT-rule dup blocks, distinct level).

## #3917 — HA: OnFenceReceived iterates the STARTUP config snapshot → day-2 redundancy-groups are never fenced → split-brain dual-active (fable-161 F-165) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, HA — split-brain dual-active):** `OnFenceReceived` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:721` area) iterates the config snapshot CAPTURED AT `startClusterComms` (a closure over `cfg` at startup), not the CURRENT config. So any redundancy-group added AFTER startup (a "day-2" RG created by a later commit) is NOT in the snapshot → when a fence message arrives, that day-2 RG is NEVER fenced. An unfenced RG means the peer can stay/become active for it while this node is also active → SPLIT-BRAIN dual-active (both nodes forwarding for the same RG → duplicate packets, MAC flaps, asymmetric state → the exact failure the fence mechanism exists to prevent).

**Fix:** `OnFenceReceived` must read the CURRENT config's redundancy-groups (re-read `d.activeConfig()` / the live cluster config at fence time), NOT the startup snapshot captured in the closure. Every RG in the current config — including day-2 additions — must be fenced on a fence event. Audit for other closures over the startup `cfg` in the HA path that would miss day-2 config (the same stale-snapshot class as #3165 OnFenceReceived-adjacent). Mirror how other HA reconcilers read the live config.

**RED-on-revert / test-failover:** add a redundancy-group via a commit AFTER cluster startup, then trigger a fence — the day-2 RG IS fenced (goes RED — day-2 RG unfenced, split-brain — on revert); RGs present at startup still fence. Unit-test OnFenceReceived reading current-vs-startup config; test-failover WARRANTED (HA fence/split-brain — batch with the other HA-Medium fixes, force-node0-primary gate).

## #3918 — flow-cache: neighbor_mac_epoch stamped AFTER neighbor resolution → TOCTOU re-opens the #3048 stale-MAC blackhole on VRRP gateway failover (fable-161 F-089) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, HA — stale-MAC blackhole on failover):** the flow cache stamps `neighbor_mac_epoch` AFTER resolving the neighbor MAC (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:3718` area) rather than reading the epoch BEFORE the resolution. This is a TOCTOU: if a neighbor-table update (a VRRP gateway failover that changes the gateway MAC — the exact #3048 scenario) lands BETWEEN the resolve and the stamp, the flow caches the OLD (pre-failover) MAC but stamps the NEW epoch → the cache entry looks fresh (its epoch matches the current epoch) but holds the STALE MAC → packets are sent to the old gateway MAC → blackhole until the entry ages out. This re-opens the #3048 stale-MAC blackhole that the epoch mechanism was added to prevent.

**Fix:** read `neighbor_mac_epoch` (the current neighbor-table generation) BEFORE resolving the neighbor MAC, and stamp the flow cache with THAT captured epoch. Then if a neighbor update bumps the epoch during/after the resolve, the cached entry's (older) epoch will NOT match the new epoch → the entry is correctly treated as STALE → re-resolved → picks up the new MAC. Mirror the #2170/#3912 record-before-use (read-epoch-then-resolve) discipline. Verify the epoch comparison on cache-hit correctly invalidates an entry stamped with a pre-failover epoch.

**Validation:** FULL cargo test --release; test-failover WARRANTED (HA VRRP gateway failover → the stale-MAC scenario — batch with the other HA-Medium fixes, force-node0-primary gate). RED-on-revert: interleave a neighbor-epoch bump between resolve and stamp → the cached entry is invalidated on the next hit + re-resolves the new MAC (goes RED — stamps the new epoch onto the stale MAC → fresh-looking stale entry → blackhole — on revert); a normal resolve with no interleaving caches + serves correctly.

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-089, x-hpc module. RUST (cargo).

## #3920 — HA: renameRethMember downs the RETH member for rename and never brings it up; programRethMAC early-returns (MAC already matches) → data link left DOWN → RG demote/blackhole (fable-161 F-057) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, HA — data-link-down blackhole):** `renameRethMember` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_reth.go:156` area) brings the RETH member interface DOWN to perform the rename (link down → rename → …) but NEVER brings it back UP. The caller relies on `programRethMAC` to do the link DOWN→set-MAC→UP cycle — but `programRethMAC` EARLY-RETURNS when the MAC already matches (a no-op if the virtual MAC is already programmed). So when the MAC is already correct, `programRethMAC` returns without the UP, and the member interface is left administratively DOWN after the rename → the RETH data link is down → the interface's track detects link-down → the redundancy-group DEMOTES (effective priority drops) → failover / traffic blackhole on that member.

**Fix:** `renameRethMember` must bring the interface back UP after the rename (don't rely on programRethMAC's UP, which is conditional on a MAC change). Either (a) `renameRethMember` does its own link UP after the rename, or (b) make `programRethMAC` always ensure the link is UP even when the MAC already matches (the UP is the invariant, the MAC-set is the conditional part). Prefer (a) — the function that downs the link owns bringing it back up. Verify the interface is UP after a rename regardless of whether the MAC changed.

**RED-on-revert / test-failover:** after `renameRethMember` (with the MAC already matching so programRethMAC no-ops), the member interface is UP (goes RED — left DOWN → RG demote/blackhole — on revert); a rename that DOES change the MAC still ends UP. Unit-test the link-state after rename (mock the netlink link ops); test-failover WARRANTED (HA RETH member link → RG demote — batch with the other HA-Medium fixes, force-node0-primary gate).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-057, go-daemon-net module.

## #3922 — HA: directSendGARPs gateway probe forces the last octet to .1 → broken on /25+ subnets → post-failover blackhole in default private-rg-election mode (fable-161 F-054) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, HA — post-failover blackhole on /25+ subnets):** `directSendGARPs` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go:565` area) — the direct-GARP gateway probe used in the default private-rg-election mode — forces the gateway address's LAST OCTET to `.1` (a pre-#2377-style assumption that the gateway is `<subnet>.1`). On a subnet that is NOT /24 with a .1 gateway — i.e. any /25 or longer prefix, or a subnet whose gateway isn't .1 — the probe targets the WRONG address (a host that may not exist, or not the gateway) → the post-failover GARP / gateway-probe doesn't reach the real gateway → the gateway's ARP cache isn't updated with the new master's MAC → traffic to/from the gateway BLACKHOLES until the stale ARP entry ages out (the exact failover-blackhole the GARP is meant to prevent). #2377 fixed the analogous forced-.1 elsewhere but this directSendGARPs site was missed.

**Fix:** compute the gateway address from the CONFIGURED gateway / the actual next-hop, NOT by forcing `.1`. Use the interface's configured default gateway (or the subnet's real gateway from the route/config), respecting the actual prefix length. Mirror the #2377 fix (which replaced the forced-.1 with the real gateway derivation) at this directSendGARPs site. Verify a /25 (and a non-.1-gateway /24) targets the correct gateway.

**RED-on-revert / test-failover:** on a /25 subnet (gateway != .1), directSendGARPs probes the CORRECT configured gateway (goes RED — forces .1, wrong target, post-failover blackhole — on revert); a /24-with-.1 still works. Unit-test the target-address derivation for /24-.1, /25, and a non-.1 gateway; test-failover WARRANTED (HA post-failover GARP — batch with the other HA-Medium fixes, force-node0-primary gate).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-054, go-daemon-ha module. Sibling of #2377.

## #3924 — userspace maps-sync: a transient netlink AddrList failure prunes VRRP VIP keys from userspace_local_v4/v6 → blackholes VIP/SSH/BGP/IKE into XSK, swallowed silently (fable-161 F-183) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, HA/robustness — VIP blackhole on a transient enum failure):** the userspace local-address map sync (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:970` area) builds the DESIRED set of local addresses (for `userspace_local_v4`/`userspace_local_v6` — the map that steers packets destined to a local/VIP address into the XSK/host path) by enumerating interfaces via netlink `AddrList`. If `AddrList` returns a TRANSIENT error (or a partial result — netlink dumps can be interrupted/ENOBUFS), the desired set is INCOMPLETE, but the reconcile still PRUNES every map key not in the (incomplete) desired set. So a transient enumeration failure removes the VRRP VIP keys (+ other local addresses) from the map → packets destined to the VIP / SSH / BGP / IKE local endpoints are no longer steered to the host path → BLACKHOLE — and the error is swallowed silently (the prune proceeds as if the empty/partial enumeration were authoritative).

**Fix:** treat an incomplete enumeration as NON-AUTHORITATIVE — if `AddrList` errors (or a per-interface enumeration fails), do NOT prune the existing keys based on the partial set. Either (a) on any AddrList error, SKIP the prune this cycle (keep the existing keys, retry next reconcile) + log a warning; or (b) set an 'enumeration-incomplete' flag that suppresses pruning until a full enumeration succeeds. Only prune keys when the desired set is KNOWN-COMPLETE. Mirror the fail-safe-reconcile posture used elsewhere (don't act destructively on incomplete input). Verify a transient AddrList error keeps the VIP keys intact.

**RED-on-revert / test-failover:** inject an AddrList error → the existing VIP/local keys are PRESERVED (not pruned) + a warning logged (goes RED — keys pruned on the partial set → VIP blackhole — on revert); a successful full enumeration prunes correctly (stale keys removed). Unit-test the reconcile with an AddrList error (mock netlink). test-failover / a VIP-reachability smoke WARRANTED (batch with the other HA-Medium fixes, force-node0-primary gate).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-183, go-usdp-programs module.

## #3926 — cluster-sync: session deletes journaled while CONNECTED (sendCh full) are never flushed until a full disconnect → standby retains dead sessions (fable-161 F-026) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, HA — standby retains dead sessions):** when a session DELETE is generated while the sync connection is CONNECTED but the send channel (`sendCh`) is FULL (backpressure), the delete is JOURNALED (`pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:840` area) rather than sent. But the journal is only FLUSHED on a full DISCONNECT/reconnect — it is NOT flushed while the connection stays UP. Meanwhile the periodic session SWEEP replays INSTALLS (session state) but NOT the journaled deletes. So a delete that got journaled during a connected-but-backpressured moment is NEVER delivered to the standby (until an unrelated disconnect) → the standby RETAINS the DEAD session (a session the primary already tore down). On failover the standby then has stale/dead sessions → wrong forwarding decisions (a torn-down flow's reverse traffic gets forwarded, or a stale NAT binding persists) → security/correctness gap.

**Fix:** flush the delete journal while CONNECTED too — when `sendCh` drains (has capacity again), drain the journaled deletes onto the wire (a connected-flush path, not only the disconnect-reconnect flush). OR have the periodic sweep also replay/reconcile the journaled deletes (mirror the install-replay). The standby must converge to the primary's DELETED set even without a disconnect. Coordinate with the #2121 rejournalTail (drop-on-full) + #2170 gen-guard so a re-sent delete carries the correct gen. Verify a journaled-while-connected delete reaches the standby without requiring a disconnect.

**RED-on-revert / test-failover:** generate a delete while connected + sendCh full (journaled), then let sendCh drain WITHOUT a disconnect → the delete is flushed to the standby (goes RED — delete stuck in journal until disconnect, standby retains the dead session — on revert); a normal (non-backpressured) delete still sends inline. Unit-test the connected-flush path (sync_conn); test-failover WARRANTED (HA session-sync convergence — batch with the other HA-Medium fixes, force-node0-primary gate).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-026, go-cluster-sync module.

## #3929 — observability: GC session stats never written on the userspace dataplane path → SessionCount / xpf_sessions_active|established permanently 0 (fable-161 F-051) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, observability — session metrics stuck at 0):** the session GC / stats path writes `SessionCount` (and the Prometheus `xpf_sessions_active` / `xpf_sessions_established` gauges) only on the LEGACY (retired eBPF) code path — it is NEVER written on the RUST AF_XDP userspace dataplane path (the only live forwarding path since #1476). So on every real deployment, `show security flow session summary` SessionCount and the `xpf_sessions_active`/`xpf_sessions_established` metrics report permanently 0 regardless of the actual live session count. Operators + dashboards + alerts keyed on active-session count are blind (a session-exhaustion or session-leak condition is invisible; capacity dashboards show 0).

**Fix:** wire the session-count stats from the USERSPACE dataplane's actual session table into `SessionCount` + the Prometheus gauges. The userspace-dp publishes session state (the conntrack table / the session snapshot the HA sync + `show sessions` already read) — derive the active/established counts from there (the same source `show security flow session` uses) and update the stats/metrics on the GC/stats tick. Verify the count matches the live session table (a non-zero, correct count under load). Do NOT re-introduce the retired eBPF path.

**RED-on-revert:** with N live sessions, SessionCount == N and `xpf_sessions_active` == N (goes RED — 0 regardless of live sessions — on revert); 0 sessions → 0; the count tracks session install/teardown. Unit-test the stats derivation from a userspace session snapshot (+ ideally a cluster smoke asserting the metric is non-zero under iperf load).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-051, go-obs module.

## #3931 — cluster config-sync: applies via unordered goroutines with no sequence number → a rapid commit pair can leave the standby on the OLDER config (no alarm) (fable-161 F-156) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, HA config divergence):** config sync applies the received config via an UNORDERED goroutine (`go OnConfigReceived(...)` at `pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:1336` area) with NO sequence number / generation on the config-sync wire. If the primary commits TWICE in rapid succession (C1 then C2), the two config-sync messages spawn two goroutines that can RACE — if the C1-apply goroutine runs AFTER the C2-apply goroutine, the standby ends on the OLDER config C1 while the primary is on C2 → the two nodes DIVERGE, with no alarm. On failover the standby serves the stale C1. Unlike the SESSION-install path (which has the #2170 gen-guard discipline), the config-sync path has no ordering guard.

**Fix:** add a monotonic sequence number / generation to the config-sync wire (the primary stamps an increasing config-gen on each pushed config; the standby applies only if the incoming gen is NEWER than the last-applied, and REFUSES/drops an out-of-order older gen). Serialize the apply (a single-consumer apply queue ordered by gen, OR apply synchronously in receive order under a mutex — not N racing goroutines). Mirror the #2170 session-install gen-guard. The standby must always converge to the NEWEST config the primary sent. Alarm/log if an out-of-order older config is dropped. Coordinate with the #3865/#3875 (commit-confirmed) config-sync path.

**RED-on-revert / test-failover:** push C1 then C2 in rapid succession (reorder the two apply goroutines) → the standby ends on C2 (the newer), never C1 (goes RED — standby on the older C1, diverged — on revert); a single config push applies normally. Unit-test the out-of-order-gen refusal (inject C2 then C1); test-failover WARRANTED (HA config convergence — batch with the other HA-Medium fixes, force-node0-primary gate).

Provenance: fable-review-161 F-156, go-cluster-sync module. Sibling of the #2170 session-install gen-guard.

## #3932 — daemon: updateFlowTrace leaks one EventReader callback per commit → O(commits) callbacks + false trace-rotation alarm (fable-161 F-061) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, resource leak):** `updateFlowTrace` (the flow-traceoptions reconcile, `pkg/daemon` — grep updateFlowTrace / applyFlowTrace) ADDS a new EventReader callback (`er.AddCallback(tw.HandleEvent)`) on every config commit that touches flow traceoptions, but does NOT remove the PREVIOUS commit's callback. So after N commits there are N registered trace callbacks — each incoming flow event is dispatched to ALL of them → O(commits) callback invocations per event (a growing per-event cost + memory leak of the old TraceWriters), and the stale callbacks keep writing → a false trace-rotation alarm (multiple writers rotating the same trace file). A long-lived daemon that re-commits traceoptions repeatedly accumulates callbacks unboundedly.

**Fix:** `updateFlowTrace` must REMOVE the previous trace callback before (or when) registering the new one — either (a) the EventReader exposes a RemoveCallback / a callback handle that updateFlowTrace stores + removes on the next update, or (b) updateFlowTrace closes/replaces the single trace writer in place (one registered callback that dispatches to the CURRENT writer, swapped on update) rather than registering a new callback each time. Prefer (b) — a single stable callback whose target TraceWriter is swapped — so there's exactly ONE trace callback regardless of commit count. Close the old TraceWriter on swap (so its file handle is released + no double-rotation). Verify N commits leave exactly 1 callback + 1 live writer.

**RED-on-revert:** after 3 commits touching flow traceoptions, the EventReader has exactly 1 trace callback (not 3) + 1 live TraceWriter (goes RED — 3 callbacks, 3 writers, growing per-event cost — on revert); disabling traceoptions removes the callback; a single event is dispatched to the trace once. Unit-test the callback/writer count across repeated updateFlowTrace calls.

Provenance: fable-161 F-061, go-cli/daemon module (updateFlowTrace).

## #3934 — feeds: dynamic address-feed fetch has no body-size / entry cap → OOM (plaintext-http MITM can amplify into a remote OOM DoS) (fable-161 F-179) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, DoS — unbounded feed fetch OOM):** the dynamic address-feed fetcher (`pkg/feeds`) reads the HTTP response body with NO size limit and parses ALL entries with no entry cap. A feed server that returns a huge (or infinite/chunked) body, OR a MITM on a PLAINTEXT-HTTP feed URL (feeds fetched over http:// have no integrity/size guarantee), can make the fetcher buffer an arbitrarily large body into memory → OOM → the daemon is killed (a remote-triggerable DoS: whoever controls or can MITM the feed URL can OOM the firewall). Also a legitimately large feed (or a misconfigured URL pointing at a large file) OOMs by accident.

**Fix:** (a) cap the response body with an `io.LimitReader` (a sane max feed size, e.g. a configurable/reasonable byte limit) — reject/truncate-with-error a feed exceeding it; (b) cap the number of parsed entries (a max prefix count per feed) — reject/log a feed exceeding it, do NOT install a partial-but-huge set that blows the dataplane map; (c) set an HTTP client timeout so a slow-loris feed server can't hold the fetch open indefinitely. Fail-safe: on an over-size / over-count feed, KEEP the last-good feed contents (don't wipe the installed prefixes) + alarm. Consider warning on plaintext-http feed URLs (integrity risk). Mirror any existing size-cap pattern (e.g. the #2744 apply_snapshot cap).

**RED-on-revert:** a feed response exceeding the body-size cap is rejected/truncated with an error (goes RED — buffers the whole body → OOM — on revert) + the last-good feed is retained; an over-entry-count feed is rejected; a normal feed fetches + installs. Unit-test with a mock HTTP server returning an over-size body + an over-count entry list.

Provenance: fable-161 F-179, robustness/DoS class, go-feeds module.

## #3937 — ipsec: parseSAOutput parses a swanctl format that swanctl never emits → all IPsec SA status (show security ipsec sa) is blank (fable-161 F-067) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, observability — IPsec SA status always blank):** `parseSAOutput` (`pkg/ipsec` — grep parseSAOutput) parses the SA-status output assuming a format that the installed swanctl does NOT emit (a stale/wrong assumed layout — e.g. an old `ipsec statusall` shape vs the current `swanctl --list-sas` output, or a field-order/label mismatch). So the parse yields nothing → `show security ipsec sa` (and the gRPC/REST IPsec SA status) is PERMANENTLY BLANK even when tunnels are UP with active SAs. An operator cannot see SA state (up/down, bytes, rekey, SPI) → IPsec troubleshooting is blind; a monitoring system keyed on SA status sees no SAs.

**Fix:** align `parseSAOutput` with the ACTUAL swanctl output format the daemon invokes (verify the exact `swanctl --list-sas` / the command actually run + its real output layout on the installed strongSwan version). Parse the real fields (connection name, IKE/child SA state, SPIs, bytes in/out, rekey time). Add a test with a CAPTURED real swanctl output sample (a golden fixture from an actual `swanctl --list-sas`) so the parser is pinned to reality (this is why it drifted — no real-output fixture). Verify a tunnel with an active SA shows non-blank status.

**RED-on-revert:** given a real captured swanctl --list-sas output (a tunnel with an active IKE+child SA), parseSAOutput returns the populated SA status (goes RED — blank / empty parse — on revert); no-SA output yields empty correctly. Pin with the captured-output golden fixture.

Provenance: fable-161 F-067, go-obs/ipsec module.

## #3939 — flowexport: NetFlow/IPFIX protocolIdentifier is 0 for GRE/ESP/non-TCP-UDP-ICMP flows (uses the parsed protocol NAME not rec.ProtocolNum) → exported flows misattributed (fable-161 F-058) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, observability/correctness — wrong exported protocol):** the NetFlow v9 / IPFIX exporter (`pkg/flowexport`) sets the `protocolIdentifier` field from a PARSED protocol NAME lookup rather than the record's actual numeric protocol (`rec.ProtocolNum`). For flows whose protocol is not in the name table — GRE (47), ESP (50), AH (51), and any non-TCP/UDP/ICMP protocol — the name lookup yields nothing → `protocolIdentifier` is exported as 0. So a NetFlow/IPFIX collector sees GRE/ESP/AH tunnel flows all reported as protocol 0 (reserved/HOPOPT) → the flows are MISATTRIBUTED (a collector can't distinguish an ESP tunnel flow from a GRE flow; capacity/security analytics on tunnel traffic are wrong).

**Fix:** set `protocolIdentifier` directly from `rec.ProtocolNum` (the record's actual IP protocol number), NOT from a name→number re-lookup. The record already carries the numeric protocol; use it verbatim (0-255). Verify GRE (47), ESP (50), AH (51), TCP (6), UDP (17), ICMP (1) all export their correct numeric protocol. Keep any name-based DISPLAY (for show output) separate from the exported numeric field.

**RED-on-revert:** a GRE flow (proto 47) + an ESP flow (proto 50) export protocolIdentifier=47 and 50 respectively (goes RED — 0 for both — on revert); TCP/UDP/ICMP still export 6/17/1. Unit-test the exported protocolIdentifier for GRE/ESP/AH + TCP/UDP/ICMP from a flow record.

Provenance: fable-161 F-058, go-obs/flowexport module.

## #3941 — ipsec: deleting an IPsec VPN never terminates its live SAs (--load-all only unloads config) → the tunnel stays UP after the operator deletes it (fable-161 F-175) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, security/correctness — deleted VPN stays up):** when an operator DELETES an IPsec VPN from the config and commits, the strongSwan reconcile applies the new config via `swanctl --load-all` (or the equivalent config reload), which UNLOADS the deleted connection's CONFIG but does NOT TERMINATE the live IKE/child SAs that are already established. So the deleted tunnel's SAs stay ACTIVE — traffic keeps flowing over a VPN the operator explicitly removed, until the SA rekey/lifetime eventually expires (or never, if traffic keeps it alive). A security gap: a VPN removed for a security reason (compromised peer, decommissioned site) remains up + forwarding after the config says it's gone.

**Fix:** on commit, DIFF the previous vs new IPsec config, and for each REMOVED connection, actively TERMINATE its live SAs — `swanctl --terminate --ike <conn>` (or `--child`) for the deleted connection names — in addition to the config reload. So a deleted VPN's SAs are torn down promptly. Handle the case where the SA is already down (no-op). Verify the terminated tunnel stops forwarding. Coordinate with the strongSwan reconcile path (pkg/ipsec).

**RED-on-revert:** delete a VPN that has an active SA + commit → the SA is TERMINATED (swanctl --terminate issued for the removed conn) (goes RED — SA stays up, tunnel keeps forwarding — on revert); adding/modifying a VPN is unaffected; a VPN with no active SA deletes cleanly. Unit-test the removed-connection diff → terminate-call (mock the swanctl invocation).

Provenance: fable-161 F-175, robustness/ipsec module.

## #3942 — frr: GetBGPSummary parses table trailer lines as phantom peers + never sets PfxRcd → 'show bgp summary' shows bogus peers with 0 prefixes (fable-161 F-064) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, observability — wrong BGP summary):** `GetBGPSummary` (`pkg/frr` — grep GetBGPSummary) parses the `vtysh -c "show ip bgp summary"` (or the FRR BGP summary) text output naively — it treats TRAILER / non-peer lines (the "Total number of neighbors", "Displayed ..." footer, or blank/legend lines) as PEER rows → PHANTOM peers appear in the summary. And it never populates `PfxRcd` (prefixes received) → every peer shows 0 prefixes received even when the session is established and has received routes. So `show bgp summary` (+ the gRPC/REST BGP status) shows bogus extra peers and 0 PfxRcd for real ones → an operator can't trust the BGP peer/prefix view.

**Fix:** (a) parse ONLY genuine peer rows — anchor on the actual peer-table columns (a row starting with a valid neighbor address/IP) and STOP at the table trailer (the "Total number of neighbors" footer / a blank line), so trailer/legend lines are not misparsed as peers; (b) populate `PfxRcd` from the correct column (the "PfxRcd"/"State/PfxRcd" column in the FRR summary — its position depends on the FRR version; verify against the actual vtysh output). Better: use `vtysh -c "show ip bgp summary json"` (FRR emits JSON) and parse the structured output — far more robust than scraping columns (mirror any existing json-vtysh usage). Pin with a captured real vtysh output/JSON fixture.

**RED-on-revert:** given a real FRR bgp-summary output with 2 established peers (each with a PfxRcd count) + the trailer, GetBGPSummary returns exactly 2 peers with correct PfxRcd (goes RED — phantom trailer-peer(s) + PfxRcd 0 — on revert); a no-peer summary returns none. Pin with the captured fixture (JSON or text).

Provenance: fable-161 F-064, go-obs/frr module.

## #3944 — routing: routeToEntry ignores netlink MultiPath → ECMP (multipath) routes are displayed as a bare 'direct' route with one/no next-hop in show route (fable-161 F-065) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, observability — ECMP routes mis-displayed):** `routeToEntry` (`pkg/routing` — grep routeToEntry) converts a netlink route into the display/route-entry struct but IGNORES the netlink `MultiPath` field (`route.MultiPath` / the `RTA_MULTIPATH` next-hop list). A kernel ECMP route (multiple next-hops for one prefix, installed by FRR or a `next-hop [ a b ]` static) carries its next-hops in `MultiPath`, NOT in the single `route.Gw`. So `routeToEntry` reads the (empty) single Gw → the ECMP route shows as a bare "direct"/no-next-hop route in `show route` (and the gRPC/REST route view) → the operator can't see the multipath next-hops (which paths a prefix load-balances over) → ECMP is invisible in the route table.

**Fix:** `routeToEntry` must read the `MultiPath` next-hop list — when `route.MultiPath` is non-empty, emit ALL of its next-hops (each with its gateway + interface + weight) as the route's next-hops, rather than the single `route.Gw`. Fall back to the single Gw for a non-multipath route. Match how `show route` / Junos displays a multipath route (multiple next-hop lines). Verify an ECMP route shows all its next-hops.

**RED-on-revert:** a kernel route with a MultiPath list of 2 next-hops → routeToEntry emits 2 next-hops (goes RED — shown as direct / single/empty next-hop — on revert); a single-gateway route shows its one next-hop; a connected/direct route unchanged. Unit-test routeToEntry with a mock netlink.Route carrying a MultiPath list.

Provenance: fable-161 F-065, go-obs/routing module.

## #3947 — userspace-dp policy: legacy address parser drops a bare 'any' when mixed with literal addresses → the term/deny narrows (fail-open) (fable-161 F-084) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, security fail-open on a drift/hand-built-snapshot path):** the LEGACY address parser in `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:2544` area handles the `any` keyword with a no-op arm (`"any" | "" => {}`) — so when an address list MIXES a bare `any` with literal addresses (e.g. `[ any 10.0.0.0/8 ]`), the `any` is DROPPED and only the literals are kept. The v3 parser correctly sets `any_v4`/`any_v6` for a bare `any`; the legacy parser does not. `any` means "match all addresses" — dropping it NARROWS the match set to just the literals. For a DENY term/policy that narrowing is a FAIL-OPEN: a deny that should match ALL sources (any) now matches only the listed literals → traffic from other sources that should be denied is PERMITTED. This bites on the drift / hand-built-snapshot / mixed-version-decode path where the legacy parser runs (not the primary v3 path).

**Fix:** the legacy address parser must handle `any` the same as the v3 parser — set the `any_v4`/`any_v6` (match-all) flag when `any` appears, EVEN when mixed with literals (an `any` in the list makes the whole list match-all, or at minimum sets the any-flag alongside the literals so the match set is not narrowed). Do NOT silently drop `any`. Mirror the v3 parser's any-handling exactly so the legacy path can't produce a narrower (fail-open) match set than v3. Ideally, converge the two parsers or route the legacy path through the v3 any-handling.

**Validation:** FULL cargo test --release; RED-on-revert: a legacy-parsed address list `[ any 10.0.0.0/8 ]` sets any_v4 (matches all), not just 10.0.0.0/8 (goes RED — any dropped, match narrowed to the literal, deny fail-open — on revert); a literal-only list is unchanged; a bare `any` alone still sets any_v4. Rust unit test on the legacy parser with a mixed any+literal list.

Provenance: fable-161 F-084, rs-policy module. RUST (cargo).

## #3948 — snmp: trap-group 'version' has no typed field → a configured v1 trap-group emits v2c traps (fable-161 F-069) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, observability/interop — wrong SNMP trap version):** an SNMP trap-group's `version` (v1 / v2 / v2c) is parsed but there is NO typed field carrying it to the trap emitter (grep the SNMP trap-group config → the trap-send path). So the version is dropped and the emitter DEFAULTS to v2c → a trap-group explicitly configured `version v1` emits v2c traps. A legacy SNMP trap receiver that only understands SNMPv1 (or a NMS configured to accept only v1 from this device) DROPS the v2c traps → the operator's traps silently don't arrive (the device thinks it's sending v1, the receiver never gets a v1 trap). An interop break for a v1-only trap sink.

**Fix:** thread the trap-group `version` (v1/v2/v2c) from the parsed config to the trap-send path — add a typed Version field on the trap-group config struct + honor it when constructing/sending the trap (emit an SNMPv1 Trap-PDU for `version v1`, an SNMPv2 Trap for v2/v2c). Default to v2c only when unspecified. Verify a `version v1` trap-group emits a v1 trap.

**RED-on-revert:** a trap-group configured `version v1` emits an SNMPv1 trap (goes RED — emits v2c regardless — on revert); a `version v2c` (or unspecified) emits v2c; the version round-trips config→emit. Unit-test the trap-group version → emitted PDU version.

Provenance: fable-161 F-069, go-obs/snmp module.

## #3950 — networkd: monitorLinkState exits permanently on a netlink ENOBUFS (no resubscribe) → interface up/down changes stop being detected for the daemon's lifetime (fable-161 F-171) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, robustness — link-state monitoring dies permanently):** `monitorLinkState` (grep monitorLinkState — the netlink link-state subscription goroutine) EXITS PERMANENTLY when the netlink socket returns ENOBUFS (a transient kernel-buffer-overrun that happens under a burst of link events — exactly when many interfaces flap at once). ENOBUFS is a RECOVERABLE condition (the socket is still usable; some multicast messages were dropped), but the goroutine treats it as a fatal error and returns → after that, NO interface up/down events are detected for the rest of the daemon's lifetime. Downstream effects: RETH member link-down tracking stops (HA priority-cost demotion never fires → a dead member doesn't demote the RG → failover doesn't happen), DHCP-on-link-up doesn't re-trigger, and the interface reconcile misses state changes. A single transient ENOBUFS silently disables link-state-driven HA + interface management.

**Fix:** on ENOBUFS (and other recoverable netlink receive errors), do NOT exit — LOG a warning, and RE-SYNC/re-enumerate the current link state (since messages were dropped, do a full LinkList to catch up on any state changes missed during the overflow), then CONTINUE the receive loop (or re-subscribe the socket if needed). Only exit on the context being cancelled / an unrecoverable error. Mirror the resilient-netlink-loop pattern (e.g. the neighbor listener's ENOBUFS/resubscribe handling if one exists). Verify a transient ENOBUFS keeps the monitor alive + catches up on missed state.

**RED-on-revert:** inject an ENOBUFS from the netlink receive → the monitor logs + re-syncs + CONTINUES (goes RED — exits permanently, no further link events — on revert); a normal link event is delivered; context-cancel still exits cleanly. Unit-test the ENOBUFS-continue path (mock the netlink receive to return ENOBUFS then a real event).

Provenance: fable-161 F-171, robustness/networkd module.

## #3952 — ipsec: swanctl PSK secrets carry no 'id' selectors → with 2+ PSK VPNs the wrong PSK is matched to a peer (fable-161 F-176) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, IPsec correctness — wrong PSK on 2+ PSK tunnels):** the generated swanctl config emits pre-shared-key (`secrets { ike-... { secret = ... } }`) entries WITHOUT `id` selectors (`pkg/ipsec` — the swanctl secrets generation). In swanctl, a PSK secret with NO `id` matches ANY peer; with 2+ PSK VPNs each having a different PSK, strongSwan picks a PSK by matching against the peer identity — but with no `id` selectors it can match the WRONG secret to a peer (the first/any PSK), so a tunnel negotiates with the wrong pre-shared key → authentication FAILS (or, worse, a peer authenticates against the wrong VPN's PSK). Two IPsec VPNs with PSK auth cannot coexist reliably.

**Fix:** emit `id` selectors on each PSK secret entry — `secrets { ike-<conn> { secret = <psk>; id-<n> = <peer-id / local-id / gateway address> } }` — so strongSwan matches each PSK to the correct peer by identity/address. Derive the id from the connection's local/remote id or the gateway address (whatever uniquely identifies the peer for that VPN). Mirror the strongSwan swanctl secrets `id` convention (RFC-ish: the secret is selected by matching the id against the IKE peer). Verify 2 PSK VPNs each get their own PSK matched to their own peer.

**RED-on-revert:** two PSK VPNs (different PSKs, different peers) generate swanctl secrets each with an `id` selector matching its peer (goes RED — no id selectors, wrong PSK matched → auth fail — on revert); a single PSK VPN still works. Unit-test the generated swanctl secrets for 2 PSK VPNs (assert each has an id selector).

Provenance: fable-161 F-176, robustness/ipsec module.

## #3954 — networkd/RSS: idempotence probe misparses 'ethtool -x' when the RSS key's first byte is decimal → spurious 'ethtool -X' RSS rewrite mid-traffic (~39% of boots) (fable-161 F-056) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, robustness — spurious RSS reconfig mid-traffic):** the RSS-configuration idempotence probe parses `ethtool -x <iface>` (show RSS indirection table + hash key) to decide whether the desired RSS config is ALREADY applied (skip) or needs `ethtool -X` (rewrite). The parser misreads the hash-key/indirection output when a value's FIRST BYTE renders as a decimal-looking token (the ethtool output format — hex key bytes, or the indirection table's column layout — is misparsed for certain byte values), so the probe concludes the current config DIFFERS from desired even when it's identical → it issues a SPURIOUS `ethtool -X` (RSS indirection/key rewrite) on every reconcile. An `ethtool -X` mid-traffic RESETS the RSS hash/indirection → in-flight flows can be re-steered to different RX queues → packet REORDERING / a brief forwarding disruption (and on the AF_XDP path, a queue-rebind). Estimated ~39% of boots hit the misparse (depends on the randomly-generated key's first byte). So on a large fraction of boots/reconciles the RSS is needlessly rewritten, disrupting traffic.

**Fix:** correct the `ethtool -x` output parser so the idempotence comparison is ACCURATE — parse the hash key + indirection table exactly as ethtool emits them (hex bytes, the real column/row layout), so an already-correct RSS config compares EQUAL and the probe SKIPS the rewrite. Add a test with CAPTURED real `ethtool -x` output (covering a key whose first byte is a decimal-looking value + the indirection table) pinned as a golden fixture. Verify: desired==current → no ethtool -X; desired!=current → ethtool -X issued once.

**RED-on-revert:** given a captured `ethtool -x` output that MATCHES the desired RSS config (incl a first-byte-decimal key), the probe reports "already applied" → NO ethtool -X (goes RED — misparse → spurious ethtool -X — on revert); a genuinely-different config → ethtool -X once. Pin with the golden fixture.

Provenance: fable-161 F-056, robustness/networkd module.

## #3956 — dhcp: DHCPv4 client treats a RENEWING-state DHCPNAK like a timeout → keeps using the revoked address until T2 instead of restarting DISCOVER immediately (fable-161 F-173) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, DHCP correctness — holds a revoked address):** the DHCPv4 client (`pkg/dhcp`), while in the RENEWING state, treats a received DHCPNAK the same as a renew TIMEOUT — it keeps the current lease/address and waits (falling through to REBINDING at T2) instead of immediately abandoning the address. But a DHCPNAK in RENEWING means the server has explicitly REVOKED the lease (the address is no longer valid — e.g. the server reassigned it, or the client moved subnets). RFC 2131 §4.4.5: on a DHCPNAK the client MUST return to the INIT state (restart DISCOVER) and STOP using the address immediately. By treating the NAK as a timeout, xpf keeps configuring + using the REVOKED address until T2 (potentially minutes) → an address conflict (another host may now hold it) / a black-holed interface (the address is invalid on the network) until the delayed rebind.

**Fix:** in the RENEWING (and REBINDING) state, distinguish a DHCPNAK from a timeout — on a DHCPNAK, immediately (a) STOP using / DECONFIGURE the current address, and (b) return to INIT and restart DISCOVER (per RFC 2131 §4.4.5), rather than waiting for T2. Handle the RENEWING NAK and the REBINDING NAK. Verify a NAK in RENEWING triggers an immediate DISCOVER restart + address removal.

**RED-on-revert:** a DHCPNAK received in the RENEWING state → the client removes the address + restarts DISCOVER immediately (goes RED — keeps the revoked address until T2 — on revert); a genuine renew TIMEOUT still falls through to REBINDING; a normal ACK renews. Unit-test the RENEWING-state NAK handling (inject a NAK).

Provenance: fable-161 F-173, go-dhcp module. RFC 2131 §4.4.5.

## #3958 — config validation: ValidateConfig warns 'address not in address-book' for literal addresses / any / feed-names / address-sets → spurious false-positive warnings (fable-161 F-045) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, observability/UX — spurious validation warnings):** the config-validation warning pass (`ValidateConfig` — grep the "not in address-book" / address-reference warning) checks that a policy's source/destination address reference resolves to a defined address-book entry, but it does NOT exclude the reference forms that are NOT address-book names: a LITERAL address/CIDR (`10.0.0.0/8`, `2001:db8::/32`), the `any`/`any-ipv4`/`any-ipv6` keywords, a DYNAMIC ADDRESS FEED name (a `security dynamic-address` feed), and an ADDRESS-SET name. So for a perfectly valid policy that uses `any`, a literal CIDR, or a feed/address-set, the validator emits a FALSE "address X not in address-book" warning. Operators see spurious warnings on every commit of a normal config → they learn to IGNORE the validation warnings (alarm fatigue) → a REAL undefined-address warning gets lost in the noise.

**Fix:** the warning check must EXCLUDE the non-address-book reference forms before warning: (a) skip literal IPv4/IPv6 addresses + CIDRs (parse-check the token); (b) skip `any`/`any-ipv4`/`any-ipv6`; (c) skip a name that matches a defined dynamic-address FEED; (d) skip a name that matches a defined ADDRESS-SET (not just address-book address entries). Only warn for a name that is NONE of {literal, any, feed, address-set, address-book entry} — a genuinely undefined reference. Mirror how the STRICT compiler resolves these reference forms (the strict path already handles them; the warn pass drifted).

**RED-on-revert:** a policy using `any` / a literal `10.0.0.0/8` / a defined feed name / a defined address-set emits NO "not in address-book" warning (goes RED — false warning for each — on revert); a genuinely-undefined address name still warns. Unit-test the warn pass across the reference forms.

Provenance: fable-161 F-045, go-obs/config module.

## #3960 — dhcp relay: giaddr not re-resolved on a same-ifindex interface address change → the relayed reply path silently breaks (fable-161 F-172) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-161 (base ddf9f58701, re-verified STILL-LIVE on current origin/master).

**Defect (MEDIUM, DHCP relay reply-path break):** the DHCP relay (`pkg/dhcp` — the relay/giaddr path) sets the `giaddr` (gateway IP address) — the relay's own interface address that the DHCP SERVER uses to route the reply back — once (at start / on the relay-interface's initial address), and does NOT re-resolve it when the relay interface's IP ADDRESS CHANGES while the ifindex stays the SAME (e.g. a DHCP-learned address renew to a different IP, a static readdress, or an HA VIP move on the same netdev). So after the interface's address changes, the relay keeps stamping the OLD `giaddr` → the DHCP server sends the reply to the old (now-invalid) relay address → the reply is BLACKHOLED → clients behind the relay stop getting leases (silently — the relay still forwards requests, but replies never arrive).

**Fix:** re-resolve the relay interface's current address for the `giaddr` at RELAY TIME (per relayed packet, or on an address-change event), not once at start. Watch the relay interface's address (a netlink address-change subscription, or re-read the current primary address each relay) so a same-ifindex address change updates the `giaddr`. Verify a relay-interface readdress updates the giaddr on the next relayed request. (Note: F-3950 fixed the link-STATE monitor's resilience; this is the ADDRESS-change re-resolution for the relay's giaddr.)

**RED-on-revert:** after the relay interface's address changes (same ifindex), the next relayed DHCP request carries the NEW giaddr (goes RED — stale old giaddr → reply blackholed — on revert); an unchanged interface keeps its giaddr; a relay with no address is handled. Unit-test the giaddr re-resolution across an interface address change.

Provenance: fable-161 F-172, go-dhcp module.
