## #4102 — vsrx-parity: predefined Junos application-SETS (junos-ms-rpc, junos-sun-rpc, junos-cifs, junos-routing-inbound) are absent → a canonical vSRX policy referencing one is hard-rejected at commit (fable-163 F14) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175 == origin/master). MEDIUM, vsrx-parity/feature-completeness. Fail-CLOSED (no security hole) but a direct parity regression. VERIFY-FIRST at HEAD.

**Defect:** pkg/config/predefined.go:11 ships 89 individual apps but NO predefined application-SET table — the RPC bundles exist only as protocol-split members (junos-ms-rpc-tcp/-udp, junos-sun-rpc-tcp/-udp), while junos-ms-rpc, junos-sun-rpc, junos-cifs, junos-routing-inbound are nowhere. ResolveApplicationSet (:164) consults ONLY user-defined sets (contrast ResolveApplication :151 which checks the predefined table). The commit gate appRefError (compiler_validate_strict.go:2147) + the runtime resolver resolveUserspaceApplicationNames (capabilities.go:395) both hard-fail an unresolved token.

**Impact:** a stock vSRX rule `set security policies from-zone trust to-zone untrust policy allow-rpc match application junos-ms-rpc` → validatePolicyMatchApplicationsStrict → appRefError (ResolveApplication misses [only -tcp/-udp defined], ResolveApplicationSet misses [no predefined-set table]) → commit/commit-check FAILS. On the tolerant/HA-sync path the strict gate warns, but resolveUserspaceApplicationNames hits the same miss → __unsupported__ sentinel → Rust SnapshotIntegrityError rejects the whole snapshot. Fail-closed but the config is unusable — a firewall cloning vSRX cannot commit a canonical vSRX policy; every migrated config using these breaks at commit.

**Fix:** add a PredefinedApplicationSets table in predefined.go seeded with the standard Junos sets (junos-ms-rpc = {junos-ms-rpc-tcp, junos-ms-rpc-udp}, junos-sun-rpc = {junos-sun-rpc-tcp, junos-sun-rpc-udp}, junos-cifs, junos-routing-inbound — verify the canonical members against a vSRX reference), and have ResolveApplicationSet/ExpandApplicationSet fall back to it (mirroring ResolveApplication's user-then-predefined order). Both the commit gate + the runtime resolver route through those functions, so one table fixes all surfaces.

**RED-on-revert:** a policy referencing `application junos-ms-rpc` commits + resolves to the tcp+udp members (goes RED — appRefError hard-reject — on revert); a user-defined set still resolves; an unknown app-set still hard-fails. Compile-path test.

Provenance: fable-163 F14, vsrx-parity/feature-completeness/applications. Closest F-160 (typo'd member) = user-defined sets. Go.

## #4103 — WireGuard hardening: (F5) #4092 responder TAI64N anti-replay high-water resets to 0 on every WG config change — a routine commit silently disarms the landed anti-replay; (F12) WG private key + PSK config carriers are non-zeroized [u8;32] Clone (fable-163 F5+F12) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175 == origin/master). Two same-file (wg/ build path) hardening findings — one PR. RUST (cargo). VERIFY-FIRST at HEAD.

**F5 (MEDIUM, security/regression — hole INSIDE the landed #4092 fix):** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/peer.rs:176-194 claims greatest_tai64n 'survives config commits (same pubkey → same Arc<Peer>)', but forwarding_build/wg.rs:20 explicitly says 'do NOT call reconcile_peers'. A byte-identical config reuses the whole engine Arc; but any identity change (wg_peers_eq compares pubkey/allowed_ips/endpoint/keepalive/PSK) builds a fresh WgEngine::new → fresh Peer::new → greatest_tai64n=[0;12], and ONLY the OUTGOING clock is re-seeded (seed_tai64n_high_water, #1432 — wg.rs:86). No seed path exists for the INCOMING high-water. So a benign WG commit (add allowed-ip, rotate PSK, add a peer) resets P's responder high-water to 0 → an attacker who captured a valid type-1 initiation from P (timestamp T0>0) replays it → check_and_update_tai64n(T0) returns true → full Noise crypto + unconfirmed session + msg2 — the exact replay #4092 closed. Diverges from kernel/wireguard-go (retain per-peer last_timestamp across reconfigure). The asymmetry is the tell: the initiator clock got explicit rebuild-survival plumbing (#1432); the #4092 responder high-water did not.
FIX (F5): mirror #1432 — add Peer::greatest_tai64n() / seed_greatest_tai64n(), and in the rebuild branch copy each SURVIVING peer's high-water from prev_engine into the fresh engine (reset only on an actual pubkey change — a pubkey change is a different peer identity). VERIFY-FIRST: confirm a routine WG change rebuilds the engine + resets greatest_tai64n (the #4095 review said 'survives config commits' — reconcile that claim with wg_peers_eq comparing PSK; if a same-pubkey change actually preserves the Arc<Peer>, report already-correct).
RED-on-revert (F5): a peer handshakes (high-water=T_last) → a benign WG commit → a replayed type-1 (T0 <= T_last) is REJECTED (goes RED — high-water reset to 0, replay accepted — on revert). Rust test: install high-water, rebuild engine, assert the surviving peer's high-water preserved + a replay rejected.

**F12 (LOW, security/key-hygiene):** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/engine.rs:176-213 — WgEngineConfig.local_private_key: [u8;32] + WgPeerConfig.preshared_key: [u8;32] are #[derive(Clone)] with NO Zeroize, even though the module's RUNTIME copies ARE wrapped (engine.rs:345 private key Zeroizing, peer.rs:61 PSK Zeroizing). Build sites deref the Zeroizing source into the plaintext carrier (forwarding_build/wg.rs:60,79) → every WG commit leaves a 32-byte X25519 private key + all PSKs in freed heap/stack (recoverable via core dump / heap-spray).
FIX (F12): make both fields zeroize::Zeroizing<[u8;32]> (or ZeroizeOnDrop), matching the runtime types.
RED-on-revert (F12): a compile/layout assertion or a drop test that the carrier is zeroized on drop (goes RED — plaintext [u8;32] non-zeroized — on revert).

FULL cargo test --release. Provenance: fable-163 F5 (hole in #4092, not the original F-190) + F12 (in-memory carrier non-zeroization, not F-087 on-disk). RUST.

## #4107 — security: the gRPC fabric listener registers the FULL mutating+destructive 48-RPC service with no auth (remote SystemAction{zeroize}/reboot/Commit), and HA heartbeat/session-sync carry election state + plaintext session data with no authentication (fable-163 F1+F23) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-01)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175, verified at HEAD). TWO findings on the same control-segment threat model → converge a plan. RESEARCH (design decision — the auth mechanism + trust posture).

**F1 (HIGH, security/authz):** pkg/grpcapi/server.go:235-258 RunFabricListener builds a server with ONLY configLockInterceptor (a lock-reaper, NOT an auth gate) and calls RegisterBpfrxServiceServer(srv, s) — the identical FULL 48-RPC service registered on the loopback listener at :211. Started on the sync-interface IP in cluster mode (daemon_ha_sync.go:549-561, %s:50051 on both fabrics). Destructive RPCs reachable UNAUTH: SystemAction{reboot,halt,power-off,zeroize} (server_diag.go:717-768) + Commit/Delete/Rollback (server_config.go:152-252). The remote client sends no identity (cmd/cli/main.go insecure.NewCredentials()). → any host on the control/sync segment (e.g. the loss cluster's em0 10.99.x shared VLAN — not a dedicated crossover) or a spoofing peer opens a plaintext gRPC channel to <peer>:50051 → SystemAction{zeroize} deletes /etc/xpf/*.conf + rollbacks + BPF pins + networkd; or Commit/Delete rewrites policy. All UNAUTH — the login-class RBAC the interactive CLI enforces is entirely bypassed. The listener's documented purpose is READ-ONLY monitor-proxying; it exposes the entire write surface.

**F23 (LOW behavior / defense-in-depth):** pkg/cluster/heartbeat.go:134-290 wire format = fixed magic BPFX + version + CLEARTEXT RG/priority/weight/state; heartbeat_manager.go:429-439 accepts any packet whose ClusterID matches + NodeID differs — no HMAC/secret/nonce. Session-sync (sync.go:233, sync_conn.go:1108) is an equally unauthenticated net.Listener carrying 5-tuples + NAT bindings in cleartext. → an L2 attacker on the control segment learns the 16-bit ClusterID (cleartext), forges a heartbeat (Weight=0 → local claims PRIMARY; or a higher-priority peer → local forced SECONDARY) → controlled failover/blackhole; session frames readable. Mitigating (why Low): a dedicated operator-controlled link matches Juniper's own unauthenticated direct-cable posture. Compounds with F1 on the same segment.

**Design questions (converge a PLAN):**
- F1: register a RESTRICTED service on the fabric listener (monitor/show + explicitly-proxied RPCs only — a separate gRPC service descriptor), OR add a peer-identity interceptor (mTLS cluster cert / bind-to-known-peer-IP allowlist) rejecting every non-whitelisted RPC. Which? (The restricted-service approach is cleaner + fail-closed; mTLS is heavier but stronger.) How does it compose with the existing sync RPCs the fabric legitimately proxies?
- F23: optional PSK HMAC (`set chassis cluster control-link authentication-key`) over heartbeat + sync frames with a monotonic/nonce anti-replay field; OR document the trust assumption if auth stays out of scope (matching Juniper's direct-cable posture). 
- Relationship to F-155 (#4047, REST non-loopback unauth — design-deferred): F1 is the gRPC fabric analog. Should these converge on ONE management-plane auth posture?
Converge PLAN-READY (restricted-fabric-service is likely the driveable F1 half) / PLAN-DEFER (mTLS/HMAC = larger). Provenance: fable-163 F1+F23, security/ha/grpc/hardening. Not in the 528-title corpus. Go.

## #4108 — security/RBAC: the 'operator' login class can request system zeroize/reboot/halt/power-off (Junos operator lacks maintenance), and destructive SystemAction (zeroize/reboot) is not written to the commit audit journal (fable-163 F8+F21) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175, verified at HEAD). TWO coupled RBAC/audit findings for destructive maintenance verbs → one PR. Go.

**F21 (MEDIUM, security/rbac/vsrx-parity):** pkg/cli/permissions.go:67-68 maps ALL of request/test → PermControl; types_system.go:558 gives operator {PermView, PermClear, PermControl}. So operator holds PermControl and passes the gate for `request system zeroize` (destructive verbs at cmdtree/tree.go:909-912). On Junos the predefined `operator` class LACKS `maintenance`, so it cannot reboot/zeroize. xpf grants a destructive maintenance verb to a non-super class — a privilege-model divergence.
FIX (F21): add a `maintenance`/PermMaint permission for `request system {reboot,halt,power-off,zeroize}` (+ cluster failover), granted ONLY to super-user; keep benign `request` verbs at PermControl. Map the destructive verbs to PermMaint in the command→permission gate. Verify operator is DENIED zeroize/reboot while super-user is allowed; benign `request` (e.g. request routing-engine, request session) still works for operator.

**F8 (LOW, audit/observability/security):** pkg/grpcapi/server_diag.go:717-776 — each SystemAction only slog.Warn's; none call the configstore journal (pkg/configstore/journal, which records commit/commit_confirmed/auto_rollback/config_sync/persist_*). → zeroize (full config wipe) + reboot leave NO tamper-resistant audit record (only a journald line that does not survive the zeroize), defeating post-incident attribution.
FIX (F8): emit a `system_action` journal entry (actor, action, timestamp) BEFORE executing the action (so it's recorded even if the action wipes/reboots). Reuse the configstore journal mechanism.

**RED-on-revert:** (F21) operator running `request system zeroize` is DENIED (permission error) while super-user is allowed (goes RED — operator allowed — on revert). (F8) a SystemAction writes a system_action journal entry (goes RED — no journal entry — on revert). Unit-test the RBAC gate per class + the journal emission.

Provenance: fable-163 F8+F21, security/rbac/audit/vsrx-parity. F-023/F-055 concern monitor-mapping/sudoers, not this over-grant. Go.

## #4109 — security/DoS: TCP half-open→ESTABLISHED promotion fires on ANY ACK-bearing segment (no reverse SYN-ACK required, defeats the #3152 SYN-flood reap with a 2-packet SYN+ACK), and TCP close/reset state is never propagated to the forward↔reverse companion (fable-163 F16+F17+F15) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175, verified at HEAD). TWO coupled TCP-state-machine findings + their test gap → one PR. RUST (session, cargo). VERIFY-FIRST (Junos syn-check semantics).

**F16 (MEDIUM, security/dos/vsrx-parity):** userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs:102-111 (mirror mod.rs:1118-1125, seed install.rs:158): `if matches!(key.protocol, PROTO_TCP) && has_ack(tcp_flags) { entry.established = true; }`. has_ack is a pure bit test — nothing requires a reverse SYN-ACK was observed or that this is the handshake-completing ACK. → attacker sends a bare SYN (OPENING, 20s, 1 slot) then a bare ACK (0x10) on the same 5-tuple (slow path — the SYN was non-cacheable) → established=true → expires_after recomputed to tcp_established_ns (300s). No real peer responded; the attacker holds a 300s session for 2 packets, refreshed with 1 packet per <300s. The #3152 half-open reap (bounds max_sessions from bare-SYN floods) is BYPASSED — the flood is 'SYN+ACK' instead of 'SYN'. A real vSRX (syn-check default-on) does not mark ESTABLISHED on a client ACK preceding the server SYN-ACK.
FIX (F16): gate promotion on evidence of a real handshake — only promote when the ACK arrives on the direction OPPOSITE the opening SYN (reverse SYN-ACK seen), OR track a two-bit handshake state (saw-SYN/saw-SYNACK/saw-ACK) requiring SYN-ACK before ESTABLISHED. VERIFY-FIRST: confirm xpf promotes on any ACK + that this diverges from the intended syn-check behavior (grep syn-check / the promotion logic — is there a no-syn-check knob that SHOULD gate this? #2078 says the knobs are accepted-only).

**F17 (MEDIUM, correctness/dos):** lookup.rs:79-101 mutates ONLY the single matched entry; the reverse companion is a separate SessionEntry (shared_ops.rs:836-844, own key_to_handle). key_to_handle is probed first (lookup.rs:37), so a packet whose wire tuple == the reverse key resolves the reverse entry directly + updates only it. `if is_closing(tcp_flags) { entry.closing = true; entry.reset |= has_rst(tcp_flags); }` — no path marks the companion. → a responder RST (unidirectional) hits the reverse entry → closing/reset → reverse expires_after = TCP_RST_TIMEOUT_NS (2s); the FORWARD entry never sees the RST → stays closing=false, 300s. The dead flow's forward half lingers up to 300s instead of 2s (#3046). Symmetric for a one-sided FIN vs #3489's 30s. → #3046's 2s reset-reap is ~50% effective under a reset workload; every RST-closed flow still pins one established-timeout entry. On vSRX a RST invalidates the WHOLE session.
FIX (F17): when a FIN/RST advances one entry into closing/reset, look up + stamp the same state onto its companion (via reverse_session_key/forward_wire_key), OR track close state once per flow on the canonical forward entry + read through from the reverse.

**F15 (test gap):** session/tests.rs:1264-1297 covers only the honest SYN→SYN-ACK→ACK order; :1061-1171 close-window tests use a single entry; no companion is_reverse:true+closing test. F16/F17 are invisible to CI. ADD: (a) a test that SYN then a forward bare-ACK with no reverse SYN-ACK keeps the entry OPENING (not ESTABLISHED); (b) a test that a RST on one direction reaps BOTH the forward + reverse companion at the short window.

**RED-on-revert:** (F16) a SYN + bare-ACK (no reverse SYN-ACK) stays OPENING/not-ESTABLISHED (goes RED — promoted to 300s ESTABLISHED — on revert). (F17) a one-directional RST reaps BOTH companion entries to the 2s window (goes RED — the other half lingers 300s — on revert). FULL cargo test --release.

## #4112 — screen: icmp/udp flood thresholds are enforced per-ZONE aggregate (Junos measures per destination IP, UDP per dest IP+port), and the per-destination SYN-flood cap is bypassed when the zone is over attack-threshold with syn-cookie active (fable-163 F18+F19) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175, verified at HEAD). TWO coupled screen findings → one PR. RUST (screen, cargo). VERIFY-FIRST.

**F18 (MEDIUM, vsrx-parity/correctness):** userspace-dp/src/screen/mod.rs:157-159 keys icmp_counters/udp_counters by ZONE NAME ONLY; :610-627 uses a zone-wide get_mut(zone) counter with no per-destination dimension. Junos `icmp flood threshold N` / `udp flood threshold N` cap the rate to a single DESTINATION (UDP additionally to a destination PORT); traffic to different destinations counts independently. → (a) two legitimate high-volume services in one zone (DNS resolver + VoIP) SUM into one counter → combined benign rate crosses threshold → false-dropped as a flood though no single dest is flooded; (b) an attacker spreading a modest flood across many destinations stays under the per-zone aggregate while no single victim is rate-limited as the operator expects. Contrast: SYN-flood grew per-dst/per-src count-min sub-thresholds (#3315); ICMP/UDP did not.
FIX (F18): give ICMP/UDP flood the same per-destination substrate the SYN-flood path has (a per-zone destination-keyed count-min sketch of RateCounters, UDP additionally keyed on destination port), keeping the per-zone aggregate as an OPTIONAL secondary ceiling. Mirror the #3315 syn_dst_sketch mechanism.

**F19 (LOW, correctness/defense-in-depth/docs):** screen/mod.rs:665-705 returns (mint cookie challenge, or Drop) on the aggregate over_attack branch BEFORE the per-dst check at :719-728, which is DOCUMENTED as always-on ('(2) per-DESTINATION cap — PRIMARY, always runs (even when cookie-active)'). → syn-cookie enabled, attack-threshold 200, destination-threshold 2: a real-client (non-spoofed) flood targets one backend, pushes the zone aggregate past 200 → over_attack==true on each SYN → every SYN takes the `if over_attack { SynCookieChallenge }` early-return → the per-dst sketch at :722 is NEVER reached → the per-destination hard-drop never engages → clients completing the cookie handshake are admitted to the flooded backend. destination-threshold's purpose (shield a single over-threshold victim even from VALIDATED clients) is defeated precisely in the high-load regime it was configured for. A concrete code-vs-comment contradiction. Test syn_flood_dest_runs_when_cookie_active (tests.rs:2146) pins per-dst only with syn_flood_threshold=100_000 (aggregate never trips); the over_attack==true case is untested.
FIX (F19): evaluate the per-dst sketch BEFORE the aggregate over_attack early-return (so a per-dst trip hard-drops even while the zone mints cookies), or correct the comment; add a test with a LOW syn_flood_threshold so over_attack fires.

**RED-on-revert:** (F18) traffic to 2 distinct destinations in one zone counts independently (each per-dst), not summed (goes RED — one zone counter, false-drop / cross-dst evasion — on revert); a single-dest flood still capped. (F19) with over_attack active + syn-cookie, a per-destination-over-threshold backend is hard-dropped even for cookie-validated clients (goes RED — admitted — on revert). FULL cargo test --release.

Provenance: fable-163 F18+F19, screen/vsrx-parity/correctness. #3315 syn-flood substrate. RUST.

## #4113 — XDP shim: record_trace forces a per-packet BPF map insert on EARLY_FILTER/BINDING_MISSING even when tracing is disabled (attacker-influenceable hot-path amplification), and USERSPACE_FALLBACK_STATS is a shared non-per-CPU Array with a non-atomic RMW (lost counts across XDP CPUs) (fable-163 F7+F13) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175, verified at HEAD). TWO XDP-SHIM findings → one PR. RUST userspace-xdp — this is the retained AF_XDP shim: a change here needs `make generate` (pinned toolchain + kernel-verifier gate, #1864, see pkg/dataplane/README.md). Serialize the cargo/generate. VERIFY-FIRST.

**F7 (LOW, perf/security/dos):** userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1074-1119 record_trace, forced set at :1084-1090: `let forced = matches!(stage, USERSPACE_TRACE_STAGE_BINDING_MISSING | USERSPACE_TRACE_STAGE_EARLY_FILTER); if !forced && (ctrl_flags & USERSPACE_CTRL_FLAG_TRACE) == 0 { return; } ... let _ = USERSPACE_TRACE.insert(&trace_key, &value, 0);` — the `forced` set BYPASSES the trace-disabled early-out → a bpf_map_update per packet even when tracing is OFF. → attacker floods UDP/TCP frames whose dst is 255.255.255.255 / 224.0.0.0/4 / 169.254/16 (or v6 ff00::/8 / fe80::/10) → should_fallback_early (:1324) true → record_trace runs with stage=EARLY_FILTER (in forced) → the TRACE-off early-out skipped → every packet does bpf_ktime_get_ns + an avalanche key compute + bpf_map_update_elem (per-bucket lock) on the native-XDP ingress core. BINDING_MISSING (:438) forces the same for every transit packet on a transiently-unbound queue during a config-reload. The codebase deliberately keeps disabled features OFF the per-packet path (the WG-gate comment lib.rs:64-74: even a bare load+compare nudged v6 best-effort into non-zero retransmits at line rate) — a forced map insert + ktime read per packet is far heavier + reachable by unauth traffic to well-known multicast/broadcast groups.
FIX (F7): gate the USERSPACE_TRACE.insert on the TRACE flag UNCONDITIONALLY; keep only the counter bump forced. If binding-missing visibility is needed, publish via the (F13-fixed) counter array or 1-in-N sample the forced insert.

**F13 (LOW, correctness/observability):** userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:377-379 (decl) + :1063-1072 (RMW), 12 call sites: `static USERSPACE_FALLBACK_STATS: Array<u64> = Array::with_max_entries(USERSPACE_FALLBACK_REASON_MAX, 0);` (NOT PerCpuArray) + `*ptr = (*ptr).saturating_add(1);` (load; add; store — NOT atomic). → native XDP runs one program instance per RX queue on distinct CPUs concurrently (loss cluster VFs = 6 RX queues → 6 workers); two CPUs take a fallback branch for the same reason in the same window → both read v, compute v+1, store v+1 → one increment LOST (classic shared-memory RMW race). The Go control plane surfaces this as the operator degraded_path_counters → undercounts exactly under the high-load/attack conditions when they matter for triage. This is the shim's ONLY visibility into strict-mode/heartbeat-stale/binding-missing/redirect-error/local-pass drops. #45 removed atomic RMW for the retired eBPF pipeline PRECISELY because those counters were on PER-CPU maps; the retained shim regressed to a shared Array while keeping the per-CPU-only-safe non-atomic increment.
FIX (F13): make USERSPACE_FALLBACK_STATS a PerCpuArray<u64> (Go already sums per-CPU arrays — verify the Go read side sums per-CPU) so the non-atomic increment is CPU-local + correct (matches #45), OR use an atomic add if it must stay a single Array. PerCpuArray is the idiomatic choice.

**RED-on-revert:** (F7) with tracing OFF, an EARLY_FILTER/BINDING_MISSING packet does NOT do a USERSPACE_TRACE map insert (goes RED — forced insert per packet — on revert); with tracing ON it still inserts. (F13) concurrent increments across CPUs for one reason sum correctly (PerCpuArray) (goes RED — lost updates on the shared Array — on revert, provable via a per-CPU-sum test or a race assertion). FULL cargo test --release + `make generate` (kernel-verifier gate) since the shim .o changes.

Provenance: fable-163 F7+F13, xdp-shim/perf/dos/observability. #45 per-CPU-counter lineage. RUST (make generate).

## #4114 — screen: port-scan/ip-sweep 'threshold' is a distinct-destination COUNT over a fixed 10s window — Junos 'threshold' is a TIME window in microseconds — so a copied Junos config either disables detection or the default false-drops normal browsing (fable-163 F11) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175, verified at HEAD). MEDIUM vsrx-parity/correctness/availability. RESEARCH (a semantics change — the threshold unit + window). VERIFY-FIRST.

**Defect:** userspace-dp/src/screen/scan.rs:112 fixes WINDOW_SECS=10; :286 compares the threshold as a COUNT of unique entries (entry.1.len() as u32 > effective_threshold). The compiler comment (compiler_security.go:50-62) states the divergence OUTRIGHT: 'Junos flags a port scan / address sweep when one source reaches 10 distinct destination ports/addresses within a 5000-MICROSECOND window. This engine interprets the threshold as a DISTINCT-DESTINATION COUNT over a fixed 10-SECOND window ... feeding 5000 here would be read as a count and clamped to the dataplane cap (1023), effectively never firing.' maxScanSweepThreshold=1023; validateScreenScanSweepThresholds only WARNS above it.
→ (a) a Junos operator writes `ip ip-sweep threshold 5000` (5000 = the Junos microsecond default) → commits with only an advisory warning → ScanCore clamps to 1023 → fires only if one source reaches 1024 distinct destinations in 10s → effectively NEVER → the operator believes ip-sweep is armed; it's inert. (b) an operator enabling the screen with NO explicit threshold gets the default 10 over a 10-second window → a single host opening flows to >=11 distinct destinations in 10s (a normal web page / fan-out client) trips ip-sweep + is dropped → Junos' 5ms window would never flag it. False sense of protection in one direction + unpredictable outage in the other.

**Design question (converge a PLAN):** interpret threshold as Junos does — a FIXED detection count (10) crossed within a CONFIGURABLE TIME window (microseconds) — rather than a configurable count over a hardcoded 10s. Options: (1) full Junos semantics (fixed count 10, configurable µs window) — the most faithful but a bigger change (the scan tracker must window in µs); (2) minimum: tighten WINDOW_SECS, REJECT (not warn) count-shaped values above the tracker cap, document the unit. Which? Converge PLAN-READY (the semantics + the wire/config mapping) or PLAN-DEFER. Consider back-compat (an existing config relying on the current count-over-10s behavior). Go compiler (the config→threshold mapping) + Rust screen (the windowing).

**RED-on-revert (once plan converges):** a Junos ip-sweep threshold value fires detection at the Junos-equivalent rate (not clamped-to-never / not false-dropping normal browsing) (goes RED — count-over-10s misinterpretation — on revert). 

Provenance: fable-163 F11, screen/vsrx-parity/availability. Distinct from feature-gaps.md:251 (vague) + #3230 (unset→0) + #2234/#2227 (tracker bounds). RESEARCH. Go+Rust.

## #4116 — VRRP: an address-owner (priority 255) with preempt disabled never reclaims mastership from a lower-priority peer — RFC 5798 §6.1 / vSRX owner semantics violated (fable-163 F22) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175, verified at HEAD). LOW, vsrx-parity/rfc-conformance/ha. Narrow (owner + preempt-disabled). VERIFY-FIRST.

**Defect:** pkg/vrrp/track.go:32-48 passes priority 255 through unchanged; pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1524-1530 resets the master-down timer on ANY advert when preempt is off:
    if !vi.getPreempt() || int(pkt.Priority) >= pri { masterDownTimer.Reset(vi.masterDownInterval()) ... }
→ operator configures the address-owner instance (priority 255, no-preempt) → owner reboots → peer (priority < 255) becomes MASTER + holds the VIP → owner returns → StateBackup → hears the peer's LOWER-priority advert → !getPreempt() true → masterDownTimer.Reset on every advert → owner stays BACKUP indefinitely though it OWNS the VIP. A real vSRX owner resumes MASTER immediately (RFC 5798 §6.1: the address owner always preempts).

**Fix:** treat priority 255 as UNCONDITIONALLY preempting (force effective preempt=true when cfg.Priority == 255), OR reject/normalize no-preempt on an owner at commit. The force-preempt-on-255 approach is cleaner (the owner always reclaims). Verify it doesn't break the owner-255-exempt logic elsewhere (the effective-priority demotion is owner-255-exempt per the HA notes).

**RED-on-revert:** an owner (priority 255, no-preempt) returning after a peer took over RECLAIMS MASTER (goes RED — stays BACKUP indefinitely — on revert); a non-owner no-preempt instance still honors no-preempt. Unit-test the owner-255 preempt behavior.

Provenance: fable-163 F22, vsrx-parity/rfc-conformance/ha. Go.

## #4117 — IPsec: ESP proposals silently fall back to strongSwan 'default' suite when a policy's proposal reference dangles with no PFS group — quietly weakens ESP crypto instead of failing closed (fable-163 F24) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175, verified at HEAD). LOW, security/ipsec/vsrx-parity. VERIFY-FIRST.

**Defect:** pkg/ipsec/ike.go:100-170 — the #2073 fallback only preserves crypto intent when pfsGroup > 0; otherwise returns the initial espProposals = "default", and policy.go:182 emits `esp_proposals = default` UNCONDITIONALLY (no `!= ""` guard, unlike the IKE `proposals` line at :157). → on the tolerant/peer-sync boot path (strict validator downgraded to warn), an ipsec-policy referencing an UNDEFINED proposal with no PFS group → 0 built proposals → "default" → strongSwan negotiates its built-in ESP suite instead of the operator's intended cipher/integrity. Asymmetric: IKE SKIPS the VPN (#2270 fail-closed), ESP quietly DOWNGRADES.

**Fix:** emit a conservative FIXED fallback (e.g. aes256-sha256) or SKIP the child like the IKE path (#2270 fail-closed), even at pfsGroup == 0 — a dangling reference should NOT silently weaken ESP crypto. Prefer the fail-closed skip (parity with IKE) unless a conservative fixed suite is more operationally appropriate (decide + document).

**RED-on-revert:** an ipsec-policy with a dangling ESP-proposal reference + no PFS group does NOT emit `esp_proposals = default` (either skips the child or emits the conservative fixed suite) (goes RED — silent "default" downgrade — on revert); a valid proposal reference still emits the intended suite. Unit-test the ESP-proposal render with a dangling ref at pfsGroup==0.

Provenance: fable-163 F24, security/ipsec/vsrx-parity. Not F-017 / #2073 / #2270 (those are the validated-reference/IKE cases). Go.

## #4118 — vsrx-parity: DHCPv4 client ignores classless-static-routes (RFC 3442 option 121 / legacy 249) — only option 3 default gateway is honored → missing/wrong routing on DHCP uplinks in provider networks (fable-163 F25) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

**Fix:** parse option 121 (+ legacy 249) in leaseFromACKv4 (the ACK is a dhcpv4 message — check if the dhcp library exposes option 121; the RFC 3442 encoding is a series of {prefix-length, significant-prefix-octets, gateway}), program the routes via the FRR recompile path (grep how the option-3 default route is programmed — mirror it for the classless routes), and honor RFC 3442 PRECEDENCE (when option 121 is present, it supersedes option 3 — do NOT also install the option-3 default route, or install both per the RFC). Verify the encoding/decoding + the route-programming path.

**RED-on-revert:** a DHCP ACK with option 121 (a classless route + gateway) programs that route (goes RED — option 121 dropped, only option 3 honored — on revert); option 121 supersedes option 3 per RFC 3442; an ACK with only option 3 still works. Unit-test the option-121 parse + route programming.

## #4119 — RA: 'router-advertisement default-lifetime 0' is both commit-rejected and runtime-coerced to 1800 — xpf cannot advertise 'not a default router' (RFC 4861 §6.2.1), hijacking host default-route selection on multi-router LANs (fable-163 F26) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Found by fable-review-163 (base 20480f5175, verified at HEAD). LOW, vsrx-parity/rfc-conformance. VERIFY-FIRST.

**Defect:** pkg/config/schema_routing.go:442-444 validator ValidateInteger(1, 65535) REJECTS 0 at commit; pkg/ra/sender.go:670-672 coerces DefaultLifetime <= 0 → 1800; types_routing.go:321 bakes `0 = default (1800)`. → an operator who wants xpf to advertise prefixes / PREF64 but NOT be an IPv6 default router (RFC 4861 §6.2.1 RouterLifetime 0) cannot express it — commit rejects 0, and even absent the reject the sender floors to 1800. On a multi-router LAN xpf always advertises >=1800s Router Lifetime, hijacking host default-route selection. Junos accepts default-lifetime 0.

**Fix:** lower the schema floor to 0 (ValidateInteger(0, 65535)) AND distinguish UNSET from EXPLICIT 0 in the sender — use a *int / a bool-set flag so an explicit 0 marshals RouterLifetime:0 (advertise 'not a default router') while ABSENT still defaults 1800 (the current behavior). types_routing.go:321's `0 = default` conflation is the crux — separate 'unset' from 'explicit 0'.

**RED-on-revert:** `set ... router-advertisement default-lifetime 0` commits + the RA sender emits RouterLifetime:0 (goes RED — commit rejects 0 / sender floors to 1800 — on revert); an ABSENT default-lifetime still defaults to 1800; a value 1-65535 unchanged. Unit-test the schema + the sender (unset vs explicit-0 vs a value).

Provenance: fable-163 F26, vsrx-parity/rfc-conformance. Distinct from F-232 (upper-bound wrap). Go.

## #4122 — security: add a fail-closed fabric-gRPC allowlist interceptor so the cluster fabric listener exposes ONLY the 6 read/monitor RPCs it proxies — closes unauth remote SystemAction{zeroize}/reboot + Commit/Delete/Rollback (fable-163 F1 driveable half, from #4107 PLAN-READY) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-04)

Driveable half of #4107 (fable-163 F1), converged PLAN-READY by /research (see #4107 comment). The F23 + peer-identity-auth (PSK/HMAC/mTLS) half stays deferred on #4107.

**Verified defect (HEAD c12c8571f):** pkg/grpcapi/server.go RunFabricListener builds grpc.NewServer(UnaryInterceptor(configLockInterceptor)) [a stale-lock reaper, NOT auth] then RegisterBpfrxServiceServer(srv, s) — the IDENTICAL full 48-RPC service as the loopback Run() listener. Started on the sync/fabric IP in cluster mode (daemon_ha_sync.go ~547-561, %s:50051). The main listener is 127.0.0.1:50051 (cmd/xpfd/main.go:222), so the FABRIC listener is the ONLY network-exposed gRPC surface. Destructive RPCs reachable UNAUTH: SystemAction reboot/halt/power-off/zeroize (server_diag.go:717, zeroize wipes /etc/xpf/*.conf+rollback+/sys/fs/bpf/xpf+networkd), Delete (server_config.go:152), Commit (:186), Rollback (:250). Client sends no identity (cmd/cli:33 insecure.NewCredentials), no source-IP allowlist.

**Fabric-safe RPC allowlist (verified — every dialPeer→NewBpfrxServiceClient call site):** GetStatus, GetSessions, GetSessionSummary, ShowText, MonitorInterface (server-streaming), ClearSessions. PLUS SystemAction is proxied ONLY for the two cluster-failover actions (server_diag.go:937 cluster-failover-data:node<N>, :1005 cluster-rg-failover...:node<N>). reboot/halt/power-off/zeroize/Commit/Delete/Rollback are NEVER proxied.

**CRITICAL NUANCE:** SystemAction MULTIPLEXES fabric-safe (cluster-failover) + destructive (zeroize/reboot) under ONE gRPC method. A pure method-name allowlist that INCLUDES SystemAction would still expose zeroize. So EITHER (a) EXCLUDE SystemAction from the fabric allowlist entirely (cost: a cross-node `request chassis cluster failover node <peer>` runs LOCALLY instead of proxying — acceptable, verify the UX), OR (b) a nested-action allowlist that inspects the SystemAction request's action field + permits ONLY the two cluster-failover:node forms, denying zeroize/reboot/halt/power-off. Prefer (a) exclude-SystemAction for simplicity + fail-closed clarity UNLESS the cross-node-failover UX must be preserved, in which case (b). Decide + document.

**Fix:** add a fail-closed fabric allowlist interceptor PAIR (Unary + Stream — MonitorInterface streams) on the FABRIC listener only, checking info.FullMethod against the allowlisted read/monitor methods, DEFAULT-DENY (codes.PermissionDenied). Chain WITH the existing configLockInterceptor (grpc.ChainUnaryInterceptor / ChainStreamInterceptor). Leave the LOOPBACK listener's full service UNCHANGED (127.0.0.1 is the local trusted surface). Self-contained in pkg/grpcapi/server.go, no proto/wire regen.

**RED-on-revert:** a fabric-listener call to SystemAction{zeroize} (+ Commit/Delete/Rollback) is DENIED (PermissionDenied) while the 6 read/monitor RPCs + MonitorInterface stream succeed (goes RED — full service exposed, zeroize reachable — on revert); the loopback listener still serves the full service. Unit-test the interceptor: allowlisted method allowed, destructive method denied, unknown method denied, on the fabric interceptor; loopback unaffected.

Provenance: fable-163 F1 (driveable half), from #4107 /research PLAN-READY. security/ha/grpc/hardening. Go.

## #4146 — host-inbound: to-zone junos-host deny not enforced for direct host-bound traffic — the XDP shim shunts local-destined packets to the kernel which has no junos-host gate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-31)

## Summary

A `from-zone X to-zone junos-host ... then deny` policy on a **plain interface IP** is silently unenforced for the DIRECT host-bound path. A configured management-plane DENY reaches the RE unfiltered. This is a vSRX-parity / management-plane security gap.

On vSRX, the standard layered management model is: a coarse `host-inbound-traffic system-services <svc>` port gate PLUS a fine `security policies ... to-zone junos-host` source/application restriction. Operators reasonably expect the `to-zone junos-host` policy to be enforced. Here it is not, for the primary host-bound path.

## Verified chain at HEAD (origin/master ~d70851156)

1. `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:621-632` — on a session miss, the `_` arm calls:
   - `if is_local_destination(&parsed) { return Ok(cpumap_or_pass(ctrl)); }` → delivered to the **KERNEL** (not the XSK userspace path).
2. `is_local_destination` (`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1347`) returns true for any `USERSPACE_LOCAL_V4`/`USERSPACE_LOCAL_V6` hit; it only excludes interface-NAT-to-self addresses.
3. `buildLocalAddressEntries` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:1383`) populates the local set from every configured interface IP plus all live kernel addresses, filtered ONLY by NAT exclusions — NEVER by junos-host policy.
4. The `junos_host_local_policy` call sites (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1160,2054`) are gated on `ForwardingDisposition::LocalDelivery`, which only exists on the XSK path.
5. The kernel host-inbound nft codegen in `pkg/daemon` has ZERO junos-host awareness — `grep -rin "junos.host" pkg/daemon/ bpf/` returns nothing. The kernel enforces only nft host-inbound admission (`xpf_hostinbound`) + the lo0 filter (`xpf_lo0`).

Net: the packet to a firewall-local interface IP is shunted to the kernel, which admits it on the coarse host-inbound port gate; the fine `to-zone junos-host` deny lives only in userspace-dp, which never saw the packet. Hit counters stay zero.

## Dedup

Distinct from closed #3019 (wired junos-host into the XSK `LocalDelivery` arm) and #3292 (flowless-arm bypass). This is the DIRECT-to-interface path that never reaches `LocalDelivery` at all because the shim shunts it to the kernel first. No commit since the review base touches junos-host or the local shunt.

## Fix directions (design decision — see forthcoming plan comment)

(a) **Withhold junos-host-policy'd interface IPs from `USERSPACE_LOCAL_V4/V6`** (Go-only, `maps_sync.go`): `is_local_destination` returns false → the packet falls through into the XSK session-miss redirect where the junos-host `LocalDelivery` gate ALREADY runs. Tradeoff: gives up the deliberate "local delivery always works even if the helper is down" availability property (`lib.rs:610` comment) — a junos-host-policy'd mgmt IP would depend on the helper being up.

(b) **Mirror source/app-scoped junos-host policy into the kernel nft `xpf_hostinbound`/`xpf_lo0` chains** — a new codegen path in `pkg/daemon`. Preserves kernel-delivery availability but is a large change and nft cannot express everything the userspace gate can.

(c) **Commit-time rejection + document the parity gap** — reject a `to-zone junos-host` deny stricter than the host-inbound gate that cannot be enforced, OR document it as a known vSRX-parity limitation.

The core tension: management-plane AVAILABILITY (a firewall must not lock out its own management if the helper crashes) vs the SECURITY gap (a configured deny silently unenforced).

Labels: bug, security, enforcement-gap, host-inbound, vsrx-parity

## #4147 — config lexer: an unterminated /* */ block comment silently truncates the config with zero parse errors — dropped security policies commit successfully [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

The Junos-style config lexer's block-comment scanner (`pkg/config/lexer.go:168-181`) consumes input up to a closing `*/`, but when the input reaches EOF **without** a closing `*/`, it silently swallows everything to EOF and returns **no error**. This is in contrast to `readString` (around `pkg/config/lexer.go:223`) which returns a `TokenError{"unterminated string"}` for the analogous unterminated case.

## Impact (config-integrity / fail-open)

An operator who types a single unterminated `/*` in their config — e.g. inside `security { ... }` — silently deletes an arbitrary **tail** of the config. Everything after the unclosed `/*` (potentially the `policies`/`default-policy deny-all` subtree, or other stanzas) is eaten as comment text, `Parse()` returns `errs=0`, `LoadOverride` accepts, and `commit` applies a config that is missing those policies — **with no operator signal at all**.

This is a fail-open config-loss path. A typo'd comment can drop half an operator's security policies and the commit still reports success. vSRX rejects unterminated comments at parse time.

## Trace

1. `load override` of a file where a `/*` inside `security {` is never closed.
2. Lexer eats every following byte — including `policies { default-policy { deny-all; } }` — leaving `security` an empty block.
3. `Parse()` returns `errs=0`; `LoadOverride` accepts; `commit` applies a config missing those policies.

## Fix direction

Track the comment start line/offset; if the block-comment loop exits at EOF without ever seeing `*/`, emit a `TokenError` ("unterminated block comment") so `parseStatements` records a `ParseError` and the load/commit paths reject it — matching the existing unterminated-string behavior. This makes the malformed config strict-rejected at commit (#1960-correct) instead of silently accepted with dropped stanzas.

The single-line `/* x */` case and `#` / `//` line comments are fine; only the unterminated multi-line block comment is the bug.

Source: fable-review-164 finding M-8.

## #4148 — config parser: unbounded lexer/parser recursion crashes xpfd on a sub-4MiB config load or HA config-sync (unrecoverable stack overflow) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (fable-review-164 H-2)

Severity: High. Confidence: High (empirically reproduced by the reviewer).

The Junos config lexer and recursive-descent parser have no recursion/size
bounds. A single sub-4 MiB config payload delivered to the localhost REST or
gRPC API -- **or one hostile/corrupt config from an HA peer over the fabric
config-sync channel** -- drives the goroutine stack past Go's 1 GiB
`maxstacksize`, producing a `fatal error: stack overflow`. That is an
unrecoverable `runtime.throw`, not a `panic`: there is no `recover()` in
`pkg/config` or `pkg/configstore`, so `xpfd` hard-aborts. On a cluster the
same content arriving in `SyncApply` takes down the standby.

## Evidence (verified at origin/master ~d708511566)

Lexer recurses one goroutine-stack frame per bracket -- `pkg/config/lexer.go`:

    case '[':
        l.advance()
        return l.Next()   // self-recursion, one frame per '['
    case ']':
        l.advance()
        return l.Next()

Parser mutual recursion with no depth counter -- `pkg/config/parser.go`
`parseStatements` -> `parseStatement` -> (on '{' block) `parseStatements` ->
... A `grep -ni "depth|recursion|nesting"` over `parser.go`/`lexer.go` returns
nothing.

Reachable UNGUARDED from three parse entry points:

- `pkg/configstore/store_command.go` `Store.LoadOverride` and `Store.LoadMerge`
- `pkg/configstore/store.go` `Store.SyncApply` (the HA peer config-sync ingress)

Transport forwards straight there with no size cap:

- `pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go` `Load` -- no `grpc.MaxRecvMsgSize` override on
  either `grpc.NewServer` (grpc-go default is 4 MiB).
- `pkg/api/config.go` `configLoadHandler` -- no `http.MaxBytesReader` on the
  POST body (entirely unbounded).

## #4150 — api: management HTTP server has no read/header/idle timeouts (slowloris) and REST mutation handlers have no request-body size cap (OOM) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

Two management-plane DoS hardening gaps in `pkg/api` (fable-review-164 M-6 and M-7). Both are on the 127.0.0.1:8080 HTTP server, but both become remotely reachable pre-auth once `system services web-management {http|https} interface <if>` binds a non-loopback address (a supported config; `api-auth` is opt-in).

## M-6 — HTTP/HTTPS server sets no read/header/idle timeouts (slowloris)

`NewServer` builds both `http.Server` literals with only `Addr`/`Handler`(/`TLSConfig`) and no timeout fields:

- `pkg/api/server.go:420` (`s.httpServer = &http.Server{Addr, Handler}`)
- `pkg/api/server.go:431` (`s.httpsServer = &http.Server{Addr, Handler, TLSConfig}`)

All timeout fields default to zero (no limit). Header read happens before `authMiddleware`, so a pre-auth attacker who opens N connections and dribbles request headers one byte at a time pins a goroutine/socket per connection indefinitely -> fd/goroutine exhaustion wedges the control-plane API. gosec G112/G114.

Fix: set `ReadHeaderTimeout` (~10s, the slowloris-header defense), `ReadTimeout` (~30s, slow-body defense), `IdleTimeout` (~120s), and `MaxHeaderBytes` on both servers. `WriteTimeout` must stay unlimited (0) because the SSE event/log streams (`GET /api/v1/events/stream`, `/logs/stream`) are long-lived and a full metrics/session-table scrape is a large slow response -- a WriteTimeout would sever those legit responses. The read-side timeouts are the slowloris-critical ones.

## M-7 — REST mutation handlers decode request bodies with no size cap (OOM)

Every mutating handler does `json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)` with no `http.MaxBytesReader`. E.g. `pkg/api/config.go:277` (`configLoadHandler`) -> `LoadOverride/LoadMerge/LoadSet(req.Content)`. A `POST /api/v1/config/load` with a ~1 GB JSON body allocates the whole `Content` string in the decoder, then the configstore parses it a second time -> daemon RSS spikes to OOM-kill. gRPC by contrast inherits grpc-go's 4 MiB default recv cap, so this is REST-specific.

Affected decode sites (all POST mutation handlers):
- `pkg/api/config.go` — configSet/Delete/Deactivate/Activate/Load/Rollback/CommitConfirmed/Annotate
- `pkg/api/system.go` — ping/traceroute/system-action
- `pkg/api/dhcp.go` — clearDHCPIdentifiers

Read-only GET handlers do not read a body and are out of scope.

Fix: cap each mutation body with `http.MaxBytesReader` (an independent sane ceiling, e.g. 16 MiB — orders of magnitude above any legit config payload) and return 413 on overflow instead of buffering to OOM. Pairs with H-2's parser-layer config-size ceiling but is the distinct transport-layer guard.

## Labels
security, dos, hardening, resource-exhaustion

## #4151 — cluster config-sync: generation high-water mark advances before the config is applied, silently stranding a diverged standby on apply failure [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## HA correctness: receiver-side config-sync advance-before-apply

The config-sync **generation high-water mark advances BEFORE the config
is actually applied** on the standby receiver. If the apply fails (or the
node crashes / early-returns mid-apply), the standby's recorded generation
says "I have generation N" while its ACTUAL active config is still N-1.
A subsequent sync sees the high-water == N and SKIPS re-sending, silently
STRANDING the diverged standby at the wrong config. On failover it then
serves stale policy/routing.

`pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go` — `admitConfigGen` stores the new generation,
then the config apply loop invokes the callback with no error path:

```go
func (s *SessionSync) admitConfigGen(gen uint64) bool {
    last := s.lastAppliedConfigGen.Load()
    if gen != 0 && last != 0 && gen <= last { return false }
    if gen != 0 && gen > last { s.lastAppliedConfigGen.Store(gen) } // advanced HERE
    return true
}
...
if !s.admitConfigGen(item.gen) { s.stats.ConfigsStaleIgnored.Add(1); continue }
if s.OnConfigReceived != nil { s.OnConfigReceived(item.text) }      // no error checked
```

`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go` `handleConfigSync` returns WITHOUT applying
on a transient RG0-primary belief or a `SyncApply` compile/promote failure;
`SyncApply` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go`) promotes the store only on
success.

1. Primary commits C1 (gen N+1), pushes to standby.
2. Standby `admitConfigGen(N+1)` stores `lastAppliedConfigGen=N+1`, returns true.
3. `OnConfigReceived(C1)` -> `handleConfigSync` returns early (dual-active
   window, or C1 rejected by a mixed-build ISSU syntax/compile error) ->
   store stays on C0.
4. Standby now has `lastAppliedConfigGen=N+1` but active config C0 --

## #4155 — screen: rate-based flood screens re-run on the owner node for fabric-redirected (already-screened) traffic, double-counting against the threshold [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

In a chassis cluster, the userspace dataplane re-runs the **rate-based flood
screens** (`icmp-flood`, `udp-flood`, `syn-flood`) on the RG **owner** node for
traffic that arrived via **fabric redirect** — i.e. traffic the non-owner
ingress node already screened before redirecting the raw packet across the
fabric link. The same packet is counted **twice** against the per-zone /
per-destination flood thresholds. A legitimate high-pps synced session can
false-trip the flood threshold on the owner and be **screen-dropped**, defeating
the very fabric-cross-chassis forwarding path that exists to keep those sessions
alive during failback / asymmetric-routing windows.

vSRX parity: Junos does NOT re-apply screens to fabric-forwarded traffic. The
flood screen must run **once**, on the ingress node where the packet first
entered the cluster.

## HA correctness basis

- Node B receives a packet on a normal interface for a session owned by A. B
  runs `stage_screen_check` and ticks **B's** per-zone flood counters.
- B fabric-redirects the raw packet to A.
- A receives it as fabric-ingress. Stage 9
  (`stage_classify_fabric_ingress`) sets `ingress_zone_override` and
  `FABRIC_INGRESS_FLAG` on `meta.meta_flags`; stage 10 re-runs the screen with
  the fabric zone override, **before** A's session fast-path.
- A's `icmp` / `udp` / `syn` flood counters for that zone increment on this
  already-screened, established-session packet. A high-pps flow with a flood
  threshold configured crosses it → A returns `Drop`, dropping the exact
  traffic fabric forwarding exists to protect.

## Evidence (origin/master ~426cc3f78)

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:635` — stage 9
  `stage_classify_fabric_ingress` runs, then stage 10 `stage_screen_check` with
  the fabric zone override.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_stages.rs:366` — `stage_screen_check` has **no**
  `FABRIC_INGRESS_FLAG` guard; it unconditionally calls
  `check_packet_with_zone_id` / `check_flowless_screens`.
- `userspace-dp/src/screen/mod.rs:655` `check_packet_with_zone_id` and
  `userspace-dp/src/screen/mod.rs:962` `check_flowless_screens` — the rate-based

## Summary

The cluster IP-monitoring ICMP probe that drives preferred-route WAN
failover (`services ip-monitoring`, #1827) accepts **any** ICMP echo
reply as a successful probe. The responder source address, the ICMP
identifier, and the sequence number are never validated against the
echo request that was sent.

`pkg/cluster/monitor.go` `probeICMP()` sends an echo request with a
fixed `ID: 0xbf, Seq: 1`, then performs a single `ReadFrom` and returns
`true` solely on `parsed.Type == replyType`:

    parsed, err := icmp.ParseMessage(proto, reply[:n])
    if err != nil {
        return false
    }
    return parsed.Type == replyType

The `ReadFrom` source (`_`, discarded), the parsed body's `ID`, and the
`Seq` are never compared.

## Why it matters (security / failover integrity)

A genuinely down monitored target can be reported reachable if any host
on the segment emits an echo reply — a misconfigured host, a proxy, a
stray/misdirected reply, or an off-path spoofer landing a reply inside
the 800 ms read window on the unprivileged ping socket. A false "path
up" **suppresses the redundancy-group weight demotion and the intended
WAN failover** — exactly the event ip-monitoring exists to trigger.

Real Junos `ip-monitoring` validates the responder (source == probed
target, matching identifier/sequence). xpf must do the same or it can
miss a genuine failover trigger.

constant-time, so a network-timing attacker on the interface-bound API

deliberate constant-time password path already present in the same file.

  uses `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`, so the fix is to make the key/token

by timing (compare skipped vs. compare run).

## #4161 — source-NAT: rule-set precedence is config-order first-match, not Junos most-specific-scope-wins (interface > zone > routing-instance) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (fable-review-164 M-3, vSRX-parity / NAT-correctness)

Source-NAT rule-set precedence in xpf is **config-order first-match**, not
Junos **most-specific-scope-wins**. Junos selects among overlapping
source-NAT rule-sets by the specificity of the match context —
**interface > zone > routing-instance** (interface most specific) — and only
then applies within-set rule order. xpf flattens all rule-sets into one Vec
in config order and returns the first rule whose scope matches, so a
broader-scope rule-set defined earlier in the config wins over a
more-specific rule-set defined later. A config that is correct on vSRX can
produce a different SNAT decision here purely from text ordering, including
bypass of a more-specific `then source-nat off` exemption.

SNAT is pure first-match, scope-blind to specificity:

- userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs:828 — `match_source_nat_result_for_tuple`
  iterates `for rule in rules { if !rule.matches(..) { continue; } .. return
  SourceNatLookup::Matched(..); }`. The first matching rule in slice order
  wins and returns immediately (including the `off` short-circuit).
- userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs:308 — `scope_matches` treats empty scope
  fields as wildcards and AND-s the present ones. It is an eligibility
  filter only; it does NOT rank a rule by how specific its scope is.
- pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat.go:141 — `buildSourceNATSnapshotsWithFeeds`
  emits rule-sets in config order (`for _, rs := range
  cfg.Security.NAT.Source`) then rules in config order, with NO precedence
  sort.

The full scope IS carried to the dataplane already — nat.go:247-252 stamps
all six scope fields (FromZone, ToZone, FromInterface, ToInterface,
FromRoutingInstance, ToRoutingInstance) onto every SourceNATRuleSnapshot, and
the Rust SourceNatRule reads them in scope_matches. So no new wire/plumbing is
needed to know each rule's scope; only the SELECTION among matches is wrong.

The finding notes DNAT/static "tier by specificity." Verified — but the axis

## #4162 — observability: /metrics bypasses auth and walks the entire v4+v6 session table on every scrape (unauth DoS + hot-path contention) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-15)

Source: fable-review-164 finding L-5 (Low severity, High confidence). Security + DoS angle. Verified at origin/master ~e35f6a421.

## Claim
The Prometheus /metrics endpoint (1) BYPASSES auth (no API-key/Bearer/Basic required), AND (2) does an O(sessions) walk of the shared conntrack table (v4 + v6) on EVERY scrape, with no cache/TTL/throttle and no scrape timeout or concurrency limit. A high-frequency (or unauthenticated remote) scrape amplifies an O(N) scan over the box's largest hot structure, competing with the Rust helper's concurrent conntrack writes.

## Verified current behavior (file:line)

Auth bypass
- pkg/api/auth.go:17-24 — authMiddleware short-circuits BEFORE any credential check for /health and /metrics: `if r.URL.Path == "/health" || r.URL.Path == "/metrics" { next.ServeHTTP(...); return }`. Every other path requires Basic/Bearer/X-API-Key.
- pkg/api/server.go:210 — `mux.Handle("GET /metrics", promhttp.HandlerFor(registry, promhttp.HandlerOpts{}))` with EMPTY HandlerOpts: no Timeout, no MaxRequestsInFlight. authMiddleware wraps the whole mux (server.go:306) but exempts /metrics.

Full-table walk, fresh every scrape (no cache)
- pkg/api/metrics_sessions.go:52-63 — collectSessionGauges calls `dp.IterateSessions(...)` + `dp.IterateSessionsV6(...)` and tallies active/established/ipv4/ipv6/snat/dnat.
- pkg/api/metrics.go:960 — Collect() calls collectSessionGauges on every scrape (after the dataplane-loaded gate at 941-942). There is NO TTL/cache/throttle; each scrape re-walks the whole table.
- pkg/dataplane/maps_session.go:43,105 — IterateSessions/V6 iterate the shared kernel `sessions`/`sessions_v6` BPF HASH maps via cilium/ebpf Iterate() = BPF_MAP_GET_NEXT_KEY + LOOKUP per entry (2 syscalls/entry, each taking the map bucket lock), concurrent with the helper's publish_bpf_conntrack_entry writes.

Scale (the DoS ceiling)
- bpf/headers/xpf_common.h:147 — MAX_SESSIONS 10000000 (10M).
- pkg/dataplane/loader_userspace_shim.go:305 — userspaceShimMaxSessions uint32 = 10000000. The `sessions`/`sessions_v6` maps are sized at 10M. BPF hash iteration walks POPULATED entries (up to ~10M forward+reverse under load). Every unauth scrape can force up to a 10M-entry, ~20M-syscall walk.

Bind posture
- cmd/xpfd/main.go:221 — default --api-addr 127.0.0.1:8080 (loopback; lower risk).
- pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1254-1259 — when `system services web-management http interface <if>` is configured, apiCfg.Addr = resolveInterfaceAddr(wm.HTTPInterface) + ":8080" — the HTTP API (serving unauth /metrics) binds a ROUTABLE management interface. In that config /metrics is remotely reachable UNAUTHENTICATED.

Key nature of the export
- collectSessionGauges emits ONLY 7 scalar aggregates (xpf_sessions_active/established/ipv4/ipv6/snat/dnat + xpf_sessions_breakdown_scrape_ok) — NO per-session cardinality. The O(N) walk yields O(1) output, so the aggregate is cacheable without losing any label.
- #333: the GC sweep is SKIPPED on the userspace dataplane (GC.SkipSweep), so there is NO existing Go-side periodic walk to piggyback on. #3929 deliberately moved these gauges to read the LIVE table (gc.Stats() was permanently 0). The helper's 1/s status poll carries session ERROR counters (status.rs:127-181) but NOT an active-session count/breakdown — so the aggregate genuinely requires a table walk.

## Why it matters
Unauthenticated (when web-management binds non-loopback) or high-frequency remote amplification of an O(N) scan over the box's largest hot structure — up to ~10M entries, ~20M syscalls per scrape — with no rate limit, competing with the forwarding/conntrack-publish path. Loopback-only default lowers exposure but does not remove the amplification (a local scraper in a tight loop still amplifies).

## Fix direction (two sub-issues)

(B) Full-table-walk — the real DoS. Add a short-TTL cache around the session-gauge walk: cache the 7 aggregates with a small TTL (e.g. 2-5s); a scrape serves the cached snapshot when fresh, else does one walk and refreshes. This decouples walk rate from scrape rate (at most one walk per TTL regardless of scrape frequency) and defeats the amplification. (Cannot piggyback the GC sweep — skipped on userspace per #333 — so a self-contained TTL cache in the collector/server, or a dedicated periodic refresh tick, is the right shape.) Also set promhttp.HandlerOpts{Timeout, MaxRequestsInFlight} at server.go:210 to bound concurrent/slow scrapes.

(A) Auth posture. Loopback (127.0.0.1) default is the standard Prometheus posture and is acceptable — document it. When bound non-loopback via web-management, gate /metrics behind auth (or add an explicit toggle). Lower priority than the cache; the TTL cache is the DoS fix regardless of auth.

Scope: Go-only, pkg/api (+ optionally pkg/daemon for the auth toggle). Design plan to follow in a comment.

## #4163 — dhcp-relay: server replies forwarded to clients without validating the source against the configured server set (rogue-reply injection) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (fable-review-164 L-12; security / DHCP relay hardening)

The DHCPv4 relay forwards server replies (OFFER/ACK/NAK/FORCERENEW) back to
clients based on packet contents alone. It does NOT validate that the reply's
source IP is one of the configured DHCP servers. An off-path attacker (or a
compromised transit host) that can route a UDP datagram to giaddr:67 can inject
a forged OFFER/ACK and have the relay deliver it to the client, or a forged NAK
to force a client restart -- classic rogue-DHCP / lease-hijack (wrong gateway,
wrong DNS -> MITM).

## Verified behavior (origin/master e0ac8e54c)

pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go:

- handleServerResponses (~1171-1234): the reply loop does
  `n, srcAddr, err := serverConn.ReadFrom(buf)`. srcAddr is used ONLY in a
  slog.Debug ("server", srcAddr) line -- it is never compared to anything.
- The server-facing socket is created via ListenPacket("udp4", giaddr:67)
  (defaultPacketConnFactory, ~line 366) and is bound, NEVER connect()/Dial-ed,
  so it accepts datagrams from ANY source that can reach giaddr:67.
- The configured server set `servers []*net.UDPAddr` IS available in
  runRelaySession (it is a parameter), but the call at ~line 1016 is
  `handleServerResponses(sctx, serverConn, conn, ir, l2, giaddr)` -- the server
  set is NOT passed in, so the reply path cannot filter on it.
- What IS checked before forwarding: OpCode == BootReply, and MessageType in
  {Offer, Ack, Nak, ForceRenew}. There is NO xid/outstanding-request table, NO
  giaddr validation (pkt.GatewayIPAddr is unconditionally zeroed, not checked
  == the session giaddr), and Option 82 is stripped (stripOption82) but never
  correlated/echo-checked.
- Scope: DHCPv4 relay only. There is no DHCPv6 relay (README mention only), so
  the fix is v4-only.

Not already fixed -- no source validation exists on the reply path.

## RFC / vSRX basis

RFC 3046 relay practice and standard vendor relays forward replies only from
the configured server set (a relay always has an explicit, small server list).
Not filtering widens the trust boundary to anything that can route to
giaddr:67.

## #4167 — screen: IPv4 L3-header extraction fails OPEN on a too-short header while IPv6 fails closed (malformed-packet screen bypass) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

The screen field extractor `extract_screen_info` (`userspace-dp/src/screen/extract.rs`) is **asymmetric** between IPv4 and IPv6 when the captured L3 header is too short to parse:

- **IPv6 fails CLOSED**: `extract.rs` returns `Err(ScreenParseError::TruncatedIpv6ExtChain)` when `l3_offset + 40 > frame.len()` (base header short) or any extension-header walk runs past the captured frame. The caller (`afxdp/poll_stages.rs`) treats every `Err` as a screen-drop (`err.screen_reason()` -> `ip-malformed`). This is the #2146/#2189/#2361 fail-closed contract.
- **IPv4 fails OPEN**: the IPv4 arm is gated by `addr_family == AF_INET && l3_offset + 20 <= frame.len()`. When the frame is too short (`l3_offset + 20 > frame.len()`), NEITHER the IPv4 nor the IPv6 branch is entered, and the function falls through to `Ok(info)` with defaults (`is_fragment=false`, `ip_ihl=5`, `saw_ipv4_source_route=false`). With those defaults `check_ping_of_death` / `check_teardrop` / `check_icmp_fragment` / `check_source_route` all early-return, so a truncated IPv4 header **passes unscreened**.

There is a second, subtler fail-open: when the IPv4 IHL field claims a header longer than the captured bytes (`l3_offset + ihl*4 > frame.len()`), the source-route option scan is skipped (guarded by `l3_offset + ihl_bytes <= frame.len()`), so `check_source_route` cannot detect an LSRR/SSRR it was unable to read.

## File:line

- IPv4 fail-open: `userspace-dp/src/screen/extract.rs` — the `if addr_family == AF_INET && l3_offset + 20 <= frame.len()` gate; the too-short case falls through to the terminal `Ok(info)`.
- IPv6 fail-closed reference: `userspace-dp/src/screen/extract.rs` — `if l3_offset + 40 > frame.len() { return Err(ScreenParseError::TruncatedIpv6ExtChain); }` and the top-of-loop `if offset > frame.len()` guard.

## Why it matters

Security / defense-in-depth: a malformed or truncated IPv4 packet bypasses the fragment/source-route/ICMP screens, while the equivalent IPv6 truncation is dropped. The two families should be symmetric. Reachability is low-confidence (a padded Ethernet frame >= 60B always carries a full 20-byte IPv4 header, so this needs a runt/malformed capture), hence low severity — but the asymmetry is a real fail-open vs the IPv6 fail-closed contract.

## Fix

Make the IPv4 too-short-header path FAIL CLOSED, mirroring the IPv6 arm exactly:

- When `addr_family == AF_INET && l3_offset + 20 > frame.len()`, return an `Err` (a new `ScreenParseError` variant mapped to the same `ip-malformed` reason as IPv6) so the caller fail-closes (drop).
- When the packet's own IHL claims `l3_offset + ihl*4 > frame.len()`, also return `Err` (the options region / source route cannot be parsed).

Do NOT over-drop a legit minimal 20-byte IPv4 header (IHL=5, no options) — that is valid and must pass.

## Dedup

#2146/#2189/#2361 hardened the IPv6 walk; no prior item covers the IPv4 short-header symmetric case.

Source: fable-review-164 finding L-11.

Junos SRX/vSRX screen profiles support an **`alarm-without-drop`** ids-option:
when set at the screen-profile (ids-option) level, a tripped screen check
still **alarms** (logs the attack event and increments the screen counter) but
**does NOT drop** the packet — it forwards. This is the standard vSRX
audit/monitoring mode operators use to tune screen thresholds against live
traffic without impacting forwarding.

Per Junos, `alarm-without-drop` is a **screen-profile-level** flag (applies to
ALL ids-options in that screen profile): every check in the profile that would
otherwise drop instead logs + counts and passes the packet.

    }

`profile.UnknownLeaves` and is fail-closed rejected at commit by

## #4171 — libvirt deploy: an HA pair attaches the SAME writable golden qcow2 to both VMs — concurrent writes corrupt the image [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

The libvirt deploy path in scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py boots VMs DIRECTLY off
the shared golden qcow2, attaching it as a WRITABLE disk. For an HA pair this
means BOTH VMs attach the SAME writable image file, and a single deploy still
mutates the golden master.

## Data-corruption basis

qcow2 is not a cluster filesystem. Two running VMs writing the same qcow2 file
corrupt it (concurrent writes to overlapping metadata/refcount blocks). The
incus backend avoids this by cloning from the image store (incus init copies
into a per-instance root disk); the libvirt backend has no per-VM clone.

Even the SINGLE-VM case is broken: --import boots and mutates the golden, so
day-0 stamps (/etc/xpf/.day0-config-applied), host keys, and the configstore DB
get baked into the master. The NEXT VM launched "from the image" comes up
pre-configured with the previous VM's identity and silently skips its own
config drive.

## Location

scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py, deploy_libvirt() (line 358):

    argv = ["virt-install", "--name", name, ..., "--import",
            "--disk", f"path=/var/lib/libvirt/images/{ap['image']}.qcow2",

The disk path is hardcoded to the golden qcow2 with no per-VM clone (line 364).
Every YAML defaults image: xpf-appliance, so
"deploy --hypervisor libvirt ha-fw0.yaml ha-fw1.yaml" attaches the same
writable file to both domains.

## Impact

- HA pair: two live VMs on one qcow2 -> filesystem/image corruption.
- Single deploy: poisons the golden master; second deploy inherits stale
  identity + skips its own config.
- libvirt is advertised as first-class in examples/deploy/README.md
  ("Both run the same qcow2"), so the very first documented libvirt deploy
  corrupts the golden image.

## #4175 — day-0 config-drive: retry is permanently dead — loader guards on bare .configdb directory existence, which xpfd creates on every start before any commit [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

The day-0 config-drive loader (`scripts/image/xpf-day0-config`) guards on
**bare directory existence** of `.configdb`, but xpfd durably creates that
directory on *every* start before any commit. After the very first boot the
empty `.configdb` dir exists, so the loader logs "system already configured"
and never re-probes the medium again — permanently defeating its own
documented reject -> fix -> reboot retry contract.

## Root cause

The loader's "already configured" short-circuit:

    # scripts/image/xpf-day0-config:194-196
    if [ -e "$XPF_DIR/.configdb" ]; then
        log "configstore DB exists — system already configured, skipping day-0 probe"
        return 0

But the DB directory is created unconditionally on every daemon start,
before any commit:

    // pkg/configstore/db.go:48 (NewDB)
    if err := fsatomic.MkdirAllDurable(dir, 0700); err != nil { ... }

`NewDB` <- `configstore.New` (pkg/configstore/store.go:196-197)
<- `daemon.New` (pkg/daemon/daemon.go:709-714), unconditionally, before any
config is committed.

The retry contract the guard is supposed to honor:

    # scripts/image/xpf-day0-config:35-38
    # a medium that fails validation does NOT write the stamp, so the operator
    # can fix the config and reboot — the system is still unconfigured

## Trace (retry death)

1. First boot with a config drive whose config has a typo. Loader correctly
   REJECTS the medium, does not stamp (retriable by design).
2. Boot proceeds; xpfd starts factory bootstrap; `daemon.New` ->
   `configstore.New` -> `NewDB` durably creates `/etc/xpf/.configdb`.

## #4178 — interface naming: positional rename loop corrupts the .link OriginalName= chain on an enumeration shift (no collision discipline, unlike device-map mode) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

The positional startup rename loop, enumerateAndRenameInterfaces in
pkg/daemon/linksetup.go:82-106, writes and overwrites .link files
mid-loop and re-reads them via recoverOriginalName within the SAME pass.
It has no collision discipline. On an enumeration shift (a NIC
added/removed/reordered changes the positional index to name mapping),
the loop can write a stale or wrong OriginalName= into a .link file and
strand renames on EEXIST. The device-map path already solved this with a
collision-safe multi-pass rename (device_map.go:166-221); positional
mode never inherited it.

## Mechanism

The single-pass loop, per enumeration index:

  1. target = assignName(idx, ...)
  2. original = recoverOriginalName(nic.name)   -- reads .link files,
     INCLUDING ones this same loop already overwrote in earlier
     iterations (linksetup.go:242-273)
  3. writeLinkFile(target, original)            -- OVERWRITES the .link
     for target before later iterations recover from it
  4. renameInterface(nic.name, target)          -- an EEXIST (target
     still held by a not-yet-renamed NIC) is warn-and-continue, no
     collision break

Two defects compound:

- recoverOriginalName in iteration N reads .link files that iterations
  0..N-1 already rewrote, so a shifted enumeration feeds a corrupted
  OriginalName into later iterations.
- renameInterface EEXIST is warn-and-continue; there is no phase-1
  temp-rename to free a target name that a later-enumerated NIC still
  holds.

## Trace

Prior boot: NIC A -> fxp0, NIC B -> ge-0-0-0. Add NIC C at a lower PCI
bus. Reboot. udev applies the .link files first (A -> fxp0, B ->
ge-0-0-0); C keeps its kernel name. xpfd enumerates in bus order:

## #4179 — HA naming: a node with node-id but no config takes all NICs with standalone names and never re-runs naming when the cluster config arrives [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

An HA node that boots with /etc/xpf/node-id present but NO committed
config (and no importable xpf.conf) takes the EMPTY-config takeover
branch. That branch derives clusterMode/nodeID from the nil active
config, so clusterMode stays false and the NICs are named STANDALONE
(fxp0, ge-0-0-X) instead of the cluster layout (fxp0, em0,
ge-{fpc}-0-X). Startup naming then never re-runs when the cluster config
finally arrives via config-sync, so the interfaces keep the wrong
standalone names until a daemon restart -- which the operator is never
told about.

## Mechanism

- computeBootClass returns bootClassNormal for a node-id-present box with
  a nil active config (the HA-node guard, pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:246-248),
  so the daemon is NOT in bootstrap mode.
- The HA-guard branch (pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:301-310) logs a loud
  error and proceeds with EMPTY-config takeover.
- Startup naming (daemon_run.go:337-341, 385) reads clusterMode/nodeID
  from d.store.ActiveConfig(), which is nil here, so clusterMode=false,
  nodeID=0 -> STANDALONE naming.
- Startup naming has exactly two call sites: normal boot (daemon_run.go:
  385) and bootstrap-exit (daemon_run.go:1845, gated on inBootstrap()).
  This path is NOT bootstrap, so the bootstrap-exit re-naming never
  fires. Nothing re-runs naming when the cluster config arrives via
  applyConfigLocked (SyncApply from the primary).

## Trace

A fresh replacement node 1 boots with /etc/xpf/node-id=1, no DB, no
xpf.conf:

- All NICs named standalone (fxp0, ge-0-0-0, ge-0-0-1, ...).
- The cluster config syncs from the primary and commits.
- The config references em0 and ge-7-0-* (node 1 uses FPC 7) which do
  not exist on this node.
- VRRP / fabric / heartbeat bind to missing interfaces and fail.
- The node stays wrong until an xpfd restart -- and the loud boot error
  never mentions that a restart is what recovers it.

## #4180 — libvirt deploy: role validation ignores the guest virtio-first PCI tiebreaker — a virtio NIC after a hardware NIC silently swaps firewall zones [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (fable-review-165 H-22)

`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` `validate_appliance()` checks each
interface's declared `role` against its **list index only**
(`expected_name(i, ...)` at `scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:179-188`),
but the guest does NOT name interfaces by attach/list order. The guest
sorts NICs **virtio-class before hardware-class** before assigning
positional vSRX names — `enumeratePCINICs()` sets `sk = 0` for
`virtio_net` and `sk = 1` for hardware, then sorts on that key
(`pkg/daemon/linksetup.go:189-204`).

So a deploy YAML that lists a **virtio-class** NIC (`net`/`bridge`/
`macvlan`) AFTER a **hardware-class** NIC (`sriov`/`physical`/`pci`)
passes validation but boots with the firewall zones on **swapped
ports** — a silent security miswiring (trust/untrust inverted).

## Trace

Operator customizes an example:

- pos1 `fxp0`, backing `bridge` (virtio)
- pos2 `ge-0/0/0`, backing `pci` VF (hardware)
- pos3 `ge-0/0/1`, backing `bridge` (virtio)

`validate_appliance` walks the list in order: pos2 role `ge-0/0/0`
matches `expected_name(1)`, pos3 role `ge-0/0/1` matches
`expected_name(2)` — validation PASSES.

In the guest, both virtio NICs sort first (`sk=0`): the pos-3 bridge
becomes `ge-0/0/0` (LAN/trust) and the pos-2 VF becomes `ge-0/0/1`
(WAN/untrust). Zones, policies and NAT written against those vSRX
names land on the wrong physical ports. Nothing errors.

All six shipped example YAMLs happen to list virtio first, so the
hazard is latent, not active, in the shipped files — but the deployer
holds every interface's backing class and can detect it.

## Severity

High — silent security miswiring (a swapped zone inverts trust/untrust).

## #4184 — Bootstrap/day-0 import failure is journald-only: no /health field, no event surface [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

### Summary (fable-review-165 H-11)

A bootstrap/day-0 config import FAILURE is visible only as a single
`slog.Warn` in journald. There is no `/health` field, no event, and no
`show` surface -- so "why didn't my config apply", the number-one day-0
support question, has no in-band answer.

### Basis / evidence

- Import failure is a lone WARN: `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:265-268`
  (`slog.Warn("failed to bootstrap config from file", ...)`).
- No bootstrap surface anywhere else:

  returns no operator-facing hit.
- Precedent exists: `/health` already carries CompileHealth
  (`pkg/api/health.go:19-33`) and config-persist-degraded (`:35-42`).

Preseeded `xpf.conf` fails to parse -> one WARN in journald -> box in
bootstrap. Operator SSHes in (fxp0 lifeline works), sees an empty
`show configuration`, nothing in `/health`; the first in-band hint is
the commit-time bootstrap-gate refusal.

Record the bootstrap cause at boot (`no-config` / `import-failed:<err>`
/ `ok`) and surface it beyond journald: a `/health` field
(`bootstrap_import_status` + error detail) plus an event. Minimal:
health field + event; do not force a 503 for the expected factory

## #4185 — Dual node identity (/etc/xpf/node-id file vs chassis cluster node leaf) never cross-checked; file parser laxer than every other consumer [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

### Summary (fable-review-165 H-12)

The node-id FILE (`/etc/xpf/node-id`) drives `${node}` apply-group
expansion + boot class; the `chassis cluster node` LEAF drives FPC
naming + heartbeat identity. Nothing rejects a mismatch, and the
daemon's file parser (`fmt.Sscanf("%d")`) is laxer than every other
node-id consumer -- it accepts `1garbage` / any integer while
check-config and the loader enforce `0|1`.

### Basis / evidence

- File parse (lax): `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:728-735`
  (`fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d", &nodeID)`).
- Config leaf compile: `pkg/config/compiler_system.go:1205-1211`
  (`strconv.Atoi` into `ch.Cluster.NodeID`).
- Strict consumers for comparison: `cmd/xpfd/main.go:167-170`
  (`-node-id must be 0, 1, or -1`); the day-0 config contract.
- `${node}` node-0 fallback when store stays nodeID=-1:
  `pkg/configstore/store.go` schemaValidateExpandedTreeForNode.

### Trace (day-0 shape)

Day-0 medium carries node-id=1 + a config whose expanded text says
`chassis cluster node 0` (literal, copied from node 0) -> check-config
-node-id 1 passes -> boot: `${node}` groups expand as node 1 while FPC
naming and heartbeat identify as node 0 -> two half-identities, node 0's
per-node IPs duplicated on the wire, no diagnostic anywhere.

### Fix direction

Single SSOT: at compile/commit-check, when the store nodeID >= 0 and the
`chassis cluster node` leaf is present, REJECT on mismatch. Harden the
daemon's file parser to the same trimmed-`Atoi` + `0|1` contract, and
log loudly on an unparseable file instead of silently going
half-standalone.
