    } else { ... };
    let dst_ok = if rule.destination_excluded {
        !(rule.destination_v4_empty && rule.destination_v6_empty)
            && !(rule.destination_literal_v4.contains(dst) || ...books v4...)
    } else { ... };

The behavior is CORRECT today (verified in triage). But the existing
NAT64 tests (userspace-dp/src/policy_tests.rs, the `#2358` block) only
exercise the NON-excluded match / source-any / wrong-host / wrong-v6-src
paths plus the reverse (V4 src, V6 dst) fail-closed. A grep of
`*_excluded` against the NAT64 fixtures returns nothing: the exclusion
inversion and the empty-set fail-closed guard on THIS arm have zero
coverage.

### Why it matters

This arm mixes families and duplicates the exclusion logic from the
same-family arms. A future edit that swaps a field (e.g. reads
`source_literal_v4` instead of `_v6`, or drops the empty-set guard)
would silently make a NAT64 `deny destination-address-excluded <host>`
fail OPEN, and no test would fail. The userspace helper is the sole
enforcement plane.

### Tests to add (test-only; no production change)

In the `#2358` NAT64 block of `policy_tests.rs`, add tests for the
untested (V6 src, V4 dst) exclusion/fail-closed paths:

## #4188 — xpf-deploy libvirt: physical backing passes a netdev name to virt-install --hostdev (invalid spec) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary
`deploy --hypervisor libvirt` with a `physical` backing passes the raw
netdev NAME (e.g. `enp8s0`) straight to `virt-install --hostdev`, but
`--hostdev` requires a PCI (or USB) address / node-device name, not an
interface name. The documented `physical` backing is therefore dead on
libvirt: the domain fails to define or mis-attaches. (fable-review-165 H-23)

## Basis / file:line
- `scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:463-464` (`deploy_libvirt`):
  ```
  elif b == "physical":
      argv += ["--hostdev", src]   # src is a NETDEV name here
  ```
  For `pci` backing (`:465-474`) `src` is already a PCI address, so
  `--hostdev src` is correct there. For `physical`, `src` is a host
  interface name (the incus backend at `:375-376` uses it as
  `nictype=physical parent=<netdev>`, which incus resolves internally).
- `examples/deploy/README.md` backing table advertises `physical` ->
  `--hostdev` on libvirt.
- Per H-21, the swallowed error means this fails silently.

## Fix direction
In `deploy_libvirt`, resolve the netdev name to its PCI BDF with the
existing `pci_of()` helper before passing it to `--hostdev` (accept a
raw PCI address too). Mirror the incus behaviour (incus takes the netdev
name directly; only libvirt needs the PCI translation). Die with a clear
message if the netdev cannot be resolved on the host.

## Labels
bug, libvirt, deployer

## #4189 — xpf-deploy fetch: anti-rollback watermark mis-orders git-describe counts and rc numbers (string compare) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary
The `fetch` anti-rollback watermark compares pre-release / git-describe
suffixes as whole strings, so `1.2.3-10-gabc` ranks OLDER than
`1.2.3-9-gdef` and `rc10` ranks below `rc9`. A valid upgrade is refused
as a "possible stale mirror / rollback", training operators to habitually
pass `--allow-rollback` (which then also lets a real downgrade through).
Reproduced by execution. (fable-review-165 H-25)

## Basis / file:line
- `scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:561-579` (`_ver_key` inside `cmd_fetch`):
  the release part is numeric-split correctly, but the suffix is compared
  as a bare string:
  ```
  elif suffix[:1].isdigit():
      pre_rank = (2, suffix)    # "10-gabc" < "9-gdef" lexically
  else:
      pre_rank = (0, suffix)    # "rc10"   < "rc9"    lexically
  ```
- Reproduction: `_ver_key("1.2.3-10-gabc") < _ver_key("1.2.3-9-gdef")`
  returns True; `_ver_key("1.2.3-rc10") < _ver_key("1.2.3-rc9")` returns
  True. Both are wrong.

## Fix direction
Numeric-split the suffix (`re.split(r'(\d+)', suffix)` with int coercion,
int/str-tagged so a mixed compare can't raise) while KEEPING the
rc < release < post-release category rank. Add a unit test asserting the
correct ordering (rc10 > rc9, describe-count 10 > 9). No canonical Go
git-describe ordering exists to mirror (the watermark is Python-only
best-effort CLI state).

## Labels
bug, distribution, deployer

## #4194 — docs/bare-metal-device-map.md: quick-start step 3 says `commit check` confirms a `commit confirmed` — it does not (rolls back the verified config) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Finding (fable-review-165 H-18)

`docs/bare-metal-device-map.md` step 3 of the device-map quick-start
(around line 58-64) tells the operator:

```
commit confirmed 5
... verify reachability + forwarding ...
commit check        # or just `commit` to confirm
```

`commit check` does **not** confirm a pending `commit confirmed`. It is
validation-only and never touches the confirm timer. An operator who
follows the doc literally — runs `commit check`, sees "configuration
check succeeds", and walks away — leaves the confirm timer running; at
T+5m the daemon auto-rolls-back the verified device-map. On bare metal
that reverts the NIC naming that was just proven reachable.

## Basis (code)

- `pkg/configstore/store_commit.go:26-41` — `CommitCheck()` compiles the
  candidate and returns; it does not clear or touch any pending
  commit-confirmed timer.
- `pkg/configstore/store_commit.go:106-120` — a **plain `commit`** during
  a pending commit-confirmed window IS the confirmation
  (`clearPendingConfirmLocked()` cancels the timer). Junos semantics: any
  subsequent explicit `commit` confirms a pending `commit confirmed`.

So the confirming command is `commit` (not `commit check`).

## Fix (doc)

Replace the misleading `commit check` line with the correct confirming
command (`commit`), and warn that `commit check` alone lets the confirm
timer expire → auto-rollback.

- File: `docs/bare-metal-device-map.md` (quick-start step 3, ~line 63)

## Labels
documentation, bare-metal, day-0

## #4195 — docs/deploy-quickstart.md: standalone 'two commands' fails on a fresh host — bridge prerequisites (and their DHCP form) are documented only for HA [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Finding (fable-review-165 H-28)

`docs/deploy-quickstart.md` "Standalone in two commands" tells the
operator to run:

```
scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py deploy examples/deploy/standalone.yaml
```

but `examples/deploy/standalone.yaml` sources three bridges —
`br-mgmt`, `br-lan`, `br-wan`. The only `incus network create` block in
the doc is in the **HA pair** section (~line 100-104). A fresh-host
operator following the standalone path has no instruction to create
those bridges, so the deploy fails (unknown source network).

Even after hand-creating them, a bare bridge provides **no DHCP**:
`standalone.conf` puts `fxp0` (mgmt) and `ge-0/0/1` (WAN) on `dhcp`, so
without a NAT/DHCP-bearing `br-mgmt`/`br-wan` the "working NAT firewall"
comes up with no management or WAN address and cannot reach the
internet.

## Basis

- `docs/deploy-quickstart.md` standalone section (~line 55-78) has no
  bridge-create block; the HA section (~line 98-105) does.
- `examples/deploy/standalone.yaml` — `source: br-mgmt / br-lan / br-wan`.
- `examples/deploy/standalone.conf` — `fxp0` dhcp, `ge-0/0/1` dhcp,
  `ge-0/0/0` static 192.168.1.1/24 + dhcp-local-server.

## Fix (doc)

Add a copy-pasteable `incus network create` block to the **standalone**
section, mirroring the HA block, with `br-mgmt` and `br-wan`
NAT/DHCP-bearing (so mgmt + WAN get addresses and reach the internet)
and `br-lan` a plain L2 segment (ge-0/0/0 is the static LAN gateway that
runs the DHCP server itself).

## #4196 — examples/deploy: standalone.conf/ha-pair.conf ship no root-authentication — SSH enabled but unusable, and vSRX would refuse to commit [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Finding (fable-review-165 H-29)

`examples/deploy/standalone.conf` and `examples/deploy/ha-pair.conf`
enable `ssh` in the mgmt/lan host-inbound-traffic, but carry **no**
`system root-authentication` and no `system login user`. Consequences:

- The baked image's factory sshd posture is `PermitRootLogin
  prohibit-password` (pubkey-only) — `scripts/image/bake.py`
  `SSHD_DROPIN`. With no root ssh key in the config, `ssh root@fxp0` has
  no credential to authenticate against → operator is locked out of SSH,
  and nothing in the config or deploy docs says how to log in.
- **vSRX parity:** a real vSRX refuses to `commit` without
  `root-authentication`. xpf's commit gate accepts a credential-less
  config silently, so the example diverges from Junos and ships an
  unusable management plane.

## Basis

- `scripts/image/bake.py` (~line 100-104) — `SSHD_DROPIN` factory
  posture is pubkey-only for root.
- `examples/deploy/standalone.conf`, `examples/deploy/ha-pair.conf` — no
  `root-authentication` / `login` stanza (grep).
- Schema supports both: `pkg/config/schema_system.go:58-67`
  (`root-authentication` → `encrypted-password` [ValidateCryptHash],
  `ssh-ed25519`/`ssh-rsa`/`ssh-dsa`); #1944.
- Under `prohibit-password`, an ssh **key** (not a password) is what
  makes `ssh root@fxp0` work; `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1228-1248`
  installs `root-authentication ssh-*` keys into root's authorized_keys.

## Fix (examples)

Add an active `system root-authentication` stanza with an `ssh-ed25519`
**placeholder** key (obvious REPLACE-ME text — parses + commits but
authenticates no one, so it fails closed if deployed unmodified) plus a
loud comment to replace it with the operator's real pubkey (and noting
the `encrypted-password` alternative + the vSRX-refuses-without-it parity
point). This makes the examples usable-once-edited and gives Junos
parity, without shipping any real/weak credential.

- Files: `examples/deploy/standalone.conf`, `examples/deploy/ha-pair.conf`

## #4197 — install.sh Tier-A one-liner cannot succeed: no publish-time bake for XPF_APT_BASE_URL (fable-165 H-2) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## H-2 (fable-review-165)

The documented Tier-A one-liner install is structurally incapable of a
one-command install.

### Basis
`docs/distribution.md:124-126` documents:

    curl -fsSL https://dl.example.com/xpf/install.sh | sh

But `scripts/dist/install.sh:130-132` (write_source) hard-dies:

    [ -n "${XPF_APT_BASE_URL:-}" ] || die "XPF_APT_BASE_URL is required ..."

There is NO publish-time substitution point for the apt base URL anywhere
in install.sh. The release build is said to substitute the archive KEY
(install.sh:26-30, gated by publish.py:196-200) but nothing bakes the apt
base URL or the default channel.

Consequences:
1. A piped `XPF_APT_BASE_URL=... curl ... | sh` binds the env to `curl`,
   not to the `sh` on the right of the pipe -> write_source dies.
2. The doc one-liner also omits sudo, so a non-root run dies at the root
   check (install.sh:181) first.
3. install.sh dies AFTER mutating the host (keyring already written), see
   H-16.

selftest.sh:225 masks the gap by setting XPF_APT_BASE_URL explicitly.

### Fix
- Seed XPF_APT_BASE_URL (+ default channel) from a publish-time
  substitution marker in install.sh (e.g. %%XPF_APT_BASE_URL%% /
  %%XPF_CHANNEL%%), env override wins, write_source die kept only as a
  last-resort fail-safe when neither marker nor env is present.
- Add a publish.py gate mirroring the placeholder-KEY refusal that dies
  if install.sh still carries an unsubstituted %%XPF_APT_BASE_URL%%.
- Fix the doc one-liner to `curl -fsSL <url>/install.sh | sudo sh` and
  note the URL is baked at publish time.

## #4198 — Publisher runbook dead-ends: no tooling substitutes the real archive key into install.sh; gate treats install.sh as optional (fable-165 H-14) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## H-14 (fable-review-165)

Following the publisher runbook verbatim produces an installer that
publish.py refuses (or no installer at all, which the gate lets pass).

### Basis
- No key-substitution tooling exists anywhere in scripts/ or the Makefile.
  `docs/distribution.md:71-74` step 4 signs the PLACEHOLDER install.sh:

      minisign -S -s /secure/xpf-image.sec -m scripts/dist/install.sh ...
      cp scripts/dist/install.sh dist/install.sh

- publish.py:194-200 refuses an install.sh that still embeds
  PLACEHOLDER-xpf-archive-keyring -> the runbook's own artifact fails the
  gate.
- publish.py:195 gates install.sh only `if os.path.isfile(installsh)` --
  ship no install.sh and the gate passes, then the Tier-A URL 404s.

Net: the release engineer either signs a placeholder (gate dies) or ships
nothing (Tier-A 404). There is no substitute-then-sign path.

### Fix
- Add tooling (publish.py stamp step) that SUBSTITUTES the real archive
  key + apt base URL + default channel into install.sh, producing a baked
  dist/install.sh.
- Make install.sh presence MANDATORY to the image gate (fail if missing
  or still carrying the placeholder / unsubstituted marker), with an
  explicit opt-out flag.
- Fix the runbook to substitute-then-sign, not sign-the-placeholder.
- Coherent with H-2 (#4197): both touch install.sh + publish.py.

---

## #4199 — install.sh mutates host before validating inputs; failed install leaves a dangling apt source that breaks apt update (fable-165 H-16) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## H-16 (fable-review-165)

install.sh mutates the host before it finishes validating inputs, and a
failed install (or a later `apt remove`) leaves a dangling apt source that
breaks `apt update` until an operator hand-deletes a file they never knew
existed.

### Basis
`scripts/dist/install.sh:180-187` main() order:

    preflight
    install_keyring     # MUTATES: writes /usr/share/keyrings/...asc
    write_source        # validates XPF_APT_BASE_URL + channel, THEN writes
    do_install

So a typo'd / missing XPF_APT_BASE_URL (or a bad channel) dies AFTER the
keyring is already installed -> half-configured host. Validation of the
apt URL/channel and the placeholder-key refusal happen after mutation.

Second defect: a failure at do_install (apt update/install) after
write_source leaves /etc/apt/sources.list.d/xpf.sources on disk pointing
at a repo that may not resolve -> every subsequent `apt update` errors.
The written xpf.sources is owned by no package and is never removed by
`debian/xpf.postrm`, while the Signed-By keyring IS package payload
(debian/rules:105-112) -> `apt remove xpf` deletes the keyring but leaves
xpf.sources dangling.

### Fix
- Reorder install.sh: validate ALL inputs (root, preflight, archive key
  not placeholder, XPF_APT_BASE_URL present, channel valid) BEFORE any
  mutation.
- Add a cleanup trap that removes the added xpf.sources on a failure after
  it was written, so a failed install does not brick apt update.
- Purge the install.sh-written xpf.sources on package remove/purge with a
  we-wrote-it marker check (mirroring link_is_owned) so `apt remove` does
  not strand the source.

---

## #4201 — apt channel isolation does not exist: one shared pool re-indexed into whichever suite is rebuilt (HB165 H-4) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-165 H-4, High)

`scripts/dist/build-apt-repo.sh` pools all .deb files channel-agnostically and
generates each suite's `Packages` index by scanning the WHOLE component pool.
There is one shared pool keyed by component only, so `stable` and `edge` debs
accumulate in the same directory and each suite's `Packages` lists the entire
pool. A `stable` rebuild after an `edge` build exists will list the `edge`
version in stable's `Packages`; `InRelease` signs it; `publish.py gate_apt`
verifies the signature per suite and passes (the bleed is validly signed). A
`stable` subscriber's `apt upgrade` then pulls the `edge` build.

## Evidence (file:line)

- `scripts/dist/build-apt-repo.sh:63` — `POOL="$APT/pool/$COMPONENT/x/xpf"`
  (no `$SUITE` component in the pool key).
- `scripts/dist/build-apt-repo.sh:110` — `cp -f "$d" "$POOL/"` (both suites'
  debs land in the same pool).
- `scripts/dist/build-apt-repo.sh:117` —
  `apt-ftparchive packages "pool/$COMPONENT"` (each suite's Packages scans the
  entire component pool, not its own subset).

## Trace

1. Publish stable `xpf 0.0.5000`; later publish edge `0.0.5100` — same pool
   accumulates both.
2. Next stable rebuild/re-sign scans the pool -> stable's `Packages` lists
   `0.0.5100`; `InRelease` signs it; `publish.py gate_apt` verifies per suite
   and passes (the bleed is signed and valid).
3. Every stable host's `apt upgrade` pulls the edge build.

## Why it matters

The stable/edge split is the operator's only blast-radius control for the
package path; it silently collapses in exactly the layout `publish.py` expects
(both suites under one tree).

## Fix direction

Isolate the pool per suite: `POOL="$APT/pool/$SUITE/$COMPONENT/x/xpf"` and scan
only that suite's pool (`apt-ftparchive packages "pool/$SUITE/$COMPONENT"`).

*(truncated — 44 lines total)*

## #4202 — deb ships xpf-kernel-promote.service but not its OnFailure= recovery unit — dangling reference on every deb-installed host (HB165 H-6) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-165 H-6, High)

The `.deb` stages `xpf-kernel-promote.service`, whose `OnFailure=` points at
`xpf-kernel-promote-failed.service`, but `debian/rules` never stages that
recovery unit. It is installed only into the baked image (`bake.py`). On a
deb-installed host the `OnFailure=` target does not exist, so the #1930 LANE-1
hang-recovery reboot is a dangling reference: a hung kernel-promotion gate
leaves the node booted on the unverified candidate and held SECONDARY forever.

## Evidence (file:line)

- `scripts/image/xpf-kernel-promote.service:18` —
  `OnFailure=xpf-kernel-promote-failed.service`.
- `debian/rules:71-72` — stages only `xpf-uefi-slots.service` and
  `xpf-kernel-promote.service`; the failed unit is not copied.
- `scripts/image/bake.py:385` — the failed unit is copied into the image only.
- `scripts/image/xpf-kernel-promote-failed.service` — the unit exists in the
  tree; it correctly has no `[Install]` section (it is `OnFailure=`-triggered,
  never enabled).

## Trace

Foreign-host `apt install xpf` -> operator runs `xpfd upgrade kernel arm` ->
candidate trial boot hangs the gate -> `TimeoutStartSec=120` fails the unit ->
systemd cannot find the `OnFailure=` unit ("Unit not found") -> no recovery
reboot; the node sits on the unverified candidate held SECONDARY.

## Fix direction

Stage `xpf-kernel-promote-failed.service` in the `.deb` (copy it under a
package-canonical name in `override_dh_auto_build`, install it to
`/lib/systemd/system`, add it to `override_dh_clean`). No enable is needed (no
`[Install]`), so install it without `dh_installsystemd` enable/start. Add a
build-time parity assert that the `OnFailure=` target referenced by the promote
unit is actually staged, so a future regression fails the build instead of
shipping a dangling reference.

---

## #4203 — No cross-check that install.sh embedded key, packaged keyring, and InRelease signer agree (HB165 H-15) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-165 H-15, Medium)

`publish.py` checks each of the three key sources for placeholder-ness
INDEPENDENTLY but never compares their fingerprints. So the installer's
embedded key, the packaged keyring, and the InRelease signer can diverge and
the publish still passes. A stale `dist/install.sh` (embedding an old, real,
retired key) publishes cleanly after a key rotation, and every new Tier-A
install then writes the old key and fails `apt-get update` fleet-wide.

## Evidence (file:line)

- `scripts/dist/publish.py:196-200` — install.sh checked only for the
  placeholder string.
- `scripts/dist/publish.py:261-264` — archive pubkey checked only for
  placeholder-ness.
- `scripts/dist/publish.py:309-315` — pooled `.deb` keyring checked only for
  placeholder-ness.
- No fingerprint comparison anywhere across the three sources.

## Trace

Archive key rotates -> keyring + `XPF_GPG_KEY` updated -> stale
`dist/install.sh` (old real key, valid minisig) passes all gates -> new
installs write the old keyring -> apt signature failure fleet-wide for new
installs.

## Fix direction

In `gate_apt`, extract install.sh's embedded armored key block, compute
fingerprints for install.sh's embedded key (I), the packaged keyring
`xpf-archive-keyring.asc` (K), and the InRelease signer (S). Require:
`I` is a subset of `K` (keyring superset allowed during a documented dual-sign
window), and the InRelease signer `S` is covered by `I` (and therefore by `K`).
Die on any mismatch. Mirror the existing ephemeral-GNUPGHOME import style in
`gate_apt`.

---

## #4204 — xpf-deploy: hypervisor-command failures surface as a bare CalledProcessError traceback, swallowing the real error (fable-165 H-21) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-165 H-21)

`Runner.run` executes every incus / virt-install / qemu-img command with
`subprocess.run(argv, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)` and
NOTHING catches the resulting `CalledProcessError`. Because `capture_output=True`
routes the tool's real message into the (uncaught) exception, the operator
sees a bare Python traceback ending in
`subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '[...]' returned non-zero exit status 1`
and NOT the actual cause (`Error: Network br-lan not found`, `Instance already
exists`, `Error: not found` for a bad image alias).

The single most common first-run failure — a missing bridge / VF / image
alias — is therefore opaque, which directly contradicts the tool's own
"fails on your laptop, not in prod" pitch.

## Location

- `scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` `Runner.run` (the `check=True,
  capture_output=True` call; ~line 344 on origin/master 0a58b92aa).
- Same swallow pattern at the config-drive mkiso build
  (`build_config_drive`, `subprocess.run(argv, check=True, ...)`) and the
  `sudo install` golden-copy fallback (`_install_libvirt_golden`).

## Fix

Capture stderr and, on a nonzero exit, `die()` with the command, the
return code, and the captured stderr — a clear
`command failed (rc=N): <cmd>\n<stderr>` message — instead of a bare
traceback. Route every hypervisor-command call site through one shared
capture-and-report helper (mirror the existing `die()` pattern).

---

## #4205 — xpf-deploy: --no-start is silently ignored on libvirt, and both docs claim the tool 'emits a command you run' when it executes it (fable-165 H-26) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-165 H-26)

Two coupled defects on the libvirt path:

1. `--no-start` is silently ignored. `deploy_libvirt` runs
   `virt-install --import` UNCONDITIONALLY (`runner.run(argv)`), which
   both DEFINES and BOOTS the domain. When `start=False` the code only
   skips a `print()` — the VM boots anyway, consuming its day-0 config
   with unpinned guest PCI slots. This makes the README's own
   pinned-guest-PCI workflow (edit slots via `virsh edit` BEFORE first
   boot) impossible.

2. Both docs misdescribe the tool. The tool EXECUTES the virt-install
   command (`runner.run(argv)`), but:
   - `examples/deploy/README.md` says libvirt "emits a `virt-install`
     command you run".
   - `docs/deploy-quickstart.md` says "the tool emits a `virt-install`
     command".

## Location

- `scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` `deploy_libvirt` (the unconditional
  `runner.run(argv)` + the `if start:` that only prints; ~line 533 on
  origin/master 0a58b92aa).
- `examples/deploy/README.md` (the incus-vs-libvirt table row).
- `docs/deploy-quickstart.md` ("## libvirt instead of incus").

## Fix

Honor `--no-start` on libvirt by generating the domain XML with
`virt-install ... --print-xml` and `virsh define`-ing it (defined,
persistent, NOT started), so `virsh edit` before first boot works. Fix
both docs to say the tool RUNS / EXECUTES the command (not "emits").

## #4206 — xpf-deploy: no preflight, no cleanup, no destroy verb — partial deploys dead-end and re-runs fail on 'already exists' (fable-165 H-27) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-165 H-27)

The deployer has no re-run safety:

- **No preflight.** `deploy_incus` runs `incus init` then N x
  `incus config device add` then `incus start` with NO existence checks —
  a missing bridge / VF / image alias is only discovered mid-mutation.
- **No cleanup on partial failure.** A device-add that throws leaves a
  half-created instance behind (init'd with some devices, no rollback).
- **No idempotency.** The re-run then hits `incus init ... already exists`
  and dead-ends.
- **No destroy verb.** The subcommand list has no `destroy` — tearing
  down a deployed VM requires a hand-run `incus delete` / `virsh
  undefine` + manual overlay removal.

Trace: HA deploy, fw0 succeeds, fw1's bridge is missing -> device add
throws (bare traceback, see H-21) -> fw1 left half-created -> fix the
bridge, re-run -> `incus init` fails "already exists".

## Location

- `scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` `deploy_incus` / `deploy_libvirt`
  (init -> device add -> start with no checks/rollback; ~line 355 on
  origin/master 0a58b92aa).
- Subcommand tuple in `main()` has no `destroy` (~line 1411).

## Fix

- **Preflight** before any mutation: the image/golden exists, every NIC
  source (managed network / host bridge / PF / PCI) exists, and the
  instance/domain name is free. Fail closed with one clear message.
- **Cleanup on failure**: delete the half-created instance / remove the
  overlay + undefine the domain when a mid-deploy step fails, so a re-run
  starts clean.
- **`destroy <appliance.yaml>` verb**: tear down the VM + its overlay +
  day-0 drive.

Full "reconcile an existing instance in place" idempotency can be a
follow-up; the minimum is preflight + cleanup-on-failure + destroy.

## #4214 — publish.py orphan sweep is suffix-shaped: unsigned dist/deb/*.deb ride the image tree unchecked (HB165 H-5) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-165 H-5)

`scripts/dist/publish.py`'s "fail-closed" image publish gate sweeps the dist
tree for orphans but only inspects files whose basename ends in an IMAGE suffix
(`.qcow2` / `.incus-metadata.tar.gz`). Every other file is skipped, so an
unsigned executable/installable file staged under the publish root rides the
whole-tree upload to `XPF_IMAGE_BASE_URL` with no signature coverage.

- `IMAGE_ARTIFACT_SUFFIXES = (".qcow2", ".incus-metadata.tar.gz")` — publish.py
- orphan sweep: `if not name.endswith(IMAGE_ARTIFACT_SUFFIXES): continue` — any
  non-image file is skipped, never flagged.
- `Makefile`: `DEB_OUT ?= $(CURDIR)/dist/deb` staged the built `.deb` INSIDE the
  publish root.

## Trace (normal workflow, not a corner case)

`make image` (`scripts/image/bake.py`) itself runs `make deb`, which drops
`dist/deb/xpf_*.deb` + `xpf-appliance_*.deb`, and also writes the signed image
set + `xpf-image.pub` into `dist/`. `make dist-publish` then uploads the WHOLE
`dist/` tree to the image URL. The unsigned debs (and any stray file) ride
along. A user who fetches the conveniently-hosted `.deb` installs bytes no
signature covers — defeating the module's stated fail-closed contract.

## Fix direction

1. Make the orphan sweep DEFAULT-DENY: every file under the image publish root
   (outside `apt/`) must be either an image artifact covered by a verified
   manifest OR on an explicit allowlist (`*.SHA256SUMS`, `*.minisig`,
   `install.sh`, `latest.json`, `xpf-image.pub`, plus the bake's
   `xpf-<ver>.manifest`). Anything else blocks the publish.
2. Stop defaulting `DEB_OUT` into the publish root — stage the `.deb` in a
   `dist-deb/` sibling OUTSIDE `dist/` (update bake.py, build-apt-repo.sh,
   cluster-setup.sh, README, .gitignore) so the mainline
   `make image && make dist-publish` does not trip the stricter gate.

## Labels

bug, distribution, security

## #4215 — publish.py gate_latest verifies only --channel's latest.json; other channels' pointers ship unverified (HB165 H-13) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-165 H-13)

`scripts/dist/publish.py`'s `gate_latest(dist, channel, ...)` verifies only the
target `--channel`'s `latest.json` freshness pointer. The whole `dist/` tree is
uploaded to `XPF_IMAGE_BASE_URL`, so a stale/tampered/unsigned
`dist/<other>/latest.json` (e.g. `dist/edge/latest.json`) rides along
unverified. `latest.json` does not match `IMAGE_ARTIFACT_SUFFIXES`, so the
orphan sweep skips it too.

- `gate_latest` opens `os.path.join(dist, channel, "latest.json")` for the ONE
  `--channel` and verifies + version-checks only that file.

## Trace

A stale/tampered/unsigned `dist/edge/latest.json` sits in the tree ->
`make dist-publish` (stable) gates stable only -> the edge pointer ships ->
`xpf-deploy.py fetch --channel edge` consumers resolve an unverified pointer.

## Fix direction

Enumerate every `dist/*/latest.json` present in the tree and gate each,
mirroring `gate_apt`'s per-suite InRelease posture. The target channel keeps the
stricter contract (must name a version present in this publish); every other
channel's pointer must at least carry a verifying signature.

## Labels

bug, distribution

## Dedup

Unreported; #1924's open scope is keys/hosting.

## #4217 — CoS schema: shaping-rate/burst-size leaves untyped — garbage commits as 0, silently removing the shaper (G-4) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-166 G-4)

The unit-level and interface-level `shaping-rate` / `burst-size` CoS
schema leaves carry NO `valueType`/`validator`, so `commit`/`commit
check` never validates the value. `set class-of-service interfaces reth0
unit 80 shaping-rate 10gg` commits: `parseBandwidthLimit("10gg")`
returns 0 (silent zero-on-garbage contract), and the compiler treats
`ShapingRateBytes==0` as "unset" — the root shaper silently disappears
and egress runs unshaped (~25G) instead of the intended cap.

Sibling leaves `transmit-rate` (ValueRate/ValidateRate) and `buffer-size`
(ValueByteSizeOrPercent) were typed in #1319 for exactly this reason;
the validators already exist.

## File:line
- `pkg/config/schema_cos.go:111-112` (unit-level shaping-rate + burst-size)
- `pkg/config/schema_cos.go:128-129` (#4021 interface-level shaping-rate + burst-size)
- `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:930-932` (parseBandwidthLimit returns 0 on garbage)

## Fix
Type `shaping-rate` via the container `keyValidator` (ValueRate /
ValidateRate) — the leaf carries children (burst-size), so keyValidator
validates the identity/rate token without flipping the walker into the
typed-LEAF branch (which would mis-treat burst-size as a presence
modifier). Type `burst-size` as ValueByteSize / ValidateByteSize.
`shaping-rate 10gg` and `burst-size garbage` then HARD-REJECT at commit.

## #4221 — CoS binding on a nonexistent interface/unit is a silent no-op (hb166 G-6) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

### Summary

A `class-of-service interfaces <name> ...` binding whose interface (or
logical unit) is NOT configured under `[interfaces]` commits cleanly and
shapes nothing. The operator believes CoS is applied; it is inert.

### Basis / where

- Apply path: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go:220-237` — the CoS
  binding only takes effect inside the `cfg.Interfaces` iteration
  (`cosIface := cfg.ClassOfService.Interfaces[name]`). A CoS interface
  name with no matching `cfg.Interfaces.Interfaces[name]` entry is never
  visited, so the binding is dropped.
- The interface-level fold `applyCoSInterfaceLevelBindings`
  (`pkg/config/compiler_class_of_service.go:511-531`) also early-returns
  when `cfg.Interfaces.Interfaces[name] == nil`, and only synthesizes
  units for CONFIGURED units — an explicit `unit N` binding on an
  unconfigured unit survives in `cos.Interfaces[name].Units[N]` but is
  never applied.
- The warn validator (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go:772-808`)
  checks that scheduler-map / classifier / rewrite-rule references
  resolve, but NEVER checks that `iface.Name` exists in
  `cfg.Interfaces.Interfaces` or that each bound `unit.Unit` is a
  configured logical unit.

### Why it matters

Junos rejects CoS on a nonexistent IFL. Here a `reth0`-vs-`reth1` typo
(or a unit number that was never configured) leaves the WAN unshaped
with only a "Runtime: unavailable" tell.

### Fix direction

Emit a commit-time WARNING (not reject — the interface could be added
later) when a `class-of-service interfaces <name>` binding references an
interface not in `cfg.Interfaces.Interfaces`, or a `unit N` not
configured on that interface. Fold into the existing CoS warn loop.

## #4222 — class-of-service fairness rss-expectation keyed by kernel ifindex is silently wrong after NIC re-enumeration (hb166 G-9) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

### Summary

`class-of-service fairness rss-expectation ifindex <n> queue <q> ...` is
keyed by the kernel ifindex. The ifindex is a transient identity that
changes across reboot/hotplug/re-enumeration, so after re-enumeration the
expectation evaluates the WRONG interface's `{a_i}` distribution while
still reporting under the old ifindex label.

### Basis / where

- Config type: `pkg/config/types_cos.go:166-173`
  (`CoSFairnessExpectation.Ifindex int`, comment claims ifindex is
  "used intentionally").
- Compile: `pkg/config/compiler_class_of_service.go:335-383` parses
  `ifindex <n>` and stores the raw kernel ifindex.
- Evaluate: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/fairness.go:213-224` matches the
  config ifindex against the live status snapshot's ifindex-keyed rows.
- Doc calls the ifindex keying "intentional"
  (`docs/per-5-tuple/state.md:396-399`), but xpf renames every interface
  to a STABLE vSRX name (`ge-0-0-2`, ...) — the NAME is the stable
  identity in xpf's interface-management model, the ifindex is transient.

### Why it matters

An expectation authored for `ge-0-0-2` silently judges whatever
interface currently holds that expectation's baked-in ifindex after the
next re-enumeration — a wrong-interface fairness verdict / Prometheus
gauge with no operator-visible tell.

### Fix direction

Key the config by interface NAME. Resolve name -> current kernel ifindex
at evaluate time from the live status snapshot (which re-reports the
ifindex<->name mapping every poll), so the expectation always tracks the
named interface even after re-enumeration. The Prometheus label can keep
the ifindex slot (now populated with the freshly-resolved ifindex), so no
metric-contract change is required. Go-only; no dataplane wire change.

Labels: bug, cos, config

## #4223 — Level-vs-unit CoS merge: unit shaping-rate override inherits the interface-level burst-size (hb166 G-10) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

### Summary

When a logical unit overrides `shaping-rate` but does not set its own
`burst-size`, the interface-level-fold pairs the LEVEL's `burst-size`
with the UNIT's rate. A shaper is a coupled `(rate, burst)` pair;
inheriting the burst from a different rate produces a mismatched shaper.

### Basis / where

`mergeCoSInterfaceLevelInto`,
`pkg/config/compiler_class_of_service.go:534-548`:

    if unit.ShapingRateBytes == 0 {
        unit.ShapingRateBytes = level.ShapingRateBytes
    }
    if unit.BurstSizeBytes == 0 {
        unit.BurstSizeBytes = level.BurstSizeBytes   // <-- fires even when
                                                     //     the unit set its
                                                     //     own rate
    }

`burst-size` is grammatically a CHILD of `shaping-rate` (both at the
interface level and unit level — `parseCoSInterfaceUnitBody`,
`compiler_class_of_service.go:396-406`), so `unit.BurstSizeBytes != 0`
implies `unit.ShapingRateBytes != 0`. The only defective case is a unit
that sets `shaping-rate` alone: it keeps the level burst.

### Why it matters

A level `shaping-rate 100m burst-size 200000` with a unit override
`shaping-rate 1g` (no burst) yields a 1g shaper carrying a 200000-byte
burst computed for 100m — a 10x rate/burst mismatch, defensible but
undocumented and surprising.

### Fix direction

Treat `(shaping-rate, burst-size)` as a coupled pair: inherit the level
`burst-size` ONLY when the unit is also inheriting the level's rate
(i.e. move the burst inheritance inside the `unit.ShapingRateBytes == 0`
block). A unit that overrides the rate then leaves burst unset (0), and

## #4226 — class-of-service: a dangling scheduler reference in a scheduler-map is warn-only at commit then fails open in the dataplane — the class silently loses its scheduling guarantee [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

A `class-of-service scheduler-maps <m> forwarding-class <fc> scheduler <name>`
entry that references a scheduler **not defined** under
`class-of-service schedulers` is only **warn-only at commit** and then
**fails OPEN in the Rust dataplane**. The referenced class silently loses
its scheduling guarantee AND is handed the *largest* best-effort surplus
share. Junos hard-rejects an unresolved scheduler reference at commit.

Found by fable-review-166 (finding G-2), verified at origin/master
`cb993896e`.

## Fail-open chain (file:line)

1. **Warn-only at strict commit.** `ValidateConfig`
   (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go:708`) only appended a warning for a
   scheduler-map entry naming an undefined scheduler.
   `validateClassOfServiceStrict` (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict.go`)
   does NOT reject it — its scheduler-map loop only checks buffer-percent
   overcommit and `continue`s past an undefined scheduler. So the commit
   succeeds.

2. **Go emitter forwards the dangling name.**
   `pkg/dataplane/userspace/cos.go` (`SnapshotForBindings`) filters only
   undefined *forwarding-classes*; it forwards `entry.Scheduler` unconditionally.

3. **Rust fails OPEN.** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/cos.rs`
   (`build_cos_iface_config`): `let scheduler =
   tables.schedulers.get(&entry.scheduler).copied();` resolves the dangling
   name to `None`, so:
   - `guarantee_enabled = false` (the class loses its guarantee), and
   - `transmit_rate_bytes = iface.cos_shaping_rate_bytes_per_sec` (the WHOLE
     interface shaping rate), which drives

## #4231 — Five security flow knobs commit clean with zero parsing and zero advisory (sync-icmp-session is dangerous in HA) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## fable-review-167 P-3

**Severity:** Medium
**Confidence:** High (grep: no handling in pkg/config on master 138434b3f)

### Junos expected
`route-change-timeout`, `sync-icmp-session`, `force-ip-reassembly`,
`multicast-session-lifetime`, `preserve-incoming-fragment-size` all alter flow
behavior.

### xpf actual
All five commit clean and do nothing, with no warning. None of them are parsed
anywhere in `pkg/config` (no schema leaf, no compiler case). This is
inconsistent with the repo's own accepted-with-advisory doctrine:

- the sibling `security flow tcp-session` knobs (#2078) are accepted WITH a
  commit advisory (`compiler_validate_warn.go`);
- screens (#3318) are rejected.

`sync-icmp-session` is the most dangerous in an HA deployment: an operator
reasonably believes ICMP sessions sync to the peer, but the userspace dataplane
does not sync ICMP sessions, so those flows do not survive failover.

### Fix direction
Add a commit advisory (the #2078 pattern) for each of the five knobs, stating
the knob is accepted but currently unenforced. They must first be accepted by
`setSchema` (typed leaves under `security flow`) and recorded by the compiler so
the advisory can fire on presence. `sync-icmp-session` gets the strongest
HA-specific wording.

### Dedup note
Tracked elsewhere as missing *features*, but the silent-accept (vs the repo's
own advisory doctrine) is unreported; `force-ip-reassembly` has partial
mitigation in #3291 but the knob itself is silently accepted.

## #4233 — security policies policy-rematch commits clean and is silently dropped (no advisory) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

`set security policies policy-rematch [extensive]` commits cleanly and is
**silently dropped**. It is absent from `pkg/config` `setSchema` (the
`policies` node in `pkg/config/schema_security.go` has no `policy-rematch`
child) and absent from `compilePolicies`' child handling
(`pkg/config/compiler_security_policy.go` — unknown children are ignored).
There is no strict gate and no advisory, so an operator who configures it
believes in-progress sessions will be re-evaluated when they will not.

This is the same "unmodeled Junos leaf commits clean and is silently
inert" class the repo has repeatedly resolved with an accepted-with-advisory
warning (#2078 tcp-session, #2008 H13 allow-dataplane-sleep, #3440 aging).

## Basis (file:line)

- `pkg/config/schema_security.go` `"policies"` node — no `policy-rematch` child.
- `pkg/config/compiler_security_policy.go` `compilePolicies` — no `policy-rematch` case.
- Doctrine to mirror: `pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go` (#2078 tcp-session
  advisory block; #2008 H13 allow-dataplane-sleep).

## Fix (this issue, driveable now)

Accept `policy-rematch [extensive]` in `setSchema` under `security policies`,
record it on `SecurityConfig`, and emit a commit **advisory** that it is
accepted but currently UNENFORCED — xpf does not yet re-evaluate in-progress
sessions on a policy change. This stops the silent drop.

The DEEPER behavior (xpf performs no session invalidation on commit at all,
including the Junos *default* drop-of-deleted-policy-sessions) is tracked as a
separate enhancement with a converged plan (filed alongside this issue).

## #4234 — No session invalidation on commit: sessions of a deleted/modified policy keep forwarding (Junos default + policy-rematch) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-01)

## Summary (stale-session security exposure)

xpf performs **no session invalidation on commit at all**. A session permitted
by a policy that is subsequently DELETED keeps forwarding until its idle
timeout. Junos, even WITHOUT `policy-rematch`, drops the sessions of a
*deleted* policy immediately at commit; `policy-rematch [extensive]`
additionally re-evaluates *in-progress* sessions against the changed policy set.

xpf does neither: #3395 re-resolves the policy id only for logging
attribution (`userspace-dp/src/event_stream/mod.rs`), never the verdict, and
`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go` invalidates no sessions on commit.

The commit-advisory half (accept `policy-rematch` + warn accepted-only) ships
in #4233. This issue tracks the actual enforcement.

## Reproduction

1. `set` a permit policy, commit; establish a flow.
2. Delete the permitting policy, commit.
3. The flow keeps forwarding (Junos would drop it at commit).

## Verdict: DRIVEABLE (deletion-clear core) + NEEDS-RESEARCH (modified re-eval)

The **deletion-clear** (Junos default) is a bounded, driveable feature reusing
xpf's existing filtered session-clear plumbing. The **modified-policy re-eval**
(`policy-rematch` semantics: re-classify in-progress sessions against the NEW
policy set) is a genuine design decision and is the research half.

## Converged plan (bounded deletion-clear -- a follow-up /engineer)

1. **Diff at commit apply** (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go`, which has both the
   pre-commit active config and the post-commit config): compute the set of
   policy stable-ids present BEFORE but ABSENT AFTER. Policy identity is
   already a stable hash -- `stablePolicyRuleID(fromZone,toZone,name)` in
   `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies.go` -- so deleting policy B does not shift
   policy A's id, and a deleted policy's sessions are identifiable by its id.
2. **Clear by policy-id**: each live session carries its `policy_id`
   (#3056; `pkg/dataplane/userspace/eventstream.go`). Add a `policy_id`
   filter dimension to the session-clear path (`ClearSessionsRequest` /

## #4239 — cos-simul-load-smoke.sh can never fail: gate booleans computed, printed, and discarded (exits 0 on FAIL) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (fable-review-166 V-1)

`test/incus/cos-simul-load-smoke.sh` — the canonical all-11-class CoS
simul-load smoke, declared "part of the canonical smoke matrix for any PR
that touches CoS scheduling" in `docs/fairness-regimes.md` — **always
exits 0**, even when its own gate verdict is FAIL. The fairness contract
it is meant to enforce is therefore a false-green.

## Basis / evidence

- `test/incus/cos-simul-load-smoke.sh:91-233` — the python reducer heredoc
  computes the gate booleans (`gate_1_small_class_divided_ceiling_floor`,
  `gate_2_priority_low_min_share`, `gate_3_retrans_floor`, or the reverse
  `gate_8_reverse_simul_22g`), writes `verdict.json`, prints
  `json.dumps(gates)`, and ends at `PYEOF` with **no `sys.exit`**. Under
  `set -euo pipefail` (:23) the script exit status equals python's exit
  status equals always 0.
- `test/incus/cos-simul-load-smoke.sh:78-79` — the iperf3 launchers are
  `|| true`, so even total generator failure exits 0.

## Why it matters

This is the ONLY harness asserting the #1614 divided-ceiling floors under
simul load. A starve-to-zero collapse of the small classes (100m/1g/3g/6g)
— exactly the regression the divided-ceiling floor exists to catch —
prints FAIL in `verdict.json` yet the script exits 0; any CI or
`&&`-chained invocation passes silently.

## Fix direction

- After the final `print(json.dumps(gates, ...))` and before `PYEOF`, add
  a per-gate pass extractor that handles the **heterogeneous** gate shape
  (dict gates carry a `"pass"` key; bare-bool gates are themselves the
  verdict) and `sys.exit(0 if all(_ok(v) for v in gates.values()) else 1)`.
  NOTE: a naive `all(gates.values())` is WRONG — a failing DICT gate is
  still truthy as a raw dict. Use `def _ok(v): return v["pass"] if
  isinstance(v, dict) else bool(v)`.
- Guard the all-error case: `gate_1` pass is `all(c["pass"] for c in
  gate1_classes)`, and `all([]) == True` if every small-class row errored —
  add `and len(gate1_classes) == len(SIMUL_FLOOR_PCT)`.

## #4241 — fairness-harness.sh single mode silently defaults SHAPER_RATE_BPS=25G for unknown ports (masks misconfig as pass) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (fable-review-166 V-11)

`test/incus/fairness-harness.sh` in single-class mode **silently defaults
`SHAPER_RATE_BPS` to 25 Gbps for any unknown port**, masking a
misconfigured port as a 25G-cap pass. The mixed-cos branch of the very
same script correctly refuses to guess (`exit 2`) — an unexplained,
dangerous asymmetry.

## Basis / evidence

- `test/incus/fairness-harness.sh:226-230` (single mode `else` branch):
  ```
  if ! SHAPER_RATE_BPS=$(canonical_shaper_rate_for_port "$PORT"); then
      SHAPER_RATE_BPS=25000000000
  fi
  ```
  `canonical_shaper_rate_for_port` (`:178-194`) `return 1`s for any port
  not in its case list, so an unknown/misconfigured `PORT` silently gets a
  25G shaper rate — the largest possible cap, against which almost any
  throughput passes.
- Compare the mixed-cos branch (`:213-217`, `:219-223`) which prints a
  diagnostic and `exit 2` when the same lookup fails.

## Why it matters

A misconfigured port must be a hard error, not a masked 25G-cap pass. The
25G default is silently permissive precisely where the harness should be
strict.

## Fix direction

Fail on an unknown port in single mode too (mirror the mixed-cos `exit 2`
diagnostic), or require an explicit rate — do not silently assume 25G.

## #4243 — CoS TX: any egress output filter (even counter/log-only) cancels input-filter forwarding-class classification [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

Attaching ANY interface egress OUTPUT firewall filter — even one whose only
terms are `then count` / `then log` (no `then forwarding-class`) — silently
CANCELS the forwarding-class an INPUT filter assigned. A packet that an input
filter classified into a CoS forwarding-class (e.g. `expedited-forwarding`)
loses that classification and falls back to the interface default/best-effort
queue the moment any output filter is present on the egress interface.

Junos semantics are output-OVERRIDES-when-set, not
output-PRESENCE-clears-ingress. A routine observability change (adding an
audit-only `then count` output filter on the WAN) therefore silently
reclassifies whole traffic classes to best-effort.

Severity: High.

## Basis (file:line, origin/master 628b44f3b)

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/cos_classify.rs`, `resolve_cos_tx_selection_internal`:

- `has_output_filter = output_filter.is_some();` gated the entire ingress
  input-filter evaluation on `!has_output_filter`
  (`(!has_output_filter && has_input_tx_selection) || has_input_three_color_policer`
  at the ingress-ifindex / ingress-filter resolution, and again in the
  `.filter(|filter| (!has_output_filter && filter.affects_tx_selection) || ...)`
  predicate).
- The captured ingress forwarding-class was then gated a third time:
  `if !has_output_filter { ingress_forwarding_class = ingress_result.forwarding_class; }`.

So when ANY output filter existed, `ingress_forwarding_class` stayed `None`.
Because a counter/log-only output filter sets no `then forwarding-class`,
`output_result.forwarding_class` is also `None`, and the queue resolution falls
through to the DSCP classifier / 802.1p classifier / `default_queue`. The
input-filter class is lost.

`has_output_filter` (needs-tx-eval predicate) is true for counter/log/terminal
output filters — see `interface_output_filter_needs_tx_eval` and the
`filter.has_counter_terms || filter.has_log_terms || filter.has_terminal_action_terms`
output_result gate. Commit `a15a6120` fixed only the zero-effect-output-filter
subcase (an output filter that matches nothing); the middle case

## #4244 — CoS TX: BA classifier code-point mapping to an unmaterialized queue is a 100% silent blackhole (commits cleanly) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary

A behavior-aggregate (DSCP / IEEE 802.1p PCP) classifier code-point that maps
to a forwarding-class whose queue is NOT materialized on the egress interface
(the forwarding-class has no scheduler-map entry, so the interface never builds
that queue) is a 100% SILENT BLACKHOLE. The config COMMITS cleanly (no reject,
no warning). Every packet carrying that code-point is dropped forever, while
traffic in other code-points forwards normally.

Severity: High.

## Basis (file:line, origin/master 628b44f3b)

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/cos.rs`:

- `build_cos_dscp_queue_table` / `build_cos_ieee8021_queue_table` copy EVERY
  code-point -> queue_id mapping from the GLOBAL classifier into the
  per-interface table `dscp_queue_by_dscp` / `ieee8021_queue_by_pcp` WITHOUT
  filtering against the queues the interface actually materializes.
- `build_cos_iface_config` admits the interface on an ANY-match gate
  (`dscp_classifier_targets_iface_queue = ... .any(|q| iface_queue_ids.contains(q))`),
  so a classifier with one code-point -> a materialized queue admits the
  interface; the OTHER code-points -> unmaterialized queues still get written
  verbatim into the per-interface table.

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/cos_classify.rs`:

- `resolve_cos_dscp_classifier_queue_id` returns `Some(unmaterialized_queue_id)`.
- `resolve_cos_queue_idx` does `root.queues.iter().position(|q| q.queue_id() == queue_id)`
  which returns `None` for a queue the interface never built.
- The enqueue path (`enqueue_cos_item`) turns that `None` into `Err(item)` ->
  the packet is dropped. There is a dead-looking `if queue_idx >= root.queues.len() { queue_idx = 0; }`
  branch that suggests a fallback that is never reachable (`position()` is
  always in-bounds), so no real default fallback exists.

Trace: scheduler-map materializes queue 0 only; a classifier maps ef(46) -> a

## #4246 — cos: v8 lease give-back never re-credits the epoch ledger — released bytes double-charged (candidate #1630 cause-2 fix) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

Fast follow-up /engineer split out of the fairness-mechanism tracking
issue #4245 (finding T-1, folding R-5(a)). Highest-value of the five
fable-review-166 fairness findings: a bounded epoch-ledger accounting fix
that is the best-fitting recoverable candidate for the long-standing
#1630 cause-2 ~6% mid-rate residual (documented-not-fixed as "transport
physics" in docs/fairness-regimes.md:1388-1404).

Verified against origin/master 38041f223.

## The bug

The v8 shared-CoS-lease acquire (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/
shared_cos_lease/lease.rs `acquire_v8_with_cause`, ~624-687) charges a
grant to THREE places: the per-epoch class ledger `packed_granted`
(Step A, gated by ClassCap at lease.rs:640-647), the legacy `outstanding`
credit (Step B, lease.rs:664), and `worker_grants[worker_id]`
(Step C, lease.rs:687).

The give-back `release_unused` (lease.rs:1027 -> `shared_cos_lease_
release_unused`, lease.rs:245-270) moves `outstanding -> available` in the
legacy `credits` word ONLY. It never decrements `packed_granted` or
`worker_grants`. Rotation (rotate_epoch_v8.rs:63-73) swaps `packed_granted`
and banks only `cap - granted`, so released-but-not-recredited bytes are
treated as claimed for the rest of the epoch.

The release fires on queue-empty: tx_completion.rs:711-715 does
`mem::take(&mut queue.hot.tokens)` then `release_unused` (line 741); the
teardown twin is token_bucket.rs:397-428
(`release_all_cos_queue_leases`). A mid-rate exact class oscillating
empty<->backlogged at epoch timescale is charged for bytes it returned ->
hits ClassCap early -> parks until the next rotation.

Concrete trace: 1G exact class, epoch cap 25,000 B; drains 23,500 and
empties mid-epoch; 1,500 B released; `packed_granted` stays 25,000 = cap;
next same-epoch arrivals break ClassCap and park -> ~94% effective
service.

The v8 consume/release pair has ZERO tests.

## #4247 — cos-simul-load-smoke CoV diverges from the Rust fairness SSOT (sample stddev + zero-flow filtering) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

hb166 V-10.

Basis: the Python CoV printed by the simul-load smoke reducer cannot
reproduce a fairness-eval verdict on identical traffic, inviting
misdiagnosis of CoS fairness.

test/incus/cos-simul-load-smoke.sh (before fix, line ~155) computed:

    cov = statistics.stdev(rates) / statistics.mean(rates) * 100

with two divergences from the authoritative Rust estimator
userspace-dp/src/fairness.rs::compute_observed_cov:

1. statistics.stdev is the SAMPLE stddev (denominator N-1). The Rust SSOT
   uses the POPULATION stddev (denominator N). For {500,500,1500,1500}
   the SSOT CoV is 0.5 but the sample CoV is 0.5774.
2. the rate vector filtered out zero-bps streams (if bps > 0), so a fully
   starved class printed CoV 0 -- the "perfectly fair" value -- exactly
   inverting the signal. The Rust SSOT never filters zeros; a starved
   flow is maximally unfair and must RAISE CoV.

Additionally the column was labelled a plain "CoV" with no indication it
is a whole-run figure (warmup included) while the Rust reducer uses the
steady-state window.

Fix: extract the estimator into test/incus/fairness_cov.py (population
stddev over the full vector including zeros, 0.0 for empty/zero-mean --
byte-for-byte the fairness.rs semantics); import it into the smoke
reducer; relabel the printed column wrCoV% (whole-run) with a legend and
verdict provenance field cov_estimator=whole_run_population; add
test/incus/fairness_cov_test.py pinning population_cov to the exact
values the fairness.rs unit tests assert (0.5 skewed, 0.0 balanced,
empty, zero-mean) plus a starved-flow-not-filtered assertion.

Severity: Low-Medium (CoV is decorative today per the #1614 re-scope, but
the divergence misleads a human reading the smoke output).

## #4248 — surplus give-back validator: lax handback derivation + no live runner produces phases.json [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

hb166 V-8.

Two coverage defects in the #1321 surplus give-back contract.

1. Lax handback derivation (driveable, fixed here).
   test/incus/fairness_surplus_giveback_validate.py accepted the first
   list-order sample matching the post-handback thresholds with NO
   monotonic-t_sec check, NO pre-handback-state sample, and NO density
   requirement. A one-element artifact carrying a single already-settled
   snapshot trivially passed the <=5 s gate -- the sample's self-attested
   t_sec was the only evidence, and the docs explicitly claim the
   validator "must derive the handback point from auditable data."

   at least --min-handback-samples samples (default 2), strictly
   increasing t_sec, consecutive gaps within --max-handback-sample-gap-sec
   (default 5 s), and a pre-handback baseline sample before the first
   post-handback sample. The derived handback time is the first
   post-handback sample that follows a pre-handback one, so the accepted
   t_sec is bracketed by the transition rather than trusted alone. New
   unit tests cover single-sample, non-monotonic, no-pre-baseline, and
   too-sparse artifacts.

   Note: timestamps remain generator-supplied; the ordered-series
   cross-check is the auditability bound available in a REDUCED artifact.
   An independent wall-clock derivation of t_sec belongs in the live
   reducer (item 2).

2. No live runner (deferred, documented).
   NOTHING in the tree produces phases.json -- the 100E100M give-back
   contract is exercised only by hand-built artifacts, so the validator
   is a MANUAL gate. Building the live reducer (iperf interval JSON +
   Prometheus/dataplane status -> phases.json + handback_samples with
   wall-clock t_sec) is the remaining work; the validator docstring and
   docs/fairness-regimes.md now state this limitation explicitly. The
   structural cross-checks in item 1 keep a hand-built artifact honest
   until the live reducer exists.

## #4256 — waterfill Phase-1 honor consumed at SELECTION not SERVICE — a zero-byte TX burns the small class's 200us epoch guarantee [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (fable-review-166 T-2, HIGH)

The guarantee-rate waterfill selector debits the Phase-1 budget and
sets the honored-epoch bit at SELECTION time, before the queue is
serviced. When the subsequent service call transmits zero bytes (TX
ring full, no free UMEM frame, or a frame-build Drop), the honor is
NOT refunded. The honored small class is then skipped by BOTH phases
for the rest of the 200us epoch, while larger Phase-2 classes stay
re-selectable (Phase 2 sets no honor bit and debits no budget). This
inverts the #1732/#1743 small-class-first intent precisely under TX
pressure.

## Mechanism / file:line (HEAD e08d681)

- Debit + honor set at selection:
  userspace-dp/src/afxdp/cos/queue_service/mod.rs ~1077-1096
  (waterfill_pass1_remaining_bytes -= phase1_cost;
   waterfill_honored_epoch_bits |= 1<<i; phase1_admissions += 1) then
  returns the selection.
- Service happens AFTER, in the wrapper
  service_exact_guarantee_queue_direct_with_info (mod.rs ~436-463):
  progress = service_exact_*_queue_direct(...); on progress==false it
  returns Some(None) with NO refund.
- Zero-byte failure sites return false:
  service.rs ~66 (Drop), ~93 (MirrorTxFrameReserve), ~106 (no free
  frame), ~155 (tx ring insert failed / inserted==0).

Asymmetry: a Phase-2 zero-byte failure loses nothing (no honor bit /
no budget debit; only cursor advance), but a Phase-1 zero-byte failure
loses the whole epoch. Small classes are exactly the Phase-1 honored
set, so they are the ones penalized.

Note: the TX-ring-full / no-free-frame condition is INTERFACE-WIDE (all
CoS queues share one xsk TX ring + UMEM pool), so refunding + retrying
the same queue next drain pass does NOT differentially starve other
queues — they all fail on a full ring anyway, and the worker reaps
completions between passes.

## Summary (fable-review-166 T-5, Medium/High)

cos_flow_aware_buffer_limit bounds the flow-aware aggregate buffer
expansion by a #717 latency-envelope clamp:

    delay_cap = transmit_rate_bytes * COS_FLOW_FAIR_MAX_QUEUE_DELAY_NS / 1e9
    return base.max(prospective * MIN_SHARE).min(delay_cap.max(base))

For an UNSHAPED (transparent) flow-fair queue, transmit_rate_bytes == 0
(rate 0 means "unshaped / full bucket", NOT "zero drain rate" — see the
guarantee_enabled field note in types/cos.rs). So delay_cap == 0, and
.min(delay_cap.max(base)) == .min(base) pins the aggregate cap at base
regardless of flow count. The flow-aware expansion collapses: a new
flow's first packet is dropped at the aggregate cap while resident
elephant bytes stay — exactly the #704/#707 regression the flow-aware
expansion was built to prevent, now for the rate-0 regime.

Post-#1735 every CoS queue is flow-fair-eligible, so unshaped queues
DO hit this path.

## file:line (HEAD e08d681)

userspace-dp/src/afxdp/cos/admission.rs ~228-234
(cos_flow_aware_buffer_limit, the delay_cap computation and the
.min(delay_cap.max(base)) clamp).

rate 0 (it uses buffer_limit / N), so the new flow is admitted per-flow
but rejected at the aggregate cap — the off-by-one the two-denominator
design was meant to close.

rate 0 is "drains at the physical link rate", not "zero drain rate".
Anchor the delay cap to an assumed link-rate floor when
transmit_rate_bytes == 0, so the delay cap does not collapse to 0 and
the flow-aware buffer still expands for a new flow. Keep the shaped
(rate > 0) path bit-identical. This gives an unshaped queue a delay cap

## #4259 — CoS MQFQ: stale flow_bucket_observed_bps survives flow death — cap-aware selector defers newcomers with a dead elephant's rate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

**Basis:** fable-review-166 R-1 (re-verified at HEAD e08d681bf).

**Mechanism (file:line):**
- account_cos_queue_flow_dequeue (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/cos/queue_ops/accounting.rs:106-129) resets ONLY flow_bucket_head_finish_bytes / flow_bucket_tail_finish_bytes on the bucket nonzero to 0 transition.
- The per-bucket observed-rate EWMA is written only by account_flow_bucket_tx (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/cos/fairness.rs:92-104). Its skip-ramp arms only when observed_bps == 0, and nothing ever returns it to 0 on flow death (decay requires TX commits, which require service).
- The cap-aware MQFQ selector cos_queue_min_finish_bucket (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/cos/queue_ops/mod.rs:134-138) defers any bucket whose observed_bps > target_bps while another is under-cap.

**Consequence:** an elephant drives bucket B's EWMA to ~2 Gbps against an ~83 Mbps target; the flow ends; the EWMA stays 2 Gbps indefinitely. A new flow hashing into recycled bucket B is deferred as if it were the old elephant. Inverts the mechanism's purpose (built to protect cool flows, it throttles the coolest). Invisible to steady-state iperf smoke; bites real short-flow churn. After hours of churn most of the 4096 buckets carry stale nonzero rates.

**Fix:** on the bucket nonzero to 0 transition (bucket identity ends), also zero flow_bucket_observed_bps / flow_bucket_last_tx_ns / flow_bucket_pending_bytes so the skip-ramp re-arms cleanly for the next flow. Add the missing selector-defers-at-finite-target test (the positive action of the cap-aware selector is currently untested).

**Dedup:** distinct from killed #1238 (per-flow token buckets) and #1229's v7 design — this is a state-lifecycle defect IN the shipped mechanism.

## #4260 — CoS v8 epoch seqlock writer: missing Release fence after EVEN->ODD claim — torn snapshots on weakly-ordered CPUs [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

**Basis:** fable-review-166 R-3 (re-verified at HEAD e08d681bf, memory-model level).

**Mechanism (file:line):** writer maybe_rotate_epoch_v8 (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/shared_cos_lease/rotate_epoch_v8.rs):
- EVEN to ODD claim CAS at :50-57 with AcqRel.
- Relaxed payload stores at :392-406 (epoch_total_grant_cap, epoch_grace_expires_ns, worker_fair_share, epoch_start_ns) plus publish_equal_flow_epoch_v8.
- Sole Release is the final ODD to EVEN publish store at :411 (the publish half fixed by #1643).

The AcqRel claim CAS's release half orders only writes SEQUENCED-BEFORE the CAS; it does not order the Relaxed payload stores that follow. A reader that reads the payload gets no synchronizes-with edge from the claim CAS (it does not read the CAS's ODD value). So the payload stores can become globally visible before the ODD claim on a weakly-ordered CPU.

Reader snapshot_epoch_v8 (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/shared_cos_lease/lease.rs:1139-1181) already seals its Relaxed payload loads with fence(Acquire) before the seq_after re-read (#1643 reader half). The writer half is missing.

**Consequence:** a reader can read seq=EVEN(old), read new-epoch payload (torn), read seq=EVEN(old) again, and pass the even-equal validation against a mix of old/new epoch fields — the #1619 tearing class, of which #1643 fixed only the reader half. Latent on x86-TSO (i40e/mlx5 deploy targets); a real hazard on ARM/POWER; a specification bug regardless.

**Fix:** add fence(Ordering::Release) immediately after the successful claim CAS (Boehm seqlock recipe) so the payload stores are published-after the ODD claim is visible. Pairs with the reader's existing fence(Acquire). One extra fence per ~200 us (EPOCH_DURATION_NS). Memory-model change — needs careful review + cluster CoS smoke.

**Dedup:** #1643 (reader half) and #1619 (tearing class) closed; the writer half is unreported.

## #4261 — CoS token-bucket refill: fractional dust discarded each refill — low-rate classes systematically under-run [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

**Basis:** fable-review-166 R-4 (re-verified at HEAD e08d681bf, arithmetic).

**Mechanism (file:line):** refill_cos_tokens (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/cos/token_bucket.rs:322-329):

    let elapsed_ns = now_ns - *last_refill_ns;
    let added = ((elapsed_ns as u128) * (rate as u128) / 1_000_000_000u128) as u64;
    if added == 0 { return; }
    *tokens = tokens.saturating_add(added).min(burst_bytes);
    *last_refill_ns = now_ns;

added floors the byte grant, but last_refill_ns is advanced fully to now_ns — the sub-byte fractional remainder is discarded every refill. A 64 kbps class (8000 B/s) refilled at the ~200 us drain cadence computes added = 1.6 to 1 and throws away 0.6 B of accrued credit per interval, delivering 5000 B/s against an 8000 B/s shape (37.5% under). ~2% under at 1 Mbps; negligible at >= 100 Mbps.

**Consequence:** kbps voice/control classes never reach their configured rate. Same failure shape as #1630 (which fixed the epoch/visit-cap layer at 100m/1g), one decade lower — this is the ns-integer-division dust layer, unreported.

**Fix:** carry the fractional remainder across refills. Rewind last_refill_ns by the time-equivalent of the ungranted fraction (equivalently, advance the clock only by the time-value of the granted whole bytes) so cumulative granted == floor(total_elapsed * rate / 1e9). No signature/field change needed — the remainder lives in the timestamp. Add a conservation unit test (N refills at non-integral cadence sum to rate*time +/- 1 byte); refill_cos_tokens currently has zero direct unit tests.

(sharded) egress is admitted at up to **N_workers x its configured
guaranteed transmit-rate** at guarantee priority, because each worker
refills its own private replica of the queue's token bucket at the FULL
configured rate with no class-wide (cross-worker) metering.

Class-wide shared metering exists only for **exact** queues (the shared

guarantee priority.

  — the FULL configured rate, per worker, with no shared metering.

## #4270 — CoS perf: false sharing on worker_active_flow_buckets + timer-wheel per-slot allocations (fable-166 R-9) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

Two perf issues on the CoS per-flow-fairness / drain hot path, verified
against origin/master ~02f8c8080. Severity: Medium (perf).

1) False sharing: worker_active_flow_buckets is the only per-worker
   per-acquire array left UNPADDED.

   epoch.rs:257 declares:
     worker_active_flow_buckets: Box<[AtomicU32]>

   Each slot is a raw 4-byte AtomicU32, so 16 workers' slots pack into a
   single 64-byte cache line. The array is:
     - written per flow-bucket activation/teardown by EACH worker on its
       OWN slot (active_buckets.rs bump/unbump, single-writer-per-slot,
       Relaxed), and
     - read on every acquire_v8 (lease.rs:593) and equal_flow_cap_v8
       (lease.rs:1229), plus the rotation sum.

   This is genuine false sharing (per-worker INDEPENDENT writes to
   adjacent slots on one line), NOT a shared gate. It contradicts the
   lease's own documented isolation rule: every other per-acquire-written
   per-worker array is #[repr(align(64))] --
   PackedEpochGrant (worker_grants / worker_starvation_events /
   worker_demand_events / worker_equal_flow_active_samples) and
   PaddedAtomicU64 (worker_requested_bytes / worker_granted_bytes). See the
   #1863 doc comment at epoch.rs:293-311 which states the isolation rule
   explicitly. worker_active_flow_buckets is the odd one out. Worst under
   short-flow churn -- the regime where per-flow fairness matters most.

   FIX: add PaddedAtomicU32 (#[repr(align(64))], mirroring PaddedAtomicU64)
   and change the field to Box<[PaddedAtomicU32]>. Keep the
   worker_active_flow_buckets_for accessor returning &AtomicU32 (deref .0)
   so the four mutation call sites are unchanged. Compile-time align/size
   asserts pin the padding.

## #4272 — cos: non-shared_exact cos_flow_fair path uses buffer_limit.div_ceil(prospective_active) without .max(1) (latent panic if 0) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

The shared_exact cos_flow_fair path guards `buffer_limit.div_ceil(prospective_active.max(1))`, but the non-shared_exact sibling path calls `div_ceil(prospective_active)` WITHOUT the `.max(1)`. If `prospective_active` were ever 0, `div_ceil(0)` panics.

Currently likely unreachable — `prospective_active` reserves +1 headroom so it's ≥1 in practice (flagged as pre-existing/out-of-scope in the #4271 R-8/R-9 review). But the asymmetry is a latent hazard: add `.max(1)` to the non-shared_exact div_ceil for consistency with the shared_exact path. 1-line defensive hardening.

## #4273 — fairness-eval: Gate 3 aggregate-throughput leg is vacuous (saturation label == gate predicate) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

hb166 fairness_eval reducer review, finding V-3.

Basis: the aggregate-throughput acceptance gate (Gate 3 in
docs/fairness-regimes.md) is unenforceable by construction. The
saturation LABEL and the GATE use the same predicate, so no single-run
harness can ever FAIL on aggregate throughput.

- userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/verdict.rs:109-117 computes "saturated"
  report-only via is_saturated().
- userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/verdict.rs:119-147 builds
  failure_reasons: Gate 1 (starved), Gate 2 (per-flow CoV), the a_i-sum
  harness guard, RSS expectation, and the CoS-vs-binding guard. There is
  NO aggregate-throughput failure reason. "saturated" is stored in
  VerdictDecision (verdict.rs:48/164) and never referenced by any gate.
- userspace-dp/src/fairness.rs:113-124 is_saturated() = aggregate >= 95%
  of the Nc/Nv-scaled cap in >=80% of buckets — the exact predicate the
  doc's Gate 3 asserts.

Consequence: a shaped class delivering, say, 50% of its cap is labeled
non-saturated, and non-saturated runs are exempt from the aggregate leg
(docs Gate 3), so a fairness-neutral throughput regression (flows evenly
slow -> CoV ~ 0, gap under epsilon) passes the whole verdict. The doc's
non-shaped "±5% of measured baseline" clause has no implementation.

Fix: break the circularity with an input observed data cannot launder.
Add an operator-declared expectation flag (--expect-saturation): when the
operator asserts the offered load is >= the structural cap, the observed
aggregate is then REQUIRED to reach >= 95% of the Nc/Nv-scaled cap, else
Gate 3 fails. The "saturated" label stays descriptive/report-only (no
change to its pass/fail neutrality); the ENFORCEMENT is driven by the
independent declaration. Reconcile the two contradictory doc sections
(Gate 3 "applies for saturated runs" vs "labeling does not change
pass/fail"). Note: the non-shaped baseline-artifact (±5% of prior-tip
measured baseline) clause needs a baseline input file and is deferred;
this issue implements the enforceable operator-declared leg.

## #4274 — fairness-eval: a_i overcount trim removes from the LARGEST bucket, which can RAISE Cstruct and loosen Gate 2 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

hb166 fairness_eval reducer review, finding V-4.

Basis: the accepted-overcount normalization trims flows from the LARGEST
bucket, which can manufacture skew and RAISE Cstruct, loosening the
Gate-2 tolerance (observed_CoV <= Cstruct + 0.05). That is fail-open in
exactly the wrong direction.

- userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/per_worker.rs:186-202
  (trim_distribution_to_sum) removes excess from the max-count bucket.
- userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/verdict.rs:91-98 applies the trim and
  feeds the trimmed distribution to compute_cstruct().

Worked example: {3,3} observed with an accepted overcount to target sum 5
trims to {2,3}: Cstruct 0.00 -> ~0.204, widening the allowed observed
CoV from 0.05 to ~0.254. An evenly-loaded overcount is thus rewarded.

Fix: the trim must never loosen the gate. Gate on min(Cstruct_raw,
Cstruct_trimmed) (fail-closed): if the trim would raise Cstruct, fall
back to the raw distribution's tighter ceiling. This preserves the
legitimate #1281 stale-overcount cases (where trimming LOWERS Cstruct,
e.g. {4,4,4,3,0,0} -> {3,3,3,3,0,0}, 0.125 -> 0.0) while rejecting the
perverse-incentive case.

## #4275 — fairness-eval: CoS-source {a_i} medians ignore absent (zero) samples — dead workers stay active [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

hb166 fairness_eval reducer review, finding V-5.

Basis: the CoS active-flow exporter emits rows only for live flows, and
the reducer takes the median over PRESENT samples only. A worker whose
flows die partway through the window keeps a non-zero median, so a dead
worker is still counted "active" — inflating Nc and distorting Cstruct.

- userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/per_worker.rs:145-160
  (aggregate_cos_per_worker) medians over present (ts, worker) samples;
  a worker absent for the back half of the window keeps median = its live
  value, not 0.

The binding-source path is immune only because its exporter zero-fills
every worker every scrape; the CoS source does not, so the reducer must
enforce the zero-fill itself.

Fix: zero-fill each worker's samples across the full in-window scrape
timestamp universe (the timestamps at which the queue was scraped, i.e.
any worker on the matched ifindex/queue emitted) before taking the
median. A worker absent at a scrape where the queue was live is genuinely
0. Applying the same zero-fill to the binding path is a safe no-op (that
exporter already emits every worker every scrape) and makes the two
sources compute the same statistic.

## #4276 — fairness-eval: steady window anchored to scrape-file min/max, not the iperf epoch — stale pre-run samples leak in [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

hb166 fairness_eval reducer review, finding V-6.

Basis: the per-worker aggregation derives its steady-state window from
the scrape FILE extent (min/max timestamp) rather than the actual iperf
run interval, so stale pre-run / cooldown-era scrapes that sit inside the
file but outside the run land in the window.

- userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/per_worker.rs:46-57
  (aggregate_per_worker) and :112-123 (aggregate_cos_per_worker) compute
  ss_start = min(timestamp) + warmup and ss_end = max(timestamp) -
  final_burst.
- The sibling reducer test/incus/fairness_equal_flow_capture.py:237-255
  anchors to the iperf "timesecs" epoch — the two reducers disagree on
  "steady state", and the cooldown-era staleness the sweep guards against
  can still contaminate the head of the fairness-eval window.

Fix: anchor the window to the iperf epoch. iperf3 JSON carries
start.timestamp.timesecs (wall-clock run start); the binding/CoS TSV
timestamps share the same epoch-seconds clock. Deserialize timesecs and
compute the window as [epoch + warmup, epoch + duration - final_burst].
Fall back to the min/max heuristic only when timesecs is absent (legacy /
synthetic input).

## #4277 — fairness-eval: 60s steady-state minimum checks DECLARED duration, not observed samples; omitted intervals unfiltered [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

hb166 fairness_eval reducer review, finding V-7.

Basis: the >=60s steady-state minimum is checked against the self-
reported iperf duration, not the number of observed 1-second buckets, so
a truncated JSON (a handful of intervals) that DECLARES a 120s run passes
and produces a CoV verdict from a few buckets — violating the contract's
"must reject such runs with an explicit error" (docs/fairness-regimes.md
"Steady-state measurement window").

- userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/windowing.rs:17-33 gates on
  iperf.start.test_start.duration (declared), never on
  aggregate_buckets_bps.len() (observed).
- iperf -O omitted intervals are not filtered; they would count as
  steady-state data (latent — the harness never passes -O, but
  fairness-eval is a general CLI).

Fix: after building the in-window buckets, require the observed non-
omitted bucket count to be >= 60 (with a small boundary slack), and skip
intervals flagged sum.omitted = true.

## #4278 — fairness-eval: verdict omits doc-mandated required metrics (per-flow quantiles, window timestamps, saturation series) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

hb166 fairness_eval reducer review, finding V-9.

Basis: the verdict JSON omits three metrics the contract marks MUST in
docs/fairness-regimes.md "Required metrics — exported from the harness":

- item 1 (per-flow throughput min/p25/median/p75/max + stream count N)
- item 6 (saturation determination AND its supporting time-series)
- item 12 (steady-state window explicit start/end timestamps)

  none of these; raw artifacts persist only when ARTIFACT_DIR is set, so
  a routine verdict cannot satisfy the MUST list post-hoc.

Fix: emit the required metrics in the verdict — per-flow throughput
quantiles (Mb/s) with stream count, the steady-state window epoch/relative
start/end timestamps, and the per-bucket aggregate throughput series with
the structural cap and saturated-bucket fraction.

## #4282 — cos: two owner-lifecycle accounting gaps (CoS-submit tx_packets/tx_bytes not bumped; no dehydrate counterpart to rehydrate_worker_active_count) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

Two behavior/design gaps surfaced during fable-166 R-10 (out of scope for the test-only #4280; recorded here for a follow-up):

(a) The CoS submit paths may not bump `binding.live.tx_packets` / `tx_bytes` — so a CoS-forwarded packet's TX counters could undercount vs the non-CoS path. Verify + reconcile the counter bump on the CoS submit path.

(b) No `dehydrate` counterpart to `rehydrate_worker_active_count`: a dropped worker runtime that still has `active_flow_buckets > 0` could PERMANENTLY inflate that worker's fair share (the count is rehydrated on rejoin but never decremented on a clean drop). Needs a dehydrate/reset on runtime teardown so a stale active count doesn't skew fairness after a worker leaves.

(b) especially interacts with the R-7 rejoin + R-2 shared-lease machinery — needs a design pass on the worker-lifecycle accounting. Likely a /research item.
