## #4285 — OSPF/OSPFv3 interface timers + DR priority silently dropped — adjacency will not form with a fast-timer neighbor [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (source-verified at origin/master 016167a15)

Junos tunes OSPF adjacency timers and DR election per interface:
`interface ge-0-0-1 { hello-interval 1; dead-interval 3; retransmit-interval 5; priority 200; }`

xpf parses only a subset of the OSPF interface leaves and silently drops
the timers and DR priority at every layer:

- Schema declares only passive/no-passive/interface-type/cost/authentication/bfd
  - pkg/config/schema_routing.go:259-274 (OSPFv2)
  - pkg/config/schema_routing.go:292-299 (OSPFv3, thinner still)
- Compiler switch has no case for hello-interval/dead-interval/retransmit-interval/priority
  - pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:84-117 (OSPFv2 iface)
  - pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:536-566 (OSPFv3 iface)
- Struct has no such fields
  - pkg/config/types_routing.go:373-386 (OSPFInterface)
  - pkg/config/types_routing.go:272-280 (OSPFv3Interface)
- FRR renderer emits only ip ospf cost + network + auth + bfd
  - pkg/frr/policy_render.go:551-580 (OSPFv2 iface block)
  - pkg/frr/policy_render.go:608-630 (OSPFv3 iface block)

All four leaves drop silently. FRR keeps its defaults (hello 10s, dead 40s,
priority 1).

## Adjacency impact (HIGH)

OSPF requires hello-interval AND dead-interval to MATCH between neighbors or
the adjacency never forms (the neighbor is dropped during the hello exchange,
stuck in Init/ExStart). A neighbor configured with fast timers (e.g. hello 1s,
dead 3s) will never adjacency with xpf's silent default 10s/40s. Priority
governs DR/BDR election; dropping it silently breaks intended DR placement.

Repro: `set protocols ospf area 0 interface ge-0-0-1 hello-interval 1` +
`dead-interval 3` commits clean; adjacency to the fast-timer neighbor never
comes up.

## Fix

Add hello-interval / dead-interval / retransmit-interval / priority to the
OSPF and OSPFv3 interface schema + struct + compiler, and emit them under the

## #4286 — BGP local-address (update-source) + passive/hold-time/per-group local-as silently dropped — iBGP loopback peering will not establish [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (source-verified at origin/master 016167a15)

Junos iBGP designs peer loopback-to-loopback and source the session from the
loopback:
`group ibgp { local-address 10.255.0.1; hold-time 30; passive; local-as 65001; neighbor 10.255.0.2 { peer-as 65000; } }`

xpf models none of local-address / passive / hold-time / per-group local-as:

- Neither the BGP schema group nor neighbor children declare them
  - pkg/config/schema_routing.go:320-382 (group + neighbor)
- The group + neighbor compiler switches have no case for them
  - pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:272-495 (group loop + per-neighbor overrides)
- The struct lacks the fields
  - pkg/config/types_routing.go:410-429 (BGPNeighbor)
- The renderer never emits neighbor update-source / passive / timers / local-as
  - pkg/frr/policy_render.go:669-704 (neighbor emission loop)

So iBGP configs that peer loopback-to-loopback silently omit update-source.

## Adjacency impact (HIGH for local-address)

Without `neighbor X update-source <loopback>`, the BGP TCP session sources
from the egress interface IP, not the loopback. The remote peer has a
`neighbor` statement for the loopback address only, so it rejects the
incoming connection (source address mismatch) — the iBGP session never
establishes / flaps. `hold-time` mismatch shortens/breaks the session;
`passive` prevents xpf from initiating (peer must connect); per-group
`local-as` changes the AS presented to that peering.

Repro: `set protocols bgp group ibgp local-address 10.255.0.1` +
`neighbor 10.255.0.2 peer-as 65000` commits clean; no update-source in FRR →
session never comes up.

## Fix

Map the group (and neighbor-override) leaves to FRR neighbor lines:
- local-address -> `neighbor X update-source <local-address>`
- passive -> `neighbor X passive`
- hold-time -> `neighbor X timers <keepalive> <hold-time>` (keepalive = hold/3)
- per-group/per-neighbor local-as -> `neighbor X local-as <asn>`

## #4287 — firewall family any filter loses the IPv6 arm - a family any discard fails open for v6 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (security fail-open)

A firewall filter authored under `family any` (Junos protocol-independent)
compiles as **IPv4-only**, silently losing its IPv6 arm. An operator who
writes a `family any` discard/deny filter expecting it to block BOTH v4 and
v6 gets a filter enforced on v4 only — v6 traffic is NOT filtered. That is a
**fail-open**: a deny that does not deny half the address families.

## Basis (source-verified, origin/master ~016167a15)

`compileFirewall` selects the destination map with
`dest := fw.FiltersInet` and only switches to `fw.FiltersInet6` when the
family token is literally `inet6`
(`pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go` ~183-185, ~236 `dest[filter.Name] = filter`).
Every other family (`any`, `mpls`, `ccc`, `vpls`, `bridge`) folds into the
single IPv4 pool. So a uniquely-named `family any filter drop6` is written
into `FiltersInet` only; the IPv6 forwarding path (`FilterInputV6` resolves
against `FiltersInet6`) never sees it.

`#3884` (`validateFirewallFilterFamilyCollisionsAST`) only rejects a same-NAME
filter reused across two non-inet6 families; it does NOT address a
**uniquely-named** `family any` filter losing its v6 arm — a distinct
mechanism.

## Repro

    set firewall family any filter drop6 term t then discard
    set interfaces ge-0-0-1 unit 0 family inet  filter input drop6
    set interfaces ge-0-0-1 unit 0 family inet6 filter input drop6

v4 is dropped; v6 passes.

## Fix

Expand a `family any` filter into BOTH `FiltersInet` and `FiltersInet6` so a
`family any` discard/deny does not fail-open for v6 (the fail-safe). Keep the
`#3884` cross-family same-name collision gate consistent (a `family any`
filter now also folds into the inet6 pool, so an `any`+`inet6` same-name reuse
must reject/warn at commit too).

## #4288 — VRRP authentication-type/authentication-key parsed but never enforced - false-security posture (VRRPv3 has no auth) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (false-security posture)

VRRP `authentication-type` / `authentication-key` are parsed, stored, and
copied into the running VRRP instance, but the packet build/receive path
never references them. The native dataplane is RFC 5798 VRRPv3, which
**removed** authentication entirely (VRRPv2 had it, v3 does not). xpf
correctly does not authenticate adverts — but it **silently accepts** an auth
config that does nothing. An operator believes mastership is protected by an
auth key when it is not: a rogue host on the segment can send higher-priority
adverts and hijack mastership.

## Basis (source-verified, origin/master ~016167a15)

- Parsed: `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go` ~721-730 (Keys-packed) and
  ~811-814 (child-node) set `vg.AuthType` / `vg.AuthKey`.
- Stored: `pkg/config/types_interfaces.go` ~111-112 (`AuthType`, `AuthKey`).
- Copied into the instance: `pkg/vrrp/vrrp.go` ~47-48.
- Never enforced: no reference to `AuthType`/`AuthKey` anywhere in the VRRP
  packet build/receive path (`pkg/vrrp/instance.go`) — the dataplane is
  VRRPv3.

## Fix (the honest one — do not silently accept dead security config)

Following the `accept-data` / `#4080` doctrine: **reject at strict commit**
(and warn on lenient load) that VRRP authentication is not supported/enforced
— VRRPv3 per RFC 5798 has no authentication. This prevents the operator from
being misled into a false-security posture. Do not silently accept auth config
that has no effect.

Labels: vsrx-parity, bug, vrrp, security

## #4289 — SNMP community clients source-IP restriction silently ignored (allow-all) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Summary (security: source-IP restriction silently ignored)

SNMP `community <c> clients <prefix>` scopes a community so it is queryable
only from the listed source prefixes. xpf parses only `authorization` under
`community` — there is no `clients` field — and the agent answers the
requesting `remoteAddr` unconditionally. An operator who scopes a community
to a management subnet gets an agent that answers EVERY source: the community
is queryable from anywhere on the network.

## Basis (source-verified, origin/master ~016167a15)

- `compileSNMP` parses only `authorization` under `community`
  (`pkg/config/compiler_system.go` ~874-897); `SNMPCommunity`
  (`pkg/config/types_system.go` ~492) has no `Clients` field.
- The agent resolves the community and serves with no source check
  (`pkg/snmp/agent.go` `handleV2cPacket` ~547-577; `remoteAddr` is read in
  `Start()` ~478 but never threaded into the handler).

## Fix (the security fix — enforce)

Parse `clients` prefixes (with the Junos `restrict` modifier), store them on
`SNMPCommunity`, thread the request source IP into the v2c handler, and
enforce longest-prefix-match against the source before serving (drop a query
from a source not permitted by the community's `clients` set). A community
with no `clients` stays allow-all (Junos default), so legit configs are
unaffected.

Labels: vsrx-parity, bug, snmp, security

## #4290 — NAT: then static-nat prefix-name <addr> compiles to an EMPTY translation target (silent broken static NAT) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## N-1 (fable-review-167): `then static-nat prefix-name <addr>` compiles to an EMPTY translation target

**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** High (probe-verified) · vsrx-parity

**Junos:** `then static-nat prefix-name <address-book-name>` is the named form
of static NAT — it installs a 1:1 translation identical to
`then static-nat prefix <ip>`, resolving the referenced global address-book
entry to its literal prefix.

**xpf bug:** the static-nat `then` target switch in the compiler recognizes only
`nptv6-prefix`, `prefix`, and `inet`. Any other target keyword — including
`prefix-name` — falls through, leaving `rule.Then = ""`. The rule commits with
no error and an **empty translation target** (probe: `STATIC rule "R1" then=""`),
a silently broken static NAT.

**Evidence:** `pkg/config/compiler_nat.go:2183-2228` (target switch, `rule.Then`
reset to "" each then-block, no `prefix-name` case). The static-nat `then` leaf
is free-form (`pkg/config/schema_security.go:495`, `children: nil`) so the typo'd
target commits clean.

**Asymmetry:** `match destination-address <name>` IS rejected
(`compiler_nat.go:348`), but the `then` target is not. The DNAT
`destination-address-name` resolver (`compiler_nat.go:1649`, #3229) is the
fix-pattern precedent.

**Repro:**
```
set security address-book global address INSIDEHOST 10.0.0.5/32
set security nat static rule-set S rule R1 then static-nat prefix-name INSIDEHOST
```

**Fix:**
1. Add a `prefix-name` case to the static-nat `then` switch that resolves the
   referenced global address-book entry to its literal prefix and assigns
   `rule.Then`.
2. Add a defensive EMPTY-TARGET guard: any `then static-nat` block that produced
   `rule.Then == ""` (unresolvable `prefix-name`, or an unhandled/typo'd target)
   is REJECTED at strict commit so no static-NAT rule commits with an empty
   target. Lenient (load / peer-sync) downgrades to a warning (#1960).
3. Add `prefix-name` to the schema description / completion hint.

## #4291 — NAT: port-overloading off / port-overloading-factor silently dropped (false src-port hardening) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## N-2 (fable-review-167): NAT `port-overloading` knobs silently dropped

**Severity:** Medium (security/compliance) · **Confidence:** High · vsrx-parity

`security nat source interface port-overloading off` (disable source-port reuse
across destinations — a src-port-uniqueness hardening knob) and
`security nat source pool <p> port-overloading-factor <n>` appear nowhere in
`pkg/config` (grep empty): neither is modeled in `setSchema` nor handled in the
compiler. Both commit with **no effect**, so `off` hardens NOTHING — the
operator believes source-port overloading is disabled when it is still on.

**Evidence:** no `port-overloading` token anywhere under `pkg/config`;
`schema_security.go` `nat source` node has no `interface` child and the source
`pool` container has no `port-overloading-factor` leaf.

**Immediate fix (Go-only, this PR):**
- Add typed `setSchema` leaves: an `interface` container under `nat source` with
  a `port-overloading` enum {off}, and a `port-overloading-factor` integer under
  `pool <name>`.
- Record the presence in typed config + emit an accept-with-advisory at commit
  ("accepted but not enforced; source-port overloading is always on") so `off`
  no longer implies false hardening. Mirrors the #2078/#4231 accepted-only
  advisory doctrine.

**Follow-up (larger, noted):** fully honoring the semantics
(unique-src-port-per-mapping when `off`; factor-scaled port allocation) requires
SNAT allocator work in `userspace-dp`. Tracked as a dataplane follow-up.

**Dedup note:** distinct from port-randomization-disable / deterministic /
address-persistent (all tracked-done).

## #4292 — NAT: translation-target routing-instance (then static-nat ... routing-instance, pool routing-instance) silently dropped [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## N-3 (fable-review-167): NAT-to-routing-instance translation TARGETS silently dropped

**Severity:** Low-Medium · **Confidence:** High (probe-verified) · vsrx-parity

The NAT translation-*target* routing-instance is silently dropped:
- `then static-nat inet routing-instance <ri>` and
  `then static-nat prefix <ip> routing-instance <ri>` — `StaticNATRule` has only
  `Then`, so the trailing `routing-instance <ri>` is discarded.
- destination `pool <p> { routing-instance <ri>; }` and the source-NAT pool
  `routing-instance` target — `NATPool` has no RI field.

All commit clean; the RI is dropped. The translated packet is NOT placed in the
target routing instance.

**Distinct from #3096:** the NAT `from/to` *scope* routing-instance (#3096) IS
implemented and verified working. The translation-*target* RI is a different
construct (where the translated packet is routed) and is unlisted.

**Fix (this PR — model + advisory):**
- Model the translation-target routing-instance leaf (source pool
  `routing-instance`; parse the static-nat `then ... routing-instance` and the
  DNAT pool `routing-instance` from the free-form nodes).
- Record it in typed config + emit an accept-with-advisory at commit
  (accepted-but-not-enforced; the translated packet stays in the ingress /
  default routing instance) so the dropped target is operator-visible. Mirrors
  the #2078/#4231 accepted-only advisory doctrine.

**Follow-up (larger, noted):** actually placing the translated packet in the
target RI is a cross-VRF-NAT dataplane change in `userspace-dp` (route the
post-translation packet against a different table). Tracked as a dataplane
follow-up.

**Dedup note:** NAT `from/to routing-instance` *scope* (#3096) works (verified
negative); the translation-*target* RI is a different construct and unlisted.

## #4296 — firewall: family-specific matches inside a family any filter are dual-compiled verbatim (imperfect v6 under-block on non-Junos configs) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

Follow-up to #4287 (F-1). A `family any` filter now correctly compiles into both the inet + inet6 pools (closing the v6 fail-open). Residual (non-blocking, flagged in the #4295 review): a `family any` filter carrying a FAMILY-SPECIFIC match (a v4 `source-address`, or a symbolic match that resolves via the ICMPv4 table for af=="any") is dual-compiled VERBATIM — the v6 pool gets a never-matching predicate.

Worst case is an UNDER-block (the v6 term never matches → the Rust matcher falls through to implicit ACCEPT — degrades to the pre-fix state), NEVER an over-block, so no legit v6 traffic is broken. These configs are also non-Junos (Junos disallows family-specific matches under `family any`) and only reachable via hierarchical/peer-sync parse.

Fix (completeness): under `family any`, SKIP or REJECT-at-commit a family-specific match (a match that only makes sense for one family) so the dual-compile doesn't silently under-block v6. Low priority — the fail-open is already closed; this is the imperfect-match residual.

## #4297 — IPsec: proposal-set standard|basic|compatible|suiteb-* unusable — common vSRX crypto shorthand cannot commit a working tunnel [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Finding (fable-review-167 V-1)

**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** High (probe-verified)

`security ike policy P proposal-set standard` (and the IPsec equivalent
`security ipsec policy P proposal-set standard`) is the standard vSRX
shorthand operators use to avoid hand-defining proposals. It expands to
Juniper-curated proposal sets (standard / basic / compatible /
suiteb-gcm-128 / suiteb-gcm-256).

## Current behavior

proposal-set appears nowhere in pkg/ (grep empty). The schema declares
only proposals / mode / pre-shared-key under ike/ipsec policy, so the
keyword is silently dropped by the compiler switch (unknown keys are
ignored). The policy then has no resolvable proposal:

- IPsec side hard-rejects with the misleading "no resolvable ipsec
  proposal" message (validateIPsecPolicyProposalReferencesStrict).
- IKE side leaves the chain unresolved (errIKEChainUnresolved) and the
  VPN is skipped at render.

Either way the tunnel cannot be built.

**Evidence:** pkg/config/schema_security.go ike policy + ipsec policy
children declare only proposals/mode/pre-shared-key; compileIKE /
compileIPsec (pkg/config/compiler_ipsec.go) have no proposal-set case.

## Fix

Implement proposal-set: expand each shorthand into its concrete IKE +
IPsec proposals per the Junos-documented sets, emitted to strongSwan.
(Alternative: reject at commit naming the manual-proposal alternative.)

**Dedup note:** F-040/F-161 cover explicit proposals[] list truncation;
the predefined proposal-set keyword is distinct.

## #4298 — IPsec: proposal protocol ah silently rendered as ESP with a fabricated cipher (crypto misrepresentation) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Finding (fable-review-167 V-2)

**Severity:** Medium (crypto correctness — operator gets a different
protocol AND a cipher they never specified) · **Confidence:** High

## Junos

security ipsec proposal P protocol ah selects AH (Authentication Header:
integrity only, NO encryption). swanctl expresses this via ah_proposals,
not esp_proposals.

## Current behavior (the security misrepresentation)

IPsecProposal.Protocol is captured (compiler_ipsec.go) but never
consulted. buildESPProposal (pkg/ipsec/ike.go) ignores it and defaults
empty encryption to aes256, and renderConfig (pkg/ipsec/policy.go) always
emits esp_proposals. No ah_proposals code exists. So:

    set security ipsec proposal AHPROP protocol ah
    set security ipsec proposal AHPROP authentication-algorithm hmac-sha-256-128

renders as esp_proposals = aes256-sha256 — the operator asked for AH
(integrity only) and silently got ESP with a made-up aes256 cipher.

## Fix

Emit ah_proposals (integrity + optional DH, no cipher) when
Protocol == "ah", OR reject AH at commit with a clear message. NEVER
silently substitute ESP + fabricate a cipher.

**Dedup note:** F-024 (ESP dangling-proposal fallback) is unrelated.

## #4303 — system syslog host/file sub-statements misparsed into bogus facility/severity pairs (hb167 S-1) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (hb167 finding S-1)

The system-syslog compiler treats *every* non-`allow-duplicates` child of a
`host`/`file`/`user` node as a `<facility> <severity>` pair. Any real
Junos host/file sub-statement (`source-address`, `port`, `match`,
`structured-data`, `explicit-priority`, `log-prefix`, `archive`, ...) is
therefore captured as a garbage facility/severity entry that pollutes the
compiled filter.

**File:line:** `pkg/config/compiler_system.go` syslog loop (`host`/`file`/`user`
`namedInstances` blocks, ~L263-305) — `len(prop.Keys) >= 2` fallback appends
`SyslogFacility{Facility: prop.Keys[0], Severity: prop.Keys[1]}` unconditionally.
Consumer `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go` `applySystemSyslog` uses
`host.Facilities[0].Facility` for `c.Facility`.

**Repro (verified):** compiling

    set system syslog host 10.0.0.5 source-address 10.0.1.1
    set system syslog host 10.0.0.5 any warning
    set system syslog host 10.0.0.5 port 5514

yields `Facilities = [{source-address 10.0.1.1} {any warning} {port 5514}]`.
`applySystemSyslog` then sets the remote client's facility from the FIRST
entry -> `ParseFacility("source-address")` -> garbage facility for all
forwarded messages. Separately, the strict commit-check REJECTS
`source-address 10.0.1.1` because the severity enum does not accept an IP.

**Fix:** switch on the known host/file/user sub-keywords before the
facility/severity fallback; capture `source-address`/`port` into typed fields
and wire them into the syslog client; add the sub-keywords to the schema so a
valid config commits.

**Labels:** vsrx-parity, bug, system, logging

## #4304 — custom system login class <name> hard-rejected at commit (blocks valid vSRX RBAC config) (hb167 S-2) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (hb167 finding S-2)

Login classes are a hard-coded built-in set; the schema has no `login class`
node, and the `login user <n> class <c>` leaf is enum-validated against the
built-ins only. A real vSRX config that defines a custom RBAC class and
assigns a user to it is HARD-REJECTED at commit — which blocks the WHOLE
config from committing.

**File:line:**
- `pkg/config/types_system.go` `ValidLoginClasses()` (~L580) + fixed
  `LoginClassPermissions` map.
- `pkg/config/schema_system.go` `class` leaf (~L143-146):
  `validator: ValidateEnum(ValidLoginClasses())`.
- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go` login loop (~L85-113): a `class <name> {...}`
  definition is silently ignored (accepted-inert).

**Repro (verified):** compiling

    set system login class noc-admin permissions all
    set system login user bob class noc-admin

passes `CompileConfig` but `SchemaValidate` REJECTS with
`system login user bob class: invalid value "noc-admin"`.

**Fix (accept-with-advisory, do NOT hard-reject a valid config):** parse
`login class <name>` (permissions/allow-commands/deny-commands/idle-timeout),
feed the defined names into the accepted set (tree-aware `class` validator),
map the Junos `permissions` tokens to xpf's coarse permission model where
feasible, wire the custom class into the runtime RBAC, and emit a compile
advisory noting which permissions map vs. are recognized-but-not-fully-enforced.

**Labels:** vsrx-parity, bug, system

## #4305 — SSH hardening knobs (ciphers/macs/connection-limit/client-alive-*/protocol-version) silently inert (hb167 S-4) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (hb167 finding S-4)

The SSH compiler reads only `root-login` and `key-exchange`. The standard
sshd-hardening knobs commit clean (unknown-key accepted-inert) and never
reach the `sshd_config.d/xpf.conf` drop-in, so the box keeps base-image
cipher/MAC defaults even when the operator configured hardened algorithms.

**File:line:**
- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go` SSH service block (~L321-333) — only
  `root-login` + `key-exchange` are read.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go` `buildSSHDConfig` (~L1167) — renders only
  `PermitRootLogin` + `KexAlgorithms`.

**Affected knobs:** `ciphers`, `macs`, `connection-limit`,
`client-alive-count-max`, `client-alive-interval`, `protocol-version`.

**Fix:** parse these into `SSHServiceConfig` and render `Ciphers`/`MACs`/
`MaxStartups`/`ClientAliveCountMax`/`ClientAliveInterval` into the existing
drop-in (sshd validates spellings at reload). `protocol-version` is
accept-with-advisory (sshd is v2-only; a non-v2 value gets an advisory, v2 is
a no-op).

## #4307 — RA reachable-time and retransmit-timer silently dropped (fable-review-167 I-2) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-167, I-2)

Junos `protocols router-advertisement interface <if>` accepts
`reachable-time` and `retransmit-timer`, two standard RFC 4861 §4.2
Router Advertisement fields. Neither leaf exists in the RA interface
schema nor in `RAInterfaceConfig`, and the sender never sets them, so
both go on the wire as 0 ("unspecified"). Operators cannot tune host
neighbor-cache / retransmit behavior via RA.

## Evidence (file:line, origin/master dd5cdbcf1)

- Schema: `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:435` (router-advertisement
  interface children) declares neither leaf.
- Type: `pkg/config/types_routing.go:216` `RAInterfaceConfig` has no
  ReachableTime / RetransmitTimer.
- Compiler: `pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:700` compileRouterAdvertisement
  never parses them.
- Sender: `pkg/ra/sender.go:698` builds `ndp.RouterAdvertisement` without
  ReachableTime / RetransmitTimer, though `github.com/mdlayher/ndp`
  (message.go:258-259) supports both (marshalled as ms on the wire).

## Fix

Implement. Add both as typed millisecond leaves (RFC 4861 §4.2 32-bit
fields, 0 = unspecified) to the schema + `RAInterfaceConfig`, compile
them, and set `ra.ReachableTime` / `ra.RetransmitTimer` on the sent RA.

## Labels
vsrx-parity, bug, ra

## #4308 — Interface ARP/addressing knobs silently dropped: unnumbered-address, gratuitous-arp-reply, no-gratuitous-arp-request, targeted-broadcast, native-vlan-id (fable-review-167 I-3) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-167, I-3)

Five common Junos interface knobs are accepted by the permissive parser
but never modeled or compiled, so they silently vanish at commit:

- `family inet unnumbered-address <donor>` (borrow another unit's
  address on a P2P/tunnel interface) — Medium: an unnumbered interface
  gets NO address, link unusable.
- `gratuitous-arp-reply` / `no-gratuitous-arp-request` (interface-level).
- `family inet targeted-broadcast`.
- `native-vlan-id <id>` (untagged-to-VLAN assignment on a trunk).

## Evidence (file:line, origin/master dd5cdbcf1)

- Schema: `pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go:27` (physical) and the
  `family inet` block declare none of these leaves.
- grep: none appear in `pkg/config` or `pkg/networkd`.

## Fix

Model each as a typed leaf so it stops silently vanishing. Full
enforcement needs design/cluster work (unnumbered-address borrow in
networkd; native-vlan-id folds into the QinQ tagging pipeline #2354; the
ARP/targeted-broadcast knobs map to per-interface sysctls / dataplane
behavior), so accept-with-advisory (accepted-but-not-enforced,
#2078-style) at commit, and enforce in follow-ups. At minimum the leaves
must be typed + surface an operator-visible advisory instead of being
silently dropped.

## Labels
vsrx-parity, bug, interfaces

## #4309 — DHCP relay overrides limited to always-broadcast; forward-only, relay-agent-option (option-82), maximum-hop-count silently dropped (fable-review-167 I-4) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

## Basis (fable-review-167, I-4)

The dhcp-relay schema models only `server-group` / `group` /
`overrides { always-broadcast }`. Three standard relay override knobs
are silently dropped:

- `maximum-hop-count <n>` — the relay hop limit (RFC 1542 §4.1.1 loop
  protection). xpf hardcodes 16.
- `forward-only` — forward without retaining per-client relay state.
- `relay-agent-option` — Option 82 (Relay Agent Information) control.

## Evidence (file:line, origin/master dd5cdbcf1)

- Schema: `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:614` overrides children =
  `always-broadcast` only.
- Compiler: `pkg/config/compiler_services.go:1501` compileDHCPRelay
  reads only `always-broadcast`.
- Relay: `pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go:877` hardcodes the hop limit at 16;
  `pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go:~750` always inserts Option 82 (circuit-id)
  unconditionally.

## Fix

- `maximum-hop-count`: implement — make the hardcoded hop limit
  configurable and enforce/count drops.
- `relay-agent-option`: accept-with-advisory — xpf always inserts
  Option 82 (circuit-id); the knob is accepted and matches default
  behavior.
- `forward-only`: accept-with-advisory — the xpf relay already forwards
  statelessly (no persistent per-client binding); accepted, matches
  default behavior.

## Labels
vsrx-parity, bug, dhcp

## #4313 — config schema is opt-in — unmodeled Junos leaves commit clean and are silently inert (X-1 cross-cutting root cause) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-06)

fable-review-167 X-1 (cross-cutting ROOT CAUSE). CONFIRMED at HEAD: `pkg/config/schema_walk.go:249-254` resolves an unmodeled Junos keyword to a nil schema child and returns nil with NO error — the opt-in gate — so any unmodeled leaf commits clean, gets no ?-help, and is silently dropped by the compiler. The closed-world reject discipline exists only at the MODIFIER level (`typedLeafErrorf "unknown modifier"` at schema_walk.go:414/418/422/438/560/563), never as a schema-wide default (the 448-450 comment notes the keyword-level gate is opt-in).

This mechanism produces the MAJORITY of the silently-inert parity findings across sections 7-13 (NAT/IPsec/Routing/Interfaces/System/CLI/Firewall) — touching security/reachability subtrees (security ipsec, security nat then, snmp community, protocols ospf/bgp, interfaces family).

**The concrete per-domain gaps are being driven separately** (this campaign filed+fixed N-1/2/3, V-1..5, R-1/2, I-1/2/3/4, S-1..5, F-1..3 with typed leaves + accept-with-advisory or reject-at-commit). This umbrella is the DOCTRINE decision: adopt a PER-SUBTREE closed-world flag so an unmodeled keyword under a vetted subtree RAISES a typedLeafErrorf at strict commit instead of silently dropping?

A BLANKET flip is INFEASIBLE (breaks the deliberate accept-with-advisory knobs #2078/#4231). Design = umbrella + per-domain allowlist children:
- Flip HIGH-RISK security/reachability subtrees to reject-unknown-keyword-at-strict-commit + lenient-warn on load (#1960/#3307/#3318), gated by an allowlist.
- Retain accept-with-advisory (#2078/#4231) for deliberately-lenient knobs.
- Mechanism: extend walkSchemaNode so a per-subtree closed-world flag makes childSchema==nil raise typedLeafErrorf instead of returning nil.

Needs a /research design pass (which subtrees to flip; a per-subtree Junos-leaf completeness matrix to avoid false-rejecting a valid-but-unmodeled config — the #4191-class false-reject risk). PLAN-DEFER candidate: drive the concrete per-domain leaves first (this campaign), THEN flip subtrees to closed-world only once each is leaf-complete.

Provenance: pkg/config/schema_walk.go:249-254 + the modifier reject sites 414/418/422/438/560/563 + the 448-450 opt-in comment.

## #4315 — CoS: traffic-control-profiles + output-traffic-control-profile unmodeled — hierarchical shaping binding silently applies zero shaping [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-05)

fable-review-167 finding F-2 (Medium severity; High confidence — grep: 0
non-test hits).

The standard Junos hierarchical shaping binding is unmodeled:

    class-of-service {
        traffic-control-profiles <tcp> {
            shaping-rate <rate>;
            guaranteed-rate <rate>;
            scheduler-map <map>;
            delay-buffer-rate <rate>;
        }
        interfaces <if> {
            unit N { output-traffic-control-profile <tcp>; }
        }
    }

xpf supports only the flat `class-of-service interfaces <if> {
scheduler-map; shaping-rate; }` binding (pkg/config/schema_cos.go:118-148).
An operator who conditions shaping via a traffic-control-profile gets a
CLEAN commit and ZERO shaping — the `output-traffic-control-profile`
token is silently dropped (SchemaValidate does not reject unknown
keywords — schema_walk.go:249-254 — and no compiler reads it), and the
TCP body never reaches the dataplane. This is the make-or-break: an
operator must not believe shaping is applied when it is not.

Fix:
- Model `traffic-control-profiles <n>` in setSchema (typed leaves:
  shaping-rate, guaranteed-rate, scheduler-map, delay-buffer-rate) and
  `output-traffic-control-profile <n>` at the interface-unit and
  interface level; capture them in ClassOfServiceConfig
  (pkg/config/types_cos.go).
- WIRE the bounded half: resolve `output-traffic-control-profile` ->
  the referenced TCP's `shaping-rate` + `scheduler-map` into the
  existing per-unit shaper plumbing (CoSInterfaceUnit.ShapingRateBytes /
  SchedulerMap, compiler_class_of_service.go), so shaping ACTUALLY
  applies.
- guaranteed-rate / delay-buffer-rate have no per-unit dataplane
  consumer today -> accept-with-advisory (accepted-but-not-enforced),
  and an undefined TCP reference warns at commit.

*(truncated — 44 lines total)*

## #4323 — userspace-dp: Stage-11 IPsec passthrough — gate NEW inbound IKE against per-zone host-inbound (Option B, deferred hardening from #3616) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

Follow-up to #3616 (CLOSED via #4322, Option A). The converged 3-way /research plan (docs/research/3616-ipsec-host-inbound/plan.md, on master) RATIFIED the ESP/AH passthrough exemption as correct-by-design (Option A shipped: document + pin local_ifindex=0 to avoid the R4 GRE-channel mis-delivery). This issue tracks the DEFERRED Option-B hardening.

Option B: at Stage 11 (stage_ipsec_passthrough_check), add a SEPARATE host_inbound_admits_iface gate for NEW inbound IKE (and inner-ESP) BEFORE the LocalDelivery reinject — so a per-zone host-inbound policy that omits `ike` drops an unsolicited inbound IKE to self, while ESP/AH established/related traffic still passes.

Why deferred (from the converged plan):
- Must reproduce the kernel chain's `ct established,related accept`-FIRST ordering (AGY M2) — else it drops return/established IKE and breaks tunnels.
- Must resolve the LOGICAL ingress zone + the GRE-inner ingress zone (Codex M6), not the physical ifindex.
- Do NOT populate local_ifindex in the routing decision (R4: slow_path.rs:213-224 diverts LocalDelivery+local_ifindex>0 into the GRE local_tunnel_deliveries channel → mis-delivers IPsec-to-self). The gate is a separate admit check, not a routing-decision field change.
- Config-gated exposure is low (default host-inbound typically permits ike), so this is hardening not a live bug.

Validation when driven: a tunnel on a zone listing `ike` still establishes; a DNAT-to-self IKE on a zone OMITTING `ike` drops; established/return IKE is never dropped. A per-zone host-inbound IPsec deny cluster smoke belongs here.

Terminal: PLAN-DEFER (recorded), driveable when the established-first ordering + logical/GRE-inner zone resolution is specced. Plan doc: docs/research/3616-ipsec-host-inbound/plan.md.

## #4328 — cli/grpc: show interfaces reth0 / detail / extensive fail for bondless reth — only 'terse' is reth-aware [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

Operator-directed (fable-review-168): every operational `show interfaces` variant EXCEPT `terse` fails to find a bondless reth. The reth CONFIG + FORWARDING are correct (addresses programmed, forwarding verified live on the loss cluster) — the break is operational VISIBILITY.

Reproduced live + at HEAD (origin/master ba4553bfa):
| Command | Result | vSRX |
|---|---|---|
| `show interfaces terse reth0` | works (synthesizes reth0.50/.80, `aenet --> reth0.50` on members) | shows reth |
| `show interfaces reth0` | `Physical interface: reth0, Not present` | full detail |
| `show interfaces reth0.50` | `reth0, Not present` | unit detail |
| `show interfaces reth0 detail` | empty | detail |
| `show interfaces reth0 extensive` | `interface extensive not found` | extensive |

Secondary: `show interfaces ge-0-0-2 detail` shows the reth virtual MAC + a bare ge-0-0-2.0 but does NOT list the reth0.50/.80 logical units or say the member belongs to reth0 (terse DOES show `aenet --> reth0.50`; detail does not).

## Root cause (file:line, HEAD)
`cfg.RethToPhysical()` / the `physToReth` reverse map is called in EXACTLY ONE place — the terse handler. Every other show path does a raw kernel-netdev lookup that can't succeed for a bondless reth (no kernel link named `reth0`):
- `pkg/cli/cli_show_interfaces.go` — `showInterfacesTerse()` (:544) builds `physToReth`/`rethToPhys := cfg.RethToPhysical()` (:552-553) — the ONLY reth-aware path. `showInterfaces()` summary (~:180) → `netlink.LinkByName` fails → `"Physical interface: %s, Not present"` (:189), no RethToPhysical. `showInterfacesDetail(filterName)` (:421) iterates `netlink.LinkList()` keeping `attrs.Name==filterName` — no `reth0` link → empty. `showInterfacesExtensiveFiltered()` (:859) same.
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_interfaces.go` mirrors it: RethToPhysical only in the terse handler (:382-383); detail prints the same "Not present" (:150). So the remote `cli` + any gRPC text consumer hit the same wall.
- #3460 (closed June) fixed the STRUCTURED `GetInterfaces` RPC to resolve kernel ifnames — a DIFFERENT surface; it did not touch the text detail/extensive/summary paths.

## Fix (copy existing working logic, not new machinery)
1. In `showInterfaces` (summary) + `showInterfacesDetail`/`…Extensive` (CLI AND the gRPC twins): before the raw netdev lookup, build `physToReth`/`rethToPhys := cfg.RethToPhysical()`. When the requested name is a reth (in rethToPhys), render it as a logical aggregate over its resolved physical member — counters/MAC/link-state from the member netdev, addresses/units from `cfg.Interfaces[reth].Units`. When the name is a reth MEMBER, add the `aenet --> reth<N>.<unit>` lines (terse does this at :702 / gRPC :572) + list the reth logical units.
2. Fold the four surfaces (CLI summary/detail/extensive + gRPC) through a SINGLE reth-resolution helper so terse + detail can't drift again.
3. Regression test: a 2-reth cluster config; assert `show interfaces reth0`, `reth0.0`, `reth0 detail` are non-empty + name the physical member (none exists today — the gap survived because only terse is covered).

Go-only (pkg/cli + pkg/grpcapi), no dataplane change.

## #4329 — cluster: flat vSRX reth config mis-resolves members on node 1 — CompileConfigForNode never stamps Cluster.NodeID from the runtime node-id [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

Operator-directed (fable-review-169): a canonical vSRX chassis-cluster config dropped into xpf as-is silently binds every reth to the NODE-0 physical member on NODE 1 (the secondary) → reth breaks on the secondary. vSRX encodes node ownership in the FPC number (`ge-0/0/N`=node 0/fpc 0, `ge-7/0/N`=node 1/fpc 7) and runs the SAME flat config on both nodes; xpf mis-resolves it.

## Reproduction (real parser+compiler, HEAD ba4553bfa)
CompileConfigForNode per node, RethToPhysical:
- FLAT node0 → reth0:ge-0/0/0 ✓
- **FLAT node1 → reth0:ge-0/0/0 ✗ WRONG (must be ge-7/0/0)**
- GROUPS node0/node1 → ✓/✓ (the xpf loss form with `groups node0/node1` + `apply-groups ${node}` works — each node's expanded config has a single candidate)
- `xpfd check-config -node-id {0,1}` PASSES the flat form on both → mis-resolution is SILENT (no commit error/warning).
- Confirm fix: FLAT + `chassis cluster node 1` leaf → node1 → ge-7/0/0 ✓. So the resolver is correct when Cluster.NodeID is right; the bug is Cluster.NodeID is wrong for a leaf-less flat config.

## Root cause (file:line)
1. `Config.RethToPhysical()` (pkg/config/types.go:64) scores each candidate member by `SlotToNodeID(InterfaceSlot(name)) == c.Chassis.Cluster.NodeID` (local→2, remote→0).
2. But `Cluster.NodeID` is populated ONLY from the config leaf `chassis cluster node <id>` (compiler_system.go:1566, guarded by NodeIDSet). Canonical vSRX has NO such leaf → `Cluster.NodeID` defaults to 0 on BOTH nodes.
3. `CompileConfigForNode(tree, nodeID)` → `compileConfigForNodeWithOpts` uses `nodeID` ONLY to set the `${node}` group-expansion var, NOT the compiled cluster identity. `/etc/xpf/node-id` → Store.SetNodeID → `${node}` expansion only (store.go:239-244).
4. `crossCheckNodeID` (store.go:293-314) explicitly ALLOWS a leaf-less config on a node-1 box.
5. With localNodeID==0 on node 1, both members score by the fallback (score==bestScore && Name<prev) → alphabetical → ge-0/0/0 wins on both.

Blast radius: RethToPhysical/ResolveReth drive the whole reth runtime → all target ge-0/0/0 on node 1: daemon_ha_vip.go:309,373,606 (VIP placement), daemon_dhcp.go:225, daemon_ra.go:94, daemon_ddns_surface_a.go:368, daemon_ipmon.go:141, daemon_rpm.go:351, daemon_ha.go:790,1341.

## Fix (small, localized)
1. In `compileConfigForNodeWithOpts`: when `nodeID >= 0` AND the config carries no explicit `chassis cluster node` leaf (`!NodeIDSet`), stamp `cfg.Chassis.Cluster.NodeID = nodeID` (creating Cluster if absent). This is the runtime SSOT identity (/etc/xpf/node-id / -node-id flag) that Store.compileTree already threads. Then RethToPhysical scores the local member correctly on both nodes → the flat vSRX form is a drop-in.
2. Regression test: the flat two-member form resolves reth0→ge-0/0/0 on node 0 AND reth0→ge-7/0/0 on node 1 (none exists — TestRethToPhysical_PrefersLocalClusterMember only exercises the already-set-NodeID case).
3. Keep the alphabetical tiebreak ONLY as a last resort for a genuinely ambiguous single-node config; it must NEVER decide between two nodes' members.

Go-only (pkg/config compiler). Touches reth resolution → HA-relevant (VIP/HA-group placement) → test-failover before merge.

## #4332 — wireguard: cookie-reply budget is global-per-tunnel, not per-source — a valid-mac1 flood can budget-suppress a legit peer's first cookie challenge [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

Follow-up to #4094 (PR-A #4330). The responder cookie-reply budget (COOKIE_REPLY_BUDGET_PER_WINDOW=40/window) is GLOBAL per-tunnel, not per-source like wireguard-go's per-source token bucket. Under a determined valid-MAC1 flood (an attacker who knows our static public key), a legit peer's FIRST cookie challenge can be budget-suppressed, adding establishment latency across windows.

Mitigated in PR-A: one budgeted cookie is enough (a MAC2-primed peer bypasses the budget on retry — verify_initiation_mac2 runs before the budget check), and the alternative (unbounded replies) makes the reply path itself a de-amplification sink. The PRIMARY CPU-DoS (skip the Noise handshake until a valid MAC2) is fully closed by #4330.

Hardening (this issue): a per-SOURCE reply rate-limit (a small token-bucket keyed by src ip:port, mirror wireguard-go device/cookie.go's RateLimiter) so a flood from one source can't starve a legit peer's cookie challenge from another source. PLAN-DEFER — not a blocker (the primary DoS is closed); a bounded hardening.

## #4338 — config: filter term "source-address 0/0" + except source-prefix-list over-strict — Junos ACCEPTS this lockdown idiom (drop-in blocker, #3359) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

The canonical "match any EXCEPT the management hosts, then reject" idiom: `source-address { 0.0.0.0/0; } source-prefix-list { management-hosts except; }`. Junos ACCEPTS this. xpf's #3359 mutual-exclusion (a positive source-address + an except source-prefix-list are mutually exclusive) is STRICTER than Junos and blocks a common lockdown pattern — AND the error wrongly claims "Junos rejects this" (false for the 0/0+except shape). Present on both inet+inet6 mgmt filters. FIX: allow a 0/0 (any) positive match combined with an except-prefix-list (they compose: match all, subtract the except set), or at minimum stop asserting Junos rejects it. (fable-review-170 B-8)

## #4339 — nat: NPTv6 single-rule rule-set flagged as overlapping ITSELF — blocks any NPTv6 inbound mapping (drop-in blocker) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

A rule-set with a SINGLE rule (`destination 2602:fd41:70::/48 → nptv6-prefix 2001:559:8585::/48`) is rejected: "rule map-v6-neutral overlaps rule-set NPTv6-INBOUND rule map-v6-neutral" — it overlaps ITSELF. NPTv6 is inherently bidirectional; the overlap detector compares the rule's mapping against its OWN reverse and reports a self-overlap. Blocks ANY NPTv6 inbound mapping. FIX: exclude a rule from its own overlap check (skip self-comparison), and/or model NPTv6 bidirectionality so a rule + its reverse aren't treated as two overlapping rules. (fable-review-170 B-10)

## #4340 — config: address-book object names cannot contain "/" — blocks prefix-named objects in real vSRX configs (drop-in blocker, 194 objects) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

fable-review-170 B-2 (THE biggest drop-in blocker). A real vSRX config names address objects by their prefix — the near-universal operator convention: `net4_sfmix_72.52.96.201/32`, `net_10.0.0.0/8`, `net_2001:559:8585:200::/64`. xpf reserves "/" and HARD-REJECTS every such name ("address-book entry name ... must not contain '/'"). The reviewed config has 194 such objects (v4+v6), and every policy/NAT/filter REFERENCE must be renamed in lockstep → a mechanical drop-in is impossible (config-wide find-and-replace, not a localized edit). This hits essentially EVERY real vSRX config that names objects by prefix.

FIX (xpf should change): allow "/" in address-object NAMES — the "/" is only a display identifier, not a path/structural token. Map it to a safe internal encoding at parse (or simply permit it in the name validator if nothing downstream treats the name as a path). ## #4342 — daemon: default-policy action/log change does not invalidate live default-permit sessions (codex-164 H01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

codex-review-164 H01. The #4234 session-invalidation clears NAMED modified/deleted policies, but a change to the DEFAULT policy (permit-all→deny-all, or default-policy-log flip) does NOT clear existing default-permit sessions. Default-permit flows install a session stamped policy_id=DefaultPolicySentinelID (0xFFFFFFFF, pkg/dataplane/types.go:438); the commit-time invalidators (deletedPolicyRuntimeIDs/changedPolicyRuntimeIDs in pkg/daemon/daemon_policy_invalidate.go) diff only PolicyIDsByStableKey (configured policies, never emits 0xFFFFFFFF). So a default permit→deny commit leaves existing default-permit sessions forwarding with stale intent until idle timeout. NOT the H02 id-0 fail-safe (sentinel is 0xFFFFFFFF, safe to sweep — cannot alias host-inbound/fabric/tunnel/synced sessions which carry 0). FIX: add defaultPolicyChanged(old,new) comparing Security.DefaultPolicy + DefaultPolicyLogSessionInit/Close; when it changes, feed {DefaultPolicySentinelID} into clearSessionsForPolicyIDs (new DeleteReasonDefaultPolicyChanged) so default-permit sessions are dropped at commit + HA-delete-synced, mirroring the named-policy clear. Wire at the same apply site under d.applySem. An action tightening (permit→deny) clears unconditionally; a log-only flip may gate on policy-rematch. + a fail-on-revert test. HA-touching (delete-sync) → test-failover.

## #4343 — daemon: policy-rematch ignores scheduler-binding changes though scheduler-inactive is a fail-closed enforcement predicate (codex-164 H03) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

codex-review-164 H03. policyMatchOrActionChanged (pkg/daemon/daemon_policy_invalidate.go:329-350) lists scheduler-name among 'non-verdict attributes' that don't affect a live session — but that premise is WRONG: policyRuleInactive (pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies.go:1295-1303) is FAIL-CLOSED and stamps a policy Inactive when its scheduler is inactive → scheduler active↔inactive IS an enforcement predicate. So a commit that flips a policy's scheduler binding (or the scheduler's active window) does NOT re-eval that policy's live sessions under policy-rematch → a policy that just went inactive keeps forwarding its established sessions. FIX: include a scheduler-binding change (SchedulerName + whether the referenced scheduler is active/inactive) in changedPolicyRuntimeIDs' change detection, gated on policy-rematch, so a scheduler active→inactive transition clears the policy's sessions. + a fail-on-revert test. HA-touching → test-failover.

## #4348 — config: a quoted value exactly "inactive:" is silently truncated — gate the inactive: marker on TokenIdentifier not TokenString (#4335 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-06)

Follow-up to #4335 (#4347). parseKeys flattens TokenString + TokenIdentifier into one []string, so a QUOTED value exactly equal to `inactive:` (e.g. `description "inactive:";`) is indistinguishable from a bare deactivation marker and gets truncated → silent value loss. This is PRE-EXISTING (the leading `if keys[0] == inactiveMarker` handler has the same behavior on a quoted `"inactive:"`), extended by #4347 to inline position. Near-zero real-world impact (no Junos field's value is the bare/quoted token `inactive:`). FIX (both the leading AND inline handlers in parser.go parseStatement): only treat a bare TokenIdentifier `inactive:` as a deactivation marker, never a TokenString (quoted) value. Requires parseKeys/the token model to preserve the string-vs-identifier distinction at the marker-check site (or a parallel token-kind slice). Low priority, cheap.

## #4360 — cluster HA: BulkSync re-drive gate uses the shared bulkEverCompleted flag — a small inbound bulk completing first suppresses the outbound re-drive (#4090 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

Non-blocking follow-up from the #4090 (#4359) review. The survivor-fabric re-drive gate is `!bulkEverCompleted.Load()`, but `bulkEverCompleted` is a SINGLE flag set by EITHER an inbound BulkEnd (peer→us) OR an outbound BulkAck (us→peer). So the gate can close early: if the peer's (small) inbound bulk completes before OUR (larger) outbound bulk strands mid-stream, the outbound re-drive is suppressed and the peer keeps an incomplete view of our sessions. NOT introduced by #4090 — it's the same flag handleNewConnection already uses for coldStart, and #4090 is strictly better than the pre-PR baseline (no re-drive at all). FIX: gate the outbound re-drive on a DEDICATED outbound-bulk-acked flag (separate from the inbound-bulk-done flag) so an outbound strand re-drives independently of the inbound bulk's completion. Also (advisory #2, narrower): a double-flap onto a different fabric (fabric0 drops→re-drive on fabric1, fabric0 reconnects, fabric1 drops mid-re-drive) leaves the CAS still-true so no fresh re-drive on the surviving fabric0 — a narrow window, still strictly better than baseline; consider re-arming the re-drive on the new survivor. Both are dual-fabric-harness-dependent to validate (plan-deferred-research class).

## #4370 — cluster: session-sync auth handshake runs synchronously in acceptLoop (10s timeout can serially stall accepts) — shorten timeout or move to per-conn goroutine (#4369 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

Non-blocking LOW advisory from the #4369 (#4107-F23) review. handleNewConnection runs performSyncHandshake INLINE in the accept path, so a stalled/slow connection holds the accept loop up to syncHandshakeTimeout (10s). This MIRRORS the pre-existing synchronous handler (doBulkSync already blocks it) + only engages when keyed, but an active control-link attacker could serially stall accepts (10s each). FIX (either): (a) shorten syncHandshakeTimeout to 2-3s (the keyed↔keyed handshake completes in ms; 10s is only the absent-peer safety bound), OR (b) move the handshake into the per-connection goroutine so a stalled handshake doesn't block accepting OTHER connections. LOW — the control link is a direct-cable/trusted segment (now PSK-gated by #4357/#4369), and the pre-existing doBulkSync has the same property. Cheap hardening.

## #4376 — vrrp: dual-stack equal-priority tie-break is family-split -> both nodes step down -> permanent no-master oscillation (RG outage) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

**Finding H-2 (severity high).**

CONFIRMED on current master f1c298e0f. pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1145-1162 (handleMasterRx equal-priority tie-break) selects the local compare address from the ARRIVING advert's family: v4 advert compares peer src vs getLocalIP() (L1151-1152, lowest v4), v6 advert compares peer src vs getLocalIPv6() (L1153-1154, link-local). A single instance is genuinely dual-stack: CollectRethInstances (vrrp.go:158/164) puts all of a unit's v4+v6 addresses on one instance, and sendAdvert (instance.go:1247-1274) emits BOTH a v4 advert (from getLocalIP) and a v6 advert (from getLocalIPv6/link-local) from two unrelated sources. Both adverts land on the same rxCh (receiver L775, receiverIPv6 L840) and are processed by handleMasterRx while MASTER. Two equal-priority nodes with DISAGREEING v4 vs v6 orderings (A: higher v4/lower LL; B: lower v4/higher LL): A steps down on B's v6 advert while B steps down on A's v4

**Evidence (file:line on current master):** pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1145-1162 (family-split tie-break: v4->getLocalIP L1151-1152, v6->getLocalIPv6 L1153-1154, nil-local falls through to stay-MASTER); dual-stack both-family send at instance.go:1247-1274; both families share rxCh at instance.go:775 and 840, dispatched via handleMasterRx at 672-673; equal-priority reachability at pkg/cluster/group_state.go:207-219; prior tie-break PRs left family logic untouched per docs/issues/pr-history.md:38983 and 43417.

**Fix:** In handleMasterRx (pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1145-1162) make the equal-priority tie-break family-consistent instead of keying on the arriving advert's family. For a dual-stack or v4-bearing instance run the MASTER-MASTER collision resolver ONLY on v4 adverts using getLocalIP() and ignore v6-family adverts for the tie-break (both nodes then decide off the same v4 ordering, symmetric); use link-local getLocalIPv6 only for v6-only instances. Two v6 hosts mapped to the same snat_v4 (single-address pool, or round-robin colliding on one address) that share a source port or ICMP echo identifier produce an identical reverse tuple -> the second install collides and replies are mis-associated. This is the exact reverse-collisio

**Evidence (file:line on current master):** userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs:396-397 (rewrite_src_port/rewrite_dst_port = None); userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs:385-386 (allocate_v4_source bare round-robin fetch_add, no id/port); userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs:127 (pool_v4: Vec<Ipv4Addr>); userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:2524 (Nat64ReverseInfo stores only orig_src_v6/orig_dst_v6 — reverse key uses untranslated port/id). Dedup-disproving: #2562 title = NAT64 non-first fragment frag-id->SNAT cache (distinct); #4074/#4088 CLOSED = pool-SNAT NAT4

**Fix:** Give NAT64 a flow-keyed source allocator that guarantees (snat_v4, id/port) uniqueness, reusing the pool-SNAT allocate_translation machinery (#4074/#4088): translate the ICMP echo Identifier (the sharpest, most-likely collision) and the TCP/UDP source port during v6->v4 translation, store the translated id/port in Nat64ReverseInfo, and reverse-translate on the v4->v6 path (with L4/ICMP checksum recompute). Handle id==0 per the #4088 flowless-classification fix. Bounded fallback if the full BIB is scoped out: enforce/document a 1:1-sized pool at commit time and reject multi-client-per-snat_v4. ## #4386 — cluster: cold-boot split-brain — heartbeat 'peer never seen' path promotes after 500ms, skipping the 30s config-apply grace -> dual-primary on simultaneous boot [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

From opus-review-171 (H-3, base f1c298e0f; HIGH, Medium confidence — the triage Workflow agent failed on a StructuredOutput cap, so this is a manual file; VERIFY the file:line premise first).

The `lastNano == 0` (peer-never-seen) branch in pkg/cluster/heartbeat.go:727-748 calls handlePeerNeverSeen after only threshold*interval (5×100ms = 500ms) then `continue`s, so the 30s config-apply grace at :746 is UNREACHABLE when the peer was never seen. handlePeerNeverSeen (heartbeat_manager.go:429) sets peerEverSeen=true + electSingleNode; election.go:325 gates the readiness check on `&& m.peerAlive`, so a never-seen node SKIPS readiness + promotes on Weight>0.

TRACE: both chassis power on together; config apply (FRR reload, fabric creation, RETH MAC down/up) disrupts the control-link RX for 10-15s (the exact reason the 30s grace exists), so the first heartbeats drop and lastSeen stays 0 on BOTH. At T0+500ms BOTH hit handlePeerNeverSeen -> both StatePrimary -> both claim the RETH virtual MAC + GARP -> 10-15s split-brain until the link recovers and dual-active resolution demotes one.

FIX: apply a STARTUP FLOOR (>= the ~15s config-apply disruption, ideally 30s) to the never-seen path before it may promote. threshold*interval (500ms) is right for a LOST peer, but too aggressive for deciding a peer NEVER EXISTED at boot — the never-seen-at-boot case must wait out the config-apply grace. Distinct from VRRP H-2 (#4376, the family-split tie-break) — this is the cluster-manager heartbeat layer. HA/cluster → test-failover (specifically a SIMULTANEOUS-BOOT scenario: boot both nodes together, assert only one promotes). ## #4388 — userspace-dp HA/NAT: peer-synced session's NAT pool port not reserved in the secondary's allocator -> post-failover port collision (ps-review-007 P1) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

From ps-review-007 (P1, HIGH; base 58a002642, ps-source low-signal profile but THIS finding is genuine + well-evidenced — VERIFY the reserve-gap on current master first).

A peer-synced session (origin PeerSynced) installed on the SECONDARY does NOT reserve its NAT source port in the secondary's local pool allocator. Evidence: userspace-dp/src/session/install.rs:223 (`if counted && !origin.is_peer_synced()` — synced sessions are excluded from the counting/reservation path); the PortAllocator `live` set (nat/allocator.rs:173) that allocate_translation (nat/source.rs:968) consults for new allocations is therefore NOT updated for a synced session's port.

CONSEQUENCE (post-failover collision): primary allocates pool port 10000 for session S, syncs to secondary; secondary installs S (PeerSynced, NAT port 10000) but does NOT mark 10000 allocated in its pool. On FAILOVER the secondary becomes primary with S active on 203.0.113.1:10000, but its pool shows 10000 AVAILABLE → a new session S2 allocates 10000 → TWO sessions on the same NAT source IP:port → the remote host sees one source, replies mis-deliver / connections fail; an attacker could deliberately create sessions to reuse a synced session's port (session-hijacking surface).

FIX: on the secondary, when installing a peer-synced session WITH a NAT translation (a translated source port), RESERVE that port in the local pool allocator (add PortAllocator::reserve_port to mark a specific port allocated without normal allocation) so new sessions don't reuse it; on session DELETE for a peer-synced session, release_port. (Alternative: on failover, iterate all synced sessions + reserve their NAT ports before accepting new sessions — but the per-install reserve is cleaner + always-correct.) Must reuse the pool-SNAT machinery (#4074/#4088 allocate_translation) + preserve address-persistent behavior. Rust, cargo. HA (post-failover) → test-failover (a NAT-pool session synced across failover, then a new session must NOT reuse the synced port). RED-on-revert: without the reserve, a new post-failover session allocates the synced session's port. Distinct from the session-limit-count issue (#4377 = C2) — this is NAT pool ports, higher-impact.

## #4392 — userspace-dp filter/PBR: 'then routing-instance' + 'then reject'/'then discard' FORWARDS the packet instead of dropping -> VRF leak + audit-log bypass (ps-review-008 P3, CRITICAL) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

From ps-review-008 (P3, CRITICAL, High confidence; base 58a002642 — VERIFY on current master, code confirmed present). A firewall-filter/PBR term that sets a routing-instance AND a drop action forwards instead of dropping.

REPRO: input filter term `from { source-address 10.0.0.0/8; } then { routing-instance blue; reject; }`. Session-miss path: evaluate_non_pbr_input_filter defers (returns Accept for the routing-instance term, eval.rs:330-331); the input-filter action check passes (Accept != Reject, mod.rs:1636); ingress_route_table_override runs the PBR evaluator, matches the term, LOGS Reject, but returns Some("blue.inet.0"); the route lookup uses the override table; the packet is FORWARDED to VRF blue. The flowless path (mod.rs:3310-3331) is identical.

ROOT CAUSE: the PBR evaluator (userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/eval.rs:531-532) returns FilterRoutingInstanceResult { routing_instance, action: term.action } — the action is captured but ingress_route_table_override (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/mod.rs:1469, ~1561-1566) uses it ONLY for log_match.action normalization, NEVER to drop, and ALWAYS returns Some(routing_instance). The caller (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1640-1681 + the flowless 3310-3331) proceeds to route-lookup-and-forward with the override, with NO check of routing_result.action.

IMPACT: CRITICAL. A `then reject`/`then discard` on a PBR routing-instance term is a false audit log (the log says Reject) + a real security bypass (the traffic is forwarded, into a DIFFERENT VRF = a VRF leak). An operator relying on a filter deny is silently bypassed.

FIX: when the matched PBR term's action is Reject or Discard, the forwarding path must DROP (synthesize the reject reply for Reject / silent drop for Discard) and NOT apply the routing-instance override / NOT forward. Either (a) ingress_route_table_override returns a drop signal (None + a drop marker) when the term action is Reject/Discard, or (b) the caller checks routing_result.action after the override and drops before the route lookup. Preserve the correct log (already shows Reject). RED-on-revert: a `then routing-instance X; reject` term drops (RST/ICMP-unreach for reject, silent for discard) instead of forwarding to X. Rust, cargo. Test both the session-miss + flowless paths + v4/v6.

## #4394 — policymatch: simulator fabricates a verdict instead of ContentRejected for protocol-less/unrepresentable/undefined apps + unresolvable addresses (dataplane fails closed) -> misleads operator (ps-review-008 P4) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

From ps-review-008 (P4, HIGH — simulator/dataplane divergence). The match-policies simulator only detects content-rejection for UNEXPANDABLE application-sets (#3727), but the DATAPLANE also fails CLOSED on: protocol-less apps, unrepresentable protocols/ports, undefined applications, unresolvable addresses. In those cases the SIMULATOR fabricates a permit/deny/default verdict instead of reporting ContentRejected. Under default-permit the simulator may say PERMIT while the dataplane DENIES (fail-closed); under default-deny with a previous-good snapshot retained the simulator may say DENY while the dataplane still PERMITS (the stale snapshot) — either way the operator is MISLED (wrong troubleshooting, potential security misconfiguration). FIX: extend the simulator's ContentRejected detection (pkg/policymatch) to cover the SAME fail-closed conditions the dataplane enforces — protocol-less app, unrepresentable proto/port, undefined app ref, unresolvable address — so the simulator reports ContentRejected (matching the dataplane) instead of a fabricated verdict. Go (policymatch) + verify against the Rust dataplane's fail-closed set (the #4352 SSOT / policy.rs). Not a security bug itself, but a diagnostic-accuracy gap that hides real fail-closed drops.

## #4399 — userspace-dp NAT: nat_reverse_index is single-value -> a 1:N reverse-key collision displaces the earlier session -> reply mis-delivery/hijacking (ps-review-009 P5, the #1758 latent collision) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

From ps-review-009 (P5, HIGH, High confidence). The reverse-NAT lookup index (userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:1712-1718) is a SINGLE-VALUE FxHashMap: `nat_reverse_index.insert(reverse_wire_key(key, nat), handle)` DISPLACES the previous handle on a reverse-key collision (a counter nat_reverse_key_collisions increments but there is NO mitigation). find_forward_nat_match (lookup.rs:210-211) does a single `.get(reply_key)` → returns ONLY the last-installed handle. So when two sessions map to the same external reverse tuple (the field doc at mod.rs:533-540 acknowledges the #1758 latent 1:N collision: interface-mode SNAT / DNAT-to-shared-backend / NAT64 / non-bijective static NAT — pool-mode SNAT is immune), the later DISPLACES the earlier → the displaced session's return traffic is delivered to the WRONG internal host (both share the external reverse tuple → the reply matches the last-installed session → reverse-NAT rewrites to the wrong host = hijacking/mis-delivery) OR drops (disruption).

FIX: make nat_reverse_index a 1:N multi-map (reverse_wire_key → SmallVec<[handle]> / a chained list) and have find_forward_nat_match walk the candidates + validate EACH against the full reply tuple (reply_matches_forward_session) to find the RIGHT session (the one whose full forward tuple reverse-maps to this exact reply), not just the last-installed. On delete, remove the specific handle from the bucket (not the whole key). Bound the bucket (a pathological collision set) + keep the nat_reverse_key_collisions counter for observability. This closes the mis-delivery for interface-SNAT/DNAT-shared-backend/NAT64. Rust, cargo. HA-adjacent (the reverse index is per-worker). RED-on-revert: two sessions with the same reverse-key → BOTH resolve their own return traffic (RED: the earlier is displaced + mis-delivers on revert). This is a substantial hot-path change — the reviewer flagged it HIGH; verify the multi-map doesn't regress the pool-mode-SNAT single-value fast path.

## #4400 — userspace-dp flow: TCP RST/FIN on session-miss creates a (closing) session instead of dropping -> session-table churn / no strict-syn-check parity (ps-review-009 P6) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

Rust (the session-miss install guard) + Go (the config knob if added). Verify a legitimate SYN still installs; a SYN-ACK on miss (asymmetric) is handled per the existing policy. ## #4418 — userspace-dp screen: scan cleanup 5-min cap reopens slow-scan evasion for configured windows > 5min (non-blocking residual from #4416) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

From the #4416 (opus-171 M-1) hostile review — a non-blocking residual, filed per the no-dismissal rule. #4416 made the scan/sweep cleanup reap floor window-aware, but clamps it at MAX_CLEANUP_WINDOW_MICROS = 300s (5min). For a configured detection window > 5min, cleanup reaps at the 300s cap BEFORE the window elapses → the slow-scan evasion technically reopens for that pathological band. ACCEPTED as a deliberate tradeoff because: (1) memory is already bounded by MAX_UNIQUE_PER_SOURCE (1024) + MAX_SOURCES_PER_ZONE (4096) regardless of window, so the cap only affects reclamation timing; (2) a >5min window is 300× the commit-warned Junos 1s max (an absurd, warned misconfiguration); (3) closing it fully means raising/removing the cap. DISPOSITION: low-priority — either (a) close as WONTFIX (documented tradeoff, the 5min cap is a defensible ceiling), or (b) if the project wants the evasion closed for ANY preserved window, make the cap track the max configured window (memory is capped anyway) + add a commit-warning for windows > 5min. Verify-first: confirm the memory caps genuinely bound a 71min-window worst case before choosing (b).

## #4449 — Stale NAT64 policy-tuple rationale comments in userspace-dp afxdp/tests.rs (pre-#2358) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

Found while verifying #4440 (codex-172 NAT64 synthetic-dest policy concern — disproven, no behavior bug).

## What
The rationale comments in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests.rs` around the NAT64 policy-tuple tests still describe the PRE-#2358 behavior and are now factually wrong:

- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tests.rs` ~L11686-11691: "NAT64 is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from post-translation matching ... the policy matcher requires same-family src+dst, so NAT64 policy is matched on the SYNTHETIC IPv6 destination, NOT the extracted IPv4 destination."
- ~L12057-12065 (`policy_inbound_nat64_matches_synthetic_v6_destination_permit`): "NAT64 (DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the #2345 post-translation tuple) ... policy matches on the SYNTHETIC IPv6 dst (the only same-family tuple available)."
- ~L12099-12104 / ~L12395-12400: same premise.

## Why it's wrong now
#2358 (commit `09d0a929b`, "nat64: match inbound policy on the real translated IPv4 destination") added a `(V6 src, V4 dst)` cross-family arm to `policy.rs::try_match_rule` and changed the forwarding path to feed `policy_dst_ip = effective_resolution_target` = the **extracted real IPv4 destination** for NAT64 (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs` ~L1505-1555, eval at ~L2467; arm at `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs` ~L3907). The accurate description lives in `docs/next-features/twice-nat.md` (#2358 section).

The tests STILL PASS (verified `cargo test policy_inbound_nat64`), but only because:
- `64:ff9b::/96` (a v6-only destination set with no v4 prefix) compiles to IPv4-match-any under the legacy address-set convention, so it matches the extracted v4 dst.
- A scratch discriminator confirmed: a rule scoped to a non-covering `9.9.9.9/32` DENIES the `8.8.8.8` NAT64 flow, and `8.8.8.8/32` (the real extracted host) PERMITS it — i.e. the match is on the extracted IPv4, exactly as #2358/twice-nat.md say. The comments claiming synthetic-IPv6 matching are stale.

## Fix (Rust, comment-only)
Rewrite the affected `afxdp/tests.rs` comment blocks to describe the #2358 cross-family (V6 src, V4 dst) behavior — matching on the extracted real IPv4 destination — and note that the `64:ff9b::/96` whole-prefix rules still permit only via the IPv4-match-any convention (a v6-only destination set), not a NAT64-specific policy path. No assertion/logic change needed; run the userspace-dp cargo suite to confirm still-green.

Low severity (test-comment accuracy). Deferred from #4440 to keep that a Go/docs PR.

## #4455 — HI-1: per-zone multicast/broadcast host-inbound admission (iifname gate + Rust lockstep) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

Split out from #4420 (HI-1), verified genuine in PR #4454 but deferred as a hardening/design change.

## Problem
The kernel `xpf_hostinbound` `chain input` matches destination address only and runs `policy accept` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go`, `buildHostInboundFilterPayload`). Host-bound **multicast** (224.0.0.0/4, ff00::/8) and **broadcast** (255.255.255.255, subnet-directed) destinations match no per-zone `daddr` set, so they fall through `policy accept` to the host stack **without** per-zone `host-inbound-traffic protocols` admission (OSPF/RIP/VRRP/PIM/IGMP, etc.). The Rust LocalDelivery classifier keys on local **unicast** addresses only (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/mod.rs`), so it does not gate host-bound multicast either.

This is a Junos-parity gap: in Junos, host-bound routing multicast is admitted per-zone via `host-inbound-traffic protocols <x>`.

## Why deferred (not folded into #4454)
1. **Needs an ingress-interface dimension.** The current chain has no `iifname` predicate; multicast admission is inherently per-zone/per-interface (the destination is a group, not a firewall address), so this needs a new `iifname`-scoped rule structure.
2. **Rust lockstep.** The codebase invariant is that the kernel nft host-inbound set and the Rust `host_inbound_admits` classifier must agree (see the "keep in lockstep" comments in `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go` / `userspace-dp/.../forwarding/host_inbound.rs`). A kernel-only change risks split-brain.
3. **Behavior/hardening change.** A zone running a routing protocol in FRR without the matching `host-inbound-traffic protocols` knob relies on today's accept; enforcing per-zone multicast admission would break such configs (Junos requires both), so it needs the strict-on-commit / warn-on-load (#1960) treatment and a migration story.

## Bounded exposure (context, not a reason to skip)
The host kernel only delivers multicast to groups a configured daemon actually joined (routing daemons the operator enabled), and the always-on control set (ND `icmpv6 133-137`, PMTUD, ESP/AH) is already globally accepted. So this is a parity/hardening gap rather than an open-door fail-open.

## Proposed direction
- Add per-zone multicast/broadcast admission scoped by ingress `iifname` in the kernel chain, expanding each zone's `host-inbound-traffic protocols` set to its well-known multicast groups (OSPF 224.0.0.5/6 + ff02::5/6, RIP 224.0.0.9 + ff02::9, VRRP 224.0.0.18, PIM 224.0.0.13, IGMP, router-discovery, etc.).
- Mirror the same admission in the Rust classifier for any host-bound multicast that reaches the XSK.
- Gate the behavior change per #1960 (strict on commit, warn on tolerant load) and document the required `host-inbound-traffic protocols` knobs.

## #4475 — opus-172 H-2: unsolicited ARP/NA installed as NUD_REACHABLE — on-link neighbor-cache poisoning/MITM [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

opus-review-172 H-2. Data-path neighbor learning installs UNSOLICITED ARP/NA MACs as kernel NUD_REACHABLE via NLM_F_REPLACE -> on-link neighbor-cache poisoning / MITM of any same-segment next-hop (incl the WAN gateway).

**Class:** security hardening. **Severity:** HIGH. Behavior source-confirmed; code itself flags solicited-only learning as an unfinished follow-up.

**Evidence:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/neighbor.rs:383-393` (add_kernel_neighbor: RTM_NEWNEIGH + NLM_F_CREATE|NLM_F_REPLACE + NUD_REACHABLE, unconditionally overwrites). `poll_stages.rs:108-135` learns an ARP Reply / NDP NA when `neighbor_ip_is_learnable && !owns_configured_ip` with NO solicited-state check and (NA) no RFC 4861 §7.2.5 Override honoring.

**Trace:** attacker on the L2 segment emits gratuitous ARP reply sender_ip=<gateway> sender_mac=<attacker> -> xpf REPLACE-installs NUD_REACHABLE -> kernel forwards transit/originated traffic to attacker MAC, suppresses revalidation. IPv6 identical via unsolicited NA. Own-IP gate (#2851) + hop-limit-255 gate confirmed present -> blast radius is other same-segment next-hops.

**Fix:** learn only solicited replies/NA (probe-driven or entry already live); honor NA Override=0 (install NUD_STALE, dont overwrite a differing LLA); prefer NUD_STALE for data-path learns. Distinct from F-089/#3048 (stale-MAC blackhole). RUST.

## #4487 — ps-017 P6b: residual LocalDelivery RST/FIN creates a session (host-IP session-table DoS + policy-skip) — #4400 covered only ForwardCandidate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-review-017 P6b (residual of P6/#4400). #4400 (P6a) added `strict_syn_check_drops_new_flow()` to the ForwardCandidate/MissingNeighbor session-miss path, but the **LocalDelivery** session-miss path does NOT apply the guard — a bare TCP RST/FIN to a firewall host IP still creates a session.

**Class:** session / tcp / dos / local-delivery. **Severity:** Medium-High (DoS + policy-bypass). Source-confirmed on base 3c3f62db5 (residual after #4400).

**Evidence:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:614-618` defines `strict_syn_check_drops_new_flow()`. Lines ~1983-1991 gate the ForwardCandidate/MissingNeighbor path only. The **LocalDelivery** disposition has separate session-miss handling at ~mod.rs:2091 and ~2212 with NO strict-SYN check.

**Trace:** attacker sends a TCP RST to a firewall IP (e.g. SSH :22) with no existing session -> LocalDelivery (to host) -> session miss -> host-inbound admits -> junos-host policy permits -> a session is CREATED with RST flags, no drop. DoS: RST flood fills the session table. Policy bypass: the RST creates a closing-state session, so a legitimate SYN hits it instead of re-evaluating.

**Why it matters:** host-bound traffic should not create sessions on teardown flags; a firewall-IP RST/FIN flood is a cheap session-table-exhaustion + a policy-evaluation-skip.

**Fix:** apply `strict_syn_check_drops_new_flow` (or a bare-RST/FIN-to-host drop) to the LocalDelivery session-miss path as well (mod.rs:2091/2212), matching the #4400 ForwardCandidate gate. RED-on-revert: a bare RST to a host IP installs NO session (like `bare_rst_fin_on_miss_installs_no_session` but for LocalDelivery). RUST (dataplane -> FULL cargo + smoke).

**Dedup:** P6 (ps-009) filed RST/FIN session creation; P6a (#4400) fixed the ForwardCandidate path; this is the residual LocalDelivery path — a refinement, not a duplicate.

## #4508 — doc: clarify 'Packets dropped' = enforcement drops (undercounts no-route/fabric/vlan/NAT64 drops) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

Non-blocking follow-up from the #4507 review. The #4477 fix bridges GlobalCtrDrops (idx 2) as totalDrops() = policyDenied + screenDrops + hostInboundDenied + natAllocFail — the four ENFORCEMENT drop reasons. It excludes other real drop paths (slow-path no-route, fabric-fwd-drop idx 32, vlan-push-fail idx 40, NAT64 fail-closed). So 'Packets dropped' is effectively 'enforcement drops' — far better than the prior false 0, but an operator should know it undercounts literal total drops. Add a doc caveat (docs/junos-cli-reference.md flow-statistics section), OR extend totalDrops() to include the other drop indices if a true total is wanted.

## #4512 — nat64: HA-sync the translated port reservation (Nat64ReverseInfo) — post-failover collision residual (follow-up to #4381) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

Flagged boundary from #4381/#4511 (stateful NAT64 port translation). After #4511, each Nat64Prefix owns a PortAllocator and reserves a unique translated (pool_v4, port) per flow. BUT Nat64ReverseInfo is NOT HA-synced, and the standby does NOT reserve the synced NAT64 port. So after a failover, a NEW local NAT64 flow on the new primary could allocate a port that COLLIDES with an in-flight synced NAT64 session (the same class of bug #4388 fixed for NAT44 pool-SNAT via reserve_synced_source_nat_allocation). Fix: apply the #4388 treatment to NAT64 — sync the translated-port reservation (Nat64ReverseInfo) in the session-sync payload + reserve it on the standby's PortAllocator (upsert_synced.rs / delete_synced.rs analog for the NAT64 allocator), so a post-failover flow doesn't reuse an owned port. Scoped follow-up; the base #4381 fix closes the same-node collision.
