## #4514 — firewall: single-rate token-bucket policer (then policer X) silently unenforced on userspace dataplane — rate-limit bypass (ps-020 F5) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-review-020 F5 (Cohort 8, MEDIUM, unenforced-control — verified on current master 5b6434f39). A single-rate token-bucket policer (`firewall policer X { if-exceeding { bandwidth-limit ...; } then discard; }` applied via a filter term `then policer X`) is SILENTLY UNENFORCED on the userspace dataplane — the configured rate-limit does nothing, so a DoS-mitigation/rate-limit control the operator relies on is bypassed with no warning.

**Evidence (current master):**
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:65-77` — PolicerSnapshot parsed into `state.policers` (PolicerState). So the config IS carried into the dataplane.
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/eval.rs:170-171` — `acc.policer_name` is captured into FilterResult but **never consumed**.
- `PolicerState::consume()` (`userspace-dp/src/filter/policer.rs`) has **ZERO non-test call sites** (grep: only `tests.rs:728-743`). Only `ThreeColorPolicerRuntime::meter` is actually applied in the engine (`apply_term_three_color_policer`).
- `buildThreeColorPolicerSnapshots` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go:576`) reads only `cfg.Firewall.ThreeColorPolicers`; single-rate `cfg.Firewall.Policers` are NOT lowered into any metered path.
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/capabilities.go:90-94` **CLAIMS** "legacy policers are supported in the userspace dataplane" — contradicted by the missing metering. No commit warning / capability rejection → a silent fail-OPEN of the rate limit.

**Why it matters:** an operator configures `then policer` to rate-limit/discard-excess a class of traffic (DoS mitigation, fair-use). On xpf it silently passes ALL traffic — the control is unenforced with no signal, and the capability doc lies that it works.

**Fix:** wire `PolicerState::consume(now_ns, pkt_len)` into the filter eval hot path when `policer_name` resolves to a `state.policers` entry (drop on non-conforming when the policer's action is discard), mirroring `apply_term_three_color_policer`; add the flow-cache gate for the metered term. OR lower single-rate policers into the existing three-color metered runtime at compile (filters.go). Also: correct/qualify the capabilities.go claim, and add a commit warning if the policer would be left unenforced. RUST (filter eval) + Go (compile/capabilities). Not tracked by #4372 (three-color status export) or #4422 (test-coverage).

## #4515 — config: 2 deliberate warn-only validation parity gaps (zone→undefined-iface, malformed addr-book value) — ps-002 F6/F11 (low, promote-with-care) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

ps-review-002 (Cohort 2 config/compiler) — two DELIBERATE warn-only config-validation parity gaps, filed per the never-dismiss discipline with the documented-tradeoff + promotion-risk rationale recorded. Both are LOW priority; NOT to be naively promoted to strict.

**F6 — zone → undefined-interface reference is warn-only, not strict** (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go:383`).
- Junos hard-rejects a zone referencing an undefined interface; xpf warns.
- **Why NOT promoted (deliberate):** `configuredIfaces` is built only from `cfg.Interfaces.Interfaces` and EXCLUDES daemon-materialized st0/lo0/tunnel/VRF interfaces. A naive strict promotion would FALSE-REJECT valid configs referencing those dynamic interfaces (the #4191 over-rejection class).
- **No proven fail-open:** an interface absent from config is brought DOWN by the daemon → fail-closed for real traffic.
- If ever pursued: first union in the dynamic-interface set (st0/lo0/tunnel/VRF), THEN use the strict-on-commit + lenient-on-load pattern.

**F11-part2 — malformed address-book VALUE (e.g. `10.0.1.0/32/24`) is warn-only** (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go:288-292`, #2229).
- Explicitly chosen as warn-only for #1960 no-brick ("never a hard reject — rejecting it would brick existing configs"), with a documented fail-closed-for-permit runtime analysis. (F11-part1, trailing-garbage TOKENS, WAS promoted to strict via #3332.)
- A narrow deny-blocklist fail-open edge exists in theory, but any promotion must still accept the non-literal forms Junos allows (dns-name / range-address / wildcard-address) to avoid false rejects → a judgment call, low value.

Disposition: DELIBERATE documented tradeoffs (recorded here, not silently dropped). Low-priority parity tracker; promote only with the dynamic-interface-union (F6) / non-literal-form-accepting (F11) safeguards.

## #4517 — screen/frame: IPv6 EH walkers stop at unenumerated EH types (MOBILITY/HIP/Shim6) — L4/fragment hidden from screens (ps-021 H-1) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-review-021 H-1 (verified genuine against current master — the ps-021 file was an unstable multi-cohort clobber, but this finding is confirmed against present bpfrx code).

**[Low, IDS-evasion / defense-in-depth] IPv6 extension-header walkers terminate at unenumerated EH types (MOBILITY/HIP/Shim6/experimental), hiding L4 + fragment status.**

**Files/lines (current master):** all three IPv6 EH walkers share the enumeration {0 HbH, 43 Routing, 44 Fragment, 51 AH, 60 DestOpt, 59 NoNext} + a catch-all break/return:
- `userspace-dp/src/screen/extract.rs:304` — `_ => break`
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:217` — `_ => return Some((offset, protocol))`
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs:298` — `_ => return false`

**Failure scenario:** an IPv6 packet `base → HOP → MOBILITY(135) → FRAGMENT(44) → TCP(SYN, dst 22)`. The walkers hit type 135, fall to the `_` arm, and STOP. `extract.rs` leaves `is_fragment=false` / `tcp_offset=None`; `inspect.rs` returns `proto=135` with no L4 and `is_non_first_fragment=false`. Result: the syn-frag / teardrop / ping-of-death fragment screens don't fire, and the packet is never recognized as a TCP SYN — forwarding classifies it as proto-135 and (if zone/address policy allows) forwards it. A MIPv6-capable end host parses MOBILITY→TCP and completes the connection UNSCREENED / UNSTATED. NOTE: the review's sub-claim "other TCP-flag screens still fire via meta.tcp_flags from a longer outer walk" is INACCURATE — the meta-producing walkers (inspect.rs) share the identical limited EH set, so a MOBILITY-hidden SYN is proto=135 with no L4 everywhere. Narrow (exotic EH; mainstream HbH/Routing/Frag/DestOpt/AH already handled) but a real IDS-evasion gap.

**Fix:** add MOBILITY(135), HIP(139), Shim6(140), experimental(253/254) as generic length-prefixed EH arms (read HdrExtLen at offset+1, advance (hdr_ext_len+1)*8, continue the walk) in all THREE walkers — mirroring the existing HOP/DEST arm. Keep `_ => break`/return only for genuine L4 protocols. Do NOT add ESP(50) (encrypted, non-walkable). Apply CONSISTENTLY so the meta-producing parser, the screen extractor, and the fragment predicate agree. Test: a MOBILITY-prefixed fragmented SYN reaches the syn-frag screen. RUST (cargo). Optional ride-along: H-3 widen extract.rs:267 frag_data_off u16→u32 (latent, unreachable under the 0..8 cap — trivial hardening).

## #4518 — nat64: port allocator reset to offset-0 on config reload collides new flows with live pre-reload sessions (ps-021 F1; sibling of #4512 HA path) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-021 Finding 1 [Medium] — NAT64 port allocator NOT preserved across a config reload/commit (same-node) — DISTINCT from #4512 (which is the HA-failover-sync path).

**Evidence (current master):** `userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs:370-371` builds `PortAllocator::new(...)` fresh; `from_snapshots(&[NAT64RuleSnapshot]) -> Self` (nat64.rs:285) takes NO `previous`, and the sole caller `afxdp/forwarding_build/mod.rs:324` rebuilds from snapshot only. Source-NAT, by contrast, PRESERVES live allocations across reload via `parse_source_nat_rules_with_previous` + `previous_allocators` (nat/source.rs:481/492/495). The in-code comment (nat64.rs:364-369) explicitly documents this as an unimplemented "scoped follow-up" using the source-NAT `reuse_pool_allocator` treatment.

**Scenario:** any config commit while NAT64 sessions are live rebuilds the allocator at port-offset 0 → the first post-commit flows deterministically reuse LOW translated ports still owned by live pre-reload sessions; if the colliding port maps to the same v4 remote, the (now 1:N) reverse index bucket holds two handles → reverse-reply mis-demux/hijack until the old session ages out.

**Fix:** add `from_snapshots_with_previous(snaps, previous: Option<&Nat64State>)` keyed on (prefix, pool_addresses); reuse the compatible Arc-backed `PortAllocator` — mirror `parse_source_nat_rules_with_previous`. RUST (cargo).

**Relationship to #4512:** #4512 is the HA path (sync `Nat64ReverseInfo` + reserve on the standby → post-FAILOVER cross-node collision, the #4388 treatment). THIS is the config-commit/same-node RELOAD path (thread previous `Nat64State` → preserve live reservations). Different mechanism, different fix — but both are "NAT64 allocator durability across a state rebuild." A single engineer could address both (reload + HA) under a durability theme; filing separately for the distinct fix.

## #4519 — nptv6: host-bits enforced by debug_assert only (masked in release) → over-broad prefix installed + lenient warning lies about rejection (ps-021 F3) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-021 Finding 3 [Low, hardening / contract-violation] — NPTv6 host-bits are enforced by `debug_assert!` ONLY (compiled out in release), and the Go lenient-load warning FALSELY promises the helper rejects the snapshot.

**Evidence (current master):** `userspace-dp/src/nptv6.rs:174` `debug_assert!` (no-op in release); `parse_prefix` returns `Some(...)` after masking `words[prefix_words..]` — it does NOT fail-closed for host-bits, so `try_from_snapshots` INSTALLS the masked prefix. The Go gate is strict at commit but LENIENT on tolerant-load/peer-sync (`compiler.go:584,689` set `lenientNPTv6:true`; `compiler_nat.go:541-549` `emit` returns `warnings, nil`). The lenient warning text (compiler_nat.go:543-547) literally promises "the helper rejects the whole NPTv6 snapshot and the previous state is kept" — which is FALSE for host-bits in release builds (the helper silently masks + installs an over-broad translation). The documented backstop contract is violated.

**Scenario:** a persisted/peer-synced pre-#2380 config with `...:2::/48` loads with a warning, but the release helper installs `...::/48` — over-translating a WIDER range than authored (not fail-open, but over-scoped, contradicting the warning's promise).

**Fix:** make `parse_prefix` return `None` (fail-closed) on host-bits, matching the #2124/#2142/#2173/#2212 fail-scoped-skip family + NAT64's fail-scoped skip — so the helper actually DOES reject the snapshot as the lenient warning claims. (At minimum an `eprintln!` release warning — the sole debug_assert! is insufficient for a helper-boundary backstop.) RUST (cargo).

## #4520 — nat64: empty-pool vs allocator-exhaustion share nat64_no_source_pool counter — Err(_) discards SourceNatFailureReason::AllocatorExhausted (ps-021 F2) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-021 Finding 2 [Low, observability]. The NAT64 empty-pool path and the allocator-exhaustion path both bump the same nat64_no_source_pool counter.

## #4521 — config/nat: SNAT source pool 'address [ a b c ]' bracket-list truncates to first IP (Keys[1] not Keys[1:]) — #2419-class (ps-022 R-02) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-022 R-02 [Medium-low, config / #2419-class silent-truncation] — SNAT source pool `address [ a b c ]` in flat-set/bracket-list form silently keeps only the FIRST IP.

**Evidence (current master, empirically confirmed):** pkg/config/compiler_nat.go:1344-1370 reads only prop.Keys[1] (a single inline value), never Keys[1:]; the to-range branch requires Keys[2]=="to", so a discrete bracket list with no `to` keeps only the first. `address` under a source pool is UNMODELED in schema (schema_security.go:353 pool children = port/persistent-nat/port-overloading-factor/routing-instance only), so SetPath's unmodeled-leaf path (ast_edit.go:235-246) collapses ALL trailing tokens onto one node → Keys=["address","a","b","c"].

**Empirical proof** (scratch test, run then removed): `set security nat source pool P address [ 203.0.113.1/32 203.0.113.2/32 203.0.113.3/32 ]` → pool.Addresses = [203.0.113.1/32] (1 of 3). Discrete `set` lines → 3/3 (works). Range `a to b` form → 3/3 (works). So the bug is bounded to the bracket-list shape.

**Scenario:** the SNAT pool silently shrinks to one address → premature source-port exhaustion under load (not a classic fail-open — traffic still NATs from fewer IPs — but the #2419 silent-accept+truncate class the project hardens against). No open issue (F-098 in all_findings.txt is this class, undriven).

**Fix:** iterate prop.Keys[1:] with per-member `to`-range handling (keep the existing prop.Children loop for the hierarchical block shape). Mirror the #2419 dual-shape multi-value read (firewallMatchValues pattern). GO.

**Optional trivial ride-along (R-04, not worth its own issue):** add `ch == '@'` to isIdentChar (pkg/config/lexer.go:289-297) for unquoted-URL completeness — no live failure (the quoted form works).

## #4524 — cli: 'monitor traffic ... matching <filter>' injects tcpdump options (-w/-z) → root file-write/command-exec past capture-only RBAC (ps-023 13-02, HIGH) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-023 [13-02] HIGH — `monitor traffic` tcpdump argument injection → privilege escalation / root file-write / command-exec.

**Evidence (current master — the review's cited path pkg/cli/monitor.go:565 is WRONG; the real code is pkg/cli/cli_request.go:568):** buildMonitorTrafficArgv (cli_request.go:568) appends `strings.Fields(filter)...` to the tcpdump argv with NO `--` separator. The `matching` clause (parseMonitorTrafficArgs, cli_request.go:519) greedily absorbs any tokens up to the next keyword, so `monitor traffic interface ge-0-0-0 matching -w /etc/cron.d/x` yields `exec tcpdump -i ge-0-0-0 -n -l -w /etc/cron.d/x`. Under glibc getopt permutation, tcpdump parses `-w` as an option regardless of position → arbitrary file write; `-z <cmd>` (postrotate) reaches command execution.

**Privilege boundary:** RBAC gates this at PermControl (pkg/cli/permissions.go:135 — its comment notes "monitor traffic = privileged capture (root tcpdump)"), so a custom login-class with `control` but NOT super-user escalates to root file-write / command-exec. It also violates the capture-only contract even for super-user. INCONSISTENT with ping/traceroute, which route through `diagcmd` and add `--` (#2084).

**Fix:** insert `"--"` before the filter tokens in buildMonitorTrafficArgv (mirroring the diagcmd ping/traceroute #2084 treatment), OR reject filter tokens beginning with `-`. Add a regression test asserting `matching -w /tmp/x` is neutralized (the `-w` reaches tcpdump as a filter operand after `--`, not as an option). GO (pkg/cli). Not currently tracked.

## #4525 — ra: randomAdvInterval returns 0 for max-advertisement-interval 1-2 → RA hot-loop (schema ValidateIntegerMin(1) too low vs RFC 4861) (ps-023 12-02) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-023 [12-02] LOW — RA randomAdvInterval can return 0 → RA hot-loop (RA/ND flood + CPU spin).

**Evidence (current master):** pkg/ra/sender.go:863 — for max-advertisement-interval maxI=1: minI=0, interval = 0 + rand.IntN(2) → 0 or 1; for maxI=2: interval = 0 + rand.IntN(3) → 0/1/2. When 0, advTimer.Reset(s.randomAdvInterval()) (sender.go:468) fires IMMEDIATELY → sendRA → re-arm → hot loop (~33-50% of ticks 0-delay). The schema ALLOWS it: pkg/config/schema_routing.go:455 uses ValidateIntegerMin(1) (only the solicited RS path has a minRAMulticastDelay floor; the unsolicited advTimer path has none).

**Scenario:** operator sets `max-advertisement-interval 1` or `2` → interval draws 0 → RA flood + CPU spin.

**Fix:** floor the returned interval to >=1s in randomAdvInterval, AND/OR raise the schema validator to ValidateInteger(4,1800) per RFC 4861 §6.2.1 (MinRtrAdvInterval >= 3s, MaxRtrAdvInterval in [4,1800]). GO. (Possibly the same root as the unmapped F-233.)

## #4526 — dhcp: renewalTimers leaseTime*7/8 int64 overflow for >41.8yr leases (impact ~nil — t1 dominates; cleanliness) (ps-023 12-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-023 [12-01] LOW (scenario overstated). pkg/dhcp/commit.go:52 t2Remaining = leaseTime*7/8 - leaseTime/2. With leaseTime > MaxInt64/7 (~41.8yr; IPAddressLeaseTime uncapped, dhcp.go:1019), leaseTime*7 wraps negative → t2Remaining clamped to 1s. BUT in that regime t1 = leaseTime/2 (>20yr) always dominates and is never clamped, so there is NO '1s T2 rebind storm' / tight renew loop (t2 fires after t1, decades out); 0xFFFFFFFF is the RFC infinite sentinel → ~68yr timer, arguably correct. Effectively nil impact. Fix (cleanliness only): t2Remaining = leaseTime/8*3 (no overflow); add a max-uint32-lease test. Low; drop if not worth chasing an overflow with no impact. GO.

## #4534 — routing/PBR: buildPBRFromFilter steers a routing-instance term even with discard/reject action — kernel-mirror fail-open VRF-steer (ps-024 M-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-024 M-01 [Low-Medium, fail-open-adjacent] — PBR kernel-mirror steers a `then routing-instance X` term even when the same term has `discard`/`reject` (the deny is ignored in the kernel slow-path mirror).

**Evidence (current master):** `pkg/routing/rules.go:770` `buildPBRFromFilter` loops `filter.Terms`, keys only on `term.RoutingInstance != ""`, and NEVER reads `term.Action` (verified 770-940). So a `routing-instance + discard/reject` term builds a steering `ip rule`. The strict conflict gate `validateFilterRoutingInstanceConflictStrict` (compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:1247, via runUniformGates) is LENIENT on load/peer-sync (opts.lenientFilterRoutingInstanceConflict, #1960 no-brick), so a contradictory term survives. Userspace IS fixed (#4392: forwarding/mod.rs:1619-1677 is_drop on Reject|Discard → RouteOverride::Drop) — so userspace drops on the filtered interface while the kernel PBR mirror still steers (slow-path / XDP_PASS / interfaces without the filter — the ip rule is global, no iif).

**Scenario:** a contradictory FBF term (`then routing-instance X; discard`) persisted via an old binary or HA sync → slow-path/XDP_PASS/unfiltered-interface traffic that should DROP is steered into the target VRF (a fail-open VRF-steer in the kernel mirror).

**Fix:** in `buildPBRFromFilter`, `continue` (skip building the ip rule) when `term.Action == "discard" || term.Action == "reject"` — mirroring the userspace `is_drop` gate (#4392). Emit a degraded warning. NOTE: the uniformgates comment rationalizing the lenient path is STALE (it says userspace "UNCONDITIONALLY returns the routing table" — pre-#4392). GO (pkg/routing).

## #4535 — config/cos: three-color policer with unspecified color mode disarms forwarding instead of defaulting to color-blind (Junos parity) (ps-024 L-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-024 L-01 [Low, Junos parity] — a three-color policer with an UNSPECIFIED color mode disarms the whole dataplane instead of defaulting to color-blind policing (Junos accepts+enforces; xpf refuses to forward).

**Evidence (current master):** `pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:85-121` leaves `tcp.ColorBlind=false` when NEITHER `color-blind` nor `color-aware` is configured (the only two `ColorBlind=true` assignments are inside the `color-blind` branch). → snapshot color_blind=false (filters.go:600) → snapshot_three_color_shape_supported false (compiler.rs:508) → build_three_color_policer_state None → fail_closed. AND `userspaceSupportsThreeColorPolicers` (capabilities.go:137) returns false for any `!pol.ColorBlind` → `deriveUserspaceCapabilities` (capabilities.go:84) sets ForwardingSupported=false with a VISIBLE reason ("userspace three-color policers require color-blind mode and then discard"), surfaced in status ("Forwarding blocked by: ..."). So it's a VISIBLE whole-dataplane disarm (commit-succeeds/apply-fails split), NOT silent traffic loss.

**Scenario:** an operator ports a valid Junos `three-color-policer { single-rate {...} }` (no color statement) → Junos defaults it to color-blind + enforces; xpf commits clean but REFUSES to forward (whole-dataplane disarm) — a parity gap (xpf refuses a config Junos accepts).

**Fix:** default `tcp.ColorBlind=true` when neither `ColorBlindConfigured` nor `ColorAwareConfigured` is set (both flags already tracked) — matching Junos's color-blind default, so the policer is enforced instead of disarming forwarding. GO (pkg/config).

## #4539 — session: should_cache_local_delivery_session_on_miss caches non-handshake TCP first packets (pure PSH/null/URG) — gate-consistency hardening (ps-029 M-02, LOW) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-029 M-02 [LOW, hardening / gate-consistency] — should_cache_local_delivery_session_on_miss caches NON-handshake TCP first packets (pure PSH/null/URG/ECE-CWR-only) contrary to its "only cache off the handshake" intent.

**Evidence (current master):** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/mod.rs:1741-1789`. The gate declines caching for bare ACK (`has_ack && !has_syn`, #2151) and bare RST/FIN (`is_closing && !has_syn`, #4487) — two NARROW decline-gates. But it returns `true` (caches) for any first packet that is neither ACK-set-SYN-clear nor closing-SYN-clear — i.e. **pure PSH (0x08), null (0x00), pure URG (0x20), ECE/CWR-only**. These non-handshake anomalous/crafted first packets seed a 300s LocalDelivery session (install gate: is_initial_syn false → established=true).

**Severity is genuinely LOW / marginal** — the policy-skip is NOT exploitable: `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:899-900` re-runs the junos-host mandatory-teardown gate on EVERY LocalDelivery session hit, so a later real SYN hitting a PSH-seeded session is re-evaluated. The only residual is narrow table-churn via crafted packets (and a bare SYN already caches a 20s OPENING session on the same path, subject to SYN-flood screens). Value = gate-consistency/hardening, NOT a security fix.

**Fix:** replace the two narrow decline-gates with a SINGLE POSITIVE predicate — cache iff `has_syn(tcp_flags)` (SYN or SYN-ACK), decline every other non-SYN first packet. This subsumes both the #2151 (bare-ACK) and #4487 (bare-RST/FIN) declines AND closes the pure-PSH/null/URG gap, aligning the gate with its stated "only off the handshake" intent. Add a test: should_cache_local_delivery_session_on_miss(TCP, 0x08) → false. RUST (cargo).

## #4543 — screen: IPv4 options walk break-on-malformed-TLV bypasses source-route screen (LSRR/SSRR after a bad option never seen) (ps-027 S-03, low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-027 S-03 [LOW, screen fail-open]. userspace-dp/src/screen/extract.rs — the IPv4 options TLV walk has `if opt_len < 2 || pos + opt_len > opt_end { break; }` (and `if pos + 1 >= opt_end { break; }`). The walk checks kind==LSRR(131)/SSRR(137) BEFORE length, so an LSRR/SSRR placed AFTER a malformed option aborts the scan → saw_ipv4_source_route=false → check_source_route → Pass. No MalformedIpv4Options err variant exists (packet.rs has only TruncatedIpv4Header/TruncatedIpv6ExtChain), so no fail-closed arm. Untouched since #2973; #4167 added TRUNCATION fail-closed but not MALFORMED-OPTION fail-closed — an inconsistency with #4167's own fail-closed philosophy. Scenario: attacker crafts IHL>5 with [type=0x44,len=0x01][LSRR...] → the source-route screen the operator enabled to drop LSRR is bypassed; the packet transits carrying the source-route option (vSRX drops malformed IP options / LSRR regardless of ordering). Bounded (the exploit packet is malformed + xpf's AF_XDP forwarder doesn't honor source-routing), but a real novel fail-open in the screen contract. Fix: on a malformed TLV return Err(ScreenParseError::TruncatedIpv4Header) ('ip-malformed'), mirroring #4167; OR continue-scan past the bad byte. RUST.

## #4544 — config: duplicate host-inbound-traffic block silently loses tokens on 'load override' (zone overwrites / interface first-wins; Junos merges) (ps-027 H-01, low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-027 H-01 [LOW, config parity / silent-loss]. pkg/config/compiler_security_zones.go — zone-level `case host-inbound-traffic: zone.HostInboundTraffic = parseHostInboundNode(prop)` OVERWRITES on a second block; interface-level `iface.FindChild(host-inbound-traffic)` reads only the FIRST. VERIFY-FIRST REFUTED the review's flat-set claim: ConfigTree.SetPath reuses an existing same-key container (merges), and LoadMerge routes through FormatSet (merges) — so flat-set and load-merge do NOT lose. The ONLY reachable path is `load override` (store_command.go:196 s.candidate = tree) which splices the raw hierarchical parse; parseStatements does NOT merge same-key blocks, and commit compiles the raw candidate (no FormatSet round-trip), with no duplicate-block schema rejection. Scenario: operator hand-authors a config file with two literal `host-inbound-traffic { }` blocks under one zone/interface (e.g. system-services ssh + a separate protocols ospf block) and runs load override → the second silently overwrites (zone) or is ignored (interface); Junos MERGES them → silent config loss (DoS for a service, OR fail-open if the lost block was the restrictive one). Narrow (a Junos-EXPORTED config always shows one merged block; needs a hand-authored dup + load override). Fix: accumulate across FindChildren(host-inbound-traffic) at both zone + interface level (merge SystemServices/Protocols), OR a commit-check rejecting duplicate host-inbound-traffic blocks. GO.

## #4546 — wg: peer_has_confirmed_session ignores REJECT_AFTER_TIME → bounded ~0-1s rekey blackhole (ps-031 F7/F-271, med→low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-031 F7 (=F-271) [MED→Low, availability] — WireGuard `peer_has_confirmed_session` ignores REJECT_AFTER_TIME → a bounded ~0-1s rekey blackhole at the session-expiry boundary.

**Evidence (origin/master):** `userspace-dp/src/wg/engine.rs:729-737` `peer_has_confirmed_session` checks only `session.is_confirmed()` (an atomic bool, session.rs:217) with NO age check. Caller `coordinator/wg_control.rs:798` gates the NoSessionEdge rekey trigger on `nosession_edge && !engine.peer_has_confirmed_session(...)` — so while an expired-but-not-yet-GC'd session still reports `confirmed`, the rekey trigger is SKIPPED.

**Bounded (why Low not the review's Med):** `expire_sessions` GCs on a ~1s tick, and `try_encap` independently enforces REJECT_AFTER_TIME + arms rekey; the consumed edge re-arms on the next send. So the blackhole is ~0-1s at the rekey boundary, self-healing. Real availability nit at a rekey edge, not a persistent outage.

**Fix:** `peer_has_confirmed_session` should also check the session age against REJECT_AFTER_TIME (return false for an expired session), so the NoSessionEdge rekey fires promptly instead of waiting for the GC tick. RUST (cargo).

## #4547 — ipsec: dynamic-hostname gateway DNS resolves synchronously per-gateway (up to N×2s commit stall) (ps-031 F3, med→low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-031 F3 [MED→Low, commit latency] — IPsec dynamic-hostname gateway DNS resolution runs SYNCHRONOUSLY in the ordered commit apply, up to 2s/gateway → an N-gateway commit stalls up to N×2s under DNS failure.

**Evidence (origin/master):** `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:717-725` `resolveHostFamilyTimeout = 2s`; `defaultResolveHostFamily` does `r.LookupIPAddr` (:743); `gatewayRemoteFamilyHint` (:780-792) calls it PER gateway; `PrepareConfig` (:562-592) runs synchronously in the ordered apply. N `dynamic-hostname` gateways → up to N×2s commit stall under DNS timeout; no cache, no parallelism.

**Bounded (why Low not Med):** scoped to `dynamic-hostname` gateways only (a minority); a normal commit with resolvable/IP gateways is unaffected. Impact is commit latency, not a dataplane fault.

**Fix:** resolve the gateway family hints in parallel (bounded errgroup) and/or cache the last-good resolution, so N gateways cost ~2s not N×2s; consider resolving off the critical commit path. GO (pkg/ipsec).

## #4548 — vrrp: learned masterAdverInterval has no minimum clamp → MaxAdvertInt=1 flaps mastership (ps-031 F5, med→low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

ps-031 F5 [MED→Low, robustness] — VRRP `masterAdverInterval` learned from a peer advert with NO minimum clamp → a peer advertising MaxAdvertInt=1 drives masterDownInterval to ~30ms and flaps.

**Evidence (origin/master):** `pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1505-1507` `recordMasterAdvert` adopts `time.Duration(pkt.MaxAdvertInt)*10ms` on any `>0` value with no floor; `effectiveAdvertInterval` (:648-656) / `masterDownInterval` (:667-674) propagate it. `MaxAdvertInt=1` → 10ms → masterDownInterval ≈ 30ms → mastership flap.

**Threat-model caveat (why Low not Med):** VRRPv3 (RFC 5798) has NO packet auth, so an L2-adjacent attacker on the RETH VLAN can already fully hijack mastership (priority 255) — a strictly stronger attack. So the marginal value is guarding against a benign misconfigured/buggy peer, not an attacker.

**Fix:** clamp the learned masterAdverInterval to a sane minimum floor (e.g. the configured advertise-interval, or a hard floor like 10-30ms matching the RETH 30ms default) in `recordMasterAdvert`. GO (pkg/vrrp).

## #4549 — cluster/vrrp/ipsec: 4 LOW crypto/HA hardening residuals (VRRP hop-limit, HA heartbeat IPv4-only, PSK zeroize, election same-node-id) (ps-031 F8-F11) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

ps-031 crypto/HA LOW-hardening batch — 4 threat-model-limited / parity / misconfig residuals (verify-first triaged from ps-review-031, all present on origin/master, all LOW). Grouped per the no-dismissal rule (low-value hardening). Drive as a batch or individually when convenient.

**F8 — VRRP raw-IPv6 fallback has no hop-limit==255 check.** `pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1155-1242` `receiverIPv6` calls `ParseVRRPPacket(buf[:n], true, ...)` (:1230) with no `!= 255` check, while the AF_PACKET path (`parseAfPacketIPv6` :1364) and the IPv4-raw path (:1115) DO; `IPV6_RECVHOPLIMIT` is never set. Near-nil exploitability: VRRPv3 IPv6 uses link-local multicast ff02::12 (unroutable off-link), so an off-link attacker cannot reach the socket; the fallback path is rare (AF_PACKET-open failure). Defense-in-depth consistency. Fix: set IPV6_RECVHOPLIMIT + reject hop-limit != 255 on the raw-IPv6 fallback.

**F9 — HA heartbeat is IPv4-only.** `pkg/cluster/heartbeat_manager.go:44,50,56,63` hardcode `"udp4"` in ResolveUDPAddr/ListenPacket → an IPv6 control link is unsupported. Parity gap, Low (the control link is near-universally IPv4 point-to-point). Fix: accept an IPv6 control-link address (udp6/udp).

**F10 — IPsec PSK not zeroized.** `pkg/config/secret.go:45` `type Secret string` (immutable Go string, no wipe); `Reveal()` returns `string(s)`; `normalizePSK` (`ipsec/crypto.go:65`) returns a new string. WG uses `Zeroizing<[u8;32]>` (engine.rs:215/245, #4103) — an inconsistency. Caveat: Go strings cannot be reliably zeroized (immutable/interned/GC-copied), and the swanctl conf is written 0600 plaintext on disk anyway (strongSwan must read it), so the heap copy is secondary. Defense-in-depth only.

**F11 — Cluster election same-NodeID split-brain.** `pkg/cluster/election.go:196-199` dual-active tie `localEff==peerEff && nodeID>peerNodeID` is false when nodeIDs are EQUAL → `electNoChange` "winner stays" → both stay PRIMARY (preempt path :172-181 same). Requires both nodes misconfigured with the same node-id (invalid config); no deterministic tie-break fallback. Misconfig-only, Low. Fix: add a deterministic final tie-break (or reject same-node-id at config/join time).

## #4562 — config: navigatePath intermediate multi-key descent walks only first sibling → path-scoped show/display-set drops duplicate-context block (ps-035 N-1, low display-only) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-07)

ps-035 N-1 [LOW, display-only] — navigatePath intermediate multi-key descent walks only the FIRST matching sibling's subtree, so a path-scoped `show`/`display-set` drops a duplicate-context block.

**Evidence (origin/master):** `pkg/config/ast.go:211` — the non-terminal multi-key branch does `current = matched[0].Children` (single-key twin at ast.go:242). When >1 sibling shares the same full multi-key prefix AND the display path continues deeper, only the first sibling's subtree is walked. This is the same read-all-siblings class as #3980 (which fixed the TERMINAL single-key case) / #3842 / #2419 — but the INTERMEDIATE descent still descends into matched[0] only.

**Scenario:** a hand-authored HIERARCHICAL config with two duplicate `from-zone untrust to-zone trust { ... }` blocks → two identical 4-key sibling nodes. `show configuration security policies from-zone untrust to-zone trust policy B` (path descends PAST the 4-key node) sets current to block A's children → policy B is omitted from the scoped show / `| display set`.

**Why LOW (display-only, not a bypass):** navigatePath is DISPLAY-ONLY — all 5 callers are in ast_format.go; the compiler reads the full AST directly, so the "hidden" policy is still ENFORCED (no forwarding/security bypass). Preconditions are narrow: a hand-authored duplicate-context config (flat-set SetPath MERGES same-key containers so flat-set never triggers it) AND a path-SCOPED display command (an unscoped `show configuration` renders the whole tree fine, so full-config backups are intact). Only a path-scoped display-set backup could drop a statement on restore.

**Fix:** accumulate children across ALL `matched` siblings (not just matched[0]) in the intermediate-descent branch at ast.go:211, mirroring #3980's terminal read-all-siblings fix onto the descent; same for the single-key branch at ast.go:242. GO (pkg/config).

## #4565 — nat64 HA: reverse-translation of a promoted synced NAT64 session needs Nat64ReverseInfo (orig v6 addrs) synced — wire-field follow-up to #4512 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

Follow-up to #4512/#4564 (noted out-of-scope there). #4564 added reserve-on-standby (prevents the post-failover 1:N port-reuse collision — the #4381 BIB violation across failover). But a promoted node still cannot REVERSE-TRANSLATE a v4→v6 reply for a NAT64 session established on the PEER: the reverse mapping needs the original v6 source/dest addresses (Nat64ReverseInfo), which are NOT carried on the synced NatDecision (only the translated port rides it). So after failover, an in-flight NAT64 session's return traffic can't be reconstructed to the original v6 endpoints until the session re-establishes. Fix: sync Nat64ReverseInfo (orig v6 addrs) as a new tag-matched wire field (Go+Rust, like #4477) + reconstruct the reverse BIB entry on the standby at handle_upsert_synced. Wire-field-sized follow-up. Distinct from #4518 (same-node reload) + #4564 (reserve-on-standby, same-tuple collision).

## #4567 — screen: UDP-flood non-first fragment counts in a separate (dst_ip,0) CMS bucket, splitting from (dst_ip,port) (ps-036-c3-4 L-01, low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

ps-036-cohort3-4 L-01 [LOW, screen counting consistency]. A fragmented UDP flood splits its CMS count across two buckets: first/atomic fragments carry L4 and take the flow path counting at (dst_ip, real_port e.g. 53) (inspect.rs:1277, :265-267), but non-first fragments go the FLOWLESS path with dst_port=0 (poll_stages.rs:491-503) → udp_flood_drop (mod.rs:681-693) → increment_ip_port(dst_ip, 0) (syn_rate.rs:212/229). So a fragmented UDP flood to victim:53 counts first-fragments at (ip,53) and trailing at (ip,0) — neither bucket alone crosses the threshold.

**Severity LOW (review's '2x effective threshold' framing DOWNGRADED):** that 2x is raw IP-FRAGMENT packet count; effective per-port DATAGRAM DELIVERY is still capped correctly by first-fragment counting (a datagram needs its first fragment, counted at (ip,port)). The residual is only un-reassemblable trailing-fragment NOISE, double-bounded by (a) the shared (ip,0) bucket cap and (b) the 8x per-zone aggregate ceiling; the degradation is already documented-deliberate at mod.rs:675-679. vSRX-parity ('an admit vSRX would deny') plausible but unproven. Novel — not in any open issue / prior ps-review / all_findings.txt (#3902 was a different closed fail-open).

**Fix:** for a non-first UDP fragment, call the per-IP-only increment(dst_ip, ...) (syn_rate.rs:197, already used by the ICMP flood path) instead of increment_ip_port(dst_ip, 0, ...) — folding trailing fragments into a consistent per-IP abstraction so they don't dilute into a separate (ip,0) bucket. OR document as a known limitation (partly already at mod.rs:675-679). RUST.

## #4569 — policy: non-first fragment bypasses a port-bearing DENY when a later permit-any exists (flowless l4_present=false skips the DENY) (ps-036-c7 F-001, low-med fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

ps-036-cohort7 F-001 [LOW-MEDIUM, policy fail-open] — a non-first fragment bypasses a port-bearing DENY policy when a later PERMIT-any rule exists.

**Evidence (origin/master):** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:3586-3620` calls the flowless transit zone-policy with `l4_present=false` (a non-first fragment is flowless per #2344, dst_port=0). `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:1856-1876` `ApplicationMatcher::matches()` gates every port-bearing term behind `if l4_present` → returns `None` ("rule does not apply") for a non-first fragment. So a DENY rule whose match is a port-bearing app (e.g. junos-https) is SKIPPED (not denied); first-match evaluation continues to a later `permit any/any/any` → PERMIT → the fragment is forwarded.

**Scenario:** operator config "deny HTTPS from 10.0.0.0/8" (a port-bearing app DENY) followed by a permit-rest. A non-first fragment of an HTTPS flow from 10.0.0.0/8 skips the DENY (l4_present=false) and falls to the permit → forwarded. The DENY is not enforced on non-first fragments.

**Why LOW-MED (bounding factor):** the FIRST fragment (carrying the L4 header) IS matched + DROPPED by the DENY, so the destination cannot reassemble a complete transport datagram of the denied flow. Only non-first fragments (payload without a transport header) leak → residual harm = reassembly-buffer DoS + theoretical overlapping-fragment evasion (bounded by RFC 5722 / modern OS fragment hardening). Real policy fail-open + Junos divergence, but capped below full MEDIUM.

**Novel (not dup):** #3291/#4024 (CLOSED) fixed the total-bypass / deny-ALL direction (default-deny now drops flowless fragments); F-001 needs the specific "deny-SPECIFIC-then-permit-rest" ordering they don't cover. The code comment at mod.rs:3446-3450 documents only the fail-CLOSED twin ("L4-specific-PERMITTED flows fall to default policy"), never this fail-OPEN twin. Not #2387/#4533.

**Fix — two tiers:**
1. MINIMAL (Junos-aligned, secure-default): fail-closed an L4-ambiguous non-first fragment against any L3-overlapping DENY it SKIPPED — if a fragment would fall through to a permit only because a port-bearing DENY whose src/dst-zone/address overlaps was skipped for l4_present=false, DROP it (deny wins for the ambiguous fragment). CAVEAT: over-drop risk — a legit non-denied-port fragment from the same L3 gets dropped; this is the Junos fragment-association behavior (security over availability). Needs a security-matrix test + careful scoping.
2. PRINCIPLED (deferred): a fragment-association-cache — remember the first-fragment's verdict keyed on (src,dst,frag-id) + apply it to all fragments of that datagram. Bigger; the correct long-term fix.

Recommend the minimal fail-closed with a security-matrix smoke, OR /research the fragment-association-cache if the over-drop trade-off needs a decision. RUST.

## #4570 — ra: configEqual omits ReachableTime/RetransTimer → a commit changing only those two RA fields is not applied to the wire (ps-036-c12-14, low) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

ps-036-cohort12-14 [LOW, config-change-not-applied]. pkg/ra/ra.go:797-840 configEqual's scalar comparison list ends at SourceLinkLocal and NEVER references ReachableTime / RetransTimer. buildRA DOES stamp them onto the wire (pkg/ra/sender.go:718-719, the #4307 fix), and Apply gates the sender restart on configEqual (ra.go:282 → `continue` when equal). So a day-2 commit changing ONLY `reachable-time` and/or `retransmit-timer` (RA fields in pkg/config/types_routing.go:346-347) → configEqual returns true → the RA sender is NOT restarted → the wire keeps advertising the OLD ReachableTime/RetransTimer until an unrelated RA-field edit or a daemon restart.

**Severity LOW:** config-authoring trigger only (not remote/attacker); blast radius = RFC 4861 ND host timing hints (ReachableTime/RetransTimer are advisory host-side ND timers, no forwarding/security bypass, NOT fail-open); self-healing on the next unrelated RA edit or restart. But a genuine 'commit clean = enforced' violation — the codebase's OWN #4119 comment in configEqual recognizes the identical bug class for the sibling DefaultLifetimeSet field, corroborating it's real. Not dup (#4307 = wire-stamping, #2865 = dead-sender — neither covers change-detection).

**Fix:** add `a.ReachableTime != b.ReachableTime || a.RetransTimer != b.RetransTimer` to configEqual's scalar list (~ra.go:805) + a configEqual unit test asserting a reachable-time-only / retransmit-timer-only change is detected as NOT-equal (so Apply restarts the sender). One-liner follow-up to #4307. GO.

## #4572 — dataplane: heartbeat map zero-init loop bound uint32(cfg.Workers)*32 overflows on a negative workers value → 4.29B-iter apply hang (ps-037-A6 F-A6-001, low DoS) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

ps-037-A6 F-A6-001 [LOW, control-plane DoS — apply/commit hang, NOT fail-open]. pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:179 `for slot := uint32(0); slot < uint32(cfg.Workers)*2*16; slot++` (heartbeat map zero-init). UserspaceConfig.Workers is int; compiler_system.go:738 SWALLOWS the Atoi error so a config value `workers -1` survives as -1. STRICT commit rejects it (ValidateIntegerMin(1), schema_system.go:258) — BUT the LENIENT ingress (Store.Load / SyncApply, configstore/store.go:398) downgrades the schema violation to a WARNING and continues. So a persisted / hand-edited / old-HA-peer config carrying `workers -1` reaches programBootstrapMapsLocked with cfg.Workers=-1 → uint32(-1)*2*16 = uint32(-32) mod 2^32 = 4,294,967,264 iterations of heartbeatMap.Update → apply/commit hangs for HOURS.

**Real absent-clamp inconsistency:** the SAME function clamps one line up — QueueCount: uint32(maxInt(cfg.Workers,1)) (line 155), and line 356 uses maxInt(status.Workers,1) — but line 154 (Workers:) and line 179 (loop bound) use the RAW value.

**Severity LOW:** DoS (apply hang) not fail-open; needs a trusted config source already carrying a negative int (no packet-path / unauth injection). But it violates the stated lenient-path 'WARN not hang' doctrine (#1960 class) and the fix is trivial.

**Fix:** clamp before the loop — `w := maxInt(cfg.Workers, 1)` (optionally an upper cap) — and use w at line 154 (Workers:) + line 179 (loop bound), mirroring line 155. NOVEL (gh search returns only worker-semantics issues, none for this overflow; not in the #4517-#4571 backlog). GO.

## #4573 — vrrp/config: VRRP GroupID (VRID) range unvalidated → uint8 truncation to RFC-reserved VRID + priority Atoi-swallow (ps-037-A3 B-001/B-002, low-med) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

ps-037-A3 B-001 + B-002 [LOW-MEDIUM, VRRP config-validation / HA cold-boot risk] — VRRP GroupID (VRID) has no range validation → uint8 truncation to a wrong/RFC-reserved VRID; and the priority/hold-time flat-set parse swallows the Atoi error.

**B-001 (Low-Med) — VRID range unvalidated:** `pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go` vrrpGroupSchemaNode (the instance slot has NO keyValidator); `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:695-698` Atoi drops non-numeric but STORES an out-of-range numeric; `pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1148/1249/1364/1425/1834/1849` do `uint8(vi.cfg.GroupID)` wire truncation with no runtime guard. Scenario: operator types `vrrp-group 256` → truncates to VRID 0 (RFC 5798 reserved) → a strict RFC peer (Juniper) discards the advert → the VIP never masters → HA cold-boot blackhole; OR `vrrp-group 1` + `vrrp-group 257` on aliases both map to VRID 1 → cross-talk / dual-master. NOVEL: the schema comment defers typing vrrp-group ids, but its safety rationale ("garbage ids silently drop") only holds for NON-numeric garbage — an OUT-OF-RANGE numeric produces a LIVE wrong-VRID instance. The chassis RG-id analog the comment cites as its model WAS subsequently hardened (validateChassisClusterStrict, compiler_validate_strict_chassis.go:72, MaxHeartbeatRedundancyGroupID=255); VRRP was left unguarded — that asymmetry is the gap. Capped below High: operator-misconfig only, no external attack surface. Fix: add validateVRRPGroupIDStrict mirroring validateChassisClusterStrict (hard-reject ID<1 || ID>255 on strict commit, warn on lenient/HA-sync #1960) + a defensive range check at pkg/vrrp instance creation.

**B-002 (Low) — priority/hold-time Atoi swallow:** `pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:732` (flat-set) + `:817` (hierarchical) do `vg.Priority, _ = strconv.Atoi(...)`. Priority DOES have a schema validator (ValidateInteger(1,255)) so strict commit rejects; only the lenient load/HA-sync path is exposed, and it's fail-closed (priority 0 = resignation) — a narrow latent parser bug. Fix: `if n, err := strconv.Atoi(...); err == nil { vg.Priority = n }`. Folds into B-001.

GO (pkg/config + pkg/vrrp defensive guard). NOTE: VRRP config-validation — a light test-failover to confirm a VALID vrrp-group still commits + masters is nice-to-have (the change only rejects INVALID configs, so failover timing for valid configs is unaffected).

## #4576 — SECURITY: request system zeroize does not wipe .configdb SSOT or master.key → prior tenant's config + IKE/WG/SNMP secrets survive factory reset (ps-037-A4 A4-01/A4-04, HIGH) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

ps-037-A4 A4-01 + A4-04 [HIGH, factory-reset data leak] — request system zeroize / performZeroizeWipe does NOT wipe the .configdb SSOT or the master.key → the prior tenant's config + secrets survive a factory reset.

**Evidence (origin/master):** performZeroizeWipe (pkg/.../server_diag.go:755-772) removes only top-level /etc/xpf/*.conf + rollback* files. But the ACTUAL source-of-truth is /etc/xpf/.configdb/ — active.json (store.go:195), master.key (db.go:71, crypto.go:34), rollback.N.json — and NONE of these are removed. `git grep RemoveAll` confirms nothing anywhere removes .configdb. Store.Load (store_persist.go:19) reloads active.json on next boot.

**Scenario:** operator runs `request system zeroize` (or a factory-reset flow) intending to wipe the device for RMA / resale / re-tenant. The top-level .conf files are removed, but .configdb/active.json (the full committed policy: security policies, address books, IKE gateways with PSKs, WireGuard private keys, SNMP communities) + master.key (which DECRYPTS the config.Secret-encrypted fields) SURVIVE. The next boot reloads the prior tenant's complete config + secrets. A subsequent owner / a device pulled from a decommission pile has the prior tenant's cleartext-recoverable secrets.

**Severity HIGH:** a real data-at-rest leak across the trust boundary a zeroize is SUPPOSED to close (RMA/resale/multi-tenant). Not a packet-path bug, but zeroize is a security primitive + this defeats it. NOT dup — #4108 is zeroize RBAC/audit only, #4549 is in-memory PSK zeroize; neither removes .configdb.

**Fix:** in performZeroizeWipe, `os.RemoveAll("/etc/xpf/.configdb")` — KEY-FIRST (remove master.key first, then the encrypted data, so a crash mid-wipe doesn't leave decryptable data behind), then the rest of .configdb. Explicitly decide the .config.journal policy (the JSONL audit journal may also carry commit context — wipe or retain-by-design, documented). A4-04 (master.key survives) is the SAME root cause + same fix — folded here. GO (server_diag.go). Add a test asserting post-zeroize .configdb is absent + a fresh Load yields the default/empty config (no prior policy/secrets).

## #4577 — configstore: commit-confirmed timer is in-memory only (not persisted) → daemon crash in the window makes an unconfirmed config permanent (ps-037-A4 A4-03, med) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

ps-037-A4 A4-03 [MEDIUM, safety-hatch loss]. confirmTimer = time.AfterFunc (store_commit.go:267-271) — the commit-confirmed rollback deadline is IN-MEMORY only; no confirm.json is persisted, and Store.Load never re-arms it. So a daemon crash (or reboot) inside the confirm window makes the UNCONFIRMED config PERMANENT — the safety hatch (auto-rollback if not confirmed) is silently lost. The classic risk: an operator commits a config that strands management (bad mgmt-interface/firewall change), relies on commit-confirmed to auto-revert, but the daemon crashes → the stranding config is now permanent + the operator is locked out. NOVEL (not #4378). Fix: persist the confirm deadline + the prev-tree (a confirm.json in .configdb); on Store.Load, if a pending confirm is past its deadline → rollback to prev-tree; if still within the window → re-arm the timer. GO (pkg/configstore).

## #4584 — vrrp: a held lower-priority master that dies mid-preempt-hold isn't detected until holdTime expires → up to ~holdTime VIP blackhole (ps-037-A5 A5-02, med) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

ps-037-A5 A5-02 [MEDIUM, HA availability] — a held lower-priority VRRP master that DIES mid-preempt-hold is not detected until the hold timer expires → up to holdTime blackhole.

**Evidence (origin/master):** pkg/vrrp/instance.go:819-829 + armPreemptHold (:776-782). When a higher-priority node returns and defers preemption of a live lower-priority master (`preempt hold-time <N>`), arming the hold leaves masterDownTimer IDLE, and handleBackupRx never resets a liveness timer for a `preempt && lower` advert. So when the held (VIP-owning, forwarding) lower-priority master DIES mid-hold, nothing detects the silence until preemptHoldTimer expires.

**Scenario:** Node A (priority 100, `preempt hold-time 300`) returns after a reboot, defers preemption of the live Node B (priority 90, MASTER, owns the VIP). B crashes 5s into the hold. A takes over only at +300s → ~295s VIP blackhole for a DEAD master. This violates the design's own "dead master → immediate takeover" invariant. Reachable — `preempt hold-time` is a real config leaf (compiler_interfaces.go:749).

**Why MEDIUM (not HIGH):** requires the preempt-hold config + the held master to die mid-hold (a specific but real operational sequence); bounded to the configured hold-time; a dead master (not a security bypass). Codex's PRIMARY mechanism (a strict `>` boundary at the masterDownTimer fire) is REFUTED — recordMasterAdvert stamps lastMasterSeen (:1536) before the timer reset, so a true dead-master fire takes over immediately. But the FIRST trace (held-master-death-during-hold, masterDownTimer idle) is real. #2900 enumerated preempt-off/track-demote but NOT held-master-death.

**Fix:** when arming the preempt hold, ALSO re-arm a liveness watchdog (masterDownTimer for masterDownInterval); on its fire while preemptHoldArmed, if lastMasterSeen is stale → disarm the hold + becomeMaster() NOW; else re-arm + continue the hold. GO (pkg/vrrp). NEEDS test-failover (VRRP failover-path change).

## #4585 — SECURITY: zeroize leaves rendered service-config secrets on disk until the completing reboot (/etc/frr/frr.conf 0644 routing-auth, /etc/swanctl PSK, /etc/kea) — follow-up to #4576 (med, HIGH if bootstrap skips reconcile) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

- **/etc/frr/frr.conf** — mode 0644 WORLD-READABLE (frr/manager.go:563); the managed section carries BGP MD5 / OSPF / IS-IS auth secrets.
- **/etc/swanctl/conf.d/<snippet>** — IKE PSKs (ipsec/manager.go:148, 0600).
- **/etc/kea/kea-dhcp{4,6}.conf** — (dhcpserver.go:80-81, 0644).
(WireGuard keys are config-only → in .configdb → already wiped by #4582.)

These are cleared only when the daemon RECONCILES TO EMPTY on the COMPLETING REBOOT (ipsec.clearConfig removes the snippet; frr.Clear strips the managed section). **OPEN QUESTION (must verify):** does a POST-zeroize BOOTSTRAP boot with NO xpf.conf actually reconcile FRR/IPsec/Kea to empty? If the reconcile is gated on a committed config existing, a bootstrap boot may SKIP it → frr.conf routing-auth would be a PERSISTENT residual, not transient. If so this is HIGH, not MED.

**Fix:** in performZeroizeWipe (server_diag.go), also erase the rendered service configs directly — /etc/frr/frr.conf's managed section (or the file if xpf owns it), /etc/swanctl/conf.d/xpf* snippets, /etc/kea/kea-dhcp{4,6}.conf — mirroring the key-first + error-surfacing discipline of #4582. VERIFY-FIRST the reconcile-on-bootstrap question to set the severity. GO.

## #4598 — SECURITY: zeroize leaves xpf-provisioned OS login accounts (/etc/shadow hashes, SSH authorized_keys, sudoers) → re-tenanted device grants prior tenant login + sudo (follow-up to #4585, HIGH) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

SECURITY follow-up to #4585/#4576 (from the #4595 hostile review). OS LOGIN ACCOUNTS survive zeroize — arguably a BIGGER re-tenant leak than #4576/#4585 because it grants LOGIN + SUDO to a re-tenanted device.

**Evidence:** xpf provisions OS users with:
- password hashes in **/etc/shadow** (pkg/.../login_password.go)
- SSH **authorized_keys** (daemon_system.go:839)
- sudoers **/etc/sudoers.d/xpf-***
All are secret/access-bearing, ALL written OUTSIDE /etc/xpf, and ALL SURVIVE zeroize: applySystemLogin runs only inside the boot-time applyConfig, which post-zeroize is SKIPPED (bootstrap mode / ActiveConfig()==nil — same boot-skip verified in #4595). Even a full reconcile early-returns on an empty config and never userdel's. So a re-tenanted / RMA'd / resold device still has the prior tenant's login accounts + SSH keys + sudo rights.

**Severity: HIGH** (grants interactive login + privilege escalation to the next owner — worse than a config-secret read).

**Fix (needs care — UID-keyed-marker-aware teardown, #1944 class):** in performZeroizeWipe, remove the xpf-PROVISIONED users only (not the operator's own / system accounts): userdel the xpf-managed login-class users, remove their authorized_keys, remove /etc/sudoers.d/xpf-*. Must be marker/ownership-aware (like the device-map #1944 managed-allowlist) so it does NOT nuke a non-xpf admin account or strand access. VERIFY-FIRST how xpf tracks which users it provisioned (a marker, a login-class registry) — if there's no clean ownership marker, this may need /research to define the teardown contract. GO (the zeroize + login provisioning path).

A Junos `security policies global policy <p> match from-zone` /
`match to-zone` (#3148) may carry a **zone list** (`[ trust dmz ]`). xpf
models the scope as a single string:

- `config.PolicyMatch.FromZone` / `.ToZone` are `string`
  (`pkg/config/types_security.go:350`).
- The compiler fills each from only the FIRST value token —
  `pol.Match.FromZone = m.Keys[1]` / `= m.Children[0].Name()`
  (`pkg/config/compiler_security_policy.go:247-256`).

Before #4505 a two-zone scope silently compiled to a one-zone scope
(`dmz` dropped, `SchemaValidate` returned nil). #4505 (L12) tagged both

commit ("the extra token would be silently dropped") — a correct interim,
but it does not implement the Junos behavior.

**Real fix (needs-research):** model the scope as a zone list end-to-end —
`FromZone`/`ToZone` -> `[]string` (or a dedicated scope set), teach the
compiler to accumulate `Keys[1:]` + `Children` (the #2419 dual-shape /
`multi: true` pattern, see `docs/config-schema.md`), and teach the
scoped-global matcher to test membership against the set. Fold in the
codex-164 vsrx-parity follow-ups **L04/L05** (file the multi-zone scope as a
parity gap) and add **L12's** positive-path list acceptance test once the
model lands. Remove the `scalar: true` guard as part of the same change.

## #4627 — intrazone-default-permit (H01-H03): product decision — likely already parity-correct (fail-closed), bench real vSRX before any opt-in knob [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

Split out from the #4420 host-inbound/policy-parity audit cluster (findings
H01/H02/H03). This is a **product/security-posture decision**, not a clean
driveable parity fix, so it is tracked separately with the converged plan.

## The finding (H01/H02/H03)
- **H01**: vSRX intrazone default-**permit** is missing from the Rust runtime —
  a same-zone flow matching no explicit rule falls to `default_action`
  (`userspace-dp/src/policy.rs` cold path, returns `state.default_action`;
  there is no `from_id == to_id` special-case).
- **H02**: the Go `MatchPolicies` simulators mirror the gap
  (`pkg/grpcapi/server_cluster.go`, `pkg/api/security.go` — exact zone-pair
  walk then `deny (default)`, no intrazone branch).
- **H03**: an intrazone flow is counted against the reserved
  `DEFAULT_POLICY_COUNTER_IDX` / `DEFAULT_POLICY_SENTINEL_ID`, not a distinct
  `intrazone-default-permit` pseudo-policy.

## Converged verdict: PLAN-DEFER (do NOT ship unconditional fail-open)
The finding's premise ("Junos permits same-zone traffic by default") is
**contested by the most authoritative source** and xpf's current fail-closed
intrazone behavior is very likely **already Junos-parity-correct**.

- **ScreenOS** (the origin of the myth) DID permit intrazone by default
  (`set zone <z> block` toggled it) — but that knob was **not** carried into
  SRX flow mode.
- **Juniper community expert answer, SRX-specific** (highest authority):
  *"No, in srx intra-zone traffic is not allowed by default. If you want to
  allow this, you need a security policy from-zone INTERNAL to-zone INTERNAL."*
  (community.juniper.net/discussion/intra-zone-traffic)
- Modern Junos SRX/vSRX has **no per-zone intrazone knob**; with no such knob,
  intrazone is subject to the same `default-policy` (deny-all) as interzone.
- The myth survives because branch-SRX *factory-default* configs ship an
  explicit `from-zone trust to-zone trust` permit — a shipped policy, not
  implicit runtime behavior.

xpf current behavior is fail-closed under the standard `default-policy
deny-all` (present in every shipped config), which matches authoritative SRX.
An **operator workaround exists today**: `set security policies from-zone X
to-zone X policy <p> ... then permit` compiles and matches via the normal
zone-pair tier (`zone_pair_key(from, to)` packs `from == to` fine; no Go
validator rejects `from-zone == to-zone`).

## #4647 — DHCP-server-in-cluster non-functional with canonical reth1.0 config + runtime knob-flip is a silent no-op (found via #2261 live smoke) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-08)

Two real bugs the #2261 DHCP-lease-failover smoke surfaced on the loss cluster (the memfile loader itself PASSED; these are in the surrounding enablement plumbing).

**BUG A (serious — cluster DHCP server never starts with the documented config).** `filterDHCPConfigForMasterRGs` (pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:1084) keeps a dhcp-local-server group only if its resolved interface string-EQUALS a master-RG reth interface. For an UNTAGGED reth unit: `rethInterfacesForRG` returns the member WITHOUT a unit suffix (`ge-0-0-1`), while `resolveDHCPRethInterfaces` (daemon_ha.go:1331) resolves `reth1.0` → `ge-0-0-1.0` (ResolveReth keeps the `.0`, pkg/config/types.go:97). Exact match FAILS → filter returns nil → daemon_apply.go:1077 `ApplyClusterCommit(nil)` → `clearFamilyLocked` (pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:280/377) REMOVES /etc/kea/kea-dhcp4.conf → Kea stays `failed`. **Falsification:** changing only `interface reth1.0`→`reth1` flipped Kea config generation from never-happening to PRESENT+serving. So DHCP-server-in-cluster is entirely non-functional with the canonical Junos `interface reth1.0` config in docs/ha-cluster-userspace.conf. FIX: normalize/strip the trailing `.0` for untagged units (or match on the base interface) in the filter so `ge-0-0-1.0` matches `ge-0-0-1`.

**BUG B (enablement gap — runtime knob-flip silent no-op).** `runDHCPLeaseSyncLoop` (pkg/daemon/daemon_dhcp_lease_sync.go:91) is launched ONLY from the cluster sync-comms setup block (daemon_ha_sync.go:811-812), gated on the knob at connect time. `set chassis cluster dhcp-lease-synchronization; commit` on a RUNNING cluster does NOT start the push loop — counters stayed 0/0 after the knob-ON commit; only an xpfd restart made them 4/4. FIX: start/stop the lease-sync loop on the knob-flip (a commit that toggles dhcp-lease-synchronization must (re)launch or stop the loop without a restart).

Also (lab-env, minor): test/incus/dhcp-lease-failover.sh invokes `xpf-cli` (binary is `cli`/`/usr/local/sbin/cli`) and defaults DHCP_CLIENT_IFACE=eth1 (LAN host has eth0) — 2 small script fixes so it runs as-is. GO. RED-on-revert: BUG-A a reth1.0 dhcp-local-server group survives the master-RG filter (Kea config generated); BUG-B a knob-flip commit launches the loop (counters increment without restart).

## #4705 — configstore: split system stanzas silently disable master-password config encryption (plaintext secrets on disk) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`masterPasswordPRF` in `pkg/configstore/crypto.go` resolves the master-password
PRF via a single first-match walk, so a config whose `master-password` lands in a
**second** top-level `system {}` stanza is missed and the whole config DB is
written to disk **in plaintext** even though the operator configured
master-password encryption.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding High-2. Verified GENUINE on current master
(`cae466c7b`).

## Evidence (origin/master)
`pkg/configstore/crypto.go:42-53`:
```go
func masterPasswordPRF(tree *config.ConfigTree) string {
    ...
    sys := tree.FindChild("system")          // returns the FIRST system child only
    if sys == nil { return "" }
    mp := sys.FindChild("master-password")   // absent in first block -> nil
    if mp == nil { return "" }
    ...
}
```
`config.ConfigTree.FindChild` (`pkg/config/ast.go:130`) returns the first matching
top-level child. Split `system {}` stanzas persist as **separate sibling nodes**
(the compiler handles this shape elsewhere with `FindChildren` /
`systemBlocksOf` — `pkg/configstore/dataplane_retire.go:140`). The crypto path was
never migrated to the multi-block helper.

## Failure scenario
```
system { host-name fw-1; }
system { master-password { pseudorandom-function sha256; } }
```
1. Tree has two sibling `system` nodes.
2. `masterPasswordPRF` finds the first (`host-name` only), no `master-password`,
   returns `""`.
3. `maybeEncryptTreeJSON` (`crypto.go:70-73`) sees `prf==""` and returns the
   config body unencrypted -> `writeTreeMarked` persists `active.json` with all
   secrets (IKE PSKs, auth keys, SNMP communities) in clear text.

*(truncated — 64 lines total)*

## #4706 — config: duplicate address-set stanzas silently drop earlier members (no merge-by-name) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`parseAddressBookEntries` merges duplicate `address <name>` nodes by name
(#2222) but the sibling `address-set` case builds a fresh struct and does
`ab.AddressSets[as.Name] = as`, so two sibling same-name `address-set` nodes make
the second overwrite the first — earlier members are silently lost.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding High-1 (verified GENUINE, downgraded to Low).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/config/compiler_security_addressbook.go:251-266`:
```go
case "address-set":
    if len(child.Keys) >= 2 {
        as := &AddressSet{Name: child.Keys[1]}
        for _, member := range child.Children { ... }
        ab.AddressSets[as.Name] = as   // overwrite, no merge-by-name
    }
```
Contrast the `address` case (~L243-250) which fetches `ab.Addresses[name]` and
merges via `mergeAddressNode`.

## Failure scenario
Two literal `address-set S { address a1; }` and `address-set S { address a2; }`
blocks (hierarchical `load`/merge of hand-authored config): the hierarchical
parser does not merge sibling blocks, so `parseAddressBookEntries` sees two
`address-set S` nodes; the second wins and `a1` is silently dropped from `S`.
Policies matching `S` then match fewer addresses than intended (silent narrowing).

## Bounding factor
The flat-set/`set`-command path is NOT affected — `SetPath` descends into the
existing `[address-set,NAME]` node so incremental members accumulate under one
node. The bug is confined to literal duplicate hierarchical `address-set` blocks.

## Fix
Mirror the `address` merge: `as := ab.AddressSets[name]; if as==nil { as=&AddressSet{Name:name}; ab.AddressSets[name]=as }`, then append members.

## Severity — Low
- Trigger: only literal duplicate hierarchical `address-set NAME {}` blocks; the
  common flat-set path is unaffected.

*(truncated — 44 lines total)*

## #4707 — api: system CPU metrics export since-boot lifetime average as a gauge, not current CPU [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
The Prometheus system collector reads cumulative `/proc/stat` ticks and exports
`(user+nice)/total*100*cpus` and `system/total*100*cpus` as `GaugeValue` with no
previous-tick delta state — so the gauge reports a since-boot lifetime average
that barely moves as uptime grows, not the current CPU load.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Medium-13 (verified GENUINE; severity Low).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/api/metrics_system.go:322-343`: `total = user+nice+system+idle+iowait(+irq+softirq+steal)`
is cumulative since boot; collector has no `prevCPU`/`lastTick` field
(`metrics.go:151` holds only the `*Desc`). Inline comment even mislabels it
"instantaneous snapshot".

## Fix
Persist prior tick counters on the collector and compute the inter-scrape delta,
or export raw `xpf_system_cpu_seconds_total` counters labeled by mode and let
Prometheus `rate()` them.

## Severity — Low
- Blast radius: observability only — real CPU spikes are invisible on the gauge
  once uptime is high, so load alarms silently never fire.
- Why not higher: no functional/security impact. Why not dismissed: a real
  metrics-correctness defect that defeats CPU alerting.

## #4708 — api: BGP routes endpoint builds full table into one string (unbounded memory) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`bgpHandler` `case "routes"` renders every BGP route into a single
`strings.Builder` with no cap/pagination; a full internet table (900k+ routes)
materializes as one multi-hundred-MB string.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding High-4 (verified GENUINE; severity Low).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/api/routing.go:85-93`:
```go
case "routes":
    routes, err := s.frr.GetBGPRoutes()   // no cap; status_parse.go:299 already materializes full text
    ...
    for _, route := range routes {
        fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-24s %-20s %s\n", route.Network, route.NextHop, route.Path)
    }
```

## Fix
Cap rendered routes (first N + "…truncated" notice) or stream/paginate
(`limit`/`offset`), and bound `GetBGPRoutes` itself.

## Severity — Low (performance / DoS-resistance)
- Exploitability: endpoint is behind `authMiddleware` (`server.go:422`,
  `auth.go:29`) and default-bound to loopback `127.0.0.1:8080`; requires valid
  creds and a full-table BGP deployment. Self-inflicted, authenticated.
- Blast radius: control-plane OOM/GC thrash (~2x amplification over the already-
  unbounded `GetBGPRoutes`).
- Why not higher: not remotely/unauthenticated reachable. Why not dismissed:
  a real unbounded allocation on a core-router config.

## #4709 — cli: dispatchWithPager buffers entire command output in memory (OOM on large session tables) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`dispatchWithPager` redirects stdout to a pipe and does `io.ReadAll(r)` into a
single `[]byte`, then `strings.Split`. `show security flow session` on a large
table (up to 10M sessions) buffers GBs before any output.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Medium-2 (verified GENUINE; severity Low).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:136-148`:
```go
go func() { output, _ := io.ReadAll(r); r.Close(); outputCh <- output }()
...
lines := strings.Split(string(output), "\n")
```
No line/byte cap on the buffered output.

## Fix
Stream to a real pager subprocess (write directly to `less`), or bound the
buffered byte count with an "output truncated" sentinel.

## Severity — Low (performance)
- Trigger: local, authenticated interactive admin CLI querying its own box.
- Blast radius: CLI-process OOM on RAM-constrained appliances at scale.
- Why not higher: not network-reachable; operator-initiated. Why not dismissed:
  a genuine unbounded buffer with a realistic large-table trigger.

## #4710 — config: Secret type lacks UnmarshalYAML (redacted-sentinel guard asymmetric with JSON) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`config.Secret` implements `UnmarshalJSON` (rejects the `SecretRedacted`
sentinel via `errRedactedSecretIngest`) and `MarshalYAML`, but has NO
`UnmarshalYAML`. If YAML config ingestion is ever wired up, yaml.v3 would decode
the literal `"<redacted>"` sentinel straight into a `Secret`, bypassing the
fail-closed guard the JSON path enforces.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Medium-8 (verified: real asymmetry, LATENT — no
YAML config ingestion path exists today, so filed as defensive future-proofing).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/config/secret.go`: `MarshalJSON` (:125), `UnmarshalJSON` (:138, rejects
sentinel), `MarshalYAML` (:155) present; `git grep 'func.*Secret.*UnmarshalYAML'`
→ empty. `git grep 'yaml.Unmarshal'` over non-test `pkg/**` → no config YAML
decode path today (comment at secret.go:151 confirms "No config YAML marshaller
exists today").

## Fix
Add `func (s *Secret) UnmarshalYAML(value *yaml.Node) error` mirroring
`UnmarshalJSON` (decode to string, reject `SecretRedacted`, else assign).

## Severity — Low (enhancement / defensive)
- Not reachable today (no YAML ingestion), so no live exposure — hence not a bug.
- Becomes a real fail-open (redacted placeholder loaded as a live secret) the
  moment anyone adds YAML config loading. Cheap 6-line symmetric guard; worth
  closing the asymmetry proactively.

## #4711 — snmp: AllowsSource re-parses client CIDR prefixes per incoming v2c packet [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`SNMPCommunity.AllowsSource` calls `parseClientPrefix(cl.Prefix)` (→
`net.ParseCIDR`) for every configured client on every incoming SNMP v2c packet,
allocating on each packet instead of using prefixes pre-parsed at compile time.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Low-8 (verified GENUINE; severity Low/perf).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/config/snmp_clients.go:39-40` loops `for _, cl := range c.Clients` calling
`parseClientPrefix(cl.Prefix)`; invoked per packet at `pkg/snmp/agent.go:588`
(`handleV2cPacket`).

## Fix
Pre-parse client prefixes into `[]*net.IPNet` on `SNMPCommunity`/`SNMPClient` at
config-compile time; `AllowsSource` then does allocation-free `Contains()`.

## Severity — Low (enhancement / perf)
- SNMP is low-rate control traffic (and this runs after community lookup), so
  the per-packet parse/alloc is negligible in practice — not a hot dataplane path.
- Worth doing as a straightforward compile-time-precompute cleanup; no
  correctness impact.

## #4712 — api: show-text endpoints iterate config maps unsorted (non-deterministic output order) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`pkg/api/show_text.go` ranges over Go maps directly (schedulers, snmp
communities/trap-groups, dhcp-relay groups, filters, feed servers, address-book,
applications, v9 templates) without sorting keys, so `/show-text` responses come
back in randomized order across calls.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Low-13 (verified GENUINE; severity Low).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/api/show_text.go`: no `"sort"` import; `for name, sched := range cfg.Schedulers`
(:26) plus snmp (:63,:69), dhcp-relay (:82,:88), filters (:102), feeds (:150),
address-book (:173,:179), applications (:191,:201), v9 templates (:213).

## Fix
Collect keys into a slice, `sort.Strings`, then iterate in sorted order.

## Severity — Low
- Blast radius: cosmetic + breaks automated config diff/validation and causes
  test flakiness; no functional/security impact.
- Why not dismissed: real non-determinism in an operator/automation-facing API.

`compileBGP` parses `peer-as`/`local-as` with `strconv.Atoi` then casts to
`uint32` with no range/negative guard; `validateBGPNeighborPeerASStrict` only
checks `== 0`. `peer-as -1` wraps to 4294967295 and renders a bogus `remote-as`
into frr.conf; `local-as` has no strict validator at all.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Low-7 (verified GENUINE; severity Low).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:305` (group) and `:464` (neighbor):
```go
if n, err := strconv.Atoi(v); err == nil { peerAS = uint32(n) }   // -1 -> 4294967295
```
`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_routing.go:497`: only `if n.PeerAS == 0`.

## Failure scenario
`set protocols bgp group G peer-as -1` → Atoi=-1 → uint32=4294967295 (≠0 →
passes) → `neighbor <ip> remote-as 4294967295` in frr.conf → session never
establishes. `peer-as 4294967297` → wraps to 1 → silently wrong AS.

## Fix
Reject `n < 0 || n > 4294967295` (Atoi returns int) before the uint32 cast, or
add a range check to `validateBGPNeighborPeerASStrict` covering both peer-as and
local-as.

## Severity — Low
- Blast radius: BGP session misconfig (no crash, no security bypass) — self-
  inflicted typo escapes validation.
- Why not dismissed: silent garbage-AS rendering with no operator warning.

---

## #4714 — config: tcp-flags parser silently accepts a dangling trailing negation ("!") [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
The `tcp-flags` expression parser tracks `pendingNeg` but never checks for a
dangling `pendingNeg==true` after the token loop, so `tcp-flags "!"` or
`"syn & !"` parse without error and the trailing negation is silently dropped —
a firewall filter term ends up with a missing/weaker constraint.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Low-9 (verified GENUINE; severity Low).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/config/tcp_flags.go` parse loop: `case "!": pendingNeg = !pendingNeg; continue`.
After the loop the function only checks `required&forbidden != 0` and
`required==0 && forbidden==0` — no `if pendingNeg` guard. `tcp-flags "!"` →
returns `(0,0,false,nil)` (no constraint); `"syn & !"` → `(SYN,0,true,nil)`
(trailing `!` dropped).

## Fix
After the loop: `if pendingNeg { return 0,0,false, fmt.Errorf("tcp-flags %q: dangling negation \"!\" with no flag", expr) }`.

## Severity — Low (fail-open, correctness)
- Blast radius: a typo yields a filter term matching more than intended (the
  negated flag constraint is lost) with no commit error — fail-open on the
  missing flag.
- Why not higher: requires an operator typo in a rarely-hand-edited match;
  bounded to one filter term. Why not dismissed: silent validation bypass on a
  security-policy input.

## #4715 — cluster: Monitor.getNlHandle lazily creates cachedNlHandle without mon.mu (FD leak + data race) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`Monitor.getNlHandle()` lazily initializes `mon.cachedNlHandle` via
`netlink.NewHandle()` with no lock and no `sync.Once`, while `Monitor.Stop()`
writes `mon.cachedNlHandle=nil` under `mon.mu`. Two concurrent lock-free callers
each create a handle (one leaks a netlink socket FD), and the read/write races
`Stop()`.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Medium-11 AND ps-review-040-a5-b1 finding 1 (same
bug, both reviewers). Verified GENUINE on current master.

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/cluster/monitor.go:543-558` — `getNlHandle` reads/writes `mon.cachedNlHandle`
lock-free. Callers reach it from different goroutines lock-free:
`pollInterfaceMonitors` (`monitor.go:260`, from `poll()` after it released
`mon.mu` at :230) and `RGInterfaceReady` (`monitor.go:506`, which unlocks
`mon.mu` at :504 first; invoked from `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:627`).
`Stop()` (`monitor.go:185-190`) writes `cachedNlHandle=nil` under `mon.mu`.

## Failure scenario
Two `getNlHandle` calls both observe `cachedNlHandle==nil` → both
`netlink.NewHandle()` → the second write (`:556`) overwrites the first, leaking
one netlink socket FD; concurrently `Stop()`'s write (`:189`) data-races the
`:556` write. (In tests `mon.nlHandle` is injected and short-circuits at :544,
so the race is production-only.)

## Fix
Guard the read-modify-write of `cachedNlHandle` in `getNlHandle` with `mon.mu`
(or use `sync.Once`).

## Severity — Low-Medium (concurrency, resource-leak)
- Blast radius: a few leaked netlink FDs under concurrent poll+status, plus a
  torn-pointer data race flagged by `-race`.
- Why not higher: leak rate is bounded (only on the cold cachedNlHandle==nil
  window); no forwarding impact. Why not dismissed: an unsynchronized shared-
  field read/write with a real FD leak and a genuine `Stop()` race.

---

## #4716 — cluster: Manager.Stop() leaves rg.holdTimer running (spurious post-stop election + Manager leak) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`Manager.Stop()` stops the monitor and heartbeat goroutines but never iterates
`m.groups` to cancel active `rg.holdTimer` timers, so a takeover-hold timer armed
before Stop fires afterward — running an election on a quiesced manager and
pinning the `Manager` in memory until it elapses.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Medium-12 AND ps-review-040-a5-b1 finding 2 (same
bug, both reviewers). Verified GENUINE on current master.

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/cluster/manager.go:388-406` `Stop()` stops `monitor`/`hbSender`/`hbReceiver`
only. `pkg/cluster/readiness.go:38-50` arms
`rg.holdTimer = time.AfterFunc(m.takeoverHoldTime, func(){...runElection()/electSingleNode()...})`;
the closure guards only `if !rg.Ready { return }` (:41) — there is no `m.stopped`
flag on `Manager`.

## Failure scenario
A timer armed while `rg.Ready==true` fires after `Stop()`, takes `m.mu`, and runs
`runElection`/`electSingleNode`. In production `Stop()` is daemon teardown
(`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1823`) so the election is moot, but the timer leaks the
`Manager` until `takeoverHoldTime` elapses → goleak/test-teardown flakiness and a
lifecycle-invariant violation.

## Fix
In `Stop()`, range `m.groups` under `m.mu` and `Stop()`+nil each non-nil
`holdTimer`; optionally add an `m.stopped` check in the closure.

## Severity — Low (lifecycle / resource)
- Blast radius: leaked timer + spurious election on a stopped manager; mainly
  test-teardown flakiness (prod path is process exit).
- Why not dismissed: timers must be cancelled on shutdown; a real lifecycle leak.

---

## #4717 — upgrade: RejoinAndConfirm discards PeerAlive/SyncEstablished errors in timeout message [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`RejoinAndConfirm` captures `aerr` from `cl.PeerAlive()` and `serr` from
`cl.SyncEstablished()` each poll but, on deadline, returns an error printing only
the `alive`/`synced` booleans — discarding the underlying transport/gRPC errors
that would tell an operator WHY a rolling-upgrade rejoin failed.

## Provenance
From gemini-review-041 finding Low-2 (verified GENUINE; severity Low).

## Evidence (origin/master `cae466c7b`)
`pkg/upgrade/kernel_drain.go` `RejoinAndConfirm`: `aerr` (:123), `serr` (:124)
captured; deadline error (:129-130) formats only `alive`/`synced`.

## Fix
Retain the last non-nil `aerr`/`serr` and wrap them into the timeout error.

## Severity — Low (observability)
- No functional impact; purely loses diagnostic context during a critical
  cluster-upgrade rejoin phase, forcing operators to dig through syslog.
