## #4895 — daemon: system login user name can inject arbitrary /etc/sudoers.d directives (no username validation) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
`system login user <name>` is an untyped keyed instance with no username validator. The daemon writes a `/etc/sudoers.d/xpf-<name>` NOPASSWD grant by formatting the raw config key directly into sudoers syntax. Because the lexer decodes `\n` inside a quoted string into a literal newline, a crafted username can inject arbitrary additional sudoers directives that pass `visudo` syntax validation and are durably installed.

## Current master (origin/master)
- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go:118-119`: `user := &LoginUser{Name: userInst.name}` — key copied verbatim.
- `pkg/config/schema_system.go`: the `user` login instance has no username validator.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:1614-1621`: `applySystemLogin(cfg)` then `reconcileSudoers(cfg)` runs unconditionally.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:898`: `reconcileSudoers` writes a grant for every `Class == "super-user"` user, gating only on `Name != ""` / `!= "root"` — no OS-account-existence gate.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:943-945`: `writeSudoersGrant` does `line := fmt.Sprintf("%s ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL\n", user)` then durably writes it.

## Scenario (input → privilege escalation)
Config (flat-set / lenient load / HA config-sync) supplies:
`set system login user "x ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL\nnobody ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL" class super-user`
The lexer materializes the `\n`. `reconcileSudoers` sees `Class==super-user` and calls `writeSudoersGrant`, producing:
```
x ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL
nobody ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL
```
Both lines are valid sudoers syntax, so `visudo -cf` passes and the drop-in is installed under `/etc/sudoers.d`, granting an unmodeled account passwordless root.

## Fix
Add a strict `ValidateLoginUsername` at schema + apply boundary (POSIX/Linux account-name regex; reject whitespace, control chars, `/`, `:`, leading `-`, empty). Have `reconcileSudoers`/`writeSudoersGrant` defensively refuse unsafe names so lenient load/sync cannot bypass strict commit. Regression tests: quoted usernames containing `\n`, spaces, `/`, leading `-` are rejected and never reach `writeSudoersGrant`.

## Severity justification
High (security, CWE-74). Trigger: any path that can set a `system login user` key — including HA config-sync from a peer and lenient/tolerant config load, not only interactive commit. Blast radius: fail-open — arbitrary root-owned sudoers directives (broad `ALL` NOPASSWD grants) installed on the host, escaping the modeled login-user privilege boundary, while passing the existing `visudo` gate (a syntax validator, not a containment validator). Bounding factor: authoring `system login user … class super-user` already implies commit privilege, so on a single-admin appliance the escalation is limited; the exposure is the sync/import/multi-operator surface. Distinct from #3889 (stale-grant revocation), #1944, #4598.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-008 (area A7). Verified present on current master.

## #4896 — flowexport: NetFlow v9 pads each record but the template advertises unpadded width — records 2+ misdecode [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
The NetFlow v9 exporter pads **each** data record to a 4-byte boundary and packs multiple padded records into one Data FlowSet, but the template advertises the unpadded sum of field lengths. A standards-compliant collector advances by the template width, so every record after the first is misdecoded. Per RFC 3954 only the enclosing FlowSet may carry terminal padding — records must be contiguous at the template-advertised width.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/flowexport/netflow.go`)
- `recordSize()` L230-238: sums field lengths then `pad := (4 - size%4) % 4; return size + pad`.
- v4 template `netflowTemplateFieldsV4` field-length sum = **61** (→ padded 64); with `flowDirection` (IE 61) = 62 (→ 64).
- v6 template sum = **109** (→ padded 112); with flowDirection = 110 (→ 112).
- `encodeRecordV4`/`encodeRecordV6` return `startOff + recSize` (L427/L497) — advancing by the **padded** size, leaving 3 (or 2) zero bytes between records.
- `encodeDataFlowSetInto` writes N records at `recSize` stride. The template FlowSet advertises each field's real length (unpadded 61/109).

The IPFIX sibling uses exact template lengths, so the two exporters disagree.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
A normal session-close burst produces a multi-record Data FlowSet. Record 1 occupies bytes `[4, 4+64)`; the collector, reading the 61-byte template width, expects record 2 at `4+61 = 65`, but the encoder placed it at `4+64 = 68`. All subsequent tuple/counter/timestamp fields are shifted 3 bytes; the collector misdecodes or discards every record after the first, corrupting addresses, ports, policy analytics, counters, and timestamps precisely when telemetry volume is highest.

## Fix
Separate `recordLen` (sum of template fields, contiguous) from `flowSetLen` (header + contiguous records, rounded once at the end). Encoders return the actual field end; append records at that offset; zero only terminal set padding. Add 2-record and max-record v4/v6 golden decoders for both flowDirection modes, asserting every record boundary against the template sum. `TestV9DataRecordSizeConsistency` encodes a single record and cannot catch this.

## Severity justification
High. Trigger: any multi-record close burst to a v9 collector (the common case under load). Blast radius: silent telemetry corruption of all but the first record per packet — wrong 5-tuples, counters, policy attribution — on the security-observability path. No security boundary, no crash, cold export goroutine only, which keeps it High rather than Critical. Distinct from #2613 (zeroed advertised fields), #3740 (SourceID collision), #2866 (SrcMask=0).

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-010 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4897 — snmp: SNMPv3 authPriv-configured user can be queried at noAuthNoPriv (no per-user minimum security level) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
An SNMPv3 user configured with authentication (and privacy) can be queried with `msgFlags = 0` (noAuthNoPriv) and is served plaintext data. Auth is verified only `if msgFlags&msgFlagAuth != 0` and decryption runs only `if msgFlags&msgFlagPriv != 0`; there is no per-user minimum-security-level enforcement, so request flags can opt out of the operator's configured auth/privacy policy.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/snmp/v3.go`)
- L255-264: `if msgFlags&msgFlagAuth != 0 { … verifyAuth … }` — the HMAC/timeliness checks are entirely skipped when the request omits the auth flag.
- L~282: `if msgFlags&msgFlagPriv != 0 { decrypt } else { plaintext scopedPDU }` — no gate requiring priv for a privacy-configured user.
- User lookup (`snapshotV3User`) only rejects unknown usernames; there is no VACM/min-security-level model. #2681 fixed only the inverse case (priv-set/auth-clear).

## Scenario (input → auth/confidentiality bypass)
1. Operator configures `user monitor authentication-... privacy-...` (authPriv).
2. Attacker who knows/guesses the username sends a v3 GET/GETNEXT/GETBULK with `msgFlags = 0` naming `monitor`.
3. Both gates are skipped; the scoped PDU is decoded as plaintext and answered in plaintext.
4. The attacker reads sysDescr/sysUpTime/ifTable inventory & counters without the configured password, and can strip confidentiality by requesting authNoPriv.

## Fix
Derive a minimum security level per user: require auth whenever `authKey != nil` and require auth+priv whenever a privacy key/protocol is configured; reject lower request levels before decoding the scoped PDU. If intentional multi-level access is desired, add explicit VACM-style config rather than inferring from request flags. Replace the current "key-bearing user served at noAuthNoPriv" test with an authPriv/authNoPriv/noAuth matrix.

## Severity justification
High (security). Trigger: SNMP enabled with a v3 user and a known/guessable username (usernames are not secret); no credential needed. Blast radius: read exposure of device identity and interface inventory/counters, plus it re-opens the unauthenticated GETBULK CPU path and makes configured privacy misleading. Bounded to read surface (SET/write not asserted here) and requires SNMP enabled, keeping it High rather than Critical. Distinct from #2681 (noAuthPriv), #2611 (context).

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-012 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4898 — pkg/ipsec/manager.go: clearConfig swallows reload errors; Apply promotes state + terminates SAs before reload success [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
Two coupled reload-error / state-ordering defects in `pkg/ipsec/manager.go` `Apply`:

1. **`clearConfig()` swallows the reload error** on the empty-config branch. Deleting the last VPN routes `Apply(nil)` → `clearConfig()`, which does `_ = m.reload(); return nil` — discarding any `swanctl --load-all` failure. The non-empty `applyConfig()` path propagates reload errors (the #4433 contract, `reload_error_4433_test.go`), so the empty-clear branch is asymmetric and reports success even when strongSwan kept the old connection loaded.
2. **State promoted and SAs terminated before reload success.** `Apply` calls `swapConnNames(newNames)` (which immediately overwrites `prevConnNames`) *before* the reload, then runs `terminateRemovedConns(removed)` unconditionally after `applyErr`, even when the reload failed and the old config is still the effective loaded config.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/ipsec/manager.go`)
- L104-122 `Apply`: `removed := m.swapConnNames(newNames)` → branch to `clearConfig`/`applyConfig` → `m.terminateRemovedConns(removed)` → `return applyErr`.
- L162-169 `clearConfig`: `_ = m.reload(); return nil`.
- L200-209 `swapConnNames`: sets `m.prevConnNames = newNames` under lock and returns removed names.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
- Delete the last VPN with a transient strongSwan reload failure: `clearConfig` removes `xpf.conf`, `reload` fails, `Apply` returns nil. Commit reports the empty IPsec policy enforced while charon still carries the old connection and can re-initiate it — a decommissioned/compromised peer stays authorized.
- Replace `site-a` with `site-b` and reload fails: `swapConnNames` already promoted `prevConnNames` to `{site-b}` and `terminateRemovedConns` terminated `site-a`'s live SAs — disrupting a still-effective tunnel while forgetting `site-a` is still loaded, so a later `Clear` won't retry its cleanup.

## Fix
Make the diff two-phase: compute `removed` without mutating `prevConnNames`; reload; only on reload success promote `prevConnNames` and terminate removed SAs. Make `clearConfig()` return `m.reload()` errors like `applyConfig()`. On reload failure, preserve the old name set and skip removed-SA termination. Regression tests for `Apply(nil)`/`Clear()` with `--load-all` failing, and for replace-with-reload-failure.

## Severity justification
Medium (fail-open lifecycle). Trigger: reload failure during last-VPN delete or connection replace (rare but reachable — strongSwan transient errors, malformed peer config). Blast radius: commit reports IPsec removal/rotation succeeded while old policy stays loaded (security-sensitive teardown) AND failed applies tear down still-effective tunnels + lose cleanup bookkeeping (availability). Bounded by requiring a reload failure. Follow-up to #4433 (which fixed the daemon commit-join for the non-empty apply path only) and related to #3941.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-009 + C175-HC-046 (area A7). Verified present on current master.

## #4899 — daemon: DHCP lease-change IPsec rebind drops swanctl reload failures (no retry/health signal) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
The runtime DHCP-lease-change IPsec rebind path logs `swanctl` reload failures and returns, with no retry, dirty flag, or health signal. When a DHCP renewal changes the address on a management-only interface, `onDHCPAddressChange` bypasses full `applyConfig` and calls `reapplyIPsecForLeaseChange`, which re-renders `local_addrs` and calls `d.ipsec.Apply(...)` best-effort. If the reload fails, strongSwan keeps binding to the stale lease address and the tunnel cannot re-establish, while the daemon reports only a `slog.Warn`.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/daemon/daemon_dhcp.go`)
- L107: `d.reapplyIPsecForLeaseChange(activeCfg)`
- L123-137 `reapplyIPsecForLeaseChange`: acquires `applySem`, `if err := d.ipsec.Apply(ipsec.PrepareConfig(cfg)); err != nil { slog.Warn("failed to re-apply IPsec config after DHCP address change", "err", err) }` — no retry/health/dirty state.
- `pkg/ipsec/manager.go` `Apply`→`reload` returns load-all errors (contract used by the commit path's fail-closed join), but this caller drops them.

## Scenario (input → stale enforcement)
1. DHCP renew changes the address on an IPsec-`external-interface`-bound uplink with no explicit `local-address` (`HasDHCPBoundGateway` true).
2. Lease callback re-renders swanctl and calls `Apply`; `swanctl --load-all` fails transiently.
3. The error is logged and dropped. No dirty/retry latch, no metric. strongSwan keeps the stale `local_addrs` until another lease event, full commit, or daemon restart happens to reload successfully — the tunnel can stay down with no operator-visible signal.

## Fix
Converge like other runtime actuators: add an IPsec lease-rebind dirty flag + bounded retry loop, or route through a retry/health mechanism that records a degraded metric until `ipsec.Apply` succeeds. Seam test injecting an IPsec reload error on the lease path and asserting a retry/health/dirty state persists rather than being treated as harmless.

## Severity justification
Medium. Trigger: WAN/mgmt DHCP address change (routine) coinciding with a strongSwan reload failure. Blast radius: IPsec tunnel bound to a stale source / down, reported only as a log warning — a stale-enforcement + observability gap. Bounded by requiring a reload failure and a DHCP-bound gateway. Distinct from the commit-path fail-closed contract (#4433) and the feature that added this path (#2884); this is the runtime callback bypassing that contract.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-045 (area A7). Verified present on current master.

## #4900 — networkd: stale 10-xpf-* file delete failures are warn-only — removed host config survives a successful commit [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
`pkg/networkd` stale-file removal treats `os.Remove` failures as warn-only. A removed interface/address/bond/bridge/rename whose generated `10-xpf-*.network`/`.netdev` cannot be deleted (EACCES, read-only fs, immutable, etc.) survives a successful commit: the delete error is neither aggregated into the write-error set nor returned, and if no other generated file changed, `Apply` returns nil without a reload. The stale unit keeps applying old addresses / VRF / bond / bridge / rename on the next reload or boot.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/networkd/networkd.go`)
- L172-181 (stale sweep): `if err := os.Remove(path); err != nil { slog.Warn("failed to remove stale networkd file", ...) } else { ... changed = true }` — failure only logged.
- L225-231: write failures are aggregated into `writeErrs` and fail the commit (#2987), but stale-delete failures are not added to `writeErrs`.
- L337-341 (Clear): same warn-only pattern before reload.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
1. Operator removes the last config that generated `10-xpf-old.network`.
2. The stale sweep hits `os.Remove` failure (read-only /etc, immutable bit, etc.).
3. Only a warning is logged; `changed` stays false; `Apply` returns nil → commit reports success.
4. The surviving `.network` re-applies the removed address / VRF membership / bridge-bond / rename on reload or reboot → route leak or management-plane surprise the operator believed removed.

## Fix
Aggregate stale `os.Remove` failures alongside `writeErrs` in both `Apply` and `Clear`, still best-effort every delete and optionally reload when any change succeeded, but return a joined error when any managed file could not be removed. Add remove-failure tests mirroring the existing write-failure test.

## Severity justification
Medium. Trigger: interface/address removal with a delete failure (rare — RO fs / EACCES / immutable). Blast radius: fail-open — a stale systemd-networkd unit resurrects removed addresses/VRF/bond/bridge/rename (route leak / mgmt exposure) while commit reports success. Bounded by the low probability of `os.Remove` failing. Distinct from #2987 (write-failure) and #2988 (empty-set skip); neither covers delete failure surfacing.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-047 (area A7). Verified present on current master.

## #4901 — routing: xfrm/bond/tunnel teardown forgets failed netlink LinkDel and returns nil (orphaned links, lost ownership) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
Routing teardown paths for xfrm interfaces, bonds, and tunnels log failed netlink `LinkDel` and then drop the object from their ownership tracking and return `nil`. A transient/EBUSY/EPERM delete failure leaves the link in the kernel while the manager forgets it owned it, so a later reconcile has no memory of the orphaned xfrmi/bond/tunnel (stale addresses, enslaved members, XFRM if_id state) and callers observe a successful teardown. The VRF and tunnel **Apply** paths deliberately retain ownership on delete failure to retry — the teardown paths violate that invariant.

## Current master (origin/master)
- `pkg/routing/xfrm.go` `deleteLocked`: `if err := x.ops.LinkDel(link); err != nil { slog.Warn(...) }` then `delete(x.xfrmis, name)`; `clearLocked` returns nil.
- `pkg/routing/bond.go` `clearLocked`: `LinkDel` failure logged only, then `b.bonds = nil; return nil`.
- `pkg/routing/tunnel.go` `clearLocked`: `LinkDel` failure logged only, then `t.tunnels = nil; t.ownedNames = nil; …` and returns nil.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
A VPN bind-interface / fabric bond / tunnel is removed (or an explicit `Clear*` runs) while `LinkDel` returns EBUSY/EPERM/transient netlink error. The failed delete leaves the link; the manager still clears its tracking map and returns nil. The next Apply has no ownership record for the removed object, so the surviving link becomes an orphan with stale addresses / enslaved members / XFRM if_id state — divergence hidden from daemon and operator.

## Fix
Return joined delete errors from `Clear`/teardown, and retain tracking for objects whose `LinkDel` failed so the next reconcile retries (mirror the VRF/tunnel Apply retention). Failure-injection tests mirroring the existing Apply retention tests.

## Severity justification
Medium (observability + retention). Trigger: netlink delete failure during teardown (rare). Blast radius: fail-open — a stale xfrmi/bond/tunnel survives with stale routing state while teardown reports success and ownership is lost, so it is never retried. Bounded by low delete-failure probability and teardown-only scope. Consistent with the project's active hardening of this class (#4822 probe-pin dump failures, bond Apply link-creation failures). Distinct from the XFRM if_id-collision and GRE-keepalive fixes.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-048 (area A7). Verified present on current master.

## #4902 — daemon: unvalidated system string leaves injected into chrony/sshd/rsyslog/resolv.conf renderers (directive injection) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
Several untyped `system` string leaves are rendered verbatim into root-owned host service/resolver config files that are then reloaded, with no validator and no control-character rejection. Because the lexer decodes `\n` inside a quoted string into a literal newline, a crafted value can inject an additional directive line (or make a reload fail). Affected renderers: chrony (`system ntp server`), sshd (`system services ssh key-exchange/ciphers/macs`), rsyslog (`system syslog file/user`), and systemd-resolved / `/etc/resolv.conf` (`system domain-name`, `system domain-search`).

## Current master (origin/master)
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:291-300` `renderChronySources`: `fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s %s iburst\n", directive, server)` — raw server, no control-char check (`net.ParseIP` only picks `pool` vs `server`).
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1204-1234` `buildSSHDConfig`: `"KexAlgorithms "+strings.Join(ssh.KeyExchange, ",")`, `"Ciphers "+...`, `"MACs "+...` verbatim.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:669-695`: syslog `file`/`user` keyed values → rsyslog drop-in content + filenames verbatim.
- `pkg/daemon/system/dns.go:56-61,118-123`: `Domains=%s` / `search %s` from `combinedDomains(DomainName, DomainSearch)` verbatim.
- `pkg/config/schema_system.go`: `name-server` is typed `ValidateIPAddress`, but `domain-name`, `domain-search`, `ntp server`, ssh algorithm leaves, and syslog `file`/`user` are untyped strings.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
`set system ntp server "pool.example.net\nlocal stratum 10\n#"` renders a second chrony directive and comments out the trailing `iburst` before chrony reloads. Equivalent quoted-newline payloads add sshd directives (accepted if valid sshd syntax by `sshd -t`), rsyslog directives (`stop`), or extra `/etc/resolv.conf` lines. Values are root-owned host-service config; a lenient load / HA sync applies them outside the modeled schema, or causes persistent reload failures that read as ordinary apply degradation.

## Fix
Add typed validators per rendered token: hostname/IP for NTP servers; OpenSSH algorithm-token grammar for KEX/cipher/MAC; safe syslog file/user names; DNS label/FQDN grammar for domain-name/domain-search. Add a shared `rejectControlOrWhitespace` helper and keep defensive checks in the renderers so lenient load/sync cannot bypass strict commit. Negative tests for embedded newline/space/control characters.

## Severity justification
Medium (CWE-74). Trigger: any path that sets these leaves — including lenient/tolerant load and HA config-sync, not only interactive commit. Blast radius: directive injection into root-owned chrony/sshd/rsyslog/resolv.conf, or persistent service-reload failures. Bounded because `sshd -t`/reload validate syntax (so only syntactically-valid injected directives survive) and authoring the config implies commit privilege — lower impact than the sudoers sibling. Distinct from prior syslog-parsing, NTP/SSH inert-knob, and SCP argv-injection findings.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-049 + C175-MC-011 (area A7). Verified present on current master.

## #4903 — daemon: unauthenticated REST --api-addr :port wildcard bind bypasses the #4047 loopback clamp [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
The #4047 runtime loopback clamp for the unauthenticated REST API misclassifies the Go wildcard bind spelling `:port` (empty host) as loopback and does not clamp it. `xpfd --api-addr :8080` with no `web-management api-auth` therefore listens on all interfaces with `apiCfg.Auth == nil`, exposing mutating REST endpoints network-wide.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/daemon/daemon_cluster_bind.go`)
- L60-66 `hostIsLoopback`: `if host == "" { return true }` (and unparseable → true).
- L86: `host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(addr)` — for `":8080"` yields `host == ""`, `err == nil`.
- `clampBindToLoopback` then returns `addr, false` (not clamped) because `hostIsLoopback("")` is true.
- `cmd/xpfd/main.go` `--api-addr` flows into `apiCfg.Addr`; `daemon_run.go` calls `clampBindToLoopback(apiCfg.Addr, hasAuth)`.

## Scenario (input → bypass)
1. `xpfd --api-addr :8080` (a common "all interfaces" spelling) with no `system services web-management api-auth`.
2. `net.SplitHostPort(":8080")` → `host=""`, `err=nil`; `hostIsLoopback("")` → true; clamp returns `(":8080", false)`.
3. The REST server binds the Go wildcard (all interfaces) with `Auth == nil` — the mutating REST surface is reachable off-loopback, the exact exposure the #4047 clamp exists to prevent (`0.0.0.0:8080` is correctly clamped; `:8080` is not).

## Fix
Treat an empty host from a successful `SplitHostPort` as a wildcard: make `hostIsLoopback("")` return false for bind classification, or special-case empty host in `clampBindToLoopback` and clamp to `127.0.0.1:<port>`. Add table cases for `":8080"` and (if supported) `"[::]:8080"`. Keep unparseable no-port strings unchanged if needed, but do not treat a parsed empty host as loopback.

## Severity justification
Medium (security). Trigger: operator/unit starts with `--api-addr :8080` and no api-auth — a plausible misconfiguration, not attacker-controlled. Blast radius: fail-open — unauthenticated mutating REST endpoints reachable on every interface. Bounded to a specific bind spelling and requires the no-auth configuration; the literal-interface and `0.0.0.0` cases are already clamped. Distinct from the broader #4047/F-155 off-loopback policy; this is the empty-host wildcard the new clamp itself misclassifies.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-050 (area A7). Verified present on current master.

## #4904 — scripts/image+dist: supply-chain provenance gaps — --skip-validate still signs publishable images; Ubuntu base authenticated by unsigned same-endpoint checksum; publish gates a mutable tree then uploads replaced bytes (TOCTOU) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

Three supply-chain provenance/integrity gaps in the image bake + distribution publish
tooling. Each lets unverified or unintended bytes carry a trust-bearing signature or reach
the published tree.

## A. `--skip-validate` still produces a fully signed, publishable image set (C175-HC-013)
`scripts/image/bake.py:470`: with `--skip-validate` the validation gate downgrades to a
stderr warning and `return`s; `finalize_artifacts` (`bake.py:526`) treats that as success
and proceeds to `sign_step()`. No durable non-publishable marker is written, so `publish.py`
sees the same valid manifest/signature shape as a validated bake. -> a dev/emergency bake
is indistinguishable from a release artifact and passes the fail-closed publish gate
despite never booting/verifying the dataplane. Fix: make skip and signing mutually
exclusive, or bind a signed `validated=true` provenance field that publication requires.

## B. Base image authenticated with an unsigned same-endpoint checksum (C175-HC-028)
`scripts/image/bake.py:208-224`: the Ubuntu cloud image and its `SHA256SUMS` are fetched
from the same configurable `base_url`; no `SHA256SUMS.gpg` / Ubuntu signing-key fingerprint
/ repo-pinned digest is checked. A compromised/custom mirror or TLS/DNS/CA compromise
supplies matching malicious bytes + hash, and XPF then signs the result with its release
key. Fix: verify Canonical's signed checksum against a pinned signing key, or pin the
expected image digest in reviewed repo metadata; bind the authenticated base digest+source
into the signed XPF manifest.

## C. Publish gates a mutable tree, then uploads whatever replaced it (C175-HC-023)
`scripts/dist/publish.py:760` gates `dist` via `gate_images` (hashes artifacts + verifies
`install.sh`), returns, retains no snapshot/lock/descriptor, then `dispatch` (`publish.py:695`)
hands the same mutable `dist` path to the backend, which reopens files. A concurrent bake/
cleanup/writer can replace an artifact, sidecar, or the Tier-A `install.sh` after the gate
-> a gate-pass log accompanies different uploaded content (including an unsigned installer).
Fix: copy allowed files into a private immutable staging dir while hashing, verify against
that snapshot, fsync it, and dispatch only the snapshot (prefer content-addressed uploads,
publish the index last).

## Severity justification
supply-chain / signing / provenance / toctou. Build/release tooling only (no runtime
packet path). Blast radius: a compromised base image or an unvalidated/replaced artifact
carries a trusted XPF release signature and passes the fail-closed publish boundary ->
release compromise or widespread install failure. Distinct from fable-review-165

## #4905 — scripts/deploy+image tooling: transient status failure misread as reboot (skipped HA rejoin); unvalidated name/image path escapes managed dirs; world-readable secret config-drive ISO; unlocked fixed Incus alias/instance deletion [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Four filesystem-safety / observability defects in the deploy + image orchestration tooling
(`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py`, `scripts/image/`).

## A. Transient status-command failure misread as a reboot (C175-HC-017)
`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:1256-1264`: in the kernel-roll wait loop, `_running_kernel`
returning empty (any SSH/Incus/`uname` failure — the command wrapper at :1086 discards exit
status/stderr) sets `rebooted=True`. The next successful poll reports the known-good kernel
and `armed=none`, classified as a completed revert; `finally` then skips rejoin because
`rebooted` is true, leaving the node drained + ForceSecondary with both leases released.
-> one observability failure silently loses redundancy. Fix: return structured cmd results;
record pre-arm `boot_id` and require a changed boot_id (or another affirmative reboot
signal); decide rejoin from confirmed drain state.

## B. Unvalidated appliance/image identifiers escape managed dirs (C175-HC-097)
`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:213/559` (+ path construction at 296/564/603/651/760/775):
`name`/`image` accept separators and `..`; overlay/golden/day-0 paths are formed with no
`realpath`/`commonpath` containment. `../../../../tmp/owned` resolves to `/tmp/owned.qcow2`;
deploy/fetch writes and destroy/cleanup removes these, often via sudo. -> a typo/crafted
YAML overwrites/removes arbitrary suffixed files outside libvirt storage or installs a
golden image to an unintended privileged path. Fix: validate identifiers and enforce
`commonpath` containment before any write/delete/fetch sink.

## C. Config-drive builder leaves secret-bearing ISOs world-readable (C175-HC-096)
`scripts/image/make_config_drive.py:68/77`: day-0 config (password hashes, IKE PSKs, SNMP
communities, tokens) is written to an ISO created under the process umask (commonly 0644)
with no restrictive umask/chmod. The duplicate deploy implementation already applies 0600
(`xpf-deploy.py:320-340`). -> any co-located account can read day-0 credentials from the
default-created ISO. Fix: chmod 0600 the ISO (match the deploy path).

## D. Image validation deletes fixed Incus aliases/instances without locking (C175-HC-085)
`scripts/image/validate.py:193/229`: `ALIAS`=`xpf-image-validate` and scenarios
`xpf-image-a..e` are constants force-deleted at import/launch/cleanup with no lock/run-ID/
ownership tag. -> a concurrent bake or an unrelated same-named VM/image is destroyed. Fix:
namespace with a run-ID and refuse to delete objects without an ownership tag.

## Severity justification
tooling filesystem-safety / observability. Deploy/build orchestration only (no runtime
packet path). Blast radius: silent HA redundancy loss (A), arbitrary privileged file
overwrite/delete (B), credential disclosure to co-located accounts (C), destruction of
unrelated VMs/images (D). Reproduced containment failures, not cosmetic.

## #4906 — test/xsk-repro: AF_XDP reproducer safety + false-result cohort — unchecked fork()->kill(-1) SIGKILL; predictable /tmp BPF object; replace-and-detach live XDP program; uninitialized-counter PASS; frame-recycle/shared-UMEM coverage gaps [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

The `test/xsk-repro` AF_XDP reproducers have a cohort of safety + false-result defects.
These are diagnostic tools run as root against the live firewall interface, so several can
harm the host or produce PASS/FAIL that does not reflect the behavior under test.

## Host/operational hazards
- Unchecked `fork()` + unconditional `kill(child,9)` (C175-HC-001, rated Critical):
  `test/xsk-repro/libbpf_xsk_test.c:232` forks with no error check; cleanup at :273 runs
  `kill(child,9); waitpid(...)` unconditionally. On `fork()==-1` (PID-cgroup exhaustion,
  RLIMIT_NPROC, memory pressure) `child==-1` and `kill(-1,SIGKILL)` signals every process
  the root caller may signal — can kill the firewall daemon + host. `libbpf_xsk_shared_test.c:268`
  repeats it. Fix: handle `child<0`; guard kill/waitpid with `child>0`.
- Predictable attacker-owned `/tmp` BPF object (C175-HC-025): `test/xsk-repro/main.rs:250`
  and `libbpf_xsk_test.c:48` write/load the fixed `/tmp/xdp_pass_redirect.o`. A pre-created
  symlink makes root `std::fs::write` clobber an arbitrary file; both C binaries load a
  world-writable-namespace path with no inode/mode check. Fix: sealed memfd or
  `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` in a 0700 dir, load via `/proc/self/fd`.
- Replace-and-detach existing XDP program (C175-HC-101): `main.rs:285/77` attach flags are
  0 (no `XDP_FLAGS_UPDATE_IF_NOEXIST`, no save/restore); normal completion detaches to -1,
  a panic after attach skips cleanup -> can replace the firewall's redirect program and
  leave the interface with no XDP program (traffic loss beyond the test window).
- Rebind runs even if the link cycle never happened (C175-HC-090): `libbpf_xsk_test.c:254`
  / `main.rs:63` ignore `ip`/capability/backend failures and proceed to phase 2 (C also
  shells with an interpolated interface name).
- Rust unmaps UMEM while socket/UMEM owners still alive (C175-HC-091): `main.rs:195/122`
  `munmap`s the packet area while `umem/sock/rx` are in scope -> teardown fault/race.

## False-result / evidence-integrity
- Uninitialized phase counters can return PASS (C175-HC-081): `libbpf_xsk_test.c:243/273`
  jump over `rx1`/`rx2` init on early failure (`-Wjump-misses-init`/`-Wmaybe-uninitialized`).
- Frame recycling without preserving received UMEM addresses (C175-HC-069):
  `libbpf_xsk_test.c:177` releases RX descriptors before reading and calls a completion-ring
  accessor on an RX ring; Rust re-returns `offsets[0..needed]` regardless of consumed
  descriptors -> fill-ring starvation / duplicate ownership / misleading RX counts.
- Shared-UMEM test passes without reading a packet on the secondary socket
  (C175-HC-095): `libbpf_xsk_shared_test.c:143/187` never polls `secondary_rx/fill`; PASS
  depends solely on owner `rx1>0`.

## Fix
Compile with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`; fix process lifecycle, atomic file materialization,
XDP save/restore, link-cycle verification, UMEM address bookkeeping, and secondary-socket

A cohort of evidence-integrity defects in the `test/incus` perf / scheduler / fairness /
latency analysis tooling. Each can emit a confident PASS/negative verdict (or exit 0) from

A cohort of low-severity CLI/show display-fidelity defects. None change a packet verdict,
but each misrepresents state on the surface operators use to diagnose the firewall, and
several silently swallow errors that should be surfaced.

- `show security alarms` labels cumulative historical screen drops as currently active
  (C175-HC-063, `pkg/cli/cli_show_security_log.go:180/196`): any past drop keeps `val>0`,

## #4909 — control-plane low-severity correctness cohort — natpoolalarm double-close panic; persistent-NAT show data race; IPv6 peer endpoint; incomplete ClearAllDUIDs; DUID-LLT ephemeral on persist fail; fwdstatus tick overflow; DDNS semantic validation; Cloudflare pagination; offline WG keygen; check-config TOCTOU [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

A cohort of low-severity control-plane correctness defects (races, silent-failure, edge
cases). Each is genuine on current master but individually low blast-radius.

- Concurrent `natpoolalarm.Stop` double-close panic (C175-HC-119,
  `pkg/natpoolalarm/natpoolalarm.go:171/178`): two goroutines both pass the `select`
  default and close `m.stop` twice -> panic. Fix: `sync.Once` / guarded close.
- Persistent-NAT show data race (C175-HC-127, `pkg/natshow/persistent.go:15`,
  `pkg/dataplane/persistent_nat.go:125/171`): `All` returns mutable pointers; a show
  evaluating `b.LastSeen.Add(...)` races a live `Save` writing `LastSeen` -> Go data race /
  torn timeout output. Fix: return a value snapshot under lock.
- Cluster CLI peer dialing builds invalid IPv6 endpoints (C175-HC-118, `pkg/cli/peer.go:49`):
  `2001:db8::2` becomes `2001:db8::2:50051` (no brackets) -> gRPC target + reachability
  probe fail on IPv6 fabric. Fix: `net.JoinHostPort`.
- `ClearAllDUIDs` clears only in-process identifiers and ignores delete errors (C175-HC-114,
  `pkg/dhcp/dhcp.go:540/548`): a persisted DUID whose client has not called `getDUID` since
  restart is not removed, and I/O/permission errors are swallowed while the API reports all
  cleared.
- DUID-LLT generation continues after persistence failure (C175-HC-123, `pkg/dhcp/dhcp.go:598`):
  a read-only/full state dir yields an ephemeral time-based DUID that differs on restart ->
  server sees a new client, old lease lingers.
- Forwarding-status CPU tick conversion overflows before division (C175-HC-124,
  `pkg/fwdstatus/builder.go:230`, `sampler.go:212`): `ticks*1e9` wraps ~18.45e9 ticks (~33
  days at 64 busy cores, 100 Hz) -> the CPU windows used to diagnose saturation go invalid.
  Fix: divide before multiply or use 128-bit intermediate.
- DDNS state loads validate JSON/version but not record semantics (C175-HC-120,
  `pkg/ddns/state.go:350`, `pkg/ddns/manager.go:1166`): valid-version JSON with a malformed
  address is trusted; cleanup silently drops the in-memory entry without a wire delete and
  without persisting -> uncleanable stale DNS, oscillating across restart.
- Cloudflare record lookup does one unpaginated request (C175-HC-117,
  `pkg/ddns/backend_cloudflare.go:177/186`): a name/type with more rows than one page can
  hide xpf-owned content -> duplicate create or false "already absent" delete.
- Offline WireGuard key generator is unreachable when xpfd is down (C175-HC-133,
  `cmd/cli/main.go:40`): `main` does `GetStatus` and exits before dispatch, so the
  no-RPC keygen fails exactly during recovery/bootstrap. Fix: dispatch local-only verbs
  before the daemon-status probe.
- `check-config` bounded-read TOCTOU (C175-MC-013, `cmd/xpfd/main.go:172`): `Stat` then
  `ReadFile` allocates before the `len(data)` cap; a raced/adversarial (FUSE-like) file can
  exceed the documented 4 MiB bound. Bounded by normally-read-only config drive. Fix:
  `io.LimitReader(max+1)` on an opened descriptor.

## #4910 — grpcapi: active MonitorInterface stream can block daemon shutdown forever (GracefulStop with no timeout) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
Both gRPC listeners call `srv.GracefulStop()` on shutdown with no timeout or `Stop()` fallback, and the unbounded server-streaming `MonitorInterface` RPC only watches `stream.Context()` (the client stream), not a server-lifetime context. A client holding a `MonitorInterface` stream open can therefore block daemon shutdown / failover / restart indefinitely.

## Current master (origin/master)
- `pkg/grpcapi/server.go:254-257`: `case <-ctx.Done(): } srv.GracefulStop()` (loopback listener) — no timeout.
- `pkg/grpcapi/server.go:309-310`: `<-ctx.Done(); srv.GracefulStop()` (fabric listener) — no timeout.
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go:416-465`: `MonitorInterface` loops on `ticker.C` / `stream.Context().Done()`, streaming forever; it never observes a server shutdown context.

## Scenario (input → hang)
During shutdown the parent `ctx` is cancelled; both listeners call `GracefulStop()`, which waits for active RPCs to finish. A local loopback client, or an authenticated fabric peer, holds `MonitorInterface` open — its `stream.Context()` stays live because the client keeps the stream. `GracefulStop` never returns, so `Run`/`RunFabricListener` never returns and the daemon cannot stop/failover cleanly.

## Fix
Bound graceful shutdown: run `GracefulStop` in a goroutine and call `Stop()` after a short timeout. Optionally store a server shutdown context on `Server` and have streaming handlers select on both `stream.Context()` and server lifetime. Regression test: open `MonitorInterface`, cancel the server context, assert `Run` returns within the timeout.

## Severity justification
Medium (availability). Trigger: any client holding an allowed `MonitorInterface` stream during shutdown (loopback client or authenticated fabric peer). Blast radius: unbounded hang of daemon stop/failover/restart — turns an observability stream into an operations/availability risk. Bounded to shutdown timing and requires an open stream; not data corruption. No exact dup for these listener shutdown paths.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-051 (area A8). Verified present on current master.

## #4911 — sessions: filtered ClearSessions (gRPC + CLI) snapshots every matching key before deleting — unbounded control-plane memory [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

## Summary
Filtered session clears (gRPC `ClearSessions` and the local CLI `clear`) materialize an unbounded snapshot of every matching key before deleting anything. A broad-but-non-empty filter (e.g. `protocol=tcp` / a valid zone) misses the `ClearAllSessions` fast path and appends every matching forward key, reverse key, and SNAT/DNAT companion key into growing slices for v4 then v6, before any deletion. On a large deployment the shim session/dnat maps are sized up to 10,000,000 entries, so the control daemon can allocate memory proportional to the matched set (hundreds of MB+) and OOM before making progress.

## Current master (origin/master)
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go:977-1030`: `var v4Keys …; v4Keys = append(v4Keys, key)` inside `IterateSessions`, then the v6 equivalent, with no cap/batch flush/`ctx.Err()` check.
- `pkg/cli/cli_clear.go:191-238`: same collect-all-then-delete pattern.
- `pkg/dataplane/loader_userspace_shim.go:312-332`: `sessions`/`sessions_v6`/`dnat_table*` sized `userspaceShimMaxSessions = 10000000`.

## Scenario (input → resource exhaustion)
An operator or authorized management/fabric client issues `clear security flow session protocol tcp` on a firewall carrying millions of sessions. The handler iterates the full v4 and v6 tables, appending every matching forward/reverse/NAT-companion key to slices before deleting anything → memory pressure/OOM in `xpfd` during an incident, exactly when the daemon is needed to recover or fail over.

## Fix
Delete in bounded batches during iteration (or add a dataplane delete-by-filter primitive that does not materialize all keys in userspace); check `ctx.Err()` during long scans and surface a clear cancellation error; keep failure aggregation bounded by operation class rather than one string per error. Regression test with a fake iterator proving the handler flushes before collecting an unbounded key set.

## Severity justification
Medium (availability / resource-safety). Trigger: a broad filtered clear on a large session table (legitimate incident cleanup, or an authorized-but-hostile client). Blast radius: control-daemon memory pressure/OOM — killing the daemon needed to recover/fail over. Bounded to a privileged API surface (not unauthenticated) and to large tables, keeping it Medium. Covers both the gRPC (A8) and CLI paths (same root). Distinct from unbounded session-display/top-talker findings.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-053 (area A8, merged with A10). Verified present on current master.

## #4912 — rpm: HTTP probe leaks a keep-alive transport+fd per bodyless (204) response [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
Each HTTP RPM probe allocates a fresh `http.Transport` with keep-alives implicitly enabled and `IdleConnTimeout == 0` (no limit), performs one GET, and drops the transport reference without `CloseIdleConnections()`/`DisableKeepAlives`. For a bodyless response (HTTP 204 or `Content-Length: 0`), closing the body returns the connection to that transport's idle pool, which — with no owner and no idle timeout — retains the socket and its read-loop goroutine indefinitely. Frequent probes to an empty health endpoint leak one TCP fd + goroutines per attempt.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/rpm/rpm.go`)
- L747-754 `probeHTTP`: `transport := &http.Transport{ DialContext: dialer.DialContext }; client := &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second, Transport: transport}` — no `DisableKeepAlives`, no deferred `transport.CloseIdleConnections()`, transport goes out of scope after the request.
- `client.Timeout` bounds the request, not idle-connection lifetime.

## Scenario (input → resource leak)
An RPM `http` probe targets a health endpoint that returns 204 / empty body on a short interval. Each attempt: new transport → one GET → body closed → connection returned to that (now unreferenced) transport's idle pool with unlimited `IdleConnTimeout`. The transport + persistent-connection read loop retain each other and the socket. Over many cycles, fds and goroutines/memory accumulate, eventually exhausting descriptors and disrupting unrelated routing/management services.

## Fix
Use a long-lived client/transport per test and `CloseIdleConnections()` when the test is removed; or for strictly one-shot probes set `DisableKeepAlives: true` or defer `transport.CloseIdleConnections()` immediately after construction. Add a repeated-204 test tracking accepted/closed connections and fd/goroutine stability across cancellation.

## Severity justification
Medium (resource leak). Trigger: a configured HTTP RPM probe to a common bodyless health endpoint (deterministic idle-pool path). Blast radius: gradual fd/goroutine/memory exhaustion in `xpfd` affecting unrelated services. Bounded — requires RPM configured and repeated probing to accumulate; no immediate failure. No existing RPM transport-ownership issue.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-055 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4913 — feeds: globally duplicate feed names start orphan refresh loops + nondeterministic provider selection [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
Globally duplicate dynamic-address feed names are not rejected, and feed workers are tracked in a map keyed by feed name. Iterating `daCfg.FeedServers` (a Go map, nondeterministic order) can start two refresh loops for the same `FeedEntry.Name`; the later `m.feeds[name] = fs` assignment overwrites the first, orphaning its cancel func. `StopAll` iterates `m.feeds` and cancels only the surviving worker, so the overwritten loop keeps fetching/logging/invoking `onUpdate` until the daemon's parent context ends, while enforcement reads whichever provider won the latest map iteration.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/feeds/feeds.go`)
- L173 `for _, fsCfg := range daCfg.FeedServers` — map iteration, nondeterministic order.
- L~30-39: `feedCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)` … `m.feeds[fe.Name] = fs` … `go m.refreshLoop(feedCtx, fs, interval)`.
- L239-240 `StopAll` cancels only entries present in `m.feeds`.
- The dynamic-address compiler/reference validator builds a declared-name set but does not reject cross-server name collisions.

## Scenario (input → wrong output + goroutine leak)
Two feed servers each declare `FeedEntry.Name == "threats"`. `Apply` starts both refresh loops; whichever server the map yields last wins `m.feeds["threats"]`, and its provider backs enforcement (nondeterministic across commits). The overwritten loop's cancel is lost: it keeps fetching the wrong provider, logging, and firing `onUpdate` policy rebuilds forever. Repeated applies accumulate orphaned fetchers; the active security set is not predictable from config.

## Fix
Reject duplicate effective feed names globally at strict validation (including nested-entry vs single-feed-fallback collisions). Build a complete unique plan before starting any goroutine. Track workers with a generation context + `WaitGroup` and wait on stop so no old generation publishes callbacks.

## Severity justification
Medium (correctness + goroutine leak). Trigger: a duplicate feed name across servers (typo). Blast radius: a denylist/feed silently backed by the wrong provider after commit (nondeterministic), plus orphaned outbound fetchers and spurious policy rebuilds that persist until shutdown. Bounded to a config-authoring mistake; fail-direction depends on which provider wins. No existing duplicate-feed-identity/orphan-loop issue.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-056 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4914 — logging: SESSION_CLOSE binary record + generic slog still emit policy_id=0 and action=deny (residual of #4796) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
Follow-up to #4796 (which fixed the standard slog line to log `rec.PolicyID`). Two live SESSION_CLOSE sinks still misrepresent closes:

1. **Binary log record** encodes `evt.PolicyID` and `evt.Action`, both of which are **zeroed for a close** — so every binary session-close record reports `policy_id = 0` and `action = 0` (which decodes to `deny`).
2. **Generic slog SESSION_CLOSE line** still emits `"action", actionStr` where `actionStr = actionName(evt.Action) = actionName(0) = "deny"` — the standard/structured text formatters were fixed to omit close action (#2513), but this generic slog branch was missed.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/logging/ringbuf.go`)
- L554-557 (live `logEvent`): on close, `rec.PolicyID = 0; evt.PolicyID = 0; … rec.PolicyID = LE(data[136:140])` — the admitting policy lands in `rec`, and `evt.PolicyID` is zero.
- L513 `actionStr := actionName(evt.Action)`; wire action byte is intentionally 0 for closes → `actionName(0) == "deny"` (L1194).
- L695 (generic slog close branch): `… "action", actionStr, "policy_id", rec.PolicyID …` — policy_id fixed by #4796, but `action` still shows `deny`.
- L1277-1310 `formatBinaryRecord` (called at L738/L783 with the zeroed `evt`): `buf[7] = evt.Action` (0 → deny) and `buf[54:58] = evt.PolicyID` (0) — should use `rec.PolicyID` and omit/flag the action for closes.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
A normal session close is emitted to the binary log sink and generic slog: binary consumers read `policy_id=0` + `action=deny`; the generic slog line reads `action=deny`. Incident tooling attributes normal terminations to a deny/drop and cannot name the admitting policy in the binary record.

## Fix
In `formatBinaryRecord`, encode `rec.PolicyID` (not `evt.PolicyID`) and give SESSION_CLOSE a dedicated action handling (omit/flag, carry close reason) instead of the raw 0 byte. Fix the generic slog SESSION_CLOSE branch to omit `action` like the standard/structured lines. Add one live extended-close fixture through `ProcessRawEvent` asserting parity across buffer, callback, slog, standard, structured, and binary sinks.

## Severity justification
Medium (telemetry correctness). Trigger: every session close reaching the binary log or generic slog sink. Blast radius: binary forensic consumers cannot attribute closes to the admitting policy and read closes as denies; the generic slog line classifies normal terminations as `deny` → false drop alerts / broken correlation. No security boundary. Residual of #4796 (which fixed only the standard slog policy_id).

## #4915 — logging: RT_FLOW SessionID is a per-event sequence number, not a stable session identity — create/close cannot correlate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
The RT_FLOW `SessionID` exposed on every telemetry surface is a per-**event** monotonic sequence number, not a stable per-session identity. `logEvent` assigns `rec.SessionID = atomic.AddUint64(&er.sessionSeq, 1)` on every event (including unrelated denies/screens), so a session's create and close records necessarily receive different IDs and cannot be correlated; a restart resets the namespace. The 144/152-byte raw event schema carries no session identity, so this is a fabricated ordinal presented as an authoritative session ID.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/logging/ringbuf.go`)
- L215: `sessionSeq uint64 // monotonic session ID counter`.
- L621: `rec.SessionID = atomic.AddUint64(&er.sessionSeq, 1)` — incremented per event, not per session.
- `pkg/logging/eventbuf.go:61`: `SessionID uint64 // unique session identifier` — surfaced to the structured vSRX renderer, binary log, EventBuffer, REST/SSE (#3337), and callbacks.
- `DecodeRawEventRecord` leaves SessionID zero (no wire source).

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
A single dataplane session emits a create event (SessionID=N) and later a close event (SessionID=M≠N). A SIEM/operator joining open+close by SessionID cannot match them, cannot distinguish reused 5-tuples (under NAT/HA/concurrency), and cannot correlate RT_FLOW with session/HA views — while the field looks authoritative. #3337 added SessionID to the APIs but the underlying value is the per-event ordinal.

## Fix
Extend the userspace RT_FLOW producer/wire contract to carry the dataplane's stable uint64 SessionID on create and close (additive field, explicit old/new length handling for rolling upgrades). Decode it directly; keep an event-sequence field under a different name only if separately useful. End-to-end create/close and HA-failover correlation tests.

## Severity justification
Medium (telemetry / vSRX-parity). Trigger: any create/close correlation attempt (routine for SIEMs). Blast radius: broken session correlation, tuple-reuse disambiguation, and RT_FLOW↔session/HA joins across every telemetry surface; the field misleads by looking authoritative. No security boundary. Distinct from #3056/#3395 (policy_id) and #3337 (API field plumbing).

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-058 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4916 — snmp: Agent.Stop leaks the context watcher + trap worker and can deliver queued traps after removal [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
`snmp.Agent.Stop()` only sets `stopped = true` and closes the UDP socket; it does not cancel the context-watcher goroutine, close/drain the trap queue, or wait for `trapWorker`. Because the daemon-wide context stays live across a day-2 SNMP disable, the `<-ctx.Done()` watcher goroutine remains blocked, and `trapWorker` ranges an unclosed channel forever. Any traps still queued (prebuilt packets, targets, old community values) can be delivered after the config that authorized them was removed, and each disable/re-enable cycle leaks another goroutine pair.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/snmp/agent.go`)
- L504-513 `Stop`: `a.stopped = true; if a.conn != nil { a.conn.Close(); a.conn = nil }` — no queue close, no worker wait, no watcher cancel.
- L471-474 (in `Start`): `go func(){ <-ctx.Done(); a.Stop() }()` — the watcher waits on ctx, which is not cancelled by `Stop`.
- L201 `trapWorkerOnce`; the trap queue is bounded but never closed/drained on Stop.

## Scenario (input → stale telemetry + leak)
Operator removes/rotates SNMP trap config; the day-2 reconcile calls `Stop` while the daemon context is live. The read loop exits but the watcher stays blocked; `trapWorker` keeps ranging the queue and sends any backlog to the old target with the old community. A blocked target prolongs the stale-send window. Re-enable creates a second agent and a second goroutine pair.

## Fix
Give Agent one lifecycle context/done channel + `WaitGroup`; have both the watcher and trap worker select it. On Stop, atomically reject new jobs, cancel in-flight sends, drop/generation-check queued jobs, close/drain safely, close the socket, and wait. Disable/re-enable tests with a blocked sender proving no post-Stop delivery and zero surviving workers.

## Severity justification
Medium (goroutine leak + stale telemetry). Trigger: SNMP disable/community-rotation with queued traps (day-2 op). Blast radius: leaked goroutines per enable/disable cycle and delivery of security-relevant traps to a removed/rotated receiver after the credential was revoked. Bounded to the queued backlog and management plane. Distinct from #3967 (missing day-2 reconcile, which is fixed).

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-059 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4917 — snmp: hostnames >26 bytes produce an oversized (>32-octet) invalid SNMPv3 EngineID [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
`initEngine` builds the SNMPv3 authoritative EngineID by appending the OS hostname to a 6-byte prefix with no length bound. SNMP-FRAMEWORK-MIB constrains `SnmpEngineID` to 5..32 octets, so any hostname longer than 26 bytes yields an invalid oversized EngineID. The config/compiler imposes no matching 26-byte hostname limit, and ordinary Linux hostnames can exceed it. Every v3 discovery, key localization, auth check, and response then uses the invalid value.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/snmp/agent.go`)
- L295-303 `initEngine`: `a.engineID = append([]byte{0x80, 0x00, 0x01, 0x86, 0xa3, 0x04}, []byte(hostname)...)` — 6 prefix bytes + full hostname, no cap. 6 + 27 = 33 > 32.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
A valid appliance hostname of 27+ bytes produces a 33+-octet EngineID. BER accepts the long OCTET STRING on the wire, but standards-compliant managers may reject it before USM — so all SNMPv3 monitoring fails while v2c continues, with no startup error explaining the incompatibility.

## Fix
Construct a bounded, standards-compliant EngineID (enterprise-specific format + a stable machine/cluster identity hash), or at minimum deterministically hash/truncate long hostnames and reject/bound to <=32 octets. Because changing EngineID invalidates localized keys and manager caches, define migration behavior (preserve existing short-host IDs). Tests at 26/27/64-byte boundaries plus uniqueness.

## Severity justification
Medium (identity / vSRX-parity). Trigger: a normal hostname over 26 bytes (no attacker needed). Blast radius: all SNMPv3 monitoring silently breaks for standards-strict managers, with no diagnostic. Bounded to SNMPv3 and long-hostname deployments; v2c unaffected. Distinct from #2611 (context), #2649/#2610 (engineBoots).

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-060 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4918 — snmp: plain GET/GETNEXT bypass trimToFit (oversized responses) + trimToFit is O(n^2) (residual of #2612) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
Follow-up to #2612 (which added `trimToFit` bounding **GETBULK** response size). Two residuals remain: (1) plain **GET/GETNEXT** bypass `trimToFit` entirely and can emit responses larger than `maxPacketSize`; (2) `trimToFit`'s decrement-and-rebuild is O(n^2) in encoded varbinds — GETBULK still materializes `len(oids)*maxRepetitions` records and rebuilds complete prefixes one varbind at a time (with v3 re-running USM framing/HMAC/encryption on each rebuild), on the single serial SNMP goroutine.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/snmp/agent.go`)
- L697-718 `handleGet` and L722-743 `handleGetNext`: both end with `return a.buildResponse(...)` directly — no `trimToFit`, no size cap.
- L802-806 `handleGetBulk`: `resp, ok := trimToFit(varbinds, effectiveMaxSize(maxPacketSize), func(vbs)...)` — bounds output, but the varbind set is fully materialized first and `trimToFit` rebuilds decrementally.
- L782-790: repeaters loop `for j := 0; j < maxRepetitions; j++` per repeater OID.

## Scenario (input → oversized/quadratic work)
- A GET/GETNEXT naming many OIDs (a 4 KiB request holds hundreds of short varbinds), or a single OID with a long configured string value, produces a UDP response exceeding `maxPacketSize` with no trim/`tooBig` — the residual #2612 did not cover.
- A GETBULK with many repeaters builds `len(oids)*100` records then trims one varbind at a time (quadratic), consuming CPU/heap and blocking every other poll on the serial serving goroutine.

## Fix
Apply one shared response budget to GET, GETNEXT, and GETBULK; generate varbinds incrementally while tracking encoded size and stop near the effective maximum; cap total generated varbinds independently of repetition count. Replace decrement-and-rebuild with exact-length accounting or binary search. Adversarial many-OID tests asserting build count, work bounds, response size, and continued service latency.

## Severity justification
Medium (management-plane DoS residual). Trigger: SNMP enabled + a v2c community or v3 username (see the SNMPv3 noAuth downgrade filed separately); one crafted datagram. Blast radius: oversized GET/GETNEXT reflection + quadratic CPU/heap that monopolizes the single SNMP goroutine and starves legitimate monitoring. Reduced from the original High because #2612 already bounds GETBULK output; the residual is GET/GETNEXT sizing + build cost.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-011 (area A9). Verified present on current master (#2612 partial).

## #4919 — frr: BGP cluster-id and route-map then-origin rendered without validation (reload-poison; cluster-id lacks the newline belt) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
Two FRR render-side validation gaps that can poison an `frr-reload.py` / `vtysh` reload for an unrelated routing change:

1. **`protocols bgp cluster-id`** is rendered verbatim with neither a value validator nor the `sanitizeFRRValue` newline belt — unlike the adjacent `router-id`, which is guarded by `validRouterID`. An invalid token fails the reload, and (because there is no sanitize belt) an embedded-newline value injects extra `frr.conf` lines.
2. **route-map `then origin`** is control-char sanitized but has no enum validator, so a non-control invalid token (e.g. `igpp`) passes sanitize and fails the FRR route-map grammar at reload.

## Current master (origin/master)
- `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:678-682`: `if validRouterID(bgp.RouterID) { … router-id … }` then `if bgp.ClusterID != "" { fmt.Fprintf(&b, " bgp cluster-id %s\n", bgp.ClusterID) }` — no validator, **no `sanitizeFRRValue`**.
- `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:1829-1834`: `fmt.Fprintf(&b, " set origin %s\n", sanitizeFRRValue(term.Origin))` — sanitized but not enum-validated.
- `pkg/config/schema_routing.go`: `cluster-id` and `origin` are untyped `args:1` leaves with no validator; the compiler copies both tokens unchanged (`compiler_protocols.go` / `compiler_routing.go`).

## Scenario (input → reload poison / injection)
- `set protocols bgp cluster-id not.an.ip` (or a quoted-newline value) renders `bgp cluster-id not.an.ip` (or an injected extra `frr.conf` line); FRR rejects it and `frr-reload.py` fails, stalling the managed section for any co-committed routing change.
- `set policy-options policy-statement X then origin igpp` renders `set origin igpp`, which fails the route-map grammar and stalls the reload.

## Fix
Add strict validators: dotted-IPv4/32-bit for `cluster-id`, `ValidateEnum([]string{"igp","egp","incomplete"})` for `then origin`; add a render-side skip/error belt for lenient-loaded bad values; and apply `sanitizeFRRValue` to `cluster-id` (parity with the #4482/#4498 set-clause/origin belts). Regression tests parallel to `router_id_2980_test.go`.

## Severity justification
Medium (reload-poison; cluster-id also injection, CWE-74). Trigger: a mistyped route-reflector/origin knob, or a lenient-loaded/synced value. Blast radius: one bad token stalls the whole FRR reload, leaving stale routing policy active while the daemon reports degraded apply; `cluster-id` additionally lacks the newline-injection belt the sibling set-clauses got. Bounded to config-author input and the RR/origin knobs. Distinct from the #4482/#4498 injection belt (which covered set-clauses/origin, not cluster-id) and prior local-pref/metric validation.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-MC-004 + C175-MC-005 (area A7). Verified present on current master.

## #4920 — api: REST include_peer=true drops cursor-mode page_size — peer sessions undercounted to the 100 default [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
The REST `include_peer=true` first-page peer fan-out drops cursor-mode `page_size`. `peerSessionsRequest` forwards offset-mode `limit` but never sets `PageSize`, so when the REST caller uses cursor pagination (`page_size` without `limit`), the peer gRPC request arrives with `Limit == 0` and `PageSize == 0`. The gRPC legacy path then defaults the peer list to 100 sessions, so the first REST page attaches at most 100 peer sessions even though the local first page is sized for `page_size` and the contract says the first page carries the peer's table.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/api/sessions.go`)
- L62 local path: `pageSize, ok := queryIntStrict(r, "page_size", 0)` — cursor mode when `page_size>0`.
- L344-368 `peerSessionsRequest`: builds `pb.GetSessionsRequest{ IncludePeer:true, Protocol/…, }`; sets `req.Limit = int32(l)` from `limit` only. **No `PageSize` from `page_size`.**
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go:588` `getSessionsLegacy`: `if limit <= 0 { limit = 100 }`.

## Scenario (input → undercount)
`GET /api/v1/sessions?page_size=1000&include_peer=true`: the local response uses cursor pagination for 1000 rows; `writeSessionList` calls the peer service with `peerSessionsRequest`, which sends `Limit=0, PageSize=0`; gRPC defaults the peer to 100. The first page attaches ≤100 peer sessions instead of the peer's full table — HA dashboards/automation undercount peer sessions by an arbitrary amount whenever the peer has >100 sessions and the client uses cursor pagination.

## Fix
In `peerSessionsRequest`, parse and forward validated `page_size` as `PageSize` for cursor-mode callers (or normalize REST cursor pagination to an equivalent peer request size). HA tests with peer cardinality >100 and `page_size` set without `limit`.

## Severity justification
Medium (HA observability). Trigger: a cursor-mode REST session list with `include_peer=true` against a peer holding >100 sessions (routine for HA dashboards). Blast radius: silent peer-session undercount — hides peer load/failover state; a REST↔gRPC schema-translation drift, not corruption. Bounded to the observability surface. Distinct from #350 (gRPC-layer PageToken forwarding) and #3423 (adding include_peer); this is the REST adapter dropping page_size.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-MC-006 (area A8). Verified present on current master.

## #4921 — grpcapi: ShowText test-routing accepts duplicate selectors with silent last-wins (unlike test-policy #3709) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
The gRPC `ShowText` `test-routing` selector parser rejects malformed and unknown keys but silently last-wins on duplicate known keys, unlike the sibling `test-policy` parser (#3709), which rejects duplicates. A repeated `dest=` or `instance=` runs the diagnostic route lookup against a different destination/VRF than the operator typed.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_routes_text.go`)
- L191-210 `showTestRouting`: `switch parts[0] { case "dest": dest = parts[1]; case "instance": instance = parts[1]; default: parseErr = unknown selector }` — no `seen` map; a repeated known key silently reassigns.
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_firewall.go:226` (`test-policy`, #3709) allocates `seen := make(map[string]bool)` and reports a duplicate selector as an error.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
`ShowText{Topic: "test-routing:dest=192.0.2.1,instance=blue,instance=prod"}` (or repeated `dest`): the parser accepts it and the last value silently wins, so the diagnostic route lookup answers for `instance=prod`/the last `dest` — a different query than the operator intended, with no error. REST/remote-CLI users are misled during routing investigation.

## Fix
Add `seen := map[string]bool{}` in `showTestRouting`, reject repeated known keys with the same error shape as `showTestPolicy` (#3709), and add tests for duplicate `dest` and duplicate `instance`.

## Severity justification
Low (diagnostic integrity). Trigger: a duplicated selector in a `test-routing` query (operator input). Blast radius: the simulator answers for a different destination/VRF than typed, with no warning — misleading during investigation, no runtime forwarding effect. Bounded to the diagnostic surface. Sibling of #3709 (`test-policy`), which fixed the analogous gap for a different parser.

## #4922 — feeds: invalid-line sample bounded by count (5) but not bytes — retains/logs ~5 MiB per feed [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
The dynamic-address feed invalid-line sample is bounded by count (5) but not by bytes. The scanner accepts malformed lines up to ~1 MiB (`maxLineBytes = 1<<20`), `parseFeed` retains the first 5 verbatim, `installSnapshot`/`AllFeeds` keep and copy them, and a changed degraded feed sends the full slice to `slog.Warn`. So a single feed can retain and log ~5 MiB of verbatim garbage, and multiple feeds multiply it — despite the "small sample" contract.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/feeds/feeds.go`)
- L33 `const maxLineBytes = 1 << 20`.
- L39 `const maxInvalidSample = 5` (count-only bound).
- L518 `if len(invalidSample) < maxInvalidSample { … append verbatim line … }` — no per-sample byte cap.
- `AllFeeds` copies the sample; a changed degraded feed logs the full slice.

## Scenario (input → resource/log bloat)
A broken or hostile provider serves near-1-MiB malformed lines. Each feed retains 5 × ~1 MiB verbatim; `AllFeeds` (REST/status reads) copies it; a changing body repeatedly emits multi-MB `slog.Warn` records. Persistent memory pressure and expensive/truncated logs, all within the advertised feed limits (the 32-MiB body cap bounds one fetch but not the retained/logged sample).

## Fix
Cap each sample to a small escaped prefix (e.g. 256 bytes), cap aggregate sample bytes, and include original byte length/hash for diagnosis. Tests for multi-byte/near-1-MiB malformed lines, `AllFeeds` copy size, and log-field size.

## Severity justification
Low. Trigger: a degraded feed with very long malformed lines (misconfigured or controlled provider). Blast radius: several MiB of retained/copied/logged garbage per feed — memory pressure and expensive log records, no correctness/security impact. Bounded by the 32-MiB fetch cap and the count bound. No existing byte-bound issue.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-111 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4923 — flowexport: packet-count fallback StartTime overflows time.Duration and can place flow start after end [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
The flow-export packet-count fallback for StartTime uses `rec.Time.Add(-estimateSessionDuration(rec.SessionPkts, proto))` with no overflow guard. `estimateSessionDuration` multiplies a uint64 packet count by a per-packet time; above ~92.2 billion TCP packets (~184.5 billion non-TCP) the multiplication overflows signed `time.Duration`, producing a negative duration that is subtracted, moving StartTime *after* EndTime. The real-created branch clamps `created.After(rec.Time)` to EndTime; the packet-count fallback has no such clamp.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/flowexport/manager.go`)
- L820-826 (real-created branch): `if created.After(rec.Time) { return rec.Time, false }` — future clamp present.
- L829: `return rec.Time.Add(-estimateSessionDuration(rec.SessionPkts, proto)), true` — fallback, no overflow/clamp guard; `SessionPkts` is uint64 end-to-end.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
An old/synthesized close frame with `Created == 0` (legacy/HA-recovery/imported records) and a very large `SessionPkts` takes the fallback. The uint64→Duration multiply overflows to a negative value; subtracting it puts StartTime after EndTime. NetFlow then emits first-switched after last-switched, and IPFIX emits contradictory absolute milliseconds — records collectors may reject, exactly on the legacy/HA recovery paths.

## Fix
Compute with checked/saturating arithmetic, cap the heuristic to a defensible maximum age, and clamp the resulting start to `[deviceBootOrEpoch, EndTime]`. Count overflow/cap separately. Boundary tests around `MaxInt64/(100ms)` and `MaxInt64/(50ms)` for both exporters.

## Severity justification
Low (record correctness). Trigger: a fallback (Created==0) record with ~10^11 packets — rare but reachable on long/high-rate sessions and legacy/HA-recovery imports. Blast radius: poisoned duration/ordering analytics and possible collector rejection, on paths where telemetry already matters. Bounded by the extreme packet count required. No existing packet-count-overflow issue.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-112 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4924 — snmp: TimeTicks BER omits the leading-zero for high-bit values — non-canonical after 248 days uptime [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
`berEncodeTimeTicks` strips leading zero bytes but, unlike `berEncodeCounter32`, does not prepend a `0x00` when the first content octet has its high bit set. TimeTicks is an unsigned APPLICATION integer, so at `0x80000000` hundredths (248.55 days of uptime) the encoding becomes negative/non-canonical signed BER until wrap (~497 days). `sysUpTime` and v1/v2 link traps all use this encoder.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/snmp/agent.go`)
- L1236-1245 `berEncodeTimeTicks`: `binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(buf, uint32(hundredths)); for len(buf) > 1 && buf[0] == 0 { buf = buf[1:] }; return buf` — **no** `if buf[0]&0x80 != 0 { prepend 0x00 }`.
- Sibling unsigned encoders (Counter32 path, ~L1221; L1343) correctly do `if bytes[0]&0x80 != 0 { bytes = append([]byte{0}, bytes...) }`.
- L856: `return berEncodeTimeTicks(hundredths), tagTimeTicks`.

## Scenario (input → wrong output)
After 248.55 days of uptime, `sysUpTime` (and link-trap timestamps) encode `0x80000000` as a 4-byte value with the high bit set and no leading zero → a negative/non-canonical INTEGER-derived application value. Standards-strict managers may reject or misdecode it, so uptime/traps appear invalid — an "outage" that surfaces only after months of runtime.

## Fix
Reuse `berEncodeCounter32(uint32(hundredths))` for TimeTicks, or share one unsigned-BER helper that prepends the leading zero. Exact tests at `0x7fffffff`, `0x80000000`, `0xffffffff`, including full varbind decode.

## Severity justification
Low (wire correctness, long-uptime). Trigger: >248.55 days uptime (no attacker; time-based). Blast radius: invalid/non-canonical sysUpTime and v1/v2 trap timestamps for strict managers. Bounded to long-running devices and SNMP enabled. No existing TimeTicks sign-encoding issue.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-HC-113 (area A9). Verified present on current master.

## #4925 — userspace-dp: NAT match address-name to an address-set with a feed-backed member is not feed-resolved (fail-closed parity gap) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Summary
NAT `match {source,destination}-address-name` references to an address-**set** whose member is a dynamic-address feed do not resolve the feed overlay for the nested member. Direct feed references (#3303) resolve correctly, and the security-policy path resolves nested feed members via `expandBookNameRecursive` (#3294), but the NAT resolver calls the static `resolveUserspaceAddressBookEntry` for nested sets, which cannot consult `feedOverlay`. The result is fail-closed (SNAT falls back to an unparseable token, DNAT installs no row), but it is a documented vSRX/policy parity gap.

## Current master (origin/master, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat.go`)
- L50-58 (comment): the recursive address-SET-with-feed-member case is "NOT resolved here … the NAT path was deliberately left out of #3294 scope … remains a tracked residual."
- L59-68 `resolveNATAddressNamePrefixes`: `resolveUserspaceAddressBookEntry(cfg, name)` (static, feed-unaware) then `feedOverlay[name]` (keyed by the direct feed name, not the containing set) — nested set members yield no feed prefixes.

## Scenario (input → wrong output, fail-closed)
Operator defines address-set `bad-set` containing feed-backed member `bad-feed`, and a NAT rule `match source-address-name bad-set`. The static expander returns no feed prefixes; `feedOverlay["bad-set"]` is empty (overlay keyed by `bad-feed`). SNAT falls back to the raw token (matches nothing); DNAT installs no table row. The equivalent security-policy usage IS feed-aware, so one operator-authored address object has different dataplane meaning across subsystems — and the NAT rule silently disables after HA sync / lenient reload while the direct-feed tests stay green.

## Fix
Replace NAT's static `resolveUserspaceAddressBookEntry` call with the feed-aware recursive expander shared with policy address-book expansion (or a NAT-specific recursive resolver that merges `feedOverlay` for nested members). Preserve fail-closed behavior for unrepresentable non-feed members. Add SNAT + DNAT tests for `match {source,destination}-address-name` referencing a set with a feed-backed member (feed-only and mixed static+feed).

## Severity justification
Low (fail-closed vSRX/policy parity gap). Trigger: NAT rule scoped to an address-set containing a feed member. Blast radius: the NAT rule matches nothing (fail-closed, not a widening/security issue), diverging from documented "policy/NAT address-name bindings" and from the policy path. Bounded and documented as a tracked residual in-source; no dedicated tracking issue exists. Distinct from #3303 (direct NAT feed, tested) and #3418 (strict-commit rejection).

## #4926 — api: malformed security-events limit fails open to the default window (queryInt), unlike the fail-closed zone filter [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
The REST security-events handler parses `limit` with the lenient `queryInt`, which returns the default (50) on a malformed or negative value instead of failing closed. Other event filter fields (e.g. `zone`) reject malformed input with HTTP 400, so `limit` is an inconsistent fail-open scoping parameter.

## Current master (origin/master)
- `pkg/api/security.go:419` `eventsHandler`: `limit := queryInt(r, "limit", 50)`.
- `pkg/api/api.go:146` `queryInt`: `n, err := strconv.Atoi(v); if err != nil || n < 0 { return def }` — malformed/negative silently → default.
- The same handler's `zone` filter fails closed with HTTP 400 on a malformed/out-of-range value.

## Scenario (input → fail-open scoping)
`GET /api/v1/security/events?limit=-1` or `limit=abc` returns up to 50 events instead of rejecting the query, silently defaulting the caller's requested scope. A caller intending a narrow window gets the default window with no error.

## Fix
Use strict event-limit parsing (reject malformed/negative with HTTP 400, keep the 10000 upper cap) instead of `queryInt` here, mirroring the zone filter's fail-closed behavior. Tests for `limit=-1`, `limit=abc`, `limit=10001`.

## Severity justification
Low (input-validation inconsistency). Trigger: a malformed `limit` query param. Blast radius: silent default-window instead of a 400 — masks client bugs and returns a different scope than requested; `limit` is not an authz predicate so no security boundary. Bounded to the forensic-events read surface. Consistent with the handler's own fail-closed zone parsing.

Source: codex-review-175 C175-MC-012 (area A8). Verified present on current master.
