## #4952 — userspace-dp reconcile: post-teardown worker-spawn failure is swallowed → silent forwarding outage + persisted snapshot [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

**Severity: High** (codex-176 S1-RUST-RUNTIME-B2-01)

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/bringup.rs`: the old workers are torn down (`teardown::tear_down`) **before** new workers are spawned. On a spawn failure the `Err(err) =>` arm only logs, records an exception, and sets `coord.last_reconcile_stage = "spawn_worker_failed:.."`, but does not abort remaining launches or return failure. Immediately after the loop `coord.last_reconcile_stage` is unconditionally overwritten with `"spawned:workers=.."`. `bring_up_workers` returns `()`; `reconcile/mod.rs` returns `Ok(())`. In `server/handlers/snapshot.rs::reconcile_status_bindings`, only the pre-teardown integrity-build path returns `Err`; on the `Ok` path the handler runs `refresh_status(guard); *persist_state = true;` with `response.ok` still true.

**Failure:** a post-teardown `pthread_create` failure (EAGAIN/ENOMEM under resource exhaustion) tears down the old dataplane, leaves queues with no XSK-bound worker, yet acks `ok=true` and persists the snapshot as the boot baseline — a silent forwarding outage with no retry. Not covered by #3789 (fail-closes only pre-teardown build errors).

**Fix:** preflight all fallible worker-thread preparation before the destructive reconcile commit; on any spawn failure, fail closed (return Err, do not overwrite the failure stage, do not persist).

## #4953 — config: P4 firewall tcp-flags + numeric-DSCP semantic rejects bypass CompileConfigLenient — upgraded/peer config blackouts boot / HA-sync [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

**Severity: High** (codex-176 R5B1-GATE-01)

`pkg/config/compiler_dispatch.go:31` `compileSections` (P4) dispatches to section compilers; `compileFirewall(...)` and `compileClassOfService(...)` receive **no `compileOpts`**, so their checks cannot be mode-gated (only `compileSystem` gets opts). `pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:277` returns unconditionally on an invalid tcp-flags expression — the #3076 comment states the pre-gate code committed cleanly and dropped the constraint on the wire (older binaries persisted such config). `pkg/config/compiler_class_of_service.go:151` returns unconditionally on numeric DSCP/PCP — the #2447 comment states older code silently masked `dscp&0x3f` (older binaries persisted numeric DSCP). P4 returns the first section error **before** the P6/P7 lenient downgrades run. `pkg/configstore/store.go` `compileTreeLenient` documents that a strict reject here fails `Store.Load` (operational blackout: `ActiveConfig()==nil`) or `Store.SyncApply` (HA sync alarm-loop).

**Failure:** a node upgraded past #3076/#2447 restarts → `CompileConfigLenient` returns the tcp-flags/DSCP error → forwarding blackout; or standby `SyncApply` rejects an un-upgraded primary’s config → HA sync loop. This is the exact class the dozens of existing `lenient*` flags fix — these two gates were missed.

**Fix:** route the tcp-flags and numeric-DSCP/PCP section rejects through the strict/tolerant policy (thread `compileOpts` into `compileFirewall`/`compileClassOfService`; tolerant path returns a config + ordered warning + fail-closed fallback — invalid tcp-flags keeps an explicit deny sentinel, never widens to match-all). Scope: tcp-flags + numeric DSCP/PCP only (the deterministic-NAT sub-claim is unproven — the cited NAT comment concerns pool-utilization alarm, not the det-NAT block — and is excluded).

## #4954 — networkd: identical retry returns success after a prior failed networkctl reload (no cross-call reload/reconfigure debt) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

**Severity: High** (codex-176 R8B2-NETWORKD-01)

`pkg/networkd/networkd.go:74` `Manager` holds only `networkDir` + protected-set resolver — no applied-generation/dirty-bit/pending-reconfigure set. `Apply` uses a call-local `changed := false` (:169). On reload failure (~:241) it returns after the files are already written to disk. `writeIfChanged` returns `(false, nil)` on byte-identical content (:658). So an identical retry sees no file change → `changed==false` → **reload skipped → returns nil** while networkd/kernel still run the pre-failure config. A process restart reconstructs no pending state → same hole. `networkctl reconfigure` failure (~:258) is warn-only and likewise never retried.

**Failure:** a commit fails on a transient `networkctl reload`; the operator re-commits identical config → green commit, but the kernel still implements the old address/rename/bond/bridge/VRF state — route leak, stranded data NIC, or management lockout persists. `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go` joins only the first `Apply` error and cannot detect the later false-success. Distinct from #2987/#2988 (write-error-fails-commit) and codex-175 (stale-file remove).

**Fix:** give the Manager reload/reconfigure activation debt: on a failed reload/reconfigure, remember the pending activation and re-run the idempotent `networkctl` command on the next apply (even with unchanged files) until it succeeds before returning nil.

## #4955 — proxy-arp: NTF_PROXY neighbor entry orphaned when an interface is dropped from proxy-arp config (stale L2 ownership) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

**Severity: High** (codex-176 S2GDPB2-01)

`pkg/dataplane/proxyarp.go:185` `ReconcileProxyARP` builds `managedIfindexes`/`managedSet` **exclusively from `cfg.Security.NAT.ProxyARP`**, lists existing `NTF_PROXY` entries only `for idx := range managedSet`, and removes stale entries only from that listing. `pkg/daemon/daemon_proxyarp.go:107` computes `hasEntries := len(cfg.Security.NAT.ProxyARP) > 0` and only calls `ReconcileProxyARP` `if hasEntries`; on full removal it runs only the #2475 sysctl teardown (`diffProxyResponders`), never `NeighDel`. An interface dropped from the config is no longer in `managedSet`, so its installed `NTF_PROXY` entry is never listed or deleted. (Secondary: the add loop `return nil,nil,err` on the first `NeighSet` failure after prior adds, and the daemon then sets `d.proxyARPEnabled = enabled(=nil)`, wiping remembered state.)

**Failure:** removing a static-NAT/proxy-ARP address (or the last one) leaves the kernel answering ARP for the retired IPv4 via the topology-dependent pneigh branch until link reset/reboot — attracting traffic to an obsolete translation or a reassigned VIP. Distinct from #2475 (sysctl teardown only) and #2197 (v6 install + re-assert of *desired* entries).

**Fix:** track applied proxy-ARP state as a union of prior+desired interfaces; sweep/`NeighDel` entries for interfaces removed from the config before responder-sysctl teardown; make the add path record cleanup debt instead of nil-ing remembered state on partial failure.

## #4956 — device-map: enumerateAndRenameMapped swallows rename/reload failures (returns nil) — consumes config-arrival retry, continues reconcile on unconverged names [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-09)

**Severity: High** (codex-176 S2GDPB2-02)

`pkg/daemon/device_map.go:132` `enumerateAndRenameMapped` logs and continues on phase-2 final-rename failure (`slog.Warn("device-map: rename failed")`), phase-3 stranded-restore failure, and `networkctl reload` failure, then **`return nil` unconditionally**. It is reached via `applyStartupNamingForConfig` (`daemon_run.go:2015`). `maybeReapplyConfigArrivalNaming` (`daemon_run.go:2059-2067`) consumes the one-shot marker `d.emptyHANamingPending.Store(false)` whenever that call returns nil — so laundered failures defeat #4182’s retry-on-error guard. `applyConfigLocked` calls it at `daemon_apply.go:613` and ignores the bool, continuing into VRF/interface/dataplane reconcile. The removal path (`device_map.go:593-608`) `os.Remove`s the `.link`/`.network` ownership record even after a rename-back failure, leaving the NIC under an xpf name with no durable recovery intent.

**Failure:** on an HA node a failed mapped-NIC rename is reported as success → config wired onto nonexistent/wrong interface names, the single retry consumed, dataplane published → stranded management or wrong-NIC bind while commit reports no error. Not covered by #2083/#4178/#4182.

**Fix:** return a typed naming outcome; on any unverified NIC leave `emptyHANamingPending` set and abort dependent VRF/interface/dataplane reconcile; retain durable ownership for every unverified NIC; verify final logical names before consuming the marker.

## #4957 — HA config-sync: active-text-match shortcut treats a promoted-but-unapplied config as converged, skipping reconcile retry [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

**Severity: High** (codex-176 R6-b1-01)

`pkg/configstore/store.go:544` `SyncApply` sets `s.active = tree; s.compiled = compiled` (promotes active) **before** `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:349` `applyConfigLocked` runs inside `syncAndApply`; on apply error `syncAndApply` returns without rolling back `s.active`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:368-375` `handleConfigSync` returns nil when `activeText == incomingText`, and (per its own doc) the config high-water advances only on a nil return. `pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go` advances `lastAppliedConfigGen` only on a nil callback and relies on same-generation retry after failure.

**Failure:** delivery N promotes C1, `applyConfigLocked` fails (transient networkd/nft/IPsec tail error), high-water stays N-1. The primary re-pushes C1; the retry hits the active-text shortcut, returns nil, high-water advances to N — reconcile/finalization never re-run. The standby acks a generation whose dataplane never converged; on failover it can expose stale/disarmed forwarding while status claims the generation applied. Residual of #4151 (fixed the opposite advance-before-apply ordering and introduced this shortcut); not #4034.

**Fix:** base duplicate-skip on successfully-*applied* identity (e.g. a digest recorded only after a nil apply outcome) inside the apply transaction, not on active-store text equality; give nonfatal tail errors a defined same-generation retry contract.

**Severity: High** (codex-176 R6-b1-02)

`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:398` `startClusterComms` publishes cancel/context/transport, then starts session-sync construction in an untracked goroutine. After a ≤60s address-resolution loop that goroutine writes the shared `d.sessionSync = cluster.NewSessionSync(...)` (:551-553) and then re-dereferences the shared field (`d.sessionSync.SetAuthProvider(...)`) with no mutex and no final `commsCtx`/generation check; it also replaces `d.fabricRefreshCh`/`fabricRefreshCh1` (:821). `stopClusterComms` (:974-991) cancels but does not join the constructor and sets `d.sessionSync = nil`.

**Fix:** make comms a generation-local object with publish-if-current + detach/cancel/join; the constructor must close over its local instance, not re-read `d.sessionSync`; `Stop` must join every tracked constructor/listener.

## #4959 — userspace-dp: address-only commit mutates XDP classifier maps in place then fails open if apply_snapshot is rejected (no rollback, ctrl stays enabled) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

**Severity: High** (codex-176 R6B2-01)

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:1515` `snapshotBindingPlanKey` covers worker/ring/interface-binding + fabrics but **not** local or interface-NAT addresses, so an address-only commit takes the `samePlanRefresh` path (`manager_compile.go:293`). That path calls `syncUserspaceClassifierMapsFailClosedLocked` (`maps_sync.go:272`) which mutates ingress/local/interface-NAT BPF maps in place and disables ctrl **only if a map op itself errors**, then falls through to `apply_snapshot` (`manager_compile.go:323`). On helper rejection the function returns an error with maps on the NEW plan, ctrl still enabled, and `publishedSnapshot`/`lastSnapshot`/hash not advanced — no restore.

**Failure:** enabled XDP reads these maps to decide kernel-pass vs XSK-redirect and local/NAT ownership while Rust still enforces the previous-good snapshot → wrong kernel delivery / wrong XSK steering / security-availability mismatch, instead of the intended previous-good retention. Distinct from codex-161 H1-H3 (Rust internal same-plan mutation) and F-A7-2.

**Fix:** make map+helper-snapshot publication one fail-closed transaction — journal the classifier-map plan, and on helper rejection either restore the prior maps or disable ctrl; never leave maps on a newer generation than the applied Rust snapshot with ctrl enabled.

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/mod.rs:519` `rewrite_prepare_eth_from_parts` writes MAC/VLAN bytes and (without headroom) memmoves the L3 payload (`copy_within(l3..source_end, eth_len)`, ~:552) **before** any fallible check. `rewrite_forwarded_frame_in_place` (:755) calls prep then runs `rewrite_apply_v4/v6`, which can return `None` (TTL/hop-limit expiry, port mismatch, non-first fragment, unknown family, malformed IHL/ext-chain, truncated L4 checksum, VLAN-push-without-headroom). The flow-cache caller (`poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs:411`) chains `apply_rewrite_descriptor(...).or_else(|| rewrite_forwarded_frame_in_place(...))` on the **same** UMEM area; TX dispatch can reinject `source_frame` after an in-place `None`.

## #4969 — userspace-dp screen: consolidate ~13 parallel per-zone FxHashMaps into one ZoneScreenState — refresh-drift fail-open + redundant per-packet hashes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-21)

**Severity: Medium** (codex-176 R3B2-SCREEN-01)

`userspace-dp/src/screen/mod.rs:162` `ScreenState` stores profile + flood/cookie state in ~13 parallel `FxHashMap<String, _>` tables synchronized only by manual retention in `update_profiles` (:400-495). The ICMP/UDP/initial-SYN screen paths each hash the same zone `&str` several times per screened packet (e.g. `profiles.get(zone)` at :798, `icmp_dst_sketch.get_mut(zone)` at :659, plus aggregate/destination/source sketches). Missing table entries default to `false`/`0`/`Pass` (:805).

**Two real issues (not pure elegance):** (1) fail-open safety — a missed prepopulation step in a future `update_profiles` edit silently converts a configured limiter into a fail-open branch instead of failing at construction; (2) perf — multiple `String`-keyed hashes per packet, paid at packet rate exactly during the floods this code exists to survive. The production caller already resolves a stable `zone_id: u16` (`poll_stages.rs:431-447`) that most hot state ignores.

**Fix:** join per-zone profile + mutable flood/cookie state into one `ZoneScreenState` value (one lookup per screened packet); make refresh-drift a construction-time impossibility. Keep string keys initially; defer numeric-ID keying until #4421 supplies a stable ID/name/profile join. Distinct from #1543/F-138/fable-173-F10 (SYN-flood function split).

## #4970 — cli: remote completion sends rune-index Pos but the server slices req.Line by bytes — corrupts non-ASCII prefixes; Tab and ? use different units [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

**Severity: Low** (codex-176 S2B3-COMPLETE-03)

`remoteCompleter.Do` (`cmd/cli/shared.go:534-541`) sends `Line: string(line[:pos])` with `Pos: int32(pos)` — a **rune** index. The server `Complete` (`pkg/grpcapi/server_cluster.go:429-432`) does `text := req.Line; if int(req.Pos) < len(text) { text = text[:req.Pos] }` — slicing the UTF-8 **byte** string by the rune count, so any multibyte rune before the cursor makes `pos < len(bytes)` and truncates/splits a code point. The `?` listener (`cmd/cli/main.go:101`) instead sends `Pos: int32(len(text))` (a byte length) — Tab and `?` assign different units to the same RPC field.

**Failure:** remote tab-completion after a non-ASCII zone/interface description or pasted UTF-8 corrupts the prefix and misparses; local completion (rune-correct) stays right. ASCII is unaffected. Not covered by #2282 (negative-pos panic).

**Fix:** pin the RPC cursor unit (validated byte offset), fix the rune-based caller and align Tab/`?`; return `InvalidArgument` on an invalid byte boundary rather than emitting malformed text.

## #4971 — afxdp/tx: remove String allocation + last_error lock from expected TX retry / partial-submit paths [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-21)

**Severity: Medium** (codex-176 R2-b2-02)

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/transmit/mod.rs:16` `enum TxError { Retry(String), Drop(String) }` allocates a fresh retry String on expected-pressure outcomes (~:93 "no free TX frame available", ~:194 "no prepared TX frame available", ~:243 "tx ring insert failed") that recur every drain pass under backpressure; `let mut retry_tail = Vec::new();` (~:251) allocates on partial producer reservation. `finalise.rs:31/39` repeats both shapes for prepared batches. Callers pass retry strings to `BindingLiveState::set_error` (`tx/drain/phase_backup.rs:101/186`), taking the `last_error` mutex on expected congestion.

**Failure:** ring pressure is a normal operational state; heap + mutex work in the retry loop amplifies stalls and tail latency on the owner worker, opposing the repo’s no-allocation packet-path discipline. The full-batch success path is already allocation-free — the cost is concentrated exactly where least tolerable.

**Fix:** replace `TxError` strings with a copyable outcome enum; reuse the existing batch-64 scratch for `retry_tail` (reverse-pop preserves FIFO); drop the expected-retry `set_error` lock in favor of a compact status code. Distinct from #4408 (god-function decomposition) and PR #4268 (CoS admission strings).

## #4974 — userspace-dp event-stream: partial-write write_buf.drain(..n) is O(n²) — use a cursor-backed backlog [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

**Severity: Medium** (codex-176 R4B2-02)

`userspace-dp/src/event_stream/mod.rs:1126` the connected loop stores pending socket bytes in one `Vec<u8>` (cap `WRITE_BACKLOG_MAX_BYTES = 16*1024*1024`, :185). Every successful short write (:1146-1152) calls `write_buf.drain(..n)`, memmoving the entire remaining suffix to offset 0. A slow reader that repeatedly accepts small writes causes repeated multi-MiB copies → quadratic total copy work in backlog size, on the single event I/O thread, during exactly the slow-consumer condition the transport documents as bounded, counted degradation. Distinct from #2381 (CLOSED — added the byte cap; this fixes an algorithmic cost *inside* the cap).

**Failure:** a wedged reader accepting small writes makes ordinary partial-write progress burn a core on memmoves, delaying ACK/control processing, filling the producer channel, dropping telemetry, and can force HA session resync.

**Fix:** replace the prefix-drain with a cursor-backed backlog — advance a start index on a successful write, `write(&bytes[start..])`, with occasional geometric compaction (amortized linear).

## #4976 — afxdp: no build-time ABI check couples the Rust xsk_ring_{prod,cons} mirror to the installed libxdp layout [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

**Severity: High** (codex-176 R2-b2-01) — memory-safety hardening

`userspace-dp/src/xsk_ffi.rs:17` hand-mirrors `struct xsk_ring_prod`/`xsk_ring_cons` in `#[repr(C)]` Rust (`cached_prod, cached_cons, mask, size, *producer, *consumer, *ring, *flags`). `build.rs` compiles `csrc/xsk_bridge.c` against the installed `/usr/include/xdp/xsk.h` but adds **no `sizeof`/`offsetof` assertion** coupling the C layout to the Rust declarations. Rust allocates zeroed boxes (`:342`, `:1163`) and passes them to libxdp creation functions for C to populate (`xsk_bridge.c:20` takes them as native libxdp structs). The static libxdp + headers come from one package, but the Rust layout is an independent third copy with no build-time coupling.

**Reachability:** an upstream libxdp/header package upgrade that changes ring struct layout — a routine ops event given the project’s image-baking + kernel/OS upgrades (#1930) — turns a clean rebuild into out-of-bounds writes / misread indices in the AF_XDP ownership core: silent memory corruption, not a bind error, hard to diagnose from Rust. The 7 `xsk_ffi_tests.rs` cases exercise ownership, not ABI size/alignment/offset. Not covered by #253/PR #1299.

**Fix:** add a build-time (`build.rs`/C static-assert) size/alignment/offset check binding the Rust mirror to the installed libxdp ring structs (ideally move ring alloc/free behind opaque C handles), failing the build on layout drift.

**Severity: Medium** (codex-176 R10-B1-003) — supply-chain

`pkg/dataplane/userspace_xdp_rust.go:11` `//go:embed userspace_xdp_bpfel.o` — the tracked object, not the Rust source, is what production executes. `make build` is a plain go build (`Makefile:44`) and by design never runs `make generate`; `pkg/dataplane/README.md` documents this. `make test` runs Go + userspace-dp tests but neither rebuilds the shim nor proves the embedded object corresponds to current `userspace-xdp/**` inputs. Debian packaging + image bake package that same binary.

**Failure:** a logic-only edit to `userspace-xdp/**` (a packet-steering or security fix) not followed by `make generate` + committing the regenerated `.o` ships the **stale** object while source review and `make test` stay green. #1864 (CLOSED) gates toolchain drift + kernel-verifier rejection of a newly-generated object; it does not bind current source inputs to the already-tracked object.

**Fix:** add a deterministic source/toolchain/object provenance manifest (digest of `userspace-xdp/**` inputs + toolchain pin) and a cheap mandatory digest check wired into `make build`/`make test`/Debian build/image preflight that fails before packaging on a source↔object mismatch, even without root.

## #4997 — userspace-dp/xsk_ffi: ReadRx writes the RX consumer ring through a *mut cast from a shared &XskRingCons (UB; mirror ReadComplete's &mut) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

`ReadRx` (the AF_XDP RX consumer-ring reader) holds a **shared** reference
`ring: &'a XskRingCons`, then in both `release()` and `Drop::drop()` casts it
to `*mut XskRingCons` and calls the libxdp bridge, which mutates the struct
(`cached_cons`, and via the C helper the shared `*consumer` pointer). Writing
through a pointer derived from a `&T` that contains **no** `UnsafeCell` is
undefined behavior under Rust's aliasing model (Stacked/Tree Borrows): the
compiler is entitled to assume the pointee of a `&T` does not change, so this
can miscompile under optimization/LTO. Miri flags it.

This is on the production RX drain path (`RingRx::receive` is not
`cfg(test)`), so it executes on every RX poll.

## Location (current origin/master)

- `userspace-dp/src/xsk_ffi.rs:865-866` — `pub struct ReadRx<'a> { ring: &'a XskRingCons, ... }` (shared ref)
- `userspace-dp/src/xsk_ffi.rs:759-766` — `RingRx::receive(&mut self)` builds `ReadRx { ring: &*self.ring, .. }`
- `userspace-dp/src/xsk_ffi.rs:889-897` — `release()`: `let ring_ptr = self.ring as *const XskRingCons as *mut XskRingCons; bridge_xsk_ring_cons_release(ring_ptr, ...)`
- `userspace-dp/src/xsk_ffi.rs:901-913` — `impl Drop for ReadRx`: same const-cast for `bridge_xsk_ring_cons_release` / `bridge_xsk_ring_cons_cancel`

`XskRingCons` (xsk_ffi.rs:29-39) is a plain `#[repr(C)]` struct with no `UnsafeCell`, so `&XskRingCons` is `SharedReadOnly` — writes through any pointer derived from it are UB.

## Invariant basis

Rust reference-aliasing model. A mutable write requires either `&mut` or
interior mutability (`UnsafeCell`). Deriving `*mut` from `&T` (no `UnsafeCell`)
and writing is UB regardless of any "logical exclusivity" argument — the
in-code safety comment ("ReadRx has exclusive logical access") does not make the
cast sound, because soundness is a property of the reference *type*, not runtime
exclusivity.

## Why it's fixable trivially — the sibling already does it right

The completion-ring reader `ReadComplete` (xsk_ffi.rs:1033-1074) holds
`ring: &'a mut XskRingCons` and calls `bridge_xsk_ring_cons_release(self.ring, ..)`
with **no** cast. `WriteTx` likewise holds `&'a mut XskRingProd`. `ReadRx` is the
only ring reader holding a shared ref + casting away const. `RingRx::receive`
already takes `&mut self`, so a `&mut` reborrow is available.

## #5005 — daemon: applySystemLogin runs root id/useradd/chown without -- and no defensive username re-validation (option injection on lenient/peer-sync path) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

`applySystemLogin` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go`) runs root-privileged
`id`/`useradd`/`chown` with the config-supplied username as a leading positional
argument and **no `--` end-of-options separator**, and does not defensively
re-validate the name. A username beginning with `-` is therefore interpreted as
an option by those tools (option injection).

The strict commit path rejects such names (`ValidateLoginUsername`, regex
`^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*$`, wired as the `user` node `keyValidator` in
`schema_system.go`), but the tolerant Load / peer SyncApply path
(`compileTreeLenient`) downgrades the same check to a warning, so a leniently
loaded or peer-synced config CAN carry a leading-dash username that reaches
`applySystemLogin`. This is exactly the #4895/#1960 doctrine the sudoers writer
already follows defensively ("a leniently-loaded or peer-synced bad name still
never reaches the sudoers writer") — but the account/SSH-key writer does not.

## Location (current origin/master)

- `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go` — `runCommandTimeout("id", user.Name)` (~L796); `runCommandTimeout("useradd", args...)` where `args` ends with `user.Name` (~L804); `runCommandTimeout("chown", "-R", user.Name+":"+user.Name, sshDir)` (~L867). The only guard is `if user.Name == "" || user.Name == "root"`; no `ValidateLoginUsername` re-check.
- `pkg/config/schema_validators.go:211` `loginUsernameRE = ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*$`; validator at ~L225; wired at `pkg/config/schema_system.go:229`.

## Trace

Peer-synced/tolerant-loaded `system login user -u` → commit-check downgraded to
warning → `applySystemLogin` runs `id -u` (id treats `-u` as a flag, prints
UID 0, exits 0) → daemon concludes the user exists and skips `useradd`. A name
like `-r` makes `useradd -m -s /bin/bash -r` create a system account (or fail),
diverging from the declared config. `chown -R -name:...` similarly misparses.

## Invariant basis

Root-executed subprocesses must separate options from operator-controlled
positional arguments with `--`, and defense-in-depth validation must apply on
the tolerant path (#4895/#1960), matching the sudoers writer.

## Fix sketch

1. Add `--` before the username in `applySystemLogin`: `runCommandTimeout("id", "--", user.Name)`, `useradd ... "--", user.Name`, `chown -R -- owner sshDir`.
2. Defensively call `config.ValidateLoginUsername(user.Name, nil)` at the top of the per-user loop (skip+warn on failure), mirroring `writeSudoersGrant`/`reconcileSudoers`.

## #5006 — ddns: DHCP dynamic-DNS Manager holds m.mu across blocking RFC 2136 DNS UPDATE I/O — stalls Stats()/OwnedRecordViews (show + Prometheus) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

The DHCP dynamic-DNS `Manager.ReconcileScoped` acquires `m.mu` with `defer
m.mu.Unlock()` and holds it for the whole pass, including the blocking RFC 2136
DNS UPDATE network I/O inside `upsertLocked`/`deleteOwnedLocked`
(`updater.UpsertLease`/`updater.DeleteLease`, bounded by the ~5s DDNS timeout).
Telemetry/CLI readers `Stats()` and `OwnedRecordViews()` take `m.mu.Lock()`, so
`show system services dynamic-dns` and Prometheus scrapes block for the full DNS
exchange when the authoritative server is slow or offline.

The sibling `SurfaceAManager` already solves this: it wraps provider calls in
`providerIO`, releasing `m.mu` around the network call. `Manager` does not.

## Location (current origin/master)

- `pkg/ddns/manager.go:576` `ReconcileScoped`, `:609` `m.mu.Lock()` / `:610` `defer m.mu.Unlock()`.
- `:1075` `upsertLocked` → `UpsertLease` at `:1081`/`:1108`; `:1191` `deleteOwnedLocked` → `DeleteLease` at `:1218` (all under the held `m.mu`).
- Readers: `:1287` `OwnedRecordViews()` `m.mu.Lock()`, `:1307` `Stats()` `m.mu.Lock()`.
- Sibling pattern: `pkg/ddns/surface_a.go` `providerIO`.

## Invariant basis

Do not hold a lock that guards telemetry/monitoring reads across external
blocking network I/O — it turns a slow/offline DNS server into a control-plane
telemetry stall.

## Fix sketch

Introduce a `providerIO`-style helper in `Manager`: release `m.mu` around
`UpsertLease`/`DeleteLease`, guarding the reconcile against concurrent state
mutation (racing-reconcile guard) the way `SurfaceAManager` does.

## Provenance

gemini-review-045 A? Finding M3 (re-verified against origin/master 6f5968f08).

## #5007 — userspace-dp HA: SetSessionV4/V6 forward+reverse companion span an m.mu drop in syncSessionRequestLocked — concurrent ApplyConfig can resolve them against different snapshots [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

`SetSessionV4`/`SetSessionV6` install a forward session and then a reverse
companion under one `m.mu` acquisition, but `syncSessionRequestLocked`
**drops `m.mu` around the control-socket I/O** (`m.mu.Unlock()` →
`requestSessionSync` → `m.mu.Lock()`, deliberately, "so snapshot publishes
aren't blocked"). A concurrent `ApplyConfig` can acquire `m.mu` in that gap and
swap `m.lastSnapshot`, so the reverse companion — built afterward by
`buildSessionSyncRequestV4`, which resolves egress/zone via `zoneNameByID` /
`sessionSyncEgressLocked` / `sessionSyncTunnelEndpointLocked` against
`m.lastSnapshot` — is resolved against a **different** snapshot than the forward
entry. Forward and reverse can then carry drifted egress-interface / zone /
tunnel-endpoint metadata.

## Location (current origin/master)

- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:864` `SetSessionV4` (`:871` `m.mu.Lock()` / `:872` `defer`), forward then reverse `syncSessionV4Locked` calls.
- `:1014` `syncSessionV4Locked` → `buildSessionSyncRequestV4` (reads snapshot-derived egress/zone) → `:1204` `syncSessionRequestLocked` which does `m.mu.Unlock()` → `requestSessionSync` → `m.mu.Lock()`.
- `SetSessionV6` is the analogous path.

## Invariant basis

The forward/reverse companion pair must be resolved against a single, consistent
config snapshot — the transactional consistency the pair depends on is broken by
the intra-pair lock gap.

## Mitigations to weigh (why impact may be bounded)

- The reverse's FIB cache is deliberately cleared (`FibIfindex/…=0`) and "re-resolved locally," so some drift may be corrected by the worker at activation.
- The window is only the forward request's socket I/O, and only a commit landing exactly in that window is affected.

Still, the forward is resolved+sent against snapshot A while the reverse is
resolved against snapshot B — a real cross-write consistency race worth closing.

## Fix sketch

Build BOTH the forward and reverse `SessionSyncRequest` structs under a single
uninterrupted `m.mu` hold (snapshot reads complete before any unlock), then
release and transmit both over the socket in sequence.

## #5010 — system/dns: name-server resolver leaf lacks a render belt (validator/belt asymmetry vs #4902) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

The `#4902` injection-hardening work (PR #5009) established a validator + render-belt double boundary for every `system` string leaf that reaches a root-owned reloaded config file (ntp/domain/ssh/syslog). The **resolver `name-server`** leaf (pre-#4902) has a commit-time validator (`ValidateIPAddress`) but **no `mergeDNSInput` render belt**, unlike the sibling `domain-name`/`domain-search` which #5009 gave both a validator AND a belt.

Under the #1960 doctrine, commit validation is downgraded to a warning on the lenient/peer-sync load path — so the render belt is the real security boundary. `name-server` currently lacks that second boundary.

## Impact: LOW / non-exploitable today

Per the #5009 review, the residual is non-exploitable in practice:
- `resolv.conf` `nameserver` ignores trailing tokens on the line,
- the `DNS=` target is masked resolved,
- a newline is globally scrubbed by `SanitizeTreeControlChars`.

So this is a **defense-in-depth symmetry gap**, not a live injection. But the #4902 pattern is now the norm; `name-server` should follow it for consistency and to close the lenient-load asymmetry.

## Fix

Add a `mergeDNSInput` render belt for `name-server` (re-validate each value with `ValidateIPAddress` at render, fail-closed skip on failure), mirroring the `domain-name`/`domain-search` belt placement (`daemon_dns.go` `mergeDNSInput`, upstream of both `RenderResolvConf` and `RenderResolvedDropin`).

## Provenance

So this is a low-impact, theoretical hardening gap, filed separately per the #5009 review's recommendation.

Validate the `time-zone` value against a zoneinfo name grammar (LDH + `/` segments, reject `..` / absolute-path components) at commit-check, and/or resolve+verify the symlink target stays within the zoneinfo root before creating `/etc/localtime`.

## #5023 — snmp: -race data race on package-global trapSender (traps.go:400 read vs traps_async_2991_test.go:23 write) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

`go test -race ./pkg/snmp/` fails deterministically (3/3 runs) on
`TestSendLinkTraps_DoesNotBlock` (`traps_async_2991_test.go`) with a DATA RACE
on the package-global `trapSender` func var:

- **Read** at `pkg/snmp/traps.go:400` (inside `trapWorker`, reached via the
  worker loop at `:356`) — the running trap worker goroutine invokes `trapSender`.
- **Write** at `pkg/snmp/traps_async_2991_test.go:23` — the test swaps
  `trapSender` for a mock during setup.

The worker goroutine (started under `trapWorkerOnce`) reads the global while the
test writes it, with no synchronization. Pre-existing on origin/master (confirmed
at 983860d17, independent of #4916/#5022 — verified the same race on a clean
master worktree).

## Impact: LOW (test-infra)

`trapSender` is only reassigned in tests (production sets it once at init and
never swaps it concurrently), so this is not a production data race. But it makes
`go test -race ./pkg/snmp/` red, which MASKS any real race in the package and
blocks clean -race CI for snmp.

## Fix

Inject the trap sender per-Agent instead of via a mutated package global — e.g.
an `Agent.trapSender` field set at construction (default to the real sender),
which the worker reads from `a` (no global). The #2991 async test then sets the
field on its Agent before starting the worker, with no cross-goroutine write to a
shared global. Alternatively guard the global behind a mutex/atomic, but the
per-Agent field is cleaner and removes the global test-injection seam.

## Provenance

Surfaced while race-testing PR #5022 (#4916 Agent.Stop leak); confirmed
pre-existing on master, so filed separately rather than folded into #5022.

## #5024 — test/incus: test-failover.sh reads $CLUSTER_LAN_HOST but env defines $LAN_HOST — failover harness uses wrong (unreachable) LAN host [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

`test/incus/test-failover.sh` reads `$CLUSTER_LAN_HOST` for the LAN traffic
source (lines 72, 94, 101, 114-148 — the reachability pre-flight, iperf3 client
launch, and liveness checks). But the canonical cluster env
`test/incus/loss-userspace-cluster.env` defines the LAN host as **`LAN_HOST`**
(`LAN_HOST="cluster-userspace-host"`, `LAN_HOST_IP="10.0.61.102"`), NOT
`CLUSTER_LAN_HOST`. So `$CLUSTER_LAN_HOST` is unset/defaulted to the WRONG host
(`cluster-lan-host`, 10.0.89.102), which is on a different subnet
(default via 10.0.89.1) with NO route to the WAN iperf3 target 172.16.80.200.

Result: `make test-failover` (default CLUSTER_ENV=loss-userspace-cluster.env)
aborts at the pre-flight with `Cannot reach iperf3 target 172.16.80.200 from
cluster-lan-host` before the failover ever runs — even though the cluster
forwards fine (verified: `iperf3 -c 172.16.80.200` from the CORRECT LAN host
cluster-userspace-host = 7.64 Gbit/s, 0 retr).

`make test-failover` / `test-double-failover` / `test-ha-crash` / etc. are
UNRUNNABLE on the canonical loss userspace cluster without manually overriding
`CLUSTER_LAN_HOST=cluster-userspace-host`. This silently blocks the mandated
HA/session-sync/failover validation gate.

## Fix

Make test-failover.sh (and the sibling test-*.sh HA scripts) read `LAN_HOST`
from the cluster env (or have the env export both names / the script fall back
`CLUSTER_LAN_HOST="${CLUSTER_LAN_HOST:-$LAN_HOST}"`). Align the variable name
across the env files and all test/incus/test-*.sh scripts that source them.

## Provenance

Found while running the mandated test-failover gate for PR #5017 (#5007 HA
session-sync). The failover harness could not reach the target from its chosen
LAN host; the correct env-declared host (cluster-userspace-host) reaches it and
sustains 7.64 Gbit/s through the deployed build.

## #5031 — api: unauthenticated /health exposes raw compile/bootstrap error strings (no scrubber before an always-public response) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

`authMiddleware` unconditionally exempts `/health` from authentication (`pkg/api/auth.go:26-32`), and `healthHandler` copies raw error strings into the public payload: `compile_last_error` from `h.LastError` (`pkg/api/health.go:23-24`) and `bootstrap_import_error` from `b.Error` (`pkg/api/health.go:41-51`). Those strings are stored verbatim upstream — `d.compileLastError = err.Error()` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_health.go:87`) and `d.recordBootstrapImport(bootstrapImportFailed, err.Error())` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1647`) — with no redaction. The day-0 import error can originate from config schema validators that quote raw submitted values, e.g. `pkg/config/schema_validators_system.go:105-107` returns `…got %q…` for a bad `system login` password, echoing a plaintext secret.

**Invariant:** a liveness/readiness probe that is intentionally unauthenticated must expose only status, counters, timestamps, and stable reason codes — not untrusted raw parser/compiler strings that may carry credentials, tokens, file paths, or topology. Error provenance currently crosses from secret-bearing configuration into an unauthenticated response with no sanitization boundary. Bounded on the loopback default (`127.0.0.1:8080`) but real on a routable authenticated listener (same rebind class as the `/metrics` hardening).

**Fix direction:** keep public `/health` to status/counters/timestamps and stable reason codes; move raw compile/bootstrap detail behind an authenticated admin endpoint, and run the same secret/error scrubber used by config-render paths before storing or returning any detail. Add a health test with a secret sentinel asserting it never appears in the `/health` body.

## #5032 — snmp/v3: privacy parameters are independent random draws, not RFC-required unique salts (no guaranteed IV uniqueness) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

`encryptDES` (`pkg/snmp/v3.go:798-820`) and `encryptAES128` (`pkg/snmp/v3.go:824-840`) each generate the 8-byte privacy parameter with a fresh `rand.Read(privParams)` and no per-key uniqueness state. For DES the CBC IV is `preIV ^ privParams` where `preIV` is a fixed key-derived constant, so the IV varies only with the random `privParams`. For AES-CFB the IV is `boots || time || privParams`, so the low 64 bits are purely random.

**Invariant/RFC basis:** RFC 3414 §8.1.1.1 (DES) and RFC 3826 §3.1.2.1 (AES) require the salt to be *unique* within an engineBoots/engineTime domain — "must be different for each packet." Independent 64-bit random draws give only probabilistic (birthday) uniqueness: DES reaches material collision odds near 2^32 messages under one key; AES reuses an IV when engineBoots and the 1-second engineTime bucket also coincide with a colliding draw. IV reuse under AES-CFB exposes XOR relationships between plaintexts; DES-CBC reveals repeated first-block structure. Confidentiality only — authentication unaffected — and the volume needed is far beyond realistic appliance SNMP rates, hence Low.

**Fix direction:** seed an agent-owned 64-bit salt counter once from `crypto/rand`, allocate values with an atomic increment (or a lock shared by response and trap encryption), and combine with the required engineBoots/engineTime fields. Treat counter wrap as a hard key/engine-rollover failure; add concurrency and near-wrap tests that inspect uniqueness state rather than just field presence.

## #5045 — metrics: counter-read errors during unloaded-dataplane boot emit no error series (pre-gate bump lost to the IsLoaded early return) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

`Collect` runs the pre-gate kernel collectors (`collectHostInboundKernelDenies`, junos-host, lo0, ICMP/ND) — each does `c.counterReadErrors.Add(1)` and skips its series on an nft read failure (`pkg/api/metrics_counters.go:64,89,115,146`). It then hits `if dp == nil || !dp.IsLoaded() { return }` at `pkg/api/metrics.go:1039`, and only reaches `c.emitCounterReadErrors(ch)` at `:1056` on the loaded path. So during a degraded/config-only boot (dataplane unloaded) with a failing nft read, the scrape carries neither the data series nor the `xpf_counter_read_errors_total` sample — a clean absence.

**Invariant:** the #3345/#3462 omit-plus-error contract — whenever a series is omitted because its read failed, the same scrape must carry the error signal, including on every early-return path. The current control flow violates it in exactly the unloaded-dataplane boot state those pre-gate collectors exist to observe.

**Fix direction:** emit `counterReadErrorsTotal` immediately before the unloaded return (once per scrape), or restructure so error-counter emission is a final phase reached by every return (deferred emit). Add a gather test with a failed pre-gate nft read plus nil dataplane.

## #5046 — NAT stats (REST + gRPC): telemetry read failures render as healthy zero usage/hits with success (no unavailable marker) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

Both the REST (`pkg/api/nat.go`) and gRPC (`pkg/grpcapi/server_nat.go`) NAT-stats surfaces swallow telemetry read errors and render them as healthy zero usage/hits with a success status:
- `pkg/api/nat.go:29-31` — `runtimeSourceNATPools` returns bare `nil` on `provider.Status()` error (indistinguishable from provider-absent / empty).
- `pkg/api/nat.go:285-288` — `ReadNATRuleCounter` error → `hitPkts/hitBytes` stay 0, still HTTP 200.
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_nat.go:133-135` — `NATPortCounter` error → `used64` stays 0.
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_nat.go:224-227` — `NATRuleCounter` error → returns `0,0`.

Missing apply-IDs legitimately mean "no counter," but the failure case is distinguishable: the ID exists and the telemetry call returns an error. An operator cannot tell idle NAT from a telemetry-bridge failure.

**Invariant:** operational counters must fail closed as *unavailable*, not fail open to a clean zero, when authoritative runtime state cannot be read (project #3345 counter-error contract, already implemented on other surfaces).

**Fix direction:** return a typed runtime result carrying availability/error/provenance; add `unavailable`/`source` fields to REST NAT stats and return an RPC error (or degraded marker) on gRPC; omit failed Prometheus samples and bump the shared read-error metric; preserve config fallback only behind an explicit `config_fallback` marker. Add injected-error tests for pool and rule counters on both surfaces.

Note: the CLI sibling (`show nat` DNAT summary, A10-b1-F6) is already tracked by #4908; these are the distinct REST + gRPC surfaces.

## #5047 — grpcapi: fabric listener listen/Serve failure is terminal and unsupervised — peer RPC surface silently lost until comms restart [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## #5048 — flowexport: batch max-depth high-water update races outside the batch mutex — high-water can regress under concurrent adds [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

The batch high-water update is done AFTER `b.mu.Unlock()`: `pkg/flowexport/transport.go:475` unlocks `b.mu`, then `:478-479` does a non-atomic load-then-store — `if depth > b.maxDepth.Load() { b.maxDepth.Store(depth) }` — outside the lock. The `:476-477` comment claiming mutex serialization is incorrect: the append is serialized, the max update is not. Two concurrent adders can interleave (A computes depth 1, B computes depth 2; both load 0; B stores 2, then A stores 1), so the published high-water mark regresses. No `-race` report fires (both ops are atomic), but it is a logical read-modify-write race; `MaxDepth()` (`:533`) exposes the under-reported value on the live NetFlow export path.

**Invariant:** a high-water counter is monotonic over its measurement epoch — every update must be `max(old, observed)` atomically; readers must never see a lower value after a higher one.

**Fix direction:** update `maxDepth` while still holding `b.mu`, or use a CAS-max loop. Add a barrier test forcing two successful compares before reverse-order stores and asserting monotonicity.

## #5049 — snmp: v1 traps supported but v1 polling (GET/GETNEXT) silently dropped — legacy v1 managers time out [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

The SNMP agent request dispatch handles only `snmpVersion2c` (1) and `snmpVersion3` (3); the `default` branch logs at debug and returns nil (`pkg/snmp/agent.go:605-618`). There is no `case 0` (SNMPv1). Yet the trap path implements v1: `buildLinkTrapV1` / `case "v1"` (`pkg/snmp/traps.go:134,197-198`). So the agent emits SNMPv1 link traps (config-selectable) but silently drops all v1 GET/GETNEXT polling (version field 0 → `default` → nil response). A legacy v1 manager configured for the same community times out and sees the device as down, even though v1 trap config implies version support.

**Invariant:** every advertised/configurable protocol version must have complete request/response semantics or be rejected explicitly at config time. v1 GET/GETNEXT responses must use v1 noSuchName/error-index rules and avoid v2-only syntax (no exception values, no Counter64).

**Fix direction:** implement a v1 request handler sharing the bounded MIB lookup with v1 error-status/index and type restrictions (GET/GETNEXT/SET, source allowlist, malformed-BER and packet-size tests); OR, if v1 polling is intentionally unsupported, reject incompatible config and document the limitation rather than time out silently.

## #5054 — ha: REST (and local-shell) commits skip peer config-sync — HA peer serves stale firewall intent after failover [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## #5055 — api: REST mutation routes lack CSRF/cross-site defense — browser-ambient Basic credentials authorize state changes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

`pkg/api/auth.go:66-84` accepts HTTP Basic (an ambient browser credential) and advertises `WWW-Authenticate: Basic`; `pkg/api/api.go:103-116` (`decodeJSONBody`) decodes bodies without checking `Content-Type`. A repo-wide grep found NO `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch`/`Referer`/`CSRF`/`SameSite` handling anywhere in `pkg/api`. State-changing routes registered at `pkg/api/server.go:~458-466` (config set/delete/activate/load, commit, clear, system reboot/halt) are therefore reachable via a cross-site credentialed POST with a safelisted content type: a malicious page can drive `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8080/...',{credentials:'include',mode:'no-cors'})` and the browser attaches cached Basic creds. Loopback bind does not mitigate.

**Invariant:** the same-origin policy prevents *reading* the response but not *sending* the side-effecting request; control-plane mutation requires proof of operator intent, not merely credential possession.

**Fix direction:** on every mutation route require `application/json`, reject cross-site `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-Site` for Basic-authenticated requests, and require a CSRF token bound to a server secret (or drop browser-ambient Basic from mutation workflows); keep header-based API-key/Bearer clients supported.

## #5057 — api: diagnostic REST/gRPC ping/traceroute have no aggregate concurrency bound — management-plane DoS [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## #5065 — snmp: GETBULK encodes multiple repeaters column-major, violating RFC 3416 §4.2.3 varbind order (v2c + v3) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

Both GETBULK loops nest `for i := nonRepeaters..len(oids)` (outer, per repeater column) around `for j := 0..maxRepetitions` (inner) — `pkg/snmp/agent.go:841-854` (v2c) and `pkg/snmp/v3.go:457-469` (v3) — emitting `A1,A2,B1,B2` (column-major). RFC 3416 §4.2.3 mandates repetition-major (`A1,B1,A2,B2`). A table-oriented manager reconstructs rows by repeater-width R and mis-associates columns. Two independent copies; existing single-repeater tests don't exercise it.

**Invariant/RFC:** RFC 3416 §4.2.3 — for R repeater columns and M repetitions the response must be repetition-major; response index `row*R + column` must derive from that column's own prior cursor, including endOfMibView placeholders in the correct cell.

**Fix direction:** keep one cursor/end-state per repeater, loop outermost over repetition and innermost over repeater, place endOfMibView in the exhausted column's cell; share one implementation between v2c/v3; add two- and three-repeater wire-order tests with early column exhaustion and size trimming.

## #5069 — cli: 'show log N' accepts an unbounded count and buffers the whole journalctl/tail result in xpfd (PermView DoS) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## #5071 — dhcp-relay: second-hop relay overwrites a downstream relay's giaddr and Option 82 (RFC 1542 §4.1.1 chaining) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

The DHCP relay stamps its own giaddr unconditionally (`pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go:1141`, `pkt.GatewayIPAddr = giaddr`) and replaces Option 82 unconditionally (`addOption82` at `:1516-1527`, `Options.Del(option82)` then overwrite), even when the inbound BOOTREQUEST already carries a nonzero `giaddr` from a downstream relay. RFC 1542 §4.1.1 requires an intermediate relay to preserve a nonzero giaddr (only increment/validate hops); rewriting it makes the server select the wrong pool and return to xpf, and destroys the original relay's circuit-id. Neither preservation nor an explicit nonzero-giaddr reject exists.

**Invariant/RFC:** RFC 1542 §4.1.1 / RFC 3046 — the first relay owns giaddr and Option 82; later relays increment/validate hops without rewriting downstream identity.

**Fix direction:** if `giaddr == 0`, stamp local giaddr + apply the trusted-edge Option 82 policy; if nonzero, preserve giaddr and the existing relay-agent option while incrementing/validating hops; add nonzero-giaddr chain tests and an explicit untrusted-client Option 82 policy.

## #5072 — ddns: Kea adapter drops IA_PD discriminator — delegated-prefix bases published as host AAAA/PTR records [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

`keaLeaseParser` converts each memfile lease into `ddns.Lease` copying only Family/Address/Identity/SubnetID/HostName/ClientFQDN and explicitly dropping the v6 discriminator (`LeaseType`/`PrefixLen`) — `pkg/dhcpserver/ddns.go:59-65`. `ddns.Lease` has no `LeaseType` (`pkg/ddns/manager.go:77-84`), so the reconciler cannot gate; `buildLeaseRecord(fqdn, l.Address, ...)` (`:832-853`) is built for every named lease with no type gate, so it parses an IA_PD prefix base (e.g. `2001:db8:abcd::`) as a host address and publishes an AAAA/PTR for a delegated network.

**Fix direction:** carry lease type into `ddns.Lease` and reject IA_PD before name/record derivation (prefer an explicit address-lease allowlist); add a mixed IA_NA/IA_PD memfile test proving only IA_NA publishes.

## #5073 — ha/dhcpserver: DHCPv6 lease-sync drops preferred lifetime — deprecated addresses/prefixes revived at takeover [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## #5076 — upgrade/kernel: failed candidate purge is followed by unconditional deletion of package-owned files (dpkg/file divergence) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

A dpkg-lock / maintainer-script failure leaves `linux-image`/`modules`/`headers-<candidate>` installed (often held) while their payload is deleted; a later `apt-get install <same-version>` without `--reinstall` sees the package current and never restores `/boot` or `/lib/modules`.

**Invariant:** package-database/file-ownership consistency + retryability — manual deletion of package-owned files must only follow confirmed package removal.

**Fix direction:** on purge failure, leave package-owned files intact and return a degraded/error result after restoring the safe slot selector; perform manual cleanup only after confirming packages are absent (or repair via dpkg/apt); require `--reinstall` on a same-version retry when payload integrity is uncertain; add a purge-failure test seam.

## #5077 — test/incus: submit-latency classifier permits negative bucket deltas after counter reset (missing submit-side K3 monotonicity) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

The submit-latency histogram classifier's delta loop (`test/incus/step1-histogram-classify.py:258-266`) normalizes whenever `count_delta > 0` without checking `buckets_delta < 0` or cumulative-count monotonicity — unlike the kick side, which has the full K3 monotonicity guard including `bucket_diff < 0` (`:229-254`). A counter reset (daemon restart) can move total count 10000→12000 while a low-frequency bucket goes 1000→0, yielding negative shape values (`-0.5`, `1.5`) fed to the D1/D2 permutation stats — a non-probability distribution passing as non-suspect (false PASS in a perf gate).

**Invariant:** histogram wire / cumulative-counter monotonicity — a reset-and-recover sequence must mark the cell suspect, not emit a shape with negative bucket fractions.

**Fix direction:** mirror K3 for submit count, sum, every histogram bucket, and `tx_packets` before computing deltas; reject any negative delta; add a reset-and-recover fixture proving the cell halts rather than classifies.

Belongs to the test/incus perf-analysis evidence-integrity theme of #4907; cross-ref #4907.

## #5078 — cluster: session-sync PSK handshake is reflection-authenticatable (no role/identity binding, equal nonce accepted, undirected key) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-21)

**Severity:** High | **Confidence:** High | **Source:** codex-review-177 `[A5-b1-F1]`

**Problem.** The mutual challenge-response session-sync handshake has no initiator/responder role, node/endpoint identity, or channel binding, and it accepts an equal (reflected) nonce. An attacker on a fabric TCP endpoint can echo the node's HELLO/proof and be accepted as the authenticated peer without the PSK, displacing the real connection and reading all plaintext session/config state.

**Current code (origin/master `812bf30c1`).** `pkg/cluster/sync_auth.go:330-408` sends `proofOut := syncAuthProof(key, peerNonce)` (L388-390) before reading the peer proof, then accepts `hmac.Equal(ppayload, syncAuthProof(key, localNonce))` (L401). `syncDeriveFrameKey` canonically sorts the two nonces (L228-240) so the derived frame key is undirected; there is no equal-nonce rejection, transcript label, or identity binding.

**Invariant / basis.** Authentication must prove possession by the opposite role and derive independent initiator→responder / responder→initiator keys; a reflected nonce/proof must be rejected.

**Impact.** A PSK-less fabric attacker is accepted as the authenticated peer, can displace the real connection, disclose session/config state, refresh sync liveness, and feed reflected signed frames into peer-state handlers — the configured security boundary is not authenticated.

**Fix direction.** Bind HELLO and PROOF to a full transcript (protocol version, cluster/node identity, endpoint/fabric identity, explicit initiator/responder role); reject equal/reflected nonces; derive separate directional frame keys and counters. Prefer a standard mutually-authenticated TLS/Noise construction over extending the custom handshake.

**Provenance.** codex-review-177 `[A5-b1-F1]`, High/High.

## #5079 — cluster: remote failover demotes owner before requester commit with no abort frame, lease, or reqID-bound rollback (both nodes can strand secondary) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

**Severity:** High | **Confidence:** High | **Source:** codex-review-177 `[A5-b1-F2]`

**Problem.** `RequestPeerFailover` drives the remote owner through `ManualFailover` (SecondaryHold, VRRP resign) before the requester's own post-ACK readiness/commit checks. If any requester-side step fails after the ACK, the only rollback (`abortRequestedPeerFailover`) restores the requester's local override — no abort is sent to the already-demoted owner, and no lease/expiry auto-restores it.

**Current code (origin/master `812bf30c1`).** `pkg/cluster/failover.go:243-277` calls the remote `fn(rgID)` before `commitRequestedPeerFailover`/`localCommitReadyFn`/`commitFn`; abort paths call only `abortRequestedPeerFailover(rgID,reqID)` (local). `pkg/cluster/sync_failover.go:422-437` runs `OnRemoteFailover(rgID)` before ACK and passes only `rgID`; `FinalizePeerTransferOut` discards `reqID`. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:672-698` calls `ManualFailover` immediately.

**Invariant / basis.** Ownership transfer requires one durable state machine keyed by (peer boot epoch, request ID, RG set) with prepare→commit|abort|expiry.

**Impact.** A transient requester readiness change or fabric write failure during planned failover can leave both firewalls secondary after the old owner has withdrawn VIP/VRRP/RA service — a persistent outage from a supposedly coordinated operation.

**Fix direction.** Make remote prepare reserve (not irreversibly demote), or install a request-bound lease that auto-rolls back. Add abort frames/ACKs, pass reqID + peer boot epoch into receiver callbacks, reject stale/replayed commits, and apply the same transaction to batch failover.

**Provenance.** codex-review-177 `[A5-b1-F2]`, High/High.

## #5080 — cluster: monitor reconciliation fails open on a missing local link and retains stale monitor debt after removal/change [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

**Severity:** High | **Confidence:** High | **Source:** codex-review-177 `[A5-b1-F3]`

**Problem.** A configured local member link that is absent (cold boot or delete/recreate between polls) is dropped with only a warning — no down-state/weight is published, so an already-primary node keeps weight 255 and stays primary while its data link is missing. Conversely, removing or changing a failed monitor only replaces the desired slice; stale ifaceState/monitorWeights/MonitorFails persist, stranding a healthy node secondary.

**Current code (origin/master `812bf30c1`).** `pkg/cluster/monitor.go:291-301` on `LinkByName` failure (local slot) only `slog.Warn("...local interface missing")`+`continue`, with no `SetMonitorWeight(down)`. `UpdateGroups` (:226-231) just sets `mon.groups=groups`; `group_state.go:41-51` clears weights only when the whole RG disappears; `election.go:308-316` gates only new promotions.

**Invariant / basis.** Every reconcile must derive effective RG weight from the complete current desired monitor set and observed state; missing local links = down, removed keys = zero.

**Impact.** Fail-open half can keep a firewall primary with an absent data link (blackhole); stale-debt half strands a healthy node secondary after the operator removes/changes the failed monitor, so applied config diverges from runtime ownership.

**Fix direction.** Reconcile monitor state as desired/applied data: build a desired key/weight map, mark missing local links down, clear removed keys from monitor state and manager weights, reapply changed weights, recompute each RG atomically.

**Provenance.** codex-review-177 `[A5-b1-F3]`, High/High.

## #5081 — cluster: committed control-link PSK / heartbeat-timing changes are absent from the transport restart key and never applied to live comms [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-21)

**Severity:** High | **Confidence:** High | **Source:** codex-review-177 `[A5-b1-F4]`

**Problem.** The cluster-communications restart trigger keys only on endpoint fields, excluding the control-link auth posture and heartbeat interval/threshold. Enabling/rotating a PSK or changing heartbeat timing updates manager desired fields but never re-handshakes live session-sync connections or resets the running heartbeat sender/receiver.

## #5082 — vrrp: publishes MASTER/advert/event before VIP netlink actuation succeeds (no fail-closed/retry); ReconcileVIPs check-then-act can re-add VIPs after demotion [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

**Severity:** High | **Confidence:** High | **Source:** codex-review-177 `[A5-b1-F7]`

**Problem.** `becomeMaster` sets StateMaster and calls void `addVIPs()`, then advertises/emits the Master event regardless of whether the kernel VIP add succeeded. `addVIPs` swallows LinkByName/AddrAdd failures with no debt, rollback, or retry. Separately `ReconcileVIPs` is a check-then-act with no ownership generation, so a concurrent superior-advert transition to Backup can interleave and re-add VIPs + forced GARP while Backup.

**Current code (origin/master `812bf30c1`).** `pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1849-1867` (becomeMaster) and `:2093-2121` (addVIPs return nothing; AddrAdd failure → log+continue). `pkg/vrrp/manager.go:594-616` ReconcileVIPs `if vi.getState()==StateMaster { vi.addVIPs() ... }`.

**Invariant / basis.** MASTER publication, peer advertisement, service event, and kernel VIP set must be one generation-owned transition; revalidate ownership generation after netlink before GARP.

**Impact.** A transient netlink failure makes the peer and dependent services trust an owner that cannot receive VIP traffic; the reconcile race can leave a Backup owning/announcing VIPs (duplicate-address, ARP/ND, split-routing).

**Fix direction.** Make VIP add/remove return structured results, track a desired/applied ownership generation, gate the Master advert/event on successful required VIP actuation, roll back or enter a degraded non-owner state on partial failure, and revalidate generation after netlink before GARP.

**Provenance.** codex-review-177 `[A5-b1-F7]`, High/High.

## #5083 — vrrp: generic collector drops Linux-name / unit / address-family identity, silently failing standalone and dual-stack VRRP [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

**Problem.** The generic VRRP collector stores the raw Junos interface name (with `/`) and no unit/VLAN, so the manager's `net.InterfaceByName("ge-0/0/0")` fails and no instance is built. Because the manager key is `(interface, VRID)` with no family/unit field, dual-stack v4+v6 groups on one unit (and different units with the same VRID) collide to one key — last-wins silently drops a family/segment.

**Impact.** A valid standalone/vSRX VRRP config can be accepted while no Linux instance starts, or one half of dual-stack is silently discarded — HA fails on exactly the segment/family the operator believes is protected.

**Fix direction.** Resolve raw interface + unit/VLAN to the canonical Linux logical name before collection; merge same-interface/same-VRID v4+v6 only when election params match or preserve family in the manager key; reject conflicting collisions deterministically.

## #5121 — lldp: Apply/Stop lack a lifecycle mutex — concurrent shutdown races WaitGroup setup and can omit an RX socket from teardown [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

**Severity:** Medium | **Confidence:** Medium | **Source:** codex-review-177 `[A7-b2-F10]`

**Problem.** `Apply` writes `m.cancel` with no lifecycle lock and calls `m.wg.Add(1)` incrementally after publishing sessions; `Stop` reads `m.cancel`, snapshots sessions, and calls `m.wg.Wait()` — only `m.mu` guards sessions, nothing guards cancel/wg. Daemon shutdown calls `lldpMgr.Stop()` without holding applySem, so a SIGTERM during an in-flight LLDP apply races wg.Add against wg.Wait (WaitGroup misuse) plus a data race on m.cancel, and can park an RX goroutine in Recvfrom outside Stop's session snapshot.

**Current code (origin/master `812bf30c1`).** `pkg/lldp/lldp.go:235-315` (Apply) and `:324-345` (Stop); reachable via `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:867` runShutdownSequence.

**Invariant / basis.** WaitGroup Add must not race Wait; every published FD must belong to the generation Stop closes; cancel/descriptor closure needs one happens-before order.

**Impact.** A shutdown or LLDP reconfiguration can hang the daemon with an RX goroutine parked in the kernel (delaying systemd restart) or leak sockets/goroutines / trip the race detector.

**Fix direction.** Add a lifecycle mutex covering the full Apply/Stop generation transition (cancel, session publication, all wg.Add); build/start one generation only while Stop is excluded; Stop detaches the complete generation, cancels, closes all its sessions, and joins its own WaitGroup; add a raced-Stop -race barrier test.

**Provenance.** codex-review-177 `[A7-b2-F10]`, Medium/Medium.

## #5128 — daemon: removing a managed system login user does not revoke its password/authorized_keys (credentials retained after deprovision) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

Removing a managed `system login user` from config does **not** revoke that
user's host credentials. The account, its password, and its
`authorized_keys` all persist; only the sudo NOPASSWD grant is revoked. A
deprovisioned operator can still SSH in (by password or key) after the config
that created them is removed and committed.

## Current code (origin/master, `812bf30c1`)

- `applySystemLogin` returns immediately when desired users are empty and
  otherwise loops only over **present** users
  (`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:856-861`).
- Password locking runs only inside that present-user loop, via
  `d.reconcileUserPassword(user)` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:922`).
- `authorized_keys` reconciliation runs only when `len(user.SSHKeys) > 0`
  (`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:928`); no path removes the key file when keys
  are cleared or the user is removed.
- The UID-keyed provenance marker (`markProvisioned` /`xpfProvisioned`,
  `pkg/daemon/login_password.go:162-205`) is consumed **only** by
  `reconcileUserPassword` for a still-present user. No sweep enumerates
  `provisionedUsersDir` to lock/`userdel`/disable a user that was wholly
  removed from config. `grep` confirms no `configuredRGs`-style absent-user
  reconcile exists.
- The unconditional follow-up reconciler (`reconcileSudoers`) revokes only the
  sudo grant, not the account/password/keys.

Note the D2 lock path (`login_password.go`) handles a *present* user whose
password *directive* was removed; it does not fire for a *removed user*, because
`reconcileUserPassword` is never called for a user absent from
`cfg.System.Login.Users`.

## Invariant / basis

Declarative removal of a login user must revoke host access for that user
(Junos semantics; the UID-keyed marker was added precisely to "lock THIS exact
account when the directive is removed"). The marker exists but no removal path
consumes it for whole-user removal.

  does **not** add it to `SHA256SUMS` (`scripts/image/bake.py:705-713`).

## #5132 — cli: '| last N' preallocates make([]string, N) from untrusted operand before reading — view-level OOM DoS [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

The `| last N` pipe filter preallocates `make([]string, N)` from the
attacker-controlled operand **before reading any output**, with no upper bound.
`show` is a view-level command, so a read-only user can exhaust daemon memory
with a single `show <anything> | last 2000000000`.

## Current code (origin/master, `812bf30c1`)

- `filterStream`'s `last` case parses any positive `int` from the pipe operand
  and immediately does `ring := make([]string, n)`
  (`pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:132-146`):
  ```go
  n := 10
  if pipeArg != "" {
      if v, err := strconv.Atoi(pipeArg); err == nil && v > 0 { n = v }
  }
  ring := make([]string, n)
  ```
- `extractPipe` forwards the operand with no numeric cap
  (`pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:32-53`).
- `show` (and the pipe family) is `PermView` (`pkg/cli/permissions.go:151-157`).

## Invariant / basis

Allocation must be bounded by actual data, not by an untrusted operand. `N`
string headers (16 B each) are allocated up front regardless of how many lines
the command actually produces, so a tiny command with a huge `N` is an
amplification DoS.

## Failure scenario

A read-only login class runs `show version | last 2000000000`, forcing an
immediate ~32 GB slice-header allocation before a single line is read → OOM /
crash of `xpfd`.

## Fix direction

## Summary

After a live RETH virtual-MAC change (no link cycle), the daemon's **mandatory**
re-apply that starts the deferred AF_XDP workers logs and **discards** its
`ApplyConfig` error, and the userspace manager only advances its snapshot
bookkeeping on success. The result: the workerless `DeferWorkers=true` snapshot
stays published, the commit reports success, and nothing re-arms the recovery —
a silent forwarding outage.

## Current code (origin/master, `812bf30c1`)

- The `rethMACPending && !needLinkCycleRecovery` branch does the deferred-MAC
  re-apply and swallows the error (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:990-997`):
  ```go
  } else if d.dp != nil && rethMACPending && !needLinkCycleRecovery {
      if _, err := d.dp.ApplyConfig(context.Background(), cfg); err != nil {
          slog.Warn("failed to re-apply after deferred MAC", "err", err)
      }
  }
  ```
  The outer apply continues and returns nil.
- The first apply publishes a deferred snapshot with `snap.DeferWorkers = true`
  (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:309-310`), and stores
  `m.lastSnapshot` / `m.publishedSnapshot` / `m.lastSnapshotHash` **only after**
  `requestLocked("apply_snapshot")` succeeds
  (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:323-340`) — an error returns
  before any state advances.
- The status-refresh replay path rebases off `m.lastSnapshot` (the deferred,
  workerless snapshot) and re-publishes it, perpetuating the deferred state
  (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:420-486`). This branch avoids
  `NotifyLinkCycle`, does not arm deferred workers, and never recorded the
  rejected snapshot as desired state.

## Invariant / basis

A failed mandatory reapply that leaves the dataplane in a workerless
(non-forwarding) generation must fail the apply or record generation debt for
retry — not be logged-and-dropped while the commit reports success and the
published snapshot stays workerless.

## #5136 — cli: ISSU prints 'traffic drained' + 'systemctl stop xpfd' immediately after ForceSecondary (async, droppable-event demotion) — can blackhole while still master [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

The ISSU CLI (`request system software in-service-upgrade`) prints "Traffic has
been drained to peer" and instructs the operator to `systemctl stop xpfd`
**immediately** after `ForceSecondary()` returns — but `ForceSecondary` only
mutates cluster-manager state and enqueues best-effort (droppable) events. The
actual dataplane demotion (VRRP resignation, blackhole insertion,
`SetRGActive`) happens later, asynchronously, and can fail. Following the
printed instruction can blackhole traffic while the node is still master.

## Current code (origin/master, `812bf30c1`)

- `handleRequestSystemSoftware` calls `c.cluster.ForceSecondary()` and, on nil
  error, immediately prints "Node is now secondary…", "Traffic has been drained
  to peer.", and "systemctl stop xpfd && …"
  (`pkg/cli/cli_request_system.go:151-186`).
- `ForceSecondary` checks only `m.peerAlive`, sets `Weight=0`/`State=Secondary`
  per RG, calls `sendEvent`, and returns nil
  (`pkg/cluster/failover.go:118-146`).
- `sendEvent` is non-blocking and **drops** the event on a full channel
  (`pkg/cluster/manager.go:371-380`).
- The real demotion (preflight, VRRP resignation, blackhole, `SetRGActive`)
  runs later in the daemon watcher and can fail
  (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:180-301`).

## Invariant / basis

A maintenance command that instructs a destructive `systemctl stop` must not
assert the drain is complete before peer-takeover readiness, VIP transfer, and
generation/session convergence are confirmed. `ForceSecondary` returning nil
proves only that manager state was mutated and an event was *attempted*.

## Failure scenario

Operator runs ISSU; `ForceSecondary` returns nil but its state event is dropped
(full channel) or the async demotion has not yet actuated. The CLI prints
"Traffic has been drained"; the operator runs `systemctl stop xpfd` while the
node is still master for one or more RGs → hard blackhole / ungraceful failover
instead of the intended zero-drop drain.

`xpf-deploy` installs a fetched golden qcow2 by copying its bytes **in place**
over the stable golden path, which is the read-only COW **backing file** for
every per-VM overlay. There is no reference scan, content-addressed/versioned
base, overlay rebase, or in-use refusal, so re-fetching the golden while VMs run
on overlays over the old base corrupts those overlays.

- `_install_libvirt_golden` copies verified bytes directly over the golden path
  (`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:567-580`):
  ```python
  golden = libvirt_golden_path(image)
  shutil.copyfile(srcq, golden)          # or: sudo install -m 0644 -D srcq golden
  ```
- `libvirt_disk` creates each per-VM overlay backed **read-only** by that same
  golden path (`qemu-img create -f qcow2 -b <golden> -F qcow2 <overlay>`) and
  documents the golden as an immutable shared backing store that "must NEVER be
  attached writable" (`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py:583-614`).
- No reference scan / versioned base / overlay rebase / replacement refusal
  exists in the install path.

## Invariant / basis

A qcow2 backing file referenced by live overlays is immutable by contract:
overlays store only copy-on-write deltas against fixed backing bytes. Replacing
the backing bytes underneath existing overlays invalidates every overlay's CoW
assumptions (corruption / unbootable guests on the next backing read or restart).

## Failure scenario

Two HA member VMs run on per-VM overlays backed by `xpf-<image>.qcow2`. An
operator re-runs a fetch/deploy that installs a new golden of the same name;
`_install_libvirt_golden` overwrites the backing bytes in place. On the next
restart or backing read, both HA members' overlays reference altered backing
content → both members corrupted/unbootable at once.

## #5138 — upgrade: ResetFailover falls back to RG {0,1,2} on status-enum failure and RejoinAndConfirm ignores per-RG state — rolling upgrade blackholes RG 3+ [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Summary

During a rolling kernel upgrade, `ResetFailover` (which must undo the prior
all-RG `ForceSecondary` demotion) enumerates RGs from status output and falls
back to a hardcoded `{0,1,2}` on any status error or parse miss. Configs with
RG ≥ 3 then keep those RGs **manually drained**, yet `RejoinAndConfirm` checks
only peer heartbeat/sync — so the orchestrator declares rejoin complete and
proceeds to drain the peer, blackholing RG 3+.

## Current code (origin/master, `812bf30c1`)

- `ResetFailover` iterates `g.configuredRGs()` and issues
  `cluster-failover-reset:<rg>` per RG (`pkg/upgrade/cluster_cli.go:504-520`).
- `configuredRGs` parses RG IDs from `statusText()` but **falls back to
  `{0,1,2}`** on a status error or when `parseRGIDs` returns empty
  (`pkg/upgrade/cluster_cli.go:523-531`). The config boundary supports higher
  RG IDs; the status parser's tests cover only 0–2.
- `RejoinAndConfirm` calls `ResetFailover` then loops only on `PeerAlive()` and
  `SyncEstablished()` — no per-RG local eligibility / applied-ownership check
  for every configured RG (`pkg/upgrade/kernel_drain.go:115-160`).

## Invariant / basis

The "never both down" rejoin gate must confirm this node has actually resumed
eligibility for **every configured RG** before the orchestrator touches the
peer. A status-enumeration failure must not silently narrow the reset set to
`{0,1,2}` while the confirm step ignores RG 3+.

## Failure scenario

A cluster is configured with RG 0,1,2,3. After cutover, a transient status RPC
failure makes `configuredRGs` fall back to `{0,1,2}`; `ResetFailover` issues
resets only for 0–2, so RG 3 stays demoted/drained. `RejoinAndConfirm` sees
peer alive + sync established and returns success. The orchestrator declares
rejoin complete and drains the peer for its own upgrade → RG 3 has no master on
either node → blackhole for RG-3 services.

## Fix direction

Fail closed instead of falling back to `{0,1,2}` when RG enumeration fails

**Defect**

Post-decap reads use raw_frame.get(meta.l4_offset) with the inner-relative offset — reading wrong outer bytes for a GRE-decapped inner ICMP packet. **Location (current origin/master):** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/mod.rs:834-849 (trim_l3_payload) → checksum.rs recompute; consumed by wg.rs / gre trim

**Invariant / basis:** L4 checksum must cover only bytes within IPv4 total_len / IPv6 40+payload_len; Ethernet padding must be excluded (invariant stated at frame/mod.rs).

**Fix direction:** Make the structurally-valid IP-declared length authoritative in trim_l3_payload (metadata only as fallback), and/or have recompute_l4_checksum_ipv4/ipv6 derive an explicit declared upper-layer end.

## #5173 — userspace-xdp: shim redirects packets on HW RX queues above the planner minimum to a socket bound to the wrong queue (global-min modulo mis-steer) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-21)

**Defect**

select_userspace_queue returns rx_queue_index % queue_count; the raw-queue fallback only fires when the modulo-selected binding is absent — but the planner (queue_count = min(rx queues)) creates a binding for every queue < queue_count on every interface, so the modulo target always exists and the fallback never triggers. RSS restriction is best-effort/mlx5-only and skipped for workers==1 / workers>=queues. A packet on a HW queue >= queue_count is XDP_REDIRECTed to an XSK bound to a different queue; kernel xsk_rcv_check drops it. Distinct from #4894 (queue IDs>=16 aliasing binding slots).

**Location (current origin/master):** userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1481 (fallback :445-450); planner userspace-dp/src/server/helpers.rs:1154

**Invariant / basis:** AF_XDP ownership invariant (netdev, actual RX queue) == socket binding; the kernel drops a redirect to a socket bound to a different queue than the packet's RX queue.

**Fix direction:** Never change the queue coordinate before XSK redirect — bind/publish the actual per-interface queues and key lookup by full (ifindex, rx_queue_index), or make exact RSS restriction to the published queue set a mandatory proven precondition that keeps control disabled on failure.

## #5177 — userspace-dp NAT64: reverse ICMP-error translation leaves the translated PAT port/ICMP-id in the embedded quote instead of the original client value [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

translate_embedded_v4_to_v6 restores the embedded IPv6 addresses but copies the quoted L4 bytes verbatim — only an ICMP type/code remap, no TCP/UDP source-port or ICMP-id rewrite. After #4381 stateful PAT the embedded source port is the translated pool port (e.g. 40000), not the original client port (12345), so the inside host cannot correlate the error to its socket. Distinct from #2371 (embedded checksum) and #4381 (outer port alloc).

**Location (current origin/master):** userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs:2448-2503 (translate_embedded_v4_to_v6; symmetric v6→v4 twin ~1711-1718)

**Invariant / basis:** RFC 6146 — for an ICMP error to the inside host the embedded invoking tuple must equal the tuple that host emitted, including pre-PAT source port / query identifier.

**Fix direction:** Pass the forward/reverse NatDecision (original/translated L4 values) into embedded translation and rewrite the quoted source port / ICMP-id back to the original client value, then recompute the outer ICMP checksum.

**Fix direction:** Iterate FindChildren per repeatable named container / screen family and merge all subtrees (SetPath merge semantics), or reject ambiguous duplicate whole-object definitions before compile; merge repeated same-name ids-option instead of overwriting.
