## #5189 — userspace-dp warmed-path allocation/contention LOW cohort (dispatch budget, backup-drain alloc, route-table intern, ECMP spill, release String, event keepalive cap) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

Low-severity hot-path allocation / bounded-work residuals in the AF_XDP userspace dataplane. Each is genuine on current origin/master and violates the warmed-path zero-allocation / bounded-work discipline.

Each item below was independently re-verified against current origin/master. Cohorted per repo convention for low-severity findings sharing a subsystem.

### A1-b4-F6 — worker command dispatch has no service budget; mem::take discards VecDeque capacity
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/mod.rs:581,604
- **Defect:** apply_worker_commands does core::mem::take on the shared pending deque (leaving a zero-cap VecDeque producers must regrow), then drains the whole captured batch in one loop with no per-loop command/time budget or yield to RX/TX; a large HA-sync/reconfig burst can stall packet forwarding.
- **Fix:** Apply a fixed command/time budget per loop (preserve FIFO/ordering groups); recycle a worker-owned scratch deque instead of leaking the old allocation.

### A1-b6-F4 — non-CoS backup drain loses the persistent pending_tx_local allocation on success + allocates a transient retry deque per batch
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/drain/mod.rs:582 + tx/drain/phase_backup.rs:157,204
- **Defect:** take_pending_tx_requests does mem::take (zero-cap deque left in the worker); phase_backup allocates a fresh retry=VecDeque::new(); on full success restore is skipped and both deques are dropped, re-allocated on the next successful non-CoS backup batch. Sibling of #4973 but a distinct path/function.
- **Fix:** Keep a persistent worker-owned retry deque and always return the emptied pending allocation to pending_tx_local on success.

### A1-b7-F5 — canonical_route_table + next-table visited chain heap-allocate on every new-flow VRF/PBR/route-leak FIB resolution
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/mod.rs:57-74, 2110, 2318
- **Defect:** #4674 fixed only the default-table case; canonical_route_table still returns Cow<'static,str> and same-family/named-VRF/opposite-family rewrites take Cow::Owned(format!/to_string), and next-table recursion clones each table via visited.push(table.to_string()) — all on the packet-driven session-miss FIB path.
- **Fix:** Intern canonical route tables into a compact TableId at snapshot build and carry IDs through PBR/next-table recursion with a fixed [TableId; MAX_NEXT_TABLE_DEPTH] visited stack.

### A1-b7-F6 — select_route_next_hop SmallVec<[&T;8]> spills to heap for ECMP fanout >=9 on every new-flow lookup
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/mod.rs:2782
- **Defect:** select_route_next_hop collects live refs into SmallVec<[&'a T; 8]>; route.next_hops is an unbounded Vec with no snapshot/type-enforced max, so a route with >=9 live members spills to heap on every new-flow lookup (v4 and v6 share the helper).
- **Fix:** Validate/document an ECMP max of 8, or size fixed storage to the supported maximum for the one-pass liveness snapshot.

### A1-b8-F5 — release-build workers allocate a String + issue statistics_v2/SO_ERROR syscalls every ~1s report tick with debug-log disabled
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/loop_body/mod.rs:975-1101
- **Defect:** The debug-report tick block is not feature-gated: String::new(), b.xsk.device.statistics_v2(), and getsockopt(SO_ERROR) all run in release builds every ~1s per worker while only the emit is #[cfg(feature="debug-log")]. Distinct from #4971 (TX retry String path).
- **Fix:** Gate summary formatting, statistics_v2, SO_ERROR, and frame-leak text under #[cfg(feature="debug-log")]; publish fixed scalar atomics for release health.

### A1-b10-F4 — event-stream idle keepalive append bypasses the 16 MiB WRITE_BACKLOG_MAX_BYTES cap
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/event_stream/mod.rs:1215-1220
- **Defect:** The idle keepalive write_buf.extend_from_slice(&ka) has no WRITE_BACKLOG_MAX_BYTES guard; that 16 MiB cap is enforced only in the producer drain loop. A live-but-non-reading local consumer stalls the drain at the cap while keepalives keep appending. NOT a dup of #4974 (O(n^2) drain cost).
- **Fix:** Gate the keepalive append on write_buf.len() < WRITE_BACKLOG_MAX_BYTES (pending data already supplies liveness).

### A1-b1-F5 — flowless malformed-drop screen events serialize protocol 0 despite the authoritative meta.protocol
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/event_emit.rs:436 (constructor), :293 (serialize)
- **Defect:** screen_parse_error_info_flowless hard-codes protocol:0; emit_screen_drop_event serializes it. The authoritative meta.protocol is available at the caller but not threaded in, so all flowless malformed-packet screen drops report protocol 0.
- **Fix:** Pass UserspaceDpMeta (or explicit protocol/pkt_len) into screen_parse_error_info_flowless and populate the real fields.

### A1-b1-F6 — flow-cache hit/LRU/active-byte accounting commits before the caller's dynamic neighbor/HA validation (rejected candidates counted as hits)
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/flow_cache.rs:905-919 + poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs:111
- **Defect:** lookup_with_observed_bytes commits hits+=1, promote_lru, last_used_epoch, observed_bytes as soon as key/generation/epoch/lease pass, then returns Some(entry); the caller afterward may FallThrough on neighbor_mac_stale/invalid decision. Dynamically-rejected candidates are still counted as served hits + active bytes (amplified by A1-b1-F4 map-wide epoch).
- **Fix:** Return a candidate index without accounting, validate (neighbor/HA), then commit the hit only on Consumed; record rejected candidates as misses/evictions.

### A1-b1-F7 — rx_oversized telemetry hard-codes a 1514-byte ceiling, misflagging valid jumbo/VLAN-tagged frames
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/rx_telemetry.rs:107
- **Defect:** rx_telemetry does `if desc.len > 1514 { rx_oversized += 1 }` plus a debug breadcrumb, a fixed constant with no per-interface MTU/jumbo/VLAN awareness. Valid jumbo or in-band-VLAN-tagged 1500-byte frames inflate an anomaly counter.
- **Fix:** Thread a precomputed per-binding L2 frame limit into telemetry, or rename/document the counter as strictly rx_over_1514.

### A1-b8-F6 — zero_unbound_slot leaves stale shared-UMEM metadata + martian_dropped/ipv6_ext_header_dropped counters on unbound slots
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/refresh_bindings.rs:64-67,79-80 (copy) vs 266-300 (reset)
- **Defect:** The copy block copies shared_umem_mode/group/socket_role/disabled_reason and martian_dropped/ipv6_ext_header_dropped, but zero_unbound_slot resets neither the four shared_umem strings nor the two drop counters (recently added in b1492e26b), so unbound slots report stale shared-UMEM metadata + drop counts.
- **Fix:** Clear the shared_umem_* fields and reset both drop counters in zero_unbound_slot (drive copy/reset from one field list).

### A1-b12-F2 — AF_XDP bind reports success after silently discarding failed busy-poll setsockopt calls
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/bind.rs:605 (call site :549)
- **Defect:** set_busy_poll_opts issues SO_BUSY_POLL / SO_PREFER_BUSY_POLL / SO_BUSY_POLL_BUDGET each discarded with `let _ =`, returns (), and the caller logs bind OK regardless. Kernel rejection (support/privilege/sysctl) is silent; the worker runs with different NAPI/poll semantics than requested.
- **Fix:** Check each setsockopt return and either propagate a bind error or record a per-socket busy-poll-degraded status.

### A1-b12-F3 — three benches advertised as performance merge gates never emit a failing verdict (always exit 0)
- **Location:** userspace-dp/benches/session_table.rs:455, snat_allocator.rs:623, tx_kick_latency.rs:136
- **Defect:** session_table ('Pass criterion'), tx_kick_latency ('Gate: p99 <= 60 ns'), and snat_allocator ('the REQUIRED merge gate') contain no process::exit/assert!/panic! verdict — a severe regression still exits 0. The sibling prefix_set_lookup.rs demonstrates the intended std::process::exit(1) gate. False-PASS gate (material as LOW).
- **Fix:** Add explicit threshold comparisons with nonzero exit (mirror prefix_set_lookup.rs), or relabel the targets as exploratory and drop the merge-gate claims.

## #5191 — userspace-dp segmentation/ICMP + WireGuard protocol-fidelity LOW cohort (segment ID/CWR/URG cloning, unrepaired ICMP checksum, multi-peer keepalive roaming, noncanonical WG type words) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

Low-severity protocol-fidelity residuals in the AF_XDP userspace dataplane's TCP segmentation, ICMP repair, and WireGuard framing.

Each item below was independently re-verified against current origin/master. Cohorted per repo convention for low-severity findings sharing a subsystem.

### A1-b2-F6 — TCP segmentation clones IPv4 Identification and TCP CWR/URG/urgent-pointer into every segment
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/tcp_segmentation.rs:177-192 (+ tx twin)
- **Defect:** Segmentation clones the original IP+TCP headers verbatim into every output and only rewrites seq + clears PSH on non-last; IPv4 ID, CWR, URG flag and urgent pointer are copied unchanged. Admission rejects only SYN/FIN/RST, so ACK+CWR/URG and DF-clear datagrams reach this path. Distinct from #4384.
- **Fix:** Assign a distinct per-output IPv4 ID when DF is clear (or decline software segmentation for non-atomic IPv4); keep CWR on the first segment; recompute/clear the urgent pointer; mirror in the prepared-TX twin.

### A1-b2-F7 — IPv4 ICMP metadata repair mutates identifier/control bytes for all ICMP types without recomputing the ICMP checksum
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/mod.rs:1409-1418 (restore_l4_tuple_from_meta) + recompute_l4_checksum_ipv4 (checksum.rs, no ICMP arm)
- **Defect:** restore_l4_tuple_from_meta overwrites ICMP bytes rel_l4+4..+6 for any ICMP/ICMPv6 with no query-type gate and returns repaired=true; recompute_l4_checksum_ipv4 has only TCP/UDP arms, so the ICMP checksum is never fixed (invalid for echo/query id changes; corrupts MTU/pointer/gateway bytes for error types). #3290 gated a different fallback.
- **Fix:** Gate the ident restore to ICMP query types (echo/timestamp) as NAT does, and recompute the ICMP/ICMPv6 checksum after the byte change.

### A1-b9-F4 — authenticated zero-length keepalive on a multi-peer interface cannot update the roaming peer's endpoint (identity dropped in try_decap)
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/engine.rs:1577-1580 (+ coordinator/wg_control.rs:1489-1497)
- **Defect:** A zero-length authenticated keepalive returns Err(MalformedInner) discarding the known session.peer_pubkey; wg_control recovers identity only via single_peer_pubkey() and returns Unauthenticated for multi-peer. Source comments flag this as the retained '#1865 plan §9 latent gap.' Server-initiated traffic to a NAT-rebound multi-peer stays blackholed until the peer sends non-empty data.
- **Fix:** Return a typed outcome (DecapResult::Keepalive { peer_pubkey }) carrying the known 32-byte identity; the coordinator learns that peer's endpoint and skips TUN write.

### A1-b9-F5 — transport-data and CookieReply parsers accept noncanonical 32-bit type words (low-byte-only check) — parser differential vs kernel/wireguard-go
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/framing.rs:83 + wg/cookie.rs:650
- **Defect:** parse_data_header checks only buf[0] != WG_TYPE_DATA (accepts nonzero reserved bytes), and decrypt_cookie_reply checks only reply[0] != WG_TYPE_COOKIE, while the handshake parser uses full-word is_canonical_type. Kernel/wireguard-go compare the full __le32 type; the differential is usable for evasion/ambiguity.
- **Fix:** Enforce u32::from_le_bytes(buf[0..4]) == WG_TYPE_* in data-header parse and CookieReply decrypt after the length guard.

## #5192 — userspace-dp memory-safety LOW cohort (UMEM drop-order latent UAF, metadata store alignment UB) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

Low-severity but memory-safety-relevant residuals in the AF_XDP userspace dataplane and XDP shim. Both are currently tolerated only by platform/library specifics; each violates an unsafe contract the codebase elsewhere already recognizes.

Each item below was independently re-verified against current origin/master. Cohorted per repo convention for low-severity findings sharing a subsystem.

### A1-b6-F6 — WorkerUmemInner drops MmapArea (munmap) before Umem (xsk_umem__delete) — violates the area-outlives-Umem unsafe contract (latent UAF)
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/umem/mod.rs:34-38
- **Defect:** WorkerUmemInner declares `area: MmapArea` before `umem: Umem`; Rust drops fields in declaration order, so MmapArea::drop (munmap) runs before Umem::drop (xsk_umem__delete), violating the xsk_ffi.rs Umem::new safety contract that area must outlive the Umem. A current UAF is refuted only because libxdp 1.6.0 delete does not read the area.
- **Fix:** Declare umem before area so Umem drops first; add a drop-order comment/test seam.

### A1-b11-F3 — XDP shim metadata store `*meta_ptr = UserspaceDpMeta{..}` assumes 8-byte alignment that generic/copy XDP does not guarantee (latent UB)
- **Location:** userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:676-682
- **Defect:** The shim writes metadata as an aligned typed store; the type gains 8-byte alignment from its config_generation:u64 field. The direct consumer (frame/inspect.rs) already uses ptr::read_unaligned with a 'would be UB on strict-alignment archs' comment — i.e. the boundary is recognized unaligned — but the writer does not. On generic/copy XDP (and strict-alignment archs, NET_IP_ALIGN=2) data_meta need not be 8-aligned, making the typed store Rust-level UB.
- **Fix:** Serialize the metadata via ptr::write_unaligned / explicit alignment-1 field stores; add a compile-time alignment assertion + a deliberately-misaligned fixture.

## #5193 — userspace-dp CoS/fairness + snapshot-integrity LOW cohort (fairness partial-cardinality false-PASS, residual-budget linearizability, duplicate tunnel endpoint IDs, unbounded CoS DSCP rewrite) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

Low-severity fairness-evidence, concurrency-linearizability, and snapshot-integrity fail-closed residuals in the AF_XDP userspace dataplane.

Each item below was independently re-verified against current origin/master. Cohorted per repo convention for low-severity findings sharing a subsystem.

### A1-b5-F3 — fairness-eval partial-cardinality stream mean divides by present-count not window-count — a 1-of-N stream scored full-rate (false PASS on the CoS merge gate)
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/windowing.rs:113-137
- **Defect:** Recent commit 25a53f6d3 (V-9) only zero-fills FULLY-absent streams and rejects globally-truncated runs; it does NOT address partial cardinality. Per-stream mean is sum/v.len(), so a stream present in 1 of 60 accepted intervals is scored at full rate (divides by 1) and yields CoV ~0 for a near-total-outage flow.
- **Fix:** Build each accepted interval against the seeded connected-socket set and zero-fill/fail on missing sockets per an explicit density contract; add a one-of-60 false-PASS regression.

### A1-b5-F4 — residual-surplus-budget reset vs refill is not linearizable — split tokens/last_refill_ns stores can resurrect a stale burst
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/types/shared_cos_lease/backlog.rs:118 + 188-208
- **Defect:** reset_residual_surplus_budget publishes two independent stores (tokens=0 then last_refill_ns). refill claims the timestamp CAS then, in a separate inner loop, adds tokens derived from the pre-reset epoch. A refill interleaved with a reset can leave non-zero tokens after a completed reset.
- **Fix:** Add a generation/seqlock so refill validates the same generation before and after its token CAS and retries if reset intervened.

### A1-b7-F1 — populate_tunnel_endpoints accepts duplicate tunnel endpoint IDs, aliasing by_ifindex to one endpoint
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/tunnels.rs:76-118
- **Defect:** populate_tunnel_endpoints inserts each endpoint.id into tunnel_endpoints and each ifindex into tunnel_endpoint_by_ifindex with no duplicate-ID preflight; a dup-ID pair leaves both maps inconsistent (last row wins the ID, both ifindexes alias it). Go producer usedIDs dedup lowers reachability but does not remove this second boundary.
- **Fix:** Preflight all nonzero endpoint IDs (and logical ifindexes) before mutating state; return a typed SnapshotIntegrityError on a duplicate (mirror the same function's #2410 TTL gate).

### A1-b7-F7 — CoS DSCP rewrite-rule value >63 is accepted then masked to a different code point on TX (no fail-closed bound, unlike the classifier builders)
- **Location:** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/cos.rs:444-446, 458-460
- **Defect:** The cos.rs classifier builders fail-closed on out-of-range DSCP (CosDscpCodePointOutOfRange), but the rewrite-rule ingest stores entry.dscp_value via bare .or_insert with no bound; the transmit helper masks dscp & 0x3f (frame/mod.rs:168), so 110 silently becomes DSCP 46 (wrong PHB). The strict Go compiler rejects it but a tolerant/mixed-version snapshot bypasses it.
- **Fix:** Validate every CoSDSCPRewriteRuleEntrySnapshot.dscp_value <= 63 before insertion, returning a typed integrity error naming rule/class/value.

## #5194 — pkg/config validation LOW cohort (port-0 wildcard sentinel, apply-groups depth budget, IPv4 range count wrap, JSON repeated-leaf overwrite, unknown CoS code point dropped, VRF-overlap quadratic, malformed WG AllowedIPs, flat parser semicolon truncation) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

Low-severity Go config-compiler validation residuals. Each admits or silently drops config that should be rejected, warned, or preserved.

Each item below was independently re-verified against current origin/master. Cohorted per repo convention for low-severity findings sharing a subsystem.

### A3-b1-F2 — bare destination/source-port `0` (and `0-0`) parses to the (0,0) unconstrained-wildcard sentinel — tolerant-load over-match
- **Location:** pkg/appid/catalog.go:427-448 (parsePortRange) consumed at :174
- **Defect:** The protocol sub-claims are fixed (#4887/#4008), but parsePortRange still returns (0,0) for a bare '0'/'0-0' spec — the same pair the Rust matcher reserves for 'no constraint'. A tolerantly-loaded destination-port 0 app is emittable and over-matches every port of its protocol.
- **Fix:** Treat a literal 0/0-0 port as unemittable (only empty encodes unconstrained; normalize 0-N to 1-N) and mirror in compileApplications.

### A3-b2-F1 — apply-groups expansion has a cycle guard but no depth/work budget — a deep acyclic group chain can exhaust stack on commit/HA-sync
- **Location:** pkg/config/ast_groups.go:176 (guard :219-222, recursion :250)
- **Defect:** expandGroupsRecursive has ONLY a `seen` cycle guard — no semantic depth or total-work budget. Parser brace-depth cap (#4148) and memoization (#4474) bound syntax nesting and DAG fan-out, not a shallow-syntax acyclic chain g1->g2->...->gN.
- **Fix:** Thread an explicit depth + total-expanded-node budget through expansion and reject cleanly before recursion exceeds it (or expand iteratively).

### A3-b2-F9 — full-domain IPv4 address range wraps inclusive count to zero (uint32) — oversized range commits as an empty pool instead of erroring
- **Location:** pkg/config/compiler_nat.go:1217 (expandAddressRange)
- **Defect:** count := highN-lowN+1 in uint32; for 0.0.0.0 to 255.255.255.255, highN-lowN=0xFFFFFFFF, +1 wraps to 0; the >256 gate passes and the generation loop runs zero times, returning an empty pool with nil error instead of the promised size error.
- **Fix:** Compute count := uint64(highN)-uint64(lowN)+1 and compare before allocation; add full-domain/256/257 boundary tests.

### A3-b2-F11 — FormatJSON (nodesToJSON) silently overwrites repeated leaf statements — display JSON drops all but the last (e.g. multiple name-server)
- **Location:** pkg/config/ast_format.go:560-567
- **Defect:** nodesToJSON projects into a single-value map[string]interface{}; every leaf writes result[n.Keys[0]], so repeated leaves like two name-server statements overwrite last-wins. Named-instance containers merge, but plain repeated leaves silently lose data (Junos display json uses arrays).
- **Fix:** Promote repeated keys to ordered arrays (schema-aware for list leaves/named instances); add round-trip cardinality tests.

### A3-b2-F12 — unknown symbolic DSCP/PCP code-point tokens silently dropped at commit (no error/warning) — inconsistent with numeric out-of-range which now warns
- **Location:** pkg/config/compiler_class_of_service.go:1242 (PCP variant :1176)
- **Defect:** expandCoSCodePointToken returns nil,nil for an unknown non-numeric, non-alias token — silent drop in strict AND lenient. Recent commit 6201c4bae hardened the NUMERIC out-of-range path to strict-reject/lenient-warn, leaving the symbolic-typo path completely silent. Possible fold into #4228.
- **Fix:** Return/persist unknown symbolic tokens and reject strict / warn-and-drop lenient (mirror the numeric path).

### A3-b3-F5 — validateVRFOverlap runs an uncapped quadratic prefix-pair scan (no op budget, no warning cap) on every compile
- **Location:** pkg/config/compiler_validate_vrf_overlap.go:163-176
- **Defect:** A nested for a in riPrefixes[riA] { for b in riPrefixes[riB] { a.Overlaps(b) } } over every unordered RI pair with no operation budget, cancellation, prefix index, or warning cap. Runs on every strict and tolerant compile (incl. HA peer-sync). Cold advisory-only path, hence LOW, but genuinely unbounded.
- **Fix:** Use a family-separated prefix trie/interval sweep; add a deterministic warning cap + a cancellation/operation budget.

### A3-b3-F6 — malformed WireGuard AllowedIPs commit successfully then silently vanish during Rust hydration (partial apply)
- **Location:** pkg/config/compiler_validate_wireguard.go:213-217; userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/tunnels.rs:237-243
- **Defect:** canonicalAllowedIPPrefix keys an unparseable CIDR verbatim and defers validation to 'the Rust IpNet boundary'; Rust hydration cidr.parse::<ipnet::IpNet>() with Err(_) => continue silently drops the malformed entry while keeping the peer. An all-malformed list yields an empty AllowedIPs set. Distinct from closed #2445.
- **Fix:** Parse every AllowedIP with net/netip.ParsePrefix in strict validation and reject malformed prefixes; on tolerant load warn explicitly.

### A3-b3-F7 — flat-command ParseSetVerb accepts and silently discards all tokens after the first semicolon (silent truncation)

## #5195 — pkg/config secret-handling LOW cohort (synthetic proposal-set name collision -> crypto downgrade, VRRP track validator echoes auth secret) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

Low-severity but security-relevant Go config-compiler residuals touching crypto namespace ownership and secret disclosure in diagnostics.

Each item below was independently re-verified against current origin/master. Cohorted per repo convention for low-severity findings sharing a subsystem.

### A3-b2-F7 — synthetic proposal-set proposal name (__proposal-set/...) can collide with and silently overwrite an operator-authored IKE/IPsec proposal (crypto downgrade)
- **Location:** pkg/config/compiler_ipsec_proposalset.go:146 (phase-1), :177 (phase-2)
- **Defect:** Both phases unconditionally do IKEProposals[name]=.. / Proposals[name]=.. with the synthetic __proposal-set/%s/%s/%d name; the lexer permits / _ . in bare identifiers, so an operator-authored proposal with that exact name is representable, and no reserved-prefix rejection or map-occupancy check exists before overwrite.
- **Fix:** Reserve+reject the synthetic prefix for authored proposal names (or keep generated proposals in a separate namespace); at minimum detect map occupancy before overwrite.

### A3-b2-F10 — VRRP track-interface shape validator echoes a packed authentication-key secret into commit errors/warnings (builds path from n.Keys, not vrrpGroupIDKeys)
- **Location:** pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:934 (feeds checkVRRPGroupTrackShape messages at :1064/:1070)
- **Defect:** validateVRRPTrackInterfaceAST builds nodePath from the FULL node keys and passes it to duplicate-track error/warning interpolation. In the Keys-packed spelling `vrrp-group 1 authentication-key SECRET track-interface X track-interface Y`, the secret is in n.Keys and gets echoed to commit error / lenient warning / logs. The later auth validator deliberately uses vrrpGroupIDKeys(n) to avoid exactly this.
- **Fix:** Build the track validator's node path with vrrpGroupIDKeys(n) before any message; add strict+lenient tests asserting a sentinel secret never appears.

## #5197 — configstore durable-delete LOW cohort (factory-reset non-durable key-first ordering, DeleteRescueConfig no parent fsync) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

Low-severity but security-relevant configstore durability residuals: two delete/erase paths report success without the fsync barrier their creation counterparts use.

Each item below was independently re-verified against current origin/master. Cohorted per repo convention for low-severity findings sharing a subsystem.

### A4-b1-F5 — factory reset key-first erasure is not durably ordered and a final directory-fsync failure is reported as a clean zeroize
- **Location:** pkg/configstore/factory_reset.go:56-86 (mirrored pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_zeroize.go zeroizeConfigDir)
- **Defect:** factory_reset does os.Remove(master.key) then RemoveAll(dbDir) with NO fsync between them (key-first ordering not durably enforced), and the final d.Sync()/d.Close() errors are discarded while return firstErr reports success. The documented key-first cryptographic-erasure guarantee ('a crash can never leave ciphertext with its key') is not enforced.
- **Fix:** Add a durable-remove primitive: fsync .configdb after the master.key unlink before recursive removal, fsync configDir after all removals, and propagate open/sync/close errors.

### A4-b1-F10 — DeleteRescueConfig reports success without fsyncing the parent dir — a deleted secret-bearing rescue.conf can survive power loss
- **Location:** pkg/configstore/store_persist.go:563
- **Defect:** DeleteRescueConfig unlinks with plain os.Remove and returns success with no parent SyncDir, while SaveRescueConfig uses fsatomic.WriteFileDurable — asymmetric durability. DB.DeleteConfirm in the same package already demonstrates the unlink+parent-fsync pattern (#4864 test). A power loss before the directory entry commits can replay rescue.conf.
- **Fix:** Use a durable-remove helper that unlinks, fsyncs the parent, and returns sync errors; add an injected SyncDir assertion analogous to confirm_delete_fsync_4864_test.go.

## #5203 — dhcpserver: nextSubnetID collision-probe is per-node position-dependent — a hash collision + asymmetric mastering can reintroduce #5041 for the colliding pair [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

The #5041 fix (PR #5201) made the Kea `subnet-id` a pure FNV-1a hash of the CIDR
(`stableSubnetID`, `pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go`), so the same subnet gets the
same id on both HA nodes. On a genuine hash COLLISION between two CIDRs,
`nextSubnetID` (dhcpserver.go ~872) probes for the next free id — but the probe
step is a function of **which other subnets are in THIS node's master-filtered
subset**, which can differ between the two nodes under asymmetric mastering. So
under a real FNV-1a collision + asymmetric RG mastering, the two nodes could
assign the colliding pair DIFFERENT ids — reintroducing the original #5041
cross-node misbind for that pair.

## Impact: VERY LOW (astronomically rare)

Collision probability is ~k²/2^33 for k subnets — effectively never in practice.
The #5201 review (rev5201) confirmed the fix is correct for the non-colliding
case (which is all realistic deployments) and flagged this only as a
completeness residual, non-blocking.

## Fix

Make the collision-probe deterministic INDEPENDENT of each node's subnet set:
derive the probe step from the CIDR itself (e.g. a salted re-hash of the CIDR)
rather than the position in the rendered/filtered set, so a colliding pair
resolves to the same id on both nodes regardless of mastering. Add a test with a

## #5212 — userspace-dp/HA: RT_FLOW session id is node-local — a peer-synced session gets a fresh id on import; make it identical across HA nodes via a session-sync wire field [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

## Summary

PR #5211 (#4915) assigns a node-unique u64 session id in the dataplane and
carries it on the RT_FLOW wire so SESSION_CREATE/CLOSE correlate and a reused
5-tuple is disambiguated. The id is **node-local**: `alloc_session_id()` uses
this node's `worker_id` in the high bits + a per-worker counter, so a session
synced from the HA peer gets a FRESH node-local id on import (it is not the same
id the peer's RT_FLOW emitted).

## Gap

For cross-node log/event correlation (e.g. an operator following one session's
CREATE on the primary and CLOSE on the peer after a failover, or a collector
merging both nodes' RT_FLOW streams), the id should be IDENTICAL on both HA
nodes for the same session. That requires carrying the assigning node's session
id on the **session-sync wire** so the importing node adopts it rather than
minting a new local one.

## Fix direction

Add the origin session id as an additive field on the session-sync wire
(mirroring the #5211 both-sides length discipline), and on import adopt the
peer's id instead of calling `alloc_session_id()`. Handle the id-collision case
(two nodes both originating) via the worker_id namespace already in the scheme.
Deferred from #5211 (analogous to the #3395 P2 deferral).

## Provenance

Documented deferral from PR #5211 (#4915 RT_FLOW stable session id).

Populate `publish_conntrack` (userspace-dp) with the same `SessionEntry.session_id`
that #5211 assigns, and have `cli_show_flow.go` render that real id instead of
the iteration-index fallback — so both surfaces agree. Additive to the existing
publish_conntrack payload; verify the Go decode/render reads the real id.

## #5225 — dataplane/userspace: mixed unresolved positive+except refs compose to match-all on an accept term (tolerant-path admit-all) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary

Follow-up from PR #5223 (#5097). #5223 fixed the sole-unresolved-`except`
fail-open. Hostile review surfaced a distinct, narrower residual on the same
tolerant/peer-sync lowering path:

A firewall term with BOTH an unresolved **positive** prefix-list ref AND an
unresolved **except** ref, no resolved positive ref, and an empty/match-any
literal → `hasPositiveRef` stays false (it is set only for *resolved* positive
refs), so the #4338 compose gate (`hasExcept && !hasPositiveRef &&
addrsAllMatchAny(positive)`) fires and lowers to match-ALL `(nil, true, true)`.

- For a `discard`/`reject` action this is an improvement (fail-closed).
- For an **`accept`** action it widens match-nothing → **admit-ALL** — a
  fail-open (the term admits every packet instead of the intended empty set).

## Reachability / severity

Narrow: reachable ONLY on the tolerant/peer-sync/persisted-invalid load path.
Strict commit rejects it twice — undefined prefix-lists
(`validateFirewallPrefixListReferencesStrict`) and mixed positive/except
(#3359). A normally-committed config never hits it. It is also a pre-existing
latent quirk (the same shape already existed for resolved-except +
unresolved-positive), not introduced by #5223. Low/Medium.

## Fix direction

Gate the #4338 match-any compose on "no positive ref present AT ALL" — i.e.
`hasPositiveRef` (or an equivalent flag) must also account for an UNRESOLVED
positive ref, so a term that had a positive ref (even unresolved) does not
compose to match-all. Add a fail-on-revert test for the `accept` + mixed
unresolved refs shape.

## Provenance

Hostile review of PR #5223 (#5097), finding 3 (residual), pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go #4338 compose gate (~filters.go:400-421 / 514-516).

## #5228 — config: duplicate hierarchical application/application-set blocks silently last-writer-wins (extend #5180 dup-block reject to applications) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

Follow-up from PR #5226 (#5181). Hostile review surfaced that a duplicate
same-name **`application-set`** (and likely `application`) HIERARCHICAL block
silently OVERWRITES the earlier definition (last-writer-wins) — the earlier
block's members vanish. This is the same fail-open config data-loss class that
#5180 fixed for `groups` / `interfaces` / `security screen ids-option`, but the
`applications { application-set <name> { … } }` container was NOT in #5180's
`pkg/config/dup_named_blocks.go` reject scope.

Under flat `set`, `tree.SetPath` MERGES repeated statements onto one node; the
hierarchical shape produces two sibling nodes and the compiler keeps only the
last (`namedInstances` does not merge-by-name like the address-book #4706 path).
A dropped application-set definition can silently narrow a policy's
`match application` set → deny under-match (security) or an unexpected permit.

## Location

pkg/config/compiler_applications.go (application-set / application named-block
compilation; `namedInstances` overwrite). The dual-AST divergence is the same
shape #5180 addressed.

## Fix direction

Extend the #5180 duplicate-named-block gate (`pkg/config/dup_named_blocks.go`
`validateDuplicateNamedBlockAST`) to also cover `applications { application-set
<name> }` and `applications { application <name> }` — REJECT a duplicate
hierarchical named block at strict commit (lenient-warn on tolerant/peer-sync
per #1960), consistent with the groups/interfaces/screen containers already
gated there. Add hierarchical + flat-set (ParseSetCommand+SetPath) tests.

## Provenance

Hostile review of PR #5226 (#5181), non-blocking observation 2. Same class as
#5180 (merged); applications container was out of that PR's scope.

## #5231 — configstore: master-password declared via groups/apply-groups silently disables config-DB encryption (plaintext secrets on disk) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
`masterPasswordPRF` (`pkg/configstore/crypto.go:56`, origin/master `33ea184d3`) decides whether the config DB is written encrypted (`maybeEncryptTreeJSON`). It resolves the PRF by scanning **only top-level `system` stanzas** via `systemBlocksOf(tree)` (`pkg/configstore/dataplane_retire.go:140`). It does **not** descend into `groups`.

`maybeEncryptTreeJSON` runs on the **unexpanded** persisted candidate tree — apply-groups expansion happens only on a compile-time clone (`pkg/config/README.md`: "Clones the tree, expands `apply-groups` ..."). So when an operator configures encryption via a group:

```
groups { enc { system { master-password { pseudorandom-function sha256; } } } }
apply-groups enc;
```

the compiled/runtime config activates master-password encryption, but the at-rest write path sees no `system master-password` at top level, `masterPasswordPRF` returns `""`, encryption is skipped, and `active.json` (IKE PSKs, WireGuard private keys, SNMP communities, user secrets) is written in **plaintext**.

## Invariant
A configuration that activates master-password encryption — directly **or** via `apply-groups` — must never persist the config DB in plaintext.

## origin/master location
- `pkg/configstore/crypto.go:56-71` (`masterPasswordPRF`), called from `maybeEncryptTreeJSON` (`crypto.go:~87`).
- Gate helper: `systemBlocksOf` at `pkg/configstore/dataplane_retire.go:140` (top-level only).

## Distinctness
- Distinct from **#4705** (split *top-level* `system` stanzas — fixed by `systemBlocksOf`; does not cover groups) and **#4578** (PRF typo).
- The codebase already ships `groupsBlocksOf` + `systemBlocksOfNode` (`dataplane_retire.go`) that the dataplane-retirement walk uses to find `dataplane-type` nested inside groups. `masterPasswordPRF` was simply never updated to use them.

## Fix direction
After scanning `systemBlocksOf(tree)`, also walk `groupsBlocksOf(tree)` → each group child → `systemBlocksOfNode(group)` → `master-password`/`pseudorandom-function`, returning the first PRF found (aligning with the compiler's apply-groups precedence). Fail closed: encrypt if any active surface carries a PRF.

## Provenance
gemini-review-046 High finding 1 (verified genuine + material + novel on origin/master `33ea184d3`).

## #5232 — pkg/api: bgpHandler streams the full BGP table with no request-context cancel check (CPU/GC waste after client disconnect) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
`bgpHandler` (`pkg/api/routing.go:80`, origin/master `33ea184d3`), `type=routes` branch, streams every route in a loop (`routing.go:109`), flushing the `bufio.Writer` + `http.Flusher` every 1024 iterations (`routing.go:115`). It **never checks `r.Context().Err()`**.

On a full internet BGP table (900k+ prefixes), if the client disconnects (curl abort, HTTP client timeout), the Go server cancels `r.Context()` but the loop keeps calling `fmt.Sprintf` + `writeJSONStringFragment` for every remaining route and writing to a dead connection — write/flush errors are silently discarded. The #4708 streaming rewrite bounded **memory** but not CPU-on-cancel.

## Impact
Wasted CPU + GC pressure proportional to table size on every disconnect. The REST API is localhost-bound (127.0.0.1:8080), so the trigger is a local monitoring client that times out on a large table rather than a remote attacker — still a real, repeatable inefficiency on a RAM/CPU-constrained firewall.

## Fix direction
Inside the `if (i+1)%1024 == 0` block, abort before flushing:
```go
if err := r.Context().Err(); err != nil {
    return
}
```

## origin/master location
`pkg/api/routing.go:109-128` (`bgpHandler` routes stream loop).

## Provenance
gemini-review-046 Medium finding 4 (verified: no context check present on origin/master `33ea184d3`; not a dup — searched). Same defect *class* as the #4708/#5060 resource-management line of work but a distinct, unaddressed handler.

## #5233 — pkg/api: session handlers walk the full conntrack map with no request-context cancel check (BPF bucket-lock contention after client disconnect) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Defect
`sessionsOffset` (`pkg/api/sessions.go:88`, origin/master `33ea184d3`) walks the entire conntrack table via `s.dp.IterateSessions` / `IterateSessionsV6` (`sessions.go:110` / `:139`). The callback returns `true` unconditionally (to compute `Total = idx`) and **never checks `r.Context().Err()`**.

On a firewall with millions of sessions, a client disconnect leaves the full BPF-map traversal running to completion — per-bucket locks + map-read syscalls — even though the response is discarded. The same unguarded `IterateSessions` pattern also appears in `sessionSummaryHandler` (`sessions.go:457`) and `sessionZonePairHandler` (`sessions.go:639`).

## Impact
CPU + BPF-map bucket-lock contention that competes with the live dataplane session-sync path, degrading dataplane→control-plane sync latency. Repeatable per disconnect on large session tables. (REST API is localhost-bound, so the trigger is a local client timing out, not a remote attacker — but the lock contention against the dataplane is the material cost.)

## Fix direction
Check the request context at the top of each iterator callback and abort the walk:
```go
if r.Context().Err() != nil {
    return false
}
```
`Total` is discarded once the client is gone, so an early/inaccurate count is harmless.

## origin/master location
`pkg/api/sessions.go:110` (primary), plus `:139`, `:457`, `:639`.

## Provenance
gemini-review-046 Medium finding 5 (verified: no context check present on origin/master `33ea184d3`; not a dup — searched). Distinct from #4708 (memory) and #5060 (grpcapi pipe/goroutine leak on Scanner ErrTooLong).

Follow-up from PR #5230 (#5185). The converge-to-C post-rename durability fix is
correct, but hostile review (rev5230) found a test-coverage gap:

The configstore converge tests inject the failure via the `writeActiveFn` STORE
seam, which BYPASSES `db.go writeTreeMarked`'s `fmt.Errorf("persist %s: %w", …)`
wrap. Because fsatomic's `afterRenameSyncDir` seam is UNEXPORTED, configstore

independently covered; a defense-in-depth coverage completeness gap, not a live
bug.

## Fix direction

Export `afterRenameSyncDir` (or add an exported test hook) so a configstore test
can drive a real post-rename failure end-to-end through `db.WriteActive` and

`%w`-wrapped error still satisfies `isPostRenameDurabilityFailure`.

## #5244 — config: sampling instance `input rate` accepts a negative value → uint32 wrap silently disables flow sampling [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
`compileSampling` stores the sampling instance `input rate` with no lower-bound
check, so a negative value is accepted at commit and then wraps to a huge 1-in-N
divisor in the snapshot builder, silently disabling flow sampling.

## Location (origin/master d1449fe77)
`pkg/config/compiler_services.go` ~1392-1396:
```go
if prop.Name() == "rate" {
    if v := nodeVal(prop); v != "" {
        if n, err := strconv.Atoi(v); err == nil {
            inst.InputRate = n            // no n >= 0 guard
        }
    }
}
```
The snapshot builder casts `uint32(InputRate)`; a negative `InputRate` becomes
~4294967295, i.e. "sample almost nothing".

## Why it matters
The sibling **port-mirroring** path in the same file already rejects this exact
class (lines ~1340-1347):
```go
return fmt.Errorf("port-mirroring instance %q: input rate must not be negative, got %d", inst.name, n)
// comment: uint32(InputRate) in the snapshot builder would wrap a negative rate
// into a huge 1-in-N sampling divisor.
```
Sampling was missed. A typo like `set forwarding-options sampling instance S input
rate -1` commits cleanly and silently turns off NetFlow/IPFIX export — an
observability fail (exfil/DDoS activity goes unexported while the operator
believes sampling is active). There is no typed leaf validator (schema arg only,
no `ValidateInteger`).

## Fix direction
Mirror the port-mirroring guard: reject `n < 0` in `compileSampling` (or add a
`ValidateIntegerMin(0)` typed leaf / strict gate `validateSamplingInputRateStrict`).
`0` remains "sample every packet" per Junos.

## #5245 — cluster: RG removal in UpdateConfig leaks the takeover holdTimer (fires on a deleted group → spurious election + timer leak) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
When a redundancy group is removed from config, `Manager.UpdateConfig` deletes it
from `m.groups` (and its monitor weights) but does NOT stop the group's armed
takeover `holdTimer`. The `time.AfterFunc` closure keeps the removed `rg` pointer
alive and still fires, taking `m.mu` and running an election against stale state.

## Location (origin/master d1449fe77)
`pkg/cluster/group_state.go` ~43-51 (removal loop):
```go
for id := range m.groups {
    if !seen[id] {
        for k := range m.monitorWeights {
            if k.rgID == id { delete(m.monitorWeights, k) }
        }
        delete(m.groups, id)          // <-- rg.holdTimer never Stop()'d
    }
}
```
`holdTimer` is armed in `pkg/cluster/readiness.go:38` (`rg.holdTimer =
time.AfterFunc(m.takeoverHoldTime, func(){ m.mu.Lock(); ... m.runElection()/electSingleNode() })`)
and is only ever stopped in `readiness.go` (re-arm/clear) and `manager.go:434-436`
(the `Stop()` cleanup path) — never in the config-removal loop.

## Why it matters
Each removed RG that had an armed holdTimer leaks one pending timer whose closure
holds the deleted group. When it fires it grabs the cluster mutex and runs a
spurious election evaluating the removed group's readiness/weight. No UAF (GC
keeps `rg` alive via the closure), but on a long-lived daemon with repeated RG
churn this accumulates timers and injects spurious election wakeups + misleading
readiness diagnostics.

## Fix direction
In the removal loop, before `delete(m.groups, id)`:
```go
if rg := m.groups[id]; rg != nil && rg.holdTimer != nil {
    rg.holdTimer.Stop(); rg.holdTimer = nil
}
```

## #5246 — cluster: ManualFailover pre-hook window races ResetFailover — an operator reset is silently overridden, node parks SecondaryHold [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
`ManualFailover` sets `failoverInProgress[rgID]=true`, then **unlocks** `m.mu` to
run the pre-failover hook (which can `time.Sleep` up to the retry timeout), then
re-locks and unconditionally sets `rg.ManualFailover=true` / `State=SecondaryHold`.
A concurrent `ResetFailover` during that unlocked window clears the failover, but
it does NOT consult `failoverInProgress`, so the trailing `ManualFailover` write
overrides the reset.

## Location (origin/master d1449fe77)
`pkg/cluster/failover.go`:
- `ManualFailover` (line 40): sets `failoverInProgress[rgID]=true`, `m.mu.Unlock()`
  (line 55), runs the retryable `preHook` loop (may sleep), then re-locks and at
  ~line 107 sets `rg.ManualFailover=true; rg.State=StateSecondaryHold`.
- `ResetFailover` (line 149): takes `m.mu`, at line 169 sets
  `rg.ManualFailover=false` and calls `recalcWeight(rg)` (restores weight, runs
  election) — **without checking `failoverInProgress`**.

The in-lock comment in `ManualFailover` ("Always clear the in-progress flag under
the same lock ... so there is no window where another caller can slip in between
flag-clear and state-commit") only guards against a competing `ManualFailover`;
it does not protect against `ResetFailover`, which ignores the flag.

## Why it matters
Operator sequence: `request chassis cluster failover` (enters preHook sleep) →
operator/orchestrator issues `request chassis cluster failover reset` (or kernel-
roll rejoin) → reset clears the failover and may make the node primary → preHook
finishes → `ManualFailover` re-parks the node in `SecondaryHold`, silently
discarding the reset. Same hazard in `ManualFailoverBatch`. Window is 0..retry
timeout (up to several seconds). Can leave a node stuck secondary after an
explicit reset — the reciprocal of the "never both down" hold that failover.go
already guards elsewhere.

## Fix direction
Have `ResetFailover`/`ManualFailoverBatch` consult `failoverInProgress` (fail with
"failover in progress" or record a generation the woken `ManualFailover` re-checks
and aborts if a reset intervened).

## Provenance
ps-review-042 (Paladin full-tree), batch A5_go_ha_vrrp_ra_conntrack-b1. Gated
against origin/master d1449fe77 (base 7f6f6b8b4, ~40 commits behind): confirmed

*(truncated — 41 lines total)*

## #5247 — dataplane/userspace: sessionMirrorFailed is sticky — never cleared on a later successful mirror, blocks HA takeover-readiness until helper restart [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
`Manager.sessionMirrorFailed` is set on any session-mirror failure and gates HA
takeover-readiness, but it is only ever cleared on a helper **process restart** —
never on a subsequent successful mirror. A single transient control-socket failure
during bulk session sync therefore keeps the standby "not takeover-ready" until
the helper respawns.

## Location (origin/master d1449fe77)
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go`:
```go
func (m *Manager) recordSessionMirrorFailureLocked(err error) {
    m.sessionMirrorFailed = true          // set on failure (line ~337)
    ...
}
// takeoverReadyLocked (line ~306):
if m.sessionMirrorFailed {
    reasons = append(reasons, "userspace session mirror unhealthy" ...)
}
```
The flag is set to `false` **only** in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/process.go:205` and
`:254` (process stop/start lifecycle). `git grep "sessionMirrorFailed = false"`
over `pkg/dataplane/userspace` shows no clear on the success path of
`syncSessionV4Locked`/`syncSessionV6Locked`.

## Why it matters
CLAUDE.md explicitly warns the helper control socket is shared by status poll, HA
sync, session installs, snapshot/forwarding sync, and that bulk sync causes
contention. A transient `requestSessionSync` failure under that contention latches
`sessionMirrorFailed=true`; even though later mirrors succeed, the standby stays
`takeoverReady=false`, so an HA failover blackholes the affected RG until the
helper process happens to restart. This is the sticky residual of the (closed)
"mirror failures swallowed during HA session install" fix (#346): failures are now
recorded but never un-recorded.

## Fix direction
Clear `sessionMirrorFailed` (and `sessionMirrorErr`) on a successful mirror in
`syncSessionV4Locked`/`syncSessionV6Locked`, or decay it by timestamp, or downgrade
it from a hard takeover-readiness gate to a health metric.

## #5248 — config: zone `interfaces` bracketed list not handled by the #2419 dual-AST SSOT — flat-set/load-override `interfaces [ a b ]` drops members or hard-rejects [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
`compileZones` reads zone `interfaces` membership from `prop.Children` only. The
schema models `interfaces` as a **wildcard** container node (not a `multi: true`
leaf), so a bracketed flat-set / `load override` form
`interfaces [ ge-0/0/0 ge-0/0/1 ]` is not converted by the #2419 dual-AST SSOT —
the second and later members are not read as sibling interfaces.

## Location (origin/master d1449fe77)
`pkg/config/compiler_security_zones.go` ~113-115:
```go
case "interfaces":
    for _, iface := range prop.Children {
        zone.Interfaces = append(zone.Interfaces, iface.Name())
        ...
```
No `firewallMatchValues(prop)` / `Keys[1:]` handling. Schema
(`pkg/config/schema_security.go:167`) is `"interfaces": {wildcard: &schemaNode{
children: {"host-inbound-traffic": ...}}}` — a wildcard, not a `multi` leaf, so
`ast_edit.go`'s multi-collapse branch (`childSchema.multi && ...`) does not fire.
Because the lexer strips `[`/`]` (#2419), `set ... interfaces [ ge-0/0/0 ge-0/0/1 ]`
flattens to `SetPath([... "interfaces","ge-0/0/0","ge-0/0/1"])`; with a wildcard
(non-multi) node the trailing `ge-0/0/1` lands as a **child of** `ge-0/0/0`, not a
sibling. `prop.Children` then yields only `ge-0/0/0`.

Note the SAME file already applies the #2419 SSOT (`firewallMatchValues`) to zone
host-inbound `system-services`/`protocols` — interfaces was not converted. The
#3703 bracket-list test explicitly excludes interface validation.

## Behaviour / why it matters
Two possible runtime outcomes, both worth closing:
- If closed-world strict validation rejects the trailing token → hard commit
  error on a Junos-legal bracketed zone-interfaces list (parity gap; operator must
  hand-split to per-line).
- If it is accepted → all but the first interface silently dropped from the zone →
  interface left unmanaged/brought-down (availability) or evaluated against the
  wrong zone.
Either way it violates the documented dual-AST contract for zone membership (a
security boundary). A repro via `ParseSetCommand()` + `tree.SetPath()` +
`compileZones` should determine which, and the fix is to mirror the host-inbound
SSOT (read `Keys[1:]` AND `Children`).

## #5261 — routing/bond: adopt path can retain a partially-realized bond forever after daemon restart [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Defect (follow-up from PR #5259 / #5119 review)

The #5119 differential-reconcile fix (PR #5259) is correct for the live
flap-on-every-commit bug. During its hostile review one narrow, non-gating
restart-edge was identified and deferred here.

`bondManager.createLocked` (`pkg/routing/bond.go`) has an **adopt** branch: when a
bond already exists in the kernel (`LinkByName` returns no error), it tracks the
bond under the desired `bondSig` and only `LinkSetUp`s it — no LinkDel/LinkAdd,
no re-enslave. That is deliberate and correct for the common daemon-restart case
(don't flap an already-good bond).

The edge: the reconcile tolerates a member that is not yet enumerated in the
kernel (#4823 — LinkSetMaster of a missing member is a soft error, the bond is
still tracked). If a bond is realized with a **partial** member set, then the
daemon restarts with **no subsequent config change to that bond**, the adopt path
tracks the *full desired* `bondSig` without ever completing the missing
enslavement. Because the tracked sig now equals the desired sig, every future
reconcile sees "unchanged" and takes the KEEP path — so the bond stays
partially-enslaved until its config next changes.

The pre-#5119 code (unconditional clear+rebuild every commit) self-healed this on
the very next commit; the differential reconcile trades that away for the (much
more valuable) no-flap property.

## Suggested fix

In the adopt branch, verify the live kernel bond's actual enslaved-member set
matches the desired member set before accepting the KEEP; if it diverges (a
member is missing from the kernel bond), complete the enslavement (or force a
recreate) rather than tracking the full sig as satisfied. Equivalently, derive
the adopted `bondSig` from the *observed* kernel state, not the desired config,
so a partial realization produces a sig mismatch → reconcile completes it.

## Severity
Low / narrow. Requires (a) a member absent at realization time AND (b) a daemon
restart with no intervening change to that bond. Orthogonal to the #5119 live
flap fix; does not affect the steady-state reconcile path.

Provenance: PR #5259 hostile review, Point 4 minor observation.

## #5267 — event-stream: replay-gap FullResync written outside producer_seq_lock can overtake a committed lower-seq channel frame [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Defect
io_thread_main stores connected=true before replay_buffered, and the gap branch allocates+writes FullResync outside producer_seq_lock, so a channel-committed lower sequence can coexist on the wire after a directly-written higher sequence, turning the HA recovery barrier itself into an out-of-order stream (repeated disconnect/resync churn; stale/missing standby sessions on failover).

## Location (current origin/master)
`userspace-dp/src/event_stream/mod.rs:962-967,1033-1036,1145-1151`

## Scenario
Producer commits seq N to the channel FIFO while replay_buffered fetch-adds N+1 and writes FullResync directly to the socket -> wire order N+1,N -> the Go reader (eventstream.go) diagnoses a session gap, drops the connection, and a stale delta can overwrite exported truth.

## Fix
Serialize the I/O-thread FullResync allocation/write under the same producer sequence discipline (or a barrier) so the direct socket write cannot reorder ahead of a channel-committed frame; do not hold the producer mutex across bounded socket backpressure. Publish `connected=true` only after replay ordering is established.

## Severity
High — see defect/scenario above.

Source: codex-review-178 [A1-b6-F1]

## #5268 — VLAN: non-fatal ensureRxVlanOff failure lets HW-stripped tagged traffic inherit the parent's first-subinterface zone (cross-zone bypass) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Defect
compiler.go returns no error when querying or disabling rxvlan fails; compilation continues into shim attachment even though the XDP path derives VLAN identity only from in-frame tags. A required security-domain-identity operation silently degrades to a warning, merging an untrusted L2 domain into a trusted zone. Distinct from #5139 (flow-cache keys physical parent ifindex while the tag is present).

## Location (current origin/master)
`pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:1368-1392; userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs (VLAN parse); userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:81-89`

## Scenario
`ethtool -K <parent> rxvlan off` fails persistently -> NIC strips the 802.1Q tag -> the XDP parser emits vlan_id=0 -> resolve_ingress_logical_ifindex falls back to the physical ifindex -> the parent maps to the first subinterface's zone -> untrusted VLAN traffic is classified into a trusted zone (screen/policy bypass), silent after one warning.

## Fix
Make RX-VLAN-offload-disable an activation precondition: ensureRxVlanOff/ensureRxVlanOff-equivalent must return an error that fails the compile/apply (or fails closed) when the offload cannot be disabled, since XDP cannot read stripped skb->vlan_tci. Do not proceed to shim attachment on failure.

High — see defect/scenario above.

## #5269 — source-NAT: address-only pool (port no-translation / GRE / portless) mints unowned, ambiguous public tuples [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
The address_only branch (port_less || tuple_unknown || no_translation) selects a pool address but leaves rewrite_src_port=None and never calls allocate_translation, so no occupancy token is minted. Reproduces with ONE rule/ONE pool/ONE address. Distinct from #5144 (two separate allocator domains across overlapping pools).

## Location (current origin/master)
`userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs:~1167,1244-1273`

## Scenario
Two internal flows behind a one-address pool with `port no-translation` (or two GRE/portless flows) receive identical translated public tuples with no ownership token; the reverse (1:N) index cannot disambiguate -> the later flow's replies are stranded or misdelivered under the first session.

## Fix
On the address_only path, mint an ownership/claim record (as the PAT path does via allocate_translation) and reject the second flow whose externally-observable reverse tuple would be identical, unless the protocol provides a separately-parsed authoritative selector. Add address-only claim/release lifecycle symmetry.

## Severity
High — see defect/scenario above.

Source: codex-review-178 [A2-b1-F2]

## #5270 — BGP group inheritance is sibling-order-dependent — `neighbor` before `export`/`peer-as` drops the inherited value [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
compileProtocols walks BGP group children once and stamps each neighbor's inherited defaults from the values seen so far, with no group finalization/reconciliation pass; a neighbor child before the group export/peer-as child captures the empty/default value. Fail-open routing, not vSRX-equivalent.

## Location (current origin/master)
`pkg/config/compiler_protocols.go:~287-456`

## Scenario
`group G neighbor 192.0.2.1` ordered before `group G export OUT` -> the neighbor compiles with an empty Export (captured from group defaults seen so far) -> FRR emits no outbound route-map -> route leak; the same order dependency exists for flat-set vs hierarchical AST shapes.

## Fix
Collect all group defaults completely (a group finalization pass) before any neighbor inherits them, so semantically-unordered Junos sibling statements compile to identical neighbor state regardless of encounter order.

## Severity
High — see defect/scenario above.

Source: codex-review-178 [A3-b3-F1]

## #5272 — HA session-sync: BulkEnd/BulkAck with no active transaction releases sync-readiness (VRRP hold) without a real transfer [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Defect
syncMsgBulkEnd checks the epoch only when bulkInProgress is already true; with no active bulk it still reconciles, ACKs, marks completion and invokes the callback. syncMsgBulkAck sets bulkEverCompleted/outboundBulkAcked and calls its callback regardless of a pending match. A buggy/mixed-version/replaying peer frame can release the stateful-failover safety gate. Distinct from #5085 (sender empty markers) and #5084 (config-apply epoch).

## Location (current origin/master)
`pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:1480-1522`

## Scenario
A peer sends a BulkEnd (or BulkAck) with bulkInProgress=false / no pending epoch -> reconcileStaleSessions no-ops, the node ACKs, sets bulkEverCompleted, and fires OnBulkSyncReceived which releases the VRRP sync hold -> the node becomes MASTER-eligible while forwarding with an empty/stale peer session table.

## Fix
Bind the cold-sync completion callback to a live, same-connection, exact-epoch transfer transaction: require a matching BulkStart/pending epoch before BulkEnd/BulkAck can mark completion or release readiness; reject out-of-state markers.

## Severity
High — see defect/scenario above.

## #5276 — applyRootAuth never revokes root password/authorized_keys on stanza/leaf removal (deleted root credentials stay live) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
applyRootAuth returns immediately when the stanza is nil and has only positive write branches for a nonempty password or key list — no removal/lock/provenance branch. Non-root reconciliation removes the last xpf-managed key and locks removed passwords via UID-keyed provenance; root uses neither. The most-privileged host credential persists after offboarding/rotation/compromise despite a green commit.

## Location (current origin/master)
`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1495-1550`

## Scenario
An operator deletes `system root-authentication` (or its encrypted-password / last SSH key) -> applyRootAuth early-returns on ra==nil (or skips empty leaves) -> the prior /etc/shadow root hash and /root/.ssh/authorized_keys remain accepted indefinitely, while the commit reports success.

## Fix
Give root the same UID-keyed provenance + revocation the non-root path has (#5128/#5204/#5224): on removal of an xpf-installed root credential, lock the password / remove the xpf-managed authorized_keys, or reject the credential-less end state; never silently retain.

## Severity
High — see defect/scenario above.

Source: codex-review-178 [A7-b1-F2]

The primary gRPC listener is explicitly unauthenticated, clamps only to TCP loopback, and installs only message-size + config-lock interceptors; destructive SystemAction methods do no identity/class check. ## #5290 — userspace-dp/HA: Coordinator::drain_session_deltas fixed BTreeMap order + caller-wide budget starves higher worker slots during event-stream fallback [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

HA state quality becomes dependent on worker-slot assignment during the exact outage the fallback exists to cover. Distinct from #2442/#2669/#2874.

Keep a persistent round-robin cursor over live slot IDs with a per-binding quantum within the caller cap (advance even when the cap is consumed); couple fallback overflow/poison to the owner-RG resync recovery.

Resolve and publish outer MTU per peer public key (including learned/roamed endpoints), look up the selected peer's value in encap_and_send, and refresh atomically with forwarding generations; or reject multi-peer configs whose effective underlays differ.

## #5307 — dataplane: shim-map deploy validator checks only presence + MaxEntries — no key/value/layout or live-pin ABI comparison before stopping the old daemon [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
validateUserspaceShimSpec checks presence + MaxEntries (and a NO_PREALLOC flag) for three maps only; production enables PinByName and can hit ErrMapIncompatible at load, not reproduced by the preflight. ## #5308 — daemon: policy-scheduler and RPM pin-retry goroutines (daemonCtx-bound) are never cancelled/joined during shutdown [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
startPolicySchedulerLoopLocked runs go scheduler.Run(daemonCtx) (schedulerCancel invoked only on config replace) and probePinRetryLoop binds to daemonCtx = context.Background() (never cancelled in production); rpm.StopAll joins only the RPM manager's own WaitGroup. Violates cancel-before-dependent-teardown. Distinct from #5165/#5121/#4958.

## Location (current origin/master)
`pkg/daemon/daemon_scheduler.go:140-147; pkg/daemon/daemon_rpm.go:288-325; pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:823-843`

## Scenario
SIGTERM -> shutdown calls only feeds.StopAll()/rpm.StopAll() -> the policy-scheduler tick can call UpdatePolicyScheduleState through a closed runtime and the RPM pin-retry tick can run routing-pin syscalls after FRR/probe teardown; for library callers where Run returns, both loops leak indefinitely.

## Fix
Cancel (schedulerCancel) and join the scheduler goroutine, and bind/join probePinRetryLoop to a cancellable context in the shutdown sequence, before dependent-subsystem teardown.

## Severity
Medium — see defect/scenario above.

Source: codex-review-178 [A7-b1-F3]

## Defect
teardownUnmappedManaged is void; rename-back failure only slog.Warns; both files are removed "regardless of the rename outcome"; standalone networkctlReload failure only warns; the caller invokes it with no result. #4956 added error aggregation only to enumerateAndRenameMapped (startup). Make teardownUnmappedManaged return errors into the commit result; retain the durable .link/.network markers when rename-back or reload fails so a later apply can retry the transition.

## Defect
applyInterfaceReconcile logs and continues; xfrmManager.Apply logs create/find/up/delete failures and returns nil; bond errors are discarded at the daemon boundary. #4823/#4901 added bond/Clear-time error returns but the create/up path still returns nil and the caller swallows it. Publish tunnel/XFRM/bond create/teardown errors into the configuration transaction (return them from Apply and include applyInterfaceReconcile in the final error join) so a failed netlink operation fails the commit or records retry debt.

## #5311 — eventengine: revision-blind armCooldown throttles a policy that redefined itself in its own commit [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
runAction calls armCooldown(policyName) after applyOnce succeeds; armCooldown stamps e.runtime[name].lastTrigger with no revision check, while Apply installs a fresh newPolicyRuntime() when semRev changes. Name-based ABA. Distinct from #5063/#5062/#2140/#3750.

## Defect
applyAggregator cancels+replaces the aggregator on every call; aggregator.Run returns on ctx.Done() with no flush (flushAndLog only on ticker.C). #4964 fixed only the callback/goroutine leak. ## Location (current origin/master)
`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:240-285; pkg/logging/aggregator.go:239-250`

Gate applyAggregator on config equality (skip when unchanged) and flush the current window (Run should flush on ctx.Done, or transfer state) before replacing the aggregator.

## #5328 — [cohort] codex-178 low-materiality + test-coverage-only survivors (15 items: DSCP/ECN, bind-mode race, fairness arg, RSS subset, REST/gRPC parity, xsk-repro provenance, ...) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-06)

Tracking issue for the low-materiality and test-coverage-only survivors of the
codex-review-178 whole-repository defensive audit (base `33ea184d3`). Each was
verified against current origin/master (still present, not already fixed, not a
duplicate of an open issue) but is individually below the bar for a standalone
tracker — grouped here per the #4422 cohort precedent. High/Medium findings are
filed as their own issues; this is the Low + test-validity remainder.

Fix independently; none blocks the others.

## Rust dataplane (userspace-dp)

- **[A1-b2-F3] TUN-origin WireGuard UDP sends omit IP_TOS/IPV6_TCLASS (DSCP/ECN dropped).**
  `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/wg_control.rs:1004-1017` — `wg_send_to` ends
  in a plain `socket.send_to` with no per-datagram cmsg, so local/TUN-origin WG
  traffic egresses with outer DS byte 0 / Not-ECT while the AF_XDP transit builder
  copies the inner DS byte. Fix: add a data-send `sendmsg` cmsg variant (retain
  default class for handshake/keepalive). Low, QoS/parity by packet origin.

- **[A1-b5-F1] BindingLiveState::snapshot loads bind_mode twice, can publish a contradictory xsk_bind_mode/zero_copy pair.**
  `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/umem/snapshot.rs:28-34` — two independent `bind_mode.load`
  calls; a concurrent set/clear between them yields `("unknown", zero_copy=true)` or
  similar. Self-repairs next scrape. Fix: load `bind_mode` once and derive both
  fields. Low, transient diagnostics.

- **[A1-b6-F2] MSG_RESUME never schedules frames consumed during pause (latent).**
  `userspace-dp/src/event_stream/mod.rs:1347-1351,1602-1609` — Resume only stores
  `paused=false` (a comment promises a flush that does not exist); paused frames go
  only to `replay_buf` and transmit only on a later DrainRequest/reconnect. Currently
  no production Pause/Resume caller, so latent. Fix: on Resume, flush the unsent

## #5334 — ddns/surface-a: withdraw-while-pending deletes the desired (unpublished) address, orphaning the live prior value [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect (follow-up from PR #5332 / #5285 review)

The #5285 durable-pending fix (PR #5332, merged) correctly closes the
save->wire crash window on the live-reconcile recovery path. During its hostile
review one narrow, non-gating compound-event edge was identified and deferred
here.

`reconcileScopeLocked` Pass 2 `withdrawOwnedLocked` (`pkg/ddns/surface_a.go`)
deletes `owned.AddrText` when a scope's binding is removed. If the record is
`PublishPending` at that moment (a crash left `{AddrText=B(desired,
never-reached-wire), PublishPending=true, PriorAddrText=A(live)}`), the withdraw
deletes B — which never reached the wire — leaving the LIVE prior value A
orphaned in public DNS.

## Scenario
1. Renumber A->B; crash between the durable pending save and the wire add
   (case (b) from the #5285 analysis) -> on-disk `{B, pending, prior=A}`, wire
   still at A.
2. Before the next reconcile re-runs the wire, the scope's binding is REMOVED
   during downtime.
3. Restart: Reconcile Pass 2 `withdrawOwnedLocked` deletes `owned.AddrText` = B
   (never published) -> A stays live and orphaned; xpf reports the scope
   withdrawn.

## Fix
When `PublishPending` is set, `withdrawOwnedLocked` should prefer
`PriorAddrText` (the real live value) as the delete target instead of
`AddrText` (the desired-but-unpublished value) — mirroring how `publishLocked`'s
`prevAddr` already threads `PriorAddrText` on the pending path. Withdraw the
value that is actually on the wire.

## Severity
Low / very narrow. Requires the compound event (a) crash in the pending window
AND (b) binding removed before the next reconcile. The pre-#5285 code was
strictly worse here (it false-confirmed B, also orphaning A). Orphaned stale RR,
not traffic misdirection. Orthogonal to the #5285 live-recovery path.

Provenance: PR #5332 hostile review, minor observation 1.

## #5338 — userspace-dp/HA: standby does not reserve address-only source-NAT tokens (reserve_synced_source_nat_allocation skips no-port decisions) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

## Defect (follow-up from PR #5336 / #5269)

PR #5336 (merged) mints an occupancy token for address-only source-NAT
translations (`port no-translation` / GRE / portless) on the ACTIVE node so the
reverse (1:N) index disambiguates. During that work an analogous HA-sync gap was
identified on the STANDBY side and deferred here.

`reserve_synced_source_nat_allocation` (userspace-dp source-NAT) still SKIPS
no-port (address-only) decisions when reserving a synced session's NAT
allocation on the standby. So after a failover, the newly-active node has no
address-only occupancy token for sessions that were address-only on the old
active — its reverse index cannot disambiguate two synced address-only flows to
the same pool address, re-introducing the #5269 ambiguity on the post-failover
path.

## Location (current origin/master, after #5336)
`userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs` — `reserve_synced_source_nat_allocation` (the
standby/synced reservation path), which mirrors the active `reserve_*` but omits
the address-only branch #5336 added to the active path.

## Fix
Mirror #5336's `reserve_address_only` token minting in the synced-reservation
path: when a synced session carries an address-only source-NAT decision, reserve
the same `(protocol, pool address, preserved src port, remote ip, remote port)`
token in `address_only_owners` on the standby, so the reverse index is
unambiguous immediately after failover. Analogous to the #4388/#4512-class
active-vs-synced reservation parity gaps.

## Severity
Medium (HA-only; correctness after failover). The active-path #5269 fix (#5336)
is complete on its own; this closes the standby parity so the guarantee survives
a failover.

Provenance: PR #5336 out-of-scope note (#5269 engineer report).

## #5341 — userspace-dp/NAT: deterministic CGNAT (mode 1) address-only sub-branch mints no occupancy token (same #5269 collision) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Defect (follow-up from PR #5336 / #5269 review)

PR #5336 (merged) closed the #5269 unowned-ambiguous-tuple gap for the
round-robin / persistent source-NAT pool address-only branch by minting an
occupancy token. During its hostile review an analogous untokened path was
found in the deterministic-CGNAT branch and deferred here.

The deterministic CGNAT (mode 1) address-only sub-branch
(`userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs` ~L1215-1250, `deterministic_v4` /
`deterministic_v6`) returns its `NatDecision` WITHOUT calling
`reserve_address_only`. Deterministic CGNAT maps a block of subscribers onto one
shared external IP; two subscribers sending port-less / `port no-translation`
traffic to the SAME remote produce the same reverse identity and are still
admitted with no occupancy token — the identical #5269-class ambiguity (the
reverse 1:N index cannot disambiguate → later subscriber's replies
stranded/mis-delivered).

## Status
UNCHANGED by #5336 (NOT a regression) — this is a separate feature path
(deterministic CGNAT, #4559) with its own address-only handling.

Mirror #5336's `reserve_address_only` token minting in the deterministic-CGNAT
address-only sub-branch: mint the same `(protocol, translated_ip, preserved
port, remote ip, remote port)` token so a genuinely-colliding second subscriber
is denied-as-exhaustion rather than handed an ambiguous unowned tuple.

## Severity
Medium — CGNAT-only; correctness for port-less/no-translation subscribers behind
deterministic CGNAT.

## #5355 — routing/daemon: tunnelManager.Apply always returns nil — GRE/tunnel create/up failures do not fail the commit (fail-open, sibling of #5310) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect (follow-up from PR #5354 / #5310 review)

PR #5354 (merged) made XFRM-interface + interface-reconcile + bond failures
fail the commit closed (#5310). The interface-reconcile tail-join wiring it
added is generic, but one stage still swallows failures:
`tunnelManager.Apply` (GRE/tunnel manager) has a single unconditional
`return nil` — so a genuine GRE/tunnel `LinkAdd`/`LinkSetUp`/delete failure is
logged and the commit reports SUCCESS while the tunnel interface is absent
(the same fail-open false-convergence #5310 fixed for XFRM/bond).

## Status
Pre-existing, OUT OF SCOPE for #5310 (which fixed the XFRM/bond/interface-
reconcile stages). The apply-error join wiring #5354 added ALREADY threads the
interface-reconcile stage, so once `tunnelManager.Apply` returns real errors
they will surface — the remaining work is only in the tunnel manager.

## Location (current origin/master, after #5354)
`pkg/routing/` tunnel manager `Apply` (the `return nil` at ~line 478 per the
#5354 review) + its caller in the interface-reconcile path.

## Fix
Mirror the #5310 xfrmManager.Apply pattern in `tunnelManager.Apply`: aggregate
genuine create/find/up/delete failures via `errors.Join` and return them, while
preserving idempotency (adopt already-exists, already-gone delete tolerated) —
so a genuine GRE/tunnel reconcile failure fails the commit closed and a routine
idempotent re-apply does not.

through the tunnel silently blackholes).

## #5362 — eventstream (Go reader): FullResync does not advance prevSeq — one bounded reconnect on the first post-barrier delta [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Defect (follow-up from PR #5361 / #5267 review)

PR #5361 (merged) fixed the Rust producer so the replay-gap `FullResync` is
emitted in seq order (wire order == seq order). During its hostile review a
distinct, pre-existing GO-READER nit was found and deferred here.

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/eventstream.go`'s `EventTypeFullResync` handling does
NOT advance `prevSeq`. So after a FullResync(S) barrier, the first live delta
(seq S+1) is compared against the stale `prevSeq` and still trips the
session-sync gap check (`seq > prevSeq+1`) → exactly ONE reconnect on the
active-traffic path.

## Status
PRE-EXISTING, NOT introduced by #5361. With #5361's wire-monotonic + replay-
buffered barrier, this now CONVERGES (bounded 2-connection recovery) instead of
the old ACK-watermark churn — so it's a single benign reconnect, not a loop.

## Location (current origin/master, after #5361)
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/eventstream.go` — the `EventTypeFullResync` /
`handleEventStreamFullResync` case (does not update `prevSeq`).

## Fix
On receiving a `FullResync(S)`, advance `prevSeq = S` (the barrier re-baselines
the sequence), so the next live delta (S+1) is in-order and does not trigger a
spurious gap → removes even the single post-barrier reconnect.

## Severity
Low (one bounded reconnect, self-converging after #5361). Cosmetic churn
reduction on the HA active-traffic recovery path.

Provenance: PR #5361 hostile review, non-blocking observation (Go-reader side).

## #5363 — verify-dataplane: stale-live-pin ABI mismatch (embedded>pinned) prints the misleading 'rebuild the shim' remediation instead of 'clear the stale pin' [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect (follow-up from PR #5360 / #5307)

PR #5360 (merged) correctly added a live-pinned-map ABI comparison to the
deploy pre-flight (`validateUserspaceShimSpec`), catching `ErrMapIncompatible`
BEFORE stopping the old daemon. Verified working: it refused a deploy where
`userspace_cpumap` embedded MaxEntries=256 vs the live pinned map's 16.

But when the mismatch is embedded > pinned (i.e. the RUNNING daemon's pin is
STALE/older, and the new embedded shim is correct), the deploy wrapper prints
the generic #1864 remediation:

    This is the #1864 failure mode. Rebuild with the pinned toolchain
    (make generate) or restore the tracked object:
      git checkout -- pkg/dataplane/userspace_xdp_bpfel.o && make build

...which is WRONG for this case — the embedded shim is byte-correct (sha256 ==
the tracked object). The actual fix is to CLEAR the stale live pin
(`/sys/fs/bpf/xpf/<map>`) on the target node (stop daemon, remove the pin dir)
so the new daemon recreates the map fresh with the new ABI. Rebuilding/
regenerating the shim does nothing.

## Fix
When `validateUserspaceShimSpec`'s LIVE-PIN comparison fails (as opposed to the
embedded-vs-expected or kernel-verifier failure), emit a distinct remediation:
"the running daemon's pinned map <name> is stale (embedded=<E> pinned=<P>); clear
the stale pin (stop xpfd; rm /sys/fs/bpf/xpf/<name>) so the new ABI is created
fresh — do NOT rebuild the shim." Distinguish the stale-pin case from the
genuine embedded-shim-wrong (#1864) case in the message.

## Severity
Low (operator-guidance/message quality). The refusal itself is correct
(prevents a brick); only the remediation text misdirects.

Provenance: hit while deploying master (userspace_cpumap 16->256) to the stale
loss cluster; surfaced during the #5359/#5361 HA test-failover.
