## #5364 — test/incus cluster-deploy: rolling deploy cannot cross a shim-map ABI change on a stale cluster — needs a coordinated pin-clear refresh mode [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-17)

## Gap

When the loss/HA cluster is running a build whose pinned BPF maps have an OLDER
ABI than the new build (e.g. `userspace_cpumap` MaxEntries 16 -> 256 across a
range of merged PRs), `make cluster-deploy`'s per-node verify-dataplane
pre-flight (correctly, post-#5307/#5360) REFUSES the deploy: loading the new
daemon would `ErrMapIncompatible` over the stale live pin. This is the intended
fail-closed behavior (it prevents a brick) — but the rolling deploy then has NO
path to actually complete the cross-ABI upgrade: every node's pre-flight rejects
because every node still runs the old pin, and hand-rolling an `incus file push`
deploy is forbidden (bypasses the lock + the verify gate).

So a cluster that drifts more than one shim-map-ABI generation behind master
becomes un-deployable-to without a manual, out-of-band pin clear (stop xpfd; rm
/sys/fs/bpf/xpf/<map>; restart onto the new binary) coordinated across both
nodes — which the tooling does not provide.

## Impact
Blocks ALL HA `test-failover` validation on a stale cluster (hit while trying to
test-failover the #5359 + #5361 HA event-stream pair — both are code-validated
(reviews + full cargo) but cannot be end-to-end failover-tested until the cluster
takes the new ABI).

## Fix
Add a coordinated cross-ABI refresh mode to `test/incus/cluster-setup.sh` /
`make cluster-deploy` (e.g. `cluster-deploy-fresh` or an auto-detect): when
verify-dataplane rejects ONLY on a stale-live-pin ABI mismatch (embedded>pinned,
embedded shim byte-correct), drain the node, stop xpfd, clear the affected
`/sys/fs/bpf/xpf/<map>` pin(s), install the new binary, and start — one node at a
time behind the existing lock, so the peer keeps forwarding. Or a full
`cluster-destroy`+`cluster-create` fast path for a wholesale refresh.

## Severity
Medium (lab/CI enablement). Blocks the HA test-failover gate whenever the shared
cluster drifts an ABI generation behind; recovery today is manual + forbidden-
by-policy to hand-roll.

Provenance: #5359/#5361 HA test-failover deploy, verify-dataplane refused
(userspace_cpumap embedded=256 pinned=16). Companion to #5363 (misleading msg).

## #5373 — config: interface member-range expansion infinite-loop/OOM via int64 loop-variable overflow when end approaches MaxInt64 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
`expandMemberRange` (`pkg/config/compiler_interface_range.go`) expands a
`member-range <start> to <end>` interface selector with a counting loop
`for i := sn; i <= en; i++`. `sn`/`en` are parsed from the raw range tokens
via `splitTrailingInt` → `strconv.Atoi`, which accepts any decimal up to
`math.MaxInt64` (member-range tokens do NOT pass through typed-schema
validation). The `interfaceRangeMaxMembers = 4096` cap only bounds the
DIFFERENCE `en - sn`, not `en`'s absolute value, so a range whose endpoints
sit just below `MaxInt64` passes the cap yet overflows the loop variable.

## Trace (verified on origin/master 9bfd48226)
`member-range ge-0/0/9223372036854775797 to ge-0/0/9223372036854775807`
1. `splitTrailingInt` parses `sn = MaxInt64-10`, `en = MaxInt64` (both valid `int`).
2. `sn > en` check passes (en >= sn); `en - sn == 10 < 4096` cap passes.
3. Loop `for i := sn; i <= en; i++`: at `i == MaxInt64` the body runs, then
   `i++` overflows to `math.MinInt64`; `MinInt64 <= MaxInt64` is true, so the
   loop never terminates — it appends unboundedly until the daemon OOMs/hangs.

The existing #4807 comment/guard addresses only the `en-sn+1` **capacity**
overflow (the `make()` negative-capacity panic); it does not guard the loop.

## Impact
Control-plane DoS (infinite loop + memory exhaustion). `expandMemberRange`
runs during config compilation, which executes at strict commit AND on the
tolerant load / HA config-sync paths — so a persisted or peer-synced config
carrying this pattern crashes the daemon on load (a fail-closed / HA-DoS
violation), not only on an interactive commit.

## Fix direction
Iterate on the bounded COUNT instead of the raw endpoint, so the loop
variable can never approach `MaxInt64`:
```go
// en - sn is already guaranteed < interfaceRangeMaxMembers here.
n := en - sn
out := make([]string, 0, n+1)
for k := 0; k <= n; k++ {
    out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", sp, sn+k))
}
```
`k` ranges `0..(en-sn)` (< 4096), bounded and overflow-free; `sn+k` yields

## #5379 — configstore: Store.Annotate bypasses config-lock ownership (no ensureHolderLocked, extends holder lease) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary
`Store.Annotate` (`pkg/configstore/store_command.go:241`) mutates the candidate
config and refreshes the config-lock idle lease (`touchConfigLockLocked`)
**without any config-lock ownership check**. Every other candidate mutator
enforces ownership via a session-scoped `*As` variant that calls
`ensureHolderLocked(sessionID)`. `Annotate` is the one user mutator missing
this, so a caller that does not hold the config lock can annotate another
session's candidate and keep the lock lease alive indefinitely.

## Trace
1. Operator A holds the config lock (`EnterConfigureSession("session-A")`).
2. A second local caller invokes annotate via the REST endpoint
   `configAnnotateHandler` (`pkg/api/config.go:399`) or the local CLI
   `annotate` dispatch (`pkg/cli/cli_dispatch.go:504`) — both call the
   unguarded `s.store.Annotate(path, comment)`.
3. `Annotate` takes `s.mu`, passes `ensureWritableLocked()`, sees a non-nil
   candidate, runs `s.candidate.AnnotatePath(path, comment)` — mutating A's
   candidate — then calls `s.touchConfigLockLocked()`, extending A's lease on
   behalf of the non-holder.
4. No `ensureHolderLocked` is ever consulted.

## Evidence it's a genuine gap
- All 7 sibling mutators call `ensureHolderLocked(sessionID)`
  (`store_command.go` lines 25, 64, 115, 145, 169, 193, 220).
- `pkg/configstore/README.md` documents the enforcement model and enumerates
  **every** session-guarded mutator (`SetAs`, `SetFromInputAs`, `DeleteAs`,
  `DeleteFromInputAs`, `DeactivateFromInputAs`/`ActivateFromInputAs`, `CopyAs`,
  `RenameAs`, `InsertAs`, `LoadOverrideAs`/`LoadMergeAs`/`LoadSetAs`,
  `RollbackAs`, `ConfirmCommitAs`). **`Annotate` is absent from that list.**
- No `AnnotateAs` variant exists.
- The README's own threat model calls out exactly this: a non-holder must not
  "extend the true holder's idle lease (`touchConfigLockLocked`) ... with no
  ownership check." `Annotate` does precisely that.

## Exposure
Reachable on the localhost REST listener (127.0.0.1:8080) and the local CLI.
`Annotate` is **not** exposed over gRPC/the HA fabric listener (no gRPC
handler), so this is a localhost multi-session / second-local-client
consistency+authorization gap, not a remote-fabric hole. Impact is bounded to
comment/metadata mutation of the candidate plus indefinite lease extension

## #5380 — userspace-dp/HA: syncSessionRequestsLocked dials a fresh socket per session mirror with no fast-fail — hung helper stalls bulk session ops for minutes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

## Summary
`syncSessionRequestsLocked` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:1406`)
mirrors session create/update/delete to the Rust helper by looping over the
requests and calling `requestSessionSync` once per request. Each
`requestSessionSync` (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/process_control.go`) opens a
**fresh** Unix-socket connection with `net.DialTimeout(..., 2*time.Second)` and
sets a 3s deadline, and there is **no fast-fail**: a dial/IO error is logged and
the loop continues to the next request. Under bulk session operations against a
hung-but-not-yet-reaped helper this serializes into a multi-minute control-plane
stall.

## Trace
1. Operator clears/invalidates a large session set → `BatchDeleteSessions` →
   `deleteHelperSessionsV4` (`manager_ha.go:1145`), which chunks keys by
   `sessionHelperDeleteChunk` and calls `syncSessionRequestsLocked(reqs...)`
   per chunk.
2. `deleteHelperSessionsV4` guards `if m.proc == nil { return }`, but `m.proc`
   is only nil'd when the helper is explicitly stopped or a periodic health
   poll fails — there is a multi-second window where the helper has hung/crashed
   but `m.proc` is still non-nil.
3. `syncSessionRequestsLocked` drops `m.mu` and loops sequentially; each
   `requestSessionSync` takes `m.sessionMu` and dials the socket.
4. If the helper accepts-but-does-not-respond, each request blocks on the 2s
   dial / 3s read deadline. A chunk of N requests → up to ~N×(2–3)s serially;
   thousands of keys → minutes. Even a fully-down helper (socket refused)
   produces thousands of sequential `socket/connect/close` syscalls + JSON
   encode + error logs per bulk op.

The calling goroutine (CLI/RPC session-clear handler) is blocked for the whole
duration, and `m.sessionMu` is held across every dial, serializing all other
session-sync writers behind it.

## Why it matters
Bulk session clear / policy invalidation during a hung-helper window can stall
the control plane for minutes, risking HA takeover deadlines and starving other
session installs on the shared control socket. (The existing #5096 chunking was
added to avoid monopolizing the socket, but it does not address per-request
dial-timeout amplification or fast-fail on a dead socket.)

## #5381 — userspace-dp: native GRE encap copies inner packet with redundant .to_vec() (extra per-packet heap alloc on egress path) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Summary
`encapsulate_native_gre_frame` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/gre.rs:837`) copies the
inner packet into a fresh heap `Vec` via `.to_vec()` even though every
subsequent use is read-only. The frame is then copied a second time into the
output buffer. This is a redundant per-packet heap allocation + copy on the
native GRE egress forwarding path.

## Evidence (current origin/master 9bfd48226)
```rust
let inner_packet = inner_frame.get(inner_l3..)?.to_vec();      // heap alloc + copy
let inner_len = packet_trimmed_len(&inner_packet, inner_meta.addr_family)?;
let inner_packet = &inner_packet[..inner_len];
...
let mut out = vec![0u8; frame_len];                            // 2nd alloc (the real frame)
...
out.get_mut(inner_start..)?.get_mut(..inner_packet.len())?
    .copy_from_slice(inner_packet);                            // copy inner -> out
```
`inner_packet` is only ever read (`packet_trimmed_len`, reslice,
`inner_tos_byte`, `.len()`, `copy_from_slice`) — never mutated — and
`inner_frame: &[u8]` outlives the function body, so the `.to_vec()` owner is
unnecessary.

## Fix direction
Borrow the slice directly:
```rust
let inner_packet = inner_frame.get(inner_l3..)?;
```
This removes one heap allocation + one memcpy per GRE-encapped packet. (Note:
the `out` buffer is still allocated; this is a reduction, not full zero-alloc.)

Severity is low — a per-packet micro-optimization on the native GRE egress path,
consistent with the project's hot-path no-allocation discipline.

Provenance: Gemini gemini-review-047, Medium; 3-gate triage.

`GetDHCPLeases` (`pkg/grpcapi/server_dhcp.go`) omits IPv6 delegated prefixes
(PD) from the response when the interface has **no** IA_NA leases (PD-only
delegation). The standalone PD lease entry is only appended when
`len(resp.Leases) > 0`, so a prefix-delegation-only interface reports an empty
lease table.

## Evidence (current origin/master 9bfd48226)

```go
        Interface:         dp.Interface,
        Family:            "inet6",

        DelegatedPrefixes: []*pb.DHCPDelegatedPrefix{pdInfo},
    })
}
```
When `resp.Leases` is empty (no IA_NA lease — legitimate for a PD-only client),
`attached` stays false and `len(resp.Leases) > 0` is false, so the PD entry is
silently dropped. The comment ("Create a standalone lease entry for PD-only")
shows the intent is to surface PD-only entries, which the `> 0` guard defeats.

Operators using prefix delegation without an IA_NA address see an empty DHCPv6
lease table, obscuring the delegated prefix during troubleshooting (vSRX/Junos
shows the delegated prefix). Display/observability parity gap, not a forwarding
bug.

Drop the `&& len(resp.Leases) > 0` constraint so a standalone PD entry is
appended whenever the prefix could not be attached to an existing lease:

```go
if !attached {
```

## #5389 — ddns/route53: UpsertLease bare full-RRset UPSERT clobbers foreign A/AAAA — Route53 arm of #3739 never implemented [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Summary

The Route 53 DDNS backend still clobbers co-resident/foreign `A`/`AAAA`
records at the published name. `route53Backend.UpsertLease` issues a bare
`ChangeResourceRecordSets` with `Action=UPSERT` and a **single-value**
resource-record set built by `buildChangeBatch` — Route 53 `UPSERT`
create-or-replaces the *entire* RRset at `name+type`, so any foreign value
(a manually configured round-robin address, or another host's A record at
the same FQDN) is silently deleted on the next publish/forced-refresh.

This is the exact Route 53 arm of #3739 (CLOSED), whose title explicitly
lists *"Route53 UPSERT replaces RRSet"* as one of the three clobber sites.
The Cloudflare arm was fixed (list-then-PATCH only the `PrevAddr`-matching
row) and the RFC2136 arm was fixed (value-specific `prevSelfOwnedRR`
delete), but **Route 53 was never actually fixed** — the ownership-safe
path was not implemented for it.

## Evidence (current origin/master 34dd996be)

`pkg/ddns/backend_route53.go`:
- `buildChangeBatch` (line ~133) appends only `rec.Addr` as the sole
  `ResourceRecord` value — no list/preserve of the existing RRset.
- `UpsertLease` (line ~191) → `change(ctx, "UPSERT", rec)` — bare UPSERT.
- `grep PrevAddr pkg/ddns/backend_route53.go` → **0 hits**, versus
  `backend_cloudflare.go` (lists then PATCHes the `prevContent` row) and
  `backend_rfc2136.go` (`prevSelfOwnedRR` value-specific delete).

## Trigger / trace

1. Operator has `wan.example.net A 198.51.100.20` (manually managed, or a

## #5390 — userspace-dp/filter: three-color policer per-packet Mutex is cross-worker shared — futex convoy caps line rate under configured policer [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

## Summary

The Junos three-color (tri-color marking) policer holds its token-bucket
state behind a `std::sync::Mutex` that is locked on **every metered
packet**, and the policer runtime is shared across worker threads via
`Arc<ThreeColorPolicerRuntime>`. When a filter with a three-color policer
term is applied to a high-rate interface, the RSS-spread flow aggregate
(6 combined RX queues → 6 workers on the mlx5 VF) all contend on the
single mutex per packet — a cross-worker futex convoy on the hot TX
selection / cache-hit replay path.

This violates the project's per-packet no-lock discipline (cf.
`shared_cos_lease` which is deliberately lock-free atomic for exactly this
reason) and can cap line-rate well below the configured policer rate under
load, undermining the CoS guarantee-guard (#4246).

## Evidence (current origin/master 34dd996be)

- `userspace-dp/src/filter/mod.rs:438` — `state: Mutex<ThreeColorPolicerState>`
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/mod.rs:585` `meter()` → `self.state.lock()`
  (line ~625), fail-closed to `Red{drop:true}` on poison (correct).
- Shared per-worker via `Arc<ThreeColorPolicerRuntime>`
  (`filter/mod.rs:254`, `CachedThreeColorPolicers` smallvec of `Arc`).
- Metered per packet on cache-hit replay:
  `afxdp/poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs:216`
  `apply_cached_three_color_policers(... .three_color_policers ...)` →
  `CachedThreeColorPolicers::for_each` → `meter()` per matched policer.

## Trigger / trace

1. Configure a Junos filter with a `three-color-policer` term on a filter
   bound to the WAN (reth0.80) output (or input) path.
2. Session established → flow-cache descriptor caches the
   `CachedThreeColorPolicers` (`Arc` clones of the shared runtime).
3. Every subsequent packet on the cache-hit fast path calls `meter()` →
   `state.lock()`. Flows for the same policer id landing on different RSS
   queues run on different workers → all serialize on one mutex.
4. At multi-Mpps aggregate the lock word + `Relaxed` counters share a
   cache line (no `#[repr(align(64))]` isolation), adding false-sharing to
   the contention; tail latency and drop rate spike, throughput falls

## #5410 — show route / REST /routes: installed static reject route is not labeled (renders as unlabeled/direct) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

Follow-up from the #5298 / PR #5409 hostile review (rev-5409). Two READ paths do not render an installed static `reject` route with its disposition, unlike `discard`:

**(a) REST `/routes` — no reject/discard label.** `pkg/api/routing.go:45` lumps a reject route into the `len(NextHops)==0` branch with no disposition label. A `discard` route hits the same branch, so neither is labeled. Behavior is unchanged by #5409 (the reject route already had zero next-hops), but now that reject routes are first-class (#5298) the REST view should distinguish `reject` / `discard` / directly-connected.

**(b) kernel-FIB reader maps only RTN_BLACKHOLE.** `pkg/routing/routes.go:238` maps only `RTN_BLACKHOLE`→`"discard"`. An installed reject route is `RTN_UNREACHABLE`, so in that kernel-table view it now renders as `"direct"` — misleading. This is a pre-existing reader gap that #5298 made newly reachable (reject routes now actually install into the kernel FIB as RTN_UNREACHABLE via FRR).

Fix direction: teach both readers the `RTN_UNREACHABLE`→`reject` mapping and surface a disposition label (reject/discard) in the REST `/routes` response, mirroring how `show route` (CLI/gRPC text) already renders it (cli_show_routing.go / server_show_routes_text.go handle reject correctly).

Non-functional / display-fidelity only — the forwarding behavior (drop the prefix) is correct. Low materiality.

## #5414 — dhcp-relay: chained-relay path trusts any nonzero-giaddr client's Option 82 (RFC 3046 §2.1 anti-spoofing not configurable) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

Follow-up from PR #5413 (#5071 chained-relay preservation), hostile review rev-5413 finding (out-of-scope, deferred in the #5413 commit/README).

**Gap.** After #5413, the relay preserves a downstream relay's giaddr + Option 82 whenever the inbound BOOTREQUEST carries a nonzero giaddr (`pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go` chained branch, ~:1172-1179). But nothing verifies the packet actually arrived from a trusted downstream relay: a host on the CLIENT segment can forge a nonzero giaddr + a crafted Option 82 and have it preserved as if downstream-authored. RFC 3046 §2.1 anti-spoofing (a relay should discard/replace Option 82 from an untrusted client, e.g. giaddr==0 on the client-facing interface, or an interface-trust flag) is not configurable today.

**Impact.** Low/medium: Option 82 spoofing can influence server-side policy/pool selection that keys on circuit-id/remote-id. Requires a host on the relay's client segment. The RFC-correct chaining behavior (#5071) is a prerequisite; this issue is the trust-policy layer on top.

**Fix direction.** Add a per-interface / per-relay Option-82 trust policy (Junos `forward-only` / `trusted` semantics): on an untrusted client-facing interface, discard a packet whose giaddr!=0 (or strip+replace its Option 82), rather than preserving it. Default should match vSRX (untrusted client unless the interface is configured as a relay uplink). Wire a config knob + commit-check + tests (trusted uplink preserves; untrusted client with forged giaddr is dropped/replaced).

**Related, lower-priority (same review):** on a chained flow, a NON-CONFORMANT server that unicasts its reply to the relay's UDP source instead of the BOOTP giaddr would hit `handleServerResponses` (relay.go ~:1357-1361), which unconditionally strips Option 82 + zeros giaddr. For a conformant server the reply goes to giaddr:67 (the downstream relay) and never traverses this relay, so it's correct in the common case; the degenerate path is pre-existing and non-conformant-server-only.

_provenance: rev-5413 hostile review of PR #5413, non-blocking follow-ups 1 & 2._

## #5428 — upgrade/kernel: isPkgInstalled false-on-query-error in the PRE-purge loop can skip purge and let the sweep delete package-owned files [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

Follow-up from PR #5427 (#5076) hostile review (rev-5427). PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by #5427.

**Gap.** `isPkgInstalled()` (pkg/upgrade/kernel_linux.go) returns `false` on ANY `dpkg-query` error. #5427 fixed the POST-purge desync (a failed `apt-get purge` no longer deletes package-owned files, and the manual sweep is gated on a per-package confirmed-absent re-query). But the PRE-purge query loop (kernel_linux.go ~:614-618) builds the `installed` set the SAME way: a false-negative there (dpkg-query errors while the package IS actually installed) yields an empty `installed` set → the purge is skipped → the sweep then deletes `/lib/modules/<candidate>` + `/boot/*-<candidate>` while dpkg still owns them — the same dpkg/file-divergence class #5076 was about, reached by a different trigger.

**Why LOW / why #5427 didn't fix it.** `dpkg-query -W` is a read-only status read that does NOT contend on the dpkg lock, so a false-negative requires dpkg-DB corruption — not the lock-contention / maintainer-script-failure path that hits `apt-get purge` (which #5427 now handles correctly). The pre-purge loop is byte-identical to HEAD~1; #5427 neither introduced nor worsened it. Severity LOW.

**Fix direction.** Make `pkgInstalled` TRI-STATE (installed / not-installed / query-error) and, on a query-error, FAIL SAFE: skip the sweep for that package (treat as possibly-installed) rather than treating it as removed. Mirror the post-purge confirmed-absent discipline #5427 added. Add a test injecting a dpkg-query error in the pre-purge loop and asserting the files are NOT swept.

_provenance: rev-5427 hostile review of PR #5427, MINOR pre-existing note._

## #5442 — config: add a commit-time strict reservation for the -xpf-chain BGP route-map suffix (parity with -xpf-redist) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

Follow-up from PR #5440 (#5277) hostile review (rev-5440). Non-blocking defense-in-depth / UX.

#5440 composes ordered BGP policy chains into FRR route-maps named with an `-xpf-chain` suffix, in the GLOBAL route-map namespace shared with operator-authored route-maps. It has a render-side collision guard (`bgpComposedChainCollision`, runs in ApplyFull before buildManagedSection) that FAILS CLOSED — an operator-named route-map colliding with a composed `-xpf-chain` name (or a delimiter-join ambiguity where two distinct chains derive the same name) causes the whole managed-section apply to fail (FRR keeps last-good, no leak). So security is airtight.

**Gap (UX/defense-in-depth):** unlike the `-xpf-redist` reserved suffix — which has a COMMIT-TIME strict validator `validatePolicyReservedRedistNameStrict` (pkg/config) IN ADDITION to its render-side guard — the `-xpf-chain` suffix has NO commit-time strict reservation. So an operator who names a policy/route-map to collide gets a late, opaque whole-section APPLY failure instead of a clean `commit check` rejection at commit time.

**Fix direction.** Add a parity commit-time strict gate `validatePolicyReservedChainNameStrict` (mirroring `validatePolicyReservedRedistNameStrict`) that rejects an operator route-map/policy name that would collide with the reserved `-xpf-chain` composed-name namespace at commit-check time, so the operator gets an immediate, clear error rather than a deferred apply failure. Also (NIT, same area) clean up the stale comment at pkg/frr/policy_render.go:993 that references the now-removed `bgpEffectiveExport`.

Low severity — already fails closed; this is commit-time UX parity + a stale-comment cleanup.

_provenance: rev-5440 hostile review of PR #5440, non-blocking minors 1 & 2._

## #5444 — userspace-dp/filter: merge_matched_modifiers heap-clones policer/routing-instance String per matched term on the eval hot path [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Defect
`merge_matched_modifiers` runs on the per-packet firewall-filter eval hot path and heap-clones two `String` fields (`policer_name`, `routing_instance`) plus an `Arc<str>` (`forwarding_class`) for every matched term.

`userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/eval.rs` (current origin/master 845ba6d8):
```rust
#[inline]
fn merge_matched_modifiers(acc: &mut FilterResult, filter: &Filter, term: &FilterTerm) {
    if term.dscp_rewrite.is_some() { acc.dscp_rewrite = term.dscp_rewrite; }
    if !term.policer_name.is_empty()      { acc.policer_name = term.policer_name.clone(); }      // String heap alloc
    if !term.routing_instance.is_empty()  { acc.routing_instance = term.routing_instance.clone(); } // String heap alloc
    if !term.forwarding_class.is_empty()  { acc.forwarding_class = term.forwarding_class.clone(); } // Arc LOCK XADD
    ...
}
```
`FilterResult` (`filter/mod.rs:839-841`) stores `policer_name: String`, `routing_instance: String`, `forwarding_class: Arc<str>`. `forwarding-class` assignment is common in CoS configs, so the `Arc` atomic refcount bump (contended cacheline when many workers hit the same term) fires on typical traffic; policer/routing-instance terms add per-packet heap allocations.

## Invariant / basis
`poll_descriptor` is a documented zero-alloc-per-packet path (`docs/engineering-style.md` hot-path allocation rule). Per-packet heap allocation jitters tail latency, fragments the allocator, and can pressure memory under a filter-matching flood.

## Fix direction
Change `policer_name`/`routing_instance` in the hot `FilterResult` to `Arc<str>` (or an interned id) so a match is a refcount bump, not a heap alloc; for `forwarding_class` (already `Arc`) compare pointer before cloning to skip the atomic when unchanged. Keep `String` storage in the cold `FilterTerm`. Prove hot code unchanged with a release-build disassembly diff.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A1_rust_dataplane_packet-b3 F1]. Not a duplicate of #5390 (policer Mutex convoy) — distinct allocation path in the eval merge.

**Dataplane change** — code driveable but final verify (`cargo test --release` + loss-cluster smoke / `make test-failover`) is lab-bound on #5364.

## #5445 — userspace-dp/session: per-packet SessionMetadata.clone() does a LOCK XADD on the policy_counter Arc (reintroduces the #919 atomic on the lookup hot path) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Defect
Every per-packet established-session lookup clones `SessionMetadata` by value, and that clone does a `LOCK XADD` atomic on the `Arc<PolicyRuleCounter>` it carries.

`userspace-dp/src/session/entry.rs` — `SessionMetadata` is `#[derive(Clone)]` and holds:
```rust
pub(crate) policy_counter: Option<std::sync::Arc<crate::policy::PolicyRuleCounter>>, // #3322 bound counter handle
```
`SessionLookup { decision, metadata: SessionMetadata }` embeds it by value, and `session/lookup.rs` clones it on the hot lookup paths:
```
lookup.rs:183  metadata: entry.metadata.clone(),
lookup.rs:240  metadata: entry.metadata.clone(),
lookup.rs:281  metadata: entry.metadata.clone(),
lookup.rs:321  .map(|entry| (entry.decision, entry.metadata.clone(), entry.origin))
```
When `policy_counter` is `Some` (the common case — most rules have a counter), each packet on an established flow does an atomic refcount bump on a counter `Arc` shared across workers for the same rule → contended-cacheline ping-pong at 16+ workers. The comment at entry.rs:22 (#919) states the hot/cold zone split was done specifically to "eliminate the `LOCK XADD` atomic on every `metadata.clone()`" — the #3322 `policy_counter` Arc reintroduced exactly that atomic.

## Invariant / basis
Per-packet lookup on the fast path must not do an atomic refcount bump on a globally-shared cacheline (`docs/engineering-style.md` hot-path / data-oriented rule). This is the ~10ns/lookup regression called out for entry.rs.

## Fix direction
Data-oriented split of `SessionMetadata` into a Copy-able hot part (ingress/egress zone u16, owner_rg_id, is_reverse, fabric_ingress) returned by the fast lookup, and a cold part (policy_counter, log flags, policy_id, timeouts, nat64_reverse) cloned only on install / HA sync. Alternatively resolve the hit counter by index in the fast path and keep the bound `Arc` out of the per-packet clone. Prove hot code unchanged with a release disassembly diff; failover-gate (cluster-deploy + test-failover) since HA sync carries the cold part.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A1_rust_dataplane_packet-b3 F3].

**Dataplane change** — code driveable but final verify (`cargo test --release` + loss-cluster smoke / `make test-failover`) is lab-bound on #5364.

## #5446 — userspace-dp/NAT: HA reserve_flow marks deterministic-CGNAT/NAT64 synced flows as non-deterministic → recycle-queue leak on standby [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

## Defect
On a standby node, HA-synced deterministic-CGNAT / deterministic-NAT64 flows are reserved via `reserve_flow`, which unconditionally records the allocation as `deterministic: false`. On teardown the release path then recycles the port, but deterministic pools never drain the recycle queue → unbounded growth + a determinism-semantics mismatch.

`userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs`:
```rust
pub(super) fn reserve_flow(&self, flow, translated, addr_index) -> bool {
    ...
    live.live_by_flow.insert(flow, LiveAllocation {
        translated, persistent_key: None, addr_index,
        deterministic: false,   // <-- always false, even for deterministic pools
        address_only: false,
    });
    true
}
```
Release (`allocator.rs` ~1285):
```rust
self.free_translated_port(existing.addr_index, translated.port, !existing.deterministic);
// deterministic == false  =>  free_recycle == true  =>  port pushed onto per-address recycle VecDeque
```
The deterministic allocation path (`allocate_deterministic_v4/v6` via `reserve()` bitmap CAS) never calls `claim()`, so it never drains the recycle queue. Both `reserve_synced_source_nat_allocation` and `reserve_synced_nat64_allocation` go through `reserve_flow`. Under HA churn of deterministic flows the recycle `VecDeque` grows without bound (memory leak) and freed deterministic ports are queued but never reused.

## Invariant / basis
Deterministic pool ports must be freed `free_no_recycle` (they are re-derivable from the block calc, not recyclable). #4559 established this for the local allocate path; the HA reserve path violates it.

## Fix direction
Thread the deterministic flag into `reserve_flow` (or a `reserve_flow_deterministic` variant) and have the HA reserve callers pass `deterministic = true` when the source-NAT rule / NAT64 prefix is deterministic, so release stays `free_no_recycle`.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A2_rust_dataplane_nat-b1 F1]. Distinct from #5341 / #5338 (address-only token minting) — this is a deterministic-pool recycle-queue leak.

**Dataplane change** — code driveable but final verify (`cargo test --release` + loss-cluster smoke / `make test-failover`) is lab-bound on #5364.

## #5447 — userspace-dp/NAT64: fragment-association cache install evicts oldest live entry without pruning expired first → legit non-first fragments dropped under frag flood [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-17)

## Defect
The NAT64 fragment-association cache evicts the oldest entry on cap without first pruning expired ones, so a first-fragment flood with many IDs can evict still-live associations, causing legitimate non-first fragments to fail closed (dropped).

`userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs`:
```rust
const NAT64_FRAG_CAP_PER_SHARD: usize = 64;
pub(crate) fn install(&self, ...) {
    ...
    if shard.len() >= NAT64_FRAG_CAP_PER_SHARD {
        shard.remove(0);            // evicts OLDEST live entry, ignoring expiry
    }
    shard.push(...);
}
// lookup() (nat64.rs:473) does prune expired: shard.retain(|e| e.deadline_ns > now_ns);
```
Only `lookup` prunes expired entries; there is no background GC. Under a burst of first fragments (each installs) toward many IDs, expired entries occupy slots until a lookup happens to hit the same shard, so `install` evicts a live association prematurely. Legitimate non-first fragments for the evicted flow then hit the #4617 fail-closed drop.

## Fix direction
In `install`, run `shard.retain(|e| e.deadline_ns > now_ns)` (or count only live entries) before the cap check. Cost is O(64) per install, on the first-fragment path (not per-packet hot).

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A2_rust_dataplane_nat-b1 F2]. Not in dedup index.

**Dataplane change** — code driveable but final verify (`cargo test --release` + loss-cluster smoke / `make test-failover`) is lab-bound on #5364.

## #5448 — dataplane/session_store: batchDeleteV4/V6 drops the unattempted chunk tail on a missing key → stale HA-synced sessions leak after bulk reconcile [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-13)

## Defect
`batchDeleteV4`/`batchDeleteV6` in the cluster-bulk session store discard the not-yet-attempted tail of a chunk when the kernel batch-delete stops on a missing key, so those sessions are never retried and stale peer-synced sessions leak.

`pkg/dataplane/session_store.go`:
```go
func (s dataPlaneSessionStore) batchDeleteV4(keys []SessionKey) (int, error) {
    deleted := 0
    for len(keys) > 0 {
        n := sessionDeleteBatchSize
        if len(keys) < n { n = len(keys) }
        chunkDeleted, err := s.dp.BatchDeleteSessions(keys[:n])
        deleted += chunkDeleted
        if err := ignoreSessionNotFound(err); err != nil { return deleted, err }
        keys = keys[n:]          // drops keys[chunkDeleted:n] — never retried
    }
    return deleted, nil
}
```
cilium/ebpf `BatchDelete` stops at the first missing key and returns `(count_before_stop, ErrKeyNotExist)`. `clearSessionsV4` in `pkg/dataplane/maps_session.go` handles this correctly (per-key fallback on `chunk[cnt:]` before advancing), proving the author knew the semantics — but the `session_store` path masks the error via `ignoreSessionNotFound` and advances by the full `n`, skipping `keys[chunkDeleted:n]`.

## Impact
`DeleteBatchKnownV4/V6` feeds `ReconcileClusterBulk` (HA bulk stale-session cleanup). A single missing key mid-chunk aborts deletion of the rest of that chunk → stale peer-synced sessions survive bulk resync, inflating the session table and delaying GC after churn.

## Fix direction
Mirror `clearSessionsV4`: on `ErrKeyNotExist`, fall back to per-key `DeleteSession` for `chunk[chunkDeleted:n]` (or re-slice to retry the tail) before advancing. Add a test with interleaved missing keys.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A6_go_dataplane_manager-b1 F1]. Distinct from the full-table clear path (legacy_dataplane batch-clear).

## #5449 — dataplane/userspace inject: slot parsed with Atoi + cast to uint32 with no negative/range check → -1 wraps to 4294967295 (OOB slot) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect
The userspace-dp packet-inject CLI parses the binding slot with `strconv.Atoi` and casts straight to `uint32` with no negative/range check, so `slot -1` wraps to `4294967295`; the default source-port derivation then truncates it to `uint16`.

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/inject.go`:
```go
slotNum, err := strconv.Atoi(args[2])   // accepts "-1"
...
slot = uint32(slotNum)                   // -1 -> 4294967295
...
sourcePort := uint16(req.Slot)           // 4294967295 -> 65535
```
`ParseInjectPacketCommand` → `BuildInjectPacketRequest` forwards the wrapped slot with no range guard (`validateInjectPacketRequestForHelper` checks emit-on-wire, not slot range). Operator gRPC `request chassis cluster data-plane userspace inject-packet slot -1 ...` produces an out-of-range slot / wrong-queue selection.

## Invariant / basis
A binding slot must be in `[0, MaxBindings)`; a negative or oversized value must be rejected, not silently wrapped (matches the `#2443` inject-length `u16::try_from` fail-closed posture on the helper side).

## Fix direction
Parse with `strconv.ParseUint(args[2], 10, 32)` (or reject `slotNum < 0`) and bound against the binding cap before building the request; return a clear error instead of wrapping.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A6_go_dataplane_manager-b2 F1/F4].

## #5450 — cluster/session-sync: delete-journal overflow evicts oldest deletes with no forced re-reconcile → standby retains stale sessions after long partition [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Defect
On a full/disconnected send stream, `rejournalTail` evicts the oldest queued session-delete records to stay under `deleteJournalCap`. Dropped deletes are counted (`DeletesDropped`) but not otherwise recovered, so the standby retains sessions the primary already closed until the next full bulk reconcile.

`pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go` `rejournalTail`:
```go
dropped := total - capN
s.stats.DeletesDropped.Add(uint64(dropped))
merged := make([][]byte, 0, capN)
if dropped < len(tail) {
    merged = append(merged, tail[dropped:]...)   // oldest deletes evicted
    merged = append(merged, s.deleteJournal...)
} else { ... }
```
## Impact
Under an extended control-link partition with high session churn, the delete journal overflows and evicts deletes for sessions already closed on the primary. Those stale sessions remain on the standby (reconciliation only happens at `BulkEnd`; a re-primed reconnect skips bulk). On takeover the standby forwards into dead flows or hits `MaxSessions` until GC/next bulk.

## Fix direction
When `DeletesDropped` increments (or crosses a threshold), force a reconciliation delta / bulk re-sync on the next reconnect instead of relying on the next natural bulk; and/or surface `DeletesDropped > 0` in cluster status so operators see divergence. Sizing the journal to expected churn is a secondary mitigation.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A5_go_ha_vrrp_ra_conntrack-b1 H2]. Not a duplicate of #5303 (accept-loop admission cap).

## #5451 — daemon/HA: warmNeighborCache opens one UDP socket per unique session IP with no cap → FD/port exhaustion + failover stall at CGNAT scale [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-13)

## Defect
On failover, `warmNeighborCache` opens one UDP socket per unique session IP with no cap or pacing, so a large session table triggers a burst of tens of thousands of `DialTimeout` calls that can exhaust ephemeral ports / file descriptors and delay failover convergence.

`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go`:
```go
func (d *Daemon) warmNeighborCache() {
    seen := ... // bounded only by session-table size
    _ = d.dp.Sessions().ForEachV4(func(key, val) bool {
        if !seen[key.DstIP] { seen[key.DstIP] = true }
        if !seen[key.SrcIP] { seen[key.SrcIP] = true }
        ...
    })
    for ip4 := range seen {
        conn, err := net.DialTimeout("udp4", netip.AddrPortFrom(addr, 1).String(), 50*time.Millisecond)  // no cap
        ...
    }
    // same for udp6
}
```
With ~50k unique destinations (CGNAT scale) this fires ~50k dials in a tight loop on the new primary right when failover latency matters.

## Impact
FD / ephemeral-port exhaustion and a multi-second stall on the failover critical path (this runs only on failover, but that is the worst time for a local resource storm).

## Fix direction
Cap the number of warmed IPs (e.g. first N=1024) and/or pace in small batches; or replace the UDP-dial storm with a lighter netlink neighbor probe (`RTM_GETNEIGH` / the existing `SendARPProbe` / ND-solicit path already used by `cleanFailedNeighbors`).

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A7_go_daemon_host-b1 H-2]. Distinct from #5288 (per-packet neighbor open) — this is a per-failover bulk dial.

## #5452 — upgrade/kernel: candidate version + uname string unsanitized in /boot Glob→RemoveAll and GRUB slot-selector → arbitrary /boot deletion + GRUB injection [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect (HIGH)
The kernel A/B upgrade channel uses the candidate kernel version and `uname -r` string directly in a `filepath.Glob` + `os.RemoveAll` loop and in the GRUB slot-selector script, with **no** `ValidateVersionSegment` (or equivalent safe-segment) check anywhere on the kernel-arm path. A version containing glob metacharacters, quotes, or newlines yields arbitrary `/boot` deletion and/or GRUB-script injection.

`pkg/upgrade/kernel_linux.go` — `PruneInactiveSlot`:
```go
if matches, err := filepath.Glob(s.rooted(filepath.Join("/boot", "*-"+candidateVersion))); err == nil {
    for _, match := range matches {
        if err := os.RemoveAll(match); err != nil { ... }   // deletes whatever the glob matched
    }
}
os.RemoveAll(s.rooted(filepath.Join("/lib/modules", candidateVersion)))
// apt package names: "linux-image-"+candidateVersion, "linux-modules-"+candidateVersion, ...
```
`WriteSlotSelector`:
```go
content := fmt.Sprintf("set xpf_slot_kernel=\"vmlinuz-%s\"\nset xpf_slot_initrd=\"initrd.img-%s\"\n", unameR, unameR)
```
`kernel_run.go` `Arm` only checks `candidateVersion == ""`; a grep for `ValidateVersionSegment` across `pkg/upgrade/kernel*.go` and the gRPC handler returns **nothing** — the kernel candidate is never validated the way binary-cut versions (`versions/<ver>`) are.

## Failure scenarios
- `candidateVersion = "*"` → glob `/boot/*-*` matches every dashed `/boot` file → `RemoveAll` deletes kernels/initrds/config → unbootable host (data loss).
- `unameR` containing `"` or `\n` → injects extra directives into the GRUB slot-selector `.cfg` → boot-selector parse break / boot failure.
- `candidateVersion` containing `..` → path traversal in `filepath.Join("/lib/modules", candidateVersion)` RemoveAll.

Reached via `xpfd upgrade kernel arm <ver>` and journal replay. Even though arm is operator-gated (super-user), the #1930 kernel channel is shipped/live and a malformed or replayed journal value should never be able to wipe `/boot` or corrupt GRUB — defense-in-depth on a destructive, boot-critical path.

## Fix direction
Call `ValidateVersionSegment` (or a stricter kernel-version regex, e.g. `^[0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*$`) at `Arm`/preflight entry and re-assert in `PruneInactiveSlot`/`WriteSlotSelector` before any filesystem/GRUB use; replace `filepath.Glob` with an `os.ReadDir` + exact-suffix filter, and reject versions containing `"`/`\n` for the selector.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A7_go_daemon_host-b3 H2/H3].

## #5453 — snmp/v3: rand.Read error ignored when generating privacy salt → predictable/zero IV on entropy failure (RFC 3414 §8.2.1) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect (HIGH — confidentiality)
The SNMPv3 privacy encrypt paths ignore the error return from `crypto/rand.Read` when generating the per-message salt. If the RNG fails (e.g. `getrandom` `EAGAIN` at early boot, or a FIPS module error), `privParams` stays all-zero and a predictable/deterministic IV is used, breaking semantic security of the encrypted PDU.

`pkg/snmp/v3.go`:
```go
// encryptDES (~797)
privParams := make([]byte, 8)
rand.Read(privParams)              // error ignored -> stays zero on failure
iv := make([]byte, 8)
for i := range iv { iv[i] = preIV[i] ^ privParams[i] }   // zero salt -> IV = preIV (derived from long-term privKey)

// encryptAES128 (~821)
privParams := make([]byte, 8)
rand.Read(privParams)              // error ignored
iv := make([]byte, 16)
binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(iv[0:4], uint32(boots))
binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(iv[4:8], uint32(time))
copy(iv[8:16], privParams)         // zero salt -> only boots|time distinguishes IVs
```
DES: zero salt makes the CBC IV a deterministic function of the long-term key → repeated-plaintext-prefix leakage across messages. AES: with a zeroed salt the last 8 IV bytes are constant, so IVs repeat for messages sent in the same (boots, time) second → CFB IV reuse. Violates RFC 3414 §8.2.1 (privacy salt MUST be unpredictable). #1710 fixed auth-param locating, not this RNG error path.

## Fix direction
Check the `rand.Read` error in both `encryptDES` and `encryptAES128`; on failure return `nil` so `buildV3Response` fails closed (downgrade/omit priv) rather than emitting a message with a predictable IV. Add a test injecting an RNG failure.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A9_go_observability-b1 HIGH].

## #5454 — grpcapi/ClearSessions: filtered clear path allocates all matching keys (O(N), unbounded) before deleting — fabric-allowed memory DoS [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect
The filtered `ClearSessions` gRPC path materializes every matching session key into unbounded slices before deleting, giving O(N) handler-goroutine allocation (N up to the full session table). `ClearSessions` is in `fabricAllowedUnaryMethods`, so a PSK-holding peer can trigger it.

`pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go`:
```go
var v4Keys []dataplane.SessionKey
var v4RevKeys []dataplane.SessionKey
var snatDNATKeys []dataplane.DNATKey
agg.add("v4 iterate", s.dp.IterateSessions(func(key, val) bool {
    if !filter.matchV4(key, val) { return true }
    v4Keys = append(v4Keys, key)                    // unbounded
    if val.ReverseKey.Protocol != 0 { v4RevKeys = append(v4RevKeys, val.ReverseKey) }
    if val.Flags&SessFlagSNAT != 0 && val.Flags&SessFlagStaticNAT == 0 {
        snatDNATKeys = append(snatDNATKeys, DNATKeyForSessionV4(key, val))
    }
    return true
}))
for _, key := range v4Keys { s.dp.DeleteSession(key) ... }
```
With a multi-million-session table, a filter matching most sessions retains hundreds of MB of keys (v4Keys + v4RevKeys + DNAT companions) before the delete loop runs. The legacy clear-all path uses bulk atomic clear; the filtered path does not stream.

## Impact
Control-plane memory pressure / GC pause / potential OOM during a bulk filtered clear; a compromised fabric peer (PSK) amplifies it to a DoS of the primary.

## Fix direction
Delete as you match inside the iteration callback, or process fixed-size batches (e.g. 1k keys) with a ctx-cancel check between batches, so handler memory is O(batch) not O(matches). Mirror the bounded cursor pattern used by `getSessionsCursor`.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A8_go_api_grpc_rest-b2 A8-01]. Not a duplicate of #5303/#5305 (session-sync caps).

## #5455 — config/tcp-flags: operator-only/trailing '&' or '()' returns no-constraint with no error → firewall term silently matches all TCP (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect
`ParseTCPFlagsExpression` returns `(0, 0, false, nil)` — i.e. "no constraint", **no error** — for operator-only / empty-operand tcp-flags expressions such as `"&"`, `"()"`, or a trailing `"syn &"`. The strict validator only rejects on `err != nil`, so a malformed tcp-flags value commits and the term silently matches all TCP traffic (fail-open widening of a security filter).

`pkg/config/tcp_flags.go`:
```go
func ParseTCPFlagsExpression(parts []string) (required, forbidden uint8, ok bool, err error) {
    ...
    case "&": ... continue        // operator with no flag operand: no error
    case "(", ")": ... continue
    ...
    if required == 0 && forbidden == 0 {
        return 0, 0, false, nil   // treated as "absent constraint"
    }
    return required, forbidden, true, nil
}
```
Caller (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:123`):
```go
if _, _, _, err := ParseTCPFlagsExpression(term.TCPFlags); err != nil { ... }  // err==nil for "&" -> accepted
```
`"&"` → `["&"]` → loop continues → `required==0 && forbidden==0` → `ok=false, err=nil`. `"syn &"` → returns SYN only, silently dropping the trailing `&`. #4714 rejected a dangling `!` but not a dangling/empty `&` or `()`.

## Impact
A typo like `from tcp-flags "&"` or `"syn &"` (common when editing `syn & ack` down to one flag) commits with no diagnostic and the intended SYN-only / no-SYN match is dropped — the term matches any TCP, weakening the firewall filter.

## Fix direction
When the token list is non-empty but no flag bits were set, return an error ("empty/operator-only tcp-flags expression"); reject leading/trailing/duplicated `&`. Add cases: `{"&"} wantErr`, `{"()"} wantErr`, `{"syn","&"} wantErr`.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A3_go_config_cli_tree-b4 F1]. Not #4714 (`!` dangling).

## #5456 — config/firewall: FilterTermExpansionCount uint32 product overflows on large prefix-list cross-product → counter-stride wrap + commit-time expansion DoS [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect
`FilterTermExpansionCount` computes a firewall-filter term's rule-expansion count as `int` products then casts to `uint32`, with no overflow check. A large prefix-list cross-product can exceed 2^32-1, wrapping the counter stride, and the same unbounded product drives term expansion (CPU/memory).

`pkg/config/firewall_filter_expand.go`:
```go
func FilterTermExpansionCount(term *FirewallFilterTerm, prefixLists map[string]*PrefixList) uint32 {
    nSrc := ...        // len(SourceAddresses) + prefix-list prefixes
    nDst := ...
    nDstPorts := ...
    nSrcPorts := ...
    return uint32(nSrc * nDst * nDstPorts * nSrcPorts)   // int product -> uint32 truncation
}
```
With e.g. `nSrc=5000, nDst=5000, nDstPorts=100, nSrcPorts=100` the product is 2.5e11 > 4.29e9, so `uint32(...)` wraps. The count is the per-term counter stride: a wrapped value makes `show firewall filter` read into neighbouring terms' counter slots (unbounded drift). The drift-guard test pins `FilterTermExpansionCount == len(expandFilterTerm)` but does not assert the product stays < 2^32, so both can wrap identically and still mis-report.

## Impact
Incorrect firewall counter accounting under large prefix-list terms; potential high CPU / memory during commit-time term expansion (config-driven DoS).

## Fix direction
Compute the product in `uint64` (or `int64`), reject / clamp when it exceeds a max expansion (e.g. a configurable cap, and > MaxUint32 always) with a strict-gate error, and keep the drift-guard test asserting the bound.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A3_go_config_cli_tree-b2 H1]. Not in dedup index (#3459 is the stride SSOT, not overflow).

## #5457 — config/NAT: parseSourcePoolPortRange accepts out-of-range/inverted source-pool port ranges (no 1..65535 or low<=high check) on the lenient path [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect
`parseSourcePoolPortRange` accepts NAT source-pool port ranges via `strconv.Atoi` with no value-range check (must be 1..65535) and no low≤high order check, so malformed ranges pass on the lenient/tolerant compile path (HA config-sync, `#1960` downgrade) and get stamped into the pool.

`pkg/config/compiler_nat_source.go`:
```go
func parseSourcePoolPortRange(toks []string) (low, high int, ok bool) {
    if len(toks) >= 4 && toks[0] == "low" && toks[2] == "high" {
        lo, err1 := strconv.Atoi(toks[1])
        hi, err2 := strconv.Atoi(toks[3])
        if err1 != nil || err2 != nil { return 0, 0, false }
        return lo, hi, true            // no 1..65535 bound, no lo<=hi
    }
    ...
    return lo, hi, true
}
```
`port [ low -1 high 99999 ]` → returns `(-1, 99999, true)`; `low 5000 high 100` → `(5000, 100, true)` (inverted/empty range). On the tolerant path (HA sync / `compileTreeLenient`) the strict validator's warning does not hard-fail, so an out-of-range or inverted source-pool port range can reach the dataplane snapshot.

## Invariant / basis
Port values are 1..65535 and ranges must be non-decreasing; the parser should fail closed (`ok=false`) on violation so the strict gate rejects and the lenient path skips (matches `canonicalPort` / `ParseCanonicalUint` used elsewhere in the NAT/appid compilers).

## Fix direction
Validate each token via `ParseCanonicalUint` (rejects sign / >65535) and enforce `lo <= hi`; return `ok=false` on failure. Add a unit test for negative, >65535, and reversed ranges.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A3_go_config_cli_tree-b1 H1/M1].

## #5458 — config/secret: RedactURL leaves user:pass@ userinfo unredacted for schemeless URLs → credential leak in logs [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-10)

## Defect
`Secret.RedactURL` only redacts `user:pass@` userinfo when the string contains `://`. A schemeless URL with credentials (e.g. `user:pass@example.com/update?token=…`) has its userinfo left intact in log output — the query is redacted but the credentials are not.

`pkg/config/secret.go`:
```go
func RedactURL(s string) string {
    const redacted = "<redacted>"
    if i := strings.Index(s, "://"); i >= 0 {
        ...
        if at := strings.LastIndex(authority, "@"); at >= 0 {
            s = s[:authStart] + redacted + "@" + authority[at+1:] + s[authEnd:]   // only inside the :// branch
        }
    }
    if q := strings.IndexByte(s, '?'); q >= 0 { s = s[:q+1] + redacted }
    return s
}
```
For `user:pass@host/x?token=SECRET` (no `://`) the first branch is skipped, so `user:pass@` survives in the redacted string; only the query is masked.

## Impact
Credential leak into journald / exported logs. The DDNS generic-backend provider URL is untyped (no scheme validator at commit), so a schemeless URL with userinfo can be configured and then logged via `RedactURL`.

## Fix direction
Redact userinfo even without a scheme: locate the last `@` before the first `/ ? #` and mask the preceding userinfo; or add a commit-time `ValidateURL` requiring a scheme for provider URLs.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A3_go_config_cli_tree-b3 F1].

## Defect
The remote CLI `show chassis cluster <subsystem> <arg>` dispatch silently falls back to the statistics/status view for an unknown `<arg>` instead of erroring, so operator typos return a valid-looking result with exit 0.

`cmd/cli/show.go`:

```go
case "control-plane":
    if len(args) >= 4 && args[3] == "statistics" {
        return c.showText("chassis-cluster-control-plane-statistics")
    }
    return c.showText("chassis-cluster-control-plane-statistics")   // any unknown arg -> statistics
case "data-plane":

```

Compare the strict `show services ip-monitoring` handler (`show_services.go`), which rejects an unknown subcommand with an error (#1827) — Junos parity is to error on an unrecognized token, not silently show something else.

Return a usage/error for an unrecognized subcommand token; only render statistics/status when explicitly requested.

## #5460 — bpf/headers: SESS_FLAG_NPTV6 (1<<8)=256 overflows the __u8 session_value.flags field (latent ABI bug) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Defect
`SESS_FLAG_NPTV6` is defined as `(1 << 8)` = 256, but the `session_value.flags` field it belongs to is `__u8`, so the constant does not fit the field — any attempt to set it truncates to 0 (colliding with "no flags").

`bpf/headers/xpf_common.h`:
```c
#define SESS_FLAG_NAT64        (1 << 7)   // 128 — fits u8
#define SESS_FLAG_NPTV6        (1 << 8)   // 256 — overflows u8
```
`bpf/headers/xpf_conntrack.h` (session_value, both v4 and v6):
```c
__u8  flags;           /* SESS_FLAG_* */
```
The flag is currently referenced nowhere else (grep across `bpf/`, `userspace-dp/`, `pkg/` finds only its own `#define`), and the NPTv6 eBPF path was retired in #1476 — so this is a latent/dead constant. But if NPTv6 session flagging is ever re-enabled it silently becomes 0.

## Fix direction
Either widen the session flags field to `__u16` (with the corresponding Go/Rust ABI mirror + size-assert bump), or redefine `SESS_FLAG_NPTV6` to an unused bit ≤ `(1<<7)` that fits `__u8`, or delete the dead constant and document that NPTv6 uses a separate field.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A10_go_services_cli_deploy-b1]. Latent ABI defect in the retained shim headers.

## #5461 — routing/xfrm: Apply falls through to LinkAdd on ANY LinkByName error (vs vrf.go isLinkNotFound) → spurious EEXIST commit failure on transient netlink error [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect
`xfrm.go` treats any error from `LinkByName` as "not present" and falls through to the create path, unlike `vrf.go` which distinguishes a transient lookup error (`isLinkNotFound`) and retains ownership. On a transient error for an interface that actually exists, xfrm attempts `LinkAdd` → `EEXIST` → spurious fail-closed commit error, leaving the interface desired-but-untracked.

`pkg/routing/xfrm.go` (~167):
```go
if link, err := x.ops.LinkByName(ifName); err == nil {
    // adopt/reuse existing xfrmi
    ...
}
// any err != nil (incl. transient EBUSY/EINVAL/netlink transport) falls through to LinkAdd create
```
`pkg/routing/vrf.go` has the correct pattern:
```go
func isLinkNotFound(err error) bool { ... }   // vrf.go:155
// retains ownership on transient (non-not-found) errors
```

## Impact
A transient netlink error during commit spuriously fails the commit (EEXIST on an existing xfrmi) instead of retaining and retrying, even though the interface is fine. Self-heals on the next tick, but the commit legitimately shouldn't fail.

## Fix direction
Extract `isLinkNotFound` into a shared routing helper and use it in `xfrm.go` Apply/Clear: only take the create path when the error is genuinely "link not found"; retain ownership (and let the next reconcile retry) on transient errors.

## Provenance
claude-review-002 [A7_go_daemon_host-b3 H1].

## #5466 — userspace-dp: in-place descriptor rewrite mutates frame (eth header + VLAN-push memmove) before its fragment/port fallback None — generic fallback reprocesses a corrupted frame [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-17)

**Defect**

`apply_rewrite_descriptor` (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/rewrite/mod.rs:53) is not transactional. It calls `rewrite_prepare_eth_from_parts` (frame/mod.rs:520), which **mutates UMEM** — it writes the Ethernet header (`write_eth_header_slice`) and, in the VLAN-push-no-headroom / unsupported-memmove case, does `frame.copy_within(l3..source_end, eth_len)` (a payload memmove) — **before** the descriptor fast path can still bail to `None`:

- the non-first-fragment gate (`if ip < packet.len() && is_non_first_fragment(...) { return None; }`, mod.rs:~99) returns None *after* prepare_eth already moved the payload, and
- the DMA-race port-mismatch guard in `apply_rewrite_descriptor_ipv4`/`_ipv6` returns None after prepare_eth ran.

The caller (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs:411) chains `apply_rewrite_descriptor(...).or_else(|| rewrite_forwarded_frame_in_place(...))`, so on any of those None paths the **generic fallback runs on the already-mutated frame**. When prepare_eth performed a VLAN-push memmove, the payload has been relocated (e.g. old l3=14 → eth_len=18); the generic fallback re-reads the original `meta.l3_offset` and re-derives from a frame whose L3/payload is no longer where it expects → corrupted/double-rewritten egress frame. (Note: `apply_rewrite_descriptor_ipv4/ipv6` themselves DO validate before their L3/L4 writes, so the corruption source is specifically the prepare_eth pre-mutation, not the L3/L4 writes.)

Secondary: the fast path retains an immutable `packet_frame: &[u8]` alias into the same UMEM that `slice_mut_unchecked` then writes through — the finding also flags this as an aliasing-contract violation across the mutation.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/rewrite/mod.rs:53-140 (`apply_rewrite_descriptor`, fragment/port None gates); userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/mod.rs:520-586 (`rewrite_prepare_eth_from_parts`, copy_within + write_eth_header before return); caller userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs:411 (`.or_else` fallback).

**Invariant:** A fallible in-place transform must be transactional w.r.t. packet bytes — a `None` (fall-back) result must leave the source frame byte-identical so the generic fallback re-derives from clean state.

**Fix direction:** Run all fallback-triggering validation (non-first-fragment, port match, L2-rewrite feasibility) BEFORE any mutation in prepare_eth; or perform the rewrite on a private copy and commit to UMEM only on success; do not memmove/rewrite L2 ahead of the fragment/port gates.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A1/C179-007], High confidence.

Dataplane change — code driveable but final verify (cargo test --release + loss-cluster smoke/test-failover) is lab-bound on #5364.

## #5467 — userspace-dp/tx: flowless packets (non-first fragments, non-query ICMP) return from CoS TX classification before any output-filter evaluation — egress deny/reject/log bypassed (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-17)

**Defect**

`resolve_cos_tx_selection_internal` (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/cos_classify.rs:404) has a `let Some(flow_key) = flow_key else { ... return CoSTxSelection { queue_id, dscp_rewrite, drop: false, reject: false, filter_log: None }; };` early return (the flowless branch, return at ~cos_classify.rs:462). It resolves the BA/DSCP CoS queue + rewrite but returns with `drop:false, reject:false, filter_log:None` — i.e. **without evaluating the interface output filter at all**. The output-filter evaluation (`interface_output_filter_needs_tx_eval` + term matching) only runs on the code path *after* this early return, which is reached solely when `flow_key` is `Some`.

Flowless traffic = a non-first IP fragment or a non-query ICMP control packet (no 5-tuple session key). An output filter's `TermMatchExtra` can still evaluate unconditional, source/destination-address, protocol, and `is-fragment` terms with no L4 ports — but the early return makes every such term unreachable on the flowless path.

**Impact:** A configured egress `filter output` deny/reject (or log) that should match by address/protocol/is-fragment is silently bypassed for fragmented or flowless traffic — a fail-open policy hole. Distinct from the deferred-neighbor action-loss finding (A1-C001) and from #5158 (post-NAT ingress re-walk).

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/cos_classify.rs:435-467 (flowless `else` branch + early return).

**Invariant:** Missing L4 context must make only L4-dependent predicates fail closed; it must not disable the entire output filter.

**Fix direction:** On the flowless branch, evaluate the output filter using frame-derived `TermMatchExtra` (unavailable L4 predicates become non-matches) and honor drop/reject/filter_log before returning.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A1/C179-011], High confidence.

Dataplane change — code driveable but final verify (cargo test --release + loss-cluster smoke/test-failover) is lab-bound on #5364.

## #5468 — userspace-dp/HA: push_delta_lossless 5s retry (LOSSLESS_QUEUE_TIMEOUT) runs on the worker loop (flush_session_deltas) — a connected-but-unread peer stalls the worker past HEARTBEAT_STALE_AFTER (5s) → false liveness loss / failover [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

**Defect**

The #2874 fix routes correctness-critical HA session open/close deltas through the LOSSLESS event-stream producer (`push_delta_lossless`) from `flush_session_deltas` (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_delta.rs:199; also the tunnel-remap purge path ha.rs:646). `flush_session_deltas` runs on the **packet worker loop** (its doc comment: "the caller latches loss-of-sync so the worker loop ...").

`push_delta_lossless` → `send_lossless_encoded` (userspace-dp/src/event_stream/mod.rs:591) loops on `TrySendError::Full`, sleeping `LOSSLESS_QUEUE_RETRY_DELAY` (50µs) until `deadline = now + LOSSLESS_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`. `LOSSLESS_QUEUE_TIMEOUT = Duration::from_secs(5)` (mod.rs:190). A **connected but not-reading** peer keeps the channel Full without disconnecting, so the loop retries for the full 5s.

`HEARTBEAT_STALE_AFTER = Duration::from_secs(5)` (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/mod.rs:372). A single 5s worker stall therefore reaches the stale-heartbeat threshold — the watchdog can mark a healthy binding unready and trigger recovery/failover while the worker is blocked on control-plane durability. The mod.rs:189 design comment ("Normal packet-path delta export remains non-blocking via try_send") is contradicted by the #2874 per-session lossless path.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** userspace-dp/src/event_stream/mod.rs:190 (5s timeout), :645-657 (retry-sleep loop); userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_delta.rs:55,199 (worker-loop caller); userspace-dp/src/afxdp/mod.rs:372 (5s stale threshold).

**Invariant:** Packet-worker publication must be nonblocking or bounded strictly below the watchdog stale-heartbeat tolerance; control-plane durability must not monopolize a polling worker.

**Fix direction:** Move lossless retry off the worker (dedicated exporter thread), or cap the worker-side retry well below HEARTBEAT_STALE_AFTER and latch out-of-sync/resync on give-up (the caller already handles the out-of-sync latch).

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A1/C179-012], High confidence.

Dataplane change — code driveable but final verify (cargo test --release + loss-cluster smoke/test-failover) is lab-bound on #5364.

## #5469 — userspace-dp: write_state holds the ServerState lock across full pretty-serialization + fsync; session-delta poll sets persist_state on every nonempty request → lock convoy under session churn [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

**Defect**

`write_state` (userspace-dp/src/server/helpers.rs:1283) takes `state.lock()`, runs `refresh_status`, `serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&payload)` over the **entire** ProcessStatus + ConfigSnapshot, then calls `guard.state_writer.persist(...)` — all while still holding the ServerState guard. The writer's durability contract includes file + parent-directory fsync, so storage latency is inside the global critical section.

The fallback session-delta poll sets `persist_state = true` on each nonempty request and drives `write_state`. Under session churn every nonempty delta poll therefore serializes + fsyncs the full state while holding the lock that also gates snapshot apply, status, and HA/control operations → lock convoying and delayed control ops. (Same anti-pattern class as configstore #4829, different component/lock.)

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** userspace-dp/src/server/helpers.rs:1283-1301 (`write_state` holds guard across to_vec_pretty + persist/fsync); delta-poll caller sets persist_state per nonempty request.

**Invariant:** Incremental session-delta handling must not hold the global ServerState lock across full serialization and synchronous durable I/O.

**Fix direction:** Mark durable state dirty under the lock, snapshot/serialize outside it, and coalesce asynchronous persistence by generation (skip redundant full writes on successive delta polls).

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A1/C179-016], High confidence.

Dataplane change — code driveable but final verify (cargo test --release + loss-cluster smoke/test-failover) is lab-bound on #5364.

## #5470 — deploy/HA: xpf-deploy.py --lease-ttl accepts non-positive values (unconstrained type=int) → kernel/image-roll lease expires immediately, two orchestrators can drain both HA nodes [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` cross-orchestrator kernel/image-roll lease treats a lease as live only while `now < expires` (the acquire shell at ~line 1110-1115: `if [ "$now" -lt "$ee" ]; then exit 1; fi`), and derives the new expiry directly from the caller-supplied `--lease-ttl`. Both `--lease-ttl` argparse parsers use unconstrained `type=int` (line ~1800 default=1800, and the second roll subcommand parser) with no positive-value floor.

`--lease-ttl 0` (or negative) is accepted; `_acquire_lease` writes `expires_at` at the current second, so the very next acquisition's strict `now < ee` check treats the lease as already expired. The per-node flock only serializes the read/replace/write transaction and is released immediately (it is NOT the roll-duration lock). A second orchestrator can then take each node's flock after the first releases it, overwrite both leases, and pass its `DrainAndConfirm` peer-ready precheck before either drain changes HA state — so two independent drivers can drain opposite nodes and produce a no-primary forwarding outage across all RGs.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py — lease acquire shell ~1110-1147; `--lease-ttl` parsers ~1800 (and sibling roll subcommand).

**Invariant:** Exactly one orchestrator owns both node reservations from before the first drain through rejoin/guarded recovery; the lease TTL that enforces this must be strictly positive with a defensible floor.

**Fix direction:** Use one shared argparse positive-integer type (reject 0/negative before any remote action) for both roll subcommands; define a minimum TTL and/or add lease-renewal/ownership rechecks for long rolls. Add parser-rejection and two-driver contention regressions.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A10/C179-027], High confidence. (Requires an operator/automation to pass a non-positive `--lease-ttl`; no positive-value validation exists today.)

## #5471 — config/ddns: generic backend with literal userinfo (http://user:secret@host) bypasses the plaintext-credential commit gate (#4861) — DDNS creds sent in cleartext [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`ddnsBackendCarriesCredentials` (pkg/config/compiler_ddns_tls.go) classifies a `generic` backend as credentialed only when `Username`/`Password` are typed or the url-template contains `%u`/`%p`. A generic template that embeds a **literal** `http://user:secret@host/...` userinfo has none of those → the predicate returns `false` → `ddnsPlaintextCredentialEndpoint` returns `bad=false` → the #4861 http-vs-https gate does NOT flag it. The generic backend then issues the plaintext HTTP request carrying those credentials.

The generic url-template validator explicitly supports a userinfo credential (see the `ddnsPlaintextCredentialEndpoint` comment: "a generic url-template legitimately embeds %h/%i/%u/%p specifiers (and a userinfo credential)"), so this is a valid config form that passes strict commit while leaking credentials in cleartext.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/config/compiler_ddns_tls.go — `ddnsBackendCarriesCredentials` `case "generic"` (misses literal authority userinfo).

**Invariant:** Acceptance-time credential classification must treat nonempty template-authority userinfo as a credential so the http-vs-https gate can fail closed.

**Fix direction:** Include nonempty url-template authority userinfo in `ddnsBackendCarriesCredentials` (and thus the endpoint-scheme check). Add HTTP/HTTPS literal-userinfo commit tests. Distinct from #5458 (log RedactURL of schemeless userinfo — a redaction gap, not the transport gate).

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A3/C179-036], High confidence.

## #5472 — config/snmp: duplicate community blocks overwrite the name-keyed map with no merge/dup-guard → later empty-clients block erases the allowlist (AllowsSource → allow-all, fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`compileSNMP` (pkg/config/compiler_system.go ~1234) builds each `community <name>` block into a fresh `&SNMPCommunity{Name: commName}`, accumulating `Clients` only from THAT block's children, then stores it with `snmp.Communities[comm.Name] = comm` (~line 1284) — a plain map overwrite with no same-name merge and no duplicate-community rejection. Hierarchical duplicate community stanzas are AST siblings, so a second `community public { authorization read-only; }` (no `clients`) constructs a community with an empty `Clients` list and overwrites the earlier `community public { clients <prefix>; }`. `AllowsSource` treats an empty client list as allow-all, so the source-IP allowlist is silently erased.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/config/compiler_system.go ~1234-1284 (`case "community"` → `snmp.Communities[comm.Name] = comm` overwrite, no merge/dup check).

**Invariant:** Same-name community blocks must merge (or a duplicate must be rejected) before the immutable client-prefix cache is built; a later block must not silently drop an earlier block's clients allowlist.

**Fix direction:** Merge same-name community blocks (accumulate `Clients`/authorization) before validation/cache construction, or reject duplicate community names with a tolerant warning. Add a duplicate-community regression (clients in block 1, none in block 2) asserting the allowlist survives.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A3/C179-041], High confidence.

## #5473 — configstore: auto-rollback deletes confirm.json unconditionally even when the replacement writeActive fails → crash before degraded retry loses the rollback recovery intent (stale commit-confirmed config persists) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

In the commit-confirmed timeout auto-rollback (pkg/configstore/store_commit.go ~615-638), the store promotes memory to the rollback target A, then `perr = s.writeActive(s.active)` (or `writeActiveMarker`). On failure it only records `noteActivePersistFailureLocked(...)` (schedules a degraded retry), then **unconditionally** calls `s.removeConfirmState()` — deleting confirm.json even though the on-disk active is still C (the pre-rollback confirmed config).

The idempotency comment ("a Load recovery re-runs the rollback as a no-op") only holds when `writeActive` SUCCEEDED — then persisted active == A. When `writeActive` FAILED, disk active is still C and confirm.json (the crash-recovery intent that would re-drive the rollback to A) is gone. A crash before the degraded retry completes therefore boots the firewall on C — the exact config `commit confirmed` was supposed to roll back — with no recovery record. `recoverPendingConfirmLocked` (store_persist.go ~177) and `SyncApply`'s `clearPendingConfirmLocked` before its degrade-not-fail active write (store.go ~570) repeat the same ordering.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/configstore/store_commit.go ~625-638 (`removeConfirmState()` after a possibly-failed `writeActive`); store_persist.go ~177-185; store.go ~570-590.

**Invariant:** A pending-confirm recovery record must not be removed until the rollback (or authoritative replacement) is durable.

**Fix direction:** Model resolution as a durable transition — write the rollback/sync target first, delete/replace confirm.json only on write success; on Option-B failure preserve enough intent for boot recovery to finish the replacement. Inject active-write failures for timeout, boot recovery, and SyncApply (fresh Store before the retry runs).

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A4/C179-052], High confidence. Distinct from #4864 (non-durable delete) and the earlier failure-to-create-record findings.

## #5474 — configstore: JSON null active body decodes as a valid empty ConfigTree (zero value, no error) instead of ErrConfigDBUnreadable → boots with policy absent [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`readTreeMeta`/DB decode (pkg/configstore/db.go ~293) does `tree := &config.ConfigTree{}; json.Unmarshal(data, tree)`. Go's `json.Unmarshal([]byte("null"), tree)` returns **no error** and leaves `tree` at its zero value, so the function returns `(tree, committed, nil)`. A legacy/plaintext or enveloped-but-unencrypted active body of literal `null` therefore decodes as a semantically-empty configuration and `Store.Load` compiles it and boots normally, instead of failing closed with `ErrConfigDBUnreadable`.

Syntactically-invalid bodies (and arrays/scalars, which mismatch the struct) error correctly; `null` is the specific gap — it is syntactically valid and decodes to a zero policy. AES-GCM protects an *encrypted* body, so the reachable cases are the legacy/plaintext / intentionally-unencrypted paths.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/configstore/db.go ~293 (`json.Unmarshal` into preallocated `*ConfigTree` with no top-level-kind validation).

**Invariant:** Authoritative persisted state must reject malformed/partial top-level JSON (null/array/scalar) rather than relying on zero-value decode.

**Fix direction:** Inspect a `json.RawMessage`/token first and require a JSON object before decoding `ConfigTree`; explicitly reject `null` (and non-object kinds) with a documented valid empty-object representation; cover plaintext and encrypted-envelope framing separately.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A4/C179-054], High confidence. Distinct from #4888 (unknown encrypted-envelope fields).

## #5475 — configstore/zeroize: factory reset does not sweep crash-leaked fsatomic temp remnants (.<base>.tmp-*) at top-level configDir → cleartext config/secrets can survive a factory reset [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`FactoryResetConfigDir` (pkg/configstore/factory_reset.go ~172-181) sweeps top-level configDir by exact match: `*.conf` suffix, `rollback*` prefix, `.config.journal[.N]`, and numbered text rollback slots. It does NOT match fsatomic crash-leaked temp files `.<base>.tmp-*` (pkg/fsatomic/fsatomic.go:311 creates `"."+base+".tmp-"` temps; README:70 documents crash-leaked temps). A `.xpf.conf.tmp-*` left by a crash mid-write (full cleartext config text: IKE PSKs, WireGuard keys, SNMP communities) fails `HasSuffix(name, ".conf")` (it ends in `-<rand>`), fails `rollback`/journal/rollback-slot matches, and so survives the reset. `.configdb` is `RemoveAll`'d so temps INSIDE it are covered — only top-level configDir temps leak. fsatomic self-heals leaked temps on the *next* write to that base, but after a factory reset + reboot there is no next write.

NOTE: the sibling "omits the external config archive" claim from this finding is already addressed by `FactoryResetArchiveDir` (#5186); this issue is narrowed to the still-uncovered fsatomic temp-remnant sweep. (Secondary: `FactoryResetArchiveDir` also deliberately skips a NON-default archive dir — logs and returns nil — which is a documented design choice, flagged here only for awareness.)

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/configstore/factory_reset.go ~176-181 (top-level sweep matcher, no `.*.tmp-*` glob).

**Invariant:** A successful zeroize must remove every xpf-owned recoverable cleartext replica before announcing erasure.

**Fix direction:** Add a `filepath.Glob(configDir, ".*.tmp-*")` (fsatomic naming) sweep to the top-level pass, fsync the parent, and verify the owned roots are empty before reporting success.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A4/C179-055], High confidence (archive portion already fixed by #5186; residual temp-remnant sweep is the genuine part).

## #5477 — cluster/heartbeat: anti-replay watermark is a single (session,counter) with no retired-session tracking — A→B→A alternation resets it, letting recorded authenticated heartbeats refresh liveness/election (replay) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-21)

**Defect**

`heartbeatAuthReplay.admit` (pkg/cluster/heartbeat.go ~492) stores exactly one `(session, counter)`. On `session != a.session` it unconditionally resets the watermark and returns true (accepts) — the design intent is to accept a genuine peer reboot (fresh random session). But there is no retired-session set or boot epoch, so an on-link attacker who has recorded authenticated frames from BOTH incarnations A and B can alternate A→B→A→B: each session switch resets the counter watermark, so the same recorded A frames replay after every B switch. HMAC prevents fabrication but not replay of an already-valid byte sequence; the cluster-ID / duplicate-node checks encode no incarnation.

The read loop calls `admit` after MAC verification but before updating `lastSeen` / `handlePeerHeartbeat` (~750-773), so an accepted replayed frame refreshes liveness and applies its (stale) role/priority.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/cluster/heartbeat.go ~492 (`admit`), ~750-773 (read loop). Existing test covers only A→B, not A→B→A.

**Invariant:** A peer incarnation must not regress; authenticated replay protection must reject a return to a retired session ID.

**Fix direction:** Bind an authenticated boot epoch, or retain a bounded retired-session set and reject a return to a retired ID (allocation-free). Test A1,B1,A2 through the real receiver and assert A2 refreshes neither liveness nor election state.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A5/C179-062], High confidence. Threat model: on-link attacker able to record + inject authenticated control-link frames. (HA/VRRP change — final verify via `make test-failover` is lab-bound.)
