## #5478 — cluster/monitor: a local monitored interface that goes missing (netdev removed/renamed/unresolved) is logged and skipped without SetMonitorWeight — incumbent primary is not demoted (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

**Defect**

In the interface-monitor poll (pkg/cluster/monitor.go ~292), when `LinkByName(linuxName)` fails and the interface is NOT a peer-slot interface, the code `slog.Warn("local interface missing")` then `continue` — returning before `evaluateTransition` / `SetMonitorWeight`. A monitor that was previously healthy keeps its prior weight contribution, so on netdev removal/rename (or an unresolved startup name) an already-primary node is NOT demoted for the missing forwarding interface. `LinkAttrsUp` only handles carrier-down after a successful lookup; readiness blocks promotion but does not demote an incumbent.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/cluster/monitor.go ~292 (local-missing branch `continue` without weight update).

**Invariant:** A configured interface monitor must demote (down) when its local netdev disappears, not retain healthy weight.

**Fix direction:** Feed a local lookup failure into the existing debounce/down state path (so transient blips don't flap) while preserving the peer-slot skip. Cover missing-at-start, disappearance-while-primary, and reappearance.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A5/C179-063], High confidence. (HA change — final verify via `make test-failover` is lab-bound.) Distinct from #4480 (display status).

## #5479 — cluster/failover: a failed requested peer-failover has no remote transfer-out abort — abortRequestedPeerFailover only restores local state, leaving the already-demoted remote in SecondaryHold (blackhole) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

**Defect**

In the requested peer-failover commit path (pkg/cluster/failover.go ~281-293), phase one makes the remote daemon demote itself via `ManualFailover` (pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go ~672) before it acknowledges. If the local `localCommitReadyFn`/`commitFn` then fails, the code calls `abortRequestedPeerFailover`, whose body (failover.go ~339) does only LOCAL work — `restorePeerTransferOutOverrideLocked`, `delete(peerTransferCommitGraceUntil)`, `runElection()` — and sends NO message to the peer. The sync protocol defines request/ack/commit/commit-ack but no abort. So the remote, having already demoted, stays `SecondaryHold` while the requester cannot assume ownership → service blackhole until an unrelated recovery/reset condition. The 2s both-yield deadlock escape is not a rollback protocol and does not cover a requester that remains ineligible.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/cluster/failover.go ~281-293 (abort call sites), ~339-349 (`abortRequestedPeerFailover` local-only body).

**Invariant:** A failed HA transfer command must leave neither participant committed to a new role without a deterministic terminal outcome.

**Fix direction:** Add a request-ID-scoped abort/rollback sync message + handler that restores the remote's role, OR make phase one a non-demoting prepare and fence demotion at commit. Exercise two managers over a real transport for every post-phase-one failure.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A5/C179-066], High confidence. (HA change — final verify via `make test-failover` is lab-bound.) Distinct from #390/#397 (commit/handoff protocol).

## #5480 — cluster/session-sync: coldStart is the sticky process-local !bulkEverCompleted flag — a survivor skips outbound bulk on reconnect, so a rebooted peer that lost its session table is never re-primed [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-21)

**Defect**

`coldStart := !s.bulkEverCompleted.Load()` (pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go ~538) is a sticky, process-local atomic. After the survivor has completed one bulk it stays non-cold. When the PEER daemon restarts (its session table + its own flag reset), the survivor reconnects, sees `coldStart==false`, and logs "skipping bulk sync on reconnect (already primed)" (sync_conn.go ~546) — it does NOT re-push its authoritative table. The restarted peer sends its own empty bulk; `OnPeerConnected` re-pushes only non-session state; old established sessions are not guaranteed to pass the incremental sweep's time filter. A transport blip and a peer restart are indistinguishable to the survivor (no peer boot-ID / incarnation in the handshake).

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go ~538 (sticky coldStart), ~546-552 (skip-on-reconnect branch).

**Invariant:** Re-prime must occur on an authenticated peer-incarnation change (preserving the deliberate avoidance of O(N) bulk on routine fabric flips).

**Fix direction:** Exchange a process incarnation/boot-ID in the sync handshake; track outbound prime completion by peer incarnation; on change send an authoritative bulk. Test an old session surviving one node's reboot.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A5/C179-068], High confidence. (HA change — final verify via `make test-failover` / `make test-ha-crash` is lab-bound.) Distinct from #466 (intentional routine-reconnect bulk suppression) and #5085 (empty-marker reconcile).

## #5481 — vrrp: a failed required IPv6 advertisement socket is swallowed (warn + continue) — an IPv6-only instance is installed and can become MASTER/claim VIP without ever advertising [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

**Defect**

In `vrrpInstance` setup (pkg/vrrp/instance.go ~437), when `openIPv6Socket` fails for an instance that has IPv6 VIPs, the error is only `slog.Warn("ipv6 socket open failed, IPv6 adverts disabled")` and the function still `return nil` — so `UpdateInstances` installs and runs the instance. `RGVRRPReady` (pkg/vrrp/manager.go ~661) returns true merely because the RG instance is in the manager map, and an IPv6 send with a nil `ipv6Conn` returns nil, so an IPv6-only MASTER can claim role + VIP ownership without emitting any advertisement. AF_PACKET receive does not help — it cannot SEND the missing raw IPv6 adverts, and IPv4 capability is irrelevant to an IPv6-only instance.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/vrrp/instance.go ~437-455 (swallowed open failure, `return nil`); manager.go ~661 (`RGVRRPReady` map-presence only).

**Invariant:** A configured VIP family's send capability must be proven before the instance is eligible for promotion / counted ready.

**Fix direction:** Fail construction when a configured VIP family lacks a send socket; close already-open descriptors; preserve any prior instance (build-before-teardown). Test IPv6-only and dual-stack socket-failure cases.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A5/C179-071], High confidence. (VRRP change — final verify via `make test-failover` is lab-bound.) Distinct from #2155 (v6 ext-header receive) / #2156 (replacement lifetime).

## #5482 — vrrp: becomeMaster/backup publish role via emitEvent without verifying VIP ownership — addVIPs/removeVIPs are void and swallow netlink errors, so control-plane role can diverge from kernel VIP state [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

**Defect**

`becomeMaster` (pkg/vrrp/instance.go ~1849) calls `vi.addVIPs()` (void, ~2093) then `vi.emitEvent()` unconditionally; `addVIPs`/`removeVIPs` only log link/parse/netlink errors and return nothing. The daemon consumes the MASTER event to make the RG active, remove blackholes, and start per-RG services (pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go ~429-455); BACKUP emits similarly after best-effort `removeVIPs`. So control-plane role can be published while the kernel VIP add failed (services active without the VIP) or while a delete failed (services deactivated while the address remains locally owned) — violating HA ownership fencing. The 2s reconciler re-reads VRRP state, not actual kernel addresses, so it repeats the same false role; `EEXIST` is a valid add-success but other errors are swallowed.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/vrrp/instance.go ~1849 (`becomeMaster`), ~2093 (`addVIPs` void), ~2125 (`removeVIPs` void); consumer pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go ~429-455.

**Invariant:** Role must be published only after the required VIP ownership is established in the kernel.

**Fix direction:** Return per-VIP operation outcomes from addVIPs/removeVIPs; publish role only after required ownership succeeds; on failure retry/fence/rollback. Inject link/parse/add/delete failures through the daemon event consumer.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A5/C179-072], High confidence. (VRRP change — final verify via `make test-failover` is lab-bound.) Distinct from #3924 (userspace local-addr pruning) / #2156.

## #5483 — dataplane/eventstream: a decode failure on a session Open/Update/Close frame is skipped (continue) instead of forcing a sync break — later telemetry advances the cumulative ACK and trims the unapplied session frame from replay (silent standby divergence) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

**Defect**

`EventStream` reader (pkg/dataplane/userspace/eventstream.go ~396) handles a complete-but-undecodable session frame with `es.DecodeErrors.Add(1); continue` — it does NOT trigger the hard sync-break that a session-sequence GAP triggers (the #2874 path only fires on a detected gap or explicit FullResync, not on a semantic decode rejection of a present frame). The malformed frame at seq N is silently dropped while `prevSeq`/`lastAppliedSeq` are preserved. A subsequent valid lossy TELEMETRY frame at N+1 records only a gap, `dispatchOrQueueDataplaneFrame` marks N+1 applied, `sendAckIfNeeded` advances the cumulative ACK past N, and the Rust replay buffer (userspace-dp/src/event_stream/mod.rs) trims entries through that watermark — including the unapplied session frame. A later session frame sees no gap because telemetry already advanced prevSeq.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/dataplane/userspace/eventstream.go ~396-402 (`decodeSessionEvent` !ok → continue).

**Invariant:** The ACK watermark may cover only contiguous, successfully-applied correctness-critical session state; a decode failure on a session-sync frame must be a hard sync break, not a skip.

**Fix direction:** Treat decode failure of any session Open/Update/Close as a hard sync break — hold the watermark at N-1, trigger the bounded full-resync, close/reconnect. Test malformed N followed by valid telemetry N+1 for Open/Update/Close.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A6/C179-078], High confidence. (HA session-sync — final verify via `make test-failover` is lab-bound.) Distinct from #2874 (producer replay hole), #2959 (impossible ACK ranges), #5362 (FullResync prevSeq).

## #5484 — dataplane/shim upgrade: live-pin ABI preflight inventory omits production shared/replacement maps (sessions_v6, dnat_table_v6, HA/counter) — an incompatible shim map ABI passes verification then fails ErrMapIncompatible AFTER the old daemon is stopped (node stranded fail-closed) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`validateUserspaceShimLivePins` (pkg/dataplane/loader_userspace_shim.go ~327) iterates `userspaceABICheckedPinnedMaps()`, which derives from `userspacePinnedShimMaps()` (~404) — a list that OMITS state-bearing shared maps replaced at load: `sessions_v6`, `dnat_table_v6`, and the HA/per-CPU counter maps (only `dnat_table` v4 is covered; `userspace_sessions` singular but not the v6/shared family). Independently, `validateUserspaceShimSpecWith` has an expected-shape arm only for v4 `dnat_table` while production replaces both v4 and v6 (~122-130 MapReplacements["dnat_table_v6"]), and `verify_userspace_shim.go` creates the candidate's anonymous maps so it never exercises the production v6 replacement.

Consequently a changed shared-map or embedded v6 ABI passes the advertised pre-stop upgrade gate, then fails with `ErrMapIncompatible` only after the working dataplane is stopped — stranding the node fail-closed and risking HA capacity loss.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/dataplane/loader_userspace_shim.go ~327 (`validateUserspaceShimLivePins`), ~404 (`userspacePinnedShimMaps` incomplete inventory), ~122-130 (v6 replacement not preflighted).

**Invariant:** Every production `PinByName` map and `MapReplacement` must be preflighted with the same Type/KeySize/ValueSize/MaxEntries/Flags contract used at production load.

**Fix direction:** Drive embedded-spec validation, live-pin ABI checks, and verify-only replacements from one production replacement inventory that includes every `userspaceShimSharedMapSpecs` entry (incl. `dnat_table_v6`, `sessions_v6`, HA/counter), retaining the explicit disposable-map (`userspace_fallback_stats`) exception. Add stale-live-pin/candidate-drift tests for state, HA, per-CPU counter, and v6 DNAT maps.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A6/C179-079], High confidence. Distinct from #5307 (field comparison for the included set) and #5363 (verify-dataplane remediation text). Final upgrade verify is lab-bound (relates to #5364).

## #5485 — dataplane/userspace: XDP shim attach (CompileUserspaceShim) + syncInterfaceAttachments detach run BEFORE apply_snapshot with no rollback — a later apply failure leaves kernel XDP attachments diverged from the retained lastSnapshot (policy bypass / outage) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-21)

In `compile`/apply (pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go ~184-209), `CompileUserspaceShim(cfg)` attaches the XDP shim to candidate interfaces, then after `buildSnapshot*` succeeds `m.syncInterfaceAttachments(result, snap)` detaches links absent from the candidate set. Both mutate kernel XDP attachment state BEFORE the later bootstrap/process/protocol/`apply_snapshot` steps. `m.lastSnapshot` advances only after a successful `apply_snapshot`; the fail-closed comment ("previously published snapshot / dataplane state is retained") protects the SNAPSHOT but no error path restores the prior XDP link set. So a failure after attach/detach leaves a formerly-protected ingress without the shim, or an unacknowledged ingress attached — kernel attachment state inconsistent with the reported retained snapshot.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go ~184 (`CompileUserspaceShim` attach), ~209 (`syncInterfaceAttachments` detach) — both before apply_snapshot, no rollback.

**Invariant:** Atomic correspondence between live XDP attachments and the acknowledged helper snapshot; staging stays off the packet path.

**Fix direction:** Build+validate first; stage candidate ADDITIONS, acknowledge the snapshot, then remove obsolete links; on any later failure remove new links and restore the prior set. Test failures after build, bootstrap, protocol checks, and apply_snapshot.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A6/C179-082], High confidence. (Runtime XDP attachment — final verify is lab-bound.)

## #5486 — dataplane/userspace: disableUserspaceCtrlLocked is void and swallows ctrl-map Lookup/Update errors before worker/UMEM teardown — shim keeps redirecting to dead XSK fds until heartbeat expiry (transit outage) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

**Invariant:** No packet may be redirected after its worker/UMEM lifetime ends; the ctrl-disabled fail-closed gate MUST be established before teardown.

**Fix direction:** Return and propagate disable errors; on Lookup failure use a checked fail-closed fallback and verify the row before worker teardown; if forced shutdown continues, explicitly detach/clear all bindings. Add Lookup/Update/readback fault-injection tests.

## #5487 — dataplane/userspace: standalone HA-state clear (clearHelperHAStateLocked) failure returns an error but has no retry/debt — a cluster→standalone reconfig with a transient control-socket error leaves stale helper HA groups → owner-RG-0 forwarding stays HAInactive (transit drop) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-13)

The snapshot has already been acknowledged; if this empty `update_ha_state` RPC fails, the helper retains old HA groups while the manager has `clusterHA=false`. The periodic status poll skips HA sync in non-cluster mode (guarded by `m.clusterHA` in process.go), and a newly-started helper has not reached `ensureStatusLoopLocked`, so the empty update is never retried. A non-empty helper HA map makes owner_rg_id<=0 forwarding candidates HAInactive → total standalone transit forwarding outage until an unrelated full apply. `clearHelperHAStateLocked` is idempotent (safe to retry).

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go ~360-368 (clear failure returns error, no debt/retry).

**Fix direction:** Record standalone-clear debt before returning and retry empty HA publication until status reports zero groups; treat the post-ack HA update as explicit convergence state. Test a successful snapshot followed by one failed empty update.

## #5488 — dataplane/policy: multi-zone scoped global deny is lowered with only the FIRST zone in the legacy singular field + full set in additive plural fields, but the snapshot protocol version was NOT bumped (still 3) — a pre-#4626 same-version helper ignores the plural fields and narrows the deny (fail-open under rolling upgrade) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-01)

`lowerPolicy` (pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_lower.go ~208) emits a scoped global deny as `MatchFromZone/MatchToZone = ScopeSingular(...)` (first zone, for backward compat) plus `MatchFromZones/MatchToZones` (full set) as ADDITIVE JSON fields. `CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is still `3` (userspace-dp/src/protocol/control.rs:22; Go `ProtocolVersion`) — the same value as a pre-#4626 helper. The protocol gate therefore accepts an old helper that parses only the singular field and ignores the additive plural fields, so a global deny scoped `[dmz trust] -> untrust` collapses to `dmz -> untrust` on that helper. The singular/plural design explicitly targets rolling upgrade, so the skew window is expected — and the compat is unsafe for deny/reject coverage.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_lower.go ~208-215 (additive plural zones under unchanged version 3); userspace-dp/src/protocol/control.rs:22.

**Invariant:** A compatibility extension that changes deny/reject COVERAGE must not be silently ignorable under the same protocol version.

**Fix direction:** Bump the snapshot protocol version (or add a helper capability bit) and refuse unsafe publication to a helper lacking multi-zone support; if compat is required, lower deny/reject scopes safely (expand) and permit scopes narrowly. Add old-helper decode/evaluation tests for deny AND reject.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A6/C179-087], High confidence. (Version-skew/rolling-upgrade window; final verify lab-bound.) Distinct from #4626 (zone-set impl for current helpers).

## #5489 — dataplane/zones: exact-unit host-inbound override branch merges (union) across zones with NO owner guard (unlike the physical-expansion branch) — a tolerated duplicate-unit ownership grants the losing zone's admissions (e.g. SSH) in the winning zone [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Fix direction:** Apply the same owner predicate (`zoneByIface[unit] == zone`) to the exact-unit branch as the physical-expansion branch; quarantine absent/losing owners. Add a lenient two-zone conflict test covering InterfaceSnapshot and ZoneHostInboundView.

## #5490 — daemon/device-map: commit preflight returns nil (skips the strand-management check) on a transient NIC-enumeration error — a candidate that strands management is accepted, then next boot's enumerateAndRenameMapped performs the unsafe rename with no re-check (durable mgmt lockout, incl. confirmed commits) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## #5493 — daemon/login: deprovisionLoginUser treats a /etc/passwd READ error as proof of account absence (lookupUID false) and deletes the provenance marker without revoking — removed user's password/keys stay active, never re-enumerated (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`deprovisionLoginUser` (pkg/daemon/login_password.go ~296) does `curUID, uidOK := lookupUID(name); if !uidOK { os.Remove(markerPath(name)); return }`. `lookupUID`→`lookupUIDGID` (~125) maps ANY `os.ReadFile(passwdPath)` error to `ok=false` — so a transient mount/permission/I/O error on /etc/passwd is indistinguishable from genuine out-of-band deletion. The caller then deletes the ONLY provenance marker and returns BEFORE locking the shadow password or removing managed authorized_keys. Once passwd becomes readable again, `reconcileAbsentLoginUsers` no longer enumerates the account (marker gone), so revocation is permanently abandoned.

Note the asymmetry: the SAME function fail-CLOSES on a shadow read error ("keep marker; retry next apply", #1944 discipline) but fail-OPENS on a passwd read error — confirming the intended contract is retry-on-uncertainty.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/daemon/login_password.go ~125 (`lookupUIDGID` read-error→false), ~296-303 (`deprovisionLoginUser` removes marker on !uidOK).

**Invariant:** Identity-database loss must be unknown-and-retryable, never proof of absence; provenance may be deleted only after a successful complete passwd read proves the account is gone.

**Fix direction:** Return `(uid, found, err)` from the passwd lookup; retain+retry on read/parse error; delete the marker only on a proven-complete read. Add passwd-read-failure-then-recovery transition tests.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A7/C179-095], High confidence. Distinct from #1916 (owner/durability), #5128 (revocation impl).

## #5494 — ipsec: a previously-loaded VPN that becomes UNRENDERABLE (broken gateway/IKE/proposal via tolerant load or peer-sync) is not diffed as removed — promoteConnNames keys off raw VPN name so terminateRemovedConns never runs and the stale child SA keeps forwarding under old selectors/credentials [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`promoteConnNames` (pkg/ipsec/manager.go ~218) diffs the applied connection set by VPN NAME (map key), NOT by renderability — the code comment states outright that "a VPN that merely became unrenderable ... is NOT treated as removed and keeps its SAs." When a valid, established VPN's config is made unrenderable by a tolerant persisted/peer-synced input (broken gateway ref, IKE chain, AH proposal), `renderConfig` omits the connection but returns SUCCESS, `load-all` succeeds, and `vpnConnNameSet` still contains every raw VPN map key. So `promoteConnNames` sees no removal, `terminateRemovedConns` is not called, and strongSwan's existing child SA keeps forwarding despite no loaded renderable connection — a stale peer remains authorized under old selectors and credentials while the apply reports convergence. (#4898 only guards the failed-reload case; here reload succeeds.)

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/ipsec/manager.go ~218 (`promoteConnNames` name-keyed diff); the render-skip path returns success with the connection omitted.

**Invariant:** After a successful apply, every forwarding child SA must correspond to a connection actually rendered+loaded, or be actively terminated.

**Fix direction:** Return the exact RENDERED connection set from renderConfig and promote/diff THAT after a successful reload; treat previously-applied-now-skipped names as removals and terminate their live SAs. Test each skip class from a valid/up starting state.

**Design note:** The current name-keyed behavior is documented as intentional (avoid tearing an SA on transient unrenderability); this issue argues it is a security fail-open on the HA/tolerant-load path and should be adjudicated on that basis.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A7/C179-100], High confidence. Distinct from #4898 (failed-reload) and #3941 (explicit deletion).

## #5495 — routing/xfrm: deleteLocked treats ANY LinkByName error (EBUSY/timeout/netlink) as 'already gone' — drops tracking and returns nil, orphaning a live kernel xfrmi with no future cleanup (sibling code uses isLinkNotFound) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`xfrmManager.deleteLocked` (pkg/routing/xfrm.go ~283) does `link, err := x.ops.LinkByName(name); if err != nil { delete(x.xfrmis, name); return nil // already gone }`. Any LinkByName error — EBUSY, timeout, netlink transport failure — takes the same branch as genuine absence: it deletes tracking and reports success. The #4901 hardening only covers a failed `LinkDel` AFTER a successful lookup; the LinkByName-error branch predates it. Full-tunnel `Clear` likewise resets ownership on lookup errors. A later apply then has no removed-desired entry to drive cleanup, so a transient error silently orphans a live kernel xfrmi (and stale routing/security state) while reporting convergence. Sibling code (normal tunnel removal, vrf.go) already distinguishes via `isLinkNotFound`.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/routing/xfrm.go ~283-289 (`deleteLocked` LinkByName error → delete tracking + return nil); full-tunnel `Clear`.

**Invariant:** Ownership cannot be discarded until absence is proven (`isLinkNotFound`) or deletion succeeds.

**Fix direction:** Treat only `isLinkNotFound` as successful absence; on any other LinkByName error retain tracking and return a wrapped error; preserve failed names across full Clear. Add transient-lookup-error retry tests.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A7/C179-103], High confidence. Distinct from #4901 (failed LinkDel after successful lookup) and #5461 (xfrm APPLY/create path LinkByName-error→LinkAdd→EEXIST).

## #5496 — grpcapi/zeroize: passwd read/parse/marker uncertainty is conflated with proven account absence — the provisioned password account survives while its provenance marker is deleted and performZeroizeWipe still returns success (fail-open factory reset) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

The zeroize account path (pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_zeroize.go ~260-268) reads /etc/passwd and maps any read error to a boolean also used for proven absence; a malformed UID or unreadable/unparseable marker enters the adjacent stale-marker branch. Neither branch records an error (`firstErr` stays nil) or disables marker removal (`removeMarker` stays true). So an xpf-provisioned interactive PASSWORD account can survive while its only retry provenance is erased, after which `performZeroizeWipe` returns nil and `SystemAction` reports a completed factory reset. Repeated resets can no longer rediscover the account (marker gone). Avoiding `userdel` under uncertain ownership is correct, but conflating I/O/parse failure with proof-of-no-credential is not.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_zeroize.go ~260-268 (passwd read→false; adjacent stale-marker branch leaves firstErr nil + removeMarker true).

**Invariant:** Security-critical ownership uncertainty must fail closed (incomplete reset) while preserving the durable evidence needed for a safe retry.

**Fix direction:** Return `(uid, found, err)` and preserve marker read errors separately; treat read/parse uncertainty as an incomplete reset (retain marker, no destructive account change); keep a proven UID-mismatch non-destructive but report it unresolved absent explicit durable stale-marker policy. Add true-absence / unreadable / malformed / mismatch / retry tests.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A8/C179-107], High confidence. Related root pattern to the day-2 login path #5493 (C179-095) but a distinct locus (factory-reset). Distinct from #4598 (normal teardown/userdel-retry).

## #5497 — grpcapi: MonitorInterface proxies to the peer whenever the LOCAL node is not RG-primary (!IsLocalPrimary) without checking the PEER owns the RG and with no hop marker — during both-secondary/election/hold states A→B→A recursion storms connections/streams/goroutines [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

**Defect**

`MonitorInterface` for a RETH interface proxies to the peer when `rg := rethRG(name); rg > 0 && s.cluster != nil && !s.cluster.IsLocalPrimary(rg)` (pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go ~387), then `proxyMonitorInterface` (~478) opens `client.MonitorInterface(ctx, req)` on the peer. It checks only that the LOCAL node is not primary — not that the peer IS primary — and stamps NO forwarded-hop metadata (unlike the chassis-forwarding proxy's `xpf-no-peer` marker). The HA state model explicitly permits BOTH nodes to be non-primary (election, maintenance, disabled, lost, both-secondary) and missing RGs return false. So node A (!primary) proxies to B; B (also !primary) evaluates the unchanged request and proxies back to A; each nested server stream blocks on another peer client stream, consuming connections/streams/goroutines/memory until a resource limit or cancellation unwinds it.

**Location (origin/master 92bc6186e):** pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go ~387 (proxy trigger on `!IsLocalPrimary`), ~478-492 (`proxyMonitorInterface`, no hop marker).

**Invariant:** One management stream must consume O(1) server/client resources; peer forwarding must have a strict hop bound.

**Fix direction:** Stamp authenticated forwarded metadata and prohibit a second proxy hop; forward only with explicit evidence the peer owns the RG, else return `FailedPrecondition` with local/peer state. Test both-secondary/hold/lost/disabled/missing-RG/one-primary with a max-one-dial assertion.

**Provenance:** codex-review-179 [A8/C179-108], High confidence. Distinct from #4910 (active monitor streams blocking graceful shutdown).

## #5504 — test regression (#5499): applyInterfaceReconcile xfrmi-create-failure test breaks — fake LinkByName returns plain error, not netlink.LinkNotFoundError [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Regression

`TestApplyInterfaceReconcileFailsClosedOnXfrmCreateFailure` (pkg/daemon/apply_interface_reconcile_failclosed_5310_test.go) **PASSES at cdfcc5c66 (before #5499) and FAILS at 0b117466e (after #5499)**. `go test ./pkg/daemon/` is RED on current master.

```
--- FAIL: TestApplyInterfaceReconcileFailsClosedOnXfrmCreateFailure
    apply_interface_reconcile_failclosed_5310_test.go:111: returned error must wrap the injected xfrmi failure, got apply xfrmi interfaces: lookup xfrmi st0.1: link not found
```

## Root cause

#5499 (issues #5461/#5495) changed `xfrmManager.Apply` to distinguish transient LinkByName errors from genuine absence via `isLinkNotFound` (pkg/routing/vrf.go:155), which recognizes ONLY `netlink.LinkNotFoundError` or the internal `errLinkNotFound` (both via `errors.As`).

The pkg/daemon test's fake ops `reconcileFakeLinkOps.LinkByName` returns a **plain** `errors.New("link not found")` (line 48) to simulate an absent interface. Post-#5499, `isLinkNotFound(plainErr)` is **false**, so `Apply`'s create path `if err != nil && !isLinkNotFound(err)` treats the fake's not-found as a **transient** error → retains+surfaces the lookup error instead of falling through to `LinkAdd`. The injected `LinkAdd` failure is therefore never reached, and the test's `errors.Is(err, injected)` assertion fails.

## Not a production bug

Production uses the real `*netlink.Handle`, whose `LinkByName` returns `netlink.LinkNotFoundError` on absence (verified in the #5499 review against netlink@v1.3.1: ENODEV / empty-dump / name-miss all map to `LinkNotFoundError`). `isLinkNotFound` recognizes that, so production correctly falls through to create. The **test fake** is simply no longer faithful to real netlink after #5499 tightened the contract.

## Why it slipped through

#5499's engineer + reviewer both ran only `go test ./pkg/routing/...`; the pkg/daemon consumer (`applyInterfaceReconcile` → `xfrm.Apply`) was not in their test scope. Discovered while verifying the "pre-existing failing test" claim during the #5502 review (the failure is a #5499 regression, not pre-existing).

## Fix direction

Make `reconcileFakeLinkOps.LinkByName` return an error `isLinkNotFound` recognizes (a `netlink.LinkNotFoundError`) so the fake faithfully simulates real-netlink absence and the create path is exercised. Preserve the #5310 fail-on-revert intent (revert applyInterfaceReconcile to swallow → RED). Verify the full `pkg/daemon` suite goes green and the bond/tunnel/idempotent sibling tests (same fake) still pass.

## Provenance
Found during #5502 review verification. Regression from #5499 (merged). Test-only fix (no production code change).

## #5509 — zeroize/factory-reset: rendered service-config dirs (/etc/frr, /etc/swanctl/conf.d, /etc/kea) are not swept for crash-leaked fsatomic temps — a mid-write crash leaks cleartext (IKE PSKs) that survives factory reset [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect

Sibling of #5475 (which fixed the configDir-scoped leak). `zeroizeRenderedConfigs` erases the RENDERED service configs by EXACT PATH only (StripManagedSectionFile / os.Remove) — it does NOT sweep for crash-leaked fsatomic write temps `.<base>.tmp-<rand>`, and there is no startup-sweep owner for those directories (configstore.NewDB sweeps only `.configdb`).

The rendered configs are written via fsatomic:
- `pkg/frr/manager.go` → `/etc/frr`
- `pkg/ipsec/manager.go` → `/etc/swanctl/conf.d` (a swanctl snippet carries IKE PSKs in cleartext)
- `pkg/dhcpserver/*` → `/etc/kea`

A daemon hard-killed mid-write in any of these leaves a `.<base>.tmp-<rand>` holding the full cleartext render. `zeroizeRenderedConfigs` removes only the known exact paths, so the temp SURVIVES a factory reset + reboot (no next write to self-heal, no startup sweep).

## Invariant
Factory reset must sweep crash-leaked fsatomic temps in EVERY directory where the daemon writes cleartext via fsatomic — not only the configDir (#5475) but also the rendered service-config dirs.

## Fix direction
Apply the same `.*.tmp-*` sweep (as #5475's `isFsatomicTemp` / configstore.NewDB glob) to the rendered-config directories in `zeroizeRenderedConfigs`, OR add a startup-sweep owner for them. Match the fsatomic temp shape precisely (leading dot + `.tmp-` infix). Add a regression seeding a `.<base>.tmp-<rand>` in each rendered dir and asserting factory reset removes it.

## Provenance
Found during the #5508 (#5475) hostile review as an adjacent, pre-existing, out-of-scope leak. Distinct from #5475 (configDir) and #5186 (config archive).

## #5512 — daemon_nft: lo0 host-inbound mirror WIDENS (drops the match) on an unrepresentable tcp-flags constraint while the userspace path fails closed — a filter term restricting by TCP flags matches all on lo0 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Defect

Divergence between the two tcp-flags enforcement paths for an *unrepresentable* tcp-flags constraint (disjunction, unknown-flag, dangling `!`, and — pre-#5455 — operator-only/empty-operand):

- **userspace filters (primary)** — `filters.go:222` sets `snap.TCPFlagsUnparseable=true` → the Rust filter compiler fails the snapshot **CLOSED** (the term is not installed permissively).
- **daemon_nft lo0 mirror (secondary)** — `daemon_nft.go:1378` DROPS the tcp-flags match with a `slog.Warn` rather than emit garbage that would fail the whole lo0 ruleset. Dropping the match **WIDENS** the term: a host-inbound filter term intended to restrict lo0 traffic by TCP flags now matches ALL TCP.

So on the nft lo0 host-inbound path, an unrepresentable tcp-flags constraint fails **OPEN** (the constraint silently disappears), whereas the userspace path fails closed. A term meant to admit only e.g. SYN packets to a host service on lo0 admits all TCP flags.

## Invariant
Both host-inbound enforcement paths must fail the SAME direction on an unrepresentable tcp-flags constraint — and for a security filter that direction must be CLOSED (reject the constraint / drop the traffic), never widen by dropping the match.

## Fix direction
On an unrepresentable tcp-flags constraint, the daemon_nft lo0 mirror should fail closed consistently with the userspace path — e.g. drop the whole TERM (deny the traffic the term was scoping) or refuse the ruleset, rather than drop just the match (which widens). Align the two paths. Add a test asserting the lo0 nft term does not widen when tcp-flags is unrepresentable.

## Provenance
Found during the #5510 (#5455) hostile review as a pre-existing divergence affecting multiple unrepresentable-tcp-flags classes (disjunction / unknown-flag / dangling-`!`), NOT introduced or worsened by #5455. Distinct from #5455 (which fixed the parser-level operator-only fail-open).

## #5517 — config/NAT64: strict commit accepts an extra-slash prefix the dataplane silently skips (commit-accepts/runtime-drops) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary
The strict commit validator for NAT64 prefixes accepts a malformed prefix with a trailing extra slash (e.g. `64:ff9b::/96/garbage`), but the Rust dataplane per-rule loader **skips** any prefix that does not split into exactly two slash-separated parts. The result is a **commit-accepts / runtime-drops** divergence: `commit` succeeds, but the NAT64 rule is silently omitted from the dataplane, so IPv6→IPv4 translation for that rule never happens.

## Evidence (origin/master)
- `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:1384` — `if len(parts) >= 2` accepts an extra-slash prefix.
- `userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs:752` — `if parts.len() != 2 { ...; continue }` skips the same input (regression test `extra_slash_prefix_skips_rule`).

## Why it matters
An operator commits a NAT64 rule that looks accepted but produces no translation. NAT64 traffic is silently blackholed/untranslated with no error — a correctness and vSRX-parity defect. The commit path is the security/correctness contract; a value the runtime drops must be rejected at commit.

## Fix direction
Require `len(parts) == 2` in `validateNAT64PrefixStrict` (reject a trailing slash / extra segment) and correct the stale Go comment. Add a compiler test asserting `64:ff9b::/96/garbage` is rejected at strict commit, mirroring the Rust `extra_slash_prefix_skips_rule` expectation.

## Provenance
codex-review-179 [C179-031] (Medium). Distinct from #5101 (static-NAT port collapse).

## #5518 — frr/BGP: remote-as-0 neighbor omitted from declaration but still emits activate/route-map/BFD lines — bricks frr-reload for all peers [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary
`pkg/frr/policy_render.go` guards the BGP **neighbor declaration** loop with `if n.PeerAS == 0 { continue }`, but the **address-family activation** loop and the **BFD** accumulator iterate `bgp.Neighbors` with **no** `PeerAS == 0` guard. A leniently-loaded or peer-synced neighbor with `remote-as 0` is therefore kept out of the `neighbor <ip> remote-as ...` declaration yet still emits `activate` / route-map / `neighbor <ip> bfd` lines for an **undeclared** neighbor.

## Evidence (origin/master)
- `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:912` — declaration loop: `if n.PeerAS == 0 { continue }`.
- `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:1056` — AF-classification loop (`inet4/inet6Neighbors`) iterates `bgp.Neighbors` with no PeerAS guard.
- `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:1291` — BFD accumulator `if n.BFD { bfd.addPeer(...) }` with no PeerAS guard.

## Why it matters
`vtysh`/frr-reload rejects configuration that activates or attaches BFD to a neighbor that was never declared. A single `remote-as 0` neighbor thus **bricks the managed frr-reload for every valid BGP peer** on the box — an availability/correctness defect that defeats the explicit fail-closed intent of #2963 (which added the declaration-loop guard).

## Fix direction
Build one `validNeighbors` slice (`PeerAS != 0`) once and reuse it in the declaration loop, the AF-classification loop, and the BFD accumulator so all three agree on which neighbors are renderable.

## Provenance
codex-review-179 [C179-098] (Medium).

## #5519 — frr: an unrenderable (zero-next-hop) static default route still suppresses the DHCP-learned default → no default route / remote lockout [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary
`renderDHCPDefaults` marks an IPv4 default as statically present (suppressing the DHCP-learned default) for **any** `StaticRoute` whose destination is `0.0.0.0/0`, but `renderStaticRoute` emits **nothing** for a zero-next-hop, non-discard default. Deleting the last ECMP next-hop of a static default route (while leaving the `routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0` stanza present) therefore leaves a `0.0.0.0/0` object that renders no FIB entry **and** still suppresses the DHCP fallback → **no default route is installed at all**.

## Evidence (origin/master)
- `pkg/frr/config_render.go:236` — `renderDHCPDefaults` sets `hasV4Default` for any StaticRoute with `Destination == "0.0.0.0/0"`.
- `pkg/frr/config_render.go:140` — `renderStaticRoute`: `if len(sr.NextHops) == 0 { return "" }` (zero-next-hop non-discard default renders nothing; #3872).

## Why it matters
A routine day-2 edit (removing the last next-hop from a static default on a DHCP-WAN box) silently drops the default route, causing **WAN / management remote lockout**. Reachable in normal operation, no malformed input required.

## Fix direction
Derive DHCP-default suppression from the static default's **actual renderability**: only set `hasV4Default` when the static `0.0.0.0/0` route will emit a FIB entry (has next-hop(s) or is an explicit discard/reject). Skip suppression for a zero-next-hop non-discard default so the DHCP-learned default survives.

## Provenance
codex-review-179 [C179-099] (Medium).

## #5520 — grpcapi/zeroize: factory reset misses the root account SSH key (/root/.ssh) and userdel -r root — prior tenant root access survives [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary
gRPC `Zeroize` (factory reset) iterates managed accounts through a generic `/home/<name>/.ssh/...` teardown loop and runs `userdel -r <name>`, with **no special case for the `root` account**. On a managed-root appliance the daemon writes a real provisioning marker for `root` (`markProvisioned("root", 0)`), so zeroize attempts to wipe `/home/root/.ssh` (which does not exist — the real key is at `/root/.ssh`) and to `userdel -r root` (which fails / is refused for UID 0). Result: the prior tenant's **root SSH authorized_keys survives a "successful" factory reset**, and the reset can permanently fail on the root account.

## Evidence (origin/master)
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_zeroize.go:418` — `keysFile := filepath.Join(zeroizeHomeBase, name, ".ssh", ...)` (generic `/home/<name>`), no `name == "root"` branch.
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1712` — `markProvisioned("root", 0)` writes a genuine `root` provisioning marker that feeds the zeroize account list.

## Why it matters
Security / multi-tenant factory-reset integrity: a decommissioned appliance retains the previous operator's root SSH access after a reported-successful zeroize. This is the same class as #5280/#5281 but a **distinct locus** — those cover the configured `-config` root path and the apply-gate/stop-xpfd race; neither special-cases the root **account** SSH key or `userdel -r root`.

## Fix direction
Special-case `name == "root"` before the generic teardown: remove `rootAuthorizedKeysPath()` (`/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`), lock the root password, and **never** `userdel` UID 0. Add a zeroize test asserting `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` is removed and root is not userdel'd.

## Provenance
codex-review-179 [C179-106] (Medium, security). Related to but distinct from #5280 / #5281.

## #5521 — grpcapi: show security dynamic-address renders feed URLs verbatim — discloses embedded basic-auth/query credentials (RedactURL bypassed) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary
`show security dynamic-address` renders each feed's URL verbatim to the client, disclosing any basic-auth userinfo (`https://user:token@host/...`) or query-string credentials embedded in the feed URL. The project already has `config.RedactURL` and applies it to sibling URL fields, but this show/export surface bypasses it.

## Evidence (origin/master)
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_security_text.go:869` — `fmt.Fprintf(buf, "  URL: %s\n", feed.URL)` (raw, unredacted).
- `pkg/config/secret.go:93` — `RedactURL` exists; e.g. `pkg/config/compiler_system.go:597` applies it to a sibling URL field.

## Why it matters
Security / credential disclosure: a read-only management client (and any command-output logging or support bundle) receives embedded feed credentials in cleartext. Dynamic-address feeds routinely carry per-tenant bearer tokens in the URL.

## Fix direction
Render `config.RedactURL(feed.URL)` on all show/export surfaces that print feed URLs (text and structured). Grep for other raw `feed.URL` / URL-bearing render sites and route them through the redactor. Add a test asserting userinfo/query tokens are redacted in the `show security dynamic-address` output.

## Provenance
codex-review-179 [C179-111] (Medium, security). Related to the RedactURL work in #5458/#5464 (which covered schemeless authority userinfo, not this show surface).

## #5522 — snmp/config: trap-group 'categories' is accepted but never enforced — excluded receivers still get every link notification (filter bypass) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary
The compiler recognizes `snmp trap-group <g> categories <cat>` in the grammar but **discards** it — `SNMPTrapGroup` has no `Categories` field, and the trap sender has no category guard. A trap-group scoped by the operator to exclude a category (e.g. `link`) therefore still receives **every** linkUp/linkDown (and other) notification. The configured category filter is silently inert.

## Evidence (origin/master)
- `pkg/config/compiler_system.go` — `case "categories":` is matched but stores nothing (no `Categories` field on `SNMPTrapGroup`).
- `pkg/snmp/traps.go` — `sendLinkTraps` / link-trap construction has no per-group category membership check.

## Why it matters
Correctness / vSRX-parity / information-exposure: an operator who scopes a trap-group to specific categories has that intent silently violated — receivers get notifications they were configured to be excluded from. This is a concrete, security-adjacent instance of the "unmodeled Junos leaf commits clean and is silently inert" root cause tracked broadly in #4313, but it is a discrete, actionable filter-bypass worth its own fix.

## Fix direction
Add a `Categories` field to `SNMPTrapGroup`, retain/validate the configured set at compile, include it in the SNMP reconcile hash, and gate link-trap (and other category-tagged) construction on category membership. Add a test asserting a `link`-excluding group receives no linkUp/linkDown.

## Provenance
codex-review-179 [C179-120] (Medium, vSRX-parity/correctness). Concrete instance under the #4313 umbrella.

## #5544 — snmp/v3: DES privacy salt omits engineBoots prefix (RFC 3414 §8.1.1.1 cross-boot uniqueness recommendation) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary

Follow-up hardening nit surfaced during the #5032 review (PR #5542, merged
fb1285454). The DES privacy salt is now a random-seeded 64-bit monotonic
counter (fixing the within-boot IV-uniqueness defect #5032), but it does
**not** embed `engineBoots`.

## RFC basis

RFC 3414 §8.1.1.1 **RECOMMENDS** the DES salt be `snmpEngineBoots(4) ||
local-integer(4)` so cross-**reboot** IV uniqueness is *deterministic*
rather than probabilistic. The current implementation
(`pkg/snmp/v3.go` `nextPrivSalt`) emits a full 8-byte counter with no boots
prefix.

## Consequence (low severity)

- **Within-boot** uniqueness — the actual #5032 defect — is now
  deterministic for both DES and AES. This issue does NOT reopen #5032.
- **Cross-reboot** DES IV uniqueness relies on the crypto/rand re-seed of
  the counter at boot (birthday bound on 2^64), not on a boots prefix. A
  cross-boot DES IV collision is astronomically improbable
  (~2^-64-per-pair) and is **unchanged from the pre-#5032 pure-random
  behavior** — this is strictly better than before, not a regression.
- The AES-CFB path already embeds `engineBoots` in its IV
  (`boots || time || salt`), so AES cross-reboot uniqueness is already
  deterministic. **This nit is DES-only, and DES privacy is a
  legacy/deprecated cipher.**
- Interop is unaffected: the 8-byte salt is transmitted verbatim in
  `msgPrivacyParameters` and the receiver reconstructs the IV from it
  directly; no manager validates a boots-prefix structure.

## Proposed fix (future hardening, priority very-low)

For the DES path only, construct the salt as `engineBoots(4) ||
counter-low(4)` (the counter supplies the local-integer). Keep the AES path
as-is. Add a test asserting the DES salt's high 4 bytes equal the current
`engineBoots`.

Priority: **very-low** — legacy cipher, RFC *recommendation* (not MUST),

*(truncated — 42 lines total)*

## #5554 — cli: 'request system zeroize' hardcodes /etc/xpf config root, not the configured root (secret retention on non-default -config) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary

Follow-up to #5280 (fixed in PR #5552, merged). The **gRPC** zeroize path now
erases the CONFIGURED config root via `configstore.Store.ConfigPath()`. But the
**local CLI** `request system zeroize` path has the SAME hardcoded-path defect,
uncorrected:

- `pkg/cli/cli_request_system.go:80` — `configDir := "/etc/xpf"` (hardcoded).

## Impact (security — secret retention)

An operator who runs xpfd with a non-default `-config` root (e.g.
`-config /srv/xpf/site.conf`) and then runs the LOCAL CLI `request system
zeroize` will wipe the wrong hardcoded `/etc/xpf` directory and LEAVE the real
config + secrets (`.configdb`, `master.key`, TLS material, rollback slots) on
disk at the configured root — the exact incomplete-wipe / secret-retention hole
#5280 fixed for the gRPC path. Same defect shape, different code path.

## Fix

Mirror the #5280/#5552 fix on the CLI path: resolve the config root from the
same source-of-truth the daemon loads/persists from (the configured `-config`
root, e.g. via the same `ConfigPath()` accessor or the value the CLI already
knows), and fail closed if it can't be determined. If the CLI cannot reach the
daemon's config-store directly, thread the resolved root through the same
mechanism the gRPC handler uses. Add a fail-on-revert test asserting a
non-default configured root is the wipe target (not hardcoded /etc/xpf).

Provenance: #5552 hostile-review residual (a). The author documented this as a
separate follow-up in _Log.md.

Related non-secret note (from the same review, NOT this issue's scope): node-id
lives at hardcoded `/etc/xpf/node-id` (daemon.go:66) and is not wiped by
zeroize — pre-existing, non-secret cluster identity (0/1); track separately if
desired.

## #5561 — api: HTTP REST :8080 config mutation endpoints (config/set, config/load, commit) have no per-principal auth — same RBAC bypass as #5278 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-13)

## Defect

Sibling of #5278 on the SECOND local control surface. The HTTP REST API on
`127.0.0.1:8080` exposes privileged **config-mutation** endpoints —
`POST /api/v1/config/set`, `POST /api/v1/config/load`, and the commit path
(`pkg/api/api.go:86`, `pkg/api/crosssite_5055_test.go` references
`/api/v1/config/set`) — that are loopback-clamped and protected only by
optional metrics-auth (`pkg/api/auth.go` `metricsRequireAuth`, default off on a
loopback bind) and #5055 cross-site (browser CSRF) checks. There is **no
per-principal authentication/authorization**: any provisioned non-super
login-class shell user (the daemon gives each a `/bin/bash` account) can `curl`
`127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/config/set|load` and mutate/commit config, bypassing the
CLI RBAC (`pkg/cli/permissions.go`, client-side only) exactly as #5278 does over
gRPC.

## Why this is its own issue

model (#4304), and enforce the required permission server-side on

## #5562 — userspace-dp snapshot refresh: validation and forwarding rotate as separate ArcSwaps — worker can stamp a stale permit with the new generation (persistent policy fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-01)

## Summary
`snapshot_refresh` publishes the per-worker validation state and the forwarding state through two **independent** ArcSwaps. A worker that loads the new validation but still holds the old forwarding can evaluate an old permit and insert it into the flow cache stamped with the **new** generation. After forwarding rotates, generation-equality no longer invalidates that cached decision, so a stale permit survives past the transient publication window — a persistent policy fail-open (a new deny is not guaranteed to invalidate every stale permit at one coherent boundary).

## Location (verified vs origin/master `0ab8a90a8`)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/snapshot_refresh.rs` — `self.validation = ValidationState{...}` is set, then near the end of the refresh:
  - `self.shared_validation.store(Arc::new(self.validation));`
  - `self.ha.forwarding.store(Arc::new(self.forwarding.clone()));`
  are two **separate** stores; CoS owner/lease maps rotate later (`refresh_cos_owner_worker_map_from_identities()`).
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/loop_body/mod.rs:364-372` loads validation and forwarding independently.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/flow_cache.rs:167-174` stamps the cache lookup with the separately-loaded validation generation.

## Mechanism
1. Refresh stores new validation (store A) before new forwarding (store B).
2. Between A and B, a worker loads new validation + old forwarding, evaluates an old permit, and caches it stamped with the new generation.
3. Forwarding rotates (store B). Because the cache entry already carries the new generation, generation-equality does not invalidate it.
4. The stale permit outlives the publication window. Status honestly reports only the new generation, hiding the incoherence.

The inverse schedule (old validation loaded before both stores, new forwarding afterward) can likewise retain an old-generation cached permit while newer policy is visible. Forwarding carries no common commit tag, so no reader-retry compares a forwarding generation.

## Why it is real vs current origin/master
The two stores are still distinct ArcSwaps (verified above). Build-first coordinator validation prevents rejection-time mutation but does not make the multiple stores one worker-visible commit; flow-cache generation checks are ineffective once an old decision is stamped with the new validation value.

## Fix direction
Build a generation-tagged `WorkerRuntimeSnapshot` bundling validation + forwarding + generation-coupled references and publish it with **one** ArcSwap; pin one bundle per worker iteration for both command drain and RX processing, and invalidate cache/session state on bundle-identity change. Add deterministic barriers around writer stores and worker loads asserting old-or-new (never mixed) permit/deny behavior, plus a stress test rejecting mixed-generation tuples.

## Severity
High (persistent firewall fail-open on the packet path).

## Related open issues (same non-atomic multi-ArcSwap publication family — likely share the single-bundle fix, but distinct store pairs)
- #5166 forwarding published before CoS owner/lease maps (forwarding↔CoS pair)
- #5169 apply_snapshot lacks the generation-monotonicity guard (reused/rolled-back generation)
- #5171 defer_workers ACKs before the full forwarding+map build
This finding is the **validation↔forwarding** store-order + new-generation cache-stamp schedule, not covered by the above.

## Provenance
codex-review-180 [C180-001] (High/High-confidence). Verified against origin/master 0ab8a90a8.

## #5563 — cluster: planned failover can promote a peer with stale security policy — transfer readiness has no applied-config epoch [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-21)

## Summary
Manual/planned failover readiness is defined solely in terms of **session** bulk state; it carries neither the sender's current config generation nor the receiver's successfully-applied config generation. A standby can therefore be promoted while running a **stale** policy/application/zone snapshot, so synced sessions and new packets are evaluated under old config: after a tightening commit the promoted node admits traffic the operator denied (fail-open); after a loosening commit it drops allowed traffic (false-deny).

## Location (verified vs origin/master `0ab8a90a8`)
- `pkg/cluster/sync.go` — `TransferReadinessSnapshot{ Connected, PendingBulkAckEpoch, PendingBulkAckAge, BulkReceiveInProgress, BulkReceiveEpoch, BulkReceiveSessions }` and `ReadyForManualFailover()` observe only session bulk markers — no config-generation field.
- `pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go` — `resetRecvGen()` clears the session gen maps and also does `s.lastAppliedConfigGen.Store(0)` on a bulk start; the comment asserts the next config is always current, but the bulk protocol does not enforce that the peer actually applied the authoritative config.

## Mechanism
First packet is admitted on node A under snapshot C2 and its session (PolicyID/counter/app-timeout, **no config epoch**) is synced to B. A restrictive C3 can fail or be dropped on B (config apply loop / full queue) while session bulk/barriers settle. `computeUserspaceTransferReadiness` returns ready from connectivity + session markers; request/ack/commit then promotes B. New packets and imported sessions are evaluated/reused under stale C2. A routine `BulkStart` also clears B's C2/C3 config-ordering high-water and can admit an older reordered config.

## Why it is real vs current origin/master
`TransferReadinessSnapshot` still has no applied-config epoch, and `resetRecvGen` still resets the config high-water on a session bulk (verified above). Connectivity/protocol-version guards exist and policy invalidation runs only after a config actually applies, but nothing proves the target applied the source's current config before promotion. `ConfigsApplyFailed`/`Errors` are status-only; session records carry PolicyID/PolicyCounterIdx/AppTimeout, not a config generation.

## Fix direction
Decouple session-install generations from config generations. Give config sync a boot/session identity + monotonic epoch; ACK only after `OnConfigReceived` successfully publishes the dataplane snapshot; expose local/peer applied epochs in transfer readiness; block planned failover until `peer_applied_config_epoch == local_authoritative_config_epoch`. Do not clear config ordering on a session `BulkStart` — reset it only on authenticated sender-boot identity change. Add an end-to-end test: C2 applied, C3 failed/dropped, bulk settled → failover refused; plus reordered-old-config-across-BulkStart.

## Severity
High (fail-open AND false-deny at failover — exactly when HA is needed).

## Related open issues (distinct mechanisms; this is the readiness-gate epoch)
- #5274 session-sync envelope lacks a config epoch (session-install-time stale permit)
- #5084 queued config-apply items carry no peer boot/connection epoch
- #4957 active-text-match shortcut treats promoted-but-unapplied config as converged
None gate **planned-failover readiness** on `peer_applied == authoritative`.

codex-review-180 [C180-002 / lane Z5-F001] (High/High-confidence). Verified against origin/master 0ab8a90a8.

## #5564 — daemon: standby config-sync tail failures permanently bypass policy session invalidation (syncAndApply returns before invalidators) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Summary
On the HA receive side, `syncAndApply` promotes the peer config to active and applies the dataplane snapshot, but returns early on **any** `applyConfigLocked` error — before the three session invalidators run. A non-fatal best-effort tail failure (host-inbound/lo0 nft, networkd, etc.) therefore leaves surviving established sessions with their **old** authorization on an armed standby. Because the store already holds the incoming text, the next peer re-push hits the equal-active-text fast path and returns success without re-entering `syncAndApply`, making the omission **permanent**.

## Location (verified vs origin/master `0ab8a90a8`)
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go` `syncAndApply`:
  ```go
  compiled, err := d.store.SyncApply(configText, chassisPreserve)   // promotes active BEFORE reconcile
  ...
  if err := d.applyConfigLocked(d.applyCancelCtx(), compiled); err != nil {
      return nil, err            // <-- early return on ANY apply error
  }
  d.clearSessionsForDeletedPolicies(oldActive, compiled)
  d.clearSessionsForModifiedPolicies(oldActive, compiled)
  d.clearSessionsForDefaultPolicyChange(oldActive, compiled)
  ```
- Contrast the primary path `applyAndSyncCommitted`, which classifies non-fatal tail errors (`applyErrSkipsPeerSync`) and **still** runs all three invalidators.

## Mechanism
1. Peer pushes a tightened/deleted policy; standby `SyncApply` promotes the new active tree; dataplane snapshot applies (armed).
2. A non-fatal tail subsystem returns an error → `applyConfigLocked` returns non-nil → `syncAndApply` returns before the three `clearSessionsFor*` calls.
3. On the next peer re-push, `handleConfigSync` takes the equal-active-text fast path and returns success, never re-running the invalidators.
4. A surviving established session retains old authorization and is eligible to forward immediately after failover under the new policy.

## Why it is real vs current origin/master
`syncAndApply` still returns `nil, err` before the invalidators (verified). The HA delete stream mitigates common cases but is bounded (`QueueDeleteV4/V6` journal evicts old deletes) and does not replace the receiver's promised local invalidation before takeover.

## Fix direction
Make `syncAndApply` mirror `applyAndSyncCommitted`: capture `applyErr`, return early only for fatal/stop classes (`applyErrSkipsPeerSync`), run all invalidators for non-fatal tail errors, then return `compiled, applyErr`. Add a synced-standby test with a real old/new policy diff, injected non-fatal tail error, surviving v4/v6 sessions, and an equal-text-retry assertion.

## Severity
High (fail-open — deleted/tightened/default-flip policy leaves the standby forwarding a revoked session; visible at failover).

## Related open issues
- #4957 (active-text-match shortcut skips reconcile retry) — related equal-text mechanism, distinct sub-defect (this is the skipped session invalidators on the receive side).

## Provenance
codex-review-180 [C180-003 / lane Z5-F003] (High/High-confidence). Verified against origin/master 0ab8a90a8.

## #5565 — host-inbound: a per-interface IKE/ident exception is widened to every interface in the zone [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary
A per-interface `host-inbound-traffic` IKE (or ident-reset) exception is projected into a single **zone-wide** bit and then emitted as a terminal nft exception across the whole zone's iifname set — ahead of the interface-specific coarse drops. A least-privilege override on one interface therefore falsely admits IKE (or actively RST-resets ident) on sibling interfaces that have no such statement.

## Location (verified vs origin/master `0ab8a90a8`)
- `pkg/config/junos_host_deny.go` `junosHostProjectProgram`: `CoarseAdmitsIKE: zoneCoarseAdmitsIKE(zc)` / `CoarseIdentResets: zoneCoarseIdentResets(zc)` are single zone-wide bits (derived by unioning per-interface overrides via `zoneEffectiveSystemServices`).
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go` `emitJunosHostDenyProgram`: `iif := nftIifnameSet(p.IngressIfnames)` (every non-lifeline netdev in the zone) then `*rules = append(*rules, "    iifname "+iif+" udp dport { 500, 4500 } accept")` when `p.CoarseAdmitsIKE` — a destination-independent terminal accept across the FULL iifname set, emitted before the per-interface destination-scoped coarse drops.

## Mechanism
Give `ge-0/0/1.0` an additive `ike` override and leave sibling `ge-0/0/2.0` at zone-default `ping`. Generated nft contains `iifname { "ge-0-0-1", "ge-0-0-2" } udp dport { 500, 4500 } accept` before `ip daddr 10.0.3.10 ... drop`, so IKE is admitted on the sibling. The same aggregate root can synthesize a TCP/113 ident RST on a sibling that should silently deny. `BuildZoneHostInboundViews` correctly builds separate per-interface views, but the earlier terminal exception ends the base chain before those drops.

## Why it is real vs current origin/master
The zone-wide `CoarseAdmitsIKE` bit and the full-zone iifname emission are both present (verified). Global ESP/AH and reply-direction exceptions are intentionally global; this is limited to exceptions whose truth was derived from one effective interface set.

## Fix direction
Derive IKE and ident exception scopes **per effective interface view**, emit each shield only for the corresponding iifname/address group (group interfaces by identical effective exception bits to keep O(1) rule/set lookups). Add `ike`/`ipsec`/`all`/`any-service`/`ident-reset` mixed-interface fixtures with rule-order AND packet-verdict oracles.

## Severity
Medium (host-inbound false-allow / management-plane over-reach without a matching config statement, deny counter, or tuple log; contradicts the additive per-interface service matrix).

## Provenance
codex-review-180 [C180-004 / lane Z4] (Medium/High-confidence). Verified against origin/master 0ab8a90a8.

## #5566 — host-inbound: kernel-established inbound host sessions retain authorization after a coarse host-service tightening (nft ct established accept precedes per-interface drops) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Summary
The nft host-input chain accepts original-direction `established,related` conntrack entries **before** the current per-interface coarse host-inbound drops, and replacing the `xpf_hostinbound` table does not flush Linux conntrack. Removing a host service (SSH/HTTPS/SNMP/...) therefore leaves an existing direct-kernel connection authorized under the OLD configuration — unlike the Rust userspace path, which rechecks the effective host-inbound set on every local-delivery session hit and tears a denied session down.

## Location (verified vs origin/master `0ab8a90a8`)
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go`: in the fine-program branch, `(5) Residual full established accept` → `rules = append(rules, "    ct state established,related accept")` is emitted before the per-interface coarse drops; in the no-fine-program `else` branch, `ct state established,related accept` is the first rule. Table replacement does not flush conntrack.
- Contrast `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs` (~1149) — the session-HIT local-delivery path re-checks the current effective host-inbound set on every hit and tears down a now-denied session (per the #3070/#3485 comment).

## Mechanism
A direct kernel-local inbound flow admitted under an old host-inbound set creates a conntrack entry. After tightening, with no fine program (and for non-denied sources with one), the broad `ct state established,related accept` precedes every per-interface coarse drop, so subsequent original-direction packets keep old authorization and produce no host-inbound deny counter/log. The equivalent userspace-local session is revoked → a false allow limited to the direct-kernel delivery path.

## Why it is real vs current origin/master
Rule ordering (established-accept before coarse drops) verified above; conntrack is not flushed on table replacement. Firewall-originated return flows legitimately need the earlier `ct direction reply` exception, but that does not cover a remote-originated flow tightened only by the coarse service set.

## Fix direction
Keep `ct direction reply` before host-inbound, but require original-direction `established` packets to pass the **current** per-interface coarse rules before acceptance. Add a netns test: establish a host flow, tighten the service set without clearing conntrack, verify the next original-direction packet drops and `xpfhi_` increments.

## Severity
Medium (host-inbound false-allow on the direct-kernel path; a service removal reports success while an existing connection persists under old authorization).

## Provenance
codex-review-180 [C180-005 / lane Z4] (Medium/High-confidence). Verified against origin/master 0ab8a90a8.

## #5567 — userspace-dp: unbuildable Time Exceeded / PTB attempts consume the process-global reply token before feasibility — cross-interface diagnostic starvation (DoS/false-deny) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary
Locally-generated ICMP Time Exceeded and Packet-Too-Big replies consume the **process-global per-reason** rate-limit token BEFORE the egress object / family builder proves any reply bytes exist. A flood of reply-eligible-but-unbuildable triggers on one interface can drain the shared token bucket and suppress buildable PMTUD/traceroute diagnostics for legitimate traffic on **another** interface, without changing the (correct) terminal drop of the trigger packet.

## Location (verified vs origin/master `0ab8a90a8`)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp.rs`: `if !allow_generated_error(GeneratedErrorReason::TimeExceeded) { ...; return None; }` runs **before** `let egress = forwarding.egress.get(&ingress_ident.ifindex)?;` and the family builders.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/dispatch/mod.rs` (~230): PTB has the same ordering — `ptb_reply_suppressed(...) && allow_generated_error(PacketTooBig)` consumes the token, then `build_frag_needed_v4` / `build_packet_too_big_v6` can return `None`.

## Mechanism
Every successful `allow_generated_error*` advances the shared GCRA TAT; denied calls do not refund. A missing egress object, missing family address, or fallible builder is reached only after that irreversible consume. Configure interface A (addressed, buildable) and interface B (no matching-family egress/builder). Flood >1000-token burst of reply-eligible TTL=1 / oversized-DF packets on B, then send a legitimate trigger on A within the refill window → A's generated error is suppressed by B's failed builds. Because TE/PTB buckets are process-global (not per-zone/interface), the failed work on B creates cross-interface false denial. The reject path already does build-first / consume-only-on-`Some(bytes)` — this path does not.

## Why it is real vs current origin/master
Token-before-build ordering verified at both sites. RFC suppression predicates run first but do not prove builder feasibility. This is not a forwarding fail-open (the trigger is still dropped), hence Medium.

## Fix direction
Build the TE/PTB frame first as a side-effect-free feasibility step, consume the reason token only for `Some(bytes)`, then classify/enqueue — matching the existing reject implementation (`#3656`). Add cross-interface tests that drain failed builders and assert a legitimate builder still receives the full burst, and that counters move only for genuinely rate-limited feasible replies.

## Severity
Medium (DoS/false-deny of PMTUD + TTL diagnostics for unrelated flows; PTB starvation can sustain blackholes for PMTUD-dependent flows; rate-limit counters misattribute suppression).

## Provenance
codex-review-180 [C180-006 / lane Z3-F003 TE-PTB half] (Medium/High-confidence). Distinct from #3656 (reject build-before-consume). Verified against origin/master 0ab8a90a8.

## #5568 — userspace-dp: filter/policy/host-inbound/embedded-ICMP classifiers derive scalar L4 semantics from Ethernet slack (not the IP-declared datagram) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Summary
`#5150` clamped the flexible-match byte slices to the IP-declared datagram end, but the **scalar** L4/fragment inputs are still derived from the physical frame length / raw `frame[l3..]` rather than the declared end. Attacker-influenced Ethernet padding beyond the declared IP length can therefore manufacture ICMP type/code presence, TCP flags, fragment state, and `l4_present` — turning a non-match into a permit, false-dropping a packet, manufacturing fragment status, touching an established session, or producing misleading policy/filter counters and logs.

## Location (verified vs origin/master `0ab8a90a8`)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/frame/inspect.rs` `term_match_extra_from_frame`:
  - `is_fragment` / `non_first_fragment` derive from `frame.get(meta.l3_offset..)` (raw), not a declared-length-bounded slice.
  - `icmp_type_code_present = ... && (frame.len() >= (meta.l4_offset as usize).saturating_add(2))` uses **physical** `frame.len()`, while `declared_end = ip_declared_end(...)` is computed only afterward and used only for the `#5150` flex slices.
- Downstream scalar consumers: `poll_descriptor/mod.rs` (~126-134 `policy_packet_icmp`; ~1712-1718 / ~2202-2226 input/lo0 filter; ~2216-2219 host-inbound).
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/parse.rs` (~45-87,180-205) bounds quoted inner L4 reads by the outer backing slice, not the quoted IP declaration.

## Mechanism
Send an Ethernet-minimum IPv4 frame with `protocol=ICMP`, `total_length=20` (no declared ICMP bytes), and bytes `8,0` at the shim-stamped `l4_offset` in padding. `term_match_extra_from_frame` sees `frame.len() >= l4+2`, sets `l4_present=true`, returns echo-request; policy/filter/host-inbound all consume the fabricated type/code. A terminal permit constrained to echo-request matches a datagram containing no ICMP header (a terminal deny false-drops it). For IPv6, payload-length 0 + padding beginning with a fragment header makes `is_fragment` true. Embedded-ICMP quote parsing can manufacture an existing-session tuple from padding.

## Why it is real vs current origin/master
`icmp_type_code_present`/`is_fragment`/`non_first_fragment` still use physical bytes (verified); `#5150` only clamped the flex slices. The metadata is documented (inspect.rs ~1315-1319) as NOT guaranteeing L4 lies within the IP-declared datagram, and no downstream validator removes the fabricated scalar match before policy/filter evaluation.

## Fix direction
Compute the family-aware `declared_end` before any fragment/L4 extraction; pass `frame.get(l3..declared_end)` to the fragment walkers; require `l4+2 <= declared_end` for ICMP and `l4`+relevant TCP bytes for flags; else `l4_present=false`. Apply the same declared-inner-bound validation to the embedded IPv4/IPv6 quote parsers (without rejecting RFC-minimum quotes whose original declared length exceeds the available quote). Add short-declared-length + physical-slack tests for ICMP type/code, TCP flags, first/non-first fragment, host-inbound, junos application policy, input/lo0 filters, and embedded-session lookup.

## Severity
Medium (packet-path classification fail-open/false-deny; security rules and host-control admission must fail closed on malformed/truncated packets).

## Related open issues (distinct loci)
- #5141 TCP segmentation promotes bytes beyond the IP-declared datagram
- #5140 post-GRE-decap ICMP/host-inbound indexes outer raw_frame with inner offset
This is the residual scalar-match/fragment/embedded-session surface outside #2361/#2449/#5150.

## Provenance
codex-review-180 [C180-007 / lane Z3-F002] (Medium/High-confidence). Verified against origin/master 0ab8a90a8.

## #5569 — userspace-dp: egress-filtered reject replies drain the per-zone reject token before being discarded (same-zone cross-protocol starvation) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Summary
On the reject path, a **buildable** generated reject passes feasibility and the TX budget and irreversibly consumes the shared per-zone reject token **before** generated-reply output-filter/policer classification can discard it. Traffic whose generated ICMP is intentionally filtered can therefore exhaust the same-zone bucket and suppress a later TCP RST that the output filter would have permitted — a same-zone, cross-protocol/source availability defect.

## Location (verified vs origin/master `0ab8a90a8`)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs`: `if !allow_generated_reject(forwarding, from_zone_id) { ... return false; }` consumes the zone token, THEN `let verdict = classify_generated_reply(...)` runs and `if verdict.drop { ...; return false; }` can discard the (already token-charged) reply.

## Mechanism
In one ingress zone, configure policy/filter reject and an output filter that discards generated ICMP but permits TCP RST. Flood rejected UDP/ICMP: each trigger builds a valid ICMP unreachable, passes the TX budget, consumes `allow_generated_reject`, then `classify_generated_reply` returns `drop`. The flood drains the zone's shared reject bucket. A subsequent rejected TCP SYN — whose RST would pass the output filter — fails at the token check and silently drops. Policy and filter rejects share the bucket by design (#3618), so either source starves the other.

## Why it is real vs current origin/master
`#3656` moved *unbuildable* frames before token consumption, but the output-filter classification still runs AFTER the consume (verified). Per-zone buckets prevent only cross-zone starvation. The behavior needs no malformed packets and works with ordinary supported filters.

## Fix direction
Ensure a reply discarded by generated-reply output classification does not consume the per-zone reject token: either a side-effect-free terminal viability pass before the token, classify-once-before-token with documented policer semantics, or a correct token-refund primitive (preserve the truthful source-split counters). Add a regression that records bucket capacity, drives repeated output-filter drops, then proves an output-permitted RST still consumes the original capacity; cover policy + filter sources and VLAN logical-zone resolution.

## Severity
Medium (availability — an attacker turns intentionally-suppressed replies into a token-exhaustion channel that downgrades unrelated output-permitted rejects to silent drops).

## Provenance
codex-review-180 [C180-008 / lane Z3-F003 output-filter half] (Medium/High-confidence). Distinct from #3656/#3618/#3615/#3661. Verified against origin/master 0ab8a90a8.

## Summary
The policy-counter clear path recognizes only the first two tokens (`policies hit-count`) and never requires exact arity before issuing an **unscoped global** clear. `dispatchOperational` → `handleClear` → `handleClearSecurity(["policies","hit-count","from-zone","trust"])` returns `err=<nil>` and issues `clear-policy-counters`; the scoped-looking trailing input is discarded and all counters reset. `len(args) >= 2` gate + unscoped global backend action verified. (`#3448/#3782` concern counter-reset races inside an already-authorized global clear — not this parser acceptance.)

## Summary
`loadDDNSState` reads the entire durable ownership file into memory with a single `os.ReadFile` before any JSON/version/record-count/semantic validation. ## #5582 — host-inbound: a fresh passive WireGuard listener is denied by restricted kernel host-inbound policy (no wireguard token / dynamic listen-port exception) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-11)

## Location (verified vs origin/master `0ab8a90a8`)
