- `pkg/config/host_inbound_tokens.go`: no `wireguard` / listen-port token (grep: none).
- `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go` (~626): the NEW-packet catch-all drop with no preceding UDP/51820 admission.

## Mechanism
For the configured listen port, local-destination WG UDP is steered to Linux. A first passive handshake on a restricted zoned address is conntrack NEW, misses the service accepts, hits the catch-all drop (on an addressed unzoned interface it hits the #4420 catch-all). Responses to an xpf-initiated handshake are admitted as established (explaining existing interop success); the interop harness makes xpf the initiator first and reuses the same tuple, so it never exercises a fresh passive listener. `system-services all` admits it, but a blanket opening is not a scoped WireGuard contract.

## Why it is real vs current origin/master
Steer-to-kernel present; no WG host-inbound token (verified). Distinct from the documented multi-tunnel steering limitation — even the first configured port is correctly steered and then denied at kernel input.

## Fix direction
Decide whether a configured WireGuard listener implies host admission or requires an explicit dynamic `wireguard` service; generate an exact listen-port, local-address/interface-scoped kernel rule accordingly (keep the shim local-destination + exact-port checks unchanged so transit/DNAT UDP is never shunted around policy). Add a clean-state live test: remove the xpf peer endpoint, flush the UDP conntrack tuple, start the external peer as initiator, prove handshake + inner traffic without `system-services all`.

## Severity
Medium (host-inbound false-deny / availability). Confidence Medium — repository policy does not clearly state whether tunnel configuration implies host admission; this issue also asks that question.

## Provenance
codex-review-180 [C180-025 / lane Z4] (Medium severity / Medium confidence). Verified against origin/master 0ab8a90a8.

## #5583 — [cohort] codex-review-180 low-materiality + doc-drift survivors (4 items) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-06)

The Low-tier survivors of codex-review-180 (base 4567ffb78), each verified LIVE against current origin/master `0ab8a90a8`. Low operational materiality — grouped per the triage cohort convention. The High/Medium findings are filed individually (#5562–#5582).

## Items

- **[C180-021] AF_XDP packet-processing doc states an obsolete non-SYN shim drop** — `docs/afxdp-packet-processing.md:32-33` still says "Non-SYN TCP without a live entry in `userspace_sessions` BPF map is dropped", but `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs` (~584-645) now redirects all ordinary session misses and delegates stale RST/FIN handling to `poll_descriptor` strict-syn-check. Doc-contract drift that can misdirect validation to the wrong enforcement layer. Fix: replace item 7 with the current all-misses-to-userspace contract, cite the Rust bare RST/FIN guard, add a drift check. Label: documentation.

- **[C180-023] Malformed DNAT prefix metadata silently narrows to one exact host** — `userspace-dp/src/nat/destination.rs` (~319): a non-empty but unparseable `destination_prefix` falls back to `DnatDest::Host(destination_address)` when the base address parses, recording no `record_parse_error`. A present-but-invalid additive field is treated as absent, silently converting a prefix rule into one exact-host rule (pre-#3164 narrowing) with no telemetry. Requires corrupt/incompatible/mixed-version snapshot metadata (ordinary Go builder emits canonical prefixes), and it narrows rather than widens → Low. Fix: if `destination_prefix` is non-empty and fails `IpNet` parse, `record_parse_error` and skip the row (reserve host fallback for a genuinely absent field); add malformed-prefix-with-valid-base + family-consistency tests. Distinct from #3029/#3164/#4718.

- **[C180-024] TCP-flags grammar discards unbalanced/reversed parentheses** — `pkg/config/tcp_flags.go` (~132): `case "(", ")":` only errors on a negated group, otherwise `continue`s with no depth/order tracking, so `(syn`, `syn)`, `syn)(` all commit as plain `syn` (`required=0x2 forbidden=0x0 ok=true`). Packet mask is not widened (SYN survives), so this is strict-grammar/auditability debt, not an admission bypass → Low. Fix: track paren depth+order, reject close-at-depth-0 / nonzero-depth-at-end / empty/misordered groups; strict tests for leading close, missing close, reversed pairs, nested balanced. Distinct from #3076/#4714/#5455.

- **[C180-026] Shutdown-abandoned SNMP trap jobs are omitted from the drop counter** — `pkg/snmp/traps.go` (~427) exits on `<-stop` without counting buffered jobs; `pkg/snmp/agent.go` (~819) closes `trapStop` but neither drains nor accounts for the pending queue. Queue-full and post-stop enqueue paths do increment `trapsDropped`, so the total specifically omits shutdown abandonment — reporting zero drops while discarding queued link-state traps during SNMP disable / target rotation / shutdown. Safety (no post-stop delivery) is correct; only accounting is wrong → Low (Medium confidence). Fix: define accepted/sent/failed/dropped counters; on stop have the sole queue owner count every dequeued-but-unsent + buffered-abandoned job exactly once (synchronized with worker exit to avoid double-count), expose via existing metrics; extend `agent_stop_leak_4916_test.go`. Label: observability.

## Dropped (not in this cohort)
- **[C180-022]** TX ring backpressure recovery allocates on the overloaded packet path (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/transmit/finalise.rs` retry_tail `Vec::new()` + owned retry `String`) — **duplicate of open #4971** (afxdp/tx: remove String allocation + last_error lock from expected TX retry / partial-submit paths). Same root, dropped.

## #5606 — userspace-dp NAT64: reverse translation broken — Nat64ReverseInfo lost at the PendingForwardRequest boundary (replies emit IPv4; ICMP errors dropped) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-17)

**Severity:** high (NAT64 return path). Surfaced while researching #5177; that
issue is being PLAN-KILLed as scoped because its named leaf fix is unreachable —
the *real* defect is here and larger. Verified read-only against origin/master
`4e0c7f74c` by an adversarial Codex audit + an independent trace, with file:line
evidence.

## Summary
The forward NAT64 BIB/session state is built correctly, but the reverse-direction
`Nat64ReverseInfo` (original v6 src/dst) is **never carried onto the
`PendingForwardRequest`** that drives TX. All three real production request
constructors hard-code `nat64_reverse: None`:

- normal live forwarding — `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forward_request.rs:288-302`
- embedded-ICMP prebuilt forwarding — `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:2537-2557`
- generated time-exceeded forwarding — `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp.rs:257-281`

The real values live only on `SessionMetadata` (`poll_descriptor/mod.rs:3003-3010`
and `:3280-3286`) and are never copied to a request. The AF_INET reverse branch of
`build_nat64_forwarded_frame` *requires* `request.nat64_reverse`
(`afxdp/frame/mod.rs:289-292`) → returns `None`.

## Two coupled defects

### 1. Ordinary reverse TCP/UDP replies emit IPv4 instead of translated IPv6
`build_nat64_forwarded_frame` returns `None` → slow-path fallback
(`tx/dispatch/mod.rs:880-882` / `:1201-1203`) → `extract_l3_packet_with_nat`
picks same-family `apply_nat_ipv4` (`slow_path.rs:379-398`), which **discards the
IPv6 rewrite addresses** (`frame/mod.rs:896-905`) while still rewriting L4 ports,
and the still-IPv4 bytes are written to the TUN (`slowpath.rs:433-467`). NAT64 is
excluded from the flow cache (`flow_cache.rs:321-329`) and the XDP shim does not
translate NAT64 (`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:1427-1437`), so there is no alternate
repair path.

**Small repair:** for an ordinary reverse session `Nat64ReverseInfo` is redundant
— `NatDecision::reverse` already sets `rewrite_src = original_dst` /
`rewrite_dst = original_src` and preserves `nat64` (`nat/mod.rs:106-120`), which
are exactly the `info.orig_dst_v6`/`info.orig_src_v6` the builder wants
(`frame/mod.rs:310-318`). The AF_INET builder can derive `src_v6`/`dst_v6` from
`decision.nat.rewrite_src`/`rewrite_dst`, dropping the dependency on
`request.nat64_reverse`.

*(truncated — 84 lines total)*

- `userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs:250,282` (`frag_assoc`, port-free key) — under a deliberately non-conformant sender reusing one Fragment ID across concurrent flows to the same (src,dst), a non-first fragment can inherit a sibling flow's round-robin pool SNAT source; result is fail-safe (receiver cannot reassemble -> drop), not wrong-destination delivery. - `userspace-dp/src/nptv6.rs:223` (`try_from_snapshots`) — NPTv6 rejects the WHOLE snapshot on any bad/overlapping rule while sibling NAT tables skip-and-continue; fail-CLOSED (safe), an availability divergence justified by the #2241 order-dependent overlap-determinism guard (#3888 scope note).

- `pkg/config/compiler_security_zones.go:134-163` — a bracketed `interfaces [ a b ] host-inbound-traffic { ... }` stanza (reachable only via a raw `load override` block; Junos grammar disallows it) attaches the per-interface override to the FIRST member only (`InterfaceHostInbound[iface.Name()]`); other members fall back to zone-level host-inbound (bounded, not fail-open beyond the zone default). Interface *membership* is already fixed via `zoneInterfaceMembers` (#5248).
- `pkg/config/host_inbound_multicast.go` — well-known routing multicast groups (OSPF 224.0.0.5/6, VRRP 224.0.0.18, PIM 224.0.0.13, ...) are admitted host-wide via the input-chain `policy accept`, not scoped by per-zone `host-inbound-traffic protocols`; fail-open-but-bounded (kernel delivers only to groups a configured daemon joined). Enforcement (iifname-scoped nft set + Rust daddr dimension) explicitly DEFERRED under #4455; the catalog backs only a commit-time advisory today.
- `pkg/config/junos_host_deny.go:884-928` (`junosHostZoneExemptNetdevs`) — IKE/ident exemption is unioned per-netdev, so two VLAN sub-units in the same zone sharing a trunk parent leak one unit's IKE override onto the sibling; IKE is authenticated and same-zone, over-shield only. Distinct from #5557's junos_host_deny.go:825 case-sensitivity item.

## #5611 — userspace-dp: lock the NPTv6 wildcard-vs-concrete overlap-reject edge with an explicit test (#5176 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

**Test-coverage lock-in follow-up to #5176 (MERGED, PR #5610).**

The #5176 NPTv6 `from_zone` scope enforcement is logic-verified correct by the
hostile review, but two edges lack an explicit regression-locking test (coverage
only — no behavior gap):

1. **Wildcard-vs-concrete same-prefix overlap REJECT** (security-critical edge).
   `zones_conflict(a,b) = a.is_empty() || b.is_empty() || a==b` correctly rejects
   a wildcard (`from_zone=""`) rule overlapping a concrete-zone rule with the same
   prefix (empty short-circuits → conflict → snapshot rejected), but there is no
   explicit test asserting it. Current coverage leans on the existing both-empty
   reject + the distinct-non-empty admit. Add a ~4-line `try_from_snapshots`
   `expect_err` for an `empty` + `"untrust"` same-prefix pair (and a
   same-concrete-zone duplicate) to lock the reject edge against a future refactor
   that breaks the empty-short-circuit.

2. **#4339 multi-scope degenerate-duplicate note** (not a bug — fail-closed).
   If the Go scope-expansion (#4339) ever emits two same-name same-prefix entries
   lowering to the SAME zone, Rust `find_overlap` rejects (no name-identity skip)
   while the Go gate admits → a fail-CLOSED config rejection, never a bypass.
   Unusual config; documenting for awareness. (#5176 strictly improves multi-scope:
   pre-#5176 Rust rejected ALL same-prefix multi-scope, even distinct zones.)

Low severity (test parity + a documented fail-closed edge). Surfaced by the
hostile review of PR #5610; explicitly flagged non-blocking for that merge.

## #5658 — nat: static block-to-block & DNAT install lack a minimum-prefix floor — /0 maps entire IPv4 internet 1:1 (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-17)

## Summary
Neither the Go strict commit-check nor the Rust helper backstop enforces a **minimum prefix length** when installing a static block-to-block (`#3031`) or DNAT-prefix (`#3228`) rule. A degenerate `/0` (or absurdly-short) prefix is therefore accepted, producing an identity NAT / local-address registration for the **entire IPv4 internet** — a fail-open the existing fail-closed backstops in the same functions were meant to prevent.

## Finding 1 — Static block-to-block `/0` maps 0.0.0.0/0 ↔ peer/0 (whole-internet 1:1)
Evidence (origin/master `a6fcd463b`):
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/static_nat.rs:387-410` — `from_snapshots` block branch rejects **family mismatch**, **length mismatch**, and **port-bearing** blocks (`#3202`), but has **no floor on `ext_prefix.len` / `int_prefix.len`**. A `/0↔/0` equal-length pair passes and is pushed as a `StaticNatBlock`.
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/static_nat.rs:223` — `host_mask_v4(0)` returns `u32::MAX >> 0 = u32::MAX`; `!hm == 0`, so `contains()` is `(addr & 0) == base(0)` → **true for every IPv4** → every inbound dst matches the first `/0` block and is translated 1:1.
- Go side: `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:947-989` (`validateNATHostMaskStrict`) — `isStaticBlockPair` (equal-length non-host same-family) is accepted; the only block-specific reject is the `#3202` port check (line 969). **No minimum-prefix reject**, so `match 0.0.0.0/0 … then static-nat prefix 10.0.0.0/0` commits.

Trace / repro: `set security nat static rule-set rs rule r match destination-address 0.0.0.0/0` + `then static-nat prefix 10.0.0.0/0`. Commit succeeds → dataplane installs an internet-wide identity/offset static NAT that shadows all inbound destination matching (mis-translation / traffic hijack / blackhole; bypasses subsequent zone policy on the translated address).

## Finding 2 — DNAT `/0` registers 0.0.0.0 as a firewall-local address
Evidence:
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/destination.rs:1049-1052` — `destination_ips_scoped` pushes `slot.network()` **unconditionally** for every non-`off` prefix slot; host expansion is gated by `MAX_LOCAL_PREFIX_HOSTS` (4096) but the **network base is always registered**. For a `/0` slot the base `0.0.0.0` (or `::`) is registered into `local_v4`/`local_v6`, i.e. as an address the firewall proxy-ARP/ND-owns and local-delivers.

Trace / repro: a DNAT rule whose destination prefix is `/0` (or the peer-sync of one) registers `0.0.0.0` as local, perturbing local-delivery classification.

## Materiality
Low–Medium. Requires an operator (or a peer-synced/leniently-loaded config) to author a `/0` NAT prefix — an unusual misconfiguration — but the result is a security-relevant fail-open (internet-wide 1:1 / bogus local address), and both sibling reject branches in the very same functions establish the fail-closed contract this case silently escapes.

## Fix direction
- `static_nat.rs from_snapshots`: in the block branch, additionally `continue` (record_parse_error) when `ext_prefix.len == 0` (or below a sane floor such as `< 8`) — mirror the existing family/length/port drops. Optionally reject when `host_mask == u32::MAX` for a non-host block.
- `destination.rs destination_ips_scoped`: skip the `slot.network()` push when the prefix is `/0` (base is unspecified) or `host_count > MAX_LOCAL_PREFIX_HOSTS` with an unspecified base.
- Go `validateNATHostMaskStrict`: hard-reject a static/NAT block pair or DNAT prefix with `Ones()==0` (and consider a minimum-length policy) so it never reaches the helper.
- Add RED-on-revert tests: `/0` static block → dropped (parse-error counter), `/0` DNAT → base not registered local.

Provenance: ps-review-044 (Paladin defensive-coverage campaign) batch A2_rust_dataplane_nat-b1, Findings 7 & 8. Verified live on origin/master `a6fcd463b`; not among the 7 post-base merges (#5651–#5657); no open-issue dup.

## #5659 — userspace-dp/host-inbound: empty-zone ingress interface (zone_id 0) registers local addrs without a fail-closed zone_id — #2391 backstop symmetry gap [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-17)

## Summary
The `#2391` helper-boundary fail-closed backstop protects only a **non-empty unknown** zone name. An interface with a configured IP but an **empty** zone string is skipped by that backstop (no `ifindex_to_zone_id` entry → resolves to `zone_id 0`) while its address is **still** registered into `local_v4`/`local_v6`. `host_inbound_admits(0)` then hits the `None => true` arm and **admits every host-bound service** (SSH/NETCONF/BGP/SNMP…). This is an asymmetry in the snapshot builder that breaks the fail-closed symmetry `#2391`/`#3405` established.

## Evidence (origin/master `a6fcd463b`)
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:62-92` — the zone→`zone_id` insert (and the `#2391` `SnapshotIntegrityError::InterfaceUnknownZone` fail-closed) are **guarded by `if !iface.zone.is_empty()`**. Empty zone ⇒ no `zone_id` entry ⇒ ingress resolves to `zone_id 0`.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:149-179` — `local_v4`/`local_v6` are inserted **unconditionally** (independent of zone), so the empty-zone interface's IP is a local-delivery target.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:493-501` — `host_inbound_admits`: `state.zone_host_inbound.get(&0)` → `None => true` (admit). The comment documents this as intentional for a "genuinely unknown / global" zone (ND/control), but it also covers a **concrete addressed data interface** that merely lacks a `security-zone`.
- Go control plane ships such interfaces: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go:204,218` (and unit path 267,282) set `Zone: zoneByInterface[name]` (== "" when unzoned) and `Addresses: addresses` with **no zone gate** in `buildInterfaceSnapshots`.
- Contradicts the documented quarantine promise `pkg/config/zoneid.go:172-175`: a `#3719` stable-id collision "**its interfaces unzoned and its traffic denied**". Zone-pair/transit traffic IS denied (README.md:540 `from_id!=0 && to_id!=0` guard → default-deny), but host-inbound (local-delivery) is **admitted**.

## Reachability (adversarial analysis — read before triaging severity)
The runtime bypass is **partially gated** and I could not confirm a clean end-to-end exploit on the common path:
1. The AF_XDP bind enumeration `buildUserspaceBindNetdevs` (`interfaces.go:147`) **skips `iface.Zone == ""`**, so a plain unzoned-but-addressed data interface is not AF_XDP-bound → its ingress goes to the kernel path, not this userspace check.
2. If `iface.host_inbound_configured` is set, an empty per-interface override in `ifindex_host_inbound` fails **closed** (`interfaces.rs:100-108`), and `host_inbound_admits_iface` prefers it.
3. A packet arriving on a *different* bound interface carries **that** interface's non-zero `zone_id`, so the firewall-owned IP of the unzoned interface is still enforced under a real zone.

So the residual is a **fail-closed-symmetry / defense-in-depth gap**, not a confirmed reachable Medium bypass: the snapshot builder registers a local address for an interface that resolves to the admit-all `zone_id 0`, relying on the bind-skip to be safe. Any future change that binds a zoneless interface (or a quarantine path that keeps an interface bound while stripping its zone) would turn this into a live host-inbound bypass.

## Fix direction
Extend the `#2391` backstop to the empty-zone case for symmetry: in `populate_interfaces`, when `iface.zone.is_empty()` for a non-lifeline **addressed** interface, either (a) fail the snapshot closed, or (b) insert an empty `ZoneHostInbound` sentinel keyed so `host_inbound_admits` **denies** (keep the global ICMP/ND/PMTUD accepts that already precede the zone lookup). Add a test: unzoned addressed interface → `local_v4` populated AND `host_inbound_admits(zone_id 0)` returns deny for SSH/BGP.

Provenance: ps-review-044 batch A1_rust_dataplane_packet-b1, finding FH-001. Verified live on origin/master `a6fcd463b`; not among #5651–#5657; no open-issue dup (distinct from #5566 kernel-established retain, #3226 system-services-all, #5568 L4-from-Ethernet-slack).

## #5660 — nat/allocator: deterministic-reverse O(N) pool scan + unchecked port_of u32→u16 cast (ps-review-044 bounded-hardening cohort) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

## Summary
Bounded low-materiality / defense-in-depth survivors from the ps-review-044 Paladin campaign (NAT allocator). Cohorted per campaign convention rather than filed individually. Both verified live on origin/master `a6fcd463b`.

## 1. Deterministic-NAT reverse mapping is an O(N) linear scan over the pool
`userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs:251` (`reverse_deterministic_v4`) and `:391` (`reverse_deterministic_v6`, NAPT64 — external side is IPv4, so `pool_v4` param is correct) both recover the subscriber via `pool_v4.iter().position(|&a| a == translated_ip)` — a linear scan of up to `MAX_POOL_PREFIX_HOSTS` (65 536) addresses. This runs on the reverse/session-miss cold path (the session table caches the hot path), so it is not per-packet in steady state, but a worst-case 64 k-entry scan per reverse resolution is an unnecessary DoS/perf cliff under session-table churn.
- Fix: build a `HashMap<Ipv4Addr, usize>` reverse index at rule-build time; O(1) lookup.

## 2. `AddressOccupancy::port_of` casts u32→u16 with no bound / debug assert
`userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs:503` — `fn port_of(&self, offset: u32) -> u16 { self.port_low + offset as u16 }`. Safe **today** because `range <= 64512` and callers keep `offset < range`, so `port_low + offset <= port_high <= 65535`. But the invariant is undocumented at the call site and a future caller passing `offset >= range` would truncate/wrap silently.
- Fix: `debug_assert!(offset < self.range)` and document the invariant (or use `checked_add`).

Provenance: ps-review-044 batch A2_rust_dataplane_nat-b1, Findings 9 & 10. Both verified on origin/master `a6fcd463b`. Low/Info severity — cohorted intentionally.

## #5666 — policymatch: test-policy/show-match-policies CLI dry-run gates predefined app-set expansion on user-only map (post-#5629 sim divergence) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

## #5669 — scheduler: republish-failure fail-open window has no bounded-age fail-closed or alert (residual on the #3780 self-heal) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

`pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go` (~24-37, evaluate/recordRepublishResultLocked ~162-182): on a scheduled-policy window transition, if `updateFn` (enforcement-snapshot republish to the dataplane) fails, the #3780 self-heal latches `republishPending` and retries on the NEXT evaluate tick (60s). During that window the stale `active=true` keeps a scheduled PERMIT forwarding past its window close — a packet-path FAIL-OPEN — and a scheduled BLOCK never engages. The comment already documents this ("a scheduled permit whose window just closed would keep forwarding (fail-open)").

**Residual gap (verified on origin/master):** the #3780 latch/self-heal mitigates via retry, but there is NO bounded-age handling — under control-socket contention (the shared socket carries status poll 1/s + HA sync + session installs + snapshot sync + forwarding sync, per CLAUDE.md) the retry can itself keep failing, extending the fail-open window indefinitely; `republishFailures`/`republishFirstFail` are tracked for metrics only, never acted on. There is no `slog.Warn` at the decision point and no fail-closed-after-N-ticks.

**Fix direction (defense-in-depth):** at minimum emit a `slog.Warn` + alert metric when `republishPending` persists past a bounded age (e.g. 2× tick), so monitoring catches the 60s+ stale-enforcement window; optionally expire the stale `active=true` entry (mark inactive locally / clear the snapshot) after that age so a scheduled permit fails CLOSED rather than forwarding indefinitely on a stuck control socket. Severity: Medium (bounded + self-healing in the common case; the tail is the contention-stall window).

Provenance: fable-review-174 (Paladin full-tree audit) finding H1, verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5670 — dhcprelay: no per-interface rate-limiting on the relay path — untrusted client segment can CPU-exhaust / amplify (1 client packet → N server packets) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-13)

`pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go` (client + server listener loops, ~1120/1353): the per-interface DHCP relay reads into a reusable 65535-byte buffer (fine, no per-packet heap) and forwards each client request to all N configured servers with an Option 82 insert — but there is NO rate limiting, token bucket, or per-interface packet-per-second cap. `RelayStats` drops cover backup / max-hops / untrusted-giaddr / unknown-server (semantic drops) but NOT rate-limit.

**Impact (verified on origin/master):** any host on an untrusted client-facing segment can send DHCP unauthenticated (broadcast/unicast to :67). A ~10k-pps DHCPDISCOVER storm incurs, per packet: `dhcpv4.FromBytes` (variable-length TLV walk) + Option 82 allocation + SEQUENTIAL send to every configured server + atomic counter bump. This is a CPU-exhaustion + **amplification** vector: 1 client packet → N server packets (factor = number of relay servers), which can also make the real servers rate-limit legitimate clients as collateral. Not memory exhaustion (buffer is reusable) — CPU + fan-out.

**Fix direction:** add a per-interface token bucket (e.g. default 100 pps, configurable via relay-group overrides) with a `RequestsDroppedRateLimit` counter for drop-excess; and/or bound concurrent in-flight relay sessions + make the Option 82 fast-drop path allocation-free. Mirror the screen/IDS per-reason-drop-counter pattern. Severity: Medium-High (unauthenticated, amplifying, no backpressure).

Provenance: fable-review-174 (Paladin full-tree audit) finding H2, verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5671 — config: memberIsNestedSet lacks the '&& as != nil' guard that lookupApplicationSet has — nil tolerant-loaded app-set → false 'not found' instead of leaf resolution [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-13)

`pkg/config/predefined.go` — asymmetry verified on origin/master:

- `memberIsNestedSet` (line 294): `if _, ok := apps.ApplicationSets[memberName]; ok { return true }` — treats a PRESENT-but-nil entry as a nested set.
- `lookupApplicationSet` (line 226): `if as, ok := appSets[name]; ok && as != nil {` — correctly skips a present-but-nil entry.

Under the #1960 tolerant-load path an `ApplicationSets[memberName]` key can be present with a `nil` value. `memberIsNestedSet` then returns `true` ("is a nested set"), so `expandAppSet` routes it to `lookupApplicationSet`, which skips the nil and the expansion errors `"application-set <name> not found"` — instead of falling through to try the member as a leaf application (which may well exist and resolve). Net effect: a rare-but-reachable false negative that turns a resolvable application reference into a hard "not found".

**Fix (one line, mirrors lookupApplicationSet):**
```go
if as, ok := apps.ApplicationSets[memberName]; ok && as != nil {
    return true
}
```
Add a fail-on-revert test: a config with a nil-valued app-set key shadowing a real leaf application name, asserting the member resolves as the leaf rather than erroring. Severity: Low-Medium (rare tolerant-load path, but a concrete correctness asymmetry).

Provenance: fable-review-174 (Paladin) second-batch finding M2, verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5673 — dataplane: pre-policy RX source learning permits spoofed neighbor-map growth + all-shard serialization (M02) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-21)

Rust AF_XDP dataplane (A1). Source-address learning runs on RX BEFORE screen/policy admission, so a spoofed-source flood grows the neighbor map with no aggregate cap and serializes across all shards. Reachable pre-policy → an attacker on an untrusted segment can inflate the neighbor/binding map and induce all-shard serialization (CPU/memory DoS) without ever passing a policy check.

Fix direction: bound neighbor-map growth (per-source + aggregate cap), and/or defer source learning until after screen admission so spoofed pre-policy traffic can't grow shared state. Add a fail-on-revert test that a spoofed-source burst does not grow the map past the cap.

Provenance: codex-review-182 (Paladin full-tree, coordinator-verified) finding M02 (High), base cbba4c37a, verified unchanged at origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5674 — HA: synced session imports bypass max_sessions and multiply state/queues across workers (M03) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-21)

Rust AF_XDP dataplane (A1), HA session-sync import path. Sessions imported from the peer via HA sync are admitted WITHOUT the `max_sessions` bound that gates locally-created sessions, and are multiplied into per-worker state/queues. A peer under session-table pressure (or a malicious/compromised peer) can drive the local node past its session cap and multiply queue state across all workers — an availability/DoS root that the local admission bound is supposed to prevent.

Fix direction: apply the `max_sessions` admission bound to the synced-import path (or a dedicated synced-session cap), and bound the per-worker queue multiplication. Fail-on-revert: a synced import burst beyond the cap is rejected/bounded, not admitted.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M03 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5675 — config: multiple top-level 'interfaces' roots bypass first-root prepasses and replace range/filter state (M09) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Config compiler (Z1/A3). First-root prepasses use `FindChild` (first matching root only) while dispatch compiles EVERY matching root. A config with multiple top-level `interfaces` roots therefore has its range/filter prepass state computed from only the first root, but later roots still compile and REPLACE that state — so range-filter / interface state built by the prepass is silently overwritten (last-root-wins) and split-root inputs survive strict admission. The review's corrected trace excludes the refuted #5631 alias arm — this is the standalone multi-`interfaces`-root defect.

Fix direction: make the prepasses iterate all matching roots (accumulate, like the #2419 multi-value pattern) or reject multiple top-level roots at admission. Fail-on-revert: a split `interfaces` root config that currently truncates range/filter state is rejected or fully accumulated.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M09 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65 (highlights confirm the FindChild-vs-compile-all structural gap persists).

## #5676 — config: address and address-set names share an untagged namespace — a set can shadow a same-named address in deny rules (M10) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-13)

Config compiler / admission (Z1/A3). Address book entries and address-SET entries share ONE untagged namespace, so a set-based name can shadow a same-named plain address (or vice versa) in policy match resolution — a set-based deny can be shadowed by an address of the same name (or the reverse), silently changing which traffic a deny rule covers. This is an admission / root-identity defect: the two kinds must be namespace-tagged so a name resolves deterministically.

Fix direction: tag address vs address-set names in distinct namespaces at admission + resolution, and reject or diagnose a collision. Fail-on-revert: a config with an address and an address-set of the same name resolves the intended one in a deny rule (test both orderings).

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M10 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5677 — config: direct-host projection resolves application-set before a same-named user application (M11) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

Config compiler, direct-host (host-inbound) projection (Z1/A3). When projecting host-inbound services, the resolver consults the application-SET table before a same-named user APPLICATION, so a user application shadowed by a same-named set is mis-resolved to the set. This is DISTINCT from closed #5629 (policy-match app-vs-set ordering) and open #5671 (memberIsNestedSet nil guard) — it is the direct-host projection site specifically.

Fix direction: mirror the app-first ordering used elsewhere (resolve user application, then application-set) at the direct-host projection site. Fail-on-revert: a user application shadowing a predefined/user set name projects the application, not the set, into host-inbound.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M11 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65; explicitly distinct from #5629 (closed) and #5671 (open).

## #5678 — routing: qualified-next-hop preference dropped at the AF_XDP snapshot boundary — backup becomes ECMP with primary (M12) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Config→AF_XDP snapshot lowering (Z1/A3). A static route's qualified-next-hop PREFERENCE (which selects primary vs backup) is lost when the route is lowered into the AF_XDP snapshot, so a lower-preference (backup) next hop is installed with EQUAL cost to the primary and the dataplane load-balances across both (ECMP) instead of using the backup only on primary failure. Silent routing-semantics change: traffic that should egress only the primary is split to the backup.

Fix direction: carry the qualified-next-hop preference across the snapshot boundary and install backup next hops as higher-cost / standby, not co-equal ECMP members. Fail-on-revert: a route with a preferred + backup qualified next hop installs a single active path in the snapshot.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M12 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5679 — daemon: ordinary full dataplane apply failure reports commit SUCCESS and preserves old policy (M17) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go` (~903-911, VERIFIED on origin/master): the dataplane `ApplyConfig` path records `recordCompileFailure(err)` on error but only returns the error when `compileErrorMustAbortApply(err)` is true; for an ORDINARY (non-abort-class) apply failure it FALLS THROUGH and the commit proceeds to report success while the OLD policy remains live on the dataplane. A tightening commit (e.g. adding a deny) can therefore be reported as applied while the looser old policy is still enforced — a fail-open-to-stale on the main config-apply path.

This is the config-commit analog of the feeds publication-debt bug (#5646 / PR #5667) but on the ordinary full-apply path; it is SEPARATE from peer equal-text retry (#4957) and the planned-failover epoch (#5563), and from the feeds path. Local desired/applied identity + retry debt is missing.

Fix direction: propagate a non-abort apply failure to the commit result (fail the commit or mark the applied-identity un-advanced so a retry re-applies), mirroring the #5667 publishedHash-advances-only-on-success gate. Fail-on-revert: an ordinary ApplyConfig failure makes `commit` report failure (or leaves applied-identity stale so the next identical commit retries) rather than success.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M17 (High), root READ + verified at origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5680 — daemon: route-only publication can ACK an old-policy/new-route hybrid as the new config (M18) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

Go dataplane manager / publication (Z2/A6). When only routes change, the publication path can acknowledge a hybrid state — OLD policy + NEW routes — as the newly-applied config, so the applied-identity advances even though the policy half was not (re)published. Downstream this reports the new config as fully live while policy enforcement is stale. This is the #5642 provenance residual (route-leak staging) surfacing as a completeness gap on the route-only publication path.

Fix direction: make the applied-identity advance only when BOTH the policy and route halves of the target snapshot are confirmed published (or split the identities so a route-only publish cannot ACK the policy half). Fail-on-revert: a route-only change with an unpublished policy delta does not ACK as the new full config.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M18 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65; #5642 residual, distinct from M17/M19.

## #5681 — HA: RG reconcile is not joined before shutdown ownership cleanup — a late pass can re-enable forwarding/VIPs during shutdown (M23) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Daemon shutdown / HA (Z2/A7). The redundancy-group reconcile goroutine is not joined/quiesced before shutdown ownership cleanup runs, so a late-scheduled reconcile pass can re-enable forwarding and re-add VIPs AFTER the node has begun relinquishing ownership on shutdown. Result: a shutting-down node can transiently re-assert mastership (VIPs/forwarding) after cleanup, causing a dual-master / blackhole window during planned shutdown or failover.

Fix direction: join/cancel the RG reconcile worker (and block new passes) BEFORE ownership cleanup in the shutdown sequence. Fail-on-revert: no VIP/forwarding re-enable occurs after shutdown cleanup starts (ordering test).

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M23 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65. HA/failover — will need test-failover before any fix merges.

## #5682 — HA/upgrade: unreadable kernel-upgrade journal bypasses candidate election hold and recovery (M24) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Daemon kernel-upgrade / HA election (Z2/A7). When the kernel-upgrade journal is UNREADABLE (I/O error, corruption), the code treats the unknown state as "not armed" and proceeds — bypassing the candidate-election HOLD and the recovery path that an in-progress upgrade is supposed to trigger. An unreadable journal (a failure mode that itself correlates with a bad upgrade) therefore fails OPEN: the node elects/promotes as if no upgrade were pending, defeating the promote/rollback safety of the #1930 A/B kernel channel.

Fix direction: treat an unreadable/ambiguous upgrade journal as fail-CLOSED (hold election + enter recovery), not "not armed". Fail-on-revert: an unreadable journal holds election rather than proceeding.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M24 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65. HA/upgrade — test-failover + upgrade-channel validation before fix merges.

## #5683 — routing: PBR builds the full six-dimensional match product BEFORE applying its 1,000-rule cap — pre-cap memory/CPU exhaustion (M28) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Policy-based routing compile (A7). The PBR compiler expands the full six-dimensional Cartesian match product (source × dest × proto × ports × ... ) and only THEN applies the 1,000-rule cap. A config whose dimensions multiply to millions of tuples exhausts memory/CPU DURING expansion, before the cap ever engages — so the cap does not protect against the blow-up it is meant to bound. A crafted (or merely large) PBR stanza can OOM/hang xpfd at commit.

Fix direction: apply the cap (or a running product-size guard) DURING expansion so it aborts before materializing the full product; reject a config whose pre-expansion dimension product exceeds the cap. Fail-on-revert: a PBR stanza whose product exceeds the cap is rejected at admission without materializing the full product.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M28 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5684 — api: custom config paths turn 'zeroize' into broad parent-directory deletion (M33) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-13)

gRPC/REST API (A8), zeroize path (merged A8-b01/A8-b02 root). When a custom config path is in effect, the zeroize operation deletes the PARENT directory of the configured path rather than only the config artifacts — so a non-default config location turns a factory-zeroize into a broad recursive deletion of whatever parent directory the operator pointed at. Data-loss / destructive-scope defect: zeroize must be bounded to the config artifacts it owns, never the enclosing directory.

Fix direction: scope zeroize deletion to the specific owned files, never the parent directory; refuse to zeroize if the target resolves to a shared/parent path. Fail-on-revert: zeroize with a custom config path removes only the config artifacts, not the parent dir (test with a custom path under a populated dir).

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M33 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5685 — build/release: release stamping embeds an unvalidated apt URL into signed root shell source (M40) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Release/build tooling (A10). Release stamping takes a lower-trust release value (an apt URL) and embeds it UNVALIDATED into shell source that is then signed and runs as root on the appliance. The unvalidated value crosses the signing trust boundary: a malformed or attacker-influenced apt URL becomes signed, root-executed shell — a supply-chain / injection root (the signature attests to whatever was stamped in, including an injected URL/command).

Fix direction: validate + strictly quote/escape the apt URL against an allowlist grammar BEFORE it is embedded into the signed shell source; reject values that don't match. Fail-on-revert: a release stamp with a malformed/injection apt URL is rejected before signing.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M40 (High), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5686 — dataplane: same-parent fabric peer replacement retains the stale old peer while the replacement is unresolved (M01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Rust AF_XDP dataplane (A1), fabric snapshot/neighbor authority. When a fabric peer under the same parent is replaced, the old peer entry is retained while the replacement is still unresolved — so the stale old peer remains a valid redirect/authority target during the resolution window, and fabric-forwarded traffic can be sent to a peer that is no longer current. Live fabric snapshot/neighbor authority root.

Fix direction: invalidate the old peer atomically with (or before) accepting the replacement, or gate fabric redirect on a resolved replacement so no stale peer is used. Fail-on-revert: after a same-parent peer replacement the old peer is no longer a redirect target.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M01 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5687 — nat: SNAT conflates real IPv4 protocol 0 (HOPOPT) with the tuple-unknown sentinel (M04) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Rust NAT (A2). SNAT uses protocol value 0 as a "tuple-unknown" sentinel, colliding with the real IPv4 protocol number 0 (HOPOPT). A genuine protocol-0 packet's reverse tuple therefore cannot be matched (it looks like the unknown sentinel), breaking reverse translation for that protocol.

Fix direction: use an out-of-band sentinel (Option / u16 with a reserved value) for tuple-unknown so real protocol 0 is representable and matchable. Fail-on-revert: a protocol-0 flow's reverse tuple matches.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M04 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5688 — nat: interface-mode SNAT forwards untranslated when no same-family egress address exists (M05) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Rust NAT (A2). Interface-mode SNAT returns `Matched` (success) even when the egress interface has NO address of the packet's family — so the packet is forwarded UNTRANSLATED (with its private/internal source) instead of being dropped or deferred. Leaks untranslated source addresses onto the egress when the interface lacks a same-family address.

Fix direction: when interface-mode SNAT finds no same-family egress address, do NOT return Matched-with-no-rewrite; drop (or hold) the packet and count it. Fail-on-revert: a flow through interface SNAT with no same-family egress address is not forwarded untranslated.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M05 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5689 — nat: flowless non-first fragments bypass ordinary NAT/NPT and forward untranslated (M06) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-18)

Rust dataplane (Z4), `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs` (~3906, VERIFIED: the flowless SessionDecision returns `nat: NatDecision::default()`). Non-first fragments with no associated flow return the default (no-op) NAT decision and are forwarded UNTRANSLATED for ordinary NAT/NPTv6 — only NAT64 has fragment association. The lower frame layer supports address-only fragment rewrites, so ordinary NAT/NPT consistency is genuinely missing (not impossible): a fragmented flow leaks untranslated non-first fragments.

Fix direction: associate non-first fragments with their flow (fragment cache) for ordinary NAT/NPT, or apply the address-only fragment rewrite the frame layer already supports. Fail-on-revert: a fragmented NAT/NPT flow's non-first fragments are translated consistently with the first.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M06 (Medium), root READ + verified at origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5690 — nat: non-query ICMP suppression makes generic embedded-ICMP NAT reversal unreachable (M07) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Rust dataplane (Z4). Non-query ICMP is suppressed on a control-flow path such that generic embedded-ICMP NAT reversal (translating the inner quoted packet of an ICMP error) becomes unreachable in production — the helper tests exercise the reversal but bypass the dead poll control flow, so the capability is tested-but-not-live. An ICMP error referencing a NAT'd flow is therefore not reverse-translated on the real path.

Fix direction: reach the embedded-ICMP reversal from the production poll path (remove the suppression that shadows it), and add a test that drives it through the real control flow, not just the helper. Fail-on-revert: an ICMP error for a NAT'd flow is reverse-translated on the production path.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M07 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5691 — config: split top-level roots bypass stable-ID collision gates for zones, VRFs, and tunnels (M08) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Config compiler (Z1/A3). Multiple split top-level roots bypass the stable-ID collision gates for zones, VRFs, and tunnels (the same first-root-prepass-vs-compile-all class as M09, but for the stable-ID assignment path). A config that splits these definitions across repeated top-level roots can assign colliding/ambiguous stable IDs because the collision gate only inspects the first root. One all-root stable-ID issue.

Fix direction: run the stable-ID collision gate across ALL matching top-level roots (or reject split roots) so zone/VRF/tunnel IDs are collision-checked over the full config. Fail-on-revert: a split-root config that currently produces a stable-ID collision is rejected.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M08 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65; sibling of M09/#5675.

## #5692 — config: repeated valid IPsec selector leaves pass strict admission and truncate last-wins (M13) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Config compiler (Z1/A3), IPsec selectors. Repeated valid IPsec selector leaves under the same parent pass strict admission but are collapsed last-wins, so earlier selectors are silently truncated — a multi-selector IPsec policy enforces only the last one. (Corrected from the refuted bracket-list trace; this is the repeated-leaf, not the bracket-list, path.)

Fix direction: accumulate repeated IPsec selector leaves (like the #2419 multi-value pattern) or reject duplicate selectors at admission. Fail-on-revert: a policy with N valid selector leaves compiles all N, not just the last.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M13 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5693 — config: next-table raw grammar and target definedness are lost before validation (M14) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

Config compiler (Z1/A3), rib-group / next-table. The `next-table` raw grammar and the definedness of its target routing-instance are lost before validation runs, so a next-table pointing at an undefined/typo'd target is not caught at commit. Distinct from #5632 (next-table `.inet` LastIndex) and #5633 — this is the target-definedness + raw-grammar-preservation follow-on.

Fix direction: preserve the raw next-table token and validate the target routing-instance exists at commit. Fail-on-revert: a next-table naming an undefined instance is rejected at commit.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M14 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65; distinct from #5632/#5633.

## #5694 — config: malformed chassis RG/node identities alias valid ID zero (M15) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Config compiler (Z1/A3), chassis cluster identities. A malformed chassis redundancy-group / node identity parses to a DEFAULT of zero, aliasing a valid ID 0 — so a typo'd RG/node number is silently treated as RG/node 0 rather than rejected, mis-assigning cluster ownership.

Fix direction: distinguish parse-failure from a real 0 (Option / explicit validity) and reject a malformed identity at commit rather than defaulting to zero. Fail-on-revert: a malformed RG/node identity is rejected, not coerced to 0.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M15 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5695 — vrrp: GARP count accepts an effectively unbounded per-VIP raw-socket work budget (M16) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

VRRP / GARP (Z1/A3). The configured GARP count accepts an effectively unbounded value with no strict admission cap or runtime clamp, so a large count schedules a huge per-VIP raw-socket send budget — a self-inflicted CPU/socket exhaustion vector on failover (each VIP fans out the full count).

Fix direction: add a strict admission upper bound on GARP count and a runtime clamp. Fail-on-revert: an out-of-range GARP count is rejected at commit (and clamped at runtime).

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M16 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5696 — daemon: route publication / FIB invalidation failures are logged and forgotten (M19) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Go dataplane manager (Z2/A6). Route publication and FIB-invalidation failures are logged but not retried or tracked — there is no completion-debt owner, so a transient failure leaves the FIB stale with no rediscovery. #5642 staged-completion-debt residual (sibling of M17/M18).

Fix direction: track failed route-publish / FIB-invalidation as pending and retry (mirror the #5667 publishedHash retry-debt pattern). Fail-on-revert: a failed FIB invalidation is retried on the next cycle rather than dropped.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M19 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65; #5642 residual.

## #5697 — daemon: failed stale-binding clears lose retry inventory — watchdog cannot rediscover extra stale rows (M20) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Go dataplane manager (Z2/A6). When a stale-binding clear fails, the retry inventory (the set of stale rows still needing cleanup) is lost, so the watchdog cannot rediscover the extra stale rows on a later pass — they persist indefinitely. Completion-debt gap on the stale-binding cleanup path.

Fix direction: retain failed stale-binding rows in a retry inventory the watchdog re-scans. Fail-on-revert: a failed stale-binding clear is retried until it succeeds.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M20 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5698 — dataplane: forward/reverse session-pair transmission is not linearizable against deletes (M21) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-21)

Rust/Go session install (Z2/A6). The forward and reverse entries of a session pair are transmitted non-atomically with respect to deletes, so a concurrent delete can interleave between the forward and reverse install — leaving a half-installed pair (forward without reverse, or vice versa). Same-epoch pair-atomicity root: breaks reverse-path matching for that flow.

Fix direction: make the forward+reverse pair install/delete linearizable (single epoch/transaction) so a delete cannot interleave. Fail-on-revert: a delete concurrent with a pair install leaves no half-installed pair.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M21 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5699 — config: base and unit-0 views emit one live address under conflicting host-inbound signatures — deterministic false deny/parity failure (M22) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

Config compiler (Z2/A6), host-inbound. The base-interface view and the unit-0 view can each emit one live address under CONFLICTING host-inbound service signatures, producing a deterministic false deny / parity failure (the two views disagree on which host-inbound services are admitted for the single live address).

Fix direction: reconcile the base vs unit-0 host-inbound signature so a single live address has one deterministic admit set. Fail-on-revert: a base+unit-0 config with conflicting host-inbound signatures resolves to one consistent admit set (no false deny).

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M22 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5700 — daemon: VRF setup/bind failure is recorded managed and discarded from commit truth (M25) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Daemon / routing (Z2/A7). A VRF setup or bind failure is recorded as "managed" and then discarded from commit truth, so the commit reports the VRF configured while it is not actually set up on the kernel — no retry owner exists to reconcile it. False convergence on the VRF path.

Fix direction: propagate a VRF setup/bind failure into commit truth (fail or mark pending) and give it a retry owner. Fail-on-revert: a VRF bind failure does not report the VRF as successfully configured.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M25 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5701 — frr: route-map Cartesian variants can overflow FRR sequence numbers and poison reload (M26) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

FRR config generation (A7). Route-map generation expands Cartesian variants whose count can overflow the FRR route-map sequence-number space, producing an invalid route-map that poisons the frr-reload. A large (or crafted) policy blows the sequence numbering and breaks the entire reload.

Fix direction: bound the route-map variant expansion against the FRR sequence-number ceiling and reject/diagnose at commit before generating an overflowing map. Fail-on-revert: a policy that would overflow FRR sequence numbers is rejected at commit.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M26 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5702 — routing: mixed-family route-filter splitting drops an off-family AND predicate (M27) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

Routing / route-filter (A7). When a route-filter term with a mixed-family AND predicate is split by family, the off-family predicate is DROPPED rather than making the term vacuously non-matching — so the surviving family term matches more broadly than authored. Policy-semantics change: the AND is silently loosened to the on-family half.

Fix direction: when splitting a mixed-family AND term, make the off-family half non-matching for the wrong family rather than dropping the predicate. Fail-on-revert: a mixed-family AND route-filter does not match traffic the dropped predicate would have excluded.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M27 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5703 — networkd: a tracked desired bond missing from the kernel is treated as unchanged forever (M29) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

Daemon interface reconcile (A7). A tracked desired bond that is MISSING from the kernel is treated as "unchanged" by the reconciler, so it is never (re)created — false convergence leading to a persistent outage of that bond (the reconciler believes it matches desired state).

Fix direction: treat a desired-present / kernel-absent bond as a change requiring creation, not unchanged. Fail-on-revert: a desired bond deleted from the kernel is recreated on the next reconcile.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M29 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5704 — networkd: RETH deletion failures are logged but reported as successful cleanup (M30) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Daemon RETH management (A7). RETH deletion failures are logged but the cleanup is reported as successful, so stale host RETH ownership persists while the daemon believes it was torn down. Leaves stale RETH state (and potentially stale VIP/MAC ownership) across a reconfigure/teardown.

Fix direction: propagate a RETH deletion failure into the cleanup result and retry, rather than reporting success. Fail-on-revert: a failed RETH delete does not report successful cleanup.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M30 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5705 — routing: unbounded tunnel keepalive interval overflows time.Duration and panics xpfd (M31) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

Daemon / tunnels (A7). An unbounded tunnel keepalive interval value overflows `time.Duration` (int64 nanoseconds) when converted, and can panic xpfd — no strict admission bound and no runtime clamp. A large keepalive value in config is a self-inflicted crash (commit-reachable).

Fix direction: bound the keepalive interval at strict admission and clamp at runtime before the Duration multiply. Fail-on-revert: an out-of-range keepalive interval is rejected at commit rather than overflowing/panicking.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M31 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5706 — HA: IPsec/DHCP full-set state can regress across redundant receive streams (M32) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Cluster HA (A5/Z5). IPsec and DHCP full-set state sync has no per-peer-incarnation / per-type sequence, so a full-set update received out of order across redundant receive streams can REGRESS the state to an older set. Stale full-set can overwrite newer on a redundant/reordered stream.

Fix direction: tag full-set updates with a peer-incarnation + per-type monotonic sequence and reject regressions. Fail-on-revert: an out-of-order older full-set does not overwrite a newer one.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M32 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5707 — api: MonitorInterface multiplies live status calls by interfaces x streams (O(N*S) contention) (M34) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

gRPC/REST API (A8). `MonitorInterface` issues live status calls multiplied by (interfaces x streams), so N interfaces across S concurrent streams produce O(N*S) manager/status calls — control-socket / manager contention that scales with subscribers and can starve other manager work.

Fix direction: share/cache one status snapshot per poll tick across streams (fan-out from a single manager query) instead of per-(interface,stream) calls. Fail-on-revert: S concurrent MonitorInterface streams do not multiply manager status calls by S.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M34 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

gRPC API (A8). The REST rate/size limiter does not cover the gRPC session list/summary scans, so a gRPC caller can issue unbounded full-session-table scans with no shared admission bound — a CPU/contention DoS via the uncovered gRPC surface.

Fix direction: apply a shared admission bound (concurrency + result cap) covering the gRPC session list/summary path, not just REST. Fail-on-revert: a gRPC session scan is bounded by the shared limiter.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M35 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5709 — ddns: two scopes can co-own one wire RR and one scope can delete the other's live value (M36) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

DDNS (A10). Two DDNS scopes can co-own a single wire resource record because wire-identity claim accounting is missing, so one scope's reconcile can DELETE the other scope's live RR value. Cross-scope RR clobber / accidental record deletion.

## #5711 — dhcpv6: bare acquisition and renewal use different DUID identities (DUID-LLT vs persistent DUID-LL) (M38) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-15)

DHCPv6 client (A10). Bare DHCPv6 acquisition and renewal use DIFFERENT DUID identities (DUID-LLT at acquisition vs a persistent DUID-LL at renewal, or vice versa), so a renewal presents a DUID the server did not bind — the server treats it as a new client and the lease is not renewed as expected.

## #5712 — syslog: in-process CLI commit overwrites configured TCP/TLS syslog clients with UDP (M39) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

Syslog / CLI (A10). An in-process CLI commit re-initializes the syslog client as a duplicate runtime owner and overwrites the configured TCP/TLS transport with UDP — so after an in-process commit, structured syslog silently downgrades from TCP/TLS to plaintext UDP (transport/confidentiality regression).

## #5713 — build: accepted '%' version specifiers rewrite systemd executable paths after STOP (M41) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

Build/deploy tooling (A10). Accepted `%`-bearing version specifiers are not sink-aware and can rewrite systemd executable paths after STOP (the version grammar admits values that, when substituted into unit ExecStart paths, redirect the executable). A malformed/crafted version can point the unit at an unintended binary.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M41 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

## #5714 — web-mgmt: bind treats authored Junos interface name as a literal Linux ifname, silently falls back to loopback (M42) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

Web management (Z6). The web-management bind passes the AUTHORED Junos interface name (e.g. ge-0-0-0) literally to `net.InterfaceByName`, which expects the Linux kernel name — so the lookup fails and the listener silently falls back to loopback, meaning web-management is not reachable on the intended interface (and an operator believes it is bound where configured).

Fix direction: resolve the Junos interface name to its Linux ifname (the same mapping networkd/linksetup uses) before binding; fail loudly rather than falling back to loopback. Fail-on-revert: web-mgmt bound to a Junos ifname listens on the mapped Linux interface, not loopback.

Provenance: codex-review-182 finding M42 (Medium), verified against origin/master fc479ca65.

Web management / host-inbound (Z6). ## #5726 — config/routing: commit-time next-hop gateway validation is incomplete — qualified-next-hop unvalidated + ECMP list validates only the first gateway (fail-open) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-12)

The `#2448`-doctrine commit-time next-hop gateway validator (`ValidateStaticNextHop`, `pkg/config/schema_validators_routing.go`) — which correctly rejects a malformed gateway literal (`1.2.3.999`, `2001:db8::garbage`, `notanip@eth0`) — is wired to the **primary** `next-hop` container's identity-arg only. Two static-route next-hop paths still commit an unvalidated gateway, so a typo commits clean, FRR renders the token verbatim, and the route/backup silently never installs — discovered only during the outage the backup existed to survive. Verified on `origin/master` `675133b84`.

## Gap A — `qualified-next-hop <gateway>` carries no validator

`pkg/config/schema_routing.go` — the `qualified-next-hop` node is `{desc, args: 1, placeholder: "<gateway>", children: {interface, preference, metric}}` with **no** `keyValidator` / `keyValueType`, unlike its sibling `next-hop` (`keyValidator: ValidateStaticNextHop`). A floating-backup gateway is therefore never validated at commit.

Repro (commits clean, no error/warning):
```
set routing-options static route 10.0.0.0/8 qualified-next-hop 1.2.3.999 preference 100
```
`SchemaValidate` → nil, `CompileConfig` → nil, `NextHops=[{Address:1.2.3.999 Preference:100}]`; FRR emits `ip route 10.0.0.0/8 1.2.3.999 100` verbatim → backup permanently inactive. Primary-path failure then has no backup.

## Gap B — ECMP `next-hop [ gw1 gw2 … ]` validates only the FIRST gateway

`pkg/config/schema_walk.go` container path (~lines 389-408): `declaredKeyTokens := 1 + childSchema.args` (= 2 for `next-hop`), and the keyValidator loop runs over `node.Keys[1:argEnd]` with `argEnd = declaredKeyTokens = 2`. A canonical Junos ECMP list collapses (bracket-strip, `#2419`) onto ONE leaf `Keys=["next-hop", gw1, gw2, …]`, so only `Keys[1]` (gw1) is validated; every subsequent gateway (`Keys[2:]`) bypasses `ValidateStaticNextHop` while the compiler (`compiler_routing.go`) installs them all as ECMP members (`#3872`).

Repro (commits clean):
```
set routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop [ 192.168.1.1 1.2.3.999 ]
```
`1.2.3.999` is never validated → FRR emits it verbatim → ECMP degrades to single-path (capacity loss) or, if FRR rejects the line, the whole managed frr-reload batch fails (one-bad-leaf).

## Why material

Fail-open validation gap on a security/availability-relevant routing surface; violates the `#2448` "malformed next-hop fails loud at commit, not a silent blackhole" contract for the canonical Junos qualified-backup and ECMP-list spellings. `ValidateStaticNextHop` already rejects these tokens — it is simply not invoked on these two paths.

## Fix direction

- Gap A: add `keyValueType: ValueIPAddress`, `keyValidator: ValidateStaticNextHop` (+ keyValueDesc/Examples) to the `qualified-next-hop` node, mirroring `next-hop`.
- Gap B: in the container keyValidator loop, when `childSchema.multi && childSchema.keyValidator != nil && childSchema.children != nil` (the `next-hop` shape), validate the full packed gateway run `Keys[1:]` minus tokens consumed by declared modifier children (`interface <name>`) — mirror the compiler's keyword-bounded gateway-run scan.
- RED tests: `qualified-next-hop 1.2.3.999` and `next-hop [ good bad ]` must both fail commit.

## Not a duplicate

- `#2448` is the RUNTIME Rust-FIB-builder silent drop (different layer; this is the commit-time schema gate that should reject before render).
- `#5678` is qualified-next-hop **preference** dropped at the AF_XDP snapshot boundary — different field, different site.
- `#5161` is interface-only ECMP members starving at runtime — different mechanism.

Provenance: fable-review-175 F-01/F-02 (A3 config/CLI), verified against origin/master 675133b84 (base fc479ca65).

These remaining items are genuinely-new but LOW — cohorted here rather than filed individually. None is a security bypass. Each line was confirmed present on origin/master.

## #5730 — frr: on-family route-filter + same-family from-prefix-list collide as same-type FRR match — route-filter constraint silently dropped (route_map REPLACE) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-13)

Surfaced during the #5729 (#5702) review. DISTINCT from #5702 (which fixed the OFF-family fail-open) — this is the ON-family same-type collision, PRE-EXISTING (not introduced by #5702).

**Root (pkg/frr/policy_render.go, emitTermBody ~1922 route-filter match vs ~1976 from-prefix-list match):** a policy term with BOTH a `from route-filter` and a same-family `from prefix-list` renders, in that family's route-map sequence, TWO clauses of the SAME FRR match type:
```
route-map MIX deny 20              <- v6 sequence
 match ipv6 address prefix-list MIX-t1_v6     (the route-filter)
 match ipv6 address prefix-list V6ONLY        (the from-prefix-list)
```
FRR's `route_map_add_match` REPLACES a same-type match rule (keeps the LAST), so the route-filter clause (`MIX-t1_v6`) is silently DROPPED — the term matches iff the route is in `V6ONLY`, REGARDLESS of the route-filter range. A v6 prefix that is in `V6ONLY` but OUTSIDE the route-filter range wrongly matches → the `route-filter AND prefix-list` intersection is silently loosened to prefix-list-only. This is the same FRR `route_map` REPLACE limitation documented in #2642, applied to route-filter + same-family prefix-list coexistence. It also fires on NON-split single-family terms (not just the mixed-family split path), so it is broader than #5702's scope.

**Fix direction:** the two same-family, same-type prefix-list matches must be COMBINED into one satisfiable constraint FRR can honor — e.g. render the route-filter and the from-prefix-list into a SINGLE prefix-list (intersection) or use distinct match mechanisms so FRR ANDs them rather than replacing. Or reject/warn at commit if a term combines a route-filter with a same-family from-prefix-list (a config that cannot be faithfully rendered). Add a fail-on-revert test asserting a v6 route in the prefix-list but outside the route-filter range does NOT match the term.

Provenance: PR #5729 (#5702) hostile-review NEW finding (rev5725), verified via rendered frr.conf against origin/master. Severity: Medium (fail-open policy-semantics loosening; needs a term combining route-filter + same-family prefix-list).

## #5732 — frr: route-map sequence bound (#5701) is per-policy-statement — a composed BGP policy-CHAIN can still accumulate seq past the FRR ceiling [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-15)

Follow-up to #5701 / PR #5731 (honest scope note from the implementer). The #5701 fix bounds each POLICY-STATEMENT to <= 6552 route-map term sequences (highest FRR seq 10*(N+1) <= 65535). That covers the documented large/crafted single-policy case.

**Residual:** the composed BGP policy-CHAIN path (`renderComposedRouteMap` in pkg/frr/policy_render.go) concatenates multiple chained policy-statements into ONE FRR route-map, ACCUMULATING sequence numbers across the chain. Each chained policy is individually bounded <= 6552 by the #5701 gate, so no single policy overflows — but a pathological chain of MANY large policy-statements (e.g. `export [ p1 p2 ... pk ]` where each p_i is near the per-policy ceiling) could sum past 65535 in the composed route-map, re-introducing the same frr-reload-poisoning overflow the #5701 gate closes for the single-policy case.

**Materiality:** LOW in practice — BGP export/import policy chains are short (typically 1-3 policies), and each policy near the 6552 ceiling is itself already an extreme config. But it is a real residual of the per-policy bound.

**Fix direction:** extend the commit gate to compute the COMPOSED sequence count for each BGP group/neighbor policy CHAIN (resolve the chain, sum RouteMapSequenceCount across its members + per-chain overhead) and reject if the composed total exceeds the FRR ceiling — mirroring how renderComposedRouteMap actually numbers the composed map. Requires chain-resolution in the commit gate (the per-policy gate does not see the chain). Add a fail-on-revert test with a chain of policies that individually pass but composed exceed the ceiling.

Provenance: PR #5731 (#5701) implementer scope note (eng5705), verified against origin/master. Distinct from #5701 (per-policy, MERGED).

## #5738 — syslog: CLI reloadSyslog omits daemon's source-interface fallback + event-mode branch (idempotence gap) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-15)

## Summary

The CLI's `reloadSyslog` (`pkg/cli/apply.go`, `buildSyslogClients`) and the
daemon's `applySyslogConfig` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go`) diverge on two
**pre-existing, non-confidentiality** points. PR #5737 (closes #5712) fixed the
transport/TLS confidentiality downgrade and made the two owners byte-idempotent
on every security-relevant field (protocol, tls.Config, #5581 fail-closed, #3351
reconnecting install, severity/facility/category/format). These two remaining
gaps are source-IP and event-mode behavior, not encryption, so they were
correctly out of scope for the confidentiality fix — filing them here to close
the "idempotent with the daemon" claim completely.

## Gap 1 — global source-interface fallback (source-IP binding)

The daemon computes `globalSourceAddr = resolveSourceAddr(cfg,
cfg.Security.Log.SourceInterface)` and uses it when a stream's
`SourceAddress == ""`. The CLI passes `stream.SourceAddress` directly with **no
global fallback**. So a stream configured via `security log source-interface
<iface>` WITHOUT a per-stream `source-address` gets:

- daemon apply: client bound to the interface-resolved source
- CLI apply (local commit): client with NO source binding → kernel-chosen source

Because the CLI writes LAST on a local commit (the same ordering that caused the
transport bug), this is not self-corrected within the commit — the stream sends
syslog from the wrong/default source until the next daemon-driven apply.

`resolveSourceAddr` currently lives in `pkg/daemon` and is un-importable from
`pkg/cli` without a shared-package move — the reason #5737 deferred it.

## Gap 2 — event-mode local-writer branch

The daemon's syslog apply honors `Mode == "event"`: it clears the remote
clients and installs a local writer. The CLI `reloadSyslog` unconditionally
builds clients from `Streams`. If a config sets BOTH event-mode AND remote
streams, a local commit re-installs the remote clients the daemon had cleared.
Pre-existing (old `reloadSyslog` did the same), non-confidentiality, orthogonal
to the #5712 transport fix.

## #5742 — grpcapi: non-fatal tail-reconcile/apply errors surface as InvalidArgument (should be Unavailable/retryable) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Summary

The commit RPC surfaces a **non-fatal tail-reconcile / dataplane-apply**
failure to gRPC clients via the default error path, which maps to
`codes.InvalidArgument`. That code means "the client sent bad input" — but these
errors are transient INFRASTRUCTURE failures, not config-validation failures:

- networkd write failure (#1778)
- Kea DHCP-server restart/stop failure (#2987)
- IPsec render/reload failure (#4433)
- interface-reconcile (xfrmi/bond/tunnel create/up/delete) failure (#5310)
- **ordinary (non-abort) dataplane-apply failure (#5679)** — a control-socket /
  helper hiccup; the config is valid, the push transiently failed and self-heals
  on the next identical commit / feed retry.

An operator (or an automation client) that sees `InvalidArgument` will conclude
their *config* was rejected and may edit it, when the correct action for a
transient control-socket error is to **retry** (or wait for the #5646 self-heal).
`codes.Unavailable` (transient, retryable) or `codes.Internal` (unexpected)
communicates that distinction; `InvalidArgument` actively misleads.

## Scope / provenance

Pre-existing — this classification applies uniformly to the whole tail-error
class, not introduced by any single PR. Surfaced as a non-blocking informational
note during the hostile review of PR #5739 (#5679 fix). Filing so it's tracked
rather than dismissed.

## Proposed fix

In the commit RPC handler (`pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go` ~231), classify the
returned apply error before mapping to a gRPC status:

- A true **config-validation / compile-reject** error (the pre-commit
  `SchemaValidate` / compiler rejects, `compileErrorMustAbortApply` gate
  sentinels) → keep `codes.InvalidArgument`.
- A **deferred tail-reconcile / ordinary-apply** error (the `errors.Join` from
  `applyTailReconciles` — networkd/dhcp/ipsec/iface/#5679-apply) → map to
  `codes.Unavailable` (transient, retryable) so clients can distinguish
  "fix your config" from "retry / it will self-heal".

## #5744 — config: two interface AST pre-walks (unit-alias collision, unsupported-stanza) still first-root-only — bypass on split interfaces roots [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-13)

## Summary

PR #5741 (#5675/#5691) added `ConfigTree.FindChildren` and routed the
interface-range expansion and the stable-ID collision gates (zones/tunnels/
routing-instances) through it so they observe EVERY top-level root, not just the
first. But two SIBLING AST pre-walks in `pkg/config/compiler_prewalk.go` still
use the identical first-root-only pattern (`FindChild` / a `for … break` on the
first `interfaces` root) and were out of scope for #5741:

- `validateInterfaceUnitAliasCollisionsAST` (`compiler_interface_unit_alias.go:76`)
- `validateUnsupportedInterfaceStanzasAST` (`compiler_interfaces_unsupported.go:87`)

A hierarchical config that splits its `interfaces { }` across two top-level roots
can therefore place a unit-alias collision, or an unsupported/silently-dropped
interface stanza, in the SECOND `interfaces` root and bypass these validators
entirely — the same latent class #5741 closed for the collision gates.

## Impact

- **Unit-alias collision bypass**: two interface units that alias to the same
  identity, split across roots, are not rejected — the later one silently wins /
  merges (same failure shape as the #5691 zone-id silent merge).
- **Unsupported-stanza bypass**: an unsupported interface stanza in a second root
  is not flagged and is silently dropped at compile, so the operator's committed
  intent is not enforced and no warning is emitted.

Both are hierarchical-only (the flat-set `SetPath` path merges every `set
interfaces …` onto one root, so split-root is unreachable via flat-set — same as
#5691).

## Fix

Route both pre-walks through `ConfigTree.FindChildren("interfaces")` and union
across all roots (mechanically identical to the #5741 change to
`expandInterfaceRanges` and the collision gates). Add fail-on-revert tests:
a unit-alias collision and an unsupported stanza each placed in a SECOND
`interfaces` root, asserted rejected/warned, RED when neutralized to first-root.

## #5748 — ddns: cross-surface RR co-ownership (Surface A interface records vs Surface B leases) not covered by the #5709 clobber guard [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-16)

## Summary

PR #5746 (#5709, codex-182 M36) added `wireRRSharedWithOther` so a DDNS lease
scope's teardown suppresses the wire DELETE when ANOTHER lease scope still
co-owns the same wire RR (same canonical FQDN + forward type + rdata). That
guard scans ONLY the lease manager's `m.state.records` (Surface B) and matches
on the `Address` field.

There is a SECOND ownership surface: Surface A router/interface DDNS records
live in a separate store (`interface-ddns-state.json`) with their rdata in
`AddrText`, not `Address`. A Surface A record and a Surface B lease record can
resolve the SAME host to the SAME address and thus co-own one wire RR — but the
#5746 guard does not see Surface A rows (they're in a different map, and their
`Address` is empty so the `owned.Address == ""` early-return also excludes
them). So a lease teardown can still issue a wire DELETE that clobbers a
Surface-A-owned identical RR — the exact cross-scope clobber #5709 fixed, just
across the two ownership surfaces.

## Scope / provenance

Surfaced as a non-blocking, out-of-scope note during the hostile review of PR
#5746 (rev5746). All cases #5709 itself cites are Surface B lease scopes, so
#5746 is NOT a regression — this is the residual cross-surface arm of the same
clobber class. Filing so it's tracked rather than dismissed.

## Proposed fix

Extend the co-ownership check to be surface-agnostic: when a lease scope tears
down an RR, also consult the Surface A interface-DDNS store for a record with
the same canonical FQDN + forward type + rdata (reading Surface A's `AddrText`),
and suppress the wire delete if a Surface A co-owner exists — and symmetrically
when a Surface A record is withdrawn, consult the lease store. A shared
"who-else-claims-this-wire-RR" query over BOTH stores (keyed on canonical
FQDN+type+rdata, normalizing `Address`/`AddrText`) is the clean form. Add a
fail-on-revert test: a Surface A record + a Surface B lease co-own one RR; the
lease teardown must leave the Surface-A-owned RR live.

Until fixed, add a one-line limitation note to `pkg/ddns/README.md` stating the
#5709 co-ownership guard is Surface-B-only.
