## #6268 — refactor(userspace-dp): give fragment-association state and policy a protocol-neutral owner [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

This issue combines two coupled but separately landable findings from review 183. The backing cache and its packet-pipeline policy facade must move in separate mechanical steps so publication order and hot assembly remain reviewable.

### R183-F1

Title: The fragment-association cache is protocol-neutral runtime state but remains owned and named by NAT64 after ordinary NAT/NPTv6 began using it.

Severity: Medium-high. This is not a current packet-corruption defect, but it puts a policy-bearing, cross-worker cache used by five translation modes behind the wrong subsystem boundary.

Confidence: High.

Refactor class: B requires guardrails.

Evidence: `nat64.rs:350-570` contains about 221 LOC of shard constants, `Nat64FragKey`, entry state, FNV keying, 64-shard `Arc<Vec<Mutex<Vec<_>>>>` storage, install/LRU/TTL/generation logic, and test-only length accounting. `Nat64State` owns it at `nat64.rs:235-263`. On 2026-07-18, ordinary SNAT, DNAT, static NAT, and NPTv6 began installing and consulting this same state from `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:165-266`. The current comment explicitly says the key/value are family-agnostic:

```rust
// poll_descriptor/mod.rs:165-173
/// #5689: on a FIRST fragment of an ORDINARY same-family NAT / NPTv6 flow that
/// translated and will forward, install a fragment association keyed by
/// `(family, src, dst, ip_id)` so its non-first fragments inherit `decision`
/// and translate L3-only (address-only rewrite) instead of being forwarded
/// UNTRANSLATED (the #5689 leak). Mirrors [`nat64_install_forward_fragment_assoc`]
/// but for the SNAT / DNAT / static-NAT / NPTv6 path. It REUSES the generic
/// `Nat64FragAssoc` cache: the key + value are family-agnostic and the `nat64`
/// flag on the cached decision distinguishes a NAT64 entry from an ordinary one
```

Callers/responsibilities: NAT64 first-fragment install and non-first consult use `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:95-162`; ordinary NAT/NPTv6 use `:184-266`; the two translation directions store optional `Nat64ReverseInfo`; reload reuse occurs in `nat64.rs:945-957`; 10 cache/fragment tests occupy `nat64_tests.rs:4411-4892`. The cache now decides whether non-first fragments inherit a prior `SessionDecision`, and its generation fence is relevant to all NAT policy changes, not merely Pref64 configuration.

Proposed decomposition: Add `afxdp/fragment_assoc.rs` with `FragmentAssoc`, `FragmentKey`, `FragmentAssocValue`, family-neutral first/non-first key extraction, sharding, TTL/LRU, and generation checks. Put one `fragment_assoc: FragmentAssoc` field directly on `ForwardingState` (or a small runtime-state child), reused from the previous forwarding state during rebuild. Keep `Nat64ReverseInfo` as an optional value imported from `nat64`; do not make the cache generic over a trait. Move cache-only tests to `afxdp/fragment_assoc_tests.rs`; leave byte translation tests in `nat64_tests.rs`. Rename the four poll helpers to `fragment_assoc::{install,consult}_{nat64,ordinary}` only if the call-site sequence remains visible.

Hot-path preservation analysis: Preserve exactly 64 shards, cap 64 per shard, 2-second TTL, FNV byte order, `ident.to_be_bytes()`, one mutex acquisition per lookup/install, linear bounded-vector search, in-place `remove/push` LRU behavior, `Arc` sharing across workers/reloads, and `Ordering` behavior outside the cache. The move must add no `Box`, `dyn`, hash allocation, packet copy, per-packet `Arc` clone, or extra lock. Keep consult wrappers `#[inline]`; keep storage and `SessionDecision` copy layout unchanged. A module move is same-crate and monomorphizable, but cross-module inlining and lock count still need assembly/counter gates.

Tests + gate: Preserve all `nat64_frag_assoc_*` tests, add ordinary v4/v6 SNAT/DNAT/static/NPTv6 install-hit-generation-miss tests beside the generic cache, and retain the fail-closed miss controls. Run `cargo test --release --manifest-path userspace-dp/Cargo.toml fragment_assoc`, `nat64`, and poll-descriptor fragment suites. Add a no-allocation lookup test and a contended 64-shard microbenchmark; compare `cargo asm` for the two consult wrappers and verify one mutex lock and no allocator calls. Full Rust suite and native fragment traffic smoke are the merge gate.

Why it matters: The name and ownership tell future maintainers that ordinary NAT changes do not need to consider this cache, while the code now does exactly that. That invites generation, reverse-direction, capacity, and observability changes to be fixed for one translation family and missed for the others.

Fix direction: First move types/storage/tests without semantic changes and keep temporary re-exports. In a second mechanical step, lift the field from `Nat64State` to forwarding runtime state and update all four callers. Only then rename NAT64-prefixed key helpers.

## #6272 — userspace-dp/cos: release_all_cos_queue_leases teardown mem::take is unconditional — an un-leased single-owner non-exact queue's banked burst is zeroed on a lease-set swap (contradicts #5156 README/comment) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

## Finding (rev6270 non-blocking MINOR on #6270/#5156, confirmed firsthand vs origin/master)

#6270 (#5156) widened `release_all_cos_queue_leases` (userspace-dp/src/afxdp/cos/token_bucket.rs) to give back EVERY queue with `hot.tokens > 0` (not just exact), gating only the CREDIT on `shared_queue_lease.is_some()`. But the `core::mem::take(&mut queue.hot.tokens)` itself is **unconditional** — it runs for every `tokens>0` queue, leased or not.

The runtime give-back `refresh_cos_interface_activity` (tx_completion.rs:~762, #4246 R-5(a)) instead gates the `mem::take` ITSELF on `has_lease` — un-leased queues KEEP their banked burst.

**Consequence**: on the two lease-set-swap callers (worker/loop_body/mod.rs:566 & :580 — which persist `cos_interfaces` and only rebuild `cos_fast_interfaces`), an un-leased single-owner NON-EXACT queue's banked burst is zeroed (nothing credited, since it has no lease), then must refill at rate. This **contradicts #6270's own README** ("a truly un-leased single-owner queue (exact or non-exact) keeps its private per-worker burst") and its code comment ("mirroring the runtime empty give-back ... keys on lease presence").

## Why it did NOT block #6270 (rev6270's assessment, verified)
- The **conservation invariant** (#5156's actual goal) is unaffected — an un-leased queue has no lease to mis-provision.
- Transient + self-healing via `refill_cos_tokens`.
- Fires only on lease-set swaps (worker join/leave / config change), NOT per-packet.
- Master ALREADY zeroes un-leased single-owner EXACT queues on this exact path (old filter `exact && tokens>0`), so #6270 extends a pre-existing pattern, not a novel regression.
- The dominant caller `reset_binding_cos_runtime` clears `cos_interfaces` right after (worker/cos/mod.rs:383) — harmless there.

## Fix (one of)
1. **Code-to-docs** (rev6270's optional one-liner): gate the teardown `mem::take` on lease presence too (mirror `refresh_cos_interface_activity`'s R-5(a) `has_lease` gate), so an un-leased burst survives a lease-swap. Fail-on-revert: a single-owner non-exact (un-leased) queue's banked burst survives a lease-set swap.
2. **Docs-to-code**: if zeroing un-leased bursts on a lease-swap is actually intended (matching the pre-existing EXACT-queue behavior), correct the #6270 README + comment to say so.

Option 1 is preferred (makes the code honor its own documented contract + matches the runtime path). CoS teardown accounting — a proper fail-on-revert test + a CoS smoke on merge.

## Provenance
rev6270 hostile review of #6270; the unconditional `mem::take` vs the runtime `has_lease`-gated take confirmed firsthand at token_bucket.rs vs tx_completion.rs:762.

## #6279 — test/incus/wg-interop.sh: P1 config commit fails — peer public-key substitutes as literal "public-key" + "no node matching wg0" (harness bit-rot blocks the WG smoke gate) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

## Symptom (observed running the #5291/#6277 WG smoke, deploy=OK, P0 preflight=PASS)

`./test/incus/wg-interop.sh all` fails at **P1 (keys + peer + xpf commit)**:
```
error: rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = path not found: no node matching "wg0"
error: commit failed: rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = commit check failed:
  wireguard wg0: peer 0 has an invalid public key
  (expected 64 hex chars / 32-byte X25519, got "public-key")
```

The config validator is behaving CORRECTLY — it rejected an invalid key. The bug is in the HARNESS: the `set groups node0 interfaces wg0 tunnel wireguard peer public-key ${PEER_PUB_HEX}` (wg-interop.sh:448) committed the literal string `"public-key"` instead of the generated 64-hex key — `${PEER_PUB_HEX}` was empty/unsubstituted at commit time. There is ALSO a separate `path not found: no node matching "wg0"` error, suggesting a config-command ordering/cleanup issue (a delete/reference to wg0 before it exists).

## Impact
The wg-interop smoke gate is **non-functional for any WireGuard dataplane change** until fixed — a WG PR cannot complete its WG-traffic validation (P2+). #6277 (#5291 per-peer MTU) was merged on its exhaustive unit/review coverage + a successful deploy + P0 preflight pass, since the P1 failure is provably this harness bug (not the #6277 code — #6277 touches only the dataplane, not the config compiler / key validator).

## Likely cause + fix
- `PEER_PUB_HEX` capture (wg-interop.sh:~149-158 generates keys via `wg genkey`/`wg pubkey` into /tmp/wgkeys/ and asserts `${#PEER_PUB_HEX} -eq 64`) — investigate why the assertion passed (or was skipped) yet the commit got the empty/placeholder value. Possibly the keygen block ran in a different shell/instance than where `PEER_PUB_HEX` is read at :448, or a phase-ordering issue (configure ran before/without the keygen output being captured).
- The `no node matching "wg0"` path error suggests the wg0 stanza set-path or the teardown/delete ordering drifted from the current config schema — reconcile the harness's config commands with the current `set interfaces <if> tunnel wireguard` schema.

## Fix direction
Repair the key-capture + config-command ordering in `test/incus/wg-interop.sh` so P1 commits a valid wg0 config, restoring the WG smoke gate. Add a preflight assert that `PEER_PUB_HEX` is a 64-hex key IMMEDIATELY before the `set ... peer public-key` line (fail fast with a clear message rather than committing a placeholder).

## Provenance
Observed firsthand running the #6277 WG smoke on the loss cluster; DEPLOY_RC=0, P0 PASS, P1 FAIL with the above. Deferred #6277's live WG-traffic validation onto this harness fix.

## #6284 — config-epoch guard (#5274) residual coverage: active/active non-authority direction + sweep-vs-advance race [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

Two non-blocking LOW residuals surfaced by the hostile review of PR #6282 (#5274 config-epoch guard). Both are documented/known and NOT regressions (pre-#5274 neither was protected); filing to track future hardening of the guard's coverage. The #5274 guard closes the primary stale-permit gap in the config-authority→peer direction.

## 1. Directional coverage limit (active/active non-authority sessions)
`lastAppliedConfigGen` only advances for PEER-pushed configs (config sync is unidirectional from the `rg0ConfigSyncAuthority` via `pushConfigToPeer`/reconcile). So `configEpochStale` fires only for the config-authority→peer session direction.
- **Active/passive**: complete — the primary owns all sessions AND is the config authority.
- **Active/active**: a non-authority node's sessions carry the frozen boot-seed epoch, so the guard is **inert** for them (fail-OPEN — no false reject, but no stale-permit protection either).
- Explicitly documented in `docs/session-sync-architecture.md`.
- **Fix direction**: give each node a locally-advancing applied-config generation comparable across the boundary (or config-sync the non-authority direction too) so the guard covers both directions. Requires the bidirectional config-gen namespace #5274 deliberately scoped out.

## 2. Residual sweep-vs-advance race (sub-µs)
Config apply is async on `configApplyLoop`; `lastAppliedConfigGen` advances only AFTER `OnConfigReceived` (which runs `clearSessionsForDeletedPolicies`) returns nil. A session installed on the concurrent `receiveLoop` in the sub-µs window between sweep-completion and high-water-advance is admitted against the stale high-water.
- Inherent to the async apply design; vastly smaller than the original #5274 bug window (the sweep is the backstop for installs before/during apply). The #5274 guard shrinks-but-does-not-hermetically-seal even the covered direction.
- **Fix direction**: advance the high-water atomically with (or before) the sweep completes, or gate installs on an apply-in-progress flag for the affected config generation.

Both LOW; neither blocks #6282. Provenance: PR #6282 hostile review (rev6282), verified against `fix/5274-ha-session-config-epoch@eace3755b`.

## #6289 — test/xsk-repro: two LOW robustness follow-ups (umem-fail leaks our XDP prog; selftest SKIP gate misses static-lib check) — #4906 follow-up [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-23)

Two non-blocking LOW follow-ups from the #4906 (PR #6286) hostile review. Neither is a firewall-harm or false-PASS path — the safety-critical properties all hold. Filing to track.

## M1 — shared-test umem-create failure path leaks our attached XDP prog (cleanup gap, LOW)
`test/xsk-repro/libbpf_xsk_shared_test.c:357,367-371`: on `xsk_umem__create` failure (and the `aligned_alloc` NULL at :357 is unchecked), `main` does `return 1` WITHOUT reaching the detach at :404-412, leaving OUR `xdp_pass_redirect` attached to the owner (and possibly secondary) iface.
- NOT a firewall clobber: attach only succeeds on an EMPTY hook (the firewall iface would have EBUSY'd at `load_xdp` and returned at :339), so it can only leak on a NON-firewall iface.
- Fix: `goto` a detach-and-exit path (or check `aligned_alloc` NULL) so the umem/alloc-failure exits also detach our program.

## M2 — selftest-compile.sh SKIP gate probes headers but not static libs (false-RED risk, LOW)
`test/xsk-repro/selftest-compile.sh:27-28`: the SKIP gate probes only headers (`<bpf/bpf.h>`, `<xdp/xsk.h>` with `-fsyntax-only`), but `make check` links against static archives (`Makefile:20` `-Wl,-Bstatic -lxdp -lbpf -lelf -lz -lzstd`). A host with dev headers but MISSING static libs (e.g. no `libzstd.a`) PASSes the SKIP gate then FAILs the link → false-RED for this selftest leg (other legs unaffected; `run_shell` exit-77 SKIP handles a clean skip).
- Works on a fully-provisioned host (validated 43/0).
- Fix: probe a trial LINK (not just header syntax), or widen the SKIP condition to detect missing static libs.

In `refresh_runtime_snapshot` the coordinator stores `shared_validation` BEFORE `ha.forwarding` (snapshot_refresh.rs ~:397-398). The worker reads `validation` (loop_body ~:411) BEFORE `forwarding` (~:419). Because the store order (validation-then-forwarding) matches the read order (validation-then-forwarding), a worker can transiently observe OLD validation + NEW forwarding in the ≤1-tick window (the acquire/release message-passing runs the OTHER way for this pair, unlike the CoS maps which #6288 reordered to store-after… i.e. CoS is now stored before forwarding so the worker's forwarding-then-CoS read is safe; validation is stored before forwarding AND read before forwarding, so new-forwarding can pair with old-validation).

- Assess: what does `validation` gate on the worker path, and is a transient old-validation + new-forwarding observation harmful (e.g. a packet validated under stale rules then forwarded under new state) or benign (validation is advisory / converges next tick)?
- If harmful: either store validation AFTER forwarding (so the worker reading validation-before-forwarding never sees new-forwarding with old-validation) or bracket with a generation check — mirror the #6288 reorder reasoning for the validation Arc.
- If benign: document the invariant (validation is eventually-consistent, not ordering-critical) in the snapshot_refresh module doc.

Provenance: PR #6288 hostile review (rev5166), verified against `fix/5166-cos-snapshot-refresh-ordering@4b1fe7a32`.

## #6294 — test: wg_encap_frame_resolves_outer_route_once_v4 is a parallel-test race on the global OUTER_ROUTE_RESOLVE_COUNT atomic (pre-existing flake; passes in isolation) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

## #6296 — configstore/ha: MarkActiveApplied stamps after syncAndApply releases applySem (TOCTOU vs a concurrent secondary-side promoter) — stamp under applySem keyed to compiled (#4957 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-23)

MINOR/robustness follow-up from the #4957 (PR #6292) hostile review. LOW severity; filing to track the cleaner hardening.

`handleConfigSync` calls `MarkActiveApplied()` AFTER `syncAndApply` has RELEASED `applySem`, and the marker reads `s.active` at stamp time (not the `compiled` value it actually applied). If a concurrent promoter (a local commit / commit-confirmed rollback on the SECONDARY) lands in that window and its own apply then fails non-fatally, the stamp could key the WRONG (unapplied) active digest → a subsequent re-push of that text would be treated as converged.

- **Why LOW**: failure requires all of — secondary-side local config activity (config normally flows primary→secondary and would be overwritten by the authoritative push) + a µs-scale window + a failing apply + the primary later re-pushing that exact text. Architecturally unlikely.
- **Fix**: stamp INSIDE `syncAndApply` while holding `applySem`, keyed to the `compiled` it applied (e.g. a `MarkConfigApplied(compiled)` variant), rather than post-release keyed to `s.active`. The other two stamp sites (`applyConfig`, `applyAndSyncCommitted`) already stamp while holding applySem — this aligns the third.
- Also fold the two conservative-safe missed stamp sites noted in review (`applyConfigResult` feed path; commit-confirmed rollback at daemon_apply.go:882) if the same-active-text idempotent-re-apply is worth eliminating (currently harmless — never false-converges).

Provenance: PR #6292 hostile review (rev4957), verified against `fix/4957-ha-configsync-unapplied-converged@de9bc869a`.

## #6297 — userspace-dp: budgeted conntrack refresh walks full historical slab capacity after a high-watermark drain (mostly-vacant slots) — cap the walk to a tracked high-watermark (#5287 M1 follow-up) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-22)

MINOR efficiency follow-up from the #5287 (PR #6295) hostile review. Harmless (bounded + syscall-free); filing to track.

`iter_with_idle_budgeted` bounds the walk to `entries.capacity()`, and the slab capacity is monotonic non-decreasing (no `shrink_to_fit`). So after a session-count high-watermark followed by a drain, each 10s cycle still walks the FULL historical capacity — mostly-vacant slots (`get(idx)` → None, skipped) — rather than the current live extent. The per-slice cost stays hard-bounded at 2048 slots/tick and the vacant-slot visits are `get(idx)` → None (no syscall, no work), so this is purely a small wasted-iteration cost, NOT a correctness or latency defect.

- **Fix direction**: cap the cycle to a tracked live high-watermark (max occupied index + 1) instead of `capacity()`, or periodically compact — so a drained table's cycle scans only the live extent. Keep the `capacity()`-bounded correctness (every live slot < len <= capacity) as the invariant.
- Low value; only matters for a workload that spikes session count then drops for a long time.

Also noted (NOT filed — pre-existing, not a regression): the fresh-boot first refresh cycle is delayed to ~10s uptime because `ct_cycle_start_ns` starts at 0 — identical to old master (`last_ct_refresh_ns=0`).

Provenance: PR #6295 hostile review (rev5287), verified against `fix/5287-conntrack-refresh-budget@52062ed1b`.

## #6301 — cluster: ResetFailover leaves a dormant remoteTransferOutLease map entry; lease sizing ignores failoverActuateTimeout/commitDelay (#5079 MINOR follow-ups) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-23)

Two MINOR non-blocking notes from the #5079 (PR #6300) hostile review. Both harmless in realistic configs; filing for hygiene/completeness.

## 1. ResetFailover leaves a dormant lease-map entry (hygiene nit)
`ResetFailover` clears `rg.ManualFailover` but does NOT clear the `remoteTransferOutLease{Until,ReqID}` map entry for that RG → a dormant leftover entry.
- **Harmless today**: the electRG lease-expiry restore is gated on `if rg.ManualFailover` (true), and EVERY path that re-sets ManualFailover=true clears the lease first (`ManualFailover`, `ForceSecondary`/ISSU, `ManualFailoverBatch` all call `clearRemoteTransferOutLeaseLocked`). So a dormant entry can never drive a wrong restore.
- **Fix**: add `clearRemoteTransferOutLeaseLocked(rgID)` to `ResetFailover` for consistency with the other reset paths (no behavior change, just no leftover map growth on repeated resets).

## 2. Lease duration scales only with localFailoverCommitTimeout
The owner-side lease is sized `2*localFailoverCommitTimeout + 20s` (floor 15s), which does NOT account for `failoverActuateTimeout` or `localFailoverCommitDelay`.
- **Not exploitable**: worst-case lease-arm→commit-arrival ≈ barrier(≤failoverActuateTimeout 3s) + settle(≤commitTimeout+delay ~3.2s) ≈ ~6.5s << the 15s floor for realistic configs. Only a pathological config (`failoverActuateTimeout ≫ commitTimeout`) could theoretically matter — and even then a timed-out barrier sends `failoverAckFailed` → a CORRECT restore (the requester side aborts), not a wrong one.
- **Optional hardening**: fold `failoverActuateTimeout + localFailoverCommitDelay` into the lease-duration computation so the lease provably exceeds the max legitimate commit-arrival latency under ANY config.

Provenance: PR #6300 hostile review (rev5079), verified against `fix/5079-remote-failover-owner-rollback@0a96fbc60`.

## #6311 — userspace-dp/HA: session-id namespace has no node discriminator — adopted peer id collides with local same-worker id (active/active) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

Follow-up from the #6309 (#5212) hostile review.

## Problem

The stable session id is allocated as `worker_id<<48 | counter` with **no node
discriminator** (`alloc_session_id` / `set_worker_id`,
`userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:749-766`; `worker_id` is a plain queue index
0..5, `setup.rs:124`). Both HA nodes run the SAME worker set (0..5 on the
6-queue mlx5 VF) and both per-worker counters start at 1.

Under #5212 a standby ADOPTS the primary's id verbatim
(`build_synced_session_entry` / `upsert_synced_with_origin`,
`session/install.rs`). So an adopted id `(w<<48)|c` collides with the importing
node's OWN worker-`w` local id `(w<<48)|c`. In an **active/active** cluster
(bidirectional sync, a supported+tested mode — `test-active-active`)
low-counter collisions early after boot are essentially guaranteed. Adoption
also never reconciles `next_session_id` (`install.rs:334-337`), so a later
local alloc can re-hand-out an already-adopted id.

This also REGRESSES pre-#5212 same-node id uniqueness: before #5212 every
import got a fresh local id, so a node's own RT_FLOW/log stream was internally
unique; after #5212 two distinct sessions on one node can share an id.

## Bound / severity

session_id is a **metadata-only** stamp — RT_FLOW correlation + the
`show security flow session` mirror id — NEVER a lookup key or slab handle
(lookups are 5-tuple keyed; `session_id_for` just reads `entry_by_key`,
`mod.rs:1010`). So there is **no** structural / forwarding / security / memory
impact. The damage is observability-only: a duplicate correlation stamp and a
non-unique mirror id in active/active. MODERATE — it partially defeats the
feature's own "one id per logical session" goal and regresses same-node
uniqueness, but cannot break the dataplane.

## Fix direction

Fold a node-discriminator bit into the id namespace so adoption is globally
collision-free while preserving cross-node correlation (the adopted id carries
the ORIGINATING node's bit, which never collides with the adopting node's own
node-bit-1 ids). Requires plumbing the node-id into the dataplane session

   only signals `warm_stop` and drops the producer handle; it never joins the

## #6368 — cluster/session-sync: config-epoch guard's install epoch-check and Put are not atomic (check-then-act residual, sibling of #6284) — pre-existing #5274 residual [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

Surfaced by the #6366 (#6284 item-2) Codex hostile review, firsthand-confirmed as PRE-EXISTING (present in the #5274 code before #6366; NOT introduced by the apply-in-progress fence).

## Residual
`configEpochStale` (pkg/cluster/sync_conn_gen.go) checks the install's ConfigEpoch against max(applyingConfigGen, lastAppliedConfigGen), then the install performs its map `Put` at a LATER line (v4 ~:452, v6 ~:481). The check and the Put are NOT atomic. So an install whose epoch-check reads the threshold BEFORE `beginConfigApply` raises the fence can PAUSE and land its Put AFTER the deleted-policy sweep — slipping past the guard.

## Why LOW / not a #6366 blocker
- **Pre-existing**: the same check-then-act gap exists in the #5274 code; #6366 closes a DIFFERENT window (sweep-completion → high-water-advance) and does not claim to serialize the install's own check→Put.
- **Practically impossible timing**: the entire beginConfigApply + full clearSessionsForDeletedPolicies sweep would have to fit inside a single install's check→Put gap (a few instructions), on the receiveLoop goroutine, racing the configApplyLoop goroutine.
- Sub-µs, no leak/crash; a slipped install is a stale-permit, self-corrected by the next config-apply sweep.

## Fix direction (if ever pursued)
Serialize the epoch-check with the install under one critical section (hold recvGenMu across check+Put), OR re-check the epoch after acquiring the map lock (check-lock-recheck). Both add a lock on the hot install path — weigh against the sub-µs/practically-impossible exposure. Belongs with the #5274 config-epoch guard residual family (sibling of #6284 item-1, active/active bidirectional namespace).

Provenance: #6366 Codex review (MAJOR-1); parent firsthand-adjudicated as pre-existing + out-of-scope for #6284 item-2.

## #6371 — cluster/failover: a failed SetRGActive(false) still fires signalFailoverActuated → UNBOUNDED dual cluster-active forwarding under persistent control-socket failure (from #6177 research) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-21)

Surfaced + firsthand-verified during the #6177 /research (docs/research/6177-reth-twoowner/plan.md, Q2/Option D). This carries #6177's REAL security content — the RETH VIP-removal timing (#6177/#6367) was benign; THIS is the actual dual-active hazard.

## Defect
On a coordinated transfer-out demotion, the daemon calls SetRGActive(false) then signalFailoverActuated (pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:367→389). If SetRGActive(false) FAILS (control-socket / helper error), the code STILL fires signalFailoverActuated → the failover ACK releases and the peer proceeds to forward as cluster-active WHILE this node's rg_active is still set → BOTH nodes forward. The only recovery is the 2s reconcile loop, which is a RETRY CADENCE, not a bound: under a PERSISTENT control-socket failure the dual-forwarding window is UNBOUNDED.

## Why this is the real hazard (vs #6177/#6367)
#5640 gates the ACK on rg_active CLEAR to prevent dual cluster-active forwarding — but only on the SUCCESS path. A FAILED clear is not fenced. The RETH VIP-removal window #6177/#6367 chased is sub-ms + benign (VIP/ARP ownership is governed by VRRP priority-0/GARP, not rg_active). rg_active is what gates FORWARDING, so a failed clear + released ACK = genuine dual-active forwarding.

## Fix direction (needs its own /research — real tradeoffs)
Option D: an rg_active forwarding fence — do NOT release the failover ACK (do NOT fire signalFailoverActuated) until SetRGActive(false) is CONFIRMED, and hold forwarding fenced until then. BUT: aborting the failover on a failed clear → the requester times out and the ~30s #5079 remote-transfer-out lease blackholes; and it conflicts with #485. The right lever (fence forwarding on the confirmed clear) needs a plan that weighs the abort→blackhole vs the unbounded-dual-active exposure. Route to /research.

Provenance: #6177 hostile plan-review (Codex + Claude SMR), surfaced while settling that the VIP-removal window was benign.

malformed persisted state) yields a nonempty basename.

`PreviousVersion != ""`. `versionDirComplete` (~632-652) validates the **new**
target immediately before start, never `PreviousVersion`. So the dangling
basename is recorded as `PreviousVersion` and passes every guard.

1. xpfd is healthy from the concrete systemd `ExecStart` path while
   `versions/current` is dangling / names a dir missing a lockstep binary.
2. A fresh cut records the basename as `PreviousVersion` and passes both

5. That flip fails (target does not exist) and the function returns with **xpfd

so the corrupt-layout fail-closed posture is the intended contract; the
standalone path is the gap.

## #6377 — policymatch: unsupported-tuple gate folds IPv4-mapped IPv6 source (To4) — false UnsupportedTupleFamily [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-23)

`pkg/policymatch/policymatch.go` (`Match`, ~line 971) classifies address
family with `net.IP.To4()`, which **folds** an IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal.
As a result a policy-match query whose source is authored as
`::ffff:192.0.2.1` and whose destination is `2001:db8::1` is wrongly
reported `UnsupportedTupleFamily` (V4 src / V6 dst), even though the
colon-strict runtime matcher (`userspace-dp/src/policy.rs`) sees the
mapped source as V6 and treats it as a valid same-family V6/V6 tuple that
should fall through and be evaluated normally.

This is a false positive on a diagnostic surface. It is **fail-safe** — a
spurious "unsupported tuple" advisory, never a hidden or fabricated
permit, and no dataplane effect — but it diverges from the runtime and
from the project's documented Go/Rust family-parity convention.

## Root cause

`net.ParseIP("192.0.2.1")` and `net.ParseIP("::ffff:192.0.2.1")` return
**byte-identical** 16-byte `net.IP` values, both with `.To4() != nil`.
All four `Query` builders parse operator text with `net.ParseIP`:

- `pkg/cli/cli_show_security.go`
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_show_firewall.go`
- `pkg/grpcapi/server_cluster.go`

so by the time the gate sees `q.SrcIP`/`q.DstIP` the colon (`:`) signal
that would distinguish a real IPv4 from an IPv4-mapped IPv6 has already
been discarded. There is therefore **no** colon-strict determination
available at the gate from the parsed IPs alone.

The colon-strict family classifier already exists and is the SSOT for
exactly this trap: `natAddrFamily` / `config.NATAddrFamily` in
`pkg/config/compiler_nat_helpers.go`. It keys family on whether the

## #6381 — test: TestMgmtReconcileTLSChange_5866 asserts a false 'fresh leaf per rebind' invariant that only passes because CI /etc/xpf/tls is unwritable [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-23)

## Defect

`TestMgmtReconcileTLSChange_5866` (pkg/daemon/management_5866_test.go:180-192)
asserts that an HTTPS rebind serves **different** leaf certificate bytes on the
second reconcile. That is the **opposite** of the durable self-signed-cert
contract (#1916 D6): a persisted `/etc/xpf/tls` pair is LOADED as-is on rebind
and deliberately NOT re-minted (re-minting would churn remote clients' TOFU
pins — see #5719 / PR #6378).

## Why it passes today (test-env artifact)

The daemon wires `certGen = generateSelfSignedCert`, which uses the production
`/etc/xpf/tls` paths with no test redirect. In CI those paths are unwritable, so:

1. `LoadX509KeyPair` finds no on-disk pair,
2. the persist write fails silently,
3. every reconcile mints a **fresh in-memory** cert,
4. leaf bytes differ → the assertion passes.

In production (writable `/etc/xpf/tls`) the second reconcile would LOAD the same
on-disk pair → **identical** leaf bytes → the assertion would FAIL. The test
encodes an invariant the shipping behavior contradicts; it is green only
because the environment can't persist.

## Fix sketch

Redirect the test to a temp TLS dir (as `generateSelfSignedCertAt` already
supports) and re-encode the INTENDED invariant: a material management change
rebinds the listener (new `*http.Server` / socket), not necessarily a new
certificate. Assert the durable-cert behavior (same on-disk pair reloaded)
rather than differing leaf bytes.

## Provenance

Surfaced while folding the Codex hostile review of PR #6378 (#5719 C-API
residual, bind-host cert SANs). Traced firsthand: the durable-cert path loads
as-is on rebind, so the "different leaf bytes" assertion is a CI-only artifact.

On the loss userspace HA cluster, the standby node (**fw1 / node1**) is permanently
stuck **`Transfer ready: no`** with **`applied config gen=0`** for every redundancy
group, so a **planned/manual failover to fw1 is refused indefinitely**. Root cause:
the config-sync payload is received on the standby but its *apply* hard-fails on the
host-inbound nftables step, and because the apply returns an error the config
high-water mark (`lastAppliedConfigGen`) is never advanced — leaving the standby
forever "behind" the primary's committed generation.

package — see the companion issue). The design has **no self-heal, no operator
alarm surfaced in the RG status line, and no netlink fallback** for the
host-inbound step, so any persistent host-inbound apply failure silently strands
the standby as non-transfer-ready even though its **dataplane forwarding + FRR
applied successfully**.

## #6391 — security/config: per-interface host-inbound on a bracketed-membership interface can leak to sibling interfaces (naive fanout unsound) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-01)

## Summary

Splitting out #5609 A3.1. The original observation: a per-interface
`host-inbound-traffic` override authored under a bracketed interface membership
(`interfaces { [ ge-0/0/0 ge-0/0/1 ] { host-inbound-traffic {...} } }`, reachable
via `load override`) is compiled onto the FIRST member only, so a sibling member
falls back to the (often more-permissive) zone-level host-inbound. PR #6389
attempted to fix this by fanning the override to ALL bracket members
(`zoneInterfaceMembers(iface)`).

**That fanout is unsound — it introduces a security regression** (firsthand-
confirmed, and caught by the Codex hostile review of #6389; #6389 CLOSED):

```
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces [ ge-0/0/0 ge-0/0/1 ]
set security zones security-zone trust interfaces ge-0/0/0 host-inbound-traffic system-services ssh
```

This valid, common flat-set config scopes SSH host-inbound to `ge-0/0/0` ONLY.
But `SetPath` (pkg/config/ast_edit.go:271/443) nests the bracket tail and REUSES
the first-member container, so the `ge-0/0/0` node carries BOTH the bracket
membership (`ge-0/0/1` child) AND the host-inbound body. The fanout then fans the
`ge-0/0/0`-scoped SSH admission onto `ge-0/0/1` (compiler_security_zones.go:202),
both interfaces are defined so the strict gate accepts it, and effective
admission is additive (host_inbound_view.go) → **SSH is opened on `ge-0/0/1`,
which the operator never configured for it.**

Verified firsthand: on the #6389 head `ge-0/0/1` gets `[ssh]`; on origin/master
it does not.

## Root cause

After compilation the two cases are STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL:
- hierarchical `ge-0/0/0 { ge-0/0/1; host-inbound {...} }` (multi-member intent), and
- flat-set `[ge-0/0/0 ge-0/0/1]` membership + `ge-0/0/0 host-inbound {...}` (single-scoped, SetPath-merged).

So a fanout keyed on the compiled AST alone CANNOT distinguish "apply to all
bracket members" from "apply to this one interface that happens to share a
container with a bracket membership." The naive fanout is therefore ambiguous
and, in the flat-set case, over-admits.

*(truncated — 62 lines total)*

## #6395 — daemon: shutdown aggregator final-flush wait is unbounded and precedes the HA fence (C179-093 residual) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-23)

## Regression (from PR #6394, C179-093)

`stopAggregator` (pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:337) now does `cancel(); d.aggWg.Wait()`
— an UNBOUNDED join on the session-aggregator goroutine — and is called from
`runShutdownSequence` BEFORE the HA/dataplane teardown (daemon_run_shutdown.go:~138).
The cancel triggers the #5313 ctx.Done final flush, which forwards the pending
aggregation report SYNCHRONOUSLY through the syslog client (pkg/logging/aggregator.go:271
→ SetLogFunc → er.ForwardLogMsg). Stream syslog allows ~4s per write (pkg/logging/syslog.go).

**Impact:** under a stalled / unreachable TCP/TLS syslog sink, each flush write blocks up
to 4s, so the final flush can delay shutdown by ~16s (4 report lines × 4s) BEFORE the HA
fence runs. The systemd stop budget is 20s (test/incus/xpfd.service), so a stalled sink can
push the fence past the budget → SIGKILL before the peer takeover fence completes. Before
#6394 the aggregator was simply leaked at shutdown (benign, process exiting), so shutdown
never waited on it — this is a new shutdown-hang/delayed-fence risk.

## Fix

Bound the flush/join: give `stopAggregator`'s `d.aggWg.Wait()` a deadline (e.g. a small
budget well under the fence's share of the 20s stop window), OR pass a deadline-bearing
context into the final flush so a stalled sink cannot delay the fence. On timeout, proceed
to teardown (the leaked-flush is the acceptable fallback — better a dropped partial report
than a missed fence). Add a test with a BLOCKING fake log sink asserting stopAggregator
returns within the deadline (and the fence still runs).

## Provenance

Codex hostile review of PR #6394 (finding 4), firsthand-confirmed. #6394 merged; this is a
fast follow-up. Tracked under #5523 (codex-179).

## #6402 — routing/bond: type-gate the bond adopt-path readback (last of the identity-assertion family; HA smoke) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

## Summary

The bond **adopt** path in `createLocked` (`pkg/routing/bond.go`, the
`if existing, err := b.ops.LinkByName(name); err == nil` steady-state
reconcile branch, ~line 273) is **not type-gated**: on a steady-state
reconcile it adopts whatever link currently wears the bond's name, without
re-asserting it is a `*netlink.Bond`. A same-name foreign link (created by an
external actor, or a leftover of a different type after a name collision) is
brought up and tracked as a satisfied bond, so the fabric/RETH bond silently
does not exist while the reconcile reports success.

This is the last member of the post-create/adopt readback identity-assertion
family:
- **xfrm** create + adopt — both gated (#5523 adopt, #6399 create readback).
- **VRF** create + adopt — both gated (#6399 create readback, `vrfTable`→recreate adopt).
- **bond** create readback — gated in #6399 (`*netlink.Bond` re-assertion).
- **bond adopt** — STILL UNGATED (this issue).

## Why it was split out of #6399

#6399 hardened the fail-closed **create-path** readbacks (fresh-device, no
steady-state behavior change → no smoke needed). Type-gating the bond **adopt**
path changes steady-state fabric/RETH bond reconcile behavior — it would
reject/recreate a non-bond same-name device on every reconcile — so it is
**HA-touching** and requires a `make test-failover` loss-cluster smoke before
merge. That is out of scope for the low-risk #6399 create-path cohort.

## Proposed fix

In the adopt branch of `createLocked`, after `LinkByName` succeeds, re-assert
`existing.(*netlink.Bond)`; on mismatch, delete + recreate (mirroring the
`vrfTable`→recreate adopt path and the xfrm #5523 adopt gate) rather than
adopting the foreign link. Add a fail-on-revert test (foreign same-name link on
a tracked bond name → reconcile deletes+recreates, does not adopt). Gate:
`make test-failover` on the loss userspace cluster (fabric bond is on the RETH
path).

## #6403 — configstore: ArchiveConfig synchronous-mirror off-lock seq race vs SetArchiveConfig reseed (latent, zero prod callers) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

## Summary

`Store.ArchiveConfig` (the synchronous archive mirror, `pkg/configstore/store_persist.go`) captures the next archive sequence under `RLock`, releases the lock, then performs the file write OFF-lock. A concurrent `SetArchiveConfig` (which holds the write lock) can reseed the monotonic counter to a HIGHER value in that off-lock window, so the low-sequence archive `ArchiveConfig` is about to write lands with a seq below the reseeded counter — and seq-ordered retention (`store_persist.go` rotation) then treats the just-written file as stale and prunes it early.

## Materiality

**Zero production callers** — `ArchiveConfig` (the synchronous mirror) is currently exercised only by tests; the live path is the async `persistRetryLoop`. So this is a LATENT ordering race, not an active data-loss bug. Filed for completeness so a future caller of the synchronous mirror does not silently hit it.

## Why it wasn't fixed in #6399

The obvious fix — hold `s.mu` across `ArchiveConfig`'s read-seq + off-lock write — **reintroduces the #6185 `QuiesceArchival` deadlock** (the write is intentionally off-lock so a long archival I/O does not block reconcile/quiesce). Closing the race correctly needs a restructuring (e.g. an atomic claim-seq-then-write reservation, or a per-dir seq token that the reseed cannot overtake), not a lock-scope widening. That is out of scope for the low-risk #6399 create-path/archive-hardening cohort.

## Provenance

Found during the #6399 Codex hostile review (MINOR 5). xfrm/VRF/bond create-path identity assertions + archive scan-error robustness were folded into #6399; this off-lock ordering race was deferred here as needing a restructure. Related deferral: #6402 (bond adopt-path type-gating).

## #6404 — configstore: archive reseed edges — post-scan-failure commit interval + disable/re-enable same-dir skip [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-23)

Follow-up from the #6399 (#6396) Codex review. The #6396 archive-reseed hardening (`maxArchiveSeq` now distinguishes a `ReadDir` error from an empty dir; `SetArchiveConfig` keys the reseed off `archiveSeedDir` and retries on a scan error instead of pinning the counter to 0) is a strict improvement. Two narrow edges of the seq-seeding path remain open — both are latent day-2 refinements, deferred out of #6399 to keep that PR to the verified core.

## 1. Commit lands in the post-scan-failure window (Codex MINOR 2)
`SetArchiveConfig` activates the new dir (`s.archiveDir = dir`) BEFORE the reseed scan, and on a scan error leaves the counter low + the dir un-seeded to retry on the NEXT `SetArchiveConfig` call. But a config **commit** can land in the interval between the failed scan and that next retry: `commitWithDescriptionLocked` (`pkg/configstore/store_commit.go:284`) captures `seq := s.archiveSeq.Add(1)` off the still-low counter and writes an archive to the new dir. If the new dir already holds higher-seq archives, that fresh archive carries a below-max seq and `rotateArchives` prunes it as stale. (The #6396 test drives `SetArchiveConfig` retry directly, so it does not exercise this production commit-interval.)

Possible fix directions: seed the counter from the target dir under the same lock the commit archive path uses before activating the dir; or have the async/sync archive writers themselves reconcile the counter against the target dir's on-disk max when the dir is not yet successfully seeded.

## 2. disable → re-enable to the SAME dir skips the rescan (Codex MINOR 3)
`archiveSeedDir` is not invalidated when archival is disabled (`SetArchiveConfig("")` early-returns without touching it). So `A` → `""` → `A` leaves `archiveSeedDir == A`, and the re-enable to `A` skips the rescan. If the on-disk max in `A` advanced while archival was off (another process/tenant wrote there), the counter stays low and fresh archives are pruned as stale. This contradicts the README's prior "re-seeds on ANY archive-dir change" wording (corrected in #6399 to describe what is actually guaranteed today).

Possible fix: clear `archiveSeedDir` when `dir == ""` (disable), so a later re-enable rescans.

## Scope / risk
Both are in `pkg/configstore` (control-plane, no HA/dataplane coupling), low-risk, unit-testable with the `archiveDirReader` seam added in #6396. Not urgent — the #6396 fix already closed the permanent-regression-on-transient-error case; these are the remaining exotic intervals.

Refs: #6396, #6399. README already corrected in #6399 (`pkg/configstore/README.md`) to note both edges as open.

## #6409 — upgrade: validateRestorableVersion cannot detect a regular+exec-bit lockstep binary with non-executable CONTENT (corrupt/text/wrong-arch) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

Split-out follow-up from #6374 / #6408 (round-5 split convergence).

## Scope

`pkg/upgrade` `validateRestorableVersion` gates whether a `current` /
`PreviousVersion` runtime is a restorable rollback target before STOP. #6408
made the predicate reject the common corruption modes:

- absent / not-a-symlink `current`
- pathful / dangling `current`
- missing version dir / non-directory version path
- lockstep-incomplete dir
- a lockstep binary that is a **directory / FIFO / socket / symlink /
  non-executable regular file**

## Residual (static-validation limit)

The check validates **metadata**: each `manifest.LockstepNames()` binary exists,
is a **regular file**, and has the **executable bit** (`Perm()&0o111 != 0`). It
does NOT — and fundamentally cannot, statically — verify the file's **content**
is actually executable by the kernel. A regular file with the exec bit but
non-executable content (arbitrary text `chmod 0755`, a truncated/corrupt binary,
a wrong-architecture ELF) passes `IsRegular + exec-bit` yet `execve` fails, so
systemd cannot restart it after STOP — the #6374 hazard on a rare
tampering/corruption mode.

You cannot prove "systemd can exec this" without exec'ing it: an ELF-magic
(`\x7fELF`) header probe is a heuristic (a legitimate `#!`-shebang runtime is
"executable" but not ELF; a valid ELF can still be a wrong-arch/corrupt image),
and actually exec-probing the rollback binary during a pre-STOP check is its own
risk. Final content-executability is systemd's arbiter at restart.

## Options

- Add an ELF-magic-header heuristic (`\x7fELF`) as a *best-effort* additional
  gate, explicitly documented as a heuristic, not a guarantee — accepting it
  would false-reject a legitimate non-ELF (script) variant runtime.
- OR leave static validation as-is and rely on the post-start health gate +
  auto-rollback, documenting the limit (current posture, documented in
  `docs/in-place-upgrade.md`).

*(truncated — 51 lines total)*

## #6419 — config-epoch guard (#5274): bidirectional config-gen namespace to protect the active/active non-authority direction (enhancement) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

Design-heavy enhancement (NOT a bug/regression). Splits out the substantive
hardening deferred from #6284 item 1 so #6284's coverage gap can close.

## Background

The #5274 config-epoch guard (`configEpochStale`) refuses a synced session
install whose stamped config epoch is strictly older than the receiver's
applied-config high-water. It closes the primary stale-permit gap in the
config-authority -> peer direction.

Config sync is **unidirectional** from the RG0 config-sync authority
(`QueueConfig` -> `nextConfigGen`), so:

- the send-stamp counter (`configGenCounter`, read by `stampInstallGen*`)
  advances only on the config authority;
- the receive high-water (`lastAppliedConfigGen`) advances only where a peer
  config is applied (`recordAppliedConfigGen`).

## The limitation (deliberate #5274 scope-out)

In an **active/active** deployment the reverse direction
(non-authority -> authority) is **inert / fail-OPEN**: a non-authority node
stamps its synced-out sessions with the frozen boot-seed epoch, and the config
authority's receive high-water never advances (it applies no peer config), so
`configEpochStale` never fires for those sessions. This is a documented,
DELIBERATE #5274 scope-out — **not a regression** (pre-#5274 neither direction
was protected). It is fail-OPEN: no false reject, but also no stale-permit
protection for that direction. Active/passive is unaffected (the primary owns
all sessions AND is the config authority).

Documented in `docs/session-sync-architecture.md` (item-1 residual section), and
the directional behavior is now regression-pinned by
`pkg/cluster/sync_config_epoch_active_active_6284_test.go` (added in #6418).

## Fix direction

Give each node a locally-advancing applied-config generation comparable across
the HA boundary (or config-sync the non-authority direction too), so the guard
covers both directions. Requires the **bidirectional config-gen namespace**
#5274 deliberately scoped out — a design-heavy change; low priority (the current

## #6440 — test/CoS: apply-cos-config.sh exits 6 on loss:xpf-userspace-fw0 (no shaper binding, auto-rollback) — investigate [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

## Summary

During the #6417 loss-cluster HA failover smoke (deploy of a config-validation
PR, unrelated to CoS), `test/incus/apply-cos-config.sh loss:xpf-userspace-fw0`
exited **6**: the post-commit CoS verification saw **no shaper/scheduler
binding** and auto rolled-back cleanly ("live state reverted" — Junos candidate
semantics preserved the live config, no half-broken state).

The failover legs then ran on the rolled-back BASE config (unshaped), which is
why the smoke reported the normal ~22-23 Gbps unshaped fast-path rate. Forwarding
+ failover were fully healthy; this is orthogonal to #6417 (which gates the HA
forwarding-arm reconcile and does not touch the CoS-apply path).

## What to investigate

- Does `apply-cos-config.sh` on `loss:xpf-userspace-fw0` reproducibly exit 6 with
  no shaper/scheduler binding after a fresh deploy? (Deploy WIPES CoS, so this is
  the standard re-apply step — it should bind.)
- Is this a real regression in the CoS-apply / shaper-binding verification on the
  loss userspace cluster, a shim/dataplane-ABI mismatch (verify-dataplane), or a
  pre-existing loss-cluster state? Bisect against recent merges if it's a
  regression (this session merged ~24 PRs, none touching CoS shaping directly).
- Confirm the per-class CoS smoke (ports 5200-5211, `cos-iperf-config.set`) still
  shapes correctly, or whether the binding failure blocks it.

Filed from the #6417 smoke (smoke6417). LOW/investigate — does not block any
merged PR; the auto-rollback left the cluster healthy.

data race between the test `TestEncryptedRoundTripNoWarn_4579` and the
production `persistRetryLoop` goroutine, on a shared log buffer.

This is **unrelated to #6444** — neither location is touched by that
patch (confirmed: #6444 only changes `ArchiveConfig`'s seed/claim
locking). The isolated `TestArchiveConfig*` tests passed 20× under
`-race`; the race is on a different test path and pre-dates #6444.

## Provenance / verification status

Surfaced by an automated Codex review, **not yet confirmed firsthand.**
The full-package `-race` run in some environments is also perturbed by
sandbox socket/netlink denials, so the first action is to **reproduce
the race at current master** in a socket/netlink-capable environment:

```
go test ./pkg/configstore/ -race -count=5
```

`TestEncryptedRoundTripNoWarn_4579` and `persistRetryLoop` on a shared

## #6455 — Pre-expansion top-level-only dup-name gates (#5180 named-block + #6452 NAT-rule) miss group-authored duplicates and skip quoted-empty names [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

## Summary

The pre-expansion duplicate-name commit gates share two inherited
limitations. This was surfaced during the #6452 hostile review (Codex
findings #1 High + #2 Medium) and confirmed to affect **both** gates
1:1, so it is filed as one family-wide follow-up rather than expanding
either gate past the other's scope. Relates to the #5649 cohort
(#6452 landed C181-M18).

Affected gates (identical structure, `pkg/config`):
- `validateDuplicateNamedBlockAST` (#5180, `dup_named_blocks.go`) —
  groups / interfaces / screen ids-option.
- `validateDuplicateNATRuleNamesAST` (#6452, `dup_nat_rule_names.go`) —
  source / destination / static NAT rule names.

## Finding 1 (High) — group-authored duplicates bypass the top-level-only scan

Both gates run **pre-expansion** and scan only top-level stanzas
(`tree.Children` where `Name()=="groups"/"interfaces"/"security"`). This
is deliberate: apply-groups DEEP-MERGES a group-provided named block that
has an inline top-level peer, so a pre-expansion scan avoids a false
positive there. But a duplicate authored **entirely inside an applied
group with no inline peer** is appended wholesale by `ast_groups.go`
(never coalesced), so after `ExpandGroups()` two same-named rows exist —
and no gate runs post-expansion to catch them.

    G {

                        rule R { then { source-nat { interface; } } }
                        rule R { then { source-nat { off; } } }
                    }
                }
            }

stage-12 flow-cache HIT — no session row, no policy re-eval, no `show security
flow session` visibility, no HA sync.

  `flow_cache`).
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/flow_cache_hit.rs:94-134` — the hit
  path validates only config_generation/fib_generation/owner_rg_epoch/lease/
  neighbor-MAC; NO session-existence check.
- Only `invalidate_slot` callers: GC reap (#3776, worker/loop_body/mod.rs:1516),
  RST teardown (worker/lifecycle.rs:235), self-evict on stale (flow_cache_hit.rs:129).
  `FlowCache::invalidate_all` exists but the only production flush is the
  RG-epoch bump on demotion — NOT a delete-path flush.

  rx_queue_index % queue_count` (userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs) — next packet of the
  revoked tuple lands on the same worker whose cache survived.
- Go: `manager_ha.go:1392-1422` BatchDeleteSessions/ClearAllSessions route
  per-key deletes with the stated #5096 goal "an operator clear ... actually
  stops forwarding under revoked decisions" — the observability lie is verbatim.

**Verifier correction (scope):** the hit path DOES validate config_generation,
so the *policy-tightening-via-commit* sub-case is mitigated (a commit bumps the
generation → all entries invalidate). The live exposure is the no-generation-
change sub-cases: **(a) operator `clear security flow session [all]`** (pure
delete IPC, no commit) — the operator's explicit revocation primitive, fully
defeated on the fast path; (b) cluster-stale sweep (BatchDeleteSessions, no
commit); (c) HA DeleteSynced propagation (standby keeps fabric-forwarding a flow
the owner revoked). (a) alone carries the High.

blast radius is a **defeated revocation primitive** — traffic the operator

boundaries.** Verifier verdict: CONFIRMED-WITH-CORRECTION.

new-flow policy evaluation, screen-profile selection, and host-inbound admission
on the receiving node, by forging a zone-encoded synthetic source MAC. The
receive-side decode validates only the magic bytes + that the zone id exists —
no fabric-link identity, no dst-MAC check, no RG-ownership check.

  `forwarding/fabric.rs:327` `resolution.src_mac = Some([0x02,0xbf,0x72,

- RECEIVE decode `parse_zone_encoded_fabric_ingress_from_frame`
  (`frame/inspect.rs:1916-1944`): requires only fabric-ingress ifindex + magic
  bytes + id != 0 + `zone_id_to_name.get(&id)` present. No identity/dst-MAC/RG check.
- Override WINS over interface-derived zone: `forwarding/mod.rs:83-85`
  `ingress_zone_override.or_else(ifindex_to_zone_id)`.
- Session-MISS consumes it for the NEW-flow policy zone-pair

- Screens + SYN-cookie resolve zone with the override FIRST
  (`poll_stages.rs:512-523`, `:815-823`) — attacker picks a zone with no screen.
- Host-inbound: `host_inbound_gated_lo0_action` receives the resolved from-zone
  (`filter.rs:614-649`); falls back to `zone_host_inbound[spoofed]` when the
  fabric iface has no per-iface override (`forwarding/host_inbound.rs:525-541`).
- `StableZoneID(name)` is a public FNV-1a fold (`pkg/config/zoneid.go:38-44`) —
  ids computable offline from Junos-convention zone names.

src MAC `02:bf:72:<MAGIC>:<hi>:<lo>` = StableZoneID("trust")/("mgmt"), a TCP SYN
to a protected LAN host or to the node's own address. `cluster_peer_return_fast_
path` refuses the initial SYN (by design) → falls through to the miss path,
which evaluates policy/screens/host-inbound under the attacker-chosen zone. The
cleanest concrete bypass (verifier): **host-inbound variant** — a spoofed
mgmt-zone frame makes the firewall's own management plane reachable from the
fabric segment, needing no transit policy at all.

**Severity: Medium — config-fail-open / unenforced-control.** Verifier: CONFIRMED.

A partially-unresolvable firewall-filter port list silently narrows a DENY term
on the tolerant-load / HA-sync path — there is no `PortsUnrepresentable` wire
marker where ICMP/DSCP/tcp-flags/flex all got one (#3406 family).

**Evidence (master):**
- `pkg/config/filter_match_resolve.go:304-324` — `resolveFilterPortTokens` keeps
  an UNRESOLVED token verbatim on `term.UnknownPorts`.
- `pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates.go:993-1000` — the strict gate is downgraded
  to a warning under `opts.lenientFilterMatchValues`; reached from
  `CompileConfigLenient`/`CompileConfigForNodeLenient` (Store.Load + SyncApply —
  boot + HA peer-sync).
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go:139-145` — `SourcePorts`/`DestPorts`
  emitted verbatim, NO marker (contrast DSCPMatchUnrepresentable :181-191,
  TCPFlagsUnparseable :230-243, ICMP*Unrepresentable :269-274).
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:784-793` — unparseable tokens dropped
  PER-TOKEN (`filter_map(parse_port_spec)`); surviving tokens still build a matcher.
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/matching.rs:310-318` — `port_match` fails
  closed ONLY when `constrained && PortMatcher::Any` (ALL dropped); a partial
  list matches the surviving subset.

**Trace:** lenient/peer-sync load of `from destination-port [ ssh bogussvc ]` +
`then discard` compiles with a warning. Rust drops `bogussvc`, keeps
`Single(22)`; a packet to the bogussvc port no longer matches term T → falls
through to the implicit accept — the discard the operator wrote for BOTH ports
enforces only ssh. **A deny term silently under-enforces.**

**Severity justification:** trigger = a persisted/peer-authored config on the
tolerant path (strict commit hard-rejects, so a clean commit never reaches this
state) — the same reachability the whole #3406/#3367/#2505 wire-marker family
was built for. Blast radius = a deny narrowed to a subset → traffic the filter
was written to drop is accepted (fail OPEN), bounded to one term. Medium (not
High) because it needs the tolerant path; not lower because the project already
rated this exact shape snapshot-reject-worthy for the sibling leaves.

**Fix:** add a `PortsUnrepresentable` wire marker set in
`buildFilterTermSnapshots` when `len(term.UnknownPorts) > 0`, plus a
`SnapshotIntegrityError` arm in `parse_term` that rejects the whole snapshot —
mirroring ICMPTypeUnrepresentable / #3406.

## #6461 — userspace-dp: blind off-path TCP RST/FIN on a session HIT demotes a live flow to the reaper window with no sequence validation (robustness-dos) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-08-22)

**Severity: Medium — robustness-dos.** Verifier: CONFIRMED (parity nuance noted).

A single blind off-path TCP RST/FIN with a guessed 5-tuple permanently demotes a
live session to the 2s/30s reaper window — no sequence validation. The flow dies
at the next idle gap; repeating the RST keeps it dead.

**Evidence (master):**
- `userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs:105-128` — on every session hit,
  `do_close = is_tcp && is_closing(tcp_flags)` sets sticky `entry.closing = true;
  entry.reset |= has_rst(...)`. No seq/window check exists (SessionEntry carries
  no seq state).
- `userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:1405` — "`closing` is sticky, exactly like
  `reset`" (#3489), never cleared.
- `userspace-dp/src/session/lookup.rs:151-156` — subsequent hits recompute
  `expires_after_ns` to TCP_RST_TIMEOUT_NS (2s) / TCP_CLOSING_TIMEOUT_NS (30s).

**Trace:** attacker sends one tuple-matching RST/FIN (guessable for well-known
services, observable on shared segments). The entry is marked closing+reset
stickily; the first >=2s idle gap (routine for SSH/BGP/IKE/mgmt) reaps it, emits
a Close delta (also killing the HA standby copy), and the next real packet is a
miss requiring a new SYN. **Teeth (verifier):** a SNAT'd flow's re-seed can
allocate a NEW pool port, changing the translated source mid-connection and
killing the endpoint TCP state; the close also propagates to the HA peer.

**Severity justification:** trigger = off-path attacker who knows/guesses the
5-tuple (tempers exploitability → Medium, not High). Blast radius = firewall
state for one flow torn down + a NAT re-seed source change + HA-peer propagation
— the textbook TCP-RST DoS shifted onto the firewall's own state. Bounding: needs
the tuple; mid-stream re-seed pickup (#3152) means the flow can recover unless
the RST is repeated or NAT re-maps. **Parity nuance:** default Junos flow also
tears down on a tuple-matching RST; out-of-window RST drop is opt-in
`tcp-session sequence-check` — so the honest class is robustness-dos, not a
straight parity failure (drop the "vsrx-parity" framing).

**Fix:** gate the closing/reset demotion on plausible sequence placement (track
last-seen seq/ack per direction; accept RST only in-window), or demote only after
the FIN/RST is confirmed in both directions.

**Dedup:** #4400 (bare RST/FIN on miss) and #3489 (sticky closing) are adjacent,
different paths; #4484 has an unrelated "RST clamp" LOW-batch item. No title

  if proto == "" && (dstPort != 0 || len(matchDstPorts) > 0) { proto = "tcp" }`.
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/destination.rs:615-687` — lookup probes
  `(protocol,dst_ip,dst_port) → (protocol,dst_ip,0) → (PROTO_ANY,dst_ip,0)`; a
  UDP packet (proto 17) hits none of the TCP-keyed entries.
- `userspace-dp/src/nat/destination.rs:399-406` — same TCP default mirrored in
  `from_snapshots`.

**Trace:** `match destination-address 198.51.100.10; match destination-port 53;
then destination-nat pool dns-pool` (no protocol — accepted by the commit gate).
UDP/53 to the VIP misses every TCP-keyed entry → NO translation → local-delivered
→ dropped by host-inbound. The UDP DNS service is dead while `show security nat
destination` shows the rule installed.

**Severity justification:** trigger = a common protocol-less DNAT config (no
attacker needed). Blast radius = UDP-only services behind port-based DNAT (DNS,
SIP, VPN) silently dead — fail direction is fail-CLOSED (no security bypass), so
Medium not High; but it is a silent outage + an observability lie (show output
claims the port is translated). Not lower because it breaks a documented,
common Junos config pattern silently.

**Fix:** when no protocol is configured and a destination-port is present, emit
BOTH a TCP and a UDP snapshot entry (mirroring `match protocol [ tcp udp ]`), or
key such rules under PROTO_ANY with the port constraint. Note the change in
docs/feature-coverage.md.

**Dedup:** dedup has DNAT port-range/truncation entries but none on the
protocol-less TCP default. Novel.

_Found by kimi-review-002 deep security audit (base ed6999000, wave-1 hunter + independent wave-2 verifier re-trace). Verified present on master a1b56c9f7; cited files unchanged since base._

## #6463 — config: partially-malformed filter address literal silently narrows a term on the tolerant path (no AddressUnrepresentable marker) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

**Severity: Low (Medium where the term is the primary deny) — config-fail-open.**
Verifier: CONFIRMED. Sibling of the port finding (F-03) via a different leaf.

A partially-malformed firewall-filter address literal silently narrows the term
on the tolerant path — `parse_address` drops per-token with no fail-closed wire
marker.

**Evidence (master):**
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:970-989` — `parse_address` returns `()`;
  an unparseable token pushes nothing (silently dropped).
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:646-649` — `source_addr_constrained =
  source_constrained || any(addr_is_real)` — a malformed token counts as "real",
  so the term stays constrained on the survivors.
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/matching.rs:260-268` — `nets_match_v4`:
  constrained && empty → fail closed; constrained && non-empty subset → matches
  the subset (narrowing).
- `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:1223-1281` — strict reject at
  commit only; downgraded at `compiler_uniformgates.go:1084-1091`.
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go:120-129` — no malformed-literal marker.

**Trace:** lenient load of `from source-address [ 10.0.0.0/8 garbage.example ]` +
`then discard` — Rust keeps the /8, drops `garbage.example`; the discard enforces
only the /8, a host in the dropped range is accepted by fall-through.

**Severity justification:** same deny-narrowing (fail OPEN) consequence and
tolerant-path reachability as F-03, but Low because a malformed literal is a
cruder authoring error than an unresolved service name (lower likelihood);
Medium when the narrowed term is the operator's primary deny.

**Fix:** add an `AddressUnrepresentable` marker (compileFilterFrom records a
token `classifyFilterAddrFamily` rejects — the classifier already exists at
compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:1287) + a snapshot-reject arm, same shape as
F-03/#3406.

**Dedup:** #581 (route-filter CIDR-slot keyword) is the routing surface; no
firewall-filter partial-address-narrowing title. Novel.

## #6464 — userspace-dp: build_global_zone_scope widens a scoped-global policy to ALL zones on an empty-string scope element (should fail closed like #3402) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

**Severity: Low — config-fail-open / robustness.** Verifier: CONFIRMED.

`build_global_zone_scope` widens a scoped-global policy to ALL zones when the
scope list carries an empty-string element, instead of failing closed like an
unresolvable zone name.

**Evidence (master):**
- `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:302-325` — `if names.is_empty() ||
  names.iter().any(|n| n.is_empty() || n == "any") { return
  Ok(GlobalZoneScope::Any); }` — ANY empty element degrades the whole scope to Any.
- `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:2895-2904` — an unresolvable zone NAME raises
  `SnapshotIntegrityError::UnresolvableZoneReference` and rejects the whole
  snapshot (#3402).
- `pkg/config/types_security.go:490-505` (sortDedupZones strips blanks) +
  `pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:799-812` (firewallMatchValues skips empties) —
  the Go control plane never emits an empty scope element.

**Trace:** a corrupt / hand-built / mixed-version-HA-peer snapshot with a scoped
PERMIT global whose `match_to_zones` decodes to `["dmz",""]` resolves to
`GlobalZoneScope::Any` — the permit now applies to every zone pair. The identical
corruption with a garbage name (`["dmz","garbage"]`) rejects the whole snapshot.
This is the one arm in the file that widens instead of failing closed.

**Severity justification:** trigger = corrupt/mixed-version snapshot only (Go
never emits it) — same reachability class the #3402 backstop was built for; Low.
Blast radius = a scoped PERMIT silently enlarged to all zones (fail OPEN); a
scoped DENY would over-deny (fail closed). Not higher because the emit paths are
verified blank-free; not lower because it is a genuine fail-open arm amid a
fail-closed doctrine.

**Fix:** treat `n.is_empty()` as `UnresolvableZoneReference` (keep the
`== "any"` short-circuit for the genuine wildcard).

**Dedup:** #485/#486 cover the mixed `any`+concrete collapse (the `any` TOKEN);
the EMPTY-element arm is distinct. Novel.

## #6465 — userspace-dp: junos-host policy gate lacks the #4569 fragment-association deny override — host-bound non-first fragment skips a port-bearing deny [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

**Severity: Low — vsrx-parity / implementation-bug.** Verifier: CONFIRMED.

The junos-host policy gate has no #4569 fragment-association deny override — a
host-bound non-first fragment skips a port-bearing `to-zone junos-host` deny and
is delivered to the local stack (the transit path has the override; junos-host
does not).

**Evidence (master):**
- `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:2972-3081` — `evaluate_junos_host_policy_l3_aware`
  walks exact/from-any/host-scoped-global tiers but never calls
  `note_skipped_frag_deny`/`apply_frag_deny_override` (those live only in
  `evaluate_policy_result_l3_aware`).
- `userspace-dp/src/policy.rs:1089-1104` — with `l4_present=false` a port-bearing
  term returns None (fail-closed for the TERM), so the deny RULE does not match.
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/flowless_verdict.rs:143-161` — the
  flowless LocalDelivery arm delivers when no junos-host rule matches.

**Trace:** `system-services all` + `from-zone untrust to-zone junos-host ...
application udp-9999 then deny`. First fragment (L4 present) → deny → dropped.
Non-first fragments → l4_present=false → term inapplicable → rule no-match →
delivered to the host stack. Bounded: the stack cannot reassemble without the
denied first fragment, so no complete datagram materializes — impact is
reassembly-queue noise on the RE + a parity divergence from the transit path.

**Severity justification:** trigger = fragmented host-bound traffic + a
port-bearing junos-host deny; Low because reassembly is blocked (the first
fragment IS denied), so no full datagram completes. Blast radius = the RE plane
(the plane the #3292 flowless gate protects) sees a fragment it should not; a
transit-vs-host asymmetry undocumented in the #4569 comments. Not higher (no
completed bypass); tracked because the asymmetry is real.

**Fix:** apply the same SkippedFragDeny note/override inside
`evaluate_junos_host_policy_l3_aware`, or document the divergence.

**Dedup:** #4569 is closed for transit; no title covers the junos-host residual.
Novel.

## #6466 — host-inbound: 'system-services all' is a literal admit-all (any proto/port) — broader than Junos; emit a commit-time advisory (documented divergence) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

**Severity: Low — vsrx-parity (documented in-code divergence).** Verifier:
CONFIRMED (Low, documented divergence).

`system-services all` is a full L3/L4 admit on the AF_XDP classifier (any
protocol, any port) — broader than Junos, which scopes `all` to the defined
service catalog. The code documents the trade-off as deliberate; filed at Low
per the honesty rule because operators porting Junos configs get a silently wider
management-plane exposure than Junos semantics imply.

**Evidence (master):**
- `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:99` — `"all" | "any-service"
  => hi.all_services = true`; `ZoneHostInbound::admits` returns true for every
  protocol/port.
- `userspace-dp/src/types/forwarding.rs:366-370` — the struct comment
  acknowledges "treating it as a full admit (slightly broader than Junos ...) is
  the safe direction". The nft mirror (`daemon_nft.go:1335-1338`) matches the
  Rust breadth (no split-brain).

**Severity justification:** trigger = an operator config that uses `all`; no
attacker. Blast radius = the firewall admits unknown/high ports (tcp/7547,
udp/161) that Junos `all` would deny — a wider management-plane surface, but
consistent across nft + Rust and explicitly documented as the "safe direction".
Low. This is a DELIBERATE divergence; the actionable residual is a commit-time
advisory so operators are not surprised.

**Fix:** classify `all`/`any-service` as the union of KNOWN service tokens, OR
(preferred, minimal) emit a commit-time advisory that xpf's `all` is a literal
admit-all.

**Dedup:** in-code deliberate divergence; no dedup title. Tracked for the
advisory.

## #6467 — routing: next-table 100-rule cap is Warn-only (no aggregated error) and diverges kernel from dataplane — leak #101+ mirrors uncapped in the userspace FIB [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

**Severity: Low — observability-lie / kernel-dataplane divergence.** Verifier:
CONFIRMED.

The next-table ip-rule 100-rule cap silently truncates the leak set (Warn-only,
no aggregated error) AND diverges the kernel from the dataplane — the userspace
FIB mirrors ALL configured next-table leaks uncapped.

**Evidence (master):**
- `pkg/routing/rules.go:147-151` — `if prio >= nextTableRulePriority+100 {
  slog.Warn(...); break }` — NO `errs = append(...)`, unlike the rib-group cap
  (:358-365) and the PBR cap (:611-614) which both aggregate a degraded error.
- `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:230-289` — the dataplane FIB captures
  next-table leaks from CONFIG static routes (uncapped) AND the kernel ip-rule
  dump (capped at 100), so leak #101+ exists in the userspace FIB but not the
  kernel.

**Trace:** a config with 150 global `next-table` routes commits SUCCESSFULLY
(warning only). Kernel: only the first 100 ip-rules exist → a slow-path (XDP_PASS
/ IPsec-reinjected / non-native-XDP fabric) packet matching leak #101+ resolves
in the main table (misrouted/dropped). Dataplane: the same packet on the AF_XDP
fast path resolves via userspace-FIB next-table recursion into the target VRF.
Two engines, two verdicts for the same flow — and apply reports success.

**Severity justification:** trigger = >100 next-table routes (a large-scale
config, no attacker). Blast radius = silent partial enforcement of a
security-relevant routing control (inter-VRF isolation) + a kernel/dataplane
verdict split on the slow path. Low because it needs >100 leaks and the fast path
still enforces zone policy; tracked because it is a silent apply-success with a
degraded result the sibling caps correctly surface.

**Fix:** aggregate an error on cap breach (mirror the rib-group/PBR caps) so the
commit surfaces degraded; align the dataplane mirror with the same cap (or raise
the window) so both engines agree; document the limit.

**Dedup:** the cap-breach no-error path is not in the corpus; adjacent
#3731-class del-error handling is already fixed. Novel.

## #6468 — cli: DHCP lease hostname printed raw to the operator terminal — client-controlled OSC/CSI escape injection via 'show dhcp server leases' [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

**Severity: Low — terminal injection / observability.** Verifier: CONFIRMED.

A DHCP lease hostname is printed raw into the operator terminal —
client-controlled escape sequences (OSC 52 clipboard write, OSC 8 hyperlinks,
CSI redraw) via `show dhcp server leases`.

**Evidence (master):**
- `pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:682` — `Hostname: field(fields, "hostname")`
  taken verbatim from the Kea lease CSV (Kea CSV-quotes commas/quotes, not
  ESC/control bytes).
- `pkg/cli/show_services_dhcp.go:283-311` — `fmt.Printf("... %-20s ...",
  l.Hostname, ...)` with NO sanitization.
- No display-side control-character filter exists anywhere in pkg/cli (grep for
  sanitizeForDisplay/stripControlChars is empty).

**Trace:** a device on a Kea-served segment sends host-name option (12) =
`evil\x1b]52;c;<base64>\x07` (or CSI erase/redraw). Kea records it (opaque string,
RFC 2132 has no charset restriction). The operator runs `show dhcp server leases`
→ the raw bytes hit their terminal: OSC 52 sets the clipboard to attacker
content, CSI hides a rogue lease or fabricates a fake "commit complete" line.

**Severity justification:** trigger = a DHCP client on a served segment
(unauthenticated network position) + an operator viewing leases; no code
execution. Blast radius = clipboard hijack + terminal output spoofing in the
management session — Low, but a real injection from an untrusted network position
into the operator's terminal. The JSON/gRPC surfaces are safe (only the terminal
renderer is affected).

**Fix:** sanitize at the display boundary (map C0/C1/DEL to `?` or
backslash-escape) in the CLI table renderer, not in the stored lease; apply the
same to other device-originated strings printed raw (DHCP client-id, DDNS
hostnames, neighbor hostnames).

**Dedup:** no hostname/terminal/escape title in the corpus. Novel.

_Found by kimi-review-002 deep security audit (base ed6999000, wave-1 hunter + independent wave-2 verifier re-trace). Verified present on master a1b56c9f7; cited files unchanged since base._

## #6469 — ipsec: swanctl remote_addrs/local_addrs interpolated without sanitizeSwanctlValue — render-belt injection gap on validation-bypassed paths [CLOSED] (closed 2026-07-24)

**Severity: Low — config-injection (latent) / hardening.** Verifier: CONFIRMED.

swanctl `remote_addrs`/`local_addrs` are interpolated without
`sanitizeSwanctlValue` — the render-time injection belt covers names/ids/PSKs but
not the endpoint addresses.

**Evidence (master):**
- `pkg/ipsec/policy.go:149-154` — `fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    local_addrs = %s\n",
  localAddr)` / `remote_addrs = %s` — raw interpolation; compare `id = "%s"`
  (:190/198) which gets `escapeSwanctlQuoted(sanitizeSwanctlValue(...))`.
- `resolveRemoteAddr` (`policy.go:347-386`) takes `gw.Address`/
  `gw.DynamicHostname` VERBATIM for the Gateways-map shape (:354-357); only the
  legacy inline shape re-checks `config.IsUsableIPsecEndpoint`.
- The render belt's own rationale (:65-72) says it is "the by-construction
  backstop for any path that reaches render without passing local commit (HA
  peer-sync, direct IPsecConfig construction, a config persisted before the fix)"
  — but it is applied to names/ids/secrets, not the address fields.
- `pkg/config/lexer.go:296-325` `readString` admits raw control chars in quoted
  strings, so a hostile value is representable on a validation-bypassed path.

**Trace:** on a path that reaches `renderConfig` without the strict commit
validators (the file's own documented cases), a gateway whose address is
`1.2.3.4\n    version = 1\n    aggressive = yes\n    #` lands verbatim in
`/etc/swanctl/conf.d/xpf.conf`, injecting strongSwan connection keys (downgrade
IKE version, flip `aggressive`, add `also`/`children`).

**Severity justification:** trigger = a validation-bypassed path (HA peer-sync of
a pre-fix config, or direct construction) — the strict gate `isPlausibleHostname`
rejects control chars on every normal commit, so Low. Blast radius = attacker-
shaped strongSwan crypto params for the VPN — high value, but bounded to the
documented render-belt threat model (the belt exists precisely because the commit
gate cannot be trusted on these paths). The address fields are the highest-value
target left unbelted.

**Fix:** run `sanitizeSwanctlValue` over `localAddr`/`remoteAddr` at the two
Fprintf sites (and reject-with-skip when sanitization changed the value,
mirroring the existing skip classes). `vpn.LocalAddr` has the same shape.

**Dedup:** #1798 (sanitizeSwanctlValue) + #2126 (quoting) fixed adjacent fields;
the address-field gap is distinct. Novel.
