## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified `session_id: 0` at both synthesis sites (master grep). `upsert_synced_with_origin` mints `alloc_session_id()` when `wire_session_id == 0` (master install.rs ~:971: `if wire_session_id != 0 { wire } else { alloc }`), and alloc ids are worker-namespaced, so each worker's reverse companion gets a different id. `DeletePolicyBatch` captures `expected_companion_rt_flow_session_id` from the listing worker and conditionally deletes by that id — mismatching on W−1 workers, leaving the companion (and its conntrack republication via repair) alive. Single-worker tests cannot see this, matching the packet's blast-radius note. - Strongest refutation/alternative: If `ListSessionsByPolicy` deduplicates and the delete fan-out re-resolves ids per worker, divergence could be healed — but the conditional-delete-by-captured-id code (`session_domain.rs:633-660`, `companion_session_id: m.expected_...`) shows the captured id is used as-is. No healing site found. - Gate: MATERIAL. - Decisive check: 2-worker synthesis→DeletePolicyBatch test asserting companion removal on both.
- Spark: Verified verbatim at both revs: `reverse_synth.rs:271` and `:527` hardcode `session_id: 0` in the synthesized `SyncedSessionEntry`. Per the claim's trace into `session/install.rs` (`upsert_synced_with_origin` mints a worker-namespaced ID when given 0), each worker that synthesizes the companion therefore holds a *different* ID for the same reverse session, and ID-checked revocation (`DeletePolicyBatch` / delete-synced guards) refuses on all but the originating worker, whose `repair_policy_bares` then republishes the revoked entry to the BPF conntrack map. The forward entry carrying a real ID makes the asymmetry unambiguous — there is no deterministic companion-ID derivation anywhere in either construction site.

## Summary
`handle_upsert_synced` Evaluates `allow_replace_local` Before Re-Resolving `owner_rg_id`, Short-Circuits Cached `LocalDelivery` Across Nodes, and Leaks Replaced Pool/NAT64 Port Reservations

Finding `D4-05` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified verbatim at master: `let allow_replace_local = synced_entry_allows_local_replace(ha_state, entry.metadata.owner_rg_id, ...)` and `is_active` are computed *before* the re-resolve block that later does `if new_owner > 0 { entry.metadata.owner_rg_id = new_owner; }` — so the replace/active decision uses the peer's stale `owner_rg_id` (incl. the #9714 `owner_rg_id==0` case). It also calls the cached `lookup_forwarding_resolution_for_session` though a `..._without_cache` variant exists for exactly this distrust. - Spark: In `handle_upsert_synced` the replace/activeness decision (`allow_replace_local`, `is_active`) is computed from the *peer's* stamped decision before the local re-resolution that yields the local `owner_rg_id` — so the guard is evaluated against the wrong node's ownership. The resolution helpers in `session_glue/resolution.rs` then trust cached `LocalDelivery`/neighbor-fallback resolutions, which on a receiving node can carry a foreign `local_ifindex`, delivering transit traffic into the wrong node's host stack. Both are order-of-evaluation defects visible in the control flow, at both revs.

## Summary
Deterministic NAPT64 (`allocate_deterministic_v6_at`) Omits Expired-BIB Garbage Collection and Activation-Rollback Bookkeeping, Enabling Permanent Per-Subscriber Port-Block Exhaustion and HA Standby BIB Destruction

Finding `D5-01` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: In `allocate_deterministic_v6_at` the only expired-lease handling is for the *candidate's own* `bib_key` (`persistent_by_source.get(&bib_key).filter(expired)`); when `claim_in_block` returns None there is no `gc_expired_for_addr_locked` sweep of the subscriber's block (that helper is called on other paths, e.g. :3237), so a block full of expired idle BIBs still reports exhaustion. The minted lease sets `activation_had_previous_lease: false` (master :4460 in the deterministic ctor) without the `0→1` promotion bookkeeping other paths set (:3423, :5002), so `rollback_flow`'s `activation_had_previous_lease` branch treats a promoted/imported BIB as fresh and removes it. - Strongest refutation/alternative: Expired BIBs for the *same* src_port are reclaimed inline, so a subscriber reusing one port is fine; exhaustion needs `block_size` distinct ports — but that is ordinary browsing behaviour over 300s, as claimed. Whether pressure-GC elsewhere eventually sweeps the block depends on unrelated allocation pressure; no deterministic-path sweep was found. - Gate: MATERIAL. Memory-cap sub-leg (max_tracked bypass on reuse branch) plausible from the branch structure but secondary. - Decisive check: claim's fill-expire-allocate allocator test + rollback-preserves-BIB test.
- Spark: In `allocate_deterministic_v6_at`, the block claim (`occupancy[ip_idx].claim_in_block`, allocator.rs:4303 at both revs) has no preceding `gc_expired_for_addr_locked` sweep — the only GC call sites are in the sibling PAT path — and the claim-failure branch consults only the *new flow's own* `persistent_by_source` key. Once a subscriber's block is fully occupied by expired idle BIB leases under *other* source ports, every new allocation fails `AllocatorExhausted` with no in-path reclamation, indefinitely (until unrelated pressure GC happens to run). The secondary legs (bitmap claimed before BIB-existence check; `max_tracked_flows` skipped on the full-block reuse branch; missing `0->1` activation-rollback bookkeeping that `rollback_flow`/`release_flow` expect) are consistent with the #14091 retrofit having bolted persistent-lease storage onto a path that never got the PAT path's lifecycle machinery.

## Summary
Same-Allocator Address-Only Source-NAT Admission Ignores `persistent_address_only_owner_counts`, Allowing Duplicate `(translated_ip, port)` Leases That Blackhole Inbound Persistent-NAT Traffic for Both Subscribers

Finding `D5-02` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Bounded check of the three reserve functions shows they consult `address_only_owners` (live) but not `persistent_address_only_owner_counts` / `address_only_owns_wire_identity` in their admission heads, while PAT/deterministic/idle-import paths do call `address_only_owns_wire_identity` (:3049, :3253, :4436...). After H1's flow releases, the live owner is gone but the idle PersistentLease + owner counts remain for 300s, so H2 with the same src port admits the same `(translated_ip, port)`; `persistent_inbound_lookup` then sees two permitted source keys for one wire identity and returns Denied for both. - Strongest refutation/alternative: The scan window (first ~4000 chars per fn) could miss a later guard, and pool rotation in roundrobin may usually pick a different IP, making collision probabilistic on multi-IP pools (deterministic on single-IP / same-start pools). - Spark: The contention state exists and is used inconsistently: `persistent_address_only_owner_counts` (allocator.rs:1002) with `address_only_owns_wire_identity` is consulted by the PAT allocation path, the deterministic path, peer-pool contention, and idle-lease import — but the three same-allocator address-only admission functions (`reserve_address_only_persistent`, `reserve_address_only_roundrobin`, `reserve_address_only_maybe_persistent`) admit on live `address_only_owners`/`pat_owns_wire_identity` alone. An idle/expired-but-counted owner therefore does not block a second subscriber from being minted the same `(translated_ip, port)` wire identity, and `persistent_by_translated` then holds two source keys for one identity, which inbound persistent-NAT lookup treats as contended (`Denied`) for both.

The scanner must also interleave a decoy before every batch that would reach 10, within one detection window. - Gate: File the sampler defect (static prefix + lowest-count victim over an unseeded set); do not file the unbounded-evasion framing until the decisive Rust test passes. - Decisive check: as in table. Finding `D6-04` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified asymmetry within one file. `export_idle_persistent_leases` *does* iterate `forwarding.nat64.prefixes` (naming them `nat64-deterministic-{idx}`, tagging `deterministic`/`V6(params)`) and the import path handles that prefix — so HA idle sync covers NAT64. But `export_display_persistent_leases` and `clear_persistent_nat_leases` iterate only `forwarding.source_nat_rules` (`pool_mode`, dedup by pool name). No NAT64 prefix loop exists in either. Therefore `clear security nat source persistent-nat-table` never calls `prefix.port_allocator.clear_persistent_leases(now_ns)` — the call that (per `allocator.rs:2221ff`) revokes leases and stamps the `last_persistent_nat_clear_ns` replay fence — so revoked NAT64 leases stay live, are invisible to `show`, and an older HA re-import is not clear-fenced for NAT64 allocators. - Strongest refutation/alternative: None found for the omission; the only correction is framing: the report index's "export" wording is wrong — idle *export/import* handle NAT64, only clear/display omit it. A daemon restart would clear state, but that is not a defence of an explicit revoke verb violating its own doc ("Revoke every persistent source-NAT lease owned by the current forwarding snapshot"). - Gate: MATERIAL (clear + display + fence legs). - Decisive check: as in table.
- Spark: Verified asymmetry in one file: `export_idle_persistent_leases` DOES iterate `nat64.prefixes` with `nat64-deterministic-{idx}` and import handles that prefix (so HA sync leg is covered), while `export_display_persistent_leases` and `clear_persistent_nat_leases` iterate only `forwarding.source_nat_rules` pool_mode — no nat64 prefix loop. So `clear security nat source persistent-nat-table` cannot revoke deterministic NAT64 leases and show-table omits them; cleared-then-reimport fence (clear generation) also bypassed for NAT64 allocators.

## Summary
`stop_workers` invokes `Coordinator::stop()` (`stop_inner(true)`), wiping all synced HA sessions, persistent NAT allocator state, and the tunnel-owner remap baseline before `rebind` runs on RETH MAC link cycles

Finding `D6-05` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified end-to-end. `stop_workers::handle` (the `PrepareLinkCycle` verb) calls `guard.afxdp.stop()` → `stop_inner(true)`. `stop_inner` defaults `self.forwarding` and `self.validation` unconditionally, and `if clear_synced_state` (mod.rs:1197-1211) clears `sessions.nat`, `sessions.forward_wire`, and — via `SharedSessionOwnerRgIndexes::clear(&sessions.synced)` at `types/mod.rs:256-275`, which locks and `sessions.clear()`s the primary synced map itself — every HA-synced session. That destroys: the synced map `rebind`'s `replay_preserved_sessions` is supposed to replay, the `PortAllocator` instances holding persistent-NAT leases (previous-forwarding migration in the later `reconcile` then sees an empty baseline), and the `tunnel_owners` baseline for the remap purge. The `rebind.rs` comment states these exact side effects are "wrong for a rebind" and asserts the link-cycle path is unaffected because Go sends a separate `stop_workers` — which is precisely the call that performs the wipe. Go side confirmed: `PrepareLinkCycle`/`NotifyLinkCycle` are the RETH MAC link-cycle hooks in `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_dataplane.go`. - Strongest refutation/alternative: One could argue a full stop is *supposed* to wipe and the HA peer will re-sync afterwards. But `rebind`'s documented contract is replay-from-memory, a standby node may have no peer to re-sync from (or only at bulk-export cost), and persistent-NAT leases are local allocator state no peer holds in identical form. No preservation snapshot is taken in `stop_workers` before `stop()`. - Gate: MATERIAL. Fix shape (preserve synced/forwar
- Spark: `stop_workers.handle` calls `guard.afxdp.stop()` with comment “Used by PrepareLinkCycle… subsequent rebind recreates workers”. `Coordinator::stop → stop_inner(true)` (mod.rs:772/1016) and at 1251 `if clear_synced_state { …clear(&self.sessions.synced) }`. `rebind.rs:18-36` comment explicitly documents stop_inner(true)'s side effects as “wrong for a rebind: wiping in-memory synced session map (should be replayed), defaulting forwarding/validation, blinding tunnel-owner remap purge” — and Go sends separate stop_workers before link cycle, so rebind's avoidance does not save the stop_workers leg. Persistent NAT/tunnel baseline wipe follows same stop_inner path per claim.

## Summary
`SocketReinjectSubmitter.DrainReinjectCompletions` Destroys In-Flight Completions by Closing `s.complete` on Idle 5ms Read Deadlines while `CapturePipeline` Unboundedly Buffers Per-Flow Frames

Finding `D8-02` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified verbatim. `DrainReinjectCompletions` sets a 5ms read deadline (`s.timeout=5ms`, :135) and on *any* `isTimeout(err)` — including 0-byte idle — does `Close(); s.complete=nil; return nil,nil`. My probe (unix socketpair, audit tree): two consecutive idle drains both return `(nil,nil)` with `s.complete==nil` after each, confirming close-on-idle (not in packet). Rust `serve_complete_conn_with_target` does `write_all(&response)` then `core.ack_ready(&ids)` with only a 100ms write timeout, and on write error `release_ready`+break — i.e. Rust commits removal on socket-buffer write, not on Go application ack. So a completion written in the window [Go deadline expiry, Go `Close()`] is acked in Rust and destroyed unread in Go; the Go `pendingReinject` then expires in `Poll` (`pipeline.go:1116-1145`) → `p.uncertain("ack timeout")` → fail-closed quarantine. Mid-frame arm also real: `readReinjectMessage` returns timeout after partial `io.ReadFull`, same close+`nil,nil`, so `Poll` never calls `failPending("completion drain error")`. Unbounded queue arm verified: `enqueueFlowLocked` (pipeline.go:640-657) appends unconditionally and `return nil` always, despite `consumeFrames` expecting drop-returns (`drops = append(drops, p.enqueueFlowLocked(frame)...)`); `p.flows` map and per-flow slices have no cap while `handoff` is capped at 16384 and `Enqueue` is try-or-drop — so memory growth is bounded only by Drain rate vs pending-head stall (`ackDeadline` default 5ms, but follower frames behind a pending head accumulate until retire). - Strongest refutation / alternative: (1) The race wind
- Spark: Verified identical both revs. `DrainReinjectCompletions` (`reinject_socket.go:224-237`): 5ms deadline (`:135` default), on *any* timeout — including 0-byte idle — closes `s.complete` and returns `nil,nil` (silently, unlike non-timeout errors which `Poll:pipeline.go:1096-1098` turns into `failPending`). Comment at `:228-230` admits partial consumption is possible, so close-on-timeout is stream-safety, but it is applied indiscriminately. Rust side (`reinject_9506.rs:266-285`): `peek_ready → write_all → ack_ready` — ack is on socket-buffer write, not Go read. So a completion written after Go's deadline expiry but before `Close()` executes is acked/purged in Rust and destroyed unread in Go; pending entry then hits `ack timeout → uncertain` (`pipeline.go:1116-1126`). Mid-frame partial timeout is additionally misreported as `nil,nil` instead of drain error. Mechanism is real and in code.

## Summary
RBAC Command Authorization Bypass via Cross-Form Longest-Match Maximization and Argument/Pipe Keyword Smuggling

Finding `D10-01` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Exactly as claimed and reproduced. `EvaluateForms` takes an independent global max per side over three projections of different lengths (matched = command+pipe, command, prefix). An end-anchored deny (`^show version$`) is capped at the short form's length while a wildcard allow (`^show.*`) grows with the piped form, flipping tier 2 to allow. Separately, `longestMatchLen` matches anywhere, so an unanchored allow phrase placed inside user-controlled pipe filter text (`| except show interfaces`) satisfies the allowlist for a command (`show configuration`) that never matched it. Both are complete RBAC bypasses for the affected (plausible, Junos-idiomatic) class shapes. - Strongest refutation / alternative: Requires the class to combine a wildcard allow with end-anchored denies, or to use an unanchored allow phrase — a class with only anchored allow+deny, or deny-only, is unaffected. Junos longest-match tier-2 semantics are upstream-documented, so part of the behavior is parity; but Junos does not measure the allow side against pipe-filter text the operator appends, and the in-code rationale (#9022/#9628) only considered narrow literal exceptions (`^show log 100$`), not wildcard allows. Parity does not cover the smuggling arm at all. - Decisive unresolved check: regression test asserting piped/arg-suffixed forms of an anchored-deny command stay denied (packet's `TestEvaluateFormsPipeAndArgDoNotDefeatAnchoredDeny` shape), run against a fix that keeps the documented `^show log 100$` exception working.
- Spark: Behaviourally confirmed on master (clean tree): `EvaluateForms("show version | match .","show version","show version")` with allow `^show.*`/deny `(^show version$)|(^show log$)` → **ALLOWED**; unanchored allow `show interfaces` + `show configuration | except show interfaces` → **ALLOWED**. Mechanism exactly as claimed: `EvaluateForms:292-365` pools matched/command/prefix into one max per side (`login_regex.go:185-209,292-407`), caller passes pipe-bearing `matched` (`permissions_regex.go:165-181`). Pipes/args inflate only the allow side vs `$`-anchored denies. This also moots the deliberate #9628 comment at `permissions_regex.go:178-180` ("pipe-less command is measured as well") — measuring more forms widens allow too.

## Summary

- Opus: After a dynamic value is consumed, `current` still points at the node's Children, so mutually-exclusive siblings (`terse`, `queue`, `name`) resolve after a positional value; handlers then ignore the extra tokens (`showInterfaces` checks `args[0]` for subcommands and last-token `detail`/`extensive`, otherwise `filterName=args[0]`) — judged string ≠ executed command again. - Spark: Both revs: `compileSystemArchival` (`compiler_system.go:547-566`) and `scpArchiveTransfer:199-237` check only `URLHasPassword` + leading `-`; no remote-target validation, no `--`. `dest="/etc/cron.d/x"` has no colon-before-slash → OpenSSH scp local-copies the root-written unredacted `ShowActive()` temp file (`archiveToSitesNow:116-156`) onto it. ## #14692 — [gemini-hostile D11-02] Unvalidated security ssh-known-hosts Rendering in applySSHKnownHosts Enables OpenSSH @cert-au… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
Unvalidated `security ssh-known-hosts` Rendering in `applySSHKnownHosts` Enables OpenSSH `@cert-authority *` / Wildcard Trust Poisoning and Newline File Injection into `/etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts`

Finding `D11-02` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: `applySSHKnownHosts` renders `fmt.Fprintf("%s %s %s\n", host, sshType, key.Key)` with no validation of any field: `host` is the raw map key, `sshType` defaults to the raw `key.Type` for anything outside the five mapped Junos spellings, and `key.Key` is unvalidated. The compiler copies name/type/first-token verbatim and the schema node is `closedWorldOpaque` with no `keyValidator`. So `host = "@cert-authority *"` or `host = "*"` renders a line OpenSSH honors for *every* host — directly defeating #10298's `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` + `UserKnownHostsFile` design for `scpArchiveTransfer`, whose payload is the unredacted active config. The reachability precondition is also plausible as an RBAC-crossing: `security` config permission is a lesser grant than `system`/super-user, yet it controls trust used by a `system archival` (system-permission) feature. - Strongest refutation / alternative: The newline/multi-line *injection* arm is much weaker: Junos-style config values come from tokenized stanzas (`nodeVal(kp)` = first token), so embedding `\n` or spaces via normal CLI/commit is not obviously reachable — it needs a lenient DB/peer-synced load or quoted-string path the packet asserts but does not demonstrate. The wildcard/CA arm needs no injection at all (single tokens `@cert-authority`, `*` are exactly what the config grammar accepts as a host name), so the claim stands on that arm alone. Also note OpenSSH still requires the attacker to present a key *certified by / equal to* the injected entry and to be on-path for the archive host — MITM positioning is required, as with any k
- Spark: `applySSHKnownHosts:1004-1053` renders `fmt.Fprintf("%s %s %s\n", host, sshType, key.Key)` raw; unknown types fall through verbatim; compiler (`compiler_security.go:71-81` — note: append/merge code, zero validation) and `closedWorldOpaque` schema (`schema_security.go:1559-1561`) validate nothing. Host `@cert-authority *` or `*`, or newline in any field, writes attacker lines into root `/etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts` (0644), which `scpArchiveTransfer` trusts with `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` — defeating #10298 and enabling MITM capture of unredacted archival config. `security`-only RBAC suffices to author `security ssh-known-hosts`.

Update path: new drop-in is written, `sshd -t` passes, reload fails transiently → `noteSSHDReloadResult(err)` latches `sshdReload=true` **and** `revertDropIn("reload-failed")` restores the prior (permissive) bytes (or deletes the drop-in). The #6800 comment claims this path "has its own retry owner" because the file now differs from desired — but the only background retry owner, `reassertServiceReloadDebtOnce`, does **not** re-render: it validates and reloads whatever is on disk (the reverted file) and on success calls `noteSSHDReloadResult(nil)`, clearing the debt and logging "sshd reload re-asserted". Net effect after one transient failure during a hardening commit (`root-login allow`→`deny`, ciphers/MACs, limits): commit reports success, disk + running sshd both enforce the old permissive policy indefinitely, telemetry shows no owed reload. But the debt-clearing reassert is the indefensible part: it 
- Spark: Verified control flow both revs: reload failure → `noteSSHDReloadResult(err)` latches debt (`:1129`) AND `revertDropIn("reload-failed")` restores permissive prior (`:1133`); `reassertServiceReloadDebtOnce:358-383` then validates+reloads the *on-disk reverted* file and clears debt (`noteSSHDReloadResult(nil):380`) without ever re-driving `applySSHConfig(ActiveConfig)`; plus `applySSHConfig:1040-1042` early-return lacks `!sshdReloadOwed()` (removal branch at `:1007` has it — asymmetry is in-tree evidence of oversight). Net: hardening commit permanently reverts + falsely reports convergence.

- Spark: `deprovisionLoginUser` reads `ownsAccount:715`, uses it only in nothing-owned return (`:730`), never `usermod`/`userdel` (grep of full body), then `forgetProvenance:891` wipes markers. xpf-created `super-user` (`useradd -m -s /bin/bash`, `:271-297`) deleted from config keeps interactive shell + account, and zeroize loses the registry entry.

## Summary

Finding `D14-03` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Order verified: `srcIsConfiguredPeer` → `UnmarshalHeartbeat` → ClusterID → `NodeID==own → NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat(); continue` (:1763) → only then `admitFrame` HMAC (:1768). `NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat`, `warnDuplicateNodeIDLocked` and the authenticated `NoteDuplicateNodeIDBeacon` all consume the *same* `duplicateNodeIDWarningDueLocked` 30 s limiter and write `EventRG` history. So a frame that never passes HMAC can (i) forge a "duplicate node-id: invalid cluster configuration" history/syslog event and (ii) keep the limiter fresh, suppressing the richer authenticated beacon diagnostic (iface/boot-id/src-mac). Packet's fix direction (verify HMAC against accepted ring for same-NodeID frames, still `continue` before replay-state admission) is correct and safe. - Strongest refutation/alternative: Packet overstates the actor: "any unauthenticated sender with spoofed source IP to UDP/4784" ignores the #6888 peer pin at :1730 — off-peer-IP datagrams are dropped *before* unmarshal. Exploitation therefore requires source-IP spoofing of the configured peer on the control link (or a compromised/misconfigured peer), i.e. an on-link attacker able to spoof the peer address — still unauthenticated w.r.t. the PSK, but a narrower boundary than claimed. History pollution is also rate-limited to 1/30 s (≤100-entry ring churn is slow). No election/liveness state is mutated (frame is discarded), so impact is alarm-suppression/forged-history, not split-brain. - Decisive check: receiver test feeding an unsigned same-NodeID frame *from the peer IP* on a keyed manager: assert no history recor
- Spark: Verified line-exact at both revs. `heartbeat.go:1735` unmarshals (header only), `:1746` checks cluster ID, `:1763-1766` calls `NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat()` and drops the frame — **before** `admitFrame` (`:1768`) runs HMAC verification (`:1815-1853`). The source pin (`:1730`, #6888) checks source IP only and its own comment states "This is NOT an authentication boundary". `NoteDuplicateNodeIDHeartbeat` (`election.go:441-458`) consumes the shared 30s limiter `duplicateNodeIDWarningDueLocked` (`:395-402`), logs at Error, and records a forged `EventRG` history entry. The same limiter gates the authenticated beacon path `NoteDuplicateNodeIDBeacon` (`dupaddr_watch_10745.go:580-585`) and `warnDuplicateNodeIDLocked` (`election.go:414-417`), so one spoofed datagram per 30s from the peer's IP (or any source if `peerAddr` is nil — `srcIsConfiguredPeer:1600-1608` fails open) perpetually suppresses genuine duplicate-identity alarms including their forensic `iface` detail.

## #14706 — [gemini-hostile D14-05] VRRP recordMasterAdvert Unconditionally Overwrites Master Priority, Source IP, and Master_Adv… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
VRRP `recordMasterAdvert` Unconditionally Overwrites Master Priority, Source IP, and `Master_Adver_Interval` on Rejected Lower-Priority Advertisements

Finding `D14-05` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified: `handleBackupRx`/`handleMasterRx` call `warnUnknownMasterAdvert` then `recordMasterAdvert` *before* any priority comparison, and `recordMasterAdvert` unconditionally sets `lastMasterPriority`, `lastMasterSeen`, per-family source (with a priority-255 carve-out), and `masterAdverInterval` (floored, not capped). Those fields feed `shouldPreemptObservedMaster` (`effective > lastMasterPriority`, staleness from `masterAdverInterval`) and the #10719 detector's known-source. A lower-priority advert therefore (a) lowers the bar the #2082 sync-hold gate compares against — a BACKUP that should not preempt a higher master can pass `effective > lastMasterPriority` after a low advert overwrites it — and (b) refreshes `lastMasterSeen`, keeping a bogus master "live". VRRP (RFC 5798) has no authentication, so any L2 speaker can send such adverts; that is the protocol's trust model, but the *local* gate must only learn from the advert it actually accepted as master. - Strongest refutation/alternative: Packet's three arms are not equal. (i) Preempt-gate arm: real, but requires sync-hold release/`preemptNowCh` or hold-expiry racing the bogus advert; ordinary Backup handling already ignores lower adverts for timer purposes. (ii) Spoof-detector arm is partly self-defeating: `warnUnknownMasterAdvert` runs *before* recording and only warns on priority 0/255; overwriting the known source with an ordinary lower-priority source is arguably correct learning (that sender *is* advertising as master). (iii) Interval arm is weakest: RFC 5798 §6.4.2 *requires* a Backup to learn Master_Adver_Inter
- Spark: Verified at both revs: `handleBackupRx:152-153` and `handleMasterRx:205-206` call `warnUnknownMasterAdvert` then `recordMasterAdvert` **before** any priority/state decision, and `recordMasterAdvert` (`:24-71`) unconditionally overwrites `lastMasterPriority`, `lastMasterSeen`, per-family master source IP (any priority 1–254), and `masterAdverInterval` (floor-clamped only, no ceiling — wire max 4095×10ms = 40.95s). All three claimed arms trace: (1) `shouldPreemptObservedMaster` (`instance_preempt.go:95-148`) returns `effective > lastMasterPriority` against the clobbered value — a Backup(100, preempt) that heard the real Master(200) and then one rogue Priority-50 advert will preempt on sync-hold release → dual-master. (2) `warnUnknownMasterAdvert` (`:78-122`) only fires for priority 0/255 from a source ≠ learned master; a prior rogue Priority-1 advert *becomes* the learned master (`:31-39`), so the follow-up rogue 255/0 from the same IP is silent (`:106-108`) — the #10719 detector is primed off by the very packet class it ignores. (3) `masterAdverInterval=40.95s` inflates `masterDownInterval()` to ~122.85s (Backup watchdog / preempt-hold staleness, `instance_preempt.go:175-297`) and `ResignRG`'s `3×masterDownInterval` safety timeout. RFC 5798 §6.4.2/§6.4.3 indeed forbid adopting `Master_Adver_Interval` from a discarded advert.

## Summary
`ShowConfig`, `ShowCompare`, and `ShowRollback` Bypass `allow-configuration` / `deny-configuration` Subtree Restrictions and Path/Format-Scoped `deny-commands` Rules

Finding `D15-01` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified end-to-end. Handlers take `_ context.Context` and render full (secret-redacted) active/candidate/rollback subtrees with no class filtering. `authorizeRPCConfigMutation` only adjudicates Set/Delete (via `configMutationLineFor`) and Load/Rollback; Show* return nil. `ShowConfig`/`ShowCompare`/`ShowRollback` are *not* in `configModeMethods9633`, so `authorizeRPCCommand` evaluates the bare canonical `"show configuration"` — a class with `deny-commands "^show configuration security"` or `"display set"`, or with only `deny-configuration "^security"`, still receives the `security` subtree via `Path:["security"]` (ACTIVE = PermView; candidate/compare = PermConfig via #9324/#9889 pricing). This contradicts the codebase's own stated invariant (#14144 header: subtrees `ShowConfig`/`Set` "conceal"). Redaction (#4051) masks secret *values* only; topology, zones, policies, address books and user/class names are disclosed. - Strongest refutation/alternative: `deny-configuration` is Junos-wise a *configuration-mode* (mutation/session) control; one could argue it was never a read-visibility control and `show configuration` is governed solely by `deny-commands`. That argument fails on this codebase's own terms: #14144 implements read-concealment for Complete explicitly by reference to what "ShowConfig/Set conceal", the CLI applies config regexes to `show` in config mode, and path/format-scoped `deny-commands` (`^show configuration security`) is unambiguously a read control that the canonical-command flattening defeats regardless. Severity is disclosure-to-authenticated-restricted-ope
- Spark: Verified at both revs. All three handlers discard ctx (`server_config.go:401,439,458`: `_ context.Context`) and render the requested subtree (or whole tree / candidate diff / rollback slot) with only secret *redaction* (`ShowActive*Redacted` etc.), never subtree authorization. The interceptor (`authz.go:288-298`) runs two gates, neither covers this: `authorizeRPCCommand` maps the methods to the bare literals `"show configuration"`/`"show configuration"`/`"show configuration"` (`authz_command_table.go:81-83` — note the report's transcription "show system rollback" is stale; actual is `"show configuration"`, which makes the path-scoping gap *worse*, not better), ignoring `Path` and `Format`; and `authorizeRPCConfigMutation` (`authz_config_regex_9154.go:39-52`) only adjudicates `Set`/`Delete`/`Load`/`Rollback` — for these three it returns nil. So `deny-configuration "^security"` (which demonstrably denies `Set` under security) and `deny-commands "^show configuration security"` / `"display set"` both fail to conceal anything on the read RPCs, in every format. The in-code assumption the claim cites is real: `authz_complete_14144.go:11-38` documents #14144 as fixing completion disclosure of "exactly the subtree those gates conceal from ShowConfig/Set" — ShowConfig does not, in fact, conceal it.

## #14710 — [gemini-hostile D16-02] RBAC deny-configuration Regex Bypass via Non-ASCII/Vertical-Tab Whitespace Tokenization Misma… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
RBAC `deny-configuration` Regex Bypass via Non-ASCII/Vertical-Tab Whitespace Tokenization Mismatch and Missing Plant-Class Attribution on `POST /api/v1/config/annotate`

Finding `D16-02` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Both sub-vectors verified by bounded lexer test on master: `lexConfigMutationLine9938("annotate system\u00a0login")` returns `["annotate","system"]` (TokenError truncates, login dropped) and the `\v` variant likewise, while the handler's `strings.Fields(req.Path)` (unicode-aware) splits to `["system","login"]` and annotates the denied node. Quoted arm: `lex…("annotate system \"login\"")` yields quoted=[…,true], so `configMutationPaths` strips the final token as the "comment" and adjudicates only `system`. Third arm verified in code: REST handler calls `store.AnnotateAs` (plantClass="") whereas every sibling mutation handler resolves `mutationPlantClass(r)` and master’s gRPC Set-annotate path uses `AnnotateAsPlantClass` — REST annotate loses plant-class attribution. - Strongest refutation/alternative: Impact is annotation-only: the caller can attach a comment to a denied subtree and dirty the candidate, not change configuration values; privilege-escalation framing should not be borrowed from D16-01. `AnnotateAs` still enforces session-holder ownership. But deny-configuration bypass + missing attribution on a candidate mutation is precisely what #9154/#9892 exist to prevent, and the gate/handler tokenizer mismatch is the canonical fail-open shape. Fix direction in packet (join Fields + synthetic empty quoted comment; use `AnnotateAsPlantClass`) is sound. - Decisive check: REST test — class `deny-configuration "system login"`: NBSP, VT, and `system "login"` annotate bodies must 403; normal `system login` control already 403s; success case must record plant class.
- Spark: Verified at both revs, both sub-vectors. Gate: `authorizeRESTConfigMutation` (`pkg/api/authz_config_regex_9154.go:242-260`) builds `"annotate " + strings.TrimSpace(req.Path)` with **no comment argument**, and `AuthorizeConfigMutation` lexes it with the real lexer (`lexConfigMutationLine9938`, `pkg/config/authz_config_mutation_9154.go:172-189`). (A) Unicode whitespace: for `system\u00a0login`, `readIdentifier` stops `system` at byte `0xC2` (not `isIdentChar`, `pkg/config/lexer.go:511-519`), `skipWhitespaceAndComments` skips only `' ' \t \n \r` (`:353`), so `Next()` returns `TokenError` and the gate lexer **stops** (`default: return tokens, quoted`) having seen only `[annotate, system]` — the deny on `system login` never matches. Handler: `strings.Fields` (`pkg/api/config.go:687`) splits on `unicode.IsSpace`, yielding `[system login]`, and annotates the forbidden node. Same for `\v`, `\f`, NBSP, U+2000s, U+3000. (B) Quoted leaf: `system "login"` lexes to `[annotate, system, login]` with `quoted=[F,F,T]`; `configMutationPaths`' annotate arm (`:139-152`) treats a quoted final token as the comment and adjudicates only `system`. Additionally the handler calls `s.store.AnnotateAs` (`config.go:691`) — `plantClass=""` — while every sibling mutating handler resolves `s.mutationPlantClass(r)` and calls the `*AsPlantClass` variant (`config.go:172,196,226,253,348,543`; store: `AnnotateAs`→`AnnotateAsPlantClass(sessionID,"",…)`, `store_command.go:382-388`), so the annotation is planted with superuser attribution, defeating the #9939 embedded-command recheck provenance.

So failures charge `(source, basic:<rotating>)` and the source bucket only — `(source, api-key)` is never charged, and a previously-locked `(source, api-key)` is never consulted when an Authorization header is present. Rotating dummy usernames gives the source-bucket budget (20) instead of the account budget (5) per window — 4× key-guessing — and dual-header presentation of the *valid* key bypasses an active api-key lockout outright. But no design comment justifies *never charging the api-key bucket for key evaluations*, nor bypassing an active api-key lockout; the minimal fix (reserve/cha
- Spark: Verified at both revs. `throttleIdentity` (`auth_throttle_10825.go:539-561`) picks exactly one identity, `Authorization` first (`:542`), so a dual-header request reserves/charges only e.g. `(source,"basic:dummy")` or `(source,"authorization-invalid")` — never `(source,"api-key")`. `authCheckCredential` (`pkg/api/auth.go:295-309`) then evaluates **both**: failed `Authorization` sets `authorizationFailed=true` (`:303`) and *falls through* to `X-API-Key` (`:305`). On dual failure, `complete` (`auth_throttle_10825.go:274-311`) charges the reservation's claimed bucket + source bucket; the api-key pair bucket is never created or charged. Consequences as claimed: (i) per-account api-key lockout (5 failures) is bypassed indefinitely from one source — only the 20-failure source budget (`:65,310`) applies, i.e. ~4× the intended guesses per window, rotating dummy Basic usernames to also dodge pair buckets; (ii) a source whose `(source,"api-key")` bucket *is* locked can keep testing keys — and a valid key still authenticates (`complete:303-305` even clears the verified api-key bucket on the fallback success) — by stapling any junk `Authorization` header; (iii) each attempt costs the failed-Authorization bcrypt (when Basic/Bearer-shaped) plus a full `constantTimeAPIKeyMatch` sweep over configured keys under one reservation.

(3) #14146 intentionally made unmapped routes deny for restricted classes; one could argue HEAD is just another unmapped route — but #9134's documented invariant ("sa
- Spark: At audit, `readPermissionFor` (`pkg/api/authz.go:932-936`) aliases any safe method to the `GET` entry, but `authorizeRESTCommand` (`authz_command_regex_9952.go:291`) keys `restRoutesNoCommand`/`restRouteCommand`/`restRequestCommand9952` on raw `r.Method + " " + r.URL.Path`. ## Summary

Finding `D17-05` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: (Echo arm — verified) `LoadMergeAsPlantClass`/`parseOverrideContent` return `fmt.Errorf("line %d: %q is not a set/delete/…", trimmed)` and `line %d: %q: %w` with the raw line (:610-613, :681-684; `LoadSetAsPlantClass` same pattern). A non-superuser with `PermConfig` — whose `show configuration` is redacted under #4099 — can `load merge /etc/xpf/rescue.conf` (or any readable-by-daemon file with ≥1 flat verb line to select the flat branch) and read off denied file lines one error at a time. The rescue loader in the same package deliberately scrubs exactly this (`rescueParseError`, coordinates only), proving the intended discipline. (Ordering arm — verified) `handleLoad` calls `ReadBoundedConfigFile(source)` (:204) *before* `AuthorizeConfigLoad` (:234), so even a `deny-configuration ".*"` class (and any restricted class using `override`, which the load gate refuses categorically) triggers a root-privileged open and gets distinguishable errors (not-exist vs non-regular vs empty vs parse), i.e. a filesystem existence/type oracle plus the echo channel above. - Strongest refutation / alternative: The read itself is bounded and safe against hangs (`O_NOFOLLOW`, regular-file check, 16 MiB cap, #6753) — no unbounded allocation or FIFO block. Files with no flat-verb line take the hierarchical parser whose errors are coordinate-only, so bulk exfiltration requires target files containing a `set/delete/…` line before the secret line (true of xpf config/rescue files — the realistic targets — not of e.g. `/etc/shadow`, whose lines would go hierarchical and not echo [needs the packet's bran
- Spark: (two separable parts):** 1. *Verbatim echo (MATERIAL):* `LoadMergeAsPlantClass`/`parseOverrideContent` return `line %d: %q is not a set/… command` with the raw line (`store_command.go:610-614,681-685`; same pattern in `LoadSetAsPlantClass`). `LoadRescue` deliberately scrubs this (`rescueParseError`, coordinates only). A non-superuser `PermConfig` class that is denied cleartext secrets (#4099 redaction) can therefore extract individual lines of any file it can get parsed as flat input, one error per load — a real, if slow, exfiltration oracle for files containing a valid first `set` line followed by a secret line. 2. *Pre-auth unconfined read (weaker):* `handleLoad` (`cli_config.go:200-213`) calls `ReadBoundedConfigFile(source)` before `AuthorizeConfigLoad` (:234), inside root-privileged `xpfd`, with no directory confinement. Existence/empty/non-regular distinctions leak via distinct errors even under `deny-configuration ".*"`. But "load a config file by path" is the feature's purpose, Junos `load merge <file>` inherently reads operator-named files, and `ReadBoundedConfigFile` already enforces regular-file + 16 MiB + `O_NOFOLLOW` (#6753). Confinement to a staging dir is a design/policy change, not a clear contract violation — this half is a hardening question.

## Summary

## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: Verified end-to-end. #14172's cover lives only in `DB.writeConfirmCover`, set at `store_commit.go:638` from the guarded tree and cleared by `defer` on return (:639) — the in-code comment even asserts the false premise ("cleared on return so no later tombstone/migration/retry write silently inherits it", and crypto.go:315-319 "keeps those records exactly under the PrevTree profile they were armed with"). In the #14172 scenario the record was *not* armed under the PrevTree profile (PrevTree has none); every later `WriteConfirm` — resolution tombstone (`markConfirmResolvedLocked`, :929, via `WriteConfirm→encodeConfirm` with cover `""`), phase-3 retry (`store_persist.go:1465`), boot rebind/migration (:392,438,999), FIRST sentinel (:1039,1574) — marshals the full PrevTree (all secret leaves) and, with `confirmEncryptionPRF(prevTree, "")==""`, writes it unencrypted and fsyncs it. The tombstone arm fires on *every* confirm resolution in this configuration, not an edge case; crash/delete-failure leaves it indefinitely, and even on success cleartext blocks were durably written. This directly defeats the operator's act of enabling master-password. - Strongest refutation / alternative: File is `0600` in the config DB dir alongside `master.key` — an attacker who can read `confirm.json` cleartext may be near the key material anyway [INFERENCE on deployment perms]. That mitigates remote-attacker severity but not the defect: #14172's whole purpose was at-rest encryption of this record, backups/snapshots/support-bundles routinely carry config DB files without keys, and the encrypted-then-c
- Spark: `commitConfirmedLocked` sets `s.db.writeConfirmCover = {profile: masterPasswordPRF(committedTree)}` with `defer` clearing it on return (`store_commit.go:638-639`) — the comment at :635-637 says clearing is deliberate so later writes don't "silently inherit" it. But `encodeConfirm` (`db.go:781`) computes `confirmEncryptionPRF(rec.PrevTree, db.writeConfirmCover)` = PrevTree's own PRF, else cover, else `""` = plaintext (`crypto.go:351-356`). In the exact #14172 scenario (PrevTree has *no* master-password; the guarded commit *adds* one), every subsequent `WriteConfirm` therefore writes plaintext: resolution tombstone (`markConfirmResolvedLocked`, `store_commit.go:923-933`), finalization retry (`store_persist.go:1465`), FIRST-rollback sentinel (:1039), boot-recovery/migration rewrites. The tombstone case is the cleanest: it rewrites the *same* `PrevTree` (with its secrets) unencrypted and fsyncs it.

## #14720 — [gemini-hostile D18-03] Cutover Pre-STOP Stamp and Pre-FLIP Guard Confusion Delete the Committed Rollback Target on Verify/Start Failure [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
**ID:** `D18-03`

Finding `D18-03` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. ## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: The identity confusion is real. For a fresh cut, `j.PreviousVersion = restorablePrev` = the *live* version (`cutover.go:520,605`), so `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy`'s guard `ver == j.PreviousVersion || ver == cur` (:1749) protects only the live dir — never live's committed predecessor. Re-stage predecessor `1.0.0` (running `2.0.0`) under a new generation: (a) if bytes differ, `copyStaged`'s predecessor-preservation (`committedPredecessorStamp`, commit_stamp.go:80-94) is explicitly *demoted* on mismatch — `stampInFlightVersion(ver)` + `removeStaleVersionDir` (:1543-1553) — deleting the rollback target before verify; (b) if the copy lands and verify fails, `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy` `os.RemoveAll(versions/1.0.0)` + `.<ver>.dbsnap` (:1756,1803) with no predecessor check. Either way `defaultRollbackTarget("2.0.0")` then finds `.1.0.0.committed` gone/non-committed and reports no restorable target. The packet's proof log ("replacing stale version dir … removed copied version dir … defaultRollbackTarget err") matches arms (a)+(b) chained. - Strongest refutation / alternative: Two packet arms need narrowing. (1) "Byte-identical reuse then cleanup deletes it": at audit, same-generation reuse skips the copy and *cleanup still deletes the pre-existing dir* — that sub-arm holds and is the worst form; but the generation-mismatch-as-mismatch claim (packet Cross-Domain note) is stale: current `existingVersionDirMismatch`/`mismatchedManagedBinary` compare SHA-256 of binaries, generation difference routes through the refuse/replace logic at :1483-1553, not a pure generation-string mismatch. (2) C
- Spark: When `v1` (committed predecessor of live `v2`) is re-staged under a *new* generation, `copyStaged` preserves its stamp only while `preservedPredecessorStamp != nil` and `ver == j.PreviousVersion` (`cutover.go:1471-1481`); the pre-STOP gate likewise keeps it a candidate only until the envelope recheck (:826-833). If `verify(j)` then fails, `cleanupFailedVerifyCopy` guards deletion with `ver == j.PreviousVersion || ver == cur` (:1749) — but in this journal `j.PreviousVersion == "v2"` (the *current* version, since the cut targets v1), so the guard does **not** fire for the re-staged v1 dir, and `os.RemoveAll(versionDir(ver))` (:1756) plus `.<ver>.dbsnap` removal (:1803) destroy the very directory `defaultRollbackTarget("v2")` would restore. The report's executed proof (dir gone, `defaultRollbackTarget` errors "no restorable… target") matches this path.

(2) `Run`'s resume branch (:276-297) calls `rollback(j)` and `return nil` (:296); `runRollingWith` treats nil as a successful cut and proceeds to re-sync + `RejoinAndConfirm`/`ResetFailover`, logging "cut complete" for a node that actually went *backwards* — the packet proof (err=nil, resetCalled=true, helper dead) is consistent. Those are precisely the degraded states the journal/resume machinery exists for, so the narrowing limits frequency, not validity. - Spark: Legs 1 and 3 proven by probe. ## #14731 — [gemini-hostile D20-04] Dual-Stack DDNS Manager.currentAuthorityLocked Collapses Per-Family Authority Fingerprints to… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Summary
Dual-Stack DDNS `Manager.currentAuthorityLocked` Collapses Per-Family Authority Fingerprints to Only IPv4 (`pol4.authority`), Breaking Cross-Surface Co-Ownership (`#5748`/`#6755`) for IPv6 `AAAA` Records and Deleting Live Router `AAAA` Records on DHCPv6 Lease Expiry

Finding `D20-04` from `gemini-4-argon-high-review-high-security-hostile-experts-100-001.md` (deep-review audit `0c5f646c`). Both independent re-review passes gate this claim **MATERIAL** at their checked `origin/master` revisions — opus: ; spark:  — with the narrowed scope below. Coordinator re-checked the cited anchors against current `origin/master` `09c6b9ed9f62e389081b8ecc3a9df7bce23da7c9` for filing (line numbers as cited by the re-reviewers; re-anchor before fixing).
## Narrowed material core (both passes)
- Opus: .** Confirmed on master despite refactor: `ReconcileScoped` builds `agg := pol4; if !agg.enabled { agg = pol6 }` and stores single `m.lastPolicy`; `currentAuthorityLocked()` (`manager.go:1196`) returns the one `p.authority`; both `wireRRSharedWithOther` (`:1147`) and `rebuildWireRRClaimsLocked` (`:1209`) stamp it on records of *both* families (`wireRRClaim(r.FQDN, r.ForwardType, ...)` — ForwardType derives from family, authority does not). With distinct ddns4/ddns6 RFC2136 servers, every v6 claim carries the v4 fingerprint. `coOwns` requires exact `Authority` equality — so (a) false negative: v6 lease expiry deletes a live Surface-A AAAA on the v6 server; (b) false positive: cross-server co-ownership suppresses a needed delete, orphaning the record. The code's own comment acknowledges the current-authority approximation but only argues policy-*change* boundedness, not dual-stack distinct endpoints — the exact #2663-supported config. **Strongest refutation/alternative.** Requires dual-stack DDNS with *different* UpdateServers *and* a Surface-A record colliding on (FQDN, type, rdata) with a lease record — a narrow but explicitly supported topology (#5748/#6755 machinery exists for it). If both families share one server, fingerprints coincide and there is no defect. `leaseAuthorityFingerprint` on master may already be per-config — check whether `policyFromConfig` fingerprints incorporate family endpoint correctly for single-family case (yes) — defect is only the dual-stack collapse. **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL. **Decisive unresolved check:** master test: dual-stack Reconcile wi
- Spark: `ReconcileScoped` collapses the aggregate policy to `agg := pol4` whenever v4 is enabled (audit `manager.go:833-840`; master retains pol4-first collapse), so `currentAuthorityLocked()` — the single scalar used to stamp *every* lease claim in `rebuildWireRRClaimsLocked` and to build the owned claim in `wireRRSharedWithOther` — is always the v4 endpoint fingerprint. An AAAA lease published to the distinct ddns6 server is stamped with the v4 fingerprint; Surface A's teardown compares it against the AAAA record's own `BackendFingerprint` (the v6 server) via `coOwns`, gets a mismatch, and deletes a live co-owned AAAA record (and symmetrically, lease teardown can delete a Surface-A co-owned RR). `coOwns` itself is correct — its inputs are wrong per-family.

NAT-pool alarm / clock-skew text). Still, defense-in-depth parity with the syslog sink is the project's own #6585 standard, and `Send` is
- Spark: All three legs code-verified, leg 2 probe-verified. (1) `LocalLogWriter.Send` formats `msg` raw into the audit file; its syslog twin sanitizes with `termsafe.SanitizeForDisplay` (#6585). `formatSyslogMsg` interpolates zone/reason fields raw, so `\n`/`\r`/ESC reaching it forges audit lines. ## #14831 — userspace-dp: session-miss TE arm double-queues TE + Live forward for TTL=1 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Found while implementing #14643 (witness control).

On the session-miss arm, a buildable TTL=1 TCP SYN queues BOTH a Prebuilt Time Exceeded (from build_local_time_exceeded_request at poll_descriptor/mod.rs ~5529) AND a Live forward (from build_live_forward_request_from_frame at ~8902). Descriptor harness evidence (nat_snapshot, pool SNAT, ifindex 24): scratch_forwards=[Prebuilt(target=24), Live(target=11)], dbg.forward=1, sessions=0. The Live frame is later refused at rewrite for TTL<=1, so no wire leak today, but the packet is counted as forwarded and occupies TX queue state.

Likely mechanism: the miss arm does not suppress the trailing Live-forward tail after queueing the TE (recycle_now=false is insufficient because the tail at ~8430 checks only disposition). Flow-cache sibling returns Consumed. Session-hit TE arm at ~3311 continues correctly.

Out of scope for #14643 (which fixes the suppressed-TE install). File + fix separately: after queueing TE on miss arm, skip the Live tail (e.g. continue or a consumed flag).

## #14850 — [build] origin/master userspace-xdp shim has a duplicate closing brace from #14645 [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

## Symptom

`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs` on origin/master does not parse. rustc and rustfmt both report `unexpected closing delimiter` at the end of `try_xdp_userspace`: the session-miss block introduced by #14645 (13905b0650) closes the match arm, the match, and the enclosing if, then has one extra `        }` before `    } else if native_gre_fragment {`.

## Evidence

- `git show origin/master:userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs | sed -n '1015,1022p'` shows three consecutive closes (`            }`, `        }`, `        }`) where sibling pre-#14645 code has two (closes the `_` arm and the match; the if is closed by the `else if` line).
- `rustfmt +nightly-2026-05-23 --edition 2024 --check` on the pristine HEAD file: `error: unexpected closing delimiter: } at 1162`, citing `if !native_gre && !native_gre_fragment` at 905.
- The sibling worktree at 4c6c8fb2da (pre-#14645) parses cleanly.
- The shipped `pkg/dataplane/userspace_xdp_bpfel.o` and gate verdict predate #14645, so the stranded source was never regenerated; the manifest lists the new gre sources but the object was built from the pre-#14645 source. This is why CI stayed green.

## Impact

Any PR touching the shim cannot run `make build-userspace-xdp` without first removing the duplicate brace. Found while implementing #14842 (per-VLAN ingress domains); that lane removes the duplicate line as a drive-by and calls it out in its PR body.

## Fix

Delete the extra `        }` line. Regenerate the shim object afterward; note the regenerated object will measure the true current verifier headroom, which the stale verdict (620456 insns, 2026-10-17) does not reflect.

Regenerate the object on current master to re-baseline the verdict honestly, then reduce verifier cost (the fully-unrolled IPv6 extension-header walk in parse_ipv6 is the documented largest consumer) or accept a lower floor with a recorded rationale.

## #14935 — userspace-dp: closing-state sessions frozen on fixed 30s fuse - active data flows idle-reaped mid-transfer (#14300 root cause) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Root cause of #14300 (loss cluster live repro, deployed 06f2d276f; mechanism byte-identical on master 27b8cba22d).

Mechanism: first FIN/RST sighting stamps closing=true + tcp_close_window (30s) on the pair (session lookup stamp_tcp_close/propagate_tcp_state_to_companion). Afterwards the FIN-owning direction can never refresh last_seen/expires: slow-path refresh predicate (lookup.rs) and flow-cache touch_if_stale both gate on !fin_own/!reset. Reaper (expire_stale_entries_ha, 1s wheel) removes the entry at FIN+30s regardless of traffic volume. Live evidence: iperf3 -P12 streams 17-20 Gbps stall to 0 at ~28-30s flow age; fw0 session count 13-17 -> 0; journal SESSION_CLOSE reason=idle Timeout on flows with 200k+ packets; per-worker survival (queues 1,3).

Fix shape: data-bearing segments (payload progress) must re-stamp expiry even in closing state; keep fixed fuse only for TIME_WAIT (both FINs) and RST. Regression: FIN one direction -> data at intervals past closing+30s -> both halves alive; stop data -> reap at last-data+window. Existing close_refresh_gate_10885 tests pin ACK-only frozen behavior - split ACK-only vs data-bearing.

Acceptance: loss-cluster long iperf3 (60s+, -P12, both directions, v4+v6) stable >=18 Gbps with no stream stall.

## #14937 — userspace-dp: payload-less keepalive wrappers still reachable from poll loop - closing sessions die at 20-30s on subset of workers (follow-up #14935) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Follow-up to #14935 / root of #14300. Live loss evidence on build b4464fda30 (includes #14936): iperf -P12 push decays per-stream all-or-nothing at 20-30s; dead workers go CPU-idle; sessions close idle Timeout with multi-GB counters. Diagnosis: #14935 threaded payload progress through main paths but kept payload_len=0 compatibility wrappers; a subset of hit paths (per-worker bimodal) still invokes them, so those closing entries keep the frozen #10885 fuse.

Fix: thread payload progress through every production lookup/touch call site; remove payload-less wrappers from poll loop reachability; regression per hit path (flow-cache, deferred-owner, fabric/shared, slow path). Acceptance: loss 60s+ -P12 both directions v4+v6 >=18Gbps, zero 0-byte streams, zero idle-Timeout closes on multi-GB sessions.

## #14939 — userspace-dp: established TCP sessions never promote out of handshake_pending - stuck on 20s OPENING window, reaped mid-flow (#14300 root) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Live discriminator on loss (master 8cece4238a): during iperf -P12, ALL sessions show Timeout: 20 (OPENING window) mid-flow instead of 300 (established). handshake_pending never clears for these installs, so sessions live on the 20s opening window; combined with 30s-scale reap they die mid-transfer (idle Timeout closes, all-stream stall ~30s, SYN-less packets then fail strict-syn-check - permanent stall).

Per Code30s analysis: local-install promotion requires a forward non-SYN ACK reaching lookup while handshake_pending (lookup.rs promotion arm); candidates that break it: completing ACK served by flow-cache hit (never reaches lookup), deferred-owner/Owner-replay path not applying promotion, or synced/materialized replicas (upsert_synced maps HandshakePending -> established=true, handshake_pending=true and completion depends on that worker seeing the ACK via lookup).

Fix: ensure handshake completion is applied on every hit path that can consume the completing ACK (flow-cache hit must complete promotion or not swallow the ACK; deferred owner replay likewise). Regression: install SYN/SYN-ACK, drive completing ACK via flow-cache hit path, assert Timeout becomes established window (300) and session survives past opening+closing windows under data traffic. Acceptance: loss 60s+ -P12 both directions v4+v6 >=18Gbps, sessions show Timeout:300 mid-flow, zero idle-Timeout closes.

## #14941 — userspace-dp: reverse-direction revalidation writes forward egress zone into reverse ingress - ACKs go Foreign and stall at ~28s (#14300) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

From #14300 wire diagnosis (build 1b2aab09b4): reverse ACKs silently dropped in fw0 ~28s into every TCP stream; forward data still passes; sessions idle-Timeout close.

Code defect (Rev14300): reverse metadata is direction-relative (shared_ops/reverse_synth.rs:90-91), resolver derives new_egress_zone from matched packet direction incl. reverse hits (session_glue/resolve.rs:514-553), but recipient writes it as forward egress_zone / reverse ingress_zone unconditionally (session/mod.rs:2231-2257; poll_descriptor/mod.rs:2278-2283). A reverse (WAN->LAN) revalidation can flip reverse ingress zone WAN->LAN; next ACK becomes Foreign (session_hit_authority.rs:190-206), skips refresh, cannot re-seed cache, may policy-drop. Fix orientation: when matched direction is reverse, map resolved zones direction-relatively. Regression: reverse-hit revalidation preserves reverse ingress=original forward egress zone; ACK stream keeps refreshing past 30s. Also check neighbor-generation flow-cache invalidation lead (flow_cache_hit.rs:160-196) as contributing trigger for the ~28s transition timing.

## #14943 — userspace-dp: flow-cache HA lease stamp frozen at insert (10s) - entries self-evict and demote to HAInactive mid-flow (#14300) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-18)

Code-provable (Lease14300 hunt, head d90ea9ff65): FlowCacheStamp::capture copies HAForwardingLease::ActiveUntil into owner_rg_lease_until at insert (flow_cache.rs:165,188-194,714); hits never refresh it (flow_cache.rs:1315-1331). Lease is 10s (afxdp/mod.rs:544, types/runtime.rs:523-531). Every seeded entry self-evicts <=~10s after seeding (flow_cache.rs:1286-1294) and before that the hit validator demotes cached resolution to HAInactive when the runtime lease expired (flow_cache_hit.rs:160-196, forwarding/ha.rs:248-262), failing closed to slow-path redirect/drop. try_refresh_ha_leases never resurrects an expired stored-active lease (ha/session_domain.rs:1681,1704-1716), so one lapse is permanent for the entry.

Live correlation (#14300): all flows cache-evict in a burst at session age ~26-28s, session-hit burst, then no re-seed/refresh, ACKs dropped, idle-Timeout closes. Fix direction: cache hits re-stamp owner_rg_lease_until from the CURRENT runtime lease (or validate against current lease, not insert stamp); allow lease refresh to resurrect stored-active when heartbeat is fresh again. Regression: seeded entry hit past insert+10s with fresh runtime lease stays cached/valid; expired-runtime-lease still fails closed. Acceptance: loss 60s -P12 both directions stable.

## #14945 — perf: userspace RSS queue imbalance - 2 of 6 workers idle while contended queues micro-drop (loss -P12 ceiling 16-19G) [OPEN]

Residual from #14300 (build e480baa5a4, loss). Dataplane counters show zero drops everywhere (AF_XDP, NIC, qdisc, session, cache all flat) yet fast-retransmit bursts (752-9426/60s) hit subset of streams with persistent 2x per-stream stratification. Worker CPU (60s): w0/w1/w3/w4 ~20.3s, w2/w5 ~2.4s - RSS pins 12 streams onto 4 of 6 queues; contended queues micro-lose/reorder silently (loss point uncounted). Fix direction: RSS/flow pinning balance across 6 workers, or per-queue backpressure accounting to expose the silent drop point; capture during burst via capture_iperf.sh. Target: -P12 both directions >=22G v4 / >=19G v6, retransmits near-zero, per-worker CPU balanced.

- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): pkg/config/compiler_nat_source.go:416-432 stores `rs.SourcePool` verbatim. pkg/dataplane/compiler_nat.go:1041-1046 returns `NAT64 rule-set %q: source pool %q not found`. pkg/dataplane/compiler_validate_4960.go:418 makes compileNAT64 a pre-pass row. pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:479-482 runs `validateBeforeMutateWithResult` before Phase 2 and returns the error. ### Summary
- **A05-05** — A generic vrrp-group without `preempt` compiles Preempt=false (Junos and RFC 5798 default to preempt), so a backup never takes over from a track-demoted master (report severity: Medium — a Junos-parity default that silently disables tracking-driven failover for xpf-native and imported configs. ## #15049 — vrrp: fix — An untagged-unit VRRP instance bound to a vlan-tagging parent is driven by a same-VRID election on a tagged sibling unit,… (A25-02) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **A25-02** — An untagged-unit VRRP instance bound to a vlan-tagging parent is driven by a same-VRID election on a tagged sibling unit, because the kernel strips the 802.1Q tag before the parent's ETH_P_ALL tap and the AF_PACKET path never checks VLAN metadata (report severity: Medium — HA ownership on the native segment is lost: a higher-priority master in VLAN N demotes the native MASTER and keeps resetting its master-down timer, so the native VIP can have no owner. - Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `pkg/vrrp/instance.go:719-720` the AF_PACKET receiver is used whenever it is opened. `pkg/vrrp/manager.go:1452-1600` uses ETH_P_ALL bound to the ifindex, with no PACKET_AUXDATA and no SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG_PRESENT (grep: none in pkg/vrrp). `instance_receive.go:354-371` detects tags only from in-data ethertypes; `acceptArrivalIfindex` is applied only at `:164`/`:281` (raw fallback).

### Fix direction

- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `pkg/feeds/feeds.go:463-480`: the snapshot writes `Hash: highWaterHash` with `Prefixes: epochPrefixes`. `:450-455`: the restore keeps the prefixes only if `hashPrefixes(canon) == hash` (the high-water hash). `:2273-2276`: an install with newCount >= highWater moves highWaterHash. `:2282-2291`: the epoch moves only on bootstrap or ack, so the two hashes diverge after one ordinary rotation (observed). `:2111-2125`: shrink and churn trips both require `fs.hasSnapshot`, which is false on cold boot. `:2282`: `if wasBootstrap || guardBypass` rebases the epoch to the candidate. `:2125-2127`: the warn

- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus1.md:268` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1029-1033`, `pkg/upgrade/flip.go:207-217`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1029-1033 `if isInteractive() { return signal.NotifyContext(parent, syscall.SIGTERM) }; return signal.NotifyContext(parent, syscall.SIGTERM, syscall.SIGINT)` is the only daemon signal capture. ## #15097 — userspace-dp: fix — The kernel-monitor NUD_PROBE token is minted even when the kernel is probing a MAC the dataplane just refused, so one… (A66-05) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary

- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): In `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/neighbor.rs:829-859` (v4) and `:875-900` (v6), `solicited = peek_arp_reply_solicited(&key) || NUD_PERMANENT` feeds `insert_arp_reply_if_solicited_allows`. Then `if (state & NUD_PROBE) != 0 { dynamic_neighbors.record_neighbor_probe(key, now_ns); }` runs before the `None => report_..._refusal; return` arm, whatever the event's lladdr. `sharded_neighbor.rs:313-329` keys the token by `(ifindex, ip)` only, valid for `ARP_SOLICITED_WINDOW_NS`. A repo grep for `gc_thresh`, `arp_accept`, `drop_gratuitous_arp` and `drop_unsolicited_na` finds no kernel hardening.

### Fix direction
- **A66-05:** On a refused overwrite, re-assert the dataplane's MAC into the kernel (`add_kernel_neighbor(key, G)` REPLACE, rate-limited) so the kernel probes G rather than A. A genuinely moved G then fails to FAILED and resolves fresh. Additionally, bind the NUD_PROBE token to the probed lladdr and accept only replies consistent with a probe of the MAC the dataplane holds. Acceptance: the v23 Rust cell keeps G at step 3. The #10704 positive control (PROBE G then REACHABLE G2) still converges. A netns run of the attack leaves both the kernel entry and the dataplane entry at G.

- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `userspace-dp/src/server/reinject_9506.rs:337-365` (submit thread) and `:367-395` (complete thread) both match `Err(err) if err.kind() == WouldBlock => sleep(1ms)` then `Err(_) => break`; the thread returns and the `UnixListener` moved into its closure is dropped. `server/lifecycle.rs:829-834` joins the handles only at shutdown. `server/lifecycle.rs:931-936,976-1038` (`accept_error_is_transient`, `accept_step`) is the retry logic used by the control and session loops only. ## #15115 — config: fix — The #9727 jumbo-MTU commit advisory omits the kernel's 256-byte XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM, so MTUs 3567..3822 commit silently… (A80-01) [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-19)

### Summary
- **A80-01** — The #9727 jumbo-MTU commit advisory omits the kernel's 256-byte XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM, so MTUs 3567..3822 commit silently while full-size frames are dropped (report severity: Low — the advisory that exists to prevent silent jumbo-frame loss is wrong by 256 bytes. Within that window full-size frames never reach a worker (copy mode: kernel `rx_dropped`) or the ZC bind is ref; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `A80-01` (Part v1-v28).
- Origin run: `review-work.fGP0SR92RV`; discoverer: claude-opus-5-5 (coordinator; worker detail in report section).
- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus1.md:383`.

### Decisive evidence (file:line)
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus1.md:383` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `pkg/config/userspace_rx_mtu_advisory_9727.go:23-28`, `afxdp/umem/mod.rs:59`, `afxdp/mod.rs:440-441`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `pkg/config/userspace_rx_mtu_advisory_9727.go:23-28` `userspaceRxMTUBudget = 4096 - 256 - 14 - 4` (3822). `/usr/src/linux-headers-6.18.5+deb14-common/include/net/xdp_sock_drv.h:35-48` `xsk_pool_get_headroom = XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM + pool->headroom`, `rx_frame_size = chunk - headroom` (4096 - 512 = 3584). Kernel `net/xdp/xsk.c:335-337` `if (len > xsk_pool_get_rx_frame_size(pool) && !xs->sg) { rx_dropped++; return -ENOSPC; }`. `afxdp/umem/mod.rs:59,83` headroom = `UMEM_HEADROOM` (256). Bind flags have no XDP_USE_SG (`afxdp/mod.rs:440-441`).

### Fix direction
- **A80-01:** Set `userspaceRxMTUBudget = 4096 - (256 + 256) - 14 - 4` (3566), name both headroom terms in the warning text, and add a test that derives the budget from XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM independently. Acceptance: 3567 warns, 3566 does not.

### Acceptance
- A regression test/fixture exercising the exact `A80-01` mechanism above (same path/spelling/state as claimed, surviving leg only) **fails on current `origin/master` and passes after the fix**; test-only-green coverage that does not exercise the mechanism does not close this issue.

### Dedup
- **A80-01:** Residual of #9727 (CLOSED), which introduced the advisory with this formula. Prior H06-02 assigned the over-MTU drop to #9727 without examining the budget. No issue or prior finding mentions headroom/3822.

- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `pkg/config/compiler_applications.go:351-359` @51d355c1d: `expandContainerTerm14340` builds `&Node{Keys: []string{"term", sub.Keys[0]}, Children: sub.Children}`, so `sub.Keys[1:]` is discarded before `applicationTermKeys`/`parseApplicationTerms`. ### Summary

- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): `pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go:416-427` inherits the domain only from `iface.Units[0]` of the same interface. The member `ge-0/0/1` has no units, so its base row keeps `routingDomainForInterfaceKey("ge-0/0/1")`=0, yet `snapshotLinuxName` maps reth0 and reth0.0 to `ge-0-0-1` through RethToPhysical. `maps_sync.go:1580-1619` emits an entry for every row. `localAddressRoutingDomain` sees domains {0,vrf} and returns (0,false), and the delete runs at `maps_sync.go:941-946`.

### Fix direction
- **A86-03:** Derive the base-row domain from the netdev. If any unit row of any interface (including a RETH whose RethToPhysical is this member) resolves to the same linuxName, inherit its domain, or give rows whose netdev is owned by another interface's unit no Addresses. Acceptance: the probe's RETH case yields a single domain-748221 entry and (748221,true).

- **A93-02** — With no xpf-only `tcp-session established-timeout` and no per-application inactivity-timeout, established TCP sessions idle out at 300 s instead of the Junos default 1800 s (report severity: Medium — affects every migrated Junos config. Any TCP connection idle 5–30 min (SSH without keepalives, DB/LDAP pools, idle SMB) loses its session, and its next segment is dropped by the SYN-first ses; consensus **MATERIAL** 3-way in validator research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw`).

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `A93-02` (Part v29-v63).
- Origin run: `review-work.fGP0SR92RV`; discoverer: claude-opus-5-5 (coordinator; worker detail in report section).
- Validator: research run `research-work.AdQvt1jMKw` (Codex `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol` / Opus `meta/muse-wonder-1.0` / Spark `meta/muse-wonder-1.0`, base `origin/master 27b8cba22d`); consensus MATERIAL at `synthesis-opus2.md:62`.

### Decisive evidence (file:line)
- Synthesis consensus row: `synthesis-opus2.md:62` — 3-way MATERIAL.
- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:196`, `pkg/config/flow_tcp_timeouts_6539.go:52`, `pkg/config/flow_tcp_timeouts_6539_test.go:213-218`, `pkg/dataplane/userspace/flow.go:95-97`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:196 `const DEFAULT_TCP_SESSION_TIMEOUT_NS: u64 = 300_000_000_000;` and :482-487 (`tcp_secs > 0` else that default). pkg/config/flow_tcp_timeouts_6539.go:52 `DataplaneTCPEstablishedWindowSecs = 300`; its comment at :62-68 says the CLI used to print "established-timeout's Junos default of 1800s" while "the session actually idles out at 300s". pkg/config/flow_tcp_timeouts_6539_test.go:213-218 fatals if the default ever equals 1800. pkg/dataplane/userspace/flow.go:95-97 fills TCPSessionTimeout only from the configured leaf. The constant predates the parity work: b0f

### Fix direction
- **A93-02:** Default the established window to 1800 s, which means updating the Rust constant, `DataplaneTCPEstablishedWindowSecs`, the inverted pin test and the show surface. Alternatively, document 300 s as a deliberate divergence in README and feature-gaps and emit a commit advisory when no established-timeout is configured. Acceptance: with no tcp-session stanza, an established TCP session survives 301 s idle, and the show output prints `1800s (default)`.
- Change only the cited mechanism in the anchored file(s)/symbol(s) above; fail closed (deny/drop/reject the operation) wherever the current path fails open, and preserve all neighbouring legitimate behaviour.

### Acceptance
- A regression test/fixture exercising the exact `A93-02` mechanism above (same path/spelling/state as claimed, surviving leg only) **fails on current `origin/master` and passes after the fix**; test-only-green coverage that does not exercise the mechanism does not close this issue.

- Fix, regression, and docs/changelog land together; stale narrowed/refuted sub-legs are not reintroduced.

### Dedup
- **A93-02:** #3152 (half-open state; title cites a stale "1800s default"), #8125 (show constant), #6539 (show honesty), #9412/#3489 (close-state windows) and Y39-05 (leaf names) — none owns the runtime default. Not in prior-full-firewall-163.md, prior-titles.txt or this run's parts.

### Summary

### Review origin
- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r2-002.md`, claim `B02-01` (Part v29-v63).

- Source anchors (report at base `51d355c1d`, validated present at `27b8cba22d`; re-anchor before fixing): `manager.go:476-480`
- Mechanism (report Evidence, abridged): manager.go:476-480 `if isSubset14589(loadedSet, rendered) { if len(loadedSet) == len(rendered) { // Summary lied ... return rendered, hashes, nil`. loadedSet is a NAME set from ListLoadedConns (:461-473), and hashes are the candidate's. :305-313 promotes pae.names/pae.hashes. :863 later tears down only when `oldHash != newHashes[name]`. Observed charon behaviour: `--load-all` reports `loading certs certificate '.../new-local.pem' failed ... loaded 1 of 2 connections, 1 failed to load, 0 unloaded`, and the refused section keeps its OLD content (`local-1 {class=pre-shared key ...}`).

### Fix direction
- **B02-01:** Drop the name-only shortcut and always take the verification-reload path, or compare per-connection content (`--list-conns --raw` auth class, ts, proposals), or treat any section named in a `loading ... failed` line as not loaded and keep its prior hash. Acceptance: on gen1 -> gen2 (an existing conn refused) -> gen3 (now loadable), gen3 enters the teardown for `a`, and after gen2 `prevConnHashes["a"]` equals the gen1 hash.

### Summary
- **B12-01** — The 1 Hz dead-worker sweep retires NAT, steering and V_min holdings but never calls `IpsecInnerWorkerTransport::retire_worker`. (report severity: Medium — conditional on a worker panic (the #925 "degraded but forwarding" posture).
