## #16510 — #15248 regression: IPv6 generated-error sources keyed by /64 make every host of one LAN /64 share a single 15/s + burst-15 TE/PTB/reject budget [OPEN]

## Summary
#15248 regression: IPv6 generated-error sources keyed by /64 make every host of one LAN /64 share a single 15/s + burst-15 TE/PTB/reject budget

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — the only thing lost is generated replies (Time Exceeded, Packet Too Big, policy/filter reject and zone `tcp-rst` replies). The trigger packet is dropped either way and no enforcement changes. The loss is limited to the IPv6 hosts of one /64 in one zone, for as long as the load lasts. That matches round-2 A67-01 (Low). It is still a regression with a benign trigger. A LAN zone is typically one SLAAC /64, so that zone's whole IPv6 generated-reply budget drops from 1000/s (each /128 had 100/s) to 15/s. One host at about 15 pps can also suppress its neighbours' replies, which used to take about 1000 pps of IID rotation. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A67-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va67.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
On IPv6 LAN segments, generated replies are shared by the whole segment. Fail-fast `reject`/`tcp-rst` degrades into silent drops (clients wait for retransmit timers), traceroute's first hop shows `*`, and PTB for non-TCP IPv6 PMTUD is lost. One chatty host at 15 pps is enough. Recovery is automatic when the load stops. Operators see only the aggregate `*_rate_limited_total`.

**Contract:** `docs/generated-reply-rate-limit.md` (#15248 section) says "benign behaviour is unchanged" and "per-source-fair within the zone" (table rows for TimeExceeded/PacketTooBig/Reject). Commit e82bff5eb0 "Risk" section: "A single legitimate source's burst is now its fair share (15 at production) ... a real traceroute/PMTUD source emits a handful per flow". Neither the fix nor its docs consider several legitimate hosts sharing one /64, which is the normal IPv6 LAN shape.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_ratelimit.rs:326-338` `addr_fold`: `IpAddr::V6(v6) => { let x = u128::from(*v6); ((x >> 64) as u64) ^ 0xA67 }`. Lines `:254` `SRC_FAIR_SHARE_DIVISOR = SRC_SLOT_COUNT as u64 + 1` and `:261-266` `src_budget` give (1000/65, 1000/65) = 15/s with burst 15. `:409-414`: the source tier denies first (`if !src_bucket.try_take(now_ns, src_rate, src_burst) { ... return false; }`). Call sites key on the trigger's pre-NAT source: `icmp.rs:401` `Some(flow.src_ip)`; `poll_descriptor/reject_reply.rs:524-529` `flow.map(|flow| flow.src_ip)` or the META source; `tx/dispatch/mod.rs:440-451` META `l3_addrs_unfiltered` source. Fix commit e82bff5eb0 is an ancestor of d1ea69f9aa.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — real `#[cfg(test)]` cells driving `allow_generated_error_zoned_at` with the production `DEFAULT_RATE_PER_SEC`/`DEFAULT_BURST` on a per-zone limiter built by `forwarding_with_all_zone_buckets`. Component scope only, no lab run.

Thus all legitimate same-/64 hosts share **one** 15-reply budget per zone/reason, with inherited component control 15/90 replies for a 30-host simultaneous burst versus 90/90 v4; enforcement itself is unchanged.
- **Refutation:** Fixed 64 slots and /64 grouping intentionally bound spoofed IID rotation; no demonstrated typical production PMTUD/traceroute rate; aggregate 1000/s remains as intended. **Important fix flaw:** adding per-/128 fair shares **inside an unchanged outer 15/s /64 cap cannot pass the proposed 90/90 same-/64 burst acceptance**, irrespective of inner fairness. **Decisive check:** preserve aggregate/IID-rotation protection but explicitly budget LAN /64 at sufficient shared capacity or separate trusted host identities, then verify same-/64 burst, abusive single host, and spoofed-IID controls together.

The loss is limited to the IPv6 hosts of one /64 in one zone, for as long as the load lasts. That matches round-2 A67-01 (Low). It is still a regression with a benign trigger. ## #16512 — IPv6 over a GRE/WireGuard tunnel whose derived inner budget is below 1280: the PTB advertises the floored 1280 and the encap guard drops the packet, so non-TCP IPv6 packets in (budget, 1280] are blackholed permanently [OPEN]

## Summary
IPv6 over a GRE/WireGuard tunnel whose derived inner budget is below 1280: the PTB advertises the floored 1280 and the encap guard drops the packet, so non-TCP IPv6 packets in (budget, 1280] are blackholed permanently

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — it needs a small underlay: GRE with an IPv4 outer and transport MTU < 1304, or WireGuard with an IPv4 outer and underlay MTU < 1355. Inside that shape, every non-TCP IPv6 datagram whose size is in (inner budget, 1280] is dropped forever and the sender gets a PTB it cannot act on. That band includes the very common 1280-byte packets: DNS with a 1232-byte EDNS buffer and QUIC with a 1232-byte IPv6 UDP payload. TCP is unaffected. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A67-03`
**Source part:** `parts/va67.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Operators running GRE/WG over a reduced-MTU underlay (PPPoE-in-tunnel, cellular, nested VPN) and carrying IPv6 see DNS (1232 EDNS) and QUIC/HTTP3 traffic fail silently at exactly 1280 bytes. Packets keep getting PTBs that cannot help, and nothing recovers until the configuration changes.

**Contract:** RFC 8200 §5 (fetched from rfc-editor.org): "IPv6 requires that every link in the Internet have an MTU of 1280 octets or greater. ... On any link that cannot convey a 1280-octet packet in one piece, link-specific fragmentation and reassembly must be provided at a layer below IPv6." RFC 8201 §4: a node must not reduce its PMTU below 1280, so a PTB can never resolve this. The project already treats sub-1280 tunnel inner budgets as a real shape: #14658 (the NAT64 fragmenter floor for sub-1280 WG/GRE underlays) and #5159 (the segmentation floor).

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/dispatch/mod.rs:218-230`: on a tunnel path `mtu = post_transform_inner_mtu_with_dynamic(..)`, which is the unfloored inner budget. `icmp_ptb.rs:146-151` and `:167-169`: an IPv6 packet with `l3_len > mtu` → `EmitPacketTooBig { next_hop_mtu: clamp_next_hop_mtu(mtu, family) }`. `icmp_ptb.rs:181-187` `clamp_next_hop_mtu`: `AF_INET6 => 1280usize ... mtu.max(floor)`. The same clamp is used on the #10705 tunnel conversion at `tx/dispatch/mod.rs:304-310`. The original packet is dropped when `mtu_signalled`. Even if it were forwarded, `gre.rs:1643-1646` (`if outer_l3_len > outer_mtu { GRE_ENCAP_DF_OVERSIZE_DROPS ... }`) and `frame/wg.rs:836-851` (`encap_mtu_drops`) refuse it without fragmenting. `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_ipv6_mtu_13936.go:16-68` gates only configured unit MTUs against `RALinkMTUMin`; a tunnel's derived inner budget is never checked.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — component cells for the PTB decision and inner budget. The drop at the encap guard is STATIC (gre.rs/frame/wg.rs guards read). No lab run.

## Ledger validation (excerpt)
- `ledger-codex-batch06.md`: - **Defect:** Tunnel TX computes unfloored inner budget (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tx/dispatch/mod.rs:218-230`); IPv6 oversized decision emits PTB with `max(mtu,1280)` (`afxdp/icmp_ptb.rs:127-169,181-186`) and drops packet, so if budget <1280 a sender cannot reduce to the advertised limit. GRE outer cap independently refuses oversize without fragmenting (`afxdp/gre.rs:1828-1840`); packet's inherited GRE-1300/WG-1350 component probes observed inner budgets 1276/1275 and misleading PTB 1280.
- **Refutation:** Small outer MTU is a configuration prerequisite; TCP MSS/segmentation mitigates TCP, and common 1500 outer budget is unaffected. No on-wire DNS/QUIC outage shown, and different tunnel/outer-family overheads matter. **Decisive check:** commit gate derived inet6 inner MTU ≥1280 **or** real fragmentation below IPv6; for GRE-1300 and WG-1350, 1280-byte IPv6 datagram must be rejected at configuration or delivered, never PTB(1280)+drop. Keep normal-budget controls.

Dispositions/sampled in parts: A55-01 DUP Q44-01 item4 (agree, enforcement leg refuted); A65-01 DUP, A66-03 DUP (agree); A67-02 NEG (agree); va59/va63 no MATERIAL (agree). No FIXED/STALE at origin/master for any batch-06 claim — re-verified anchors below; censuses still red at master.

Packet in (budget,1280] → PTB(1280) + drop; sender at RFC8201 1280 floor can never comply → permanent blackhole incl. 1280B DNS-EDNS/QUIC. Executed decision/budget cells; encap guard drop STATIC gre.rs/wg.rs. TCP unaffected (segmentation/MSS).
- Refutation: no commit gate on derived budget (#13936 units only), no outer fragmenter. Underlay MTU 1300 legal — reachable config, RFC8200 §5 link must fragment below v6 or config refused. Either fix (commit reject vs outer frag) is owner decision.
- Unresolved: prevalence of sub-1304/1355 underlays unknown; mechanism certain.


## Impact
Low — it needs a small underlay: GRE with an IPv4 outer and transport MTU < 1304, or WireGuard with an IPv4 outer and underlay MTU < 1355. Inside that shape, every non-TCP IPv6 datagram whose size is in (inner budget, 1280] is dropped forever and the sender gets a PTB it cannot act on. That band includes the very common 1280-byte packets: DNS with a 1232-byte EDNS buffer and QUIC with a 1232-byte IPv6 UDP payload. TCP is unaffected. [reporter: Low]

## Acceptance / fix direction
Either reject at commit an inet6-carrying tunnel whose derived inner budget is below 1280 (mirroring #13936, using the same overhead SSOT as `native_gre_inner_mtu` / `wg_inner_mtu`), or fragment the outer datagram for IPv6 inners ≤ 1280 (link-specific fragmentation, as RFC 8200 §5 requires). Acceptance: the GRE-1300 / 1280-byte cell either fails commit or results in delivery, never `EmitPacketTooBig{1280}` followed by a drop. The 1400/1500 controls stay unchanged.

- Regression test demonstrating the defect at current master, then passing after the fix.
- No fail-open weakening of any existing gate.

## #16513 — #15155 regression: a `primary` designation on any address of a zoned untagged unit 0 other than the string-first one makes the helper refuse every snapshot (`InterfaceSharedIfindexAttributeConflict{primary_v4|primary_v6}`). On... [OPEN]

## Summary
#15155 regression: a `primary` designation on any address of a zoned untagged unit 0 other than the string-first one makes the helper refuse every snapshot (`InterfaceSharedIfindexAttributeConflict{primary_v4|primary_v6}`). On shared-ifindex shapes that are not consistently zoned, the designation is silently ignored instead.

**Finding ID:** R3-B15-02
**Severity (source):** High — the helper rejects the whole snapshot on a supported, documented knob. While the config is present, no config change (policy, NAT, routes) reaches forwarding, and each commit reports a dataplane error. A restart with the persisted config has no acceptable snapshot to bring up. The rejection is demonstrated; the boot-time outage is inferred and was not run. [reporter: High]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact


**Contract:** #15155 (fix 49b5be6f6d) and `docs/feature-gaps.md:1049` state that userspace `primary_v4/v6` selection "now honours the designated primary via `InterfaceAddressSnapshot.primary`", and that "designating `primary` explicitly is the supported way to choose". A config the compiler accepts must yield a buildable snapshot. `populate_egress` (#13181, 90b99536db) treats primary disagreement between rows of one consistently-zoned ifindex as snapshot corruption, which is not the case here.

**Trace:** 

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)


**Probe:**

Make the shared-ifindex merge carry the designation. Either the Go builder overlays the unit-0 configured marker onto the base row it collapses onto (when `snapshotLinuxName(unit0) == linuxName`, the same predicate #14331 uses for routing domain), or Rust lets a marked primary win the shared-ifindex merge instead of comparing per-row picks.

## #16514 — A configured `interfaces gr-… [unit N] mtu` is not used on userspace transit. The PTB decision, the GRE MSS clamp and TCP re-segmentation all size the inner packet from the physical transport MTU through `native_gre_i... [OPEN]

## Summary
A configured `interfaces gr-… [unit N] mtu` is not used on userspace transit. The PTB decision, the GRE MSS clamp and TCP re-segmentation all size the inner packet from the physical transport MTU through `native_gre_inner_mtu`, and the gr- logical MTU that the dispatcher already has never constrains it.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium. This is a lost operator knob on the only forwarding path. Operators lower the tunnel MTU when the underlay path beyond the first hop is smaller. With this defect, DF IPv4 and IPv6 transit flows larger than the configured MTU are encapsulated rather than answered with Frag-Needed/PTB. TCP SYNs are clamped to the physical-derived MSS (1436 rather than 1360 for MTU 1400). Because nothing learns the underlay PMTU (#13957 closed with a DF knob only), the result is a PMTUD black hole for those flows. There is no enforcement or isolation loss, and workarounds exist (`tcp-mss gre-out`, `clear-dont-fragment-bit`). Demonstrated at component level. The end-to-end black hole is potential. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A68-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va68.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Any GRE deployment across a provider path smaller than the local link (PPPoE, MPLS, nested tunnels) uses the tunnel MTU knob. For transit it silently does nothing, so DF TCP and IPv6 flows stall after the handshake, and nothing tells the operator the knob is ignored. The effect lasts until the operator finds a workaround.

**Contract:** `docs/feature-coverage.md:138-156` says the PMTUD trigger is the "effective egress MTU (the minimum of the nonzero egress interface MTU and selected route RTAX_MTU)", and that tunnel PMTUD composes overlay and transport MTUs. `docs/userspace-native-gre-plan.md:134` lists "tunnel MTU / effective payload MTU" as part of the endpoint model. Junos treats the gr- logical MTU as the tunnel IP MTU. The configuration is accepted (`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:181,873,956`) and applied to the kernel anchor (`pkg/routing/tunnel.go:614-620`, `reconcileAnchorMTULocked` `:693-708`).

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/tunnel.rs:82` sets the tunnel resolution's `egress_ifindex: logical_ifindex`. `tx/dispatch/mod.rs:205` has `let egress_mtu = forwarded_egress_mtu(decision, forwarding);`, and `:2158-2166` returns `egress[egress_ifindex].mtu` unmodified when `tunnel_endpoint_id != 0`. `:218` hands it to `post_transform_inner_mtu_with_dynamic`. In `icmp_ptb.rs:380-392` the non-NAT64 tunnel arm calls `tunnel_inner_mtu_with_dynamic`, then takes `min_nonzero_mtu(tunnel_inner, route_mtu)`. The `egress_mtu` argument is read only by the `is_nat64` arms. `icmp_ptb.rs:426` reads `TunnelKind::Gre => native_gre_inner_mtu(forwarding, decision)`. In `forwarding/mss.rs:126-148`, `tunnel_outer_mtu` uses transport `tx_ifindex`, then `egress_ifindex`, then `.or_else(|| forwarding.egress.get(&endpoint.logical_ifindex))` (`:141`), so the transport row always wins. `frame/tcp_segmentation.rs:260` and `forwarding/mss.rs:69-86` (`native_gre_tcp_mss`) use the same helper. `forwarding_build/tunnels.rs` never reads `endpoint.mtu` (no `mtu` token in the file). The snapshot MTU source is `pkg/dataplane/userspace/interfaces.go:1518` (`mtu = link.Attrs().MTU`), with `tunnels.go:217` `MTU: iface.MTU`.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED. A component probe ran against `post_transform_inner_mtu`, `native_gre_inner_mtu` and `native_gre_tcp_mss` with a resolution shaped as `resolve_tunnel_forwarding_resolution` builds it. The Go producer chain was checked by static reading only.

## #16515 — The #15161 fix charges actual decoded bytes but keeps the fixed 256 MiB retention bound. The 520-byte struct floor alone means 8 workers × 65536 forward sessions cannot fit. At realistic IPv4+SNAT rows (about 646 bytes) the bound trips... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The #15161 fix charges actual decoded bytes but keeps the fixed 256 MiB retention bound. The 520-byte struct floor alone means 8 workers × 65536 forward sessions cannot fit. At realistic IPv4+SNAT rows (about 646 bytes) the bound trips at about 415k deltas, which is below 7 workers' ceiling. Every cold prime and FullResync from such an owner then fails closed.

**Finding ID:** R3-B16-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — the consequence when reached is HA-recovery class: the standby is never cold-primed or re-driven, and pre-existing sessions not re-sent incrementally are lost at failover. The attempt fails on every retry while the table stays above the threshold. Reach is bounded to owners configured with 7 or more workers and a table above about 415k–500k owned forward sessions. The 6-worker reference sizing is unaffected. The failure is demonstrated at component level; the end-to-end consequence is potential (not lab-driven). [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Exactly the operators who follow the documented scale-up guidance lose standby priming once their table is busy. The only signal is repeated owed-cold-prime and bulk-sync failure warnings. A failover then drops every long-lived session the incremental path never re-sent. Recovery requires shrinking the table below the threshold.

**Contract:** The #15161 fix direction requires the retention budget to be "never below `workers*DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS/2` forward deltas". The helper side is sized for 16 workers (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/mod.rs:505-512`, "16 full workers × DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS × two records"). `workers` is min-only in the schema ("the runtime owns its ceiling", `pkg/config/schema_system.go:461-472`). Operators are told to scale workers for headroom (`docs/userspace-dataplane-architecture.md:2914-2917`).

**Trace:** owner node with N≥8 workers holds more than about 500k owned forward sessions → the peer rejoins, the daemon restarts or a forced resync runs → cold-prime sweep (`pkg/cluster/sync_conn_sweep.go`) or FullResync (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_stream.go:597-605`) → `userspaceBulkSnapshotWithConfig` / `exportUserspaceOwnerRGSessionsWithConfig` → `ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged` appends 8192-delta pages to one slice → the byte bound trips around page 62 → `ErrOwnerRGExportIncomplete` → `doBulkSync` "bulk sync table-truth snapshot" error → the obligation is re-armed and fails identically on every sweep.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
All at d1ea69f9aa: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/owner_rg_export_paging_9344.go:52` `ownerRGExportMaxAccumulatorBytes = 256 * 1024 * 1024`. `:81-89` `ownerRGExportActualDeltaBytes` = `unsafe.Sizeof(*d)` plus string lengths. `:252-263` charges each page and returns `"%w: export accumulator exceeds %d-byte bound"`, discarding everything collected. `:58` `maxOwnerRGExportDataPages = 512` is never reached. Per-worker table cap: `userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:268` `DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS: usize = 131072`, enforced in `session/install.rs:81,542` on entries. Each logical session is forward plus reverse (`afxdp/coordinator/session_manager.rs:179-190`), so the forward ceiling is 65536 per worker. The export emits forward entries only (`afxdp/worker/loop_body/export_slice.rs`: "Reverse (unreachable: the walk predicate skips them)"). Callers propagate the error: `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_export.go:72,133`. `pkg/cluster/sync_bulk.go:100-109` aborts the bulk when `src()` errors. The #15161 cell `owner_rg_export_paging_9344_test.go:382-405` pins 48 pages (6 workers).

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 timeout 900 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestVB16AccumulatorByWorkerCount|TestOwnerRGExportCompletesSixWorkerWindow15161' -count=1 -v`. Fixture: `RUN/verify/vb16/probes/vb16_probe_test.go`. Output: `RUN/verify/vb16/probe-b16-01.out`. `unsafe.Sizeof(SessionDeltaInfo)=520 budget=268435456`. `workers=6 ... collected=393216 err=<nil>`. `workers=7 pages=56 window=458752 -> collected=458752 err=<nil>` (positive control). `workers=8 pages=64 window=524288 -> collected=0 requests=62 err=owner-RG session export incomplete: export accumulator exceeds 268435456-byte bound`. The #15161 cell passes in the same run. The reporter's realistic-row probe (`RUN/workers/b16/evidence/probe02-accumulator.out`) shows a 646-byte IPv4+SNAT row failing at page 51 of an 8-worker window. Re-run by vb16 with that realistic row (`RUN/verify/vb16/probes/vb16_probe2_test.go`, `TestVB16RealisticRowSevenWorkers`, output `RUN/verify/vb16/probe-b16-01-rerun.out`): `v4+snat workers=6 pages=48 window=393216 charge=646 -> collected=393216 requests=48 err=<nil>` (positive control) and `v4+snat workers=7 pages=56 window=458752 charge=646 -> collected=0 requests=51 err=owner-RG session export incomplete: export accumulator exceeds 268435456-byte bound`. This agrees with 268,435,456 / 646 ≈ 415.5k < 458,752. Limit: a fake helper delivers the pages.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Stream each page into the bulk sink or snapshot builder (the #15161 first-preference direction) instead of retaining `[]SessionDeltaInfo`. Alternatively, convert each page to the compact cluster row before retention, or derive the budget from the helper-reported worker count (≤16) × 65536 × the actual row cost, with a hard ceiling. Acceptance: a fake-helper cell with 16 × 65536 realistic IPv4+SNAT deltas (128 pages) completes; the 513-page unterminated cell and the dropped-delta cell still fail closed.

The trigger is an owner node configured with `workers 8` (or 7 with realistic rows) whose owned forward-session count exceeds about 415k–500k, followed by a peer rejoin, daemon restart or forced resync.
- **Evidence:** All at d1ea69f9aa: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/owner_rg_export_paging_9344.go:52` `ownerRGExportMaxAccumulatorBytes = 256 * 1024 * 1024`. `:81-89` `ownerRGExportActualDeltaBytes` = `unsafe.Sizeof(*d)` plus string lengths. `:252-263` charges each page and returns `"%w: export accumulator exceeds %d-byte bound"`, discarding everything collected. `:58` `maxOwnerRGExportDataPages = 512` is never reached. Per-worker table cap: `userspace-dp/src/session/mod.rs:268` `DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS: usize = 131072`, enforced in `session/install.rs:81,542` on entries. Each logical session is forward plus reverse (`afxdp/coordinator/session_manager.rs:179-190`), so the forward ceiling is 65536 per worker. The export emits forward entries only (`afxdp/worker/loop_body/export_slice.rs`: "Reverse (unreachable: the walk predicate skips them)"). Callers propagate the error: `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_export.go:72,133`. `pkg/cluster/sync_bulk.go:100-109` aborts the bulk when `src()` errors. The #15161 cell `owner_rg_export_paging_9344_test.go:382-405` pins 48 pages (6 workers).
- **Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 timeout 900 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestVB16AccumulatorByWorkerCount|TestOwnerRGExportCompletesSixWorkerWindow15161' -count=1 -v`. Fixture: `RUN/verify/vb16/probes/vb16_probe_test.go`. Output: `RUN/verify/vb16/probe-b16-01.out`. `unsafe.Sizeof(SessionDeltaInfo)=520 budget=268435456`. `workers=6 ... collected=393216 err=<nil>`. `workers=7 pages=56 window=458752 -> collected=458752 err=<nil>` (positive control). `workers=8 pages=64 window=524288 -> collected=0 requests=62 err=owner-RG session export incomplete: export accumulator exceeds 268435456-byte bound`. The #15161 cell passes in the same run. The reporter's realistic-row probe (`RUN/workers/b16/evidence/probe02-accumulator.out`) shows a 646-byte IPv4+SNAT row failing at page 51 of an 8-worker window. Re-run by vb16 with that realistic row (`RUN/verify/vb16/probes/vb16_probe2_test.go`, `TestVB16RealisticRowSevenWorkers`, output `RUN/verify/vb16/probe-b16-01-rerun.out`): `v4+snat workers=6 pages=48 window=393216 charge=646 -> collected=393216 requests=48 err=<nil>` (positive control) and `v4+snat workers=7 pages=56 window=458752 charge=646 -> collected=0 requests=51 err=owner-RG session export incomplete: export accumulator exceeds 268435456-byte bound`. This agrees with 268,435,456 / 646 ≈ 415.5k < 458,752. Limit: a fake helper delivers the pages.
- **Trace:** owner node with N≥8 workers holds more than about 500k owned forward sessions → the peer rejoins, the daemon restarts or a forced resync runs → cold-prime sweep (`pkg/cluster/sync_conn_sweep.go`) or FullResync (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_stream.go:597-605`) → `userspaceBulkSnapshotWithConfig` / `exportUserspaceOwnerRGSessionsWithConfig` → `ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged` appends 8192-delta pages to one slice → the byte bound trips around page 62 → `ErrOwnerRGExportIncomplete` → `doBulkSync` "bulk sync table-truth snapshot" error → the obligation is re-armed and fails identically on every sweep.
- **Refutation attempt:** Checked each possible guard. Per-worker forward ceiling: 65536, not 131072. The reverse entries share the 131072 cap, which narrows the reporter's arithmetic in the correct direction. Reverse entries in the export: not exported. Helper page cap: 512 pages, not the trigger. Worker ceiling: no config upper bound, and the helper asserts 16. Partial fallback: removed by design (#5085), so the failure is closed. #15161 fix b689632817: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` is true, and its predicate (the 1863-byte charge per delta) is gone. Strengthened the claim: the 8-worker failure is independent of string width, since 8×65536×520 = 272.6 MB exceeds 268.4 MB. Narrowed the claim: 7 workers pass with minimal rows and fail with realistic rows (now executed). Inference, not executed: the 6-worker realistic window has only about 5.6% headroom (415.5k vs 393k), so a full 6-worker table with more than about 22k in-window tombstones would also trip the bound.
- **HPC/invariant check:** The memory bound is legitimate; its unit is wrong. It must scale with the helper-reported worker count, which the helper already bounds structurally at 16, or retention must be removed by streaming per page. A 16 × 65536 realistic window retained in full would be about 680 MB, so streaming or a slimmer retained form is the sound fix, not a bigger constant.

## #16516 — wire-routing-separation's #11416 "fixture-shape guard" cells match `$(cat "$0")` against literal needles that also appear on the guard's own lines. Removing the populated lan->wire-vrf policy and SNAT statements, and their cleanup delete... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
wire-routing-separation's #11416 "fixture-shape guard" cells match `$(cat "$0")` against literal needles that also appear on the guard's own lines. Removing the populated lan->wire-vrf policy and SNAT statements, and their cleanup deletes, still passes both cells. Only the zone-is-not-wan term can fail.

**Finding ID:** R3-N06-06
**Severity (source):** Low — Low — the selftest cell cannot detect its named defect. A live run with the policy/NAT pair dropped would collide with the #11061 validator and fail loudly (or leave residue on the shared cluster) rather than read green. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
the cells are the claimed unit-level proof for #11416. In practice the regression they name is caught only by a live run on the shared cluster, which costs a lock slot and may leave config residue. The impact is bounded to future edits.

**Contract:** test/incus/wire-routing-separation.sh:190-195: "Reverting the zone to wan (or dropping the policy/NAT pair) makes the populated commit collide with the #11061 validator again — these cells are the unit-level proof that cannot happen by construction."

**Trace:** edit drops the policy/NAT pair → `--selftest` (hermetic, run by `make test-wire-routing-separation-lib`) still matches the needles in the guard's own text → green → the defect surfaces only in the live cluster run as a commit rejection.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
:196 @d1ea69f9aa `script_text="$(cat "$0")"`. :198-200 needles `*'set security zones security-zone %s interfaces %s'*`, `*'from-zone lan to-zone %s policy wire-vrf-allow'*` and `*'rule-set lan-to-wire-vrf to zone %s'*`. :208-210 the three `delete ...` needles. Each needle is a literal on these same lines. :197 `wan_zone_lines` excludes its own line and is the only term that can fail. The transaction is at :532 (add printf) and :543 (cleanup printf).

**Probe:** Mutant (RUN/verify/vn06/probes/wrs-mutant.diff, scratch copy of test/incus): the four policy and four SNAT `set` statements are stripped from :532, and the policy/NAT deletes from :543. Running `bash /var/tmp/vn06/mutwrs/wire-routing-separation.sh --selftest` from the repo root gives `PASS populated GRE member uses dedicated wire-vrf zone, not wan`, `PASS populated cleanup deletes owned zone policy and SNAT`, and `33 passed, 0 failed`, identical to the original (wrs-orig.out). Positive control: the zone set to `wan` at :532 gives `FAIL populated GRE member ...` and `32 passed, 1 failed` (wrs-wanzone-control.out). Instrument note: running with cwd=test/incus gives 28/5 in both arms (cwd-relative fixtures), so the probe must run from the repo root.

## Acceptance / fix direction
extract the populated add/cleanup transaction into a function that prints the CLI transcript (no incus), call it in selftest mode and assert on its output statement set. At minimum, match only the body of `cli_commit_populated` excluding the guard. Acceptance: the mutant above reds both cells, and the zone control still reds.

## #16517 — The native-GRE anchor is a TUN that keeps the kernel default MTU of 1500 when no MTU is configured, and adoption actively resets it to 1500. The local-origin encap guard then refuses every packet whose outer would exc... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The native-GRE anchor is a TUN that keeps the kernel default MTU of 1500 when no MTU is configured, and adoption actively resets it to 1500. The local-origin encap guard then refuses every packet whose outer would exceed the transport MTU. For a 1500 underlay that is inner 1477–1500 with an IPv4 outer (1481–1500 keyed) and 1457–1500 with an IPv6 outer. The drop only `debug_log!`s and never sends Frag-Needed/PTB back into the TUN, so the kernel never learns a smaller MTU.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium. On a default-config GRE tunnel, the firewall's own large packets are discarded without a PMTUD signal. This covers OSPF LSUpdates filled to the interface MTU, BGP UPDATE segments at MSS 1460 when the peer advertises 1460, and DF `ping size`. Adjacencies and sessions come up on small packets and then stall on bulk exchange. The scope is bounded to self-originated traffic on tunnels without an operator MTU, and transit is unaffected (it has its own PTB). Demonstrated at component level. The protocol stall is potential. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A68-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va68.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Routing protocols over GRE are a primary reason to run GRE on the firewall. A default-config tunnel brings OSPF/BGP up and then wedges under load, which looks like a peer problem. The only signal is an aggregate counter. Recovery requires an operator to configure `mtu` by hand.

**Contract:** The #2300 single-source-of-truth contract is that the tunnel device MTU is defaulted from the underlay, not from a literal 1500. It is implemented for WireGuard only (`pkg/routing/tunnel_wireguard.go` `wgTunMTUForEndpoint`). The repository's own comment at `pkg/routing/tunnel.go:941-944` says "kernel GRE/IPIP devices have protocol-specific default MTUs (1476/1462/...), not the TUN 1500". `docs/userspace-native-gre-plan.md:178-199` describes the #2331 guard as a final backstop, with PTB handled by the transit dispatcher beforehand. No such PTB exists on the local-origin path.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`pkg/routing/tunnel.go:587-623` creates the anchor as `TUNTAP_MODE_TUN` and sets an MTU only `if tc.MTU > 0`. In `:693-708` `reconcileAnchorMTULocked`, the `case adopting:` branch sets `want = 1500` (`:699-700`). `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tunnel.rs:722-723` calls `encapsulate_native_gre_frame(...).ok_or_else(|| "encapsulate_native_gre_frame_failed")?`. In `gre.rs:1641-1648`, `if outer_l3_len > outer_mtu { GRE_ENCAP_DF_OVERSIZE_DROPS.fetch_add(1); return None; }`, and the check does not depend on DF. In `tunnel.rs:403-413`, the `Err` arm only runs `debug_log!` (compiled out without the `debug-log` feature). It writes no ICMP into the TUN and calls no `record_local_tunnel_exception`.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED. The Go anchor MTU reconcile probe and the Rust `build_local_origin_tunnel_tx_request` size sweep both ran. The kernel TUN default of 1500 (ETH_DATA_LEN) is a kernel fact, not executed here.

Encap guard in gre.rs refuses `outer > transport_mtu` DF-agnostically, local-origin error arm only `debug_log!`s, no PTB into TUN, no `record_local_tunnel_exception`. Executed Go probe (create writes [], adopt 1476→[1500], 1400 control [1400]) + Rust sweep (IPv6 outer: inner ≤1456 OK, 1457–1500 ERR + oversize counter). ## #16518 — `ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged` drops `m.mu` for each page RPC and applies that page's attached helper status on re-lock. Its fence checks only proc, procGen, config generation and socket. A disarm that queued behind the page RPC on... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
`ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged` drops `m.mu` for each page RPC and applies that page's attached helper status on re-lock. Its fence checks only proc, procGen, config generation and socket. A disarm that queued behind the page RPC on `controlReqMu` applies its fresh DISARMED status first, and the pager then overwrites it with the older ARMED one. The result is `userspace_ctrl.Enabled=1` and `lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=true` while the helper is disarmed, until the next page or poll applies fresh truth.

**Finding ID:** R3-B16-02
**Severity (source):** Low — each occurrence lasts until the next page reply. That is normally milliseconds, longer if the page waits on a slow worker ACK, and up to one 1 Hz poll tick after the final page. During that time ctrl steers into a disarmed helper and `takeoverReadyLocked` loses its "forwarding not armed" blocker. It is consequential only for durable fail-closed disarms (protocol-failure or unsupported-publish disarms); a plain operator disarm is re-armed by the desired-state reconcile anyway. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Cold prime and FullResync windows run tens to hundreds of pages and recur on every peer rejoin, which is when commits and protocol-gate disarms cluster. Each overlap briefly steers traffic into a disarmed helper and manufactures a takeover-ready reading. It self-corrects without operator action.

**Contract:** `applyHelperStatusLocked` is the single writer of `userspace_ctrl`/`userspace_bindings` from helper truth, and the helper's truth must be applied in RPC order. The fail-closed disarms (`disarmSnapshotProtocolFailureLocked`, `disarmBeforeUnsupportedPublishLocked`) rely on nothing re-enabling ctrl from an older status (#13093 risk note: "worker and forwarding fail-closed gates unchanged").

**Trace:** export page N RPC in flight (it holds controlReqMu, and the helper answers ARMED) → a disarm path takes `m.mu` and blocks on controlReqMu → the page reply returns → the disarm RPC runs and applies DISARMED under `m.mu`, then releases → the pager re-locks, passes its fence (same proc, same generation) and applies the ARMED page status → ctrl=1 and ForwardingArmed=true → page N+1 (or the next poll) applies fresh truth.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
All at d1ea69f9aa: `pkg/dataplane/userspace/owner_rg_export_paging_9344.go:154-166` unlocks before the RPC. `:167-170` `requestDetailedAtSocket(ControlRequest{Type: "export_owner_rg_sessions", SessionExport: &req}, controlSocket)` sends no SuppressStatus. `:171-182` re-lock fence on proc/procGen/generation/socket. `:183-187` `status = *resp.Status; statusErr = m.applyHelperStatusLocked(&status)`. `process_control.go:178-180` `requestDetailedAtSocket` holds `controlReqMu`. `manager_status.go:218-220` `SetForwardingArmed` holds `m.mu` across its RPC. Rust `server/handlers/mod.rs:637-650` attaches a status after `owner_rg_collect` unless `suppress_status`. The daemon discards the returned status: `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_userspace_export.go:72,133` `deltas, _, err := exporter.ExportOwnerRGSessionsPaged(rgIDs)`.

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 timeout 900 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run TestB16ProbeExportPageAppliesStaleStatusOverDisarm -count=1 -v`. Fixture: `RUN/workers/b16/evidence/b16_probe_export_stale_status_test.go`. Output: `RUN/verify/vb16/probe-b16-02-03.out`. Control (no disarm): `ctrl.Enabled=1 lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=true; helper actually armed=true`. Positive control inside the defect arm: `after disarm applied: ctrl.Enabled=0 lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=false`. Defect: `at page-2 RPC (after page-1 status applied): ctrl.Enabled=1 lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=true; helper actually armed=false`. Limit: the hook-routed disarm does not take `controlReqMu`, and the production ordering is argued from the lock structure.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Set `SuppressStatus: true` on export page requests and drop the per-page `applyHelperStatusLocked`, since both production callers discard the status. Alternatively, fence the apply with the same newer-status sequence R3-A30-03's fix introduces. Acceptance: the probe's defect arm leaves `ctrl.Enabled=0`, and the #9344/#15161 paging cells stay green.

Positive control inside the defect arm: `after disarm applied: ctrl.Enabled=0 lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=false`. Defect: `at page-2 RPC (after page-1 status applied): ctrl.Enabled=1 lastStatus.ForwardingArmed=true; helper actually armed=false`. Limit: the hook-routed disarm does not take `controlReqMu`, and the production ordering is argued from the lock structure.
- **Trace:** export page N RPC in flight (it holds controlReqMu, and the helper answers ARMED) → a disarm path takes `m.mu` and blocks on controlReqMu → the page reply returns → the disarm RPC runs and applies DISARMED under `m.mu`, then releases → the pager re-locks, passes its fence (same proc, same generation) and applies the ARMED page status → ctrl=1 and ForwardingArmed=true → page N+1 (or the next poll) applies fresh truth.
- **Refutation attempt:** Checked each fence and possible mitigation. The re-lock fence: no field moves on a disarm. `ctrlMustStayDisabledLocked`: keys only on rgTransitionInFlight and the link-cycle lease. The desired-state reconcile: it re-arms plain operator disarms anyway, so durable disarms are the consequential case. R3-A30-03's fix scope: its acceptance is poll-only (`process_status.go`). va30's fix direction names this site, but its acceptance cell does not exercise it, so this is not a DUP. Narrowed the reporter's window: the next page's fresh status normally corrects it within milliseconds. The tick-long window applies only after the final page or a slow ACK page.
- **HPC/invariant check:** Single-writer ordering invariant. Fix cost is O(1): suppress the per-page status, which the callers discard, or compare an apply sequence captured before the unlock.

## #16519 — The #8597 parse node budget is per-block again. The #15195 fix (8ac8a61868) resets `p.nodes` to `before + 1 + len(Keys)` after each statement, which throws away every unit the statement's children charged. Several blocks, each just under the… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary

The #8597 parse node budget is per-block again. The #15195 fix (8ac8a61868) resets `p.nodes` to `before + 1 + len(Keys)` after each statement, which throws away every unit the statement's children charged. Several blocks, each just under the budget, therefore build an AST of any size without an error.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A01-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium. The documented memory guard (maxParseNodes 200k, about 37 MB of live AST) is gone on every hierarchical ingress. That includes the HA peer `SyncApply` text, which store.go:1108-1112 itself calls "a network-reachable parse entry point (a hostile/corrupt peer config)" and which it parses under…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL. This regression removes a documented load-bearing resource guard on every hierarchical parse path, and the probe demonstrates it.

## Mechanism

A config body of at most 16 MiB passes `checkConfigSize`. It then goes through `config.NewParser(content).Parse()`, where each `parseStatements` frame resets its child budget. The full tree is retained, and only then does compile or validation run. In SyncApply all of this happens while `Store.mu` is held.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/config/parser.go:458` has `before := p.nodes`, and `:459` calls `node := p.parseStatement()`, which recurses through `parseStatements` for a `{` body and charges the children into `p.nodes`. `:468` has `p.nodes = before + 1 + len(node.Keys)`, an assignment, not an addition. `parseKeys` at `:797` only reads `p.nodes` (`if p.nodes+len(keys) >= maxParseNodes`) and never adds to it. The only other budget checks are `store_command.go:72-80` and `:854-905`, which cover the flat SetPath and replay paths. The hierarchical ingresses are `store.go:1117` (SyncApply), `store_command.go:612` and `:691` (load), `store_commit.go:1882`, `store_persist.go:696`, `rollback_metadata.go:82` and `check.go:28`. None of them recounts after the parse.

## Impact

One payload pins hundreds of MB to GB of heap before any gate runs. On the standby, SyncApply holds the store lock while doing this, and a restart that reloads the same DB or rollback text repeats it. Recovery is restarting xpfd with a sane config. The guard was added for exactly this denial of service, so its silent removal also invalidates the README's stated bound.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Replace the assignment with `p.nodes += 1 + len(node.Keys)`, or charge the node before recursing. Add a regression test with K sibling blocks and with nested blocks whose combined size exceeds 200k while each block stays under it. The acceptance criterion is that the budget error fires and the existing `*_15195` and `*_8597` tests stay green. The mutation run shows they do.

## Contract (where cited)

parser.go:47-85 says `maxParseNodes` "bounds the number of AST nodes a single parse BUILDS". The pkg/config README section "Recursion and size bounds" calls it the fifth guard and states that it is parser-wide rather than per-block. `TestNestedStatementsCountTowardTheBudget_8597` exists because "a per-block cap bounds nothing".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A01-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A01-01 | Medium | The #8597 parse node budget is per-block again. The #15195 fix (8ac8a61868) resets p.nodes… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:7: - **R3-A01-01 — MATERIAL (Medium).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/parser.go:458-469` restores `p.nodes` to `before+1+len(node.Keys)` after recursively parsing a block; charges for its descendants disappear. Its key counter and 200,000-node limit (`parser.go:85,797`) do not constrain the *sum* of sibling subtrees; the report's old positive-control test accepted 480,006 nodes. **Refutation/bounds:** `ParseConfig` still has an independent 16-MiB input limit, so “unbounded AST” and a guaranteed OOM are too strong; this is control-plane allocation/GC during authorized config parsing, not a packet-path performance measurement. **Decisive check:** bounded current-revision parser test of several individually sublimit blocks, asserting aggregate rejection and peak heap if impact is to be quantified.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L11: ### R3-A01-01 — parse node budget per-block reset — **MATERIAL** - Defect (strongest): `pkg/config/parser.go:458-468` @origin/master: `before := p.nodes; node := p.parseStatement(); p.nodes = before + 1 + len(node.Keys)` — assignment overwrites children's charges accumulated during recursion. Doc at `parser.go:47-85` promises parser-wide bound (~37 MB). `parseKeys:797` only reads `p.nodes`. Reachable via every hierarchical parse incl. HA `SyncApply` (called "network-reachable … hostile/corrupt peer" in store), `CheckText`, load override/merge, rollback — all config-authority / sync-peer / day-0 actors, no unprivileged remote actor. - Refutation (strongest): Actors all need config authority/peer trust; 16 MiB cap bounds input; OOM (GB extrapolation) not demonstrated; per-block budget still caps any single block at 200k. This bounds severity (Medium, availability of xpfd, not bypass) but does not refute guard loss. - Evidence: Source confirmed at origin/master (above). [SMR-run] `TestSMRBudgetSibling` in codex-batch01: 3 sibling `system{80k leaves}` → `NodeCount=480006 errs=0` — no budget error at current master. Report's mutation control (`+=` fixes, *_15195/*_8597 green) is coherent with the assignment mechanism. - Unresolved/decisive: Heap/OOM at 16 MiB under `SyncApply` holding `Store.mu` (lock-hold duration + RSS) — needs bounded RSS measurement; not needed for MATERIAL (guard regression proven). ### R3-A01-04 — `show | compare` ignores token grouping/quote provenance — *

## #16520 — The local tunnel loop chooses the TX binding with a per-packet counter (`next_slot % candidate_count`) instead of a flow hash. Consecutive packets of one self-originated flow therefore land on different bindings, whic... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The local tunnel loop chooses the TX binding with a per-packet counter (`next_slot % candidate_count`) instead of a flow hash. Consecutive packets of one self-originated flow therefore land on different bindings, which are drained by different worker threads, and intra-flow order is not preserved.

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low. This is a performance and robustness issue for firewall-originated TCP over GRE (BGP, LDP, ssh): reordering causes duplicate ACKs and spurious recovery. There is no enforcement impact. Modern Linux RACK tolerates moderate reordering, and the rate is unmeasured. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A68-04`
**Source part:** `parts/va68.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
Bulk control-plane TCP over GRE (BGP full table, ssh/scp to tunnel-side hosts) sees avoidable reordering on multi-queue underlays.

**Contract:** Every other ECMP and queue choice in the dataplane is flow-hashed so that per-flow order is kept. No document specifies per-packet spraying for local-origin tunnel TX.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/tunnel.rs:273` declares `let mut next_slot = 0usize;`. At `:382-389`, `select_live_binding_for_ifindex(&identities, &live, plan.tx_ifindex, next_slot)` is followed by `next_slot = next_slot.wrapping_add(1)` for every built packet. `:1006-1044` returns the `next_slot % candidate_count`-th bound binding of the ifindex. `tunnel_tests.rs:74` `select_live_binding_for_ifindex_round_robins_without_allocating_candidates` asserts consecutive slots pick different bindings. `plan.tx_request.flow_key` is available but unused for the choice.

**Verification (research):** STATIC — the code path and the existing test that pins the rotation were read. Reordering on the wire was not measured.

## #16521 — After the post-link-cycle rebind, `notifyLinkCycle` calls `markAppliedSnapshotLocked()` with no check that the helper holds `m.lastSnapshot`. A commit that lands in Compile's XSK-liveness-unproven deferral window and also needs a RETH... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
After the post-link-cycle rebind, `notifyLinkCycle` calls `markAppliedSnapshotLocked()` with no check that the helper holds `m.lastSnapshot`. A commit that lands in Compile's XSK-liveness-unproven deferral window and also needs a RETH MAC cycle therefore records the deferred generation as applied. The daemon can then discharge the commit's policy-invalidation debt early, which skips the designed re-capture at the real publish boundary.

**Finding ID:** R3-B16-03
**Severity (source):** Low — the Manager authority lie is executed. The enforcement consequence is static: sessions admitted under a now-deleted or denied policy between the commit-time capture and the actual deferred publish are never revoked. That window is Compile time plus about one status tick after the rebind. The trigger is narrow (a RETH-MAC-changing commit within the liveness window after a helper start or a previous link cycle) and depends on applySem ordering. [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Positional policy IDs and revocation debt are only meaningful under the config the helper enforces. Advancing the authority early lets a deleting or tightening commit report its invalidation complete while flows admitted under the old policy in the window keep forwarding indefinitely. Who hits it: a cluster commit changing RETH membership or MAC shortly after a boot, a helper restart or a previous cycle.

**Contract:** `pkg/dataplane/userspace/applied_nat_view.go:91-95`: the caller "MUST call this only AFTER a successful full apply_snapshot (or on the status-loop catch-up path where the helper already echoes m.lastSnapshot.Generation)". `builder.go:49-52` says the capture-authority committer exists because preparing a snapshot "must not mutate the currently active packet authority before the helper acknowledges that snapshot". `pkg/daemon/daemon_policy_invalidate_capture.go:1499-1502` says the deferred-publish re-capture exists "so sessions admitted during the deferral window can be rebound or deleted under the same one-shot decision".

**Trace:** commit C needs a RETH MAC cycle (new RETH, RG or cluster-id change, VF reset), within about 10 s of a helper start or previous cycle, or on an idle link whose probe keeps extending → daemon pre-check sets DeferWorkers (`daemon_apply_dataplane.go:75-115`) → commit-time policy capture and debt → Compile takes the pendingXSKStartup branch (gen N+1 retained, helper still on N) → RETH loop → NotifyLinkCycle → `markAppliedSnapshotLocked` → `appliedSnapshot=N+1`, `policySnapshotCommitter(N+1)` → the discharge worker queues on applySem → after the apply, ordering (a): discharge deletes the commit-time capture and clears the debt and plan, then `completeDeferredSnapshotApply(N+1)` runs → the next tick's pre-publisher sees debt==nil and does no re-capture → N+1 publishes → sessions admitted under the old policy since the capture survive. Ordering (b) (pre-publisher first) captures against the lying `PolicyReadConfig`. The reporter states this refuses and holds publication; that is static and not executed.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
All at d1ea69f9aa: `process_linkcycle.go:909` `m.markAppliedSnapshotLocked()` runs unconditionally after the `rebind` request. The comment at `:901-908` justifies it only for DeferWorkers. `applied_nat_view.go:111-132`: the only guard is `m.deferWorkers`, which the daemon clears before NotifyLinkCycle per the comment. The function then sets `appliedSnapshot` from `m.lastSnapshot` and calls both committers. `manager_compile.go:586-590` `pendingXSKStartup := ... publishedSnapshot != 0 && !xskLivenessProven && !xskLivenessFailed`. `:645-697` defers every such commit, same-plan or not: `m.pendingFullSnapshotMetadata = true; m.lastSnapshot = snap`, `SnapshotPublishDeferred`, no publish. `process_linkcycle.go:870` `m.xskLivenessProven = false` on every cycle. Daemon side: `policyInvalidationSnapshotPublished` (`daemon_policy_invalidate_capture.go:1523-1541`) spawns a discharge worker. `dischargePolicyInvalidationAfterPublish` (`:1547-1586`) discharges when `generation >= debt.publishGeneration`. `dischargePolicyInvalidationDebtLocked` clears the debt and plan and marks the digest applied (`:1592-1630`). `capturePolicyInvalidationBeforeDeferredPublish` returns nil when `debt == nil` (`:1473-1476`).

**Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 timeout 900 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestVB16LinkCycleAppliedTwin|TestB16ProbeNotifyLinkCycleMarksUnpublishedSnapshotApplied' -count=1 -v`. Fixture: `RUN/verify/vb16/probes/vb16_probe_test.go`. Output: `RUN/verify/vb16/probe-b16-02-03.out`. LEGIT twin (#2079 r11: gen 6 published, helper echoes 6): `helperEcho=6 published=6 -> appliedSnapshot=6 PolicyReadConfig==newCfg:true policyCommitter=[6] captureCommitter=[6]`. DEFECT (gen 6 retained unpublished, helper echoes 5): `helperEcho=5 published=5 -> appliedSnapshot=6 PolicyReadConfig==newCfg:true policyCommitter=[6] captureCommitter=[6]`. The reporter's control (status apply only) keeps `appliedSnapshot=5`. Limit: no daemon-level cell was run.

## Acceptance / fix direction
In `notifyLinkCycle`, call `markAppliedSnapshotLocked()` only when the helper holds `m.lastSnapshot` (the predicate above, plus `!applySnapshotOutcomeUnknown`). Otherwise leave the mark to the deferred publish (`process_status.go:336`). Acceptance: The defect arm keeps `appliedSnapshot=5` and fires no committer. The #2079 r11 DeferWorkers cell (published, helper echoes N+1) still records N+1. A daemon cell (deferred same-plan commit + RETH cycle) shows the discharge only after the tick publish, with the deferred-window re-capture taken.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vb16.md)</summary>

The daemon can then discharge the commit's policy-invalidation debt early, which skips the designed re-capture at the real publish boundary.

The protection is commit-time policy session revocation (deleted, modified and default-policy clears) and the IPsec capture authority. The challenged assumption is that `m.lastSnapshot` is always the helper-applied snapshot when NotifyLinkCycle runs. That is true for #2079's DeferWorkers case and false for Compile's pendingXSKStartup branch.
- **Evidence:** All at d1ea69f9aa: `process_linkcycle.go:909` `m.markAppliedSnapshotLocked()` runs unconditionally after the `rebind` request. The comment at `:901-908` justifies it only for DeferWorkers. `applied_nat_view.go:111-132`: the only guard is `m.deferWorkers`, which the daemon clears before NotifyLinkCycle per the comment. The function then sets `appliedSnapshot` from `m.lastSnapshot` and calls both committers. `manager_compile.go:586-590` `pendingXSKStartup := ... publishedSnapshot != 0 && !xskLivenessProven && !xskLivenessFailed`. `:645-697` defers every such commit, same-plan or not: `m.pendingFullSnapshotMetadata = true; m.lastSnapshot = snap`, `SnapshotPublishDeferred`, no publish. `process_linkcycle.go:870` `m.xskLivenessProven = false` on every cycle. Daemon side: `policyInvalidationSnapshotPublished` (`daemon_policy_invalidate_capture.go:1523-1541`) spawns a discharge worker. `dischargePolicyInvalidationAfterPublish` (`:1547-1586`) discharges when `generation >= debt.publishGeneration`. `dischargePolicyInvalidationDebtLocked` clears the debt and plan and marks the digest applied (`:1592-1630`). `capturePolicyInvalidationBeforeDeferredPublish` returns nil when `debt == nil` (`:1473-1476`).
- **Probe:** `GOFLAGS=-p=2 timeout 900 go test ./pkg/dataplane/userspace/ -run 'TestVB16LinkCycleAppliedTwin|TestB16ProbeNotifyLinkCycleMarksUnpublishedSnapshotApplied' -count=1 -v`. Fixture: `RUN/verify/vb16/probes/vb16_probe_test.go`. Output: `RUN/verify/vb16/probe-b16-02-03.out`. LEGIT twin (#2079 r11: gen 6 published, helper echoes 6): `helperEcho=6 published=6 -> appliedSnapshot=6 PolicyReadConfig==newCfg:true policyCommitter=[6] captureCommitter=[6]`. DEFECT (gen 6 retained unpublished, helper echoes 5): `helperEcho=5 published=5 -> appliedSnapshot=6 PolicyReadConfig==newCfg:true policyCommitter=[6] captureCommitter=[6]`. The reporter's control (status apply only) keeps `appliedSnapshot=5`. Limit: no daemon-level cell was run.
- **Trace:** commit C needs a RETH MAC cycle (new RETH, RG or cluster-id change, VF reset), within about 10 s of a helper start or previous cycle, or on an idle link whose probe keeps extending → daemon pre-check sets DeferWorkers (`daemon_apply_dataplane.go:75-115`) → commit-time policy capture and debt → Compile takes the pendingXSKStartup branch (gen N+1 retained, helper still on N) → RETH loop → NotifyLinkCycle → `markAppliedSnapshotLocked` → `appliedSnapshot=N+1`, `policySnapshotCommitter(N+1)` → the discharge worker queues on applySem → after the apply, ordering (a): discharge deletes the commit-time capture and clears the debt and plan, then `completeDeferredSnapshotApply(N+1)` runs → the next tick's pre-publisher sees debt==nil and does no re-capture → N+1 publishes → sessions admitted under the old policy since the capture survive. Plan-changing commits: these restart the helper rather than defer (`manager_compile.go:595-639`), but same-plan commits do defer, so the path remains reachable. Whether ctrl stays off long enough after the rebind to close the admission window: `ctrlEnableAt` is set only on the first prewarm (`helper_status_apply.go:123-141`), so later rebinds re-enable once readiness passes, before or around the next-tick publish. ## #16522 — `applyEditLine` rejects any annotate line containing a `;` byte, including one inside a quoted comment or a quoted value. `annotate` and hierarchical `/* ... */` comments both accept `;`, so the box's own `show | display set` output fails `load… [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary

`applyEditLine` rejects any annotate line containing a `;` byte, including one inside a quoted comment or a quoted value. `annotate` and hierarchical `/* ... */` comments both accept `;`, so the box's own `show | display set` output fails `load set`, and its `show` output, or any Junos file with such a comment, fails `load merge`.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A01-02`
**Severity (source report):** Low. The failure is closed: the load is atomic and refused, and `load override` and HA SyncApply, which parse hierarchically, are unaffected. It does break the documented backup/restore and migration round trip for ordinary comment prose. [reporter: Low-Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (load and restore round trip of the box's own output: R3-A01-02, R3-A01-03, R3-VA01-S1). The defect is real and fail-closed, and it sits on the same restore contract as its cohort.

## Mechanism

A hierarchical comment or an `annotate` command sets `Node.Annotation`. `FormatSet` or `FormatSetForLoadMerge` then emits an annotate line with a quoted `;`. Replay goes through `applyEditLine`, the raw `;` test fires, and the whole load is refused.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`pkg/configstore/store_command.go:757-763` contains `annTrim := strings.TrimSuffix(annLine, ";")` and `if strings.Contains(annTrim, ";") { return fmt.Errorf("invalid annotate command") }`. That check runs on the whole line, including quoted tokens. `Store.AnnotateAsPlantClass` (:406-436) accepts the same text, and the emitters print `annotate <path> "<comment>"` with the `;` inside the quotes.

## Impact

`show | display set > backup` followed by `load set`, and `load merge` of Junos files whose prose comments contain `;`, fail with an error that does not identify the comment. Operators have to edit the comments by hand.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Lex the line, strip one trailing structural `;`, and refuse only a structural `;` that the strict lexer reports (`lexConfigMutationLineStrict15167`-style). The acceptance criterion is that the probe's `;` cells round-trip and the structural-`;` control is still refused.

## Contract (where cited)

## #16523 — `AnnotatePath` resolves its target through the pair-consuming display walker (`navigatePathWidth`). That walker cannot address a node with three or more keys and an odd count, such as `address a1 10.0.0.1/32`. The emitted `annotate ... address a1… [OPEN]

## Summary

`AnnotatePath` resolves its target through the pair-consuming display walker (`navigatePathWidth`). That walker cannot address a node with three or more keys and an odd count, such as `address a1 10.0.0.1/32`. The emitted `annotate ... address a1 10.0.0.1/32 "<comment>"` line therefore fails, which aborts `load set` of `display set` output and `load merge` of a commented file.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A01-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low. The failure is closed (atomic refusal), while `load override` and HA sync are unaffected. It breaks restore and migration for comments on one of the most commonly commented statements. [reporter: Low-Medium]
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (load and restore round trip of the box's own output: R3-A01-02, R3-A01-03, R3-VA01-S1). The root cause and fix differ from R3-A01-02, but the contract and consequence are the same.

## Mechanism

A hierarchical comment or annotate sets the annotation on the 3-key node. `FormatSet` emits the full identity. Replay goes through `ParseAnnotateCommand`, then `AnnotatePath`, then `navigatePath`, and returns `ErrPathNotFound`, which aborts the load.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

In `ast.go:741-764`, `consumed := 2`, and the loop continues only while `i+consumed+1 < len(path)`. For the path `... address a1 10.0.0.1/32` it consumes 2, then descends (`unionChildren`) into the leaf's nil children looking for `10.0.0.1/32`, and returns nil. `ast.go:1029-1039` (`AnnotatePath`) uses `navigatePath` and returns `ErrPathNotFound`. `deactivate` uses a different walker (`setInactiveAtPath`) and round-trips the same path, which the worker's `zz_a01_inactive3_probe_test.go` shows.

## Impact

Restoring a display-set backup, or merging a Junos file with comments on address-book entries, fails with a `path not found` error that does not mention the comment.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Resolve annotate targets by full identity (a `matchNodeKeysFull`-style exact-keys walk), falling back to the display walk only for prefix addressing. The acceptance criterion is that both probe cells round-trip and the #4587 and #15718 tests stay green.

## Contract (where cited)

#15718 states that annotations round-trip through FormatSet, load set and load merge. The `AnnotatePath` doc (ast.go:1014-1027) says multi-key nodes "resolve".

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A01-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A01-03 | Low | AnnotatePath resolves its target through the pair-consuming display walker… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:10: - **R3-A01-03 — COHORT (Low; restore round-trip, distinct fix).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/ast.go:712-770` has a path walker which consumes a two-key chunk then descends; an address-book leaf with keys `address`, name, prefix has no descendants to resolve the last token. `AnnotatePath` uses this walker (`ast.go:1029-1037`), so its own full-identity annotation cannot be restored. **Refutation:** short-form annotation of the named address succeeds, and the repository has a separate exact-key matcher (`ast.go:1041+`); the failure is not universal to addresses or to `deactivate`. **Decisive check:** annotate an odd-arity leaf, export it, reload both formats, and preserve exact target identity.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L29: ### R3-A01-03 — `annotate` cannot address odd-key-count node — **COHORT** - Defect: `pkg/config/ast.go:712ff navigatePathWidth` consumes pairs (`consumed:=2`, loop `i+consumed+1 < len(path)`); `AnnotatePath:1029` uses it, returns `ErrPathNotFound`. 3-key leaf `address a1 10.0.0.1/32` (among most-commented statements) descends into leaf's nil children → emitted full-identity annotate line fails on replay; aborts load set/merge. `deactivate`'s different walker round-trips same path (asymmetry evidence). - Refutation: Fail-closed; name-only interactive `annotate … address a1` works; override/sync unaffected. Bounds to replay-of-own-output + commented Junos files — exactly the #15718 round-trip contract claimed. - Evidence: Walker arithmetic re-read at origin/master; note `matchNodeKeysFull:1155` exists elsewhere — supports fix direction (full-identity walk) and shows walker choice is the defect. Report controls (2-key, 4-key pass; 3-key fails) consistent. - Unresolved: Census of odd-arity addressable nodes beyond address-book (fix completeness), not existence. ### R3-VA01-S1 — load classifier routes hierarchical file to flat replay if any line starts with flat verb — **COHORT** - Defect: `pkg/config/authz_config_load_9892.go:197-198` @origin/master: `ClassifyLoadContent` sets `flat=true` on first `IsFlatLoadLine(TrimSpace(line))`, no brace-depth context. ## #16524 — After an RG failover and failback, a session that DemoteOwnerRGS rewrote to FabricRedirect keeps that redirect after the RG is locally active again, whenever its destination is reached through a gateway route rather than a connected prefix. [OPEN]

## Summary
After an RG failover and failback, a session that DemoteOwnerRGS rewrote to FabricRedirect keeps that redirect after the RG is locally active again, whenever its destination is reached through a gateway route rather than a connected prefix.

**Finding ID:** R3-N07-01
**Severity (source):** High — High — this is HA ownership and recovery. After failback, every surviving session whose destination sits behind a gateway (in practice every Internet-bound flow) has its forward leg sent over the fabric to the peer that no longer owns the RG. The peer-side drop is inferred from source, not executed. [reporter: High]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Any HA deployment that does planned failback, maintenance, `request chassis cluster failover` followed by reset, or a double failover loses the forward leg of every surviving Internet-bound session. Clients retransmit into the blackhole, which keeps the sessions alive. Recovery needs a session clear or new 5-tuples. Only sessions to destinations on connected prefixes recover.

**Contract:** CLAUDE.md "Fabric forwarding … prevents TCP death on VRRP failback". docs/session-sync-architecture.md says a new primary continues forwarding established flows after an RG move. The code's own comment at every call site says "Unknown owner (dest_rg==0) is NOT peer-ownership: keep the candidate (no redirect)". The doc comment of `rehome_or_retain_fabric_redirect_scoped_15958b` says that if the destination's RG is locally active, the candidate wins and the retained marker must not defeat failback.

**Trace:** Config: chassis cluster with a fabric and RG1 owning the WAN RETH, a LAN host with a long-lived TCP session to an Internet address, and a policy permitting lan→wan. Compile and wire: the forwarding snapshot holds the egress RG ownership and the fabric list. Runtime: the RG1 move to node1 publishes the demoted rg_runtime, and DemoteOwnerRGS stores FabricRedirect. Failback publishes RG1 active, and RefreshOwnerRGS finds the stored FabricRedirect. Because `dest_rg = 0`, the owner counts as active, and the fresh candidate is ForwardCandidate on the WAN. But `connected_ifindex = 0`, so the zone-encoded FabricRedirect is stored again. Every later hit in resolve.rs:519-548 makes the same decision. Node1, now standby, receives the packet on the fabric, gets HAInactive, and drops it.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_glue/resolution.rs:729-788` @d1ea69f9aa: `if destination_owner_active { if let Some(target) = target { let connected_ifindex = connected_ifindex_for_target_in_table(..); … if candidate.disposition == ForwardCandidate && connected_ifindex > 0 && candidate.egress_ifindex == connected_ifindex && !egress_is_fabric { return candidate; } // Owner active but … (transient FIB lag): retain the redirect below` … `match super::forwarding::resolve_zone_encoded_fabric_redirect_by_id(forwarding, destination_zone) { Some(current_redirect) => current_redirect,`. `connected_ifindex_for_target_in_table` (`resolution.rs:658-724`) returns 0 for a target outside every connected row and ledger prefix. The callers compute `destination_owner_active = dest_rg == 0 || …`: `session_glue/commands/refresh_owner_rgs.rs:175-198`, `session_glue/commands/demote_owner_rgs.rs:95-117`, `session_glue/resolve.rs:519-548` (every session hit), `session_glue/resolve.rs:772-795` and `shared_ops/reverse_synth.rs:494`. `resolution_target_for_session` (`resolution.rs:3-6`) is `rewrite_dst.unwrap_or(dst_ip)`, the final destination and not the next hop. At 51d355c1d, `refresh_owner_rgs.rs:171` called only `redirect_session_via_fabric_if_needed`. Inference: the peer's fabric-ingress hit takes `decision.resolution = enforced_resolution`, which is HAInactive (`resolve.rs:536-537`).

**Probe:** `flock RUN/locks/cargo.lock timeout 1800 cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp n07_failback` with `RUN/workers/n07/evidence/n07_failback_probe_tests.rs` wired temporarily into session_glue/mod.rs. The test installs a ForwardFlow session lan→wan (RG1), runs handle_demote_owner_rgs with RG1 inactive, then handle_refresh_owner_rgs with RG1 active. Control `n07_failback_connected_destination_rehomes_control` (dst 172.16.50.200, connected /24): ok. It shows FabricRedirect after the demote and ForwardCandidate on egress 12 after the refresh. Defect `n07_failback_routed_destination_rehomes` (dst 8.8.8.8 via the default gateway): FAILED with `ForwardingResolution { disposition: FabricRedirect, … egress_ifindex: 21, tx_ifindex: 21, next_hop: Some(10.99.13.2) … }`. Output: `RUN/verify/vn07/n07_failback.out`. Limits: this is component-level. The packet-hit path at resolve.rs:539 calls the same helper with the same inputs (static), and the peer drop was not executed.

## Acceptance / fix direction
When the destination owner is active and the fresh candidate is a non-fabric, locally owned ForwardCandidate, re-home whenever `dest_rg == 0`. Apply the connected-interface equality test only when the target lies in a connected prefix (`connected_ifindex > 0`). Do this in all five callers through the shared helper. Acceptance: the routed cell turns green, the connected control stays green, the #15958b split-RG and transient-mixed-state cells stay green, and a lab failover and failback with a routed destination (for example via a gateway route on the loss cluster) keeps a TCP stream alive with returning-primary fabric_redirect TX at 0.
