## #16525 — When current's committed predecessor is no longer restorable, defaultRollbackTarget falls back to the newest-committed version, so a bare `xpfd upgrade --rollback` puts the node on a newer, operator-rejected release, restores an... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
When current's committed predecessor is no longer restorable, defaultRollbackTarget falls back to the newest-committed version, so a bare `xpfd upgrade --rollback` puts the node on a newer, operator-rejected release, restores an older-era DB snapshot, and reports `rollback complete` (#10851 residual)

**Finding ID:** R3-B17-01
**Severity (source):** Medium — the incident-recovery verb lands on a release the operator rolled away from, and does so with a cut-boundary DB from an earlier era. The live DB is retained at `<ConfigDBDir>.old` (operator path), so nothing is destroyed, and `--target` recovers. The result is a bounded but real operator-contract failure during an incident [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Standalone appliances where the operator rolls back more than once after a bad release are affected. The node ends on the rejected build with an old-era config, and the success message hides it. The condition lasts until someone notices and runs `--target`.

**Contract:** #10851 acceptance: "Default = last committed predecessor ... failed-cut dirs stamped non-committed and excluded". cmd/xpfd/upgrade.go:303 says the verb will "rollback the current runtime to a retained compatible version". The `--target` help at :305 ("default: newest restorable non-current version") is the pre-#10851 wording, and it literally describes the faulty fallback.

**Trace:** cuts 1->2->3->4 -> gc at the 4.0.0 COMMIT removes 1.0.0 -> `xpfd upgrade --rollback` (4->3, predecessor present) -> again (3->2) -> again: predecessor 1.0.0 is missing -> fallback committed[0]=4.0.0 -> STOP, restoreDBSnapshotRetainOld(.2.0.0.dbsnap), flip to 4.0.0, START, health OK -> `rollback complete`.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/upgrade/rollback.go:296 `if present && (stamp == nil || !stamp.Committed) { continue }` is the only exclusion. :329-341 takes the predecessor branch only when `byName[currentStamp.Predecessor]` exists, and otherwise logs `WARN committed predecessor ... is not a restorable candidate`. :342-345 `if len(committed) > 0 { ... return committed[0].name, nil }` returns the newest CommittedAtUnixNano, with no older-than-current predicate. :162 prepareRollback refuses only `to == from`. :169 the snapshot is always `.<from>.dbsnap`. flip.go gc keeps protected target/previous/current, then the newest by commit time (`kept < retainVersions`).

**Probe:** RUN/verify/vb17/probes/probe_vb17_bare_chain_test.go (uses the reporter's probeB17History helper) plus RUN/workers/b17/evidence/probe_b17_rollback_forward_test.go. Output in RUN/verify/vb17/probes/rollback.out: `bare rollback chain: [4.0.0 3.0.0 2.0.0 4.0.0]`, `DEFECT: bare rollback step 3 moved FORWARD 2.0.0 -> 4.0.0`, log `rollback restored config DB from .../.2.0.0.dbsnap`. Positive control (depth 3, predecessor retained): `control chain: [3.0.0 2.0.0 1.0.0]` PASS. Limit: fake systemd. Selection is pure filesystem logic, so this does not affect the result.

## Acceptance / fix direction
when the predecessor is missing, refuse and require `--target`, or restrict fallback candidates to versions whose commit time is earlier than current's. Update the stale `--target` help. Acceptance: the chain probe never selects a version newer than current (refusal is acceptable), and the control still yields 3->2->1.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vb17.md)</summary>

### R3-B17-01 — When the committed predecessor has been GC'd, a bare `xpfd upgrade --rollback` moves FORWARD to the newest committed version
- **Finding ID:** R3-B17-01
- **Title:** When current's committed predecessor is no longer restorable, defaultRollbackTarget falls back to the newest-committed version, so a bare `xpfd upgrade --rollback` puts the node on a newer, operator-rejected release, restores an older-era DB snapshot, and reports `rollback complete` (#10851 residual)
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker b17 (A10 upgrade/release engineer, second pass); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vb17
- **Severity:** Medium — the incident-recovery verb lands on a release the operator rolled away from, and does so with a cut-boundary DB from an earlier era. The live DB is retained at `<ConfigDBDir>.old` (operator path), so nothing is destroyed, and `--target` recovers. The result is a bounded but real operator-contract failure during an incident [reporter: Medium]
- **Confidence:** High — executed against the real Runner with the package fake system. The only assumption is that GC retention N=3 removes the predecessor, and the probe takes that path itself.
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — `go test ./pkg/upgrade/ -run 'TestProbeVB17_|TestProbeB17_'` drives real cuts, GC, RollbackTo and defaultRollbackTarget.
- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — a reachable sequence of bare rollbacks (4->3->2->4) moves forward, which violates the #10851 acceptance. No guard or test covers this.
- **Contract:** #10851 acceptance: "Default = last committed predecessor ... failed-cut dirs stamped non-committed and excluded". cmd/xpfd/upgrade.go:303 says the verb will "rollback the current runtime to a retained compatible version". The `--target` help at :305 ("default: newest restorable non-current version") is the pre-#10851 wording, and it literally describes the faulty fallback.
- **Adversarial analysis:** The protection owed is that rollback moves to a known-good OLDER runtime. The actor is the operator, as root, repeating the documented verb after a bad release. No adversary is needed; this is a fault-plus-procedure defect. The assumption challenged: "the predecessor is always retained". GC ranks by commit time and keeps target, previous and current plus the newest, so a two-step rollback walks past the retention window.
- **Evidence:** pkg/upgrade/rollback.go:296 `if present && (stamp == nil || !stamp.Committed) { continue }` is the only exclusion. :329-341 takes the predecessor branch only when `byName[currentStamp.Predecessor]` exists, and otherwise logs `WARN committed predecessor ... is not a restorable candidate`. :342-345 `if len(committed) > 0 { ... return committed[0].name, nil }` returns the newest CommittedAtUnixNano, with no older-than-current predicate. :162 prepareRollback refuses only `to == from`. :169 the snapshot is always `.<from>.dbsnap`. flip.go gc keeps protected target/previous/current, then the newest by commit time (`kept < retainVersions`).
- **Probe:** RUN/verify/vb17/probes/probe_vb17_bare_chain_test.go (uses the reporter's probeB17History helper) plus RUN/workers/b17/evidence/probe_b17_rollback_forward_test.go. Output in RUN/verify/vb17/probes/rollback.out: `bare rollback chain: [4.0.0 3.0.0 2.0.0 4.0.0]`, `DEFECT: bare rollback step 3 moved FORWARD 2.0.0 -> 4.0.0`, log `rollback restored config DB from .../.2.0.0.dbsnap`. Positive control (depth 3, predecessor retained): `control chain: [3.0.0 2.0.0 1.0.0]` PASS. Limit: fake systemd. Selection is pure filesystem logic, so this does not affect the result.
- **Trace:** cuts 1->2->3->4 -> gc at the 4.0.0 COMMIT removes 1.0.0 -> `xpfd upgrade --rollback` (4->3, predecessor present) -> again (3->2) -> again: predecessor 1.0.0 is missing -> fallback committed[0]=4.0.0 -> STOP, restoreDBSnapshotRetainOld(.2.0.0.dbsnap), flip to 4.0.0, START, health OK -> `rollback complete`.
- **Refutation attempt:** I looked for an older-than or not-rolled-from predicate in prepareRollback, validateRollbackPlan and executeRollback, and found none. I looked for a test pinning the fallback: #14720/#15280/#10851-era tests assert only the predecessor-present case. I checked whether operator rollback demotes the version it rolls away from: it does not touch stamps. Correction to the reporter: the live DB is retained at `.old` on this path. Which snapshot is restored is A56-02's (round 2) domain. This entry claims target selection only.
- **HPC/invariant check:** not applicable — control-plane tooling with no hot path. The invariant is version ordering across retention and GC.

## #16526 — The under-load cookie-reply token bucket (`source_reply_allowed`) is keyed on the unauthenticated datagram source IP. A spoofer who knows the responder public key sends valid-MAC1 initiations with a victim peer's addr... [CLOSED] (closed 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The under-load cookie-reply token bucket (`source_reply_allowed`) is keyed on the unauthenticated datagram source IP. A spoofer who knows the responder public key sends valid-MAC1 initiations with a victim peer's address (any port, or any address in the victim's IPv6 /64) and spends the victim's reply budget, so the victim's own initiations are dropped silently without a cookie. Both reference implementations reply without a limit and rate-limit only MAC2-valid packets.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — an unauthenticated remote attacker who can spoof source addresses can block victim-initiated handshakes for the length of the flood. That holds even at modest rates: about 2 % per-attempt success at 1 kpps of 148-byte frames with jittered arrival, and 0 % in a deterministic simulation. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact. The impact is bounded because xpf-initiated handshakes toward the victim still complete: type-2 responses are not under-load gated, and xpf initiates on NoSession, rekey, dead-peer and keepalive triggers. The outage therefore lands on peers whose traffic depends on their own initiation, such as roaming or remote-access clients with no xpf-side egress or persistent keepalive toward them. This is demonstrated at the classifier, with the end-to-end outage inferred. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A69-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va69.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
The mechanism meant to keep legitimate peers serviceable during a handshake flood becomes a cheap, targeted lock-out: one spoofer can name every configured peer's address at once, at ~1 kpps per victim. It hits roaming and remote-access peers hardest, because they depend on their own initiations. Recovery is automatic once the flood stops.

**Contract:** The module's own contract (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/cookie.rs:1-16`): under load a valid-MAC1 initiation gets a cookie reply bound to its real source, so "only a peer that actually received the reply at that source can echo a valid MAC2". Reference behaviour, read from source: wireguard-go `device/receive.go:325-338` (local module v0.0.0-20260522210424): `if !device.cookieChecker.CheckMAC2(...) { device.SendHandshakeCookie(&elem); goto skip }`, then `device.rate.limiter.Allow(...)`. `SendHandshakeCookie` (`send.go:177-193`) has no limiter. Linux `drivers/net/wireguard/cookie.c` `wg_cookie_validate_packet`: `wg_ratelimiter_allow` runs only after the MAC2 compare. `receive.c:126-139` sets `packet_needs_cookie` for VALID_MAC_BUT_NO_COOKIE under load and sends the cookie with no limiter. In both references the only per-source limit applies to MAC2-valid packets, a key the attacker cannot forge.

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/wg/engine.rs:678` @d1ea69f9aa: `let under_load = self.cookie.note_initiation(now_ns);` counts every type-1 from any source. `engine.rs:690-692`: the MAC1 check uses the precomputed public-key-derived key, which forged packets pass. `engine.rs:697-704`: a MAC2-valid packet goes to `source_handshake_allowed`, which is fine because MAC2 binds IP:port. `engine.rs:705-711`: "Per-source limiting is the only cookie-reply rate gate ... `if !self.cookie.source_reply_allowed(from.ip(), now_ns) { ... hs_cookie_reply_budget_drops; return InitiationAction::Drop; }`". `cookie.rs:448-449`: `let src_ip = source_bucket_key(src_ip);`. `cookie.rs:245-257`: v4 keeps the /32, v6 zeroes `octets[8..]`, and the port is never part of the key. `cookie.rs:114,118`: 20/s and burst 5. `coordinator/wg_control/dispatch.rs:125-130`: the `Drop` arm returns `Unauthenticated` with no reply. Recovery path: the `WG_TYPE_RESPONSE` arm (`dispatch.rs:174`) calls `consume_response` with no under-load gate, and `coordinator/wg_control/attempt.rs:192-217` starts an xpf-initiated attempt on rekey, NoSession, DeadPeer or KeepaliveNoSession when an effective endpoint exists.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — a cargo unit probe drove `WgEngine::classify_initiation` through a 60 s simulated 1 kpps spoofed flood with defect and control arms. STATIC — the victim-side timers and the xpf-initiated recovery path.

## Ledger validation (excerpt)

| R3-A70-03 explicit CoS buffer/burst <96k floored to 96k | MATERIAL | Medium |
| R3-A70-01 shared_exact BDP floor class-rate/local-N | MATERIAL | Low |

Executed probe: v4 spoof 60k pkts/60s → victim 434 tries, 0 cookies; v6 same-/64 arm 0; other-IP control 434/434. Both references (wireguard-go receive.go, Linux cookie.c — read in part) reply unthrottled and rate-limit only MAC2-valid packets; reply 64B < initiation 148B so unlimited reply is not amplification.
- Refutation: needs off-path source spoofing — on BCP38-filtered paths unreachable, and victim must know responder pubkey (public by design) + victim IP. That narrows deployment blast radius but does not refute: WG's threat model explicitly assumes spoofable unauthenticated initiations (that is what MAC1/MAC2 exist for), and charging a victim's budget on unauthenticated source identity is the design error. xpf-initiated recovery (type-2 ungated) correctly narrows claim to victim-initiated handshakes (roaming clients) — part's narrowing accepted, Medium not High.
- Unresolved: none. Fix (reply unthrottled, keep MAC2 bucket) matches references.

## #16527 — `nodesEqual` and `alignSiblings` compare nodes by `KeyPath()`, which is the keys joined with spaces. A `change-configuration commands` entry that changes from two quoted members (`"set" "system host-name pwned"`, which the event engine rejects)… [OPEN]

## Summary

`nodesEqual` and `alignSiblings` compare nodes by `KeyPath()`, which is the keys joined with spaces. A `change-configuration commands` entry that changes from two quoted members (`"set" "system host-name pwned"`, which the event engine rejects) to one bare command (`set system host-name pwned`, which it applies) is therefore reported as `[no changes]` on both the plain and the redacted compare.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A01-04`
**Severity (source report):** Low. This is a lie on the operator review surface: the diff a reviewer reads before commit hides the arming of an automated configuration change that runs with the policy's plant-class authority. It is bounded. The author already holds config authority, `CommitDiffSummary` still reports "2 statement…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL. The compare surface misses a semantic difference that the compiler and the executor both act on, and the probe demonstrates it at the store level.

## Mechanism

The candidate tree has a changed key grouping. `FormatCompare` and `diffNodes` decide `nodesEqual` is true, so nothing is printed. On commit, the compile produces a different `ThenCommands`, the event engine's `classifyPlan` accepts the batch, and the command is applied when the event fires.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`ast.go:249-251` defines `KeyPath()` as `strings.Join(n.Keys, " ")`. `ast_format.go:958-975` (`nodesEqual`) returns false on a KeyPath mismatch and otherwise compares only IsLeaf, Inactive, Annotation and children. It never looks at KeysQuoted, KeysBracketed or the key count. `alignSiblings` (around :654 and :659) pairs siblings by `KeyPath()`. `compiler_services.go:2848-2861` (`eventMultiWordLeafValues`) returns per-member tokens when key 0 is quoted and joins them otherwise. `pkg/eventengine/evaluate.go:38-76` (`classifyPlan`) sends a bare `set` member, which lacks the `"set "` prefix, to the default arm, and the whole batch is rejected.

## Impact

A reviewer who approves by `show | compare` sees nothing while the commit arms an automated configuration change. HA sync and the archives then carry it. Recovery requires noticing the change some other way.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `nodesEqual` and `alignSiblings`, compare key count plus per-key `KeyQuoted(i)` and `KeyBracketed(i)`, for example through `QuotedKeyPath()` or a provenance-aware identity. Render both sides with `QuotedKeyPath` so the difference is visible. The acceptance criterion is that the probe's compare is non-empty, and all-bare trees produce unchanged output because nil provenance reads as all-false.

## Contract (where cited)

#15168 and #15758 made compare a faithful, content-aware diff ("sibling order is semantic"). `Node.KeysQuoted` (ast.go:77-101) is documented as "the one bit about a key that its TEXT cannot carry", and quote provenance decides event-command grouping (#6673).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A01-04` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A01-04 | Low | nodesEqual and alignSiblings compare nodes by KeyPath(), which is the keys joined with… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:8: - **R3-A01-04 — MATERIAL (Low).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/ast.go:247-266` joins key strings for `KeyPath`; `pkg/config/ast_format.go:647-661,958-975` aligns and compares by that joined string without key grouping/quote provenance. Yet `pkg/config/compiler_services.go:2842-2859` expressly uses `KeysQuoted` to separate event `change-configuration commands`, so a changed executable command can display as `[no changes]`; old report probes also found this in redacted compare. **Refutation:** a committed command requires already-authorized configuration mutation and `CommitDiffSummary` in the old probe still counted two changed statements; neither stealth privilege escalation nor totally invisible commit is established. **Decisive check:** current compare/compilation regression with two quoted command members versus one bare multiword command, including both display variants and event-plan classification.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L17: ### R3-A01-04 — `show | compare` ignores token grouping/quote provenance — **MATERIAL (Low)** - Defect: `pkg/config/ast_format.go:958ff nodesEqual` @origin/master compares `KeyPath()` (= `strings.Join(Keys," ")`, `ast.go:249ff`), IsLeaf, Inactive, Annotation, children — never `KeysQuoted`/`KeysBracketed`/key-count. `alignSiblings:647` pairs by KeyPath. Event-options grouping is provenance-sensitive (compiler `eventMultiWordLeafValues`, eventengine `classifyPlan` rejects bare `set` member), so `"set" "system host-name pwned"` (inert) → `set system host-name pwned` (applicable) renders `[no changes]` on plain+redacted compare. - Refutation: Author already holds config authority; `CommitDiffSummary` counts "2 changed"; policy fires only on event; most grouping changes are inert — scope correctly narrowed to grouping-sensitive consumers. This caps severity, not existence: the review-before-commit surface is the stated contract (#15168/#15758 faithful diff). - Evidence: `nodesEqual` body re-read at origin/master (no provenance check). Report store-level probe (`ShowCompare="[no changes]"`, summary counts change, control shows diff) consistent with code. - Unresolved: Whether any other provenance-sensitive consumer (beyond event-options) is compare-hidden — sweep of `KeysQuoted` consumers vs compare; widens/narrows blast radius only. ### R3-A01-02 — replay rejects `annotate` line containing `;` even quoted — **COHORT** - Defect: `pkg/configstore/store_command.go:759-763` @origin/m

## #16529 — A non-operator ROLLINGBACK journal preserved by the #14721 health gate (old daemon running) is resumed by the next `xpfd upgrade`. The resume STOPs the healthy daemon, re-restores the cut-boundary snapshot, and removes... [OPEN]

## Summary
A non-operator ROLLINGBACK journal preserved by the #14721 health gate (old daemon running) is resumed by the next `xpfd upgrade`. The resume STOPs the healthy daemon, re-restores the cut-boundary snapshot, and removes `<ConfigDBDir>.old`, so config commits made after the rollback are destroyed with no copy

**Finding ID:** R3-B17-02
**Severity (source):** Medium — this is durable config-integrity loss: operator policy, NAT or interface commits are irrecoverably erased, and so is the configstore history in the same directory. The prerequisite is a double failure: the target is unhealthy AND the rollback's helper is not confirmed within StartHealthDeadline. That bounds it below High [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Standalone nodes after a bad upgrade whose rollback helper was slow are affected. A later routine re-run or package upgrade silently erases the fixes made in the meantime, including commit history. Recovery is only from external backups.

**Contract:** docs/in-place-upgrade.md:62 says re-running `xpfd upgrade` "resumes" and is idempotent. cutover.go:271-275 states the operator path uses retained-DB semantics "so a retry cannot destroy ConfigDBDir+".old"". #6556 and #10307 treat a rollback that silently reverts commits made in a window as a defect.

**Trace:** 1.0.0 live -> cut 2.0.0 -> START health fails -> rollback(): restore .2.0.0.dbsnap, flip 1.0.0, START -> HelperHealthy(1.0.0) times out -> journal preserved at ROLLINGBACK, daemon running -> operator commits -> `xpfd upgrade` (operator, or the next apt postinst cut) -> cutover.go:276 resume -> STOP -> restoreDBSnapshot over the live DB -> `.old` removed -> START -> healthy -> clearJournal.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
pkg/upgrade/flip.go:405-421: `j.State = StateRollingBack; saveJournal`, StopUnit, then `if j.AdvancedStateFloor && j.DBSnapshotPath != "" { r.restoreDBSnapshot(...) }` with no restored bit. :438-440: a HelperHealthy failure returns "rollback journal is preserved for operator recovery" after StartUnit. In restoreDBSnapshotWithRetention(retainOld=false), `_ = os.RemoveAll(old)` before the swap (:595) and after it (:609-610), and the byte-identity skip runs only `if retainOld`. cutover.go:276-305: a ROLLINGBACK resume runs first, and non-operator journals go to `r.rollback(j)`. rollback.go:238-243: RollbackDBRestored exists only on the operator path. debian/xpf.postinst:539 `re-run: xpfd upgrade`.

**Probe:** RUN/workers/b17/evidence/probe_b17_rollback_rerestore_test.go, re-run by vb17, output in RUN/verify/vb17/probes/rollback.out. Defect: `calls: [stop dropin daemon-reload start health:1.0.0]`, `live after re-run: "...{}"; .old present=false`, `DEFECT: post-rollback operator commit destroyed`, `re-run STOPPED the already-running rolled-back daemon`. Positive control (rollback healthy the first time, journal cleared): commit kept, PASS. Limits: the operator commit is modelled as a direct active.json write. The restore replaces the whole directory, so the result holds for real configstore writes. systemd is faked.

## Acceptance / fix direction
persist a restored bit for auto-rollback before the swap and skip the restore on resume, or use restoreDBSnapshotRetainOld with a byte-identity check. When the journal is preserved while the daemon is running, either clear AdvancedStateFloor or require an explicit operator acknowledgement. Acceptance: in the defect cell the commit survives in the live DB or in `.old`, and a healthy daemon is not stopped. The control is unchanged.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vb17.md)</summary>

Positive control (rollback healthy the first time, journal cleared): commit kept, PASS. Limits: the operator commit is modelled as a direct active.json write. The restore replaces the whole directory, so the result holds for real configstore writes. systemd is faked.
- **Trace:** 1.0.0 live -> cut 2.0.0 -> START health fails -> rollback(): restore .2.0.0.dbsnap, flip 1.0.0, START -> HelperHealthy(1.0.0) times out -> journal preserved at ROLLINGBACK, daemon running -> operator commits -> `xpfd upgrade` (operator, or the next apt postinst cut) -> cutover.go:276 resume -> STOP -> restoreDBSnapshot over the live DB -> `.old` removed -> START -> healthy -> clearJournal.

The recovery branch of the restore fires only when the live dir is ABSENT. #12174's fix (a632bf7065) re-snapshots at a STOPPED resume, not a ROLLINGBACK one. The reporter's claim stands as stated.

## #16530 — `ASPathDef.RegexUnquotedBracket` is derived only from the bracket provenance persisted in the JSON DB. `ConfigTree.Format()`, which produces the HA config-sync payload and the rollback slots, renders the keys without `[ ]`, so after… [OPEN]

## Summary

`ASPathDef.RegexUnquotedBracket` is derived only from the bracket provenance persisted in the JSON DB. `ConfigTree.Format()`, which produces the HA config-sync payload and the rollback slots, renders the keys without `[ ]`, so after `Format`→`Parse` the flag is false. The peer, or a `rollback N`, then strict-accepts and renders the mangled regex that the primary omits.

**Finding ID:** `R3-A01-05`
**Severity (source report):** Low. The reach is narrow. An active tree carries the flag only if it was loaded from a JSON DB written by a binary between 422b43908c (#6668) and 15be546a1b (#9881). The next strict commit on the primary refuses the flagged node anyway. Within that reach, the two HA nodes can run different BGP as-pa…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (provenance lost across `Format()` text surfaces). The loss is real and bounded, and it reaches only grandfathered state.

## Mechanism

The flagged node is loaded from a pre-#9881 JSON DB. On the primary, a lenient compile omits the as-path list. The primary sends Format text to the peer, which runs `SyncApply`, parses with no flag, and renders the as-path. `rollback N` follows the same text path.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

`ast.go:257-268` (`QuotedKeyPath`) never renders `[ ]` for a leaf. The HA payload is `ShowActive()` → `Format()`, which the peer re-parses with `config.NewParser` (store.go:1117). Rollback slots are Format text, re-parsed at store_commit.go:1882. SyncApply's digest equivalence compares Format text, which is identical on both sides.

## Impact

On an upgraded pair that carries such an as-path, HA nodes can disagree on BGP import/export filtering until the next successful strict commit forces the operator to quote the regex.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Have `Format()` keep `[ ... ]` on leaves that carry bracket or gap-loss provenance, as `FormatSetForLoadMerge` already does. Alternatively, refuse or quarantine flagged as-paths on the sync and rollback paths. The acceptance criterion is that the probe's flag survives `Format`→`Parse`.

## Contract (where cited)

`types_routing.go:26-36` says "the FRR renderer omits it on the lenient path" and that the strict gate rejects it. Tolerant SyncApply exists so the peer runs the same config as the primary.

## Validation provenance

## #16531 — Two WireGuard tunnels on one listen-port (default instance, or default plus one VRF) commit with no diagnostic. At runtime each tunnel binds its own `[::]:port` socket with no SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT, so whichever t... [OPEN]

## Summary
Two WireGuard tunnels on one listen-port (default instance, or default plus one VRF) commit with no diagnostic. At runtime each tunnel binds its own `[::]:port` socket with no SO_REUSEADDR/SO_REUSEPORT, so whichever tunnel spawns second fails with EADDRINUSE, its control thread exits and respawns every 3 s, and that tunnel never completes a handshake.

**Severity (source report):** Medium — Medium — an accepted commit leaves a configured tunnel permanently down: no handshake, no transit, no host traffic. The only signal is a repeating `wg_bind_listen_port:<port>:...EADDRINUSE` exception and journal line. There is no isolation loss and no effect on the surviving tunnel. The trigger is operator-authored, but the code base treats it as a supported shape (#14326/#15123 same-port selection). The outage is demonstrated at the commit and socket layers. The helper end to end was not run. [reporter: Medium]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A69-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va69.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
An operator following the shape the code and docs present (several tunnels on 51820, #14326/#15123) gets a tunnel that is dead from the moment of commit, with no commit-time error. Spawn order decides which tunnel dies, so it can change across a helper restart, moving the outage to the other tunnel. Recovery needs journal diagnosis and a port renumber.

**Contract:** A committed tunnel must either work or be refused at commit. The project has treated "validated at commit, tunnel permanently dead, no signal" as a defect (#3863 class; GRE's identical-outer analogue is hard-rejected by the #10654 strict gate). The code base presents same-port WireGuard tunnels as a supported runtime shape: `wg/decap.rs:230-252` (#14326: "`(dst_port, transport_instance)` does not identify a listener when several tunnels share a port", plus #15123 two-pass selection), and `docs/wireguard-interop.md:1032` ("Two WG tunnels that SHARE one listen port contribute one set entry and draw no warning").

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/tunnel_supervision.rs` ~1051-1161 @d1ea69f9aa: one `wg_control_loop` per endpoint, with `listen_port = endpoint.wg_listen_port` and `outer_bind_device = wg_outer_bind_device_for_transport_table(&endpoint.transport_table)`. `coordinator/wg_control/sock.rs:212-221` returns `None` for `inet.0`/`inet6.0` and `vrf-<ri>` otherwise. `sock.rs:159-171`: `bind_dual_stack_v6` first; `Err(V6BindError::Fatal(_err)) if bind_device.is_none() => bind_v4(...)`. `sock.rs:282-335` sets only `IPV6_V6ONLY=0`, `SO_BINDTODEVICE` and pktinfo, then `bind([::]:port)`; there is no reuse option anywhere in the module (grep). `coordinator/wg_control/mod.rs:203-221`: on bind Err it records `wg_bind_listen_port:{listen_port}:device=...`, eprints "WG control thread exiting" and `return`s. `tunnel_supervision.rs:19` `WG_SPAWN_BACKOFF_NS = 3_000_000_000` gates the respawn. The code authors acknowledge the collision in comments only: `pkg/config/compiler_validate_wireguard_multiport.go:145-149` ("they collide on the kernel UDP bind instead (bind_wg_socket sets no SO_REUSEPORT), which is a different failure and not this gate's subject") and `pkg/config/wireguard_multiport_warning_1434_test.go:90-95`. The #10654 duplicate-outer gate explicitly skips WireGuard (`compiler_validate_tunnel_gre_dup_10654_test.go:115-123`, arm (h)). Inference (static): initiations from the dead tunnel's peers reach the surviving socket, and MAC1 keyed on the surviving engine's key rejects them (`wg/engine.rs:690-692`).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — strict `CompileConfig` probe with shared-port, distinct-port and malformed-key arms. A socket probe mirroring `bind_dual_stack_v6` plus the `bind_v4` fallback, run under `unshare -Urn` with real VRF devices. STATIC — the helper spawn/respawn loop and the MAC1 mismatch on the surviving socket.

## #16532 — The LocalDelivery session-miss install has no pressure-shed preflight. Since #15951 made refusal fail closed, a transit SYN flood that holds a worker's table at its cap drops every new host-bound TCP SYN or SYN|ACK and every UDP first pa... [OPEN]

## Summary
The LocalDelivery session-miss install has no pressure-shed preflight. Since #15951 made refusal fail closed, a transit SYN flood that holds a worker's table at its cap drops every new host-bound TCP SYN or SYN|ACK and every UDP first packet. On the same table a transit initial SYN would be admitted by shedding an embryo.

**Finding ID:** R3-N07-02
**Severity (source):** Medium — Medium — this is a remotely inducible denial of new control-plane and management sessions (BGP, SSH, IKE, DNAT-to-self, and the inbound SYN|ACK of firewall-originated TCP) on the saturated workers for as long as the flood lasts. It does not bypass enforcement, established cached host sessions are unaffected, and the plane recovers when the flood stops. [reporter: Medium]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A remote unauthenticated flood through any allowed transit policy can stop BGP re-establishment, new SSH management sessions, IKE initiations and DNAT-to-self services on the affected workers, without touching host-inbound policy. Before #15951 these packets were delivered (fail-open). Now they are dropped while transit traffic still gets in.

**Contract:** The #10890 contract (`session/install.rs:281-286`): at high occupancy, reclaim handshake-incomplete local TCP sessions before refusing an initial SYN, and never evict established sessions. #15951 (docs/log/15951.md) intended "count the refusal and recycle" in place of sessionless delivery. It did not intend host-plane admission to be weaker than transit admission.

**Trace:** Config: any permit policy into a zone without syn-cookie, and host-inbound services or DNAT-to-self allowed. Runtime: flood SYNs install pairs until `can_admit` fails, then each new flood SYN sheds one embryo pair and installs one, so the table stays at or near the cap. A host-bound SYN (BGP, SSH or DNAT-to-self) goes LocalMiss → capacity "true" → install refused → `admission_refused` → recycled. A UDP first packet (IKE or DNS reply) is refused the same way, and so is the SYN|ACK of the firewall's own outbound TCP.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:5953-5961` @d1ea69f9aa: `let local_session_capacity_available = if let Some(reuse_key) = owner_syn_reuse_key.as_ref() { sessions.can_admit_after_closing_tcp_pair_for_syn(..) } else { true };`. There is no shed. `mod.rs:6014-6031` installs through `install_helper_local_session_on_miss` (`forwarding/local_delivery.rs:94-104`), which reaches `session/install.rs:538-545` `if self.len().saturating_add(self.reserved_session_slots) >= self.max_sessions { self.create_drops += 1; return false; }`. On refusal, `mod.rs:6133-6144` runs `sessions.note_admission_refused(); … binding.scratch.scratch_recycle.push(desc.addr); continue;`. The transit sibling at `mod.rs:6763-6790` runs `if needed_sessions == 0 || reuse_fits { … } else { sessions.can_admit_new_syn(needed_sessions, meta.protocol, meta.tcp_flags) }`. The caching predicate `forwarding/local_delivery.rs:20-52` caches all non-TCP traffic and TCP SYN or SYN|ACK, so all of these reach the refusing install.

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_localmiss_probe_tests.rs`, wired temporarily, run with `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vn07_localmiss -- --nocapture`. It uses the same DNAT-to-self fixture as tests_host_inbound_15951 (wan 198.51.100.10 → 203.0.113.9:443 → 10.0.61.1:8080) and a table capped at 16, filled with local ForwardFlow TCP-SYN embryos. Control `vn07_localmiss_one_free_slot_delivers_control` (15 embryos) printed `one-free: local=1 create=1 refused=0` and passed. Defect `vn07_localmiss_full_of_sheddable_embryos_refuses_host_syn` (16 embryos) printed `full: host local=0 create=0 refused=1 | transit-shaped can_admit_new_syn(2)=true shed=2` and failed. Output: `RUN/verify/vn07/vn07_localmiss.out`. n07's probe also failed with refused=1 (`RUN/verify/vn07/n07_localmiss.out`). Limits: the transit admission is shown at the `can_admit_new_syn` level, not by a transit frame through the poll path. That the transit call site calls it is static.

## Acceptance / fix direction
On the LocalMiss arm, run `can_admit_new_syn` for initial SYNs with the same NAT, BPF and shared-row release sequence as the transit site, and consider a small reserved host-local headroom for non-TCP and SYN|ACK. Only then fail closed. Acceptance: the vn07 defect cell turns green, the one-free-slot control and the #15951 cap-0 cells stay green, and a shed caused by a host SYN releases NAT holds exactly as the transit shed does.

## Full validated claim

The caching predicate `forwarding/local_delivery.rs:20-52` caches all non-TCP traffic and TCP SYN or SYN|ACK, so all of these reach the refusing install.
- **Probe:** `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_localmiss_probe_tests.rs`, wired temporarily, run with `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vn07_localmiss -- --nocapture`. It uses the same DNAT-to-self fixture as tests_host_inbound_15951 (wan 198.51.100.10 → 203.0.113.9:443 → 10.0.61.1:8080) and a table capped at 16, filled with local ForwardFlow TCP-SYN embryos. Control `vn07_localmiss_one_free_slot_delivers_control` (15 embryos) printed `one-free: local=1 create=1 refused=0` and passed. Defect `vn07_localmiss_full_of_sheddable_embryos_refuses_host_syn` (16 embryos) printed `full: host local=0 create=0 refused=1 | transit-shaped can_admit_new_syn(2)=true shed=2` and failed. Output: `RUN/verify/vn07/vn07_localmiss.out`. n07's probe also failed with refused=1 (`RUN/verify/vn07/n07_localmiss.out`). Limits: the transit admission is shown at the `can_admit_new_syn` level, not by a transit frame through the poll path. That the transit call site calls it is static.
- **Trace:** Config: any permit policy into a zone without syn-cookie, and host-inbound services or DNAT-to-self allowed. Runtime: flood SYNs install pairs until `can_admit` fails, then each new flood SYN sheds one embryo pair and installs one, so the table stays at or near the cap. A host-bound SYN (BGP, SSH or DNAT-to-self) goes LocalMiss → capacity "true" → install refused → `admission_refused` → recycled. A UDP first packet (IKE or DNS reply) is refused the same way, and so is the SYN|ACK of the firewall's own outbound TCP.
- **Refutation attempt:** I checked the following. (1) Under shed-and-replace, does the flood keep the table below the cap? No: the transit path sheds only after `can_admit` fails, so occupancy stays at max (or max-1, depending on install-group parity; a single 1-slot install puts it back at max). (2) `reserved_session_slots` is an IPsec reservation, not host headroom. (3) The syn-cookie screen avoids the condition only where the operator enabled it. (4) The #15951 tests cover only cap-0. (5) The #15951 log calls drops under pressure intended, but never considers shedding. The reporter's positive control did not run the same path, so I replaced it with a same-path one-free-slot control. The claim held. I narrowed it: UDP host traffic is also refused at a full table, but transit UDP is refused as well, so the asymmetry is TCP-initial-SYN only, while the outage covers all host-bound first packets.
- **HPC/invariant check:** Admission accounting: the fix must reuse the existing #12862 tuple-gate lease and NAT release for shed rows, as the transit site does. That path is cold because it runs only when the table is full. It needs no per-packet allocation beyond the existing `PressureShedSessions` vector.

## #16533 — A firewall-filter term packed on one line whose `then` tail carries any unmodelled token (typo, `next term`, `sample`) passes strict commit with zero warnings and installs a terminating ACCEPT [OPEN]

## Summary

A firewall-filter term packed on one line whose `then` tail carries any unmodelled token (typo, `next term`, `sample`) passes strict commit with zero warnings and installs a terminating ACCEPT

**Finding ID:** `R3-A02-01`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — [verifier: High; downgraded by the independent High re-check: The mechanism is real and I re-ran it at d1ea69f9aa. In worktree RUN/wt/a02 (production files untouched), TestVA02PackedThenStoreCommit and TestVA02PackedThenLenient reproduce every row. A term-line packed `then` tail with one un…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — reachable with a documented spelling, it causes a concrete loss of enforcement, and both fail-closed gates are bypassed.

## Mechanism

Hierarchical text → parser: term node with Keys `[term t1 from ... then dicsard]` and no children → schema walk consumes the identity and ignores the tail → `packedBody` declines on `dicsard` → no `then` child → Action "", UnknownActions empty → strict `validateFilterActionsStrict` silent → `BuildFirewallFilterSnapshots` gives Action "" and NextTerm false → Rust gives terminating Accept for every packet matching the `from`.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa. - pkg/config/compact_tail.go:186-189: `if childSchema == nil { // Outside the modelled grammar at every open level. Do not guess. return node.Children }`. A packed term has no children, so `then` vanishes. - pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:707-708: `termBody := packedBody(termInst.node, termSchema)`. - compiler_firewall.go:778-784: `for _, thenNode := range termBody.FindChildren("then") { compileFilterThen(...) }` followed by `failClosedUnknownFilterAction(term)`. - compiler_firewall.go:2526-2529: `if len(term.UnknownActions) > 0 { term.Action = FilterActionDiscard }`. Nothing populates it here. - userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:1442: `"" => FilterAction::Accept`. - The `from` half survives only because of the #10071 raw re-scan, which has no `then` counterpart.

## Impact

Common lo0/transit filter idioms (`term count-all then count all next term; term block from ... then discard; term rest then accept;`) written compactly become accept-all, and a one-character typo in a packed `discard` turns a deny into a permit. The commit is clean and `show` reflects the intent. The blast radius is every interface the filter is bound to, plus the lo0 nft mirror that consumes the same term. It lasts until someone notices. Recovery is to rewrite the term braced.

## Acceptance / fix direction

In `compileFirewall`, when the packed term tail is non-empty and `packedBody` declines, re-scan the raw `then` segment(s) as the #10071 `from` re-scan does, and record every unrecognised token in `UnknownActions`, so that strict rejects it and tolerant forces discard. Also model `next term` in the packed then grammar. Acceptance: - The probe's packed typo, `sample` and inet6 rows are strict-rejected naming the token, and compile to discard on the tolerant path. - `term t0 then count all next term;` compiles to `next_term=true count="all"` or is refused. - The packed `discard` and braced controls are unchanged.

## Contract (where cited)

- docs/config-schema.md "Compact (packed) stanza bodies": the packed and nested forms "are the same configuration". It names "a filter term with an empty action does not discard (#6685)" as the defect class. - #11357/#2399: an unknown `then` token must fail closed (strict reject; tolerant discard), never become the empty action. - userspace-dp/src/filter/README.md: fall-through is ONLY the authored `next term`, and an empty action TERMINATES as Accept (#14632).

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A02-01` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A02-01 | Medium | A firewall-filter term packed on one line whose then tail carries any unmodelled token… | votes codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:16: - **R3-A02-01 — MATERIAL (Medium, conditional enforcement loss).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/compact_tail.go:183-193` silently returns empty authored children when an unmodelled token breaks an otherwise packed filter term; `pkg/config/compiler_firewall.go:708-713,779-785` sees no `then` action, and `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:1442` maps `""` to terminating `Accept`. The historical store test bound a compact filter and observed `warnings=0`, empty action and unknown-actions on a `dicsard` typo, with valid-packed and bad-braced controls. **Refutation:** requires an authorized author/peer, a specifically term-line packed spelling, and a bound filter; packet acceptance is source-derived from the Rust matcher, not newly measured, and a broad unconditional high-severity network claim is unwarranted. **Decisive check:** current end-to-end regression for typo/`next term` term-line tails, including strict rejection, lenient fail-closed action and snapshot-to-Rust action decoding.

## #16534 — install.sh cleanup_on_fail `rm -f`s xpf.sources whenever this run wrote it, even when it overwrote an existing working source. A failed re-run (the documented channel-rebind procedure) leaves pin and keyring restored but no apt source... [OPEN]

## Summary
install.sh cleanup_on_fail `rm -f`s xpf.sources whenever this run wrote it, even when it overwrote an existing working source. A failed re-run (the documented channel-rebind procedure) leaves pin and keyring restored but no apt source, so the host stops receiving xpf updates

**Finding ID:** R3-B17-03
**Severity (source):** Low — the host silently stops receiving updates, but the failure is announced on stderr and a successful re-run restores the source [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/COHORT/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
A perimeter firewall that silently drops off its update channel after a routine channel rebind.

**Contract:** docs/distribution.md:134-136: "Rerun `install.sh` to rebind channels ... rolls back its marked pin if installation fails". install.sh:83-90 describes restoring prior state. docs/distribution.md:377 says "removes the source", which literally matches the code but was written for the first-install shape. The asymmetry with #11133/#12543 is the defect.

**Trace:** existing install (stable) -> `curl … | sudo sh` with XPF_CHANNEL=edge -> install_keyring (backup) -> write_source overwrites -> apt-get update fails -> EXIT trap restores the keyring and pin and removes the source -> apt never sees xpf again.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
scripts/dist/install.sh:94-97 `if [ "$SRC_WRITTEN" = "1" ]; then ... rm -f "$SRC"`. :416-418 `printf '%s\n' "$body" > "$SRC"; SRC_WRITTEN=1`, with no backup. Pin backup at :463-466 (`PIN_BACKUP=... cp -p`) and restore at :101-109. main() (:548-555) runs write_source before do_install (:514-525: apt-get update, verify_channel, apt-get install). Only debian/xpf.postrm references xpf.sources, and no maintainer script recreates it.

**Probe:** RUN/workers/b17/evidence/probe_b17_install_source_restore.py, re-run by vb17, output in RUN/verify/vb17/probes/install_source_restore.out: `[re-run fails] ... source exists after: False`, `pin exists after: True  restored-to-old: True`. Controls: `control success keeps source: True | first-install failure removes source: True`. Limit: the apt failure is modelled with `false`.

## Acceptance / fix direction
back up a pre-existing source (same-dir temp plus rename), restore it on failure, and remove it only when it did not pre-exist. Update docs/distribution.md:377. Acceptance: the defect cell restores the source byte-for-byte, and both controls still pass.

## Full validated claim

## #16535 — The #6697/#7126 slot-escape and #2419 spelling gates omit the parser-admitted one-child multi-token block spelling `leaf { v1 v2; }`: 13 multi-value sites validate only `c.Keys[:1]`, so a rejected value commits or a valid one is silently dropped… [OPEN]

## Summary

The #6697/#7126 slot-escape and #2419 spelling gates omit the parser-admitted one-child multi-token block spelling `leaf { v1 v2; }`: 13 multi-value sites validate only `c.Keys[:1]`, so a rejected value commits or a valid one is silently dropped (e.g. a proxy-arp address)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A02-03`
**Severity (source report):** Low — this is an assurance and validation gap on a non-Junos spelling. Measured consequences: a proxy-ARP address is silently dropped, and rejected tokens reach the compiled config for RA dns-server-address, login-class permissions and rip neighbor. The RA and sshd runtimes re-validate. [reporter: L…
**Gate verdict (source part):** COHORT (#2419/#6697 gate-completeness gaps on non-Junos spellings) — real, but a minor validation-gate hole.

## Mechanism

Text → parser: one child with Keys `[v1 v2]` → `validateMultiValueLeaf` checks v1 only → compiler reads Keys[0] (drop) or every key (unvalidated) → compiled config.

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa. - pkg/config/schema_walk.go:1806-1818: `keys := c.Keys[:1]; if leafSchema.allChildKeysAreValues { keys = c.Keys }`. - pkg/config/compiler_nat_source.go `proxyARPAddressValues`: `for _, vn := range prop.Children { ... vals = append(vals, vn.Keys[0]) }`. Only Keys[0] of each block child is read.

## Impact

These gates are the evidence other lanes cite to close #2419-class issues. The uncovered form silently drops proxy-ARP entries, which makes the NAT'd address unreachable, and lets commit-check accept values its own validator rejects.

## Acceptance / fix direction

At the walker, refuse a multi-token statement inside a value-list block (one value per statement), or validate all of `c.Keys` wherever the compiler accumulates every key. Add form F to `TestSchemaSpellingDifferentialGate` and `TestSlotEscapeSweep`. Acceptance: 0 escapes in the sixth-form sweep, and the one-child proxy-arp row either compiles both addresses or is refused.

## Contract (where cited)

docs/config-schema.md and `schema_slot_escape_gate_test.go:239-242` claim the gates cover "all five spellings the grammar admits". The parser admits a sixth. #6659 says every authored proxy-arp address is installed or refused.

## Validation provenance

- Source report: `claude-opus-5-5-review-full-firewall-hostile-r3-002.md`, finding `R3-A02-03` (parts file for this claim in `parts/`, synthesis §1).
- Synthesis line: `- R3-A02-03 | Low | The #6697/#7126 slot-escape and #2419 spelling gates omit the parser-admitted one-child… | votes codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT`
- Validated-by three lanes (codex / smr / wonder excerpts from ledgers):

**Codex:** batch00:19: - **R3-A02-03 — COHORT (Low).** **Defect:** `pkg/config/schema_walk_leaf.go:420-441` validates a child's first key where the parser admits `leaf { v1 v2; }`; consumers such as `pkg/config/compiler_nat_source.go:317-327` likewise take only `child.Keys[0]`. Thus the second value can escape a validator or disappear. **Refutation:** that sixth shape is not canonical Junos list spelling; many affected runtime consumers reparse/ignore malformed values, and no reported packet overpermit follows from this source chain. **Decisive check:** establish which multi-value leaves contractually allow a multi-token *single child*, then assert both values are validated and emitted, or reject that shape consistently before compile.

**SMR:** smr batch00 L63: ### R3-A02-03 — one-child multi-token block `leaf { v1 v2; }` escapes slot/spelling gates — **COHORT (Low)** - Defect: Gates enumerate 5 spellings; parser admits 6th. Sites validate/read only `Keys[:1]`/`Keys[0]` (e.g. proxy-arp `proxyARPAddressValues` reads `vn.Keys[0]`) → second value dropped (proxy-arp address lost) or unvalidated tokens reach compiled config (RA/login/rip — runtimes re-validate). - Refutation (strong): Non-Junos spelling; Junos range form `{ A to B; }` is strict-rejected; RA/sshd re-validate; no privilege gain shown. Correctly Low assurance/cohort, not MATERIAL. - Evidence: Mechanism (`schema_walk.go` validateMultiValueLeaf dispatch; Keys[0] readers) consistent at origin/master (file since split into schema_walk_* family — line drift noted). Report executed proxy-arp drop + reject-control asymmetry. - Unresolved: Full 13-site census re-run at origin/master after schema_walk split; rip→FRR consequence untraced (reporter admits). --- ## va03

## #16536 — #11768 residual: the shared_exact per-flow admission cap computes its BDP floor from the class-wide rate over the worker-local flow count, so after per-shard buffer partitioning one flow can hold 75-100% of a worker's... [OPEN]

## Summary
#11768 residual: the shared_exact per-flow admission cap computes its BDP floor from the class-wide rate over the worker-local flow count, so after per-shard buffer partitioning one flow can hold 75-100% of a worker's admission budget

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — the #914 per-flow mouse protection inside a shared_exact (>= 2.5 Gb/s) class is weakened by about `active_shards`x at low-to-moderate local flow counts. The aggregate per-worker cap, the class rate and MQFQ dequeue order are unaffected, so there is no enforcement or isolation loss. The mouse drop consequence is inferred, not lab-measured. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A70-01`
**Source part:** `parts/va70.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=NEEDS_VALIDATION/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
On the 6-worker lab cluster, a >= 2.5 Gb/s exact class (iperf-b/c style) loses #914's mouse protection at the flow counts it was tuned for. A worker's elephant can fill 75-100 % of that worker's admission budget, and mice hashed to the same worker see `admission_buffer_drops` and extra queueing. This is bounded to one worker's share, and recovery is natural as the elephant backs off.

**Contract:** `cos/admission.rs:212-237` (#914): the shared_exact per-flow cap `max(fair_share*2, bdp_floor).clamp(MIN, buffer_limit)` exists because pass-through "allowed a single elephant to occupy the entire queue buffer, starving mice". `admission.rs:123-127` defines the BDP floor as "Per-flow BDP at the queue's rate divided across active_flows". `cos/README.md:300-306` (#11768) says the configured base "is divided by active shards".

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`cos/admission.rs:242-257`: `let prospective = cos_queue_prospective_active_flows(queue, flow_bucket); let fair_share = flow_share_div_ceil(buffer_limit, prospective); let bdp = bdp_floor_bytes(queue.transmit_rate_bytes(), prospective); return clamp_flow_share_to_buffer(fair_share.saturating_mul(SHARED_EXACT_BURST_HEADROOM).max(bdp), buffer_limit);`. `admission.rs:137-140`: `per_flow_rate = transmit_rate_bytes / active_flows.max(1)`, multiplied by 10 ms. `tx/cos_classify.rs:2345-2361`: `buffer_limit = cos_shared_exact_buffer_limit(queue, flow_bucket, active_shards)`, with the shard count taken from the root lease. `admission.rs:355-375`: shard limit = `buffer_bytes / active_shards` (+ #707/#717). `flow_hash.rs:193-211`: prospective count = this worker's `active_flow_buckets` (+1 when the target bucket is empty).

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — a Rust unit probe called the production `cos_shared_exact_buffer_limit` + `cos_queue_flow_share_limit` with a single-shard positive control. The field consequence is NEEDS_VALIDATION.

## #16537 — `candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` enumerates every address of the matched pool-mode source-NAT rule (and every NAT64 pool_v4 address) for every SYN in syn-cookie mode. The caller then clones the vector and scans it even when no bindl... [OPEN]

## Summary
`candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` enumerates every address of the matched pool-mode source-NAT rule (and every NAT64 pool_v4 address) for every SYN in syn-cookie mode. The caller then clones the vector and scans it even when no bindless IPsec fence is configured. With a /16 pool this costs milliseconds per SYN.

**Finding ID:** R3-N07-03
**Severity (source):** High — High — appliance availability. In the affected configuration, an unauthenticated flood of about 350 challenged SYN/s per worker (by the release-mode model) saturates a worker. RSS spreads the flood across all workers, so forwarding collapses appliance-wide, and the flood-defence feature is the amplifier. The configuration is a condition: syn-cookie active on the zone where the flood enters, plus a pool-mode SNAT rule matching the flooded flows with a large pool (/20 to /16). With a /24 pool the extra cost is about 2 µs per SYN, which is only a Medium-class degradation. [reporter: High]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=MATERIAL/MATERIAL/MATERIAL (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Operators enable SYN cookies precisely for hostile traffic. In a CGNAT-style deployment with a large pool, enabling them makes each flood SYN thousands of times more expensive than a normal packet, so a modest flood stalls RX servicing on every worker and every flow hashed to those workers starves.

**Contract:** docs/engineering-style.md hot-path discipline: no per-packet allocation on the hot path. SYN cookies exist to make the per-SYN cost of a flood constant and small. The call-site comment calls the rework "predicate-only … before any NAT allocation".

**Trace:** Config: `security screen ids-option X tcp syn-flood` on zone lan with syn-cookie protection mode, a lan→wan source-NAT rule with a pool of 198.51.0.0/16, and a permit policy lan→wan. Compile: the pool expands to 65536 `pool_addresses_v4`. Runtime: the zone goes over threshold, the screen mints a challenge, and the prescreen passes. On the session-miss arm, `candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` builds 65536 NatDecisions (about 3 MB), merge-collects them, clones about 3 MB into `fence_candidates`, and scans all of them, only then emitting the SYN-ACK. This repeats for every flood SYN on every worker.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:5256-5300` @d1ea69f9aa: `if let Some(challenge) = deferred_syn_cookie_challenge.take() { let candidate_nats = nat_exception::candidate_source_nats_for_challenge(…); let fence_candidates: Vec<NatDecision> = match &candidate_nats { Some(list) if !list.is_empty() => list.clone(), _ => vec![decision.nat] }; … fence_candidates.iter().any(|candidate| …bindless_ipsec_selector_fence.matches_with_nat(source, destination, *candidate))`. `poll_descriptor/nat_exception.rs:264-275` (NAT64: every `prefix.pool_v4`) and `:319-326` (`candidates.into_iter().map(|c| base_nat.merge(c)).collect()`). `nat/source/mod.rs:1509-1519`: "Every pool address" `rule.pool_addresses_v4.iter().map(|addr| NatDecision{…}).collect()`, with the same pattern for v6 at `:1521-1535`. `nat/source/expand.rs:21` `MAX_POOL_PREFIX_HOSTS: u64 = 65536`. The trigger is at `screen/zone.rs:518-545` (MintChallenge for every over-attack SYN, with no mint-rate cap) and `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1628-1652` (`deferred_syn_cookie_challenge = Some(challenge)` after the `syn_cookie_reply_admitted` prescreen, which does not consider NAT).

**Probe:** `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_syncookie_probe_tests.rs`, run with `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vn07_syncookie -- --nocapture --test-threads=1` (debug). Control, interface-mode SNAT: `1 candidates, 1.364µs per challenged SYN` (pass). Scaling: `/24: 256 candidates, 21.088µs`, `/20: 4096, 283.136µs`, `/16: 65536, 4.615138ms`. `size_of NatDecision = 48`. The bound cell failed. Release model `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_syncookie_release_model.rs` (rustc -O): `/24 2.001µs`, `/20 126.219µs`, `/16 2.834877ms per SYN`. Outputs: `RUN/verify/vn07/vn07_syncookie.out` and `vn07_syncookie_release_model.out`. Limits: the probe calls the dominant function and the clone, not the whole poll iteration, so the real per-SYN cost is a superset. The model is a reconstruction, not production code.

## Acceptance / fix direction
Precompute, per source-NAT rule (and per NAT64 prefix) and per fence generation, whether any pool address intersects the bindless selector fence. Skip candidate enumeration entirely when the fence is empty. Keep the `is_some` allocation-failure shape check as an O(1) rule-level predicate. Never allocate per challenged SYN. Acceptance: the per-SYN challenge cost is independent of pool size (the vn07 bound cell turns green), the #15947 fence-suppression and allocation-failure cells stay green, and a lab flood with a /16 pool shows worker pps comparable to interface-mode SNAT.

## Full validated claim
<details><summary>Source claim (vn07.md)</summary>

### R3-N07-03 — The SYN-cookie challenge path builds, merges and clones one NatDecision per source-NAT pool address for every challenged SYN, at O(pool) cost per packet during a SYN flood
- **Finding ID:** R3-N07-03
- **Title:** `candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` enumerates every address of the matched pool-mode source-NAT rule (and every NAT64 pool_v4 address) for every SYN in syn-cookie mode. The caller then clones the vector and scans it even when no bindless IPsec fence is configured. With a /16 pool this costs milliseconds per SYN.
- **Discovery origin:** deep-review run review-work.RPb6LXop3w; discovering agent worker n07 (A6/A1 session-glue + poll-descriptor engineer); model inherited from coordinator claude-opus-5-5, not separately reported; verified by vn07
- **Severity:** High — appliance availability. In the affected configuration, an unauthenticated flood of about 350 challenged SYN/s per worker (by the release-mode model) saturates a worker. RSS spreads the flood across all workers, so forwarding collapses appliance-wide, and the flood-defence feature is the amplifier. The configuration is a condition: syn-cookie active on the zone where the flood enters, plus a pool-mode SNAT rule matching the flooded flows with a large pool (/20 to /16). With a /24 pool the extra cost is about 2 µs per SYN, which is only a Medium-class degradation. [reporter: High]
- **Confidence:** High for the mechanism and its linear scaling, which are measured. Medium for the absolute magnitude, because the debug test build and a release-mode model ran on a loaded shared host (loadavg 5.6/11.1/10.4).
- **Verification:** EXECUTED — I ran the production `nat::candidate_source_nat_translations` plus the caller's clone in a debug test, and ran a release-mode standalone model of the same map/collect/merge/clone/scan shape. The full per-SYN pipeline (screen → miss path) was not driven end to end, and no lab flood was run.
- **Gate verdict:** MATERIAL — the trigger is a reachable remote flood in a committable configuration (pools up to 65536 hosts are accepted), the cost is measured and linear, and it was introduced by c1b86e871b (#15947).
- **Contract:** docs/engineering-style.md hot-path discipline: no per-packet allocation on the hot path. SYN cookies exist to make the per-SYN cost of a flood constant and small. The call-site comment calls the rework "predicate-only … before any NAT allocation".
- **Adversarial analysis:** The protection at stake is SYN-flood resistance and worker-loop availability. The actor is a host that can send SYNs that match a pool-SNAT rule through a permitted policy, for example a subscriber or inside host in a CGNAT-style deployment. Sources inside the matched range can be spoofed. The prerequisites are syn-cookie protection mode with the zone over its attack threshold, which is exactly the flood state. The challenged assumption is that the challenge predicate is cheap.
- **Evidence:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:5256-5300` @d1ea69f9aa: `if let Some(challenge) = deferred_syn_cookie_challenge.take() { let candidate_nats = nat_exception::candidate_source_nats_for_challenge(…); let fence_candidates: Vec<NatDecision> = match &candidate_nats { Some(list) if !list.is_empty() => list.clone(), _ => vec![decision.nat] }; … fence_candidates.iter().any(|candidate| …bindless_ipsec_selector_fence.matches_with_nat(source, destination, *candidate))`. `poll_descriptor/nat_exception.rs:264-275` (NAT64: every `prefix.pool_v4`) and `:319-326` (`candidates.into_iter().map(|c| base_nat.merge(c)).collect()`). `nat/source/mod.rs:1509-1519`: "Every pool address" `rule.pool_addresses_v4.iter().map(|addr| NatDecision{…}).collect()`, with the same pattern for v6 at `:1521-1535`. `nat/source/expand.rs:21` `MAX_POOL_PREFIX_HOSTS: u64 = 65536`. The trigger is at `screen/zone.rs:518-545` (MintChallenge for every over-attack SYN, with no mint-rate cap) and `poll_descriptor/mod.rs:1628-1652` (`deferred_syn_cookie_challenge = Some(challenge)` after the `syn_cookie_reply_admitted` prescreen, which does not consider NAT).
- **Probe:** `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_syncookie_probe_tests.rs`, run with `cargo test --bin xpf-userspace-dp vn07_syncookie -- --nocapture --test-threads=1` (debug). Control, interface-mode SNAT: `1 candidates, 1.364µs per challenged SYN` (pass). Scaling: `/24: 256 candidates, 21.088µs`, `/20: 4096, 283.136µs`, `/16: 65536, 4.615138ms`. `size_of NatDecision = 48`. The bound cell failed. Release model `RUN/verify/vn07/probes/vn07_syncookie_release_model.rs` (rustc -O): `/24 2.001µs`, `/20 126.219µs`, `/16 2.834877ms per SYN`. Outputs: `RUN/verify/vn07/vn07_syncookie.out` and `vn07_syncookie_release_model.out`. Limits: the probe calls the dominant function and the clone, not the whole poll iteration, so the real per-SYN cost is a superset. The model is a reconstruction, not production code.
- **Trace:** Config: `security screen ids-option X tcp syn-flood` on zone lan with syn-cookie protection mode, a lan→wan source-NAT rule with a pool of 198.51.0.0/16, and a permit policy lan→wan. Compile: the pool expands to 65536 `pool_addresses_v4`. Runtime: the zone goes over threshold, the screen mints a challenge, and the prescreen passes. On the session-miss arm, `candidate_source_nats_for_challenge` builds 65536 NatDecisions (about 3 MB), merge-collects them, clones about 3 MB into `fence_candidates`, and scans all of them, only then emitting the SYN-ACK. This repeats for every flood SYN on every worker.
- **Refutation attempt:** I checked these possible guards. `#[cold] #[inline(never)]` affects only code layout. There is no early exit when the fence is empty: the scan runs, and the full vector is built because `candidate_nats.is_some()` is part of `admitted`. Only the deterministic-NAT arm is O(1). The screen has no cap on challenges per second, and per-source thresholds do not stop spoofed sources. In this run, a60 deferred this to n07. The reporter's claim held. I narrowed the severity condition to large pools (/20 and above) and noted that /24 is minor.
- **HPC/invariant check:** The cost unit is O(pool) work plus about 2×48×pool bytes of heap per challenged SYN on the worker's single-threaded loop. Large allocations are mmap-backed, so page faults dominate. There is no ownership or concurrency hazard; this is pure cost amplification.

## #16538 — Brace-elided `ssh no-password-authentication;` / `no-passwords;` and `api-auth metrics-require-auth;` pass strict commit and compile to false; the #2419/#8690 compact-block ratchet that should catch them is red at base (36 new compact-blind rows) [OPEN]

## Summary

Brace-elided `ssh no-password-authentication;` / `no-passwords;` and `api-auth metrics-require-auth;` pass strict commit and compile to false; the #2419/#8690 compact-block ratchet that should catch them is red at base (36 new compact-blind rows)

**Finding ID:** `R3-A02-04`
**Severity (source report):** Medium — management-plane authentication hardening the operator committed is silently not applied. sshd keeps PasswordAuthentication at the host default, so the password brute-force surface stays open. Loopback `/metrics` stays readable by any local UID (the #16072 exposure). The scope is bounded to…
**Gate verdict (source part):** MATERIAL — a reachable, strict-clean authoring spelling silently drops security hardening, and the guard designated for this class is red, so it detects nothing.

## Mechanism

Text → parser: `ssh` node with Keys `[ssh no-password-authentication]` → schema walk ignores tokens past the identity → compact normalizer does not admit the pair → `FindChild` finds nothing → `NoPasswordAuthentication=false` → sshd drop-in omits `PasswordAuthentication no` → host default (password auth on).

## Evidence (source report / ledgers, at base `d1ea69f9aa`; see ledgers for current-master re-check)

All at d1ea69f9aa. - pkg/config/compiler_system.go:1336-1338: a single `ssh` node "Preserve[s] the existing normalizer path". Only the multi-block arm (:1341-1344) calls `packedBodyChildren`. - :1429-1434: `sshNode.FindChild("no-password-authentication")` (children only). - pkg/config/compact_normalize_scope.go: the admitted ssh pairs do not include the two flags, and api-auth admits only `api-key`. - pkg/daemon/daemon_hostauth_apply.go:1401-1406: `if ssh.NoPasswordAuthentication || ssh.NoPasswords { lines = append(lines, "PasswordAuthentication no") }`.

## Impact

An operator hardening SSH or /metrics sees the hardening in `show configuration`, while sshd still accepts passwords and /metrics stays open to local users. This persists across reboots until the stanza is rewritten. More broadly, every new child-only leaf lands silently while the ratchet stays red.

## Acceptance / fix direction

Admit `(ssh, no-password-authentication)`, `(ssh, no-passwords)` and `(api-auth, metrics-require-auth)` to `compactNormalizeInScope`, or expand single `ssh`/`api-auth` nodes with `packedBodyChildren` as the multi-block arm does. Triage the other 33 rows (admit them or record a reasoned exclusion). Make the ratchet blocking for pkg/config. Acceptance: - `TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` is green. - The elided ssh and api-auth probe rows compile to true. - The elided flag-only `metrics-require-auth` is refused like its braced twin.

## Contract (where cited)

- docs/config-schema.md, the #8690/#9056 admission rule: a brace-elided site that compiles to the empty stanza must be admitted to `compactNormalizeInScope` or recorded as a reasoned exclusion. - `TestCompactBlockEquivalenceInventory2419` is the ratchet that fails on a "NEW compact-blind site". - #15282/#15630 define `no-password-authentication`/`no-passwords` as rendering `PasswordAuthentication no`. - #16072 makes `metrics-require-auth` gate loopback /metrics, and refuses the flag without a credential.

The leaves exist in the schema (`schema_system.go:651-653,682-683`) but the compact normalizer has no matching rewrite for these flags. Historical #2419/#8690 regression had 36 red compact rows at report base; do not extrapolate that exact count to this master. **Refutation:** actual remote password acceptance requires a live sshd configuration, configured credentials and reachability; actual metrics exposure depends on bind/auth defaults. ## #16539 — install.sh validate_archive_key (the #14833 pin) does `mkdir -p /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir` and uses it as the GNUPGHOME parent whenever TMPDIR is unset, which is always the case under `curl … | sudo sh`. This leaves a... [OPEN]

## Summary
install.sh validate_archive_key (the #14833 pin) does `mkdir -p /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir` and uses it as the GNUPGHOME parent whenever TMPDIR is unset, which is always the case under `curl … | sudo sh`. This leaves a developer-convention tree on every installed host, and the install aborts if that path cannot be created

**Finding ID:** R3-B17-04
**Severity (source):** Low — host hygiene, plus an unnecessary install-failure mode. The reporter's GNUPGHOME hijack needs a pre-existing group-writable /var/worktrees, which a production host does not have (root creates it 0755), so I give it no weight [reporter: Low]
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED per synthesis)

## Mechanism / impact
Every Tier-A install carries a stray developer directory. Hosts with an unusual or read-only /var layout fail to install.

**Contract:** #14833 is scoped to "build/test scratch". docs/distribution.md:360-377 enumerates what the installer mutates (keyring, apt source, pin, apt install), and a /var/worktrees tree is not on that list.

**Trace:** `curl … | sudo sh` -> validate() -> validate_archive_key -> mkdir under /var/worktrees -> gpg --show-keys under it -> rm of the key home only, so the tree is left behind.

## Evidence (at current master / source base d1ea69f9aa, re-verified at origin/master in ledgers)
scripts/dist/install.sh:196-199 `if [ -z "${TMPDIR:-}" ]; then mkdir -p /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir || die "cannot create scratch dir."; fi` / `_key_home=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir}/xpf-archive-key-check.XXXXXX")`. The commit 99e8f3f26d (#14833, ancestor) message says "make dist/install.sh create the pinned dir only when TMPDIR is unset". scripts/scratch-pinning-selftest.sh:37 audits install.sh.

**Probe:** RUN/workers/b17/evidence/probe_b17_install_scratch.sh, re-run by vb17 (stubs only, nothing mutated), output in RUN/verify/vb17/probes/install_scratch.out: `mkdir -p /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir`, `mktemp -d /var/worktrees/.cache/tmpdir/xpf-archive-key-check.XXXXXX`. Control (TMPDIR set): `mktemp -d /var/tmp/b17/...` only.

## Acceptance / fix direction
in shipped scripts, use `mktemp -d -t ...` (honours TMPDIR, otherwise /tmp), and exempt scripts/dist/install.sh from scratch-pinning-selftest. Acceptance: the probe's unset cell performs no /var/worktrees operation.

## Full validated claim

## #16540 — fairness-eval returns PASS (exit 0) when every flow delivers zero bytes across the whole steady-state window, and no harness arms the aggregate-throughput gate that would catch it [OPEN]

## Summary
fairness-eval returns PASS (exit 0) when every flow delivers zero bytes across the whole steady-state window, and no harness arms the aggregate-throughput gate that would catch it

**Severity (source report):** Low — Low — a false green on the CoS fairness merge/regression gate in a narrow outage shape, with no dataplane effect. The sweep summary still prints avg_mbps of about 0, so a human reader can notice it. [reporter: Low]

**Finding ID:** `R3-A70-02`
**Source part:** `parts/va70.md` in research synthesis `r3-002`
**Validated:** codex/smr/wonder=COHORT/COHORT/COHORT (codex/smr/wonder lanes; at least 2 MATERIAL/COHORT, no NEG/FIXED)

## Mechanism / defect
The fairness sweep is the regression gate for CoS scheduler changes, the area where wedge/stall defects (C08-01 class) have been found. A run that blackholes the class across the window is recorded as a fairness PASS. Automation keyed on `verdict` would accept it, and a human would have to notice avg_mbps of about 0.

**Contract:** `docs/fairness-regimes.md` "Acceptance gates" Gate 1 defines a starved flow as one below 1 % of the mean per-flow throughput for the whole window. The doc avoids the word "zero-throughput" only so as not to imply strictly 0 Mb/s, which makes 0 the canonical starved case. `userspace-dp/src/fairness_eval/README.md` calls the tool "a merge gate for the CoS fairness contract". `fairness_eval/windowing.rs:113-127` (#7206) calls a near-total outage scoring PASS "a false PASS that can carry a merge decision".

## Evidence (at source base `d1ea69f9aa`, verify at current master)
`userspace-dp/src/fairness.rs:84-90`: `if total_cells == 0 || total_bytes == 0 { return 0; }` (no flow counts as starved). `fairness.rs:58-63`: `if mean == 0.0 { return 0.0; }` (CoV 0). `fairness_eval/verdict.rs:204-218`: Gate 3 runs only `if input.expect_saturation`. `test/incus/fairness-harness.sh:726-757` (`run_eval`): `eval_args` never adds `--expect-saturation`. A repo-wide grep finds the flag only in `args.rs`/`verdict.rs`/`report.rs` and the blackbox test. `fairness-harness.sh:802-804` exits with iperf3's status before evaluating when iperf3 fails.

**Verification (research):** EXECUTED — the fresh `fairness-eval` ran on synthetic iperf3/binding inputs, with positive controls in both directions. Field reachability is STATIC.
